title: Cosme

reviews.review:
Good food, super expensive!

The decor is beautiful, dark, and classy, what you would expect from a upscale Chelsea restaurant.

We had: 

- Uni & Bone Marrow Tostada - delicious, wonderful combination  

- Duck Carnitas - very good

- Striped Bass with Plantains - tasty

- Corn Husk Meringue - delicious  and unique

This meal was very good but extremely expensive. If you come here, expect to pay serious coin.
Service was great, all of the food tastes great- but definitely on the small side. Our server initially said everything is to share but the plates were all minuscule besides the duck carnitas.

Love love love the vibes here! The dining room is so beautiful and the lighting is very dark but in a good way. 

I was really impressed with the food and the portion sizes. I feel like sometimes with restaurants like these, it can be hard to be full, but we ordered the guac to share (so delicious) and then one entree each from the middle section of the menu and we were satisfied! I had the octopus and it was incredible -- so tender and flavourful and it also comes with corn tortillas on the side. 

But of course we couldn't stop there and we had to have dessert also -- we ordered the chocolate guava cake. 

One thing that I thought could be better -- we asked for more tostadas for our guac and then it wasn't until we got the bill that we realised extra tostadas came at a charge. Wish they told us that before we ordered them. Plus they only give like 4.

First, why the eff is this place so dark? Did a black hole take up residence inside and decide it liked paying NYC rent prices?

Seriously, the interior is darker than Satan's crotch. It isn't dim, it isn't candlelit, it isn't ambient--it is just a graveyard for light. It's darker than Elon Musk's web browser history. I've climbed caves miles under the Earth's crust that were brighter than this restaurant.

Second, the food is overpriced mediocrity. To call it "elevated Mexican" is an insult to both Mexicans and elevators. 

I came with a group of friends, so we shared everything family-style. The Uni Tostada was okay, but nothing I haven't had from a million other tasting menus, upscale Japanese/Korean spots, etc. Conversely, the Tataki al Pastor was probably our best dish, and the fish was perfectly prepared. 

The Carrot Tlayuda wasn't bad, but it was too heavy on sauce and cheese, and oversalted. The Mole de la Casa was disappointingly bland; I'm sure it took forever to make, but someone at the end of the assembly line apparently forgot to add any seasoning.

And the much-touted Duck Carnitas--the main reason we came here--was a joke. Don't get me wrong, the duck was well made, and I have no complaints about the tortillas. But come on! $112 for a serving of, maybe, six tacos at best? You people realize you could have, like, THREE actual whole Peking ducks--perfectly marinated and roasted--for the same price at any decent Chinese restaurant? FFS with this pretentiousness.

The only bright spot--and I mean that both figuratively and literally, given the aforementioned cavern of blackness we dined in--was the famous Cornhusk Meringue dessert. Of course, at $22 per plate, it had better be good. Or...You could go to, say, Konban and get their gorgeous Corn Ice Cream dessert (which takes just as much, if not more, skill to make) for $13.

Obligatory libation mention: I wasn't really interested in dropping another $20+ to sip a teeny-tiny cocktail in pitch blackness, so I shared the Cherry Smash mocktail, which was decent.

I'm sure Cosme was the bees knees way back when, but the version I experienced recently feels like a faded beauty queen that's long worn out her welcome. 

Also, turn on some damn lights.

Cosme Review

If you're looking for a place that nails modern Mexican cuisine in a sleek Manhattan setting, Cosme should be at the top of your list. This is the kind of spot that somehow manages to feel both lively and laid-back--where you can post up at the bar for a solo meal or celebrate something major with friends and a few too many mezcal cocktails.

From the moment you walk in, the dining room's warm lighting and open kitchen draw you in. But what really commands your attention is the smell of freshly made tortillas and slow-cooked meats. The staff here is friendly in that way that makes you feel like they've been saving a seat for you all day--even if you just wandered in off the street. And while Cosme's menu is full of intriguing small plates, the larger shared dishes are the real show-stoppers.

The photos I snapped pretty much tell the story. First up, the carnitas (here, duck carnitas are a signature, but you can also find other slow-cooked options). Served in a cast-iron skillet, the meat is perfectly crisp on the edges, impossibly tender on the inside, and arrives with bright garnishes like thinly sliced radish, cilantro, and a pop of heat from sliced chiles. The side of chunky green salsa adds a tangy brightness that you'll want to spoon over every bite. Roll it all up in a warm tortilla, and you'll understand why people keep coming back.

Another standout is the sweet potato tostada, which might sound simple, but Cosme manages to make it a textural wonderland. The sweet potato is whipped into a silky purée that contrasts perfectly with the crunchy tostada shell, while the fresh greens piled on top give it a garden-fresh feel. It's hearty enough to stand on its own but doesn't weigh you down--exactly what you need before diving into a heavier main.

Make sure you save room for dessert, too. Cosme's famous corn husk meringue might not be pictured here, but it's worth mentioning as a must-try. It's the kind of dish you'll still be thinking about days later (and telling everyone you know they have to try it).

Yes, Cosme is on the pricier side, and it's typically packed--so you'll want to make a reservation or be ready to wait at the bar (which is never a punishment if you order one of their agave-forward cocktails). But if you're in the market for an upscale Mexican feast that feels both inventive and deeply satisfying, Cosme is more than worth the splurge. This is the type of restaurant that'll make you swear you'll be back before you've even finished the last bite of carnitas. And trust me--you really will.

Loved the food, drinks, ambiance, and service. We started with the Cadillac margarita and the prickly pear cocktail. The Cadillac was a great margarita and really enjoyed it. The prickly pear drink was very refreshing and not too sweet. The starter tostada with the sauces was really delicious. Especially loved the orange spicy one. 

We ordered the cauliflower tamal and the duck carnitas. The tamal was delicious. I loved the take on cauliflower many ways and it was vegan! The duck was really good. I loved the blue corn tortillas. The salsas were also delicious and I loved the vegetables. The duck was a bit dry in some spots. Super flavorful and loved the skin. This was enough food for two people. 

We had the meringue for dessert. This was a great dessert. Not too sweet and I loved the concept. 

The espresso dessert drink was also great. Would definitely recommend. 

We sat at the bar and the service was flawless. The bartender we talked to was so nice and even let us try the mandarin oranges with work salt with a shot mezcal only found at their restaurants. 

Would definitely recommend and also recommend a reservation.

Cosme has been on my Hitlist for a while now and earlier this week I'm happy to say that it was worth the wait. We had an amazing dinner service here, with a mellow and cozy atmosphere without the pretentiousness of most restaurants of this caliber here in NY. Standouts were the fluke tosada, the duck carnitas, the mole, and the cauliflower tamal. Everything was well seasoned, nicely portioned, and beautifully plated. We finished the feast with pumpkin cheesecake and their signature cornhusk meringue. Overall we were satisfied and will most likely come back.

Initially, I was looking forward to our visit. Though we originally came for drinks, I ordered the guacamole, which I found excellent. I had planned to return and explore more of your menu. As a Yelp Elite member, I was even considering writing an amazing review.

However, our experience took a turn at the end of our meal. Upon reviewing our bill, we noticed an extra drink had been mistakenly added. We brought this to the staff's attention, and while the issue was corrected, this was the first mistake. After settling our tab and leaving a generous tip, I got up to put on my coat near the exit when our waiter, Jose, suddenly panicked. He loudly asked the hostess if I had paid, then frantically ran to the bartender, causing a scene. His behavior was completely unacceptable and implied that I was attempting to walk out on my bill, despite having just paid.

Shocked and appalled, I addressed my concerns with the hostess, who did not offer to get a manager but instead led me to the bar, where the staff tried to justify the confusion by claiming one drink had been left open. Even though everything was accounted for, they excused Jose's actions and offered drinks to make up for it. This response only made matters worse. The entire incident was unprofessional, embarrassing, and completely ruined what had been an otherwise pleasant evening.

My friend and I left feeling disrespected and disappointed, and we have no plans to return. I hope your management takes this feedback seriously, as no paying customer should be subjected to such treatment.

I reached out to the restaurant directly using the same email, and the response I received from Christian Muñoz was shockingly unprofessional. His dismissive reply not only disregarded the entire experience but also added insult to injury. After reading his response, it's clear why his staff behaved the way they did. It all starts at the top. Unbelievable.

Cosme is the first restaurant in NYC that brought in sophisticated CDMX food as early as 2015 (maybe even earlier?), and paved the way for other nicer CDMX restaurants to flourish. For this I always appreciate Cosme. Plus the food is genuinely delicious! I don't get the 3+ rating at all.

I was at Cosme this week for a group dinner, and I was pleasantly surprised by both the beautiful atmosphere and the kind service. 

The duck carnitas at Cosme are unforgettable - order that, for sure. I loved the spiked hot chocolate, as well.

Seriously underwhelming. I got the duck which is their most requested dish. It's was just ok. The drinks were bad, which I heard before trying. Wouldn't go again. Wouldn't recommend. Good service though

a very lovely resturant and delicious food.  the vibe and atmosphere was very cool and fun and my daughters had a great time.  their nachos and dip blew us all away, we had to ask for more.  the food is excellent and we all enjoyed it as a family!

Well..., what can I say about so many negative reviews. The more upscale a restaurant is, the more pretentious clientele is: harder to please, who will give 3 stars just because a napkin wasn't folded perfectly. To me, the most hyped about Meringue was just good, not mind-blowing.  But every other dish was very good. Duck was heavenly. Given that there are extremely few places where I come repeatedly, this one is definitely one of them.

Elevated Mexican dining in the heart of Nomad! Plenty of space and calm ambiance so great for group catch-up -- we especially loved all the corn flavors: corn husk meringue and corn omelette were to die for!

The ambiance inside was so lovely. Food was excellent, an upscale twist on Mexican cuisine with well balanced flavors. Drinks are a bit spirit forward but otherwise good. Service was good, only mildly irked by the fact that they got my drink order wrong and then marked it as "didn't like" on the receipt when they voided it. Might just be how the system defaults, but I was given the wrong order, it wasn't just that I didn't like the drink lol

I brought some colleagues to dinner at Cosme to celebrate a milestone and was excited to eat there again. While overall the food was wonderful there were a few missteps that surprised me along the way. Firstly, when we arrived I asked about non alcoholic drinks since my colleagues don't drink. Despite my question, the server took away the drink menus and left us alone at the table (no menus) for several minutes. Eventually she came back and acted pleasantly surprised when we gave her our drink orders. 
We ordered 3 smaller plates and one large between three of us - Hiramasa Tostada, Tataki Al Pastor, the Octopus and the Duck Carnitas for two. Honestly, this was a bit too much food and we were so full. The Hiramasa tostada was light and fresh but hard to share, the tataki al pastor was a Cobia sliced thin with delicious seasonings and a pineapple puree that was bliss. The octopus was the best of the three small plates and quite hearty - one frustration was that they served this with a dull fish knife but the octopus needed to be cut with a sharp knife. Finally the duck was perfectly moist and fabulous, always get this one! Overall it was great but I was glad to be leaving at 8:45 since starting around 8pm the noise level got so high we had to shout to hear each other. Fun but not perfect!
Andrea is a star!!! Top quality service. Incredible meal overall. All three dishes we ordered and our drinks were so delicious.

Had a lot of hopes surrounding this restaurant, being one of the world's best 50 restaurants. I don't know if I would agree.

The espresso martini was pretty good, one of the better ones I've had.

Onto the food, literally everything came with a tortilla or a tostada (they even start with it as an appetizer). I think that just threw me off because all the food just seemed repetitive. 

The duck and the steak alone each being $100 is crazy, not worth that price point. 

Service was good. But I wouldn't return, I wasn't blown away by the food.
Food was excellent and creative.   Service was swift and courteous.  But the room is so loud we could hardly hear eachother.   We think the prices are high relative to the overall experience.

Upscale yet relaxed vibe.  Excellent service. Delicious food with an intriguing take on Mexican cuisine.  The avocado sauce for the beef was out of this world and the corn husk meringue dessert was heavenly!  

We will return!!
Awesome place. Their crudo tostada and the black garlic ancho steak were both delicious. Great cocktails too. Highly recommend for a nice occasion.
Best meal in New York. Always hits. Actually worth the price. Anyone who says anything else is lying!!

Food was decent, service was not. Hostesses were great but our server was god awful. The repeated egregious mistakes and then entitled attitude about gratuity was disgusting. This place does not deserve a star.
Food was pretty decent and service was also good. I don't think the ambiance was special but overall a decent spot.
I like the food a lot here. Get the asparagus and mole for sure but everything is good

- steak tacos were great.
- margarita was good.
- it was too loud to hear my server or talk to others at the table. 
- the tostados and 2 starter sauces were NOT good.
- all the other food was just okay. 
- when I first ate here, years ago, it was awesome.  Today, I was very underwhelmed

This was the most delightfully magnificently magically gracefully perfectly place for a nice family dinner!! Food was great and so fulfillingly tasty. Service was quick despite the many people being here. 10/10!!!

Kind regards 

(PS: I would come again if I was as rich as Elon musk or Jeffery bezos or smth!! )

Cosme is a delightful place to visit for a fine dining experience. The ambiance is classy and minimalistic, the service is courteous, and each dish on the menu is thoughtfully curated and plated to perfection. The drinks are fantastic too! We really enjoyed our visit and would highly recommend it!

Disappointed at the food. 
A little blend and noting special that I can remember for the meal
The worst Mexican food I've ever had, with very mediocre tastes. The ambience is nice, but very suited towards finance bro culture the service was unremarkable.

Everything went well at Cosme. I was expecting a fusion of food with Mexican traditional dishes, and this was one of the most memorable dinners I had in New York. The service was efficient but still friendly. The Telenovela Part IX is probably my favorite drink here. Laid-back vibes, but the food was outstanding. We had the aguachile, the octopus, and the dove Soler al Pastor: moist, tender, and the flavor was spot on. We ended up (I don't know how, really) having some room for dessert and decided to split the cornhusk meringue. True to its roots. Can't wait to be back.

Service was wonderful but ridiculously priced food for very small plates. Food was good but nothing spectacular. Cocktails also not worth it, pours are small and inflated with large amounts of ice. You'll spend a couple of hundred and leave hungry.

Taco Bell service with passable/good food - 

Went there for father's day lunch to enjoy a high end and elegantly presented Mexican meal with my in-laws and kids .... at high end prices to boot. Today's Cosme is a far cry from the one that made a splash for many years after opening. The food is good but not above any reasonably decent Mexican restaurant doing a modern take on the cuisine. The service on the other hand is entirely absent. We were rushed to put in our entire order at once since the meal was going to be coursed... as it should be. However all the food was delivered at the same time. We had asked early on if we could order more food should our order not be sufficient and were assured that would not be a problem. When we tried to order additional dishes we were told the kitchen was closing in 5 mins so it would not be possible... at 2:15pm. We saw our waitress only twice - when we were initially seated and then when we put in our order. she didn't come by once to inquire on the drinks/food, if we needed anything else etc. We had to struggle to flag down wait staff that were ill informed about the menu and beverages/wince. I asked for the manager twice but he/she never came by. And funnily enough the restaurant was at half capacity and the staff was hanging around far from the dining area, unconcerned. We felt they just wanted us in and out asap. Its abundantly clear this place is running out the steam from its heyday and milking whatever is left of it. There is nothing high end or elegant left about Cosme. What a poor reflection on a chef with a big reputation. Don't waste your time and money.

Cosme has delicious food, let's start with that. We had reservations on the first night we arrived in NYC, so we were plenty tired from the trip. Very upscale and not a little pretentious --I mean, we're talking corn and tortillas and beans which, even organic? are hardly pricey commodities. The duck was delicious and their dessert a standout --but the prices astronomical, even by NYC standards. The drinks...c'mon. So much ice and relatively small. 
What would keep us away? The *noise level* was utterly unbearable. You're literally shouting at one another to hear above the din, and no real chance of conversation. The waitstaff must bellow in your ear to be heard. Halfway through we stopped trying and just ate our meal without trying to compete. 
   This venue absolutely must address this problem. A few curtains along the side, some swags on the ceiling and a rug or two would go a LONG way toward alleviating this awfulness. We will not go back until this is altered ---it's just too bloody unpleasant. For us, it quite ruined the experience and we were so relieved to leave.

For a very pricey restaurant I left sort of disappointed. It took the server a very long time to even get my drink order (a tiny cup of fresh juice for $12). My two dining companions and I offered a lot of dishes on the menu and nothing really stands out. The fish was ok. The mole was ok. The guacamole wasn't very good. The meringue desert was not good. The taco was a bunch of veggies and that's it. The asparagus was boring. I just can't believe this place has so much hype. Save your money and go elsewhere for a couple hundred dollars.

Went to Cosme last night and it was a wonderful experience! Andrea was our server and she was attentive and gave great service. Ordered the guacamole 10/10, the octopus, soft crab, octopus/ steak and had the corn husk merengue for dessert, all delicious. Can't wait to go back!
I'm usually not a duck fan however I made it an exception to try out their duck carnitas and it was absolutely amazing.

I've been trying to get to this place for a few years. Something kept interrupting my timing.  So I have had my expectations growing...not a particular good thing. How could Cosme live up to my expectations? Well...they did. Our party tried about 10 different dishes and they all delivered.  Beautiful plating and even more delicious flavors. Ceviche's were all divine.  The tortillas...I'd heard so much about these tortillas...I could have just eaten those and been happy. The Duck Carnita's were a standout favorite, as was the Molé de la casa and the soft shell crab.  And of course the corn husk meringue was everything I ever heard it to be. The service was friendly and a perfect pace...overall a spectacular experience for a group of four very demanding diners. Yes...it's pricey...but worth it. Looking forward to another trip.

Our experience at cosme was one for the books . Visiting NY for the first time , experiencing great dining  by one of the best chefs in my book was and will always be one of my most special memories. Anyway , food was savory ! The duck carnitas and cobia al pastor which by the way were such outstanding dishes for sure are both a 9/10. Service was great , the waiters were attentive at all times . Hands-down lo mejor que he comido ! Don't mind my hands on the pic lol , couldn't get great lighting

Cosme was one of the best meals I've had in NYC. The food was extremely fresh - all with very unique flavors. The duck carnitas were INSANE. This was a huge portion that can feed up to 4 people, but definitely recommended trying. The service was very friendly and helpful with what to order. Lastly, the ambiance was vibey and moody! Great for a date night or cocktails!

One of the most gorgeous lunches I've ever had. We did the private dining room experience. 

Every single bite was spectacular. The meal began with guacamole with edible flowers, which was a stunning presentation. Then we had a white fish aguachile with a delightful, verdant broth. Next, we had the most beautiful endive salad with pomegranates and bean puree. This was particularly visually stunning, with deep purple greens accentuating the plate.

We had both the green and the red chilaquiles. The green chilaquiles in particular with chicken had a beautiful acidic green sauce that I thoroughly enjoyed. There were two types of quesadillas, both of which were delicious. For entrees, we had the duck mole (stunning) and lamb barbacoa with shishitos.

Staff was super friendly and knowledgeable. The sommelier chose beautiful and interesting wines for our meal pairing. One was a 100% gamay from beaujolais that went perfectly with the duck mole sauce.

Highly elevated food. Do recommend.
Everything was good. Was a little expensive for what you get but hey it's NYC! Def would recommend trying!

I came here for a friend's birthday dinner on a Sunday evening and enjoyed myself. Cosme is a Mexican restaurant with a chill vibe and cozy atmosphere, despite being larger than I expected. The menu consists of mostly small plates, and we ordered a few items so that we could try different things. The food was fresh and reasonably priced overall. Our server was attentive and answered any questions we had and everyone was friendly. I would come back again.
Falsely advertised a "brunch" When they had no orange juice, no Bloody Mary, and a very limited weird menu that is not even close to a reasonably Mexican high cuisine offering. Stay away.
One of the best meals I've ever had. The mole, aguachile, and drinks were incredible. Not to mention the service was great. Would definitely go again.

Cosme is one of my favorite restaurants in NYC. Expect to pay more for quality and freshness. We loved every single dish we ordered. The service here is great, everyone is very attentive. The appetizers can be a little small, but the entrees make up for it. The cocktails here are amazing! You can tell they put a lot of thought into pairing the drink menu with the food menu. They also have an incredible tequila and mezcal selection. The restaurant itself is sleek and is dimly lit. If you love Mexican food I highly recommend.
Lovely atmosphere and super kind wait staff. Yes, the duck carnitas are as amazing as people say but don't miss the scallops. Super tender and a very refreshing dish !

I am honestly shocked the average star review is 3.5/5 stars. Cosme is one of the best restaurants I've ever been to. Their menu is so creative and combines so many great flavors together and then the dishes are outstanding.

My favorite savory dishes are the strip steak, duck, octopus, and fluke. And then the must-have desserts are the corn husk meringue and chocolate tart. I wish I could have all of these everyday. 

Our service was wonderful recommending the appropriate number of dishes for our party size and the food was paced perfectly.

Came in for a work event with a team of 5 gals. We shared the guacamole, broccolini, lobster al pastor, strip steak and the duck. The duck is a MUST. It was a feast! Definitely a solid amount for the 5 of us. The drinks were solid and fun. I got the paloma and the yuzu raspado, which were both delightfully refreshing. Would I come back without the corporate card, probably not. Also, strangely enough, none of us had decent cell reception. So a solid spot if you want to make sure everyone stays off their phone.
A friend invited us out into town for dinner. This upscale was by far one of my favorites. Being Mexican-American I thought all flavors were spot on. I can't wait to come back!

Ambiance is great , loved the dim lit area for a cocktail. Service was spectacular. The dining experience is sumptuous. To start I tried the spicy margarita they were able to make it with mezcal for me which was nice. We tried the octopus which was delicious and surprisingly spicy, guacamole was good. And my favorite believe it or not were the sweet tamales. we had the fish entre which was also tasty. 3 stars because of the smaller menu. Also the food was not too special even the drinks - it was good but I expected something a bit more l.

Food was good but overpriced, hostess forgot about our reservation and seated us 40 minutes late, and we were charged for a dish we never received. Overall, wouldn't return and your money is best spent elsewhere.

Overall, the place left me wanting more.

Like all other reviews, skip the margarita. Overpriced, no alcohol, too much ice. Ask for less ice, get less drink. They wont even give you more mix haha!

Guacamole was good, flavorful and actually had some heat. Fluke was decent, but a pretty small portion. Sweet potato wasnt bad, but wasnt anything memorable. Lobster, two tiny pieces! The duck carnitas are their signature, but even that had a lotttt of fat served so not edible. 

To have this little quantity, you need the quality to justify the price. But at Cosme, you dont get the quantity, and get only a bit of quality. Very loud, not a place you can hear the waiter or conversate. Wont be back!

We booked a reservation to Cosme a few weeks in advance and on the day of had a wild trip walking across town to get here.  When we arrived, we were greeted by the staff and we let them know about our reservation.  After a quick look up we were brought to our table.

The space is a bit dark and moody.  I really enjoyed the vibe.  The space is also pretty large, especially for NYC as most of the places we visited were half the size or smaller.

We were presented some menus and had a chat with our server.  After some discussions we were asked if we were interested in any drinks and we got some recommendations on beer.  A few minutes later we got some Mexican beers on the hot day.

After a glance through the menu we decided on the mole (just a heads up it's pretty steep @ $25 but it's also a ton of work!), guac and chips as well as the steak tacos.

As I sipped on my beer I just really enjoyed the dark, clean, minimal atmosphere that was lit up.  Really cool vibe and you could definitely just swing by for drinks or drinks and snacks.

The table next to us got the duck which looked excellent!  If I was a bit hungrier we may have added that to our list as well

I've never been a fan of mole so was really curious how this was going to be.  Once it arrived, I have to say, I understand the questions about the price.  However I also know the amount of work that goes into that thing!  All that to say, I think this is the first mole that I really enjoyed.  It had some dark, rich, smoky flavours.  If that's not your thing, definitely skip this.  We agreed to hold off eating all the mole early.  A round of guac and chips came.  This was really good as well but we were holding off for the steak tacos.

Once they arrived, we did a round of steak tacos with just everything that came on the plate.  That was really good.  We then decided to mix and match with the dishes that we didn't finish and got some great tacos out of it.  I was definitely a fan of the dining experience here.

Washrooms are downstairs though there is one on the main floor.  Staff are great, probably the best staff we encountered on this trip.  Good night here and would definitely come back to try other items
The best meal I've had in NYC in a long time! Amazing tostadas, mole is absolutely incredible. Would come back just for the corn husk meringue!

The food was exceptional. 

-guac was fresh and flavorful
-duck carnitas was super tender and between 2 people, we easily had 4-5 tacos each 
-corn husk meringue may be a top 10 dessert in the city 

The drawback is how $$$$ everything is.

Ambiance and service were pleasant. Great neighborhood. 

I'd definitely recommend, but you will be spending quite a bit.

Amazing flavors in all the salsas/sauces. We had the Uni Tostada with bone marrow very delicious and a nice petite portion wonderful balance flavors. 2nd course the Blue Crab Chili Reno wonderfully crusted to perfection the Chili had a nice clean fresh flavor and crab was very mild and delicious even if you don't like seafood or shellfish you have to try this dish, lastly we shared the Duck Carnitas nice mild not fatty flavor as I expected again exquisite flavors and balance. Wonderful service and just the right amount of attention. Recommend wine pairings by the glass to accompany our dishes. The very light tostado crisps to start were amazing and light as well!!! I might need to move to NYC just to eat here again. Atmosphere modern very dimly lit bring readers if you use them!

Absolutely stellar meal. The duck carnitas were perfect. The blue crab relleno was unlike any I'd ever had -- usually these are so heavy. The crisp on this was delicate. My favorite savory item was the octopus. But wow wow wow that corn husk meringue. Simply the best dessert I've ever had. Husband got the basque cheesecake -- I had a bite and it was great too. Excellent service. Really enjoyed everything about this meal.

*must* get the corn husk meringue, even if you're not a meringue nor dessert person. like the one thing you have to do if you visit. portions are on the smaller side, so you might have to get a couple items but they're all sooo good! was packed on a sunday night and the restaurant is pretty big on the inside (outside looks one of those tiny wine bars). highly rec if you're looking for fancier Mexican-inspired food! not exactly your typical taco place
Everything is too sour. If this is authentic Mexican food. I will pass. Been there many times cocktails are good though. Extremely small portion except for the duck.

Starting with the desserts bc they are my highlights. As we all know, the cornhusk merigue is Cosme's signature and well deserved. BUT they also have churros and I can't pass on churros. Look at this beautiful coil  It comes out fresh and crispy, with the perfect soft chew. The merigue is just as exciting. A soft crunch paired with a dreamy mousse and the most delicate hints of corn. Would go back just for these.

For the actual meal, keep in mind I don't like Mexican food so not the best judge. The guac is good. Beautiful presentation and the herbs are super fragrant but lacked a wow factor. I know, it's just guac but at this price point I expect a bit more  I did not expect the duck enmoladas to come out covered in mole negro but it was def unique and I liked it more than I thought. Probs wouldn't order again tho. Chilpachole is TINY and had a burnt taste all throughout. Kinda salty too so wish it came with tortillas on the side.

Churros with dulce de leche $18*
Cornhusk meringue $20*
Herb guacamole $24
Duck enmoladas covered in mole negro $28
Shrimp, clams, and mussels chilpachole $29 

Cosme는 디저트 맛집! 멕시칸 음식을 안좋아해서 메인 디쉬들이 맛있다는 느낌이 안든다. 가격대도 높고 양도 적어서 굳이..? 하지만 디저트 때문에 다시 갈듯. 시그니쳐 옥수수 머랭은 필수다. 바사삭 무너지는 머랭 식감과 달달한 무스 & 은근히 느껴지는 옥수수맛이 매우 조화로움. 츄러스는 그냥 존맛. 갓 튀겨저 따듯하게 나와서 바삭함과 쫀득함이 두배로 느껴진다. 폭신한 비주얼과 다르게 머랭이 묵직해서 약간 질린다 싶을때 츄러스를 먹어주면 됨.

It was fine. Sat us at a table for two. Drinks were probably 2 oz margaritas with a lot of ice. Appetizers were good but not mind-blowing. The chilaquiles came without the chicken that we requested.

Dessert was the best part. Yummy cornhusk meringue. 

Expensive and decent flavors but I don't get the hype.

I have been going to Cosme (and other Michelin-calibre establishments in NYC) for many years so here's a calibrated take. 

- Drinks: A++. This is the best spicy margaritas in the city and I order this to go from their sister restaurant Atla on a weekly basis (yes a $39 bottle of 2 spicy margs). They make their own serrano juice which gives the margs a unique and flavorful kick. 

- Food: I believe most of the disgruntled reviews is because folks don't know what to order and ended up spending a fortune to leave hungry. You should absolutely get the duck carnitas - that's what they are known for and is well worth the $100 price tag because it's a lot of food. Do not order a bunch of the tostadas that run $30 per plate and expect to get full. Tostadas ARE the best things here however, so do give them a try. They change the menu frequently but I have not been disappointed by these. Do not order the guac, you will feel cheated because it tastes like guac you can get anywhere. The random salads are hit or miss but I don't like salads.

- Vibe: A+. Sit at the bar if it's just a party of two. The dining room is substantially less cool and way darker. I've seen a dad eat with his daughter who was on her phone the whole time. The bar is always hopping and the bar is a huge marble counter which in and of itself is very classy. 

- Service: is fine. Not sure what staring contest the reviewer below was talking about (also, kind sir, the chef is not a woman and hasn't been for multiple years so that's not the reason for the 'hype' but what a weird comment). I've occasionally had slow service but nothing offensive. Some bartenders are better than others but on the whole they're all good. I love that I can come by this place after a workout or a shopping trip and get a seat and sip on spicy margs. It's the best of NYC ;)

The food is amazing. Unique and well thought out creative dishes. 
I would not recommend getting wine by the glass or champagne. I have never seen such tiny pours for a glass of wine that are not inexpensive. They are definitely getting 8 glasses per bottle. I would stick to cocktails or wine by the bottle.

I was looking forward to our dinner experience at Cosme, since there was so much hype about it on social media and YouTube. Food wise our dinner started strong with the strip bass and the crab chile rellenos. But the last two dishes were not as strong (Cobia fish and the potato leek tostada).
When a restaurant has such a small menu, you would expect every dish to be great (specially for the price they charge). But only half the experience was great. 
Dinner service was also slow (it was a Wednesday night) and I thought the servers did not smile much here and they were too serious. So the service also did not deliver as well. At one level they even brought us a chipped plate and I had to ask them to bring me an other one.
I thought I they have a Michelin star or have been rated Michelin star. But for sure I was more impressed by other restaurant during my trip to NY.

Food is good, flavorful and pretty funky. 
For starters, save your money on the margarita. They sit down a good-sized glass, full of large ice cubes and probably 1-2 ounces of a drink, not even kidding. I thought it was a joke at first. The food was good though. Dark and very very loud inside.

Came here on a Saturday for lunch with a reservation. The ambiance is lovely, and they had marigolds for Day of the Dead. I enjoyed their 2 mocktails - amaranth horchata and chamomile apple yuzu - very much. Service was somewhat lacking. We ordered the octopus but got the ceviche instead. Also had the shrimp aguachile and chilaquiles verdes with chicken. We went ahead and enjoyed the ceviche - it had a lovely presentation on top of a flat rock. The shrimp was very fresh  and tender. The chilaquiles were extremely spicy, and we were given extra crema, but then it showed up as $4 on the bill. While something like an egg would be extra, I was surprised that a couple tablespoons would be an extra charge. Otherwise, it was an enjoyable experience!

Food 9/10
Each dish had a solid kick to it. The shrimp and cabbage really stood out to me because of how fiery the flavors were. The octopus had a nice sauce. The duck carnitas were solid, but they were slightly dry so that was a small let down. Definitely recommend their appetizers though, a big variety. The cocktails I thoroughly enjoyed, all had very distinctive and complex flavors. 

Atmosphere 9/10
Very modern and sleek design, we sat near the bar because it was a walk-in, but the interior had slate stone tables and dark wood details, with brass/bronze accents. 

Service 9/10
Very informative when we were selecting dishes on the menu, friendly.
Returned here for dinner after years and the duck carnitas were just as I had remembered them - a must order and probably why I will keep returning.

We had a great experience here, but for the hype I would say I would have to give it 1 less star b/c it didn't blow me away.  The cocktails are delicious ($20 a piece). The duck carnitas (But $96), corn dish AND the corn husk meringue were the stars of the show.  We also enjoyed the guacamole! I would definitely not get the mole... very underwhelming and minimal (and I love mole).  Wouldn't come rushing back here, but had a nice time and would recommend to try it.

Service was so rushed it made our whole dining experience horrible. They didn't ring in our guac and gave us another appetizer we didn't order, and charged us for it. Tried to clear our table several times when we still had food on our share plates. Our water was never empty but our cocktails were. Some of the chips were stale. The steak was good but not worth the overall experience.

Loved the food and the service was great !! Even though they gave us a lot of the wrong dishes they were still delicious I ate most of them because my friend only eats kosher but they were so sweet they only charged us for the drinks so of course we left a great tip !! Also the drinks are so good 
Can't wait to be back

I traveled here from California to eat at this restaurant. Unfortunately the check in staff here were not friendly and ruined the entire experience. They gave our table away even though our friend was already there and seated us after the restaurant had already closed (930p) almost 1 hour after our reservation time (845p). The rest of the staff, however, was pleasant. The tlayuda and shrimp sope were tasty but the scallops and duck were okay. I will not be returning and am disappointed with my experience when there are so many other restaurants I could've visited in NY. I can't believe this made the list for one of the 100 best restaurants in the world.

Visited Cosme while in NY for the US Open
Definitely NOT a top 100 restaurant in the world maybe their neighborhood!
The mixed drinks were delicious however they serve in plastic glasses? For $20 a drink I think they can afford glassware and a dishwasher. 
Food was good however the octopus was cold and tamale was crumbly which made it of a weird texture unlike what tamales should be like and where the flavor resides
The menu is very limited and staff is not very helpful navigating through it. The duck was great but very simple and the skin was not crackling pretty disappointed. 
The serving utensils were worn out and cheap 
I just hate eating with Restaurant Depot forks and
knives specially when presented with such high end food
Service very spotty and missing the food experience when food was served just a food runner that barely spoke English and just mumbled the plate being served.
Never saw a manager and had to wave the waiter many times before he left and "closed the area" then another waitress took over who was very nice and attentive 
I think for Modern Mexican food , there is lack of imagination and creativity, the food is pretty bland and without the delicious sauces it would just be just that bland!
I think chef and owners should travel to places like Tulum, Oaxaca, Houston,Dallas , Mexico City and get
Inspired again 
These food felt uninspired and "pushed" to be liked when they missed so many things that could have been better
So good. Love the corn dessert and the Scallop, especially the spice sauce with pumpkin seeds is amazing.
Premier service and the food is obviously quality and made with incredibly fresh ingredients. Should this be on a Top 100 restaurant in America list? Absolutely not.

I was shocked that this place has dipped under 4 stars on Yelp. I had such a great experience here. Service was perfectly attentive, ambiance was chic but not at all stuffy and the duck carnitas exceeded the hype. Our group also loved the corn husk meringue - delish and really interesting. Cocktails were top notch too. 

Tons of gluten free options! Servers were well trained around allergens in general.
Food was spectacular as was the service. Spicy margarita is a must. Would definitely return.

We recently went in for husbands birthday, the food was delicious, the service was amazing and loved the ambiance. We ordered one appetizer, two tapas and one main dish to share, honestly the portions are very good so for two people i would say it's best to do one, one and one but overall everything we tried was delicious!

I'm shook to see that this place only has 3.5 stars...

From the incredibly high level of service, the amazing communication about each dish and the attention to detail for each plate we were given. The plating was fun to see, the color kept popping and I love to see the way the chefs here play with height with the food, one of my favorite dishes looked a bit like a tortilla balloon. 

The duck carnitas were stacked with toppings. I mean layer upon layer. The butternut tamal-- smooth and rich in taste. The tortillas-- purple and crisped on one side-- kept coming to us. 

Overall, a vibrant and cultural experience at hits highest level. 

With love, 
Renee from the Bay

Decided to go to Cosme for my bday dinner after a friend's rec. Everything from the ambience to the food was spectacular. 

1. Guac: good 
2. Tlayuda sweet corn: omg this was fire. Sweet corn and coconut- very very tasty. Must order. 
3. Duck carnitas: generous hunk of duck meat. Good with the shaved fennel and herbs. Pretty good but not as phenomenal as I thought it would be - flavors not as punchy and a tad dry and meat-y but a great main for sharing. 
4. Mole: phenomenal mole. A bit lighter since it's just veg with mole. The move is totally to douse that duck carnitas with the mole. Pure yums
5. Corn husk meringue: I'm usually not a meringue person but I knew I had to get this. DAMN. One of the top desserts I've had in a while. Salty sweet combo. MUST ORDER. Would dream about this dessert
6. Comped tres leches for my bday: totally appreciated this! Not the best tres leches though - could use more condensed milk?
7. Guava thing: good ending to a meal

Overall, Cosme is such a great Mexican resto! Food is unique with great flavors. Would come back for sure, especially for that corn husk meringue

This was a unique and incredible meal. I went with a large group and we tried the guacamole, tamal, tlayuda, mole, one of each of the desserts, mezcal flight, and a variety of cocktails. Everything had phenomenal flavor - it was clear that a lot of care had been put into giving a good variety of flavors and textures with everything, all at a very high quality. The others in my group ordered a few meat and seafood dishes that I didn't try, but they really seemed to enjoy those as well. I'd highly recommend the tlayuda, mole, and corn husk meringue. This is absolutely worth the experience.

This place is overrated, overpriced I am not Mexican but I do love Mexican food. I have being in puebla an Oaxaca . As I was looking on the menu I didn't recognize many of the words so I send the menu to a Mexican friend she said she didn't recognize many words in the menú that the only one she recognizes was the mole so I order the mole also because I had mole rojo,café pipian and negro so I figure I was not going to choose wrong to my surprise it was not what I was expected it was a scary mole I was expecting some chick and rice lol 
But nop it was mole with some type of Mexican spinach. 
To my experience whoever that is making the mole in there is not Mexican . The food looks very Japanese not Mexican at all if you want to have the real Mexican experience with less money go to little Mexican restauran you will definitely have the Michelle star experience at a low price .

Too expensive and average food. Had to send the $100 steak back to be re-fired. $400 for dinner & drinks for two was too much. Service and Ambiance were fine but unmemorable.

Plus, what the hell are these cocktails?
Truly amazing food! The Octopus, Duck Carnitas, and dessert options are delicious and a food experience I've never had but always remember. Hands down one of my favorite restaurants in NYC.

It sucks! I had high hopes for the place. But besides amazing service the actual food and drink was trash. We tried 4 things for the already extremely small menu. The guacamole was ok, the mole was terrible bc the flavors was off balance. The quesadilla was fried in a low temp oil with was not properly made. And the huevos rancheros the sauce was broken( the sauce was separating from oil) and just had an off putting taste. So sad! Save your money!

Took my BF here for his birthday & we were both glad I did. The service, from the moment one enters, is friendly & attentive without being overbearing. While the menu descriptions are so barebones--"conch tostada, xo sauce, avocado"--that one hardly knows what to expect, it doesn't really matter because everything was delicious. I had the Potato Tamal | Parsnip | Caviar--which the kitchen was kind enough to make vegetarian for me by withholding the caviar--& the Mole de la Casa | Quelites | Golden Sesame which was, surprisingly, already vegetarian--it's hard to find anything mole-related that is vegetarian, so I was on Cloud 9. Although the portions are small, the dishes are filling; we did not leave hungry.

For dessert, we shared the Burnt Tostada Chocolate Tart & Black Sesame Tamal | Caramel | Palanqueta, & I'd definitely go back for seconds of either of those. The mandarina cocktails were also superlative.

Is there less expensive delicious food available in NYC? Sure. I'll leave it to the reader to determine whether ~$300 for dinner for two is within the budget. The only constructive criticism I will provide is the need for more descriptive menus, as it's a little loud in the space--making it difficult to hear a server's explanation of a dish--& the menu should be doing that lifting, anyway.

Vegetarian options: While there are vegetarian options on the menu--& the staff is happy to help you find them--they were also willing to make slight modifications to existing, non-vegetarian dishes to make them vegetarian.

Cosme was an average experience. Came during Memorial Day weekend and reservations were easy to make for a party of 3. 
Was having high expectations for the food because my friend from out of town heard this about Cosme and wanted to come try it.

Food: 3/5
Service: 3/5
Ambiance: 3/5

Char Chintextile Tostada had about 5-6 pieces thinly sliced fish and Avocado arranged nicely on a round flat stone. Presentation was good. Taste wasn't memorable. Pass.

Octopus Pasilla Mixe Sorrel was good. Best dish of the night. Octopus was grilled well, nicely salted. Order it.

Potato Tamal with parsnips and caviar - I love potatoes. I love parsnips. I love caviar. I did NOT love the hard block amalgamation that this dish was. Pass.

Eggplant Tlayuda - dish was good. The eggplant with mixed veggies such as arugula and mushroom and carrots with the sauce was a flavorful combo. Order it. 

Skirt Steak - the steak tasted ok. Server said this and the duck carnitas were the best entrees they had. It was too salty. Dish came with many tortillas and green sauce. It's almost as if they knew they were charging too much for the steak because it came hidden under a blanket of arugula greens and grilled green spring onion. Pass

Duck Carnitas - big disappointment. Lots of overcooked duck. Not so much flavor. Undersalted. Came with tortillas and green sauce and chilli red sauce. Pass

Corn Husk Meringue - unique dessert flavor. The creamy light corn flavor mixed well with the crisp white macaroon like cookie. Order it. 

We also ordered two classic alcoholic drinks. Choco Y Hongos and La Tanga Narizona. My friend and wife drank one each. Average. 

TLDR: food is very average. All the food had the same flavor profile. Felt like all their meat dishes came with green and red sauce to make up for the lack of flavor. Too much $$$ from what can be better spent elsewhere. They are a well established restaurant with lots of clients even on a relatively quiet Monday of Memorial day weekend. It just felt like as if the restaurant had made it and so they lack the movtiavtion to try hard anymore.

I've been to Cosme twice first time pre pandemic for lunch and second time recently on a Friday night had an 8:00pm reservation made on resy.
Different vibes but food is still solid.
Huge space and you aren't really on top of each other but you are sitting side by side with a few inches to spare to slide sideways in to the seat. 
Lunch vibes was much quieter but dinner vibes was like you're eating in a club.
Hostesses were gracious and welcoming and seated us right away for our reservation 
Our waiter was nice and pleasant and he explained all the food incredibly well with passion for many of the dishes. 
We opted (for two people 2 appetizers 2 tapas and 1 main) 
1. Hiramasa aguachile
2. Octopus Padilla mixe Sorrel 
3. Lobster Al pastor 
4. Eggplant tlayuda mushroom sunchokes 
5. Duck Carnitas 
6. Cornhusk meringue

Yuzu cocktail $24
Non alcoholic apple drink $11

Total bill with tax and an exact 15% tip was $372.12 the duck carnitas is a $98 dish

We ordered enough food that would honestly serve 4 people very comfortable so highly suggest 4 min to share - the portions were incredibly generous. So if it was a dinner for 4 with a cocktail each you'd spend at least $110 which is reasonable for the quality of the food.

The could pass item would be the Lobster Al pastor 
Complimentary item was 2 tortillas and 2 condiments to dip in. 

The star of the meal absolutely was the duck - so tender and the toppings worked perfectly - generous amount of tortillas. Cornhusk meringue still consistently good - if you're into creamy desserts.

Service by everyone was great - 
Knocked of one star because the waiter Omar could have been a bit more even with his attention. We were adjacent to two tables flanking us that he spoke Spanish to the entire time - no problem with that but he checked on them multiple times and offered them much more personal attention. I get it - he's more comfortable with his own people - he was never rude to us he was pleasant but at least three times we had to ask our bus boy clearing dishes to bring us things an to bring us the desert menu and we never could get a second drink because our waiter literally did not think to follow up with us ever. No slight to him we just see this often - you speak the same language as the waiter in a Mexican restaurant and the waiter will bring more attention to you. The adjacent tables were never with out extra drinks and the waiters attention. 
We had to give our check to the bus boy to bring to someone to close us out.

Would we come back? Probably never again because of that experience. Would we have ordered more drinks - totally! But never got a chance to. 
Overall - I would still suggest the restaurant if you are looking for a menu that is friendly to a variety of proteins and fresh ingredients and your budget is open.

Food- the flavor was very good. Despite having ingredients that I wasn't a fan of, I won't take it away from them the presentation, the flavor and taste of the food. The duck could have used more flavor but the octopus was phenomenal.

Service- service was ok. The waiter had a sense of urgency but kept forgetting what we order. She also spoke too fast 

Environment- love the ambiance, nice setting. Love that it was spacious, so uncommon in the city.

I appreciate creative dishes -- from the taste to presentation. Everything was new to me. Even the guacamole looked and tasted different. There seemed to be more vegetarian than meat options and the plates were designed to be shared so it was a tad challenging for a solo diner. It had great beverage options however! The place was loud and packed and a little on the pricey side. Great for groups for sure.

I wanted to really like this place, and when I first got there I thought it might be similar to one of my favorite restaurants in the city: ABC Cocina. There were a few things I didn't love: had an 815 reservation, got there a few minutes early, and didn't get sat until after 830. The hiramasu dish was very meh. The chips and guac and the tostado samplers didn't have even close to the right amount of chips for the sauce / guac. The service was kind of slow. That said, the corn husk merengue was one of my favorite deserts ever and I was with a pescatarian so I didn't get to try a lot of the best dishes.

Cosme is definitely worth a visit. This contemporary Mexican restaurant, located in the Flatiron District, offers a menu that celebrates local and seasonal ingredients while staying true to traditional Mexican flavors and techniques.

I had the pleasure of trying the duck carnitas, which came with onions, radishes, and cilantro. The dish is advertised as "to share," but I can assure you that it makes for a satisfying and delicious entree all on its own. The duck was tender and flavorful, and the accompaniments provided a nice balance of crunch and freshness.

For dessert, I opted for the famed corn husk meringue, which had been highly recommended by the staff. I can see why it's such a popular dish - the meringue was light and airy, and the corn husk gave it a unique and slightly savory flavor that was unexpected but enjoyable.

Throughout the meal, I was impressed by the quality of the ingredients and the care taken in the preparation of each dish. The beverage program also deserves a mention, as the artisanal spirits and cocktails perfectly complemented the flavors of the food.

The ambiance of the restaurant is sleek and modern. The staff was attentive and knowledgeable, providing excellent recommendations and answering any questions we had.

Overall, I highly recommend Cosme for anyone looking for a dining experience that is both inventive and rooted in tradition. The duck carnitas and corn husk meringue are must-tries, and the rest of the menu is sure to impress as well.

Really hate to leave a bad review but I will have to say this is the WORST place.

To be specific, the service was decent and not bad. The atmosphere was good.

Got 2 recommendations from the server for Hiramasa & Potato Tamal, and they were the worst. First of all, the portions are extremely small. Though I would have not cared on the portions if those were delicious. But they were BAD. No such tastes on both, and not sure what they were supposed to be. I really don't know what to say. (Just to clarify I am not a super picky person when it comes to food but it was THAT bad)

Duck carnitas was okay. But it wasn't the best, and was advised by the server that the portions were for 2-3 ppl. However it is extremely overpriced. Again if it was like really good, I wouldn't have even brought up about the portion or price.

I love Mexican food and honestly I could have gone to other places to have a feast for more than half the price I paid.

Had so much expectations on this place but I am greatly disappointed. Not worth for even one visit, not worth the money. Wasted my time.

Food was good, service was fine, ambiance was fine I guess? One supposes that poorly lit is what passes for classy nowadays. The food was quite good but the serving sizes were small and definitely not worth the $$$$.

Went to this restaurant with two other couples and I have to say, the food and service was so disappointing. The waiter's suggestions on the amount of food that was needed for the table was completely wrong. He was  trying to sell us way more than was needed, thank god we didn't listen because we would've ended up with so many leftovers. The food in this place is so overrated and definitely overpriced. I've been to his restaurant Pujol in Mexico and I don't think this restaurant does justice to his cooking. If you read this review and still feel like you would like to give this restaurant a shot, I would recommend getting the lobster Al pastor pineapple, the farro rice and the hiramasa tostada, and maybe some of the desserts. We spent around $650 per couple and that includes two bottles of wines. Don't think we will visiting this restaurant again.
A very cool experience with fun food. Definitely something worth trying once, but wouldn't go again at the price point. Loved the esquites and the desserts the most.
Swanky, cool NYC spot. I was surprised to eat Mexican food in New York, but was told by my foodie friend that it was a must do! We sampled many items, family style it was very different in very good.

This was an highly anticipated and severely underwhelming meal. The service was fantastic! The food was shockingly disappointing. Scallop was almost unpalatable. One of the most poorly balanced dished I have ever tasted. The tamale and duck were fine, but given the price point one would expect at least a slightly innovative or intriguing flavor profile. None delivered. Some of us look forward to a high priced meal as a special occasion. This was ours. Very disappointed. Please improve.

I recently had the pleasure of dining at Cosme. This restaurant completely exceeded my expectations.

I was particularly excited to try the duck tacos, as I had never seen them offered at a Mexican restaurant before. And let me tell you, they were absolutely amazing.

The duck was perfectly cooked and had a wonderful flavor that was complemented by the other ingredients in the tacos. I saw a video of the chef beforehand cooking the duck confit which was really interesting. I also appreciated the portion size, as the single duck order was the perfect amount to satisfy two people. The tortillas were made fresh, held up well, and the toppings were all incredibly fresh and delicious.

The service throughout the meal was impeccable - attentive without being overbearing, and always with a smile.

I would highly recommend Cosme to anyone looking for a memorable dining experience. Whether you're in the mood for classic Mexican dishes or unique offerings like the duck tacos, this place has something for everyone.
As a DF girl and fan of Enrique Olvera, I was in heaven. Cool spot and absolutely Delicious!
Food was not good at all!  We ended up leaving with a big tab and empty bellies. Service was just ok.

Terrible service for a restaurant of this reputation. The waiter was condescending and rude because we did not want the duck which is the only item he could recommend. I spoke to the manager who provided us with a new server however this was not enough. Our experience and evening were ruined. The food is good but underwhelming and for nearly 200$ a person I would expect more.

O. M. G.

This is the most amount of food I've ever eaten and the most amount of money I've ever spent in one place.

My friend and I absolutely LOVED EVERYTHING on the menu so much so that we ordered multiple servings over what I think was about 4 hours of nonstop eating.

Thanks to the kind and generous staff for not kicking us out on a busy weeknight and letting us stay and savor our multi-course meal.

We were extremely excited to try Cosme having visited other restaurants by Enrique, we held it to those standards with their dishes, service, and ambience. Food once served, just as savory as always. Service, not as great as we've received at other's like Pujol or Damian. Our server was "Jonni" and having visited Damian in Los Angeles just the week before, we had questions on the menu given the similarities in dishes. We were rudely told that he had no clue what they serve over there and the way they do things here are the way they do things here and walked away without giving any further information on our questions on the dishes. I proceeded to order after he returned quite some time later and had put no mind to it. The staff members bringing us our dishes and cocktails were extremely welcoming, friendly, and informative on what was being served unlike Jonni. It seemed like we always had to look for him and call him over to ask for service whether it be for cocktails, extra salsa, or tortillas. And even for the check without it being a busy night and right before close. Despite the service, the food, cocktails, and ambience were all good.

Lovely fresh food that's served beautifully too. Also the Agua Fresca selection is so phenomenal (Like the Jasmine, Yuzu, Avocado one I got). Restaurant is in a convenient location close to Madison Park. Went in for lunch .. Will have to try the restaurant for dinner next time I'm in the Big Apple since the menus looked a lil diff.

Video: https://www.instagram.com/p/Cm2Wo-GI0Ba/

been hesitant to come here cus of the star rating.... and this trip I was like ok lets go.... i had reservations due to it was the holidays tho i was seated at the bar - which was fine cus i was solo.... anyways cousin said get the duck carnitas  (shareable) and meringue... guess this was the go to for first timers , and first impression and OMG , why did I wait 4 trips before actually diving into to this place... not to exaggerate but that duck carnitas was worth the 98$ , which I was very iffy about , hence I didnt go here right away - but man now its a must go to place when I go to NY.... and that meringue , is like heaven on a plate... a guy sat next to me, which was his first time as well and yup I recommended those 2 dishes... another gentleman was seated to my left and he was actually a local , who often went to cosme casually --- so he was also saying those 2 were the go to for first timers... unless youre not into duck and/or carnitas -- overall a great experience and bartender was cool -- great vibe of a place and the ambience is nice -- will def be back over and over.. but now even if it wont be my first time, Ima still have to order that duck carnitas just because it was that goooooood...

Too bad there's only a sheet. Literally just a sheet (MENU) with just a couple of things to order and nothing apart from that. 

What they serve, on the other hand; was AWESOME. You've got to try the guacamole. Omg

Girlfriend and I have both been here once before. Recently came to celebrate a birthday.

The atmosphere is dark and vibey. We were seated at a 2-person table in the back of the restaurant. Service was efficient.

We ordered the:
- Kampachi pastrami, which was not made clear to us that it would be fish, although it was very good
- Eggplant tlayuda, which was good but the eggplant was pretty subtle and the dish was very mushroom-forward
- Duck carnitas - by far the highlight of the meal. The meat was seasoned well and so soft and juicy

They also gave us a complimentary serving of tostadas and guac, which we were very pleased about - yay! :)

For dessert, we got the corn husk meringue and a helping of the tres leches. The meringue was a bit too creamy for our taste. The tres leches was very sweet but I really enjoyed it. 

We will be returning to Cosme soon, hungry for more.

Came for brunch - had visited Pujol and was excited to try an Olvera menu stateside. The guac ($23) was delicious, although you can decide if the value is there. The shrimp aguachile was tasty, but pretty heavy handed on the shaved cucumber. The corn omelette (eggs filled with spinach, Cojita and American cheese smothered in corn sauce) was delicious. The huevos were a miss for me - over sauced and then beans were so finely blended into the sauce that the dish was pretty one note. Wish I had done the chilaquiles instead. Lastly we shared the mole duck emoladas. Not much to say, very tasty, served with a side of crème fraiche. Also fairly one note, but that one note was a delicious (negro) mole. A coffee cocktail and a guava pisco were both great. The wine by the glass left a bit to be desired - the somm didn't mention the red I ordered was very carbonic, while the white (after asking for a simple full bodied chard) was a funky Riesling. All in all definitely recommend, would like to come back for dinner

I came to Cosme on Sunday 11-20-2022 with my girlfriend for a birthday dinner. Having heard a lot about this place online, we finally decided to come and see what the hype was all about. Having been to Casa Enrique I wanted to see how it compared to greats such as Casa Enrique.

The ambiance of the place was quite nice. The decor was modern and it was dimli lit. The great thing about the lighting was that while the table was lit quite well, it accentuated the food and its coloring which I found quite smart. It was not a very noisy place and people there were dressed from casual to semi-formal. I always found this nice as it does not force a certain image. Overall ambiance and decor is a 5/5.

For drinks I had a Dirty Mezcal Martini. It was made well, but did not have quite the flavor I was looking for. I wanted a more of a bite in flavor that I am used to. Although this is not a drink you normally order, it was good, but not great. A 4/5 on the Dirty Mezcal Martini.

Additionally, our waiter was also very accommodating. He was attentive when he needed to be and was not forceful in terms of overly recommending foods. Most servers I have encountered always end up recommending the whole menu which makes no sense and bears no help on the situation, but ours was quite excellent and we ended up ordering all the vegetarian dishes anyways. Overall service is a 5/5.

For the appetizers we had the "Herb guacamole. corn tostadas" and the "Farro esquites. goat gouda." The guacamole was made fresh which was good. It was a lil sour for my taste though. The tostadas made here were excellent and had a strong crunch that I truly enjoyed. The star of the show was definitely the "Farro esquites. goat gouda." This was by far my favorite dish of the night and I genuinely enjoyed this. It was creamy, salty and made to perfection. Overall, the appetizers are a 4.5/5.

For the main course we got the "Mole de la casa. quelites. golden sesame" and "Eggplant tlayuda. mushrooms. sunchokes." I would say the "Mole de la casa. quelites. golden sesame" was definitely not my taste. It was overly bitter and I did not enjoy it at all. I gave it a 2/5 and did not want to eat anymore of it. The "Eggplant tlayuda. mushrooms. sunchokes" was okay, but not great. The flavor from the eggplant was a bit plain, but the tostada that it was on was excellent. That combined with some of their homemade sauces they offer as pre-appetizer made this dish much better. I gave it a 4/5. However, overall the vegetarian mains was a 3/5.

The restaurant was quite nice and they brought over a small birthday dessert for me since it was my 30th birthday. I really appreciate that so thank you Cosme! For dessert, we had the "Cornhusk merinque." This was excellent and so was my birthday treat. For dessert this is definitely a 5/5.

I think this was a nice place to try, but not the best Mexican restaurant I have had in New York. Food was good, but not great. The food may be attributed to the fact that we are vegetarians and do not eat meat. However, the service and ambiance was impeccable. Had a great time and want to see what others think of this place!

Dining at Cosme as seen on Michelin guide, cool vibe, friendly people, contemporary Mexican food and handmade dish-wares by Jono andolfi.

My favorite of the night had to be the Scallop Yuzu Augachile, mixing with the crunchiness of the jicama and fresh scallops softened up by the citrusy marinade, a gentle kick of spiciness delivering an umami taste.

Recommending the drinks for mezcal lovers, all the desserts were on par with the others but the Husk Meringue was the most aesthetically pleasing dessert.

Restaurant is overpriced and the portions are very small.  Food is Ok but nothing special.  Staff is very nice.  The wine list is one of the most absurd lists I have ever seen.  Almost a scam!  A 2009 Lopez heredia tondonia reserva is $450 dollars.  This is a $45 bottle.  Check wine searcher.  Its a nice wine but in no world should it be marked up 10X.  A 2001 tondonia was similarly mispriced at $550 which is $95 retail.  The list has many wines $300-600 bottles that are marked up literally 5-6x or more.  Do not order a bottle off this list.  Every restaurant is entitled to charge what they want but as a consumer you should not be taken advantage off.  Bottles at restaurants are marked up 3-2 times based on original acquisition cost.  I collect wine and have never seen anything this egregious.  Caveat emptor!!!

Pujol in Mexico City is one of my favorite restaurants ever, so I really wanted to try chef's counterpart Cosme -- it did not disappoint! Beautiful ambience and good service; dark mood lighting perfect for a date. The duck carnitas were decadent; we had leftovers to take home and enjoy the next day. The corn husk meringue was my favorite bite: sweet but not too sweet, subtle but powerful corn flavor came through, and the texture of the light crunch was just perfect. Finishing my meal with a carajillo cocktail was also just sublime; I'm still thinking about how good it was. Amazing!!!

Enrique Olvera!!!!!!!! YESSSSSSS!!!! I'm a loyal Ticuchi CDMX fan and Cosme replicated the quality, the ambiance, the perfection. Ordered the Casa Dragones spicy margarita (a must I'm a loyal Casa Dragones fan). Do the guacamole, do the mole. The corn esquites were the favorite of the night. The tylayuda was good.

Very delicious. The Corn Husk Meringue is the most delicious dessert I've had in recent times. But there was also one other dessert that baffled our whole table. It was sweet, bitter, sour at the same time. Maybe it is an acquired taste. I guess.

This place is 5 star all the way!! Its beautiful and elegant atmosphere set you up for wonderfully and carefully crafted cocktails and food. My husband and I sat at the bar which was very pretty and neat. Service was top tier! Cesar our bartender was friendly, knowledgeable and crafted perfectly balanced cocktails. We started with the Invisible friend and Lagrimas de una Hada. Both of them were so good. I loved the umami flavor of the Lagrimas which had just the right amount of black sesame. The Invisible Friend was crisp and clean similar to a white Negroni. We tried the octopus tostada and scallop and celery root aguachile. Both were so delicious!! The scallop was so heavenly I could have drank all the juice in the bowl. We tried a couple of exclusive mezcals which we enjoyed. The Smoked Gibson was great for us who love martinis. It was spirit forward in the best way. For dessert we had the black sesame tamal which was AMAZING! If you can appreciate a slightly savory dessert you would love this. I do not understand the low ratings because this place really gave us an amazing night with high quality cocktails and delicious upscale food.
Very "basic" menu as they have very typical Mexican dishes, but you can't ask for more from the dishes. The duck mole and barbacoa are the top pics!

Pretty solid experience. We had a group of six, and the server did a great job of walking us through the menu and describing everything for us. We ended up just ordering several different dishes and sharing it all family-style. I think that's the idea of the restaurant, but it's hard to tell from the layout of the menu.
Some of the standouts would be the octopus, the squash, and the duck. (The duck was fantastic. Highly recommend the duck.) The mole was ok, but there wasn't a whole lot to the dish, so I'd probably skip it on a return visit.
It was an excellent restaurant. We had the guacamole, scallops, farro, and the duck dish. Every bite was excellent. I had the corn husk merengue as a dessert and it was worth the hype.

This restaurant used to be named one of the world's 50 best restaurants. We made a dinner reservation for a group of eight people on a weekday night. Honestly, the food was a little disappointing. The appetizers and entrees were just ok. The dessert was good. The corn husk meringue was my favorite. Also, the food portion was quite small, and we ordered at least two for each dish.

My worse experience in any $$+ resturants in my life.
1) We had a reservation and arrived only 10 mins late!! They asled us to wait for our table. Long story short, we were standing there for 80 mins!!!
I talked with the hosts 4 times and they just smiled and say wait a little bit more!
They put 2 times more than their capacity in their resevation I guess. While we were standing there wiaitng 2 other parties who arrived later than us were seated since they knew the hosts!!
The host told me no they are just going to restroom!
Name of the girl was jay or jane!
I told them, I am gonna write a reveiw for you guys!
Unfortunately, it was late Friday night and we could not find any place near by at that time!!  

2) The food does not offer anything new! Assume you get the food from a $ mexican resturant at the corner of wherever you live and just presnet it in nice plate and charge it $$$$!

I do not understand why anyone goes to this place!

I hate writing bad reviews but they really deserve no star! We made a reservation for 9:30PM, we were there at 9:37PM and they gave us a table at 10:45PM. The reservation means nothing to them!!! While we were waiting for our table to get ready, a few people just arrived and entered the main salon. We said to the waitress that we are waiting with reservation and they just arrived! she told us that they are going to use the restroom and guess what, they never came back from the restroom within 45 minutes that we were there. They looked us in our eye and lied!! It was not the only one! A couple arrived after us and were also waiting. The lady went to the waitress and talked to her and they got seated while their reservation was for 9:45PM (based on them)!! I will never come back!

We came here because of the rave reviews for the corn husk merengue. Womp womp. It was alright, but don't go out of your way for it. We also tried the  churro which was presented really nicely in a basket, and was really thin and crispy- very light and airy.

The horchata latte was the worst, most overpriced for absolutely no discernible reason, beverage I have had. I thought wow, this must be really delicious if this latte costs $14- must be something special to it. I usually love horchata and coffee... this was horrible. The coffee was bitter as can be, the horchata was watery, the ice cubes stacked too high - kept hitting my nose, and served to me with the bottom of the glass all wet with coffee. Not a napkin in sight, it kept dripping and got on my sleeve.

Don't go here just for the corn husk merengue. Don't go out of your way, it's not worth it. It's OK but not amazing. Too much whipped cream in my opinion. And definitely don't get the horchata latte. You will regret it

We came here for dessert. The $14 horchata was poor to mediocre. The espresso was also poor (mercifully only $5). 

The much ballyhood corn husk meringue was much ado about nothing. It was fine, but not extraordinary. And it definitely did not justify the $20 price tag. I feel like it would be a wonderful base for an additional component, like a kiwi coulis. 

The Churro was pretty neat, nice and airy. And there was a lot of it. But, again, not as extraordinary as you would expect. Definitely not worth $19. 

I know many places falter on their desserts, but from what I've seen and heard, I would not trust their entrees either.

TLDR: not really sure why Cosme has a lower rating on Yelp than I expected - great food and good service. 

Came in a group of 8 so we had the opportunity to try almost every dish! Everything was vibrant, beautiful and delicious I'm glad we were able to have a little of it all. Not sure if it was because I was in a large group, but we kept having to ask for more tostadas for all the crudo. Also, unless you're really a huge chilaquiles fan i thought that you could avoid this and try others; we had bother versions and they were great but seemed pretty standard to me for how much they cost. My favorites from the menu were the guacamole, shrimp aguachile, vuelve a la vida, corn omelette, duck enmoladas, and of course, the corn husk meringue. The corn husk meringue is probably one of my favorite desserts I've had. I would return just for that meringue.

Service was friendly and they even allowed us to accommodate one more in our group that wasn't indicated on the original reservation. Honestly, I can't wait to come back!

Elevated Mexican cuisine with such unique dishes that burst with an array of flavors. Expect to spend around $70-80 not including drinks, but is definitely a must try at least once. Incredibly fresh corn tortillas too! 

While the menu rotates, their signature Duck carnitas stays on - get this for sure! Other note worthy dishes during this recent visit were the Octopus Tostada, and the Farro Esquites with Goat Gouda. 

They lost their Michelin Star this year, which I feel was likely for the service not the food. Still really great but took a little while to call the attention of a server when needed.
