We came here for brunch on a Sunday, and only saw the reviews on Yelp after we were seated. The ratings surprised me - this place is incredible and deserves 5 stars. Granted, brunch reservations were easier to get for two people than dinner, but the food was delicious. The guacamole was perfect, the chilaquiles are probably the best I've had, and the corn omelette was a great complement to these dishes. I'd love to come here again.

High end level of service. The team of the restaurant such a great professionals. Everyone. Since greeting till end. Plus excellent wine explanation from sommelier. Highly recommended! Thanks for experience!

Just wow. Probably the most elevated Mexican cuisine in the world. The entire Planet. Earth. Just wow. Anyone who disagrees just doesn't know about great food. Nothing isn't excellent. Go here. Bring the wallet. You're welcome.

Best corn dish I've ever had. The fish was also amazing. However, the service felt hurried and the entire time we felt rushed. They kept trying to bring us the check before we were finished with our meal and cocktails. But food was excellent, service not so much.

Came here for the churros (only served during lunch), but ended up having a fantastic dinner. 

By far the best charred octopus in all of NYC. Wish the mole was served with rice, but will be returning for the churros soon.

Inventive Mexican with great cocktails. Can't go wrong with most menu items. Fun atmosphere but a bit noisy.  Second visit here; confirmed first impression. Would have merited another star with some acoustics management.

Stellar twist on Mexican , Cosme is completely different from any other Mexican restaurant I've been to. 
Very high end, amazing decor, fabulous music, outstanding service, food I've never heard of and the thought and prep that goes into the menu, is above par. 
Seated as soon as we arrived, and it's New York, so your packed in next to others, but this still had its little space where I didn't feel on top of my neighbors. 
One thing I wish could have been better was that they speak very fast and explain the menu so quickly I couldn't understand them. Especially considering some of the ingredients were not normal things I'm use to. 
The fact that all the food was amazing, kinda made that not as important! 
Drinks! I had a mezcal Paloma, and a Rosé for my friend. Paloma was so good, I had 3. 
There are 3 parts to the menu, and you basically have to order all 3 together. Then dessert is an extra. 
So first we picked scallops with yellow bell pepper, Oro Blanco aguqchile. Scallops in a fresh orange juice , so fresh and refreshing and the best scallops I've eaten in a long time. Kinda like a chunky ceviche. So delicious.
Next we had the Milpa Tamal, black bean purée base , above was a wrapped masa cheese, bean mix that was spicy and warm, deliciousness. Mixed greens, zucchini blossoms, onions, jalapeño all fresh on top too. This was unusual but perfect, the filling was so good. 
Next the Bean Tlayuda, Maitake, with spring onions. Tostada with black beans, onions, carrots, cheese, a awesome spicy sauce, lots of greens. The sauce was really spicy and added to the tostada made it great. The tortilla was extremely crunchy!  Little overkill on the greens! We had to push them aside! Maybe they had extra! 
For dessert we got the Nixtamalized peaches with oats and vanilla ice cream and cream. Interesting take on a cobbler, grilled peaches, with a great crunchy oat coating and base, the ice cream was great with it, not a huge fan of the warm cream. The peaches were perfectly grilled, paired well with the oats and ice cream. Loved this. Not overly sweet either. 
Great finish to a fabulous meal. Didn't realize til the end that it was pretty veggie friendly even though we weren't trying to be. 
The scallops were my favorite. Everything else was great though and just different from your local Mexican fare. 
Highly impressed with the service, not often they change out your silverware every course! 
Great time at Cosme .

Finally got to try the infamous duck carnitas that were really worth the hype. The ayocote bean salad was also such a positive surprise. Overall delicious and did not disappoint. Perfect fun, dim lit ambiance for a long dinner.

Mexican high-end restaurant with very nice flavors but a bit pricey.

Restaurante mexicano de alta gama con sabores muy agradables pero un poco caro.

Thought this place was way overpriced and overrated. Drinks were ok but tiny. I had the Gaxpacho. Better than at other places, but so little. My friend got something with yuzu and it was mostly ice. My favorite dish was the octopus. It was on the salty side though. The farro was good. Tataki al pastor was good.  Least favorite was the mole with greens.  The greens were bitter and did not compliment the mole.  The dishes were described as family style.  But again, very small. So needed two of each for three people. The peaches and ice cream dessert was good. Overall, meh and would not return.

We just came here for the desert. We ordered corn husk meringue. This was definitely amongst the best deserts I have eaten. 

Idk how cocktails feel or food tastes but dessert is amazing! 

So don't hesitate to come for a desert for sure!

Honestly - felt this place was overrated. It's impossible to get a reservation, so originally was extremely excited to finally try it. Service was not stellar -- we waited a very long time for each course and during dessert my sorbet arrived way earlier than the coffees we ordered. Once the coffees arrived, one was cold. 

Food wise, the dishes were thoughtful but a lot of sauce on everything which did a disservice to the main events of the plate (e.g. the halibut). The tataki al pastor was a very good dish, well balanced etc. - would highly recommend if you do visit this establishment.

It's my second time here. We came for brunch. Party of 2. Overpriced and overrated. The friendly staff and minimalistic interior with earthy tones are the only pros. 
Service: they need to up their game. First of all, they brought the cocktails and appetizer after the main dish. The main dish, lamb barbacoa, had some peppers as a side (not the green ones mixed with the lamb). These were extremely spicy and the waiter who served them, gave no warning. I am definitely expecting spicy food in a Mexican restaurant but this was spicy to the extreme. It was a shock to my system.
Food: lamb was very fatty. Mushroom quesadilla was meh. Cornhusk meringue was good. 
Pricing: $23 for a mediocre spicy margarita and $80 for the lamb are unreasonable for the food quality and experience. To put things into perspective, the night before, I dined at The Grill and payed $25 for a cocktail and $85 for the prime rib. These prices are reasonable for the food quality, service and ambiance of The Grill. 
I wouldn't recommend this place.

Gorgeous, sexy space! Amazing tapas-style Mexican, all done with a touch of elegance. 

We started off with drinks at the bar and the bartender Isaac was awesome. He was knowledgeable and made great drinks for us. After a couple drinks our table was ready. Our waiter Omar was awesome as well, he really made the experience there magical. All the staff was just very good and worked as a true team. The food was amazing, the flavors and presentations were spot on and played well with the different taste buds. The duck carnitas was my favorite, the meat was s

My favs are the shrimp aguachile with cucumber which was out of this world fresh and has generous portion of shrimps.  The quesadilla epazote was another 

Everything was really good, I didn't have not one bad dish. Dessert was the corn husk which was amazing as well. I really recommend this place, it's a reason why it's considered one of the best in the world and we agree!

What an interesting twist on food this place gives off. A lot of wonderful dishes!

I would deff recommend this place!

Very stylish and fashionable spot.  Great experience overall. 
Super friendly hostesses, as I made a reservation for Sunday and thought it was for Saturday, they helped us out despite this and we got seated at the bar (fyi, they have a very comfortable sitting area at the bar). As we were sitting at the bar our server was a bartender, and she was semi friendly, with tons of attitude, and she seemed to hate that I asked her questions (sorry but it's not a basic menu where things are self explanatory). With all her appearance she was showing that she is annoyed by us. I put three stars for this place just because of her and a bad dessert! 
The food was interesting, very uncommon, lots of different tastes, beautifully presented. 1. "Octopus tostada" was delicious in terms of all the tastes it has combined, apart from octopus being extremely salty and a bit over cooked. 2. "Milpa Tamal" - was good, nothing crazy, but just good, the tastes combined was interesting. Presentation was beautiful. 3. We loved "Ayocote beans" - highly recommended. 4. Our waiter recommended "Mole de la casa" - we did not really like it, it had chocolate sauce to it, and it was just odd. Not bad, but we did not really enjoy it. 
5. Lastly we ordered their super famous dessert, "meringue" - it was missing a nice presentation, reminded us of female genitals (ooops) if you look from above, and the taste was completely off ... It had something creamy on top, tasted like non pasteurized sheep or goat milk, it was a bit disgusting. 

Cocktails look interesting (I am a cocktail freak), but we were not impressed. One was uncomfortably spicy, the other one was too gingery, and two others tasted like bad margaritas. They were not balanced at all. 
I kinda want to go back to this place to check out more food on the menu, because it was extraordinary in some way and for the ambience.

From start to finish Cosme was a quintessential amazing New York meal. The exact experience you would hope for at a place like this - the food was incredible, the atmosphere was upscale but not stuffy, and the service was great. Every dish we had was excellent and we would recommend this restaurant to anyone.

Came here on a Sunday evening, was seated quickly. Ordered the octopus, soft shelled crab and duck carnitas and the corn meringue. The octopus and duck were pretty good but nothing special. For $98 the duck carnitas was quite large and filling. The soft shelled crab was just Ok. Tasted kind of like general Tsos crab. The corn meringue was good but the presentation was kind of unappetizing. The chips/salsa served before the meal was kind of stale and hard. For the price I don't think this place is worth the hype

I came by myself to Cosme one night during a trip to NYC; I wasn't able to find someone else to join me on short notice, so alas, I ate alone. However, I wasn't going to let that stop me from enjoying everything I wanted on Cosme's menu, so I ordered a small tasting menu's worth of food.

Scallops: The Aguachile gave it a sour taste and was really punchy on the pallet. It didn't overwhelm the scallops themselves though, so the combination was quite nice.

Octopus Tostada: Octopus was cooked extremely well, and the tostada miraculously did not get soggy and held up the entire time. Amazing dish that I would highly recommend. 

Black Garbanzo Tetela: The black beans were smooth and creamy, real big difference from the crunchiness of earlier tostada, so you get a nice variety of textures and "Mouth feel." Uni was delicious on top of it. Really rich dish. 

Duck Carnitas: This dish was probably the highlight of the night. Extremely tender and well cooked duck, combined with some beautiful salsas and soft tacos. Yes, there was some assembly required, but every bite was delicious and exciting. This is a must-get if you are eating at Cosme in my opinion. 

Corn Husk Meringue: After seeing enough photos of this dish, I knew I had to get it. It was visually beautiful, but the combination of the crunchy exterior along with the smooth merengue was wonderful. The corn flavor was present, but not overpowering, and it still had the nice sweetness you expect from a dessert. Great way to end the night. 

I don't think any of these 5 dishes disappointed me. Every single one was unique and delicious, and I left feeling bloated but extremely satisfied. There's a reason that Cosme has been on the World's 50 Best list so many times now, and my meal was about as good as anything I've eaten in a long time.

Had an incredible birthday meal at Cosme! We had amazing service from start to finish which I was surprised to see based on the comments on here. Everyone was so friendly to us and attentive. 

For our meal, the standouts were the octopus tostado, soft shell crab, milpa tamale, and the duck carnitas- all unreal! The drinks were good too but we got pretty standard margaritas/ paloma. We of course had the famous cornhusk meringue dessert which was amazing! They also brought me a complimentary piece of tres leche cake for my birthday with a candle which was really nice of them. 

We will definitely be coming back again!!
What a beautiful place to dine! Food was amazing and the tortillas were exceptional. The tostada was my favorite! High end Mexican food is the way to go!!!

Came for drinks late Friday night and there was quite an energetic vibe with the after dinner crowd. Came comment on the food, but the drinks were all three star at best. 

I'm going this place a 4 star just for attentive and caring service. We didn't like the Una Noche cocktail and the server offered to change them. She was sweet and understanding and even offered alternatives. 

Based on service, I'm likely to come back and try the food.

Wow this place blew my mind. The service was incredible, everyone knew the menu and helped walk us through an amazing dinner. When you go to the restroom you napkin was folded and chair pushed in, not an expectation of mine but just the fact they paid attention to every little detail really opened up my eyes. Food is out of this world.

The whole thing was perverse. The food was super overpriced, 23$ for guacamole, $98 for a meat dish. The portions were tiny. And the music was ear piercing. So loud you couldn't talk/hear. Go here if that's what you want.

Soft shell crab was very flavorful and ranked No.1 in my mom's mind. Octopus Tostada was a bit too salty for my taste, but the texture was perfect. Reading the fellow reviews, I am grateful we had excellent service throughout the night.
It's not often I give a 5 star review, Cosme was completely on point! From the service, to the sleek Interior and the delicious,every  bite popping with magical favor! I promise it won't disappoint!

Read previous reviews. Don't ruin your evening. Never come back. Food is ok. But what's my expectations from a nominated Michelin Star restaurant are totally ruined! Huge mistake to go there . I  experienced issues with the service and asked for a manager.  The GM is rude. No manner and didn't bother to introduce himself. After 20 minutes waiting  and no manager  show up i had to ask for him again. Eventually this royalty showed up. No introduction, but asked about my problems.Then accused me in intoxication and without any response or resolution left.  
This accident happened few months ago. I didnt want to post this review but yesterday this place came up in the conversation and apparently I'm not the one who experienced so disrespectful attitudes from the stuff there. I tried to find the name of GM on their website and LinkedIn but was not able to find him. Definitely, never gonna be back there.

This is not my first visit to cosme but it's likely to be my last. Our server was almost non existent, we were always needing for a drink or a new plate. Our scallops weren't cleaned properly, they were gritty and also very fishy, meaning they were not a fresh catch. We sent it back because it was borderline inedible. The guacamole was very spicy, good but it should be noted the spice level. I ordered a mezcal margarita and was brought a spicy margarita, and was made to feel as if the error was my fault. Additionally when the correct drink was brought over it was less filled than my friends margarita who had already had 3 sips. To top it off, when our plates were finally refreshed from our appetizers, I was given a dirty plate. The only consistency that I received from that meal was poor service and a lackluster meal. The carnitas were great, but don't offset the rest of the experience . COVID isn't a valid excuse any longer, graces have been given during the height of the pandemic but you aren't charging discounted prices so why should it be a terrible service experience with old fish....

Fine. The corn husk meringue was the highlight. Everything else - all I can say is that a random (but authentic) mexican place down the street from where I live has more flavorful dishes. Service - impeccable. Atmosphere. nice. Glad I went, but will likely never go back.

Great brunch option! Brunch is more casual and chill, still enjoy the amazing Mexican food. Over all the food was really good, the size was incredible bigger than I expect. 

The roast duck enmoladas was amazing, the duck still very juicy. Herb guacamole was a good option to kick off the meals, very fresh, with the flavorful and crispy corn tostadas. Fresco also a good options, if you come with a group of people ( at least 4), Fresco is a better option for starter. The contextual is a little bit similar to guacamole one, but spicy. Recommended just pick up one fro them. 

The only thing is concerned to me was the services team not really know what to recommend to the costumer.

This restaurant was recommended to me and I was invited out to dine here. Reservation seems to always be needed as it is a very popular and fills up fast especially on weekends. The have a quite limited menu with a special that is not on there. You have to ask for it or in some cases I guess they present it to you. The servers are very informed and can explain every item on the menu and how many you should order for two people. All the items on the menu are intended to share and they recommend 4-6 items for two people. We ordered 5 items and the special ( al pastor fried clams). The timing of when the dishes are coming to your table and the constant attention you get is what to expect at a restaurant like this. We drank water as we don't drink alcohol and the total bill landed with tip around $250. The one thing that surprised me is that they didn't have a signature dish that seemed to always be available. They always change the menu and have new items on there. I would prefer to have one dish that I could have many times if I found a favorite. For dessert we had an awesome espresso and cheesecake. All in all a great restaurant with great staff but some of the dishes didn't have the wow factor I expected for a restaurant like this.
Loved the vibe and ambiance. Drinks were really nice. Duck carnitas are a must. Also the dessert!!!

I visited Cosme on my short trip to NYC and I was extremely excited because it's one of the most talked about restaurants in NYC right now. I've heard so much about it and was ready to indulge! We ordered a few dishes to share including the scallops, octopus, tataki, the stripped bass -- honestly this was way too much food for 2 people and I wasn't that impressed.

They did have a LARGE selection of orange wines, which was nice. The ambiance was perfect! I would definitely recommend this place for drinks, but the food ? Not so much.

We also tried the corn husk meringue, which was highly recommended but we didn't finish it -- the texture was very strange. 

Cute restaurant, great service but probably won't be back

Portions here are actually quite generous, and extremely filling! If you want to try their meringue dessert like we initially wanted to, definitely save some room and order accordingly. Between 2, we got the Blue shrimp aguachile, cucumber, Chilaquiles, queso fresco and Duck enmoladas, mole negro, creme fraiche.

The blue shrimp is a light start to the meal, which I would highly recommend since the main dishes may err on the heavier side and hence, extremely filling. The duck enmoladas were so surprisingly delicious, it was just flavours that weren't expected, and everything was just so soft it melted away (in the best way!) with every bite. If I were to go back, I'd get this again and save space for the meringue...

Even though this place commented on my weight one time, the margaritas (even at 11AM) are exceptional and the corn omelette is to die for. Despite that one comment, the staff have over extended their nicety to me and my party on every dining occasion. I prefer this spot for a "lunch" (yes YT girlies, us sophisticated individuals dare not incorporate the word "brunch" in our vernacular). Always be sure to order the churros dulce de leche (with another marg or 4) as an after treat. This restaurant needs to invest in swanky matches for collectors like myself. I am inclined to return to this venue. 

P.S. this restaurant does not accept food stamps
P.S.S. For whatever reason, if your "Resy" happens to be linked here, be sure to unlink them!

Brought my significant other for her birthday. We just moved to NY and there aren't a lot of Mexican restaurants represented in the city so we wanted to support a renowned one with an elevated experience. We are both Mexican and from California so we were both really excited to experience this and expected a unique experience. But the food was fine. There was nothing unique about the flavors or dishes.  I expected to spend a lot but the the food and service was mehhh. 

We ordered 6 things based on the recommendation of the waiter who demanded we put in our entire order within the first 5-10 min of us being there. 

We started with a drink each and immediately got asked to put in our entire order and there is no description of the dishes on the menu. I felt like we were ordering blindly and we definitely over ordered since we wanted to enjoy cocktails as well. 


It would have been a much better experience to let us order at least 2 dishes at a time. 

Would never come back or recommend.

The food is tasty and worth the price but be careful with ordering sprits from the bar. We asked for a unique Mezcal experience when the bartender said they specialize In Mezcales. He proceeded to serve us on miniature sampling cups without using a jigger to measure the pour. By the 1/4 filled cups the volume was approximately 1/4 ounce each, making 1 ounce total from the 4 small pours. When the bill came he charged 4 ounces ($80+tax+tip=$110), overcharged each miniature cup as an ounce serving instead of the 1/4 ounce. I'm very disappointed with the experience when I can get much better Mezcal for a much better price at other establishments with the correct pour size.
STUNNING ambiance. Duck dish was insane, so was the guacamole. Order as much as you can!

Wow!!!! This place is amazing from the moment you enter until you leave if I could give 100 stars I would. It's a little on the pricey side but so worth the happy dance your mouth will make. The duck is out of this world and great to share as a main dish defiantly try a couple of starter plate like the pastor fish and huarache.. the margarita with champagne was a great drink choose but a good wine would have been great as well. Do your self a favor and treat your self to Cosme..

So happy I finally got to experience this place! Came here after work, a little wait yes, but so well worth it. Wagyu Beef Huarache and duck carnitas tacos were out of this world! Absolutely in love with the spicy Margaritas that they serve in a very special way. Makes you want to keep drinking and drinking. Sat at the bar. Loved the bartenders! Cheers Daniela and Cezar!

Amazing, amazing, amazing. Came here twice and both times were delicious. 

Must orders: scallops, the duck carnitas tacos, and the corn husk meringue dessert (maybe the best dessert I have ever had).

Also good but would probably skip: the Paloma, tataki al pastor (slices of fish - tasted like hamachi), the chips and guacamole, and the halibut meztlapique (the fish was a little over cooked and needed more flavor). 

Can't wait to come back! They have a nice private dining room in the back if you want a private event. I understand that there are a few tables and the bar at the front available for walk ins if you can't get a reservation.
Overpriced and stale tostadas... drinks were decent though. Extra star for the decor and ambiance

Reputation exceeds the food. Would only go back for drinks at the bar. Our party had stomach issues the evening and next morning of our meal. Also minor but it's the little things...served meal in a cracked dish. Doesn't compare to any other high end place I've been, especially for the price.

Cosme is definitely worth the hype! Everything was so good, especially the "tataki al pastor" blew my mind it was fish! The famous duck carnitas also live up to expectations! Had about 4 spicy margaritas and don't sleep on the carajillo for dessert probably my favorite thing of the night!

author.name: Madison M.
author.location: Upper East Side, New York, NY

reviews.review: We spent our 4 year anniversary dinner here last night! Their duck carnitas and cornhusk meringue were some of the best dishes we've had so far in NYC, and the service was impeccable. However I didn't really enjoy the texture of the garbanzo and Uni quesadilla (everything was just mushy), and my boyfriend didn't love the sweetness of the tataki al pastor, but the octopus tostada was amazing.

Gorgeous but shockingly bland fish appetizer. Expensive pricing and nice plating, but flavors didn't wow me. Food is still delicious but giving it 2 stars because it is clearly not up to the price in my view.

I came after I saw that it was ranked 22 on the international restaurant list. Very underwhelming. Price aside, the only thing worth writing about was the force meringue which was actually great. Wouldn't come back

The restaurant ambience is lovely, really good food, the duck tacos were incredible and unique. The mole was just the sauce, it did not include a protein which was surprising but was delicious nonetheless. They sat us on the side, which I thought was a bit odd. We had a high top and there were like 6 other seats on our table, meant to share or meant for groups that want to get drinks before dinner perhaps? We asked for an actual low-top dining table but they said they did not have any. I would suggest the restaurant to ask the patrons if this is okay, we didn't mind as we are not picky but I can see it being an issue for others. This restaurant is on the list of world's best restaurants, with Cosme being the first in USA! Great job, Cosme!

Returned post pandemic to enjoy their duck carnitas and their legendary husk meringue dessert.  While the food has maintained its high quality, the price has gone insane.    A single order of the carnitas is now $98.   It wasn't terribly big either--certainly not an entire duck as claimed.  The meringue at $19 is almost as crazy.   Just those 2 items rang up over $150 out the door.   Come on.
My fav Mexican spot in NYC! Love their guac, duck carnitas, octopus tostada, and potato caviar dish. Such great cocktails too!!! 10/10

I knew I was coming to Cosme twice, so I waited till my second trip to write up this review. The menu changed from a winter to a spring menu, and I felt like the winter was a 5 star while the spring, a 4 star.

If I were trying to be strategic, I would not get the guacamole. It's good, but is it $20 good? No. In fact, none of their dishes in the first section of the menu - the raw/small bites, are that good. You are asked to pay $20-$25 for a single bite of food, and I just don't think Cosme's strengths are in ceviche or in seafood. I didn't care that much for their bass or octopus tostadas. Their al pastor had a lovely mango citrus sauce, but it wasn't a super harmonious dish.

What you really should get here are the dishes in the middle section. Roasted cauliflower, fried tetelas, bean tyaluda... this is where Cosme really shines, in their cooked appetizers.

And then of course their duck carnitas is a must get. They serve half portions now, so you don't need a massive group to come here.

The corn husk meringue is also ethereal - it's a lovely essence of corn with light and airy textures.

Cosme is a great place to have a celebratory night out if you are prepared to spend a little bit of money.

The food was pretty good and lots of flavor. However, I would not return. I came with my mother and the price does not match the service and what you receive. It is very nosy and we could not have an easy conversation. Also, my mom's drink was taken away while she was in the bathroom and she had not finished it. They did not even ask her if she had finished. I was hoping to have a better experience. Not at the caliber of Central in Lima, for sure!

Cosme has been one of our favorites for many years. It has now become a New York classic. This is true Mexican cuisine like you would eat at the best restaurants in Mexico City. These dishes all talk traditional Mexican food and add a creative, contemporary flavor. Everything on the menu is wonderful. The cocktails are the best.

Walking into Cosme transports you to what you would hope every restaurant in Flatiron would look like. Sexy, minimalist, dark, beautiful people, great smells, awesome looking cocktails and food flying about you. The dark room is always abuzz with people who are having such a great time, and I love being one of those people as often as I can.

For dinner the must have is the Duck Carnitas, and for brunch it's the Lamb Barbacoa. Both of these dishes are cooked in the most beautiful way possible and will allow you to feel confident that your meal is grounded in something mind blowing. Outside of that the world is your oyster.

There are always many different types of meats and seafood that are worth trying. Scallops are usually quite good, the wagyu on the menu right now is full of flavor and will hit the mark for that savory steak dish, but the Kanpachi and Uni dishes at the moment are very nuanced and interesting. The Kanpachi comes with a pineapple butter that takes a momentary break from what you think of as mexican cuisine, while still living up to the brightness and flavor that you would hope to get from mexican cuisine. It wins hands down as one of the most interesting dishes that I love at Cosme.

The white mole with cabbage and truffle is interesting as well, but it's not one of my favorite dishes. It does appeal to many as the vegan dish on the menu, but it lack depth that so many other dishes on this menu really have. 

The drink menu is fantastic, the wines are great, but the mezcal selection is worth writing home about.

I'd come back any day to Cosme and try to come as often as I can. Hopefully my next visit will be quite soon :)

GOOD:
All of the food we ordered was delicious.

Guacamole- 9/10- best guacamole I've ever had. Simple but creamy and amazing. Was addicting to eat. Only complaint was that they only gave us 3 tostadas to eat it with (for 2 people) so make sure to ask for extra
Scallops- 8/10 - perfect texture and flavor, scallops were fresh and cleaned well (no grit, sand, etc). I wish, though, that they had more time to marinade in the ceviche sauce as we found ourselves scraping more sauce on the fork after the scallop was in our mouths to give us the flavor 
Bass tostada - 7.5/10 - bass was fresh and had good texture, no fatty pieces or anything. The flavor was delicious, the sauce on the tostada was amazing. Don't know what, but something was missing that prevented this from being an incredible dish, instead it was just good
Wagyu beef - 8/10 - very yummy but there was enough wagyu to even taste the meat. The other toppings were great, but then why bother adding the wagyu?
Duck carnitas - 10/10 INCREDIBLE. Only complaint is that we couldn't order more (see bad section for details). One of the best things I've put in my mouth. Could've eaten that for hours. 
Corn husk meringue - 10/10. One of the best desserts I've had recently. Never had a dessert like this before, presentation was amazing. Creamy, delicious, but not overpowering. Perfectly balanced end to meal 


BAD 
Garbanzo bean tetela - 4.5/10 - one of our least favorite dishes of the night. It was good and creamy, but it lacked depth of flavor. It tasted like fast food. When we smother lime juice and the hot sauce they gave us all over the top, it tasted decent. I would skip ($25 Taco Bell potato taco)
Key lime cheesecake - 4.5/10 - the actual cheesecake was great! I love key lime pie and cheesecake so this was the perfect dessert for me!...on paper. In its attempt to be innovative, this establishment slopped on what I believe was an attempt at a lime sorbet, but what really tasted like a frozen ball of lime juice. Also, the texture was like a gremulata making it melt all over the cheesecake and destroying the flavor of the dish. For such a small addition it was really disappointing how much damage it caused. 

REALLY BAD
Service: We waited 20 minutes past our reservation time, which wouldn't have been much of an issue had they not relegated us to standing in the corner of the restaurant unable to even get a drink from the bar.
Running out of food: This isn't the type of restaurant where you'd be a regular given it took months to get a reservation, so when I came here I was excited to try all of their "famous" dishes, namely the octopus tostada, the duck carnitas, and the corn husk meringue. They ran out of the octopus tostada. It shouldn't happen, but I get it I guess. But the worst was when they told us that "all they could offer us" was a half portion of the duck carnitas as we were a two top. This confused me because--based on our previous orders--we were clearly more than willing to pay the amount for the full portion...so why does it matter if we're a two top when we had ordered and payed for enough food for 6??? We left hungry, the portions were small, and had to resort to eating our layer cake back at home. 

It was good, food was yummy, so I give it 4 stars

Had the fortune of coming to Cosme for a birthday dinner. How had I not found or heard of this place already? Forget the sub 4 star total here, this is definitely a top 5 star dining experience in NYC. 

From the excellent service, to the immaculate NYC vibes of feeling like a '90s bond trader, to the exquisite food .. Cosme hit the spot of being a World Top 50 restaurant apparently? Ok, for me a top 10 spot as of now in NYC.

It doesn't sit on a $400 per person Le Bernadin or Benu vibe, so maybe that's more of an appeal actually. Relatively affordable, a great looking bar, and well...

The duck. Holy. I've called out excellent duck dishes before, but Cosme's truly lands in a hall of its own. Also the guac, to scallops, to striped bass, each dish had a unique flavor and presentation, but that duck dish. Fire.

An ending with the meringue. A must. It's the taste of delightful air almost? Oof. Well, TLDR, just come. Enjoy the bites (apparently gluten free), drinks (didn't have enough), and get that duck and meringue. Cheers!

I went to Mexico City a few months prior and coming here brought back all of those amazing food memories. I'm gluten free, so Mexican food is an obvious choice for me. Everything on the menu is gluten free which makes life so much easier. My partner and I had a variety of dishes, but the duck stole the show. Cooked to perfection and really fun build it yourself tacos. The drinks were delicious and if you haven't heard of it, make sure to get a carajillo next time. It's the "pick me up drink" very similar to an espresso martini meant to be enjoyed at the end of dinner. If you're looking for a fun dinner spot with ambiance and mood lighting this should be your next reservation.

I've been dreaming of eating at this restaurant for quite some time due to the fact that it had a Michelin star. The restaurant was very nice, with a nice ambiance. 
We were sat at the tables next to the bar and our waiter's name was Jose. The service by the rest of the staff was incredible, except for Jose. 
From the beginning his attitude was hostile. I had seen photos of different desserts online, and was asking about them. Immediately, he turned me away and said that "we will talk about that when we get there." I didn't realize I wasn't allowed to ask questions...
From the time we sat down, Jose told us to order everything we wanted as soon as possible because it would get busy later and our order would be delayed due to high volume at the restaurant. We ordered promptly as he suggested. The drinks were ordinary; i feel I could've gotten them anywhere else. 
The only plate that stood out was the duck carnitas. Everything else was plain. 
Jose returned once we finished eating, and brought the dessert menus. We ordered 2 carajillos and the corn merengue. We finished our dessert but continued to enjoy our drinks. Before we were even done with our dining experience Jose had already brought the check and asked us to move tables because more people were already coming in. Despite the fact that there had been other people at other tables that had been at the restaurant since before we had even arrived. 
Jose made us order everything at once, rushed our meal and brought us the check before we were done. I'm truly disappointed and dissatisfied with my experience at Cosme. What if I wanted to order another dessert? Which I did... what if I wanted another drink? Which I did... I didn't get a chance because I was asked to move and basically asked to leave. I will not be returning to this establishment; I will not be recommending this establishment and I definitely do not think that the food nor the service deserves a Michelin star. I could've gotten a better meal, with a more pleasant service for a quarter of the price. Which by the was a  hefty $328 without the tip included....

Best food I've ever had. Pricy but amazing. Duck, wagu, cauliflower, octopus and al pastor we're all fantastic. I was stuffed to the brim but I took a blind shot at the dessert menu and I got the husk. Best thing my lips and tongue have ever touched. It's funny, you read some of the other reviews on this place and people are snobs trying to tear it down. Best food I've ever eaten. Period.

We went to the this place because it is the #22 restaurant in the world and we love Mexican! Boy, were we disappointed. The margaritas were subpar so we were off to a bad start. The dinner menu is quite short with mostly seafood options. Felt like they were trying to be so unique in their food that they just missed the mark on good Mexican/TexMex food. The duck dish for two is large - it was decent but pretty gamey (a little expected for duck, but that was one of the two meat options). The guac was ok, nothing extraordinary and their toastadas were far from impressive. Overall the food wasn't bad but I wouldn't have high expectations.

Massively underwhelmed!  I went in with high expectations and this did not come close to meeting them.  The flavors were good but nothing was a wow.  Nothing was special, nothing was memorable.   I get that fancy restaurants like to give tiny portions but really a quarter of a sweet potato is all I get with the mole????  I had three dishes and left very hungry.  If you are looking for a fancy mexican meal go to Casa Enrique which is way way better.

We came here for a weekend brunch with some friends. The smaller plates were pretty good, but the stars were the lamb barbacoa and the desserts. 

The barbacoa is big enough to share with several people. It comes with all the fixings to assemble your own tacos. Salsas, avocado, tortillas, and a big bowl of lamb. So flavorful!

The desserts were well executed and not too sweet. The infamous corn husk meringue lives up to the hype. The churro was so crispy and came with a dipping sauce. They are a must!

First time coming, my bf and I got a nice quiet table in the back on a Saturday night right before Valentine's Day at 5:30pm. By the time we sat, looked at drinks and ordered it was already 6. From there, everything was mouth watery goodness. 

They start off with free chips and two housemade dipping sauces (note: if you cant handle spice of any kind...cosme might not be for you...not that they use a lot but if you dont like onions, sweetness, acidity and your occasional jalapeño, steer away) for everyone else...keep reading. 

We ordered two of the specials as our waiter told us, half portion of duck carnitas, mole, scallops, clams, striped bass tostadas, kampaci al pastor and ofc their signature merengue. 

My favorite dishes were the striped bass toastadas and the merengue. As NYCs say now "this sh*t slapped". All the flavors that explode in your mouth leave you wanting more!

The ones that I would probably pass on was one of the specials (if you look at the photos it's the triangle with uni on top) and the mole. They were just okay imo. 

All in all, service was 11/10 and everyone was vert respectful and attentive. Highly recommend for date night as it was a very romantic setting but can also be fun with friends.

Ofc I had to get Duck carnitas and corn husk meringue and they are both as amazing and unique as everyone says. And if you go there you should def try them both and honestly nothing else!

My 3 star rating justification:

1. Nothing else we ordered stood out and it's supposed to be top 22 restaurant in the entire world and the best in the US? NO!

2. Even though the duck was amazing but it was still slightly over salted (I admit my salt tolerance is much lower than average population tho) and unevenly seasoned. Again it was really amazing but I didn't except to taste chunk of salt unevenly at some part of the dish,  just more expectation for top 50.

3. Some tables are positioned too awkwardly and waiters "behind" could be at someone's face when they are serving other tables. Again not really ok for top 50.

I would still say you should go but only get the duck and the corn husk. Also bring down your expectation before you go.

Here's what makes it a Top 50/James Beard winner- but there is also a big miss.

The combination of flavours without being overbearing. Every dish works with each other. This is something most top restaurants don't get. 
Scallop aguachile was outstanding had flavours of Subtle bergamot with seasonal (and $$$) Nantucket bay scallops and well worth 2 orders! Duck carnitas literally melt in your mouth perfectly cooked with homemade tortillas and just the right heat side sauces.
Drinks are all creative and use artisanal mezcal and tequilas however would be nice for description (ie.. citrus, herbaceous etc).

Here's where I think much improvement is needed- service is impeccable but cold. No one asked how food tasted, no interaction with waiters/bartender who were laser focused on perfect execution, unless asking a question. Ambience is modern but sterile.
It's worth a trip just not sure I would run back.

Went here for dinner and it was such a great experience. The staff was very attentive and helpful. We started off with drinks at the bar and the bartender Isaac was awesome. He was knowledgeable and made great drinks for us. After a couple drinks our table was ready. Our waiter Omar was awesome as well, he really made the experience there magical. All the staff was just very good and worked as a true team. The food was amazing, the flavors and presentations were spot on and played well with the different taste buds. The duck carnitas was my favorite, the meat was so tender and season well. Everything was really good, I didn't have not one bad dish. Dessert was the corn husk which was amazing as well. I really recommend this place, it's a reason why it's considered one of the best in the world.

Food was excellent. Waiter recommend 2 starters, 2 middle and 2 entrees.  We went with 3, 1, 2 and it was more than enough food.  Loved every bite, especially the Octopus and the Cevechi.  Halibut is an award winner somewhere and the brisket was perfectly cooked.

Waiters were well above average.  Menus explanations both; before ordering and when food was served by the back waiter who took the time to explain some of the finer details of what was on each plate.  Busboys were timely and cleaned up every crumb.

Atmosphere is hip and cool.

I see and taste why it's one of the top 25 restaurants in the world.

My only criticism is the with the margarita's, but it's more of margarita recipes discussion.  I think the classic should be tequila, triple sec and lime juice.  No simple syrup and not too much lime juice, they were a little too tart for me.

I usually never leave reviews but after seeing some of the less than stellar reviews here I just wanted to share that I had a great experience and all the food was fantastic! What also made it stand out was that the hostess and all the staff were so friendly and helpful! Probably the nicest wait staff I've experienced in nyc in a while- they created a very friendly and comfortable environment in a very high end and trendy place. We started out with the guacamole and octopus tostada- and while the tostada is only for one person they packed it with a lot of octopus! I'm usually not a huge guacamole fan but I tried a little and it was actually really good- very creamy! I had the al pastor dish for an entree and the pineapple butter with the thinly sliced fish was one of the best things I've had in recent memory. And then the desserts were out of this world- of course we got the signature corn husk meringue which was heavenly- especially once you get into the middle with the corn mousse. But also would recommend to try the chocolate flan- such a surprise underdog but it was a wonderful explosion of chocolate and cinnamon in a creamy flan dish!

So bad. Besides salty I barely taste anything else. How come it was rated Mechlin Star?! I just came back from Mexico city three weeks ago, the food I tasted In nice restaurant of Polanco is way better and less cheaper! Very disappointing!

Had heard about Cosme and it being featured in the best 50 restaurants in the world for a while and was very excited to try it. We loved our time here but don't think it is one of the best restaurants I have been. 
The location and the ambience are incredible. We were greeted by two very friendly staff and were seated immediately. The environment is very elegant and upscale. 

The waiters are pretty good at the job - friendly, well-spoken and happy to explain the menu or make suggestions. 

With respect to the food, the duck carnitas were amazing and you should definitely try them! We also tried the brisket, which exceeded our expectations! 

The only negative point is that the menu is very limited for a restaurant that purports to be one of the top 50 in the world. I would accept that more easily, if the restaurant had a pre-fix mandatory menu, but an a la carte menu should be a little more broad, especially in the appetizers section.

All in all, this is a great Mexican restaurant! You won't find many restaurants that can match or exceed Cosme's quality. We would definitely go again!

Cosme is absolutely one of the best restaurants I have been to. The food is delicious and well-made, and there is no wonder they are on the best restaurants in the world list and have a Michelin star.

The service was also wonderful. The servers were so attentive and kind!

I would love to come back here some day!

Went there for brunch. We don't eat beef and pork and had plenty of options. We have been to Enrique Olivera's restaurant in Mexico City which was fantastic! This restaurant is a notch below. I got the Sea Bass ceviche and it was good, but I think the fish could have been a little more fresh and the salsa was a little too sour. The best ceviche that I've had in Chile was flavored with simply salt, pepper, lemon, and jalapeño. 

We also got the chilaquiles with green sauce. It was fantastic. Very filling. 

Overall the ambiance was nice and would make for a great date spot. 

Pricing was very reasonable.  

Will definitely consider going back.

This place is a solid 4.5 stars.
Excellent service, delicious food, and creative (yet approachable) cocktails. Great vibes, too!
The food was amazing! Every single Item I had to eat was superb and worth every penny.  The service was excellent and everyone was super nice! Totally recommend this restaurant.

Shocking to see that this spot has such low reviews on here. People are insane. I went for brunch recently and didn't have a bite I didn't love. The guacamole was so fresh and flavorful, the chilaquiles (one of my favorite Mexican dishes) was perfectly crunchy and delicious. And don't get me started on the churro. A true work of art. 

I'll definitely be back for more and it's certainly deserving of the recognition it has been receiving. For those who think it's overpriced - it's a fine dining experience in New York City, I think your expectations were a bit off when you walked in the door.

I was very excited for this lunch now that Cosme has cracked San Pellegrino's 50 best restaurants list. Expectations were very high and Cosme met them. We came and a group of 10, easily the largest group in the dining hall, but the servers were fantastic and able to keep up throughout. The dining room is chic industrial, open and modern, tables are far apart so it feels intimate even though the space is so big. Drinks were good all around but the "con piquete" stole the show! Highly recommend. It was brunch time we ended up trying almost everything off the brunch menu. Here's the rundown:

Guacamole 4/5
Blue shrimp aguachile 4/5
Mushroom quesadillas 3.5/5
Chilaquiles (green salsa and chicken) 4.5/5
Chilaquiles (red salsa and egg) 5/5
Mushroom birria 4/5
Duck enmoladas with mole negro 5/5
Lamb barbacoa to share 5/5
Corn tortillas 5/5
Churros 3/5
Cornhusk meringue 5/5

The smaller shared plates like the guacamole, aguachile, quesadillas, and birria were all good, but none really stood out. The highlights were the larger plates. The chilaquiles rojos were so good, barely edging out the green chilaquiles with chicken but both were amazing. The duck enmoladas were divine and the mole was to die for. The showstopper obviously was the lamb barbacoa which was huge, easily could serve 3-4 and came with blue corn tortillas and avocado and habaneros for accoutrements. Finally, for dessert we had some middling churros with a delicious dulce de leche sauce and the unparalleled Cornhusk meringue. You cannot get a better balance of textures, subtle sweetness, and richness than this meringue and custard. Perfection on a plate.

Overall, this is upper echelon dining. It was on the expensive side for brunch at $105 per person with tip, but compared to other places in New York that may be a bargain.

Food 4.5/5
Service 5/5
Ambiance 4/5
Value 4/5
Overall 4.4/5 (Outstanding)

Worth every penny.  Beautiful minimalist setting.  Extremely attentive service.  With three people, we tried a couple of margaritas, red wine, guacamole, striped bass, scallop tostada, cobia al pastor (fish), wagyu beef, ayocote beans, brisket and halibut meztlapique.  Margaritas were just ok.  Preferred the wine better.  Wagyu beef also underwhelmed.  The ayocote beans, striped bass, halibut and brisket were exquisite.

The reviews don't lie but I don't think it was as bad as I expected it to be.  That's because I went in expecting $50 7-11 burritos.  

To give Cosme some benefit of the doubt, I found it odd that so many people give Cosme low ratings for having overpriced food for what is essentially the dressed up version of grandma's Mexican dishes.  I love the NYC food scene, but Cosme is a great example of the usual fine dining experience here; if not absolutely internationally heralded as the top of the top and you're still paying top dollar, chances are you're going to be in for a bad time if you're not used to the pretend-haughtiness that dominates Manhattan these days.  

On to why most reviewers are absolutely right to roast this laughably poor attempt to hide the Taco Bell kitchen in the back. 

SALT FAT ACID HEAT.  This restaurant has zero understanding of what makes a dish taste good.  Everything was either severely underseasoned or way too fatty, and the temperature of every dish was questionably just lukewarm/room temp.  It's as if they aimed for every dish to be the same temperature as the human body; mildly disconcerting to say the least.  Cosme provided limes with almost every dish, as if some poor bloke in the back of the kitchen was making a small statement against the head chef to protest the utter lack of acid in every dish.  You can't simply smash lime juice on top of every dish to compensate for a lack of balance in the body of the food itself.  

Service and restaurant arrangement.  What is with the 2-person tables crammed into what resembles more like a poorly constructed dining hall table that seats 20 than it did individual dining tops.  It's a problem if the server can't hear what you're ordering because the guests sitting at the table next to you are literally closer to you than your partner is sitting across from you.  The servers themselves were at times oddly attentive, refilling water when I had literally only taken a single sip: how mildly invasive and unnecessary.  At other times, especially as the night wore on, we sat there without a single checkin to grab our empty plates or refill our water for 20 minutes.  This would have been somewhat acceptable had we not reset our expectations based on the hurried cadence an hour earlier.  

Taco Bell.  I'm an ignorant American.  My baseline definition for Mexican isn't even Mexican, it's tex-mex fast food.  One step up from that is my understanding of fast casual tex-mex burritos called Chipotle and Dos Torros.  One step up from that is any number of authentic taco joints across the country.  Unfortunately, some of the dishes I ate at Cosme can be legitimately found at Taco Bell, but better.  Cosme serves a potato dish that's essentially one of their awful blue corn tortillas folded over a mashed potato into the shape of a triangular hot pocket with shredded lettuce on top, served with a side of sour cream and caviar.  I shit you not the Taco Bell soft shell potato taco is a thousand times better than this deconstructed atrocity.  I like the guac at chipotle more than this mashed avocado and adult, thick-stemmed, uncut cilantro-topped horror at Cosme, wish I was kidding.  

Presentation and general quality of food.  I implore you to take a look at some of my hastily taken pictures (lest someone at the restaurant think I'm relishing the experience at Cosme by immortalizing these sad excuses for fine dining) and revel in how distasteful it all is.  From the mound of guacamole that was probably shoveled with a large spoon and catapulted across the kitchen into my bowl in an impromptu game of IRL age of empires, to the shallots designed to mimic the juicy grub hidden beneath the shrubbery so colorfully presented in Disney's The Lion King, with all the grace of Pumba himself, I mustered my best effort to dig into a completely raw wagyu filet that had been brutalized into tatters and then used as a cocoon for young sprouts.  Why so unrefined in your choice of bringing food to your mouth you might ask?  Because the only cutlery provided to us all night was a spoon, a fork, and a... butter knife?  This is why I and another guest sitting next to me ended up gnawing at sinewy raw meat with our bare hands, not unlike a pack of hyenas scavenging the remains of a dead zebra.  Why was the wagyu such poor quality to begin with?  So many questions.  There is plenty more I could get into but the nausea is coming back from this brief stint at Scar's Diner. 

1/10, +1 for the corn husk meringue dessert, -9 for Cosme, or should we say Robme in the words of other yelpers.

This is the second time at Cosme. It is truly amazing. I always look for places with really bold flavors. Everything we had was bold and flavorful and definitely worth coming back for. Order the tostadas and the aguachiles, the moles and pretty much everything. The corn dish with crab and Gorgonzola was mind blowing too.

Huge letdown. Service from bartenders and waitstaff cold, detached. Except for the mole', the dishes lacked subtlety and nuance. The fish was bland. While I liked the corn crab dish, it was just ok. Not worth it.

I wanted to looooooove this so much and give it 5 stars but was a little disappointed. The overall experience was good but the food was quite average except for the duck carnitas and corn merengue. They were phenomenal! The carnitas meat was perfectly cooked and as soft as butter and the corn merengue was the best dessert I've ever had in my life!! My girlfriend and I literally ordered it twice. 
We also tried the crab esquite which was ok, kinda bland and watery. The wagyu beef dish was also dry and the guac was not memorable.

I went last night for my birthday, I was so excited about finally being able to get a table! Omg, what a waste of money... We sat at the bar to wait for our table, I ordered a margarita, it came in a huge water glass served half way, awful.
They had ran out of the "famous" duck carnitas.  We ordered 7 dishes! All mediocre at best, except for the mole, and the chocolate flan... those 2 were ok.
Tortillas were cold and hard!! The most basic in a good Mexican restaurant! 
At the end, they brought me a tiny tiny bite of a cake with a candle.  Our waiter never showed up again, he sent someone else to take care of our table. The fish was bland and over cooked! 
Anyway, 500 dollars later, I was very sad to have gone there.
I wanted so much to love it.  I'm from Mexico City and live here in Manhattan, what a disappointment.
Que lastima

How the place became one of the best in the USA let alone the world is beyond me.   The waitress doesn't understand allergies or know what is in the food or put in orders when you request food.  After taking the order the waitress disappears.   Didn't even ask if we needed more drinks after removing our finished ones.  The bus people that fill the water glasses and food runners on the other hand are fantastic.  A food runner is the one that revealed that there was an allergen in what we ordered.  I guess the waitress was just happy to sell me the $100 duck that it ends up I couldn't eat.   Noise level was horribly loud.  We could barley have a conversation.  The food was fair to good, not great and definitely not in the top 50 in the world.   I went there to be wowed, left disappointed.   To put Cosme on the same list as Le Bernardin?  Something is wrong with this rating system.

Words cannot describe how great this place is. It definitely deserves a Michelin star on food quality/preparation alone. Definitely go with a group of people to get the full menu experience so you can taste everything! The duck while $$ is well worth it if you have 3 people or more. Everything was solid and each dish had lots of dimension to them. Can't wait to go back!

Mediocre food!! 
Overpriced restaurant!! 
Any Mexican grandma would do 100% better food than this. 
Can NOT believe they are "BEST RESTAURANT IN NORTH AMERICA LOL. The PR COMPANY is working IT hard. 
The only good item was the tortillas maybe, but you can get them somewhere else.
My advice, skip it,l!! 
Hyped to the max.

Waited 2 months for our reservation and was super excited to finally get to try it: Went to cosme last night with my partner and waited 20 minutes after our reservation to be seated but that wasn't so bad because you could tell it was just busy and tables were tied up. We ordered 8 courses and they were all pretty good. The potato dish was a bit bland and if it did not have the caviar on top it would just be a boring unsalted potato and tortilla dish. We also ordered the duck dish (basically why everyone goes) as soon as we put in all our order, and when it was finally time for the last course the server said the chef miscounted and there was no duck left. Bummer. But they gave us free duck tacos (not on the menu) to compensate and told us to pick whatever we wanted else off the menu and it would be on them. We ordered more drinks and brisket and it was amazing. The server was kind enough to make up for the kitchens mistake which saved our experience. I think the food was pretty good but not "top 50 restaurant" quality in my opinion.

Love this place!! First time I went 2-3 yrs ago, it seemed a little avant-garde, sterile, and I don't remember the flavors really popping like they did when I went back last week. 

The brisket tacos are incredibly tasty, like almost no other taco or brisket I've ever been served. Succulent and savory and you're gonna want two orders. 

The guacamole is next level. 

The ambiance is hip and pumping with music. Fun spot for sure. 

Every single server and host and water pourer and bartender said "you gotta try the duck carnitas."  We did not. Gotta go back and are fired up to do just that.

Visited back in 2018. This is one of my favorite restaurants and although I haven't been back in a while... I can't wait to visit next month. The staff, ambieNce and food ( the duck carnitas!!!-oh WOW)  are an absolute experience. I completely recommend this restaurant!!

So I had to check this restaurant out since it was ranked #22 in the 2021 World's 50 Best Restaurants. The duck carnitas were AMAZING! The serving is good for sharing, so try not to order too many appetizers to spoil your appetite. The disk was very tender, and the lime, onions, greens, jalapeños and dressings just balance out the grease to perfection. What happens next is a beautiful complement of flavors in your mouth to savor. I honestly think this is the best duck entree I've had so far, including Peking and con fit plates. For dessert, we had the corn husk meringue, and it was an interesting cream corn and sweet meringue combination, with the mezcal +  coffee. Perfect pairing as the bitter liqueur complemented the sweet meringue with what seemed like creamy corn pudding. 

The servers are super attentive. My water glass was always refilled without asking. The music was great, atmosphere very . The lighting and decor was perfect. Loved the 2 pay phones downstairs which you pass by on the way to the bathroom. Do they still work? Not sure, but now I'm nostalgic for NYC payphones. :) 

Never thought I would understand and love upscale Mexican food this much (cause food trucks and homey restaurants in Brooklyn are AWESOME!) but I am now your fan. Well done, Cosme!

Well I won't be coming here again.

First off was the 45 minute-plus wait for the table we had reserved, during which the hostess came by and actually said "It may be a while so I'd suggest you order an appetizer if you're hungry." Then, once seated nearly an hour late, we waited another 30-40 minutes for a server to take our order, during which she tried to upsell us to the most expensive item on the menu (the ONLY item she recommended). THEN it took 30-45 minutes for any food to arrive. As we were leaving we spoke to the manager who offered a tepid apology in which he basically said "we're really busy tonight and it couldn't be helped." For a restaurant this expensive, this is inexcusable service.

Interior design was cozy and neat. Modern and classic. There is a nice waiting area seating on the left as you enter and a bar area on the right. We were seated pretty quickly. We asked to change to a smaller table since our party downsized and they accommodated us. The waiters are knowledgeable but basically recommended all the food choices. We had five dishes plus a dessert. Def recommend the blue shrimp, duck enmoladas and lamb. We came during lunch time so choices were limited. For dessert we got the cornhusk meringue and it was a unique dish. Def try that out. It was a frienda bday so they brought out a slice of tres leches cake with a candle. Bathroom is down the stairs and it was hard to tell which bathroom was women, men. Further down is the men and the one closes to the exit is the women. Shared sinks outside. Overall, a well worth restaurant to try. There is a reason why Cosme is ranked #22 best restaurant in the world. Go try it out and see why.
Found this gem and I am so happy I chose to come here. The food is fresh and the cocktails are great. Contemporary Mexican.

I'll start off with the good: the duck was the most perfectly cooked meat I've ever had in my life. The cornhusk was iconic...

Unfortunately, two stars were deducted because there was sand ALL in our scallops (on the tostada). It was disgusting. The cocktails weren't great either. I had higher hopes for a James Beard Award winning restaurant.

Cosme was a heavenly experience. 
Everything we ordered was beyond amazing, but we particularly will forever remember the duck carnitas and the corn husk meringue - both are things we had never tasted anything like before.

I highly recommend this place! It is worth every penny!

Came here this year for my birthday, since Mexican is my favorite cuisine and I'm also a bit of a foodie, so this was a match made in heaven. Make sure to prepare your wallet, as this place is very expensive, but man, it was one of the best meals I've had in the 6 years I've lived in NYC. Crazy unique Mexican themed dishes. This place is wonderful.

Extraordinary!
The food is incredibly accurate and sophisticated, and still relatable and surprising at the same time. Beautifully presented. The space and the service are refined in a very natural and contemporary way. 
One of New York contemporary classics

I was VERY hesitant about dining at Cosme given the negative reviews. After last night though, I had to write to say...it is worth the hype! Almost everything - down to the accompanying sauces were flavorful and thoughtful

- el ninja: 4.5/5; liked how refreshing it was so much so that I ordered two 
- guacamole: 4/5; Solid but could've used a touch more salt. The chili oil + guac though? 
- scallop tostada: 4.5/5; fresh, light, and yum 
- octopus tostada: 5/5; dreaming about this still!! a smoky and unique take on octopus
- corn + crab: 4.75/5; super creamy! want to bring this to a bougie picnic by the lake lol
- potatoes + caviar: 4/5; who doesn't feel rich eating caviar?? more than 'solid' dish. 
- black bean tlayuda: 2/5; we wanted the mole but I have a nut allergy  so feel bad for my dinner guests but I'm here to tell you to get the mole! 2 points for the chanterelles though.. it was OK but there are better options. 
- DUCK CARNITAS: 20/5; if nothing else, get the duck. 
- corn husk meringue: 20/5; i lied. you also HAVE to get this dessert. another dish that makes you feel rich! 
- we also got a bottle of orange wine, which was good as well. 

i'd go again. even after getting the bill.

The corn husk meringue is the reason I revisit Cosme ($19)

Their soft shell crab dish ($30-something) was good, but not mind blowing. Too much lime or vinegar on both the crab and radish.  Lime only on radish would've been perfect.  Duck carnitas are delicious. 

Decent cocktail list ($17-). But better wine list ($16-20)

This is a review for a summer 2021 dinner experience. All views expressed are my honest opinion.

Overall: 4/5
Food: 4.5/5
Ambiance: 4/5
Value: 3/5
Service: 3.5/5

TL;DR: Impressed by almost every dish we ordered. Flavors were absolutely on point; service & ambiance had some room for improvement.

------------------

EXPERIENCE

The good:
- Ambiance: upscale Mexican restaurant - very chic

The ish:
- Ambiance: our 2-person table was wayyyy too close to the next table over. We could hear everything our neighbors were saying. Like other reviewers said, the restaurant is dark, so you'll likely not get good photo ops
- Service: our waiter seemed pushy to us - he wanted us to get more food, which we didn't. He recommended we go with 2 small plates per person (total 4), plus 1 large plate to share. We ended up going with 3 small plates to share with 1 large plate. It felt like he was irate at our decision, and rarely came by to check on us. Honestly, we were so stuffed by the end of our meal that we were puzzled at why Cosme would recommend folks to get so much food.

------

FOOD

What we liked:
- Small plate: HEIRLOOM TOMATOES, SUN SWEET MELON, CHICATANAS. This was a very refreshing veggie appetizer. I loved how fresh and sweet the melons were.
- Small plate: COBIA AL PASTOR. My favorite small plate from our meal. This dish comes with a stack of corn tortillas, which you then use to build tacos. Very unique flavors
- Large plate: BRISKET, CHILE MORITA, AVOCADO. I really liked this dish as well - it was super filling, and the brisket was delicious. Also came with its own stack of tortillas.
- Dessert: CORNHUSK MERINGUE. Very unique dessert dish. Definitely meant to be shared - I was definitely slowing down after having a few bites myself.

What was just okay:
- Small plate: OCTOPUS TOSTADA, CHINTEXTLE, SORREL. I wasn't impressed because the tostada was so overloaded with octopus that the ratio of protein to carb felt off to me. Additionally, this dish was for a single (1x) large tostada - our waiter tried to have us order 2x these, which we gladly did not do

We were there yesterday 6 members of my family went to dine  because we read reviews about this place, great ambience even though too dark for me you can hardly  hardly the menu,  staff was fast and friendly, we ordered 3 appetizers and 7 entrees that they explain uus they were supposed to be shared, they were so small that each of us jus can have a bit of each, mole was horrible, melon with heirlooms tomato nice and fresh  very innovative but bland for me, duck was a 98 dollar dish was nice and tender you suppose to wrapped in tortillas that were tiny but tasty, sea bass in  a citrusy juice was one of my favorite , soft crab with a cucumber salad spaghetti like cut was nice and fresh, the brisket was slice so thin but tasty I didn't like at all the purple tortillas, too dry and bland, and a tiny octopus tostada  that cost 25 for I piece octopus salty and dry for me. I like  some of the sauces  one that was like a very smooth guacamole, and another orange one that was like a hot pepper sauce , we also ordered 3 of the desserts, the chocolate flan, the sorbets and the merengue that was delicious, anyway to complemented two capuchones 6 alcoholic drinks and 3 more beverages, I'm describing all this because one of my nephews took care of the bill which I can tell was over 600, we spend 2 hours there when we finish our dessert and we still have our e presos and cappuccinos one guy approach t our table and ask us to leave because people was waiting  we were  completely mortified after this, I couldn't believed that they did that to a table that spend so much much that night. We were at Le Bernardin restaurant as on Friday and this is an exquisite restaurant we stayed almost 3 hours and our bill was a little less and they never asked us to leave. Off course I will never ever come back food it's ok but nothing to make me desire to go back and after the treatment forget about Cosme.

I eaten at Cosme many times, both for lunch and dinner.  The standards were always high.  However, my group of five were all a little disappointed.  The duck for $95 was good but hardly worth the price.  The brisket was uninteresting and not very tender.  Halibut was disappointing.  Cocktails were interesting and flavorful, the better part of the meal.  The signature cornhusk meringue was no longer an hard egg shaped but a cracked egg with pudding on the top.  Why they change it is a mystery.  Chocolate flan was rich and hard. The hoja santa raspado was refreshing but not very exciting.  The small plate tomatoes and wagyu beef were very good.  The service could use improvement.  The waiters were not very helpful, dishes were whisked away while others were still eating.  The restaurant packed and  was noisy with loud music so conversation is difficult. At $900 for five people this restaurant needs improvement.

Soullessly underwhelming.

Cosme plays like a culinary cemetary, with the specters of past ambition and flavors dissapointing you with each bite.

Every dish has theoretical potential - the original chef and owner is obviously talented - but the execution just isn't there. Like a haunted mansion, I'm sure at some time past it was once beautiful.

Basic things like texture and acid are now perpetually missing. Even the drinks (which sound cool) managed to be bland.

Unfortunately, you also won't taste a single thing spicier than this review.

Cosme rolls out the red carpet when it comes to presentation, quality and creativity. Eating here is truly an experience with rich flavors capturing authentic Mexican cuisine while putting a creative spin to tradition. My favorites were the duck carnitas and corn husk meringue - you must try these! I asked for a sipping mezcal and the waiter did a fantastic job filtering through the hundred or so available, answering my questions and settling on one they fit my criteria. Will be back!

Price aside, Cosme would probably be a 3. But price + hype are inextricably linked with Cosme, and for that it gets two stars. 

The restaurant is chic, but incredibly loud. Waiters are at once overbearing (I think our water was refilled about 25x, almost any time we took a sip) and missing in action -- we asked for sauce 3 times before we gave up, and we were never asked if we wanted another drink the entire time. Which is just as well, as both the iced + mezcal margarita were incredibly bland. 

But I could forgive all of that had the food lived up to the hype. All I can say is that it is patently absurd that this is considered one of the best restaurants in the world. There are so many amazing restaurants in NY (much less, you know, the world) at a variety of price points that are so well worth a visit. 

We had the tomato & melon salad (one of the nicer things I had, but not $35 good), the mackerel escabeche tostados (also one of the better dishes), the potato tateles (which were basic mashed potatoes wrapped in a tortilla), and the soft shell crab (fine, bland, and with tasteless daikon). We then got the duck carnitas since it was a "can't miss" -- again, just bland. There were no interesting textures, sauces or flavor to it, and the skin wasn't crispy (a duck crime, if you ask me). Finally, we got the chocolate flan (fine) and the corn husk meringue (sickly sweet and one note). There wasn't a single memorable or stand out dish amongst them -- just a lot of bland, uninspired dishes. 

I wish I liked this more, but then I wish they made better food.

The best and most authentic upscale Mexican restaurant in NY. The service here is also incredible.

I'll come back to update this more specifics, but everything was delicious, full of flavor, and unique  (but yet authentic). 

We will certainly be back soon.

3.75/5.

Cosme is a ridiculously overpriced upscale Mexican restaurant in NYC that has good to great food. The legendary dishes don't necessarily live up to expectations, but they are tasty.

Last night, I had the opportunity to dine at Cosme along with 7 colleagues. Thankfully, we were able to expense the meal. I believe that Cosme is about double the price it should be. It makes Casa Enrique much more approachable (and Casa Enrique is expensive too!).

The service was both excellent and invasive/problematic. Let me explain.
Our waiter was extremely aggressive - he pushed guac and drinks from the start and when I ordered food for the table, he very quickly added 2 and 3 of items with little regard for price and preference. It was hard to slow him down. On the other hand, he was very knowledgeable and answered questions well. I just was not comfortable with his style and felt like he quickly ran up our tab. The other servers were well choreographed when placing and removing dishes and were very professional.

When I received the check, I noticed that multiple additional drinks were added to the bill. The server says that someone else placed drinks from another table on our check and he worked with me to remove what wasn't ours. However, I still believe we were overcharged for a drink that we didn't order. I spoke with a friend who visited Cosme last week and he had the same experience (aggressive waiter and additional drinks on the check).

As for ambiance, the restaurant is cool and busy. But it is DARK. I did not appreciate eating in the dark - outside of the scope of the targeted light on our table.

As for the food, standouts were Duck Carnitas, Cobia al Pastor, Brisket, and the Banana + Matcha dessert. The guacamole, scallops, octopus were also enjoyed by the table.

Cosme is good for corporate events and for those looking to accumulate Michelin stars. It would be optimal to visit with an experienced Cosme diner in order to stick to the greatest hits and to keep costs down.

Hadn't been back to Cosme since my first experience a few years ago. It was excellent the first time around, and I still keep asking myself why I didn't go back sooner? The food/service/ambiance were all fantastic! Order whatever your heart desires (nothing really disappoints), but whatever you do, don't miss out on the duck carnitas. Go hungry and/or wear strechables.

Just go. It's so good.  The creativity is crazy, the food is tasty and thought-provoking.  The vibe is chic and fun, and the people are some of the most wonderful in the industry.  The cocktails and wine program are off the charts.  There is truly not another place like it in the city.

Traditional Mexican cuisine is not fully present, it is a cuisine that favorably represents a personal style of the chef who with talent manages to meet the expectations of the international Gourmet trend, the authentic flavors and portions are much more generous in reality, thus representing a culture of splendor and abundance in every sense.
 Overprice, it is for most of the clients a sad disappointment

La cocina tradicional mexicana no está presente en plenitud, es una cocina que representa favorablemente un estilo personal del chef quien con talento logra cumplir la expectativa de la tendencia internacional Gourmet, los auténticos sabores y porciones son muchos más generosos en la realidad, representando así una cultura de esplendor y abundancia en todo sentido. 
 
Los precios son por encima de lo que se recibe como experiencia, resulta para la mayoría de los clientes una triste decepción de la  expectativa.

3.5/5 rounded up. Great service in a trendy setting with some standout dishes (aka the large-format Duck Carnitas and the culinary media darling Cornhusk Meringue dessert). However, stray away from the aforementioned and you're looking at some very low bang-for-your-buck items that you would find better (and cheaper) elsewhere.

The restaurant's ambience is modern and sleek, like someone shut the lights off at a Muji warehouse and plopped a candle on every table. The service is great - happy to recommend drinks and guide a group through a menu.

For a group of four, we were able to sample a good chunk of the menu including the guacamole, scallops and bass aguachile (a soupier, less acidic ceviche), octopus tostada, wagyu beef huarache (picture an open-faced taco or less crunchy, oval-shaped tostada), black bean tlayuda (basically an open-faced quesadilla),  their mole de la casa topped with spinach, both of the large-format dishes (fish and duck carnitas), and the chocolate flan and cornhusk meringue for dessert. 

THE GOOD...
