If you must order any dish at Cosme, it's this one. The duck is cooked to perfection and is perfectly balanced with the raw onions and bright salsas - and the skin! *chef's kiss* Ooh, the skin is the best part! It's like a combination of peking duck and tacos, two of my favorite things, so really I can't complain. The size is good for 2-3 people, if you order a couple of other items. In terms of dessert, the cornhusk meringue is a well-executed dish that is well-deserving of its fame. Not too sweet - the ultimate compliment I can dish out to a dessert.

THE BAD...
Everything else on the menu that we tried was honestly underwhelming and ranged from "meh" to "good... if you didn't look at the prices." The guacamole was tasty, but nothing better than what you'd find your favorite taqueria. The aguachile was nothing to write home about and same went for the octopus tostada and wagyu. These smaller dishes (first two sections of the menu) can really only be shared among 2 people. It's too much food for just 1 - which we learned after each getting a personal order of the octopus tostada and aguachile - but not enough when dividing among 4 (which we did with the wagyu).

AND THE UGLY
The black bean tlayuda was underwhelming and uninspired. It is literally just bean purée over a tortilla - I fail to see how this dish was elevated at all to justify its placement on an upscale menu (and at its price!). The mole with spinach is also a definite pass (especially at $30 - I expect more than just a ladle of sauce with boring greens). I did not find the mole very appetizing - I am someone who would travel far for a good mole, but this one was not one of them.

Overall? Come for the good service, cool ambience, delicious cocktails, the duck, and the meringue. Don't order anything else and you'd probably leave happy.
Good food, nice vibes, and the food it's out of the ordinary, exquisite! very appreciative of the excellent service isaac

I am impressed, Cosme was really astonishing. Very cute spot with great prices and good menu options. Pretty much every thing that we have ordered was really fresh and yummy. Service is incredibly good, no issues at all. Cosme is a really nice place, I will be back!

Delicious upscale Mexican food and a chic ambiance. 

Came here for their reopening and was very happy with the food and service. We brought our own wine for a corkage fee. 

Food: Guacamole to share is always a great choice. The carabineros are AMAZING absolutely get these. We tried all 6 of the items in the top part of the menu, but weren't blown away by the others. The duck carnitas are the real star of the show. It comes with a massive slow cooked duck and tortillas to make your own tacos. Finally the corn husk meringue is very unique and a great sweet/salty combo. I came in a party of 3 and we split 6 small plates and 1 main plus 2 desserts but definitely didn't need all 6 small plates (maybe 3-4).

Got a last minute reservation at 9:15 on a Friday night for 2 and we had to try this place out. We had to wait about 15-20 minutes until we got seated, but we were comfortable waiting in a front booth and ordering drinks for the table. The ambiance is upscale and trendy. The food was really good, but the duck carnitas for two was a standout - seriously best duck we've ever had. The starters were basically a potato quesadilla and beef on a corn tortilla with avocado (I know the menu's names are not descriptive). The dessert was amazing too - we were skeptical, but it is also a must try. Would love to come back and try their brunch when that reopens!

This is one of those trendy expensive places in New York that you go to once and don't need to go again (although I would say I didn't need to go in the first place).  The menu is organized by appetizers in the top two sections, entrees in the next two sections, and then desserts. The best thing of the night was the octopus tostada which was $30 for one tostada. They gave tortillas with a couple sauces before the food came. The sauces were a black bean paste, a salsa verde, and one other orange sauce. We got the dessert the restaurant is known for, the corn one, and it was sickly sweet. I had one bite and that was enough.
We went there for desert and drinks. Our server was so kind and helpful. The deserts were amazing. The drinks were very good. We would come back when we are next in the area.

This sleek and trendy Flatiron restaurant hits the spot if you are looking for upscale Mexican cuisine, but be warned that this place is not friendly on the wallet!

If you are down to splurge, which I highly suggest when dining at Cosme, I would order the Duck Carnitas. This dish is very large so it is ideal to split with another person or two. The duck is beyond tender and when paired with the pickled onions, homemade corn tortillas and a huge helping of cilantro creates a taco that is truly divine. In addition to the Duck Carnitas we also ordered the Cobia Al Pastor which was light and fresh with a perfect tang from the pineapple puree. For dessert the Caramelized Cacao Butter with pistachio sorbet and raspberries was decadent and a satisfying way to end the meal. 

The ambiance is dim, chic and bustling. It is perfect for a special date night. The service was great which is what you would hope for with an upscale establishment like Cosme.

Cosme lives up to expectations. All of the food is of superb quality - it only gets a 4 for me because I find the menu to be quite limited and I wish they had more options. Otherwise, everything is perfect including the decor, service, etc. - I will be back!

Modern refined Mexican cuisine, leveraging local seasonal Hudson Valley ingredients. Cosme is owned by Chef Enrique Olvera, who you may recognize from Netflix's Chef's Table. His Mexico City restaurant, Pujol, is often rated among the hallmarks of The World's 50 Best Restaurants. Ferran Adrià of El Bulli is quoted saying, "There was Mexican food before Enrique Olvera, and Mexican food after Enrique Olvera." So when one comes to Cosme, you pay homage to the King. That said, Chef Soto-Ines did leave in December 2020, which I'm sure will prompt cascading changes at the restaurant that are not yet known.

Cosme's interior is cool, modern, lively. And the food is robust and powerful. The duck carnitas slowly braise in the meat's own fat, interlaced with orange and Mexican Coca-Cola. It comes out rich, juicy, fatty, and decadent. Wrapped in the best tortillas in NYC. They're made from old strains of blue, yellow, purple and white corn grown in Mexico. And they're perfectly balanced when wrapped with the pickled accoutrements. The soft shell crab made with yellow mole, green papaya salad and lemon verbena is a textural delight when you crunch thru the shell and you sop up all the sauce. It's unexpected for a Mexican restaurant, but is a great addition. And the famous dessert, the delicate corn husk meringue stuffed with a sweet corn cream, perfectly balances sweet and salty. You're hit with the the burnt vanilla cream, mascarpone sweet corn, the crunch and then the fluff of the delicate  meringue. Overall, a beautiful meal at reasonable value.
Excellent trendy atmosphere and the best, upscale take on Mexican food I've had.

We really wanted to like Cosme, and had great first impressions when we walked into their beautiful restaurant for dinner, and were seated without wait or a line (we had a reservation). We went for a special occasion. 

First the positives - the ambience and decor are fantastic. The guacamole, and plantain tortilla(?) was so unique and refreshing. 

The issues began with the starters. To preface, I have been a vegetarian my whole life, and do not speak Spanish. When I was ordering off the predominantly Spanish menu, I explained, and requested the waiter to please tell me if I mistakenly order anything that is not vegetarian.

For the first course, I ended up ordering the "uni" - which I didn't know at the time, and overlooked it assuming it was a Spanish word I didn't know, and reassured that the waiter would have told me if it was something I wouldn't eat. Once it came, it was clear it was not vegetarian, and I didn't even take a bite of it. When I bring my kindly suspicion to the waiter, he confirms it was sea urchin, and exclaims "oh, I thought you knew what Uni was. Maybe the manager will let you switch it out". This is pretty ridiculous - not only did he not apologize that he didn't notify me of my choice (1 of 4 courses for almost $100) when I clearly asked him to, but he acted like he was doing me a favor to fix this. While I thanked him at the time - not wanting to ruin the special dinner by starting an argument - I did not appreciate the attitude, or lack of apology, at all. They did end up swapping it out for another course, but it didn't leave a good impression on me. 

My partner also exclaimed her dissatisfaction on the fact that her fish was not scaled, but I'm not sure about whether this is normal, or expressed in the menu. 

The food overall is underwhelming. We ended up spending $350+ on the pre-fixe meal and drinks here, but only maybe 1 or 2 of the 9 dishes and 4 drinks (2 of us) combined were memorable. There are better Mexican restaurants in the city for the same price range - and even a lower budget.

We will not be returning - save yourself some money!

Went here for a special valentines/bday dinner. It exceeded my expectations in every way (and I had high expectations!) A manager introduced himself to us and invited my date, a cook at another upscale restaurant, to see the kitchen. The food is some of the best I've ever had. It is worth every penny. Daniela Soto-Ines is a genius with a huge heart and you can taste it with each bite. I never knew tortillas could taste like that. If you do not have the means to drop a few hundred on dinner and drinks (totally understandable!), I recommend that you come in for one drink/dish at a time or just to try one if Isabel Coss' mind blowing desserts. You won't regret it.

We had dinner last night and obviously, things have changed after coronavirus.  The changes are not too bad because it used to be a very busy and noisy but now it feels calm and quiet, which makes your experience even more enjoyable.

The Menu has changed to set menu format with 4 courses - seafood, vegetable, protein, dessert - paid around 95 per person, plus 65 for wine pairing.  Personally i just get two spicy margaritas.

Highlights for me were the scallops, uni, beet and lamb dishes.  Of course with the guacamole and plantain tostada.

We will be back!

Just had dinner there with my husband.  Due to a cancellation, we were able to grab an early dinner reservation.  So glad we were able to check things out.  Good was awesome (we did pre fixe menu with pairing), service was impeccable (no surprise) and facilities were very clean.

All the Covid protocols we expected were adhered to, and we felt completely at ease eating indoors.

Highly recommend the mole, pairings and the dessert with the fried crisp, cheese, walnuts and compote/jelly.

We'll be back.

We came here to celebrate my husband's birthday, I have to say this is the most expensive Mexican food we've ever had. After 3 appetizers, we were still starving, but the last one,the duck taco was pretty good and there was a lot of meat for 2 ppl to share,and the sober was good too. Nice experience, and nice ppl.
Must say the atmosphere is great, the service was also very good. The cocktails were delicious and the duck was divine! Love this place

Especially fresh, palpably authentic. 

This place caught my eye when I discovered it was developed from acclaimed chefs Enrique Olvera (Pujol) and Daniela Soto-Innes (World's Best Female Chef 2019), and I was very impressed. You can tell these two chefs had a vision for this place, and it has been fulfilled.

From the interior design to the presentation of the food, the atmosphere is elegant but not to the point of pretentiousness. In fact, although it may seem quite modern, the decor and meals themselves reflect a sheer, genuine admiration for Mexican culture.

The food itself can be a bit pricey for the size of the portions, compensated however by the freshness of it all, as well as the flavors of each dish. 

I went here two times, one during brunch and the other during lunch - these were my favorite dishes:

Arctic Char Tostada (brunch): The freshness of the raw fish was boldy complemented by the acidity of the roe and lime as well as the unique tang of the salsa macha. Probably one of the more contemporary dishes, but the tostada was fye nonetheless.

Huevos Rancheros (brunch): A simple but perfect rendering of an iconic dish. The insanely fresh tortilla was the star of the dish.

Duck Carnitas: I regret not eating more of this. Cosme's duck carnitas gave me some of the best tacos I have ever had. The skin is crisp and the meat is fatty. The tortillas are always so mf fresh. This must be ordered every time you visit Cosme, such a dish demands proper attention. 

Honey Nut Tamal: The most unique dish I had here. It is a simple tamal, but the earthy and subtly spicy flavor of the Mayan ha'sikil pa'k (pumpkin seed salsa) with the saltiness of the castelrosso cheese is a very distinct combination. Order this one 

Corn Husk Meringue: The desert may have been the spotlight dish for both visits. I have never had any desert like this before. They managed to capture the essence of a corn husk into a cream and meringue, and it's amazing on a taste and texture basis.

This restaurant oozes a love for Mexican culture, and chef Soto-Innes has a very bright future. Definitely come give this place a try

Cosme is without out a doubt a restaurant worth visiting; from it's upscale ambiance, to its friendly staff, to its one of a kind dishes, this restaurant offers creative ways to present traditional Latin dishes. The only gripe I have with the restaurant is its prices. Ever since Chef Daniela gained traction as one of the best young chefs under 30, the restaurant has started to gouge its patrons like Disney World charging $10 hot dogs. Which I understand is well within their right, I mean they have bills to pay. However, paying $20 for a small portion of well seasoned mushed avocados "guacamole" seems a little excessive. I also paid about $50 for 4 Duck Carnitas, and while it was very delicious, you can not help but feel a little pain in your wallet. I finished my meal with the $14 Husk Meringue, and once again, it was magnificent. The perfect end to a very delicious culinary journey. 

Conclusion:
The restaurant itself warrants a visit, if you are not afraid of the price. The food offers authenticity, with creativity that you will not be able to find elsewhere. The drink menu was also creatively complementary to the ambiance and the delicious adventure ahead.
This place is great, duck was fantastic and the drink were too it's definitely a good Michelin Star and it deserves it but the Al Pastor could use more spice to it.

We'd just returned from a culinary trip to Mexico, so we had high expectations. That said, we were completely underwhelmed. We asked the waiter to recommend his 5 favorite dishes, which we figured would guarantee a memorable meal. But only one was interesting (a complex yellow mole w crispy sweet potatoes in a bowl with julienned vegetables). But plated dishes were small, expensive and only okay and one, the mole de casa for $34, was really bizarre, in taste, texture and even conception: a smear of chocolate mole on a plate with a small bowl of runny burata on the side. It was also odd that the $19 cocktails were served either overflowing with tiny ice balls or only 2/3 of the glass filled. Was it an off night? Possible. But the friends who'd recommended Cosme told us that another couple who'd gone recently had been similarly disappointed.

Was my favorite place for a couple years , the chef and Sous chef in the beginning used to hang w us customers at the bar towards end of night, very real and genuine ppl here, !! the creativity is what makes it special, your eating Mexican food through eyes of a 2 star Michelin team , they may have one star (not sure)but it's the approach to food that separates this place, only 4 stars because of the very casual feel  they purposely want

Very surprised by the low yelp ratings. Cosme had one of the best dishes I'd ever had. Chef Soto-Ines is a genius and glad she is a female minority as well. Although lacking a Michelin Star, I thought Cosme is more than deserving and doesn't have the required dress code of some of the three stars in NYC. 

I came here on a Saturday night with reservations made a few days before. Easy to get a good time on a Saturday night and we stuck with them even during the COVID-19 outbreak since they required a credit card deposit to make a reservation.

Onto the food! Corn grits were amazing. I don't like corn nor grits, but this was amazing. The tataki al pastor was decent. Came as a taco with homemade tortillas and the tortillas were the highlight of this dish. The black bass.... I need to take a moment to enjoy the memory... it was the best. The other dishes could have been dog food and with the black bass I'd still give Cosme 5 stars. Tender fish, flakey/crunchy edible scales, and amazing tortillas, the bass was to die for. Truly unique and by far the best seafood dish I ever had. The size was also good too. Since it's not a 13 course meal, I felt like i had enough time to fully enjoy this dish. 

In all, not a Michelin Star restaurant but deserves to be. Not a 13 or 16 course meal but each dish is enjoyed longer. Get the black bass or the other shareable dishes, the black bass was amazing and our neighbors duck looked amazing too.

I wanted to check out Cosme after having heard of Pujol while I was in Mexico. Also to dine at a restaurant by Daniela Soto Ines truly seemed like a treat. 

I was really impressed with the entire service, and especially the food. I had heard that the restaurant was a bit overrated prior to coming, which I completely disagree with. Each dish was elevated. We had the fluke toastada, artic char, crab infladita, mole de casa, and black bass for our main course.

Looking forward to coming back to trying the other items on the menu, and to visiting Alta!

The food went beyond my expectations, HOWEVER do not listen to the server when they tell you portions are too small for one person. A friend and I ended up sharing the corn omelet, a salad,the lamb (which was supposedly for 2 but felt like it was good for 4 people), and the cornhusk meringue and we were STUFFED. Would go back, but maybe order less!

Definitely need reservations and do not listen to the yelp reviews. Do yourself a favor, if you are a foodie of any sort, check out this place as it's home to the WORLD'S BEST FEMALE CHEF--HELLOOOOO?!?!  

Second time here and I was a fan the first time but super impressed the second time. Definitely a place for 4 (ish) people, so you can sample more of the menu. 

Came here visiting from LA on a girls trip and the food was on point. We ordered several small plates and some share plates and everything was delicious and the flavors carried throughout each dish from the garnish to the salsas/sauces. It was memorable from the first to last bite. Everyone left HAPPY! 

We ordered: 
Herb guac
Uni tostada (small, order one pp)
Crab infladito (small, order one pp or per two ppl)
Black trumpet volcan--personal favorite (order one pp or per two ppl) 
Broccoli tamal (least fave)
Black bass--best fish I've had (served 4 ladies)
Duck carnitas (served 4 ladies)

Dessert:
Corn husk meringue 
Mexican chocolate 

Order the coffee, it's absolutely delicious and so full or cinnamon flavor; I wish they were open for breakfast so I could have my morning coffee here!

Cosme is my go-to restaurant that I take all my family and friends to when they come to visit. I've been to Cosme many times for dinner, and they always impress. The host team is always welcoming and gracious. The bar team always attentive and fun. The floor was quick to refill our water glasses, replace silverware and plates, and made sure our table was clean between courses. The food is always amazing as per usual. We ordered the guacamole, razor clam tostada, and tataki al pastor to start. For our main course we ordered the butternut squash and the black bass. I'm not a huge seafood person, but everyone raves about the black bass so I had to try it; and I'm so glad I did! The bass was AMAZING. I would definitely recommend it, even to people who aren't seafood lovers like myself. Everything we ate was delicious. For dessert we had the husk meringue and acacia Mexican chocolate. Love it here.

We had an 830 reservation and they kept telling us that we were the next table and the wait should be a few more minutes. Fast forward to 915 they say we're still waiting on the table and give us a round of free drinks and chips/guac. The host assured us that the table would be ready soon and that the issue was the table sent something back before so they're taking extra long (not a good sign lol) and that the food will be well worth the wait. Finally, we get seated over an hour later at 935. 

We ordered a bunch of food and all of it was pretty average or less than average except the duck which was amazing but very expensive (looks like at some point they increased the price from like 59 to 95$). Overall if everything went well I'd say this place is fine and maybe worth a try but for the money I've been to a ton of better places in the area and Im not craving going back. After the whole wait experience I actually feel like telling others not to try. 

Overall, average or less than average considering the price. I guess the ambience is pretty cool but that doesn't do it when you're paying 100$ for an entree.

Read somewhere this restaurant was one of the top 50 places to eat, big disappointment and I still don't get where the chefs/writers gather to come up with these ridiculously ideas.
Plate dishes are small, extremely expensive and not even tasty at all.
This place is a total rip-off.
I feel pretty bad because my girlfriend and I were very eager to eat there, she treated me to this restaurant because we were celebrating my birthday, what a clumsy place. 
Will never go back again.

The food is good, the bartender was great, drinks were great, and service was beyond horrible from start to finish. For this price I expect more. It's getting an an additional star just due to the great and informative bartender.
Cosme honestly deserves more stars. My favorite dishes were the Uni tostada, duck carnitas, and the corn husk meringue. All so good and service was good also.
Brunch at Cosme was great, the drinks and plates were full of flavor. My favorites were the tostada, chilaquiles, and the corn husk meringue.

I had been looking forward to checking out Cosme after hearing great things, but unfortunately only found the experience just okay. The interiors feel a bit bachelor pad in my opinion and the service wasn't exceptionally friendly or helpful. The food was good and there were some interesting items on the menu.

I always tell people to come here! I feel like a promoter! From welcoming hostess', to the best mezcal margaritas, and 'artsy' crafted dishes!  This place is a must! Also the music in there is always great! From start to finish you can see they focus on being their own one of a kind. Which I love. Will forever be supporting this place. Great intimate date spot with upbeat vibes.

This place is horrendous I don't even know where to start. The worst place I have been to in New York City.  We walked in and we were greeted by the hostess and we decided to sit in the lounge seats. The menu was not clear and it looked very rushed as if it were typed in a Microsoft Word document. It took us a while to figure out the menu because everything was thrown together and not explaining the dish. We are not asking for much but it would have been better if they gave a brief, clear description of the dish. They just listed the ingredients and it didn't give us a sense of how the dish would be like so we didn't know what we were getting into. Not to mention, the dishes were very overpriced. The dishes served to us were in miniature portions. The waitress had mentioned to us that the dishes would be small. But she also described them in a positive way when we asked her for recommendations. At first she was friendly, but she was not very attentive. She rarely came to the lounge area, and it set the mood for the overall experience.

We got the razor clam tostada, which the waitress recommended. While the arrangement was nice, it had NO taste at all. But we were still willing to give them a chance because it was only the appetizer (even though the appetizer should not be that overpriced). Then came the yellow corn grits, which were awful. The waitress warned us how spicy it would be, but it was not spicy AT ALL. It was basically just corn with cheese, nothing to write home about.

But the major disappointment was the black bass. Everything about it was terrible, from the tortillas that came with it to the actual fish. The tortillas looked like Mission tortillas where you can get them for $5 at a local supermarket. The hoja santa looked as if they were just placed on top of the tortillas and tasted like Play-Doh. The presentation of the bass looked interesting, but when I tasted it, I asked myself, "$60 for a flavorless bass?!" I can't describe it any more than that because it was so flavorless. That was the last straw.

I admired the creativity of the place, but the execution of the dishes was horrible. Don't come to this place and waste your money. Look somewhere else if you want authentic Mexican food because this is definitely not it. It's overpriced "Mexican" fusion. I would know because I'm half Mexican.

Went here with a group of friends. We got the prawns tostada, chilaquiles, duck enmoladas, branzino, and lamb barbacao. Everything was quite tasty! The commonly instagrammed dessert from this place, husk meringue, failed to impress me, but maybe it's just me?
I was here with my girlfriend for our anniversary and we had a great experience. Don't leave without try their Mole, best mole I've ever had in my life.

When we first walked in the hostess was very gracious and attentive.  We waited at the bar for our table and had a very tasty margarita.  The bartenders were friendly and the manager was there taking drink orders as well.  When we were seated our waiter came right over to present us with our menus and explained to us what the dishes were and what he would recommend.   We ordered the Herb Guacamole, Fluke Tostada, Takati al pastor, pineapple, Duck carnitas & Corn husk meringue.  All dishes were amazing and played with your taste palette!  6 margaritas, apps, dinner, desert at the 23rd BEST RESTAURANT IN THE WORLD was a bargain.  Overall, a great experience! Thank you!

I have been to Cosme several times.  I had a booking for last evening for at 8:30pm and was hosting clients. I was running late and tried to call the restaurant to alert them to the delay.  I called 4 times but one one ever answered the phone.  When we finally arrived it was just at over the 15 minute grace period that the hostess was so readily to say was their seating policy.  I advised that I attempted to call to alert them of the delay and pointed to the phone that was on the podium.  I asked, was there any reason why no one was answering the phone or if their phones were not working.  I just received a shrug and a reply of 'I don't know'.  We were told we would have to wait 30 minutes for a table to open up.  We decided to wait at the bar.  We had 2 rounds of drinks and the manager came over to say it would still be longer but would not give a specific time.  We waited close to an hour before we were sat.  Whilst we were offered a round of drinks and seats at the communal table, I declined.  Being in the hospitality industry I have to say that Cosme has lots to work on in terms of customer service and training their staff.  If I were Enrique Olvera, I would be very concerned to have my name attached to a place that pales in comparison to delivering a great experience like Pujol does.  Once we sat, the food was amazing as always and the service fine.  I am going think twice to recommending this restaurant to anyone.

Innovative! I truly enjoyed my experience. Isaac was an excellent bartender. Great selection of wines and was given great recommendations with wine and food. The uni twas absolutely amazing. Blowfish dish also very nice. I had great service and great food. I can easily give 5 stars.

Back again. Tried a few different things and was not disappointed. Repeated the Guacamole and Uni tostada were a must and were amazing. Arctic char sashimi was light and flavorful. Black bass was a nice piece of fish and enough for me and my boo. 

I will be back again in the future. The 3.5 star rating  on Yelp is not accurate. Some people are just  haters. This is one of my favorite spots in NYC. Period stop.

Terrible value - $410 for two for a light dinner and 3 cocktails each.

Guacamole and the crab puff thing were ok.

Found a hair in the uni tostada, they offered to replace it, we said no (it wasn't really good), another was brought anyway.

Do not under any circumstances order the burrata and mole. One of the worst dishes I've ever eaten. Terrible way to finish the main meal. 

Desserts were really tasty.

The pricing of these dishes was just ludicrous. You can eat at restaurants with Michelin stars for less. This restaurant should be empty.

Beware of the reservation restrictions here. If you don't like what you see when you arrive you'll still be charged $$$$.
When our waiter described the menu as being mostly "small bites" he wasn't kidding. The fluke tostada arrived - it was an oval tortilla about 1 1/2 times the size of a dollar bill with a top coating thinner than a slice of American cheese....for $25.00. I knew we were in for ( expensive) trouble. 
 Of the things I would wave off.....A very tired Burrata came with an over sweetened mole for $34.00.
 We ate the Burrata but nobody at our table liked the mole enough to have more than a small taste. 
Lastly the Infladita ( small pastry filled with with a golfball sized bit of crabmeat) was pretty tasteless...for $32.00. A $16.00 1" pour of wine was the cheapest on the menu. I was glad to get a Mexican bottle of beer for $6.00. Best deal in the house!!!
   All in all, for $275.00 for three of us ( not including tip) it was like a light ladies lunch and I would plan on $150 with tip per person for a whole meal. Some of the flavors were okay but none of the ingredients were anything exotic, just standard fare. Very elegant setting. I think Cosme is best left to the well healed downtown denizens who have unlimited funds for a very light meal on a night out.
The food and service were  amazing from the cocktails to dessert. The attention to details and extraordinary flavors and textures. It was a blissful experience.

This is a prime example of the emperor's new clothes.  The lunch menu is expensive  and repetitive.    Small first courses of similarly sauced raw fish were overpriced and uninspired.  $24-30 very small plates with the same pink sauce were basically tasteless.   Sea buckthorn aqua chile ,
prawn tostada and tataki al pastor all were served cold.  We did not have the $61 berkshire pork chop or the $65 Dover sole!  Thought Dover Sole tacos  should be against the law!
They never did make me a good martini--after 3 tries.
Cold expresso..
Skip this place

This was a special occasion. I was all set for a great meal with my wife and my in-laws. I sat at the Bar for a pre-meal cocktail, and I asked the Bartender what the most popular cocktail is... please make me one. He looks at me as if I asked him to name his first born after me. He was so pretentious. The cocktail was OK... tasty, but mostly a large ice cube. The food way over-priced, with small portions.  I also ordered a $100 bottle of vino, which was obviously corked. I called over the sommelier and instead of comping me or replacing the bottle of wine, they poured a complementary glass for me, and still charged me for the bottle of wine.  Needless to say, I will not be back to this overrated establishment.

This restaurant is so sleek, sexy and soulful.  It's been around for ages and is still as exciting and relevant as ever.  The husk meringue is as good as ever, too. 

On a recent visit, we had the Arctic char aguachile, pork chop with flying ants (!!), Duck carnitas and cobia al pastor.  Each dish had clear-cut flavors and textures, thoughtful composition and perfect use of salt.  

The husk meringue dessert needs no introduction or comment.  Just get the damn thing.

There are restaurants that you just have to try. Cosme, I felt was one of those. Their acclaimed chef Enrique Olivera is part of that reason. 

I tried making a reservation at his Mexico City restaurant last time I was in town and was unable to, even 2 months in advance.

Luckily I got a table for New Year's Eve in  New York City. 

Walking in the ambience is dark, with a relatively minimalist mid century feel. We got seated in a corner table towards the back, which I appreciate. Sometimes it's nice to be away from all of the action. 

I soon realize that the clientele wasn't quite what I was expecting. It definitely seemed to be more hoity toity Latin people. Which is not our scene. 

Service was relatively slow and the tables pretty close to each other so eaves dropping was inevitable. 

We started off by ordering cocktails and eventually looked at the mezcal list. Our waitress recommended some really good mezcal.

We had their Cosme cocktail and "El Ninja" both tasty. 

For dinner we ordered the shared plates: 

-Yellow mole with squash. Surprisingly very filling. 
-Uni tostada with bone marrow. Was delicious, every bite very decadent
-Artic char aguachile. Small serving but the sauce surrounding this fish makes every bite count. 
-Black bass served on a green "mojo de ajo".  The scales were fried and sticking out they looked like rice (see picture). I've never seen this before nor eaten fried scales but it worked? 

All in all it was a neat experience and I'm glad we went. 

With that being said Cosme is definitely meant for wealthier Latin Americans coming to NYC for a fancy meal.  Something to tell their friends about. At least that was the vibe I got that night. 

Being Mexican American, Cosme was simply too modern for me. It's hard to wrap your head around ingredients you grew up with, which have deconstructed and reconstructed into something completely different. The brain just does not compute sometimes. 

I do appreciate the effort and time it takes to create the food. You can definitely sense the passion and their mission to elevate Mexican flavors. In this case I felt like I was eating art pieces rather than dining. The tortillas had beautiful dehydrated leaves on them for God's sake. I wanted to frame that thing not eat it.

My support for Mexican Chefs, art and culture is here to stay. Voy a seguir apoyando al Mexicano, pero al mismo tiempo dando mi crítica.

Perfect espresso. Usually volume and quality do not go hand in hand. But here, the espresso was plentiful and the flavor and caffeine was perfect. Very happy with Cosme's espresso. NYC dining is lacking in that department but here it is very satisfying .

Cosme has a really cool ambiance and overall solid food.  Some dishes were excellent, others a bit underwhelming.  Overall the food costs a bit more than it probably should given the portion sizes and quality, but it is mostly tasty.  The cocktails are fine, but not great for the price.  The husk meringue is among my favorite desserts in the entire city though and I sometimes visit the bar after a meal elsewhere just to get my fix of this wonderful creation.  That dessert alone takes this place from a 3.5 to a 4.

A pleasant surprise! At first glance of the menu, it was easy to assume the plates would be small and overpriced, but thankfully that was not the case. While portions were on the smaller side, four dishes were more than enough for two people. My personal favorites were the Crab Infladita and Tataki Al Pastor, and Yellow Corn Grits.

This restaurant is OFFENSIVELY expensive! Portions are tiny -- and not shareable, as the server suggested. My glass of wine was $25, and the server tried to upsell us at every turn, including when we said we didn't want dessert, and he proceeded to give us "customer favorites." Go to Union Square Cafe if you're in this neighborhood! It's better in every way!

Last night I had the most overpriced and underwhelming meal of my life at Cosme. My friend and I had three plates of one smaller plate and two larger plates at $30 each, with each plate consisting of one or two bites at the most. Not a single dish was anything to write home about--even the drink was extremely dull. I happily go to Michelin starred restaurants and have never batted an eye at the prices of meals that justify a few hundred dollars, as they usually do not leave one feeling completely hungry and unsatisfied. After spending an inexcusable amount here for those three plates and one drink, I immediately left Cosme and went directly next door to Sugarfish, where I had a full meal for the cost of one bite at Cosme and was finally happy. Never coming here again.
Absolutely terrible. Food was okay and it was highly overpriced. The service was horrible to begin with. Definitely not worth it at all.
Duck tacos - These are to die for and when paired with strong margaritas... it was a great night. Went there twice for a date and work dinner and we had a great time.

I've eaten at so many pricey establishments in NYC and never felt utterly ripped off before. Tonight at Cosme, I did. $234 before tax (4 small plates, 1 "large" plate, and two cocktails) and we left hungry! Walked over to get pizza. 

There were nonedible filler elements in most of our dishes - rocks and paper filled with stuffing - this is simply absurd. If you want to do a creative, artful playing, and the food quantity is minimal, there are ways to do this without adding fillers.

Service was mediocre for the price, too.

Never going back.

I cannot begin to convey the disappointment at the cookie cutter decor, gravely over-inflated prices, mediocre food, lackadaisical service.

There are too few redeeming qualities to this place at even half the price. But at the price we paid, we felt utterly ripped off.

This has been on my list for years. My wife took me for my birthday. Special occasion prices... We loved the food, and the restaurant is beautiful. We had just 1 quibble about the service. It was very fast for the first half of the meal. We ordered a bunch of small plates. They came and went in a blur, although I must say each dish was memorable in flavor and incredible presentation. Next we shared the duck. This is quite a large dish, and the pace of the meal slowed so we could take in the experience better. We noticed that the vibe in the dining room was quite relaxed. All the guests seemed to be casually enjoying a midweek meal out. Guess that's Manhattan for you. If I had an infinite dining budget it would probably be my regular neighborhood spot too.

Service and decor were outstanding however the restaurant is substantially overpriced.  Not a good value at all.  I was hesitant to leave a negative review however I am in need of a receipt from them.  I tried calling countless times to no avail.  In addition, I have sent several emails to three different email addresses listed on their website and have not heard back.  This is unacceptable.  I would have gotten more value and certainly a response had I gone to a local diner ?????????

So, here is the story on Cosme. Went last night and very unimpressed with the menu.
All snack style food and $$$$.
Extremely limited menu, have seen lager selection at a simple bar.
In our case we had to order doubles on certain items.
Closing statement, you may be forced to grab a slice on your way home.

I had originally visited Cosme back when it initially opened in 2014 or so but never found the time to write a review. I decided an update trip was necessary to see if Cosme still lived up to its mythology in my head and, let me assure you after my visit last night, I'm convinced Cosme is one of the best restaurants in the city at this moment.  

If you're expecting this to be a Mexican restaurant serving Mexican food with which you're familiar, you're going to be disappointed. I get the feeling this is authentic, native Mexican food (or a twist on the same) and you're not going to readily familiar Mexican flavor combinations.  They very point of Cosme seems to be opening your eyes to what Mexican food really can (should?) be.  And if you're confused or scared by unknown words on the menu, maybe fine dining as a learning experience isn't for you.

As to the experience itself, I do sense a bit of a coolness coming from the hosts, as mentioned in other reviews, but not enough to have it impact my experience.  The hosts were obligatorily pleasant with me, took our coats and bags to check, and promptly lead us to our table which was in a quieter corner near the back (perfect for the fluctuating volume level as the crowd grows as the night wears on).  We were immediately provided with water of our choice (sparkling, the bottle for which was left on the table and denoted with a black rubber band at the bottom to signal to service staff that it was in fact carbonated) and walked through the menu as to about how much food to order (two from the first group, one/two from the second group, and share something from the third is my rec unless you're starving) and what the favorites were.
  
I'm one of those people who comes in knowing what I'm going to order for every course and Cosme was no exception (As a server, I would also suggest newer items, or experimental items on the menu, if any, as I would always order the same things each time I came without more convincing).  Starting the meal with the guacamole, one might be stunned at the $19 price, but the flavor made it absolutely worth it.  Taking on qualities reminiscent of Schrödinger's Guacamole, the guac seemed to take on any flavor profile you focused on for any given second. The delicate spice allowed the smokey, spicy, cayenne (or a similar, but light, spice) notes to come through but the longer you focused on the taste you started going down roads of citrus and fruit, reminding you why mango salsas are a thing.  Topped with herbaceous delights ranging from cilantro to what seemed like dill to some kind of spring onion flower(?) gave this guac (served with homemade blue corn tostadas) a multitude of flavor dimensions lacking in its competition.  

The uni tostada was equally fantastic and surpassed my prior memory of the dish. Be sure to spritz liberally with the lime that accompanies it, which provides a necessary cut against the inherent fishiness of most uni.  The fresh simplicity of this dish was a delight, leaving a clear, crisp taste on the palate, priming me for the decadent duck carnitas.  As someone who has a bias towards uni, I wholeheartedly recommend this dish to anyone looking for a reason to love it.  The only draw back is that a single, crunchy tostada can cause some challenge to sharing the dish, but it cut surprisingly well and even down the middle.

The tataki al pastor was the only dish I had not had in the past and it was equally as amazing as the rest (though I forgot to eat it with the delicious homemade corn tortillas until my last few bites).  If you're a fan of the sweet complex flavor of al pastor tacos, you will love this take.  Spiced with ginger, vinegar, and citrus, the tuna(?) provided the perfect vehicle for the inimitable pineapple puree, which convinced me I had never ACTUALLY tasted pineapple before that moment. Should you order the tataki, take a taste of that puree on its own.  Your eyes will be opened.

The duck carnitas were as fantastic as my memory suggested.  Pull apart tender with the rich, umami fattiness of the duck skin, cut by the fresh, lightly pickled(?) onions and radishes, stuffing the duck into the homemade corn tortillas and topping with your choice of the bright orange habanero salsa or the cooler verde option is a once in a lifetime, taco-based experience.  Do your best to eat the whole thing; there isn't a bone in sight.  

The corn husk meringue dessert hardly needs an explanation.  Earthy. Sweet. Crisp. Creamy. The dessert marries sweetness and earthiness in a way only sweet corn can, with a touch of expert technique the creates a one of a kind dessert that deserves all the praise it has received.  

Thank you to our outstanding server, Elizabeth, Christian, Isabel, and the rest of the staff for a truly terrific experience.  Cosme, through its care, focus, and discipline, conjured yet another unforgettable experience that will leave me (and my guest) talking about it for years to come.

The most amazing experience for taste, texture and cocktail delight. Although the bar menu is different than than dining room menu, I just experienced the most amazing culinary meal ever! The combinations of flavors, the authentic ingredients and the warm relaxing environment make this 5 stars!!  Love this place! Small plates, but worth every bite! Take it slow! Parker at the bar was a great guide to the culinary and beverage treasures that are offered. Thanks for another amazing dining experience.

Honestly?  Meh!  I had heard so much hype for this restaurant and it didn't live up to the word of mouth.  It definitely wasn't bad, but it wasn't anything to write home about with the exception being the corn husk meringue.  That dessert is everything everyone says it is and more...a must do for sure!  Everything we got food was was good, not great, and not worth the prices.  Maybe next time, I'll skip the meal and go straight for the dessert!

I don't understand how this restaurant is rated so well. We started with an okay guacamole on a big stale corn chip. We then had low grade salmon in a tart orange sauce (which we didn't order, but was comped when we pointed that out) that was like a child's experiment gone wrong. The next few dishes were very bland. The crab infladita and duck carnitas were nice, but woefully small for the price point. Somehow, we spent 150 each and I'm still hungry. Don't believe the hype; you can do so much better.

Cosme hits all the home runs and then some. Foos is of course, unparalleled. But the atmosphere and the character of the staff is every bit as delectable. Ambiance is so cozy that I felt I was eating in my Grandmother's house back when I was child.

Turrible.

Honestly below average, would have rather gone anywhere else.... like anywhere.

Had guacamole- painfully lemony, crab appetizer - literally awful, tataki al pastor - average at best, black bass - basic boring fish, also painfully lemony. $19 average overly-lemony cocktails. 

Total joke. Lemony joke.

I was in town for a few days and a friend recommended this restaurant. I'm so glad I made a reservation! The food was delicious and the service was impecable. Alfredo took care of us, making sure to check in on us and made great recommendations. I would definitely return!

Cosme is still a great restaurant. The service is great, the ambiance is coz, modern and comfortable. We had a beautiful, if tiny, ceviche and a stuffed poblano to begin with. Then we went onto the duck carnitas and the squash. The duck is a never fail here and the squash has a delicious sauce which was a pleasant surprise. We ended the meal with the corn husk merengue, which we used to love, but somehow doesn't taste the same anymore. We also had the chocolate desert which was so clearly the high point we were looking to end the meal with.  I'd definitely keep going back for more.

Highly recommend if you are on an expense account or someone else is treating. The food and drinks were fabulous.  For example, we had the Tataki al Pastor. It was about 2 ounces of fish with pineapple butter on the side (my new favorite condiment!). We loved it, but at $30 for an appetizer - not sure we'll be back. The free samples at Wagamama that we passed on the way to the restaurant were larger! Also, an "A" for service. We had the Honeynut Squash which is kind of a play on satay with fried squash and avocado. It came with shiso embedded tortillas; when I mentioned to our server that the shiso had no flavor, he promptly brought fresh leaves! While the portions were small, they were very filling and delicious.

I enjoyed my experience at Cosme. My friend and I snuck a table at the front after going to an improv show. The margaritas were to die for... I would definitely go back for drinks with someone who is visiting. For food, we started with the guac which was tangy with thick chunks of avocado throughout. For the meal we got the pork chop and the cheese corn. The food was good but portions were really small. I was definitely hungry after the meal and it even said "pork chop for two", so that was disappointing. If I were to go back it'd be for apps and margaritas - leave it at that!

I might not be fancy enough for these types of places but for a ~$350 meal for 3 people, I thought I would be more full. Portions are small and I was pretty much looking under the tortilla to see if there was any other food in the dish. Service was okay; it took a long time to get a drink order taken but rest of dishes came out fast. I did love the ~chic~ atmosphere though.

This place is a 100% overrated, yeah I get it Enrique Olvera is a big name, but they should treat customers better. We decided to give it a try on a Saturday night, we were seated right away (amazing!!) we started taking a look at the menu and realized it's a simple menu, nothing incredible about it and average dishes (like in any other upscale mexican restaurant) then after about 30 minutes someone decided to come and take our beverages order, my husband asked for a cider and the person was rude enough to say they have an apple cider but it's $84 and he doesn't think we can afford it, like really? We asked for the menu and no explanations were given. Finally we decided to get 2 plates each, honestly best thing was the tostadas and the sauce they give you at the beginning. It's sad to see how a Mexican restaurant turns out to have missing service and lack of flavor. If you are Mexican don't spend your money here, not worth it! Better Mexican places out there without the necessity of feeling denigrated when servers don't think you can afford a meal there! 
The stars are for the hostess who sat us right away when we got late for our reservation!

Updating original review to reflect the EXCELLENT Duck Carnitas and a much better Uni Tostada the second time around.

Mushroom tacos were delicious.

The husk merengue is sooo good (and I'm not even a dessert person).

Really good mezcal and tequila selection and great whiskeys as well - definitely lacking in the vodka department.

Overall, I will definitely give them another shot.

I'm honestly not sure how this restaurant is a top 50 because we walked away underwhelmed after a $550 dinner for 4 (and still a little hungry!)

None of the dishes really blew us away except maybe the corn meringue dessert and the corn grits. The trumpet mushroom dish was pretty good but small (although the waiter had warned us about this, so that was helpful.) Everything  else was rather forgettable, unfortunately.

I will say the cocktails are delicious though! If you really wanna check it out, come for the drinks and the dessert, but don't have high expectations for the food. 

Also, we got seated a little after 10 pm for our 9:30 reservation.

Cosme is surprising and finally a Mexican food place which is different and innovative. Not your usual one around the corner. It's worth traveling for. Bet to go with at least 4 persons so you can share and try different dishes. And the deco is lofty, yet cool.

The food here is weird. The flavors are bad. Seems like they are trying way to hard to be innovative with their dishes - I would have rather gone to McDonalds, because at least I know it would have tasted good. 

It's expensive and I left hungry. Don't bother

LOL- I wrote a review highlighting how terrible my food and experience was at cosme and the restaurant had it removed!! No wonder there are so many positive reviews here because they ween out the ones that show the true colors of this place.

It was fucking delicious. If people left bad reviews it's probably because they haven't actually tasted home cooked Mexican food and are comparing it to the super salted, greasy burrito they're used to having as "Mexican" food. Incredible, simple ingredients and wouldn't think the best Mexican food I've had was in NY. And yes it's pricey but what are you expecting???

Someone needs an eye patch, and it ain't Pirate Depp. At Cosme, someone's eye has fallen so far off the ball that I doubt they'll ever be able to retrieve it...

Lukewarm, burnt, greasy, salty lamb tacos--two tiny ones for $26. I could barely swallow one and sent the dish back, but was still charged half price for it because they had "never heard a complaint like that before". Imagine such a response!...I love mole. I have had it in all the best places, including Oaxaca, but never have I had it served ice cold. I don't know if this was intended or an oversight by the kitchen, but I didn't dare ask after the response to my prior critique. Nice flavors, but, sorry, I don't care for cold mole ($34!!?)...The guacamole ($19) was good, as were the tostados and tortillas, both beautifully made with great texture and grit. But when I am paying close to $200 (OMG!!) for a casual dinner, I expect more than just the guac and chips, and tortillas to be on point...

And, silly me, when I was asked at the end of the "meal" "How about a little more wine?" (I had had two glasses), I expected a free pour for all of the aggravation and expense. Silly me indeed!

Until they retrieve that eye and put it back on the ball, Cosme will remain a cosmic rip-off.
Love their food. Don't bring your little one they don't have high chair and no kids menu. It is crazy that all each menu they have is so good. You can stay, drink and eat like forever...

We got the recommendation for this restaurant from eater's most romantic restaurants in nyc.  Eaters top picks are always amazing and this was no exception, but im surprised this made the romantic list. It is dark and secluded but a little too loud  to be romantic 

The food snd cocktails were amazing. The duck carnitas and the taktaki al pastor were two of the best dishes i have ever tasted. 

Our waiter Aaron was perfect, the only gringo working here by the way! He Suggested house specialties, attentive and friendly.  

But i wanna make sure that you know the food is really fantastic and very fast service!

Maybe can look a little expensive but it really fit in the prices!

Is not authentic mexican food, just to make sure, is Mexican food in a high level

I was in a bad mood when i got here and the food and service turned my mood around. 

Ended up being a perfect evening for two. 

I guess it was the romantic evening i needed after all.

Would much rather give this place a five star but I have to be honest. This should not be rated a top 50 period. The al pastor was mediocre to say the least. The cheese mushroom taco was nice but also not impressive. Bokchoy was interesting but once again just not memorable. Duck was amazing and just like everyone else said worth it to come just for that. The Marange was nice and definitely different!! Would not come back when there are way better Mexican restaurants (such as Atla)

(Drinks are really good though)

Cosme is an upscale dining spot featuring  Mexican inspired cuisine that showcases the culinary creativity of chefs Enrique Olvera and Daniela Soto-Innes.

Since my stay in NYC was a short one, I wanted to pack as many meals into an evening as I could, so we ordered "light". The crab infladita certainly qualified as a light dish, coming in the form of a puffed shell filled with chilled fresh crab mixed with avocado and a slight spicy nudge from the morita.

Next was the burrata with the house mole, listed as a main entree. And for good reason, as it consisted of a gigantic portion of burrata surrounded by a light shallow pool of sauce made from quelites.

Accompanied with it was a plate of dark aromatic mole and a helping of small warm corn tortillas.

The burrata tasted fine, although I personally prefer a creamier texture than the one provided. The quelites added a nice vegetal contrast. The mole when eaten alone was slightly smoky, had a nice soft and smooth texture, and a muted umami flavor.

However, when the burrata, quelites, and mole are eaten together, the flavors explode! The mole's texture changed to a thicker and pastier consistency, spreading it across your palate and magnifying the flavors of all ingredients that went into the mole, from the mild savory heat of the chilies, the spices, the sweetness, to the nutty earthiness. Sensational culinary alchemy!

Next came the duck caritas meant to be shared for two. A generous mound of pre-pulled boneless duck meat came topped with onions, radishes, and cilantro. Again, warm corn tortillas were provided. Wrapping a bit of the meat, a piece of the unctuous fatty skin, some garnishes, and a drizzle of one of two sauces provided made for a happy marriage of complementary flavors.

Finally for dessert came the popular corn husk meringue filled with a mild sweet corn cream. The light and delicate meringue was perfect with a hint of the corn husk powder tweaking the taste buds. A scattering of salt crystals added a nice contrast to the sweetness of the cream and the meringue itself, resulting in a very satisfying close to the meal.
Don't waste your time. Long wait even if you have a reservation. The food is decent, not great, and the wait staff is really unorganized.

High end Mexican food that does not disappoint. I was excited to try Cosme and made a reservation a week or so in advance (necessary). The restaurant is spacious with high ceilings and a subdued atmosphere for a calm, lovely dinner. We ordered the guacamole, crab in mole sauce, and the famous husk meringue with corn mousse for dessert. The dishes were, as everyone else seems to be saying, surprisingly small for the price. However, it was clear the dishes used the highest quality of ingredients. The guacamole was delicious and complimented by two large black chips. The chips had an almost burnt flavor that was the perfect accompaniment to the sharper guac. The mole with the crab was also wildly flavorful, and we were told takes hours to make and develop the full flavor profile. Surprisingly, the most disappointing part of the meal was the dessert, which was too sweet for me or my dining partner. 
Overall, the food was delicious, but if you want to be satisfied by the meal, I would recommend ordering at least two dishes each (which can be quite expensive!).

I came here wanting to enjoy some wonderfully prepared food, this in fact was not.

Think of basic Mexican, as one of the finest foods in the World, and Imagine if you wanted to do it upscale. You might bring a chef from Mexico City, or Oaxaca, use the best Pork, Beef, Camarones, etc., and then augment it with authentic salsas, and occasional preparations like a Pig Roast, a Lamb Roast, or Chile Relleno en Nogada... 

Instead, they got some guy, probably from Orlando or New Jersey, pretending to know what he's doing...

Mediocre bottled tasting Salsas, corporate culture cocktails, and poorly conceived abominations such as Razor clam tostada, salsa macha, peanuts, Fluke tostada, blue corn aioli, Tomatoes, chamoy, sunflowers, or Green mole, bok choy, cucumber will surely disappoint.

Think Chi Chi's meets PF Changs and you're here.

I wanted to like the food, the pretty designs and ambiance have all the charms of a Vegas-themed show restaurant... sadly the food is awful, ill-prepared, and out of context. The space will turn over soon, and perhaps something better will replace it in our neighborhood. 

Sad But True...

I'm heading to Mexico City next year for vacation and my first priority in trip planning is always researching restaurants. Enrique Olvera's Pujol consistently appears on the greatest hits lists, so I decided to try out his acclaimed Cosme in Flatiron this past Saturday night.

The restaurant is sleek and gorgeous, with overflowing plants and cacti being a strong decorative statement. Dark, moody, contemporary, and meticulously outfitted with chic tchotchkes, I delighted in my environs. The service was another strong point, with our waitress eagerly describing many of the dishes, all hands helping clear the table, and expedient mezcal margarita refills. Additionally, all of the plating was beautiful, with tiny edible flowers, and carefully placed adornments.

Unfortunately, the food did not measure up to the setting and service. My main complaint was the soft and muted flavors in each dish. The guacamole lacked sourness and acidity, the salsa lacked spiciness, the razor clam tostada, while beautifully plated, was overly simplified. The duck carnitas was delicious, but the duck was prepared in a very straightforward way, with minimal spices. I appreciated the flavor of the perfectly cooked duck itself, but I felt that I could replicate this in my own kitchen at home.

My other complaint is the value. There are no prices on the website, but you can expect to pay around $30 per appetizer. While this may seem a little high for a seafood app, it becomes glaringly high for many of the vegetarian appetizers. Even for a prime locale like Flatiron, this pricing is fairly exorbitant compared to the portion size and pricing at other Manhattan restaurants. I hope that Pujol lives up to my expectations when I visit Mexico City next year, but based on Cosme, I may have to temper them quite a bit.

The positive: food is phenomenal - we went for brunch.  The chilaqueles, corn omelette, lamb barbacoa, Pan dulce, meringue with corn purée, churros - all of it was so dreamy.  It took me back to dining in Mexico.  The negative: the service is atrocious.  What a let down.  Our server was beyond inattentive.  What should have been a 2 hour meal stretched beyond 3.  It was next to impossible to get refills of drinks, despite multiple requests for more coffee/tea.  When the coffee/tea finally arrived, we had to repeat requests for more milk for said beverages.  The silverware was removed between courses but not replaced.  Questions about the menu were responded to monosyllabically.  ALL of the diners in our section were visibly frustrated at various points in their meals.  The manager (floor captain?) was no help, either.  It's disappointing that a restaurant of this caliber is let down by the service - the food shines so brightly.  Maybe dinner is better?  Hard to say.  We'll give it another try and hope for the best.

Great vibe and friendly service at this high-end Mexican. It is quite pricey, but I would go back and order the green chilaquiles and spicy margarita, both great. Bar stools are the highest I have ever seen, so don't plan to sit at bar if you have mobility issues.

Ordered and shared the prawn tostada, lamb barbacoa, and the lobster, black bean, and chorizo for lunch today. They were delicious! My favorite was the cold dish, the prawn tostada, crispy, flavorful, and refreshing. The corn mousse with meringue husk was clever in it's appearance and just the right amount of sweet.

I have no problem paying $500 per person and eating small portions if it is good.  The service was bad we waited at least 1/2 hour between one of our courses. The waiter did not explain the dishes well. The burrata was tough and did not have much flavor. The Cobia tataki with pineapple  was overpowered by the tortilla because there was hardly any fish just a few bites. The grits were fairly tasty but not fantastic and such a tiny amount it stood out as absurd. I just felt this was a case of the Emperor's new clothes, food styling with out much substance behind it and overpriced to the point that that you felt taken advantage of.

BIG Ripoff! Avoid this stupid place. Super cool venue. Nice room. Good music.  The food is ridukously over priced. $25 for a "tomato salad (aka a bunch of small tomatoes). We spent a lot of money last night and left just as hungry as when we left. We ordered guacamole. It was so small we could have ate three orders. Ridiculous place.

The duck was good but everything else we tried on the menu are overrated. I think us included people came here with high expectations for the marketing it did as "No.1 Chef in America" obviously no one can claim that.
Hands down my favorite restaurant in New York. Can't go wrong with anything you order. The bartenders are great and make an amazing spicy margarita. Stick around for dessert too

I would want to give this place 3.5 stars. I came in knowing that this place was going to be pricey, but at these price points, i would think it would be mind blowing. 

The three dishes we ordered that weren't meant for two were subpar:
Fluke tostada with blue corn aioli: tasteless fish presented nicely on a chip that also didn't taste of much
Arctic char with sea buckthorn aguachile: this whole dish was completely lost on me. There was a very tangy sauce poured over some sliced bland fish. 
Crab infladita: crab meat in a chip. This was ok but really not much meat. Not too flavorful either. 

Before I give up, the black bass with mojo de ajo (to share) was awesome - they cooked this perfectly and it was filleted. I also don't know how they did it but the scales standing up on the fish requires a lot of technique and was delicious. The mojo sauce went really well with the dish too. And they provide soft flour tortillas to eat the fish with. 

We had to order the much raved about dessert: husk meringue with corn mousse. This was delicious- not too sweet and nice hint of corn.

Totally on Trend.  The Mole was served cold which was 
Weird, but very flavorful.  Cocktails on point. The meringue dessert are what dreams are made of.

I usually prefer simple fare but this restaurant was exceptional- not only in its beautiful and artistic presentation of dishes but absolutely delicious  
Will definitely be going back for the brunch - 
Recommend the duck and the crab - corn husk dessert and a cocktail w ginger - can't remember the name - it was great !

Made a reservation here because I heard it was something special.  It well deservingly appears on the worlds 50 best restaurants.

Reservations were made about a week and a half in advance.  The prime dinner times were booked but we still managed to snare something later in the evening.  

The restaurant is on the louder side, although casual conversation is still possible.  The two tops are close to the other tables so sometimes you can hear someone else's conversation.

Portion size is small.  Expect to have one main dish and 2-3 appetizers per person.  Highlights of the meal for us were the crab infladita.  The crab was super fresh and tasty.  The Tataki al pastor with the pineapple puree was sweet and savory all at once.  We enjoyed the duck carnitas.  The duck was juicy and the fixings were nice.  

Highlight was the dessert.  The serve a corn mousse that is amazing.  Smooth vanilla taste with a strong corn flavor.  The chocolate mousse was good, really good actually, but if you have to pick one dessert go with the corn mouse.

Overall, we loved this place.  its on the pricey side but the dishes were tasty and unique.  If you're in NYC its a must try.

Food is awesome but waitress is horrible they need lots of training 
Very disorganized

Rounding down from 3.5 stars. Quite disappointing as I loved Pujol so much, and was going as a very special occasion. I marked the res as such and nothing was done to reflect that, so not sure why there is availability to mark it. 

Despite excellent quick service and beautiful atmosphere, stuffing oneself with tortillas (even very good ones!) doesn't make a balanced meal. Cocktails were a highlight--we ordered El Ninja and Gin and Scrub (strawberry). Very good, $19 apiece but this is common for NYC. The portions were overall pitifully small, and you can get much better quality food in quantity and flavor innovation elsewhere in the city. Pictured is the tataki, five tiny pieces of fish served with five tortillas (yes, one sliver each)--though the pineapple sauce was great. Mole wasn't as good as Pujol. I wasn't surprised or wowed by anything amongst the four things we shared (overly sweet and salty corn husk meringue, lackluster burrata and mole, plain chanterelle tostada, tataki). The kind couple at the next table offered a bite of their $98/for two duck carnitas and it was pretty dry. we did walk away with a $180 bill for two people and a stomachful of 9 tortillas each though. It's a menu I wouldn't return for.

Cosme has been on my list to try for a bit, so we gave it a shot. Overall, it was a good experience with very good food.  Just pricey....  ordering tapas style as suggested - two people, four dishes and the duck, one cocktail each - it was almost $300 before tip. While we didn't have a bad experience, we probably wouldn't go again for dinner - it just felt incredibly overpriced for tapas. Drinks after work, definitely.

Vibe when you walk in is very cool and very much young New York. Music is loud, lights are dim and it just feels like a good spot to have a cocktail or two after work.
As we walked back towards the restaurant area, we were immediately greeted and welcomed; checked in and seated within a couple minutes. 

We had a table for two and at the back of the restaurant. Tables are a good size (unlike some tiny tables at popular restaurants), but they are close together. Be friendly!

Service was excellent - friendly, open, and happy to answer questions or make suggestions. Very attentive from cleaning plates away to filling water glasses. 

Food - server lets you know these are small portions and you should order three per person, exception being the duck which is equal to two.

We started with the herb guacamole $19 - it was good, not great. 

We ordered the crab $32, server suggested we try two - this was disappointing. While perfectly baked (pastry shell), it didn't have good flavor. Not bad, just not good and $32 each.

Then we had the Tataki al pastor $30 - ten slices of tuna sushi with delicious pineapple purée served al pastor. This was great.

Last we had the duck carnitas $98 - we were told this is the best on the menu. It was! Great taste and a good quantity of food. Really, really good.

Cocktails we had were El Ninja (really good) and Striptease (good) and they were low $20s.

Finally made it to Cosme. I'd seen the Chef's Table episode with Enrique Olvera. The focus was primarily on Pujol in Mexico City - one of the top restaurants in the world. However, given I wasn't going to be in Mexico City anytime soon His Mew York restaurant Cosme seemed like a worthy alternative to try his upscale Mexican cuisine. The restaurant is pretty and has a good beat playing. The bar stools are oddly huge and heavy and while I felt like I was sitting in a high chair - I got over it. The drinks were special - Paloma, Margerita were simple and delicious. If you want to try something with mezcal - there is a lot - but if you don't like smokey then don't get it.

Service was friendly although not as informed as I'd like but still good and attentive. The food was great:
- Arctic char, sea buckthorn aguachile, turmeric (tasty)
- Chanterelle volcán, cordyceps, quesillo, NY cheddar (good)
- Green mole, bok choy, cucumber (awesome and the soft tortillas that accompany it were fantastic) 
- Duck Carnitas - as advertised these were brilliant. So tender and rich and fatty delicious. It was perfect and the tortillas were plenty - in fact perfectly balanced as the last tortilla literally lined up with the last bite. That said we ordered more to sop up the fat...

Husk meringue, corn mousse - SO good - I don't know how to describe it but it was delicious 

Acacia, Mexican chocolate- very good but husk was better 

This meal was also pretty expensive so while I really loved much of what I ate at Cosme, and I'll be back, it's not somewhere I'd frequent simply because of the price. ...but it was goooood!

This place is good. Nice place, modern, like the music. 
The service was good, they take a little extra time to bring us the food but also give us some extra plates from house and that was nice.

Came to Cosme with 2 other friends and the food was wonderful... We ordered a lot of food thinking the serving would be so small, but we were so full at the end! The duck was my favorite and I absolutely would come back again for special occasions because it's towards the pricey side. The ambience is great too, you can bring your date for a special night and you will not be disappointed with the food and the service!

I picked this place as a special occasion dinner for a double date with friends who were visiting from out of town. As Cosme is ranked on the list of world's 50 best restaurants, we all had high expectations for dinner. 
Though we were 15 minutes late for our reservation, the staff were accommodating and seated us immediately. They brought us water and menus right after we were seated, and gave us ample time to order drinks and food. 
They recommended 2 dishes per person, so we decided on ordering 7: guacamole, crab infladita, taco al pastor, razor clam tostada, mole and their signature, the duck carnitas. 
The guacamole, crab infladita, al pastor tacos and the clam tostada were presented first as appetizers. The guacamole was good, but I couldn't distinguish between Cosme's high end guacamole and a cheaper version. The razor clam tostada was fresh, with an interesting sauce. My favorites of the starter dishes were the al pastor tacos with a pineapple sauce, that we wrapped ourselves, and the crab infladita. The crab infladita consisted of a shell pastry with crab and a spicy sauce on the interior. 
I'd heard great things about the duck carnitas, so we ordered that along with the mole. The mole was about $30, and I hadn't realised at the time of ordering, that it was a sauce and nothing else. I didn't see the value at all in paying $30 for sauce, and would not recommend ordering this at all. 
As their signature dish, we all had high hopes for the carnitas. When it arrived, we all dug in eagerly. Consensus was that it was good, but we all also thought the appetizers were better than the mains. 
Service was friendly, we didn't have any complaints in this department. 
The ambience here is modern, trendy and understated. 
Based on this experience, I don't feel the need to dine here again, but would recommend to others for an upscale Mexican dinner.

Came here for brunch and we were so impressed! The red chilaquiles was smoky, spicy and fresh with so many layers of flavors. I also ordered a take out for my friend. And they aced the packing game - the chips, sauce, herbs, pickled onions and egg yolk were all packed in different containers so that the chips wouldn't get soggy and when we had it later it was as good as in the restaurant!

The duck enmoladas was less a wow but decent. The husk meringue was rightfully the star of the meal! It was heavenly, even transcendental. A plate of pure happiness, sweet with vanilla and corn. The cream and meringue created a great combination of texture. From now on, I will come back every time when I'm in New York for this!
Great place, great vibes, absolutely amazing food, exploading tastes, wonderful, patient and kind service!

Good food , small portions and loud music. Not a place to go with friends for good conversation over a tasty meal. 

Waiters are a bit inpatient if you don't order quickly and order lots of different dishes...we felt a bit uncomfortable with this.
I was very impressed with the flavors and presentation of food though. Everything we had was delicious.
If you are hungry (and we were) be prepared to spend lots of money. One brest of duck (for the "duck carnitas") is US$98 but it serves 2 easily, if you order more dishes.
Great atmosphere, food, service, cocktails, and desserts are amazing! We enjoyed it a whole lot, and feel so proud of the entire staff, hard working and in communion!

Don't go here if you are actually hungry. Only go here if you've already eaten a meal (or two). Portions bite size with entree prices. I understand it is trying to be an "upscale" Mexican restaurant but the food is not even that good considering how expensive it is. I expected to be wowed and certainly was not.

Not impressed at all. Made reservation for a birthday dinner a few weeks ago but had to change a day before to add another person. The restaurant requires you to call them but i was told (when i got there) that their phone doesn't work. They sat us at the communal table, we can't even hear each other. Food was average, not worth the price. I won't be going back again.

very nice place to go before a night out. prettt pricy but most of the food is worth it. Service was very good and the vibe was amazing. Would definitely get the duck carnitas and the al pastor tataki
Three courses thrown down in front of us at once rather than being able to enjoy our meal. Terrible service.

We first heard of this restaurant while watching an episode of Chef's Table. My husband and I are big foodies, so we love to check out unusual experiences, and we very much looked forward to this. We made a reservation far ahead of time for my husband's birthday. Walking in, the ambiance was quite nice. The decor is modern and looks very cool. We were seated right away. One thing we noticed quickly is that the tables are on the longer/larger side, so with it just being the two of us, we were a bit far apart. I think this is why other reviewers felt it was loud- it's not that the music is excessively loud, but in order to speak to each other, we had to speak louder than we normally would since we were far apart. I was much closer to the people at the table next to us than I was with my husband. Also, our server had a very quiet voice, and it was generally really hard to hear her. One of the things we love about restaurants like this is the experience they give, but this fell short. For instance, at one of our favorite restaurants in the city (where we usually run up a similarly high bill), part of the experience is how the wait staff explain the menu and really sell it to you. We didn't have that experience here. We (and the other tables around us) got a generic explanation of one item from each section, then the waitress later asked if we had any questions. Well, it is a complex menu, so of course, we did. One of the things I noticed is there wasn't any excitement about it. In some places, when the menu has a lot of unfamiliar items or ingredients, the staff will ask you what sort of things you like to eat and make some recommendations, but that was not the case here. It was more like we'd ask a question, we'd get an answer, then she left while we decided. We ordered 2 items from each of the 3 menu sections. 

The food was delicious. The guacamole was fresh and herbaceous, different from other places in that it did not have a mushy texture. The crab infladita was delicious, but very difficult to eat.
