It falls apart as you cut into it, and it is served in a dish with very small crevices. We had to put it on another plate so we didn't lose pieces of it. The tataki al pastor was delicious and very unusual. The pineapple puree that came with it was particularly memorable. The chanterelle volcan was delicious, but again, difficult to eat the way that it was presented. However, it was worth it. The mole was soulful and complex, but the presentation was a bit off. It was served with burrata and tortillas, which were good, but if you are hungry, this dish would not be enough. The duck carnitas were substantial and very flavorful, but I'm not sure I would pay so much to have that dish again (I believe it was $98). I understand that duck can be more expensive, but this seemed excessive. The husk meringue was not much to look at, but we loved the unique flavor. 

Our biggest issue was the service. There were a few missteps here. It felt rushed and at times, pretentious. With one particular course, we explained that we were not done, yet the plates were taken away. At one point my husband said he wasn't done with something as they took the plate, and the server explained he would bring another plate for it, and brought new plates and utensils for a dish that we had partially completed. Why bring a new one when we already had one? It was just a bit odd- but it felt like they were not listening to us, and there was a hurry for some reason (we are not particularly slow eaters, so I don't really get it). At another point where we were still chewing and they came and wiped the table. Yet another where we were in the middle of a conversation and the waitress just came over and interrupted us, and didn't seem fazed by it. These are all little things, but these are the things that really top-notch restaurants pay attention to. This service could have been smoother and less aloof for sure. 

We really wanted to love this place. The food was delicious, but part of why we go back to restaurants such as this one and are willing to spend $300+ is that we enjoy the whole experience. This experience, however, just fell flat. It lacked the hospitality that we have seen at other similarly priced restaurants, but that is exactly what makes us go back to them. Unfortunately, we won't go back again, which is a bummer.

The BF took me to Cosme for my birthday, celebrated on a Tuesday night. We both came in with low expectations. The restaurant itself is spacious and as trendy and nice as most of its kind in the Flatiron area, but we both agreed that overall the food wasn't very impressive. The dessert, actually, was the best part of the meal.
We started with the razor clam tostada, fluke tostada, and crab infladita. All three were tiny in portion and unimpressionable. The tostadas were overly smoked and smeared with a spicy sauce, which is actually a horrible combination for fine raw seafood. We then had the tataki al pastor, which was my favorite savory dish of the evening. It was served with a very unique pineapple cream and warm, delicious tortillas. We finished with the pork chop which was surprisingly very fatty in texture. It would have been nice if the pork chop was served with an accompanying side dish.
Finally, for dessert we had their infamous meringue, which was excellent. They also gave us a complimentary small portion of some type of tres leches pudding with a birthday candle that was also very good.
My recommendation is to sit at the bar for a cocktail and dessert rather than going out of your way to dine here for a full meal.

Let me start by saying there were some excellent dishes and flavors.  But Chef Enrique Olvera and Daniela Soto-Innes should be ashamed.  First, the atmosphere was one of an upper east side bar, not a fine dining establishment. The music was so loud and acoustics so bad, we couldn't hear each other or the servers.  The restaurant is not about the food, it's about the scene.  Four times we asked to have the music turned down.  I challenge Enrique or Daniela to take one of their elders to Cosme.  So now the meal. The guacamole and chips were excellent and the server did his best to explain. We could barely hear, so we have no idea what was special or what the side sauces were.  Before that was even cleared (big faux pax) the appetizers came out.  This time the server plopped them on the table as he cleared the guacamole dishes, with not a word, no explanation, nothing.  One was a $24 razor neck clams dish and the other a $32 crab dish. I'd remember the details if the server had explained.  Each was no larger than a Chinese dumpling.  Tastes were excellent but the service and atmosphere diminished these to a very expensive taste you couldn't savor or remember.  Entrees were the shared pork/half fat dish - very tasty and my father loved the bone but a $62 entree described as a shared dish and the fattiest pork chop I've ever seen. Then a fish taco dish was embarrassing small; too small to even taste what it was.  My father had the soft shell crabs - he's in his 80s and has eaten at dozens of 1,2,3 star Michelin restaurants and in fifty or more countries. He goes to Mexico several times a year and is the consumate foodie.  His review, "that was the smallest soft shell crab I ever ate."  I have no problem paying for food and have paid much more than this, but with class, elegance, appreciation of the food - not just a hip scene.  We mentioned some of this to the manager who told us "lunch is much better."   We complained to many and all had an explanation but not one said they were sorry.  We declined dessert and left to have ice cream down the street.  Shame on the owners. You make great food in a terrible atmosphere, with embarrassingly small portions (and we do NOT like big portions), with horrible uncaring service.   I'm sure you'll be  very busy with wealthy millenials who love the scene and won't know what they ate, but will tell all their friends and actually enjoy the overpriced food and noisy atmosphere... until the next shiny thing comes along.  Our waiter told us about the plan to add more to the 7 Mexican locations and 2 NY locations.  I truly hope that Chef Enrique Olvera and Daniela Soto-Innes rethink their commitment to food and culture, or else give it up and open a nightclub.

Service was outrageous! Drinks arrived with the food (which took quite a a while), when one of us complained about the 20 some dollar cocktail the waiter had recommended, he rudely argued and only after many words were said did he take the drink back to the bar for them to fix it. Waiters had to be begged to explain the menu (which is very minimalistic and hard to understand without guidance), and even once they were willing to explain they basically read out the menu rather then give details or clarifications. 

Extremely over priced! We don't mind spending money, but portions were tiny and I definitely got home hungry. Food was fine but nothing special.

Would NOT go back!

We booked our reservation in advance and almost cancelled due to some unflattering reviews we read here. Boy am I glad we didn't! Our dining experience was nothing short of phenomenal. Our server took time to explain the menu and how best to order and he completely on point with his recommendations. Our dinner choices included Guacamole, Chanterelle Volcan, Tataki al Pastor & the Duck Carnitas, Cosme's signature dish. Yes the duck carnitas are expensive and we almost did not order it but you will see it on every table for good reason. It is absolutely delicious and the serving size is enormous. It could easily feed 3. We were so full that we had no room left for the signature corn husk dessert. We decided that on our next visit (which we are already planning) we'll go for the duck carnitas and either 1 or 2 other dishes so we don't miss out on dessert. Highly recommended and we will be back!

A buzzy, alive atmosphere, Cosme is like the downtown version of Pujol. This is Mexican cooking that should snap anyone out of thinking Mexican food is solely the stuff of street carts, no matter how delicious they are; like the Nordic-meets-Baja sea buckthorn aguachile, aptly lauded duck carnitas (perfect bites, but I wish we got much more crispy skin), and revelatory husk meringue (which is pops cereal for grown ups). Cosme has a very palpable soul that permeates the space, but know, you will pay (quite a bit) for that soul.

Unfortunately when I came here I just wasn't hungry. The hostess was very understanding and suggested I just sit at the bar and order an appetizer. So I ordered the Arctic Char with Sea Buckthorn and Tumeric sauce. It was pretty good but imo not worth $28. I then ordered the Acacia Mexican chocolate which was very good. I liked how the different sets of chocolate were layered within the dessert. It did however have a weird, what I think was, a caramel like aftertaste. It was $19. The bartender was a super cool and upbeat dude who was quick to refill my water and who I noticed was very hardworking attending to other clients. My only issue was the pricing of the items I had. I basically had an appetizer and a dessert and paid $51, which to me seems very steep. I wouldn't have minded having a full fledged dining experience but I just wasn't hungry enough. I'll add that all of the staff were super friendly and accommodating and would always give you the right of way when you are walking. Staff gets five stars easy. All in all it was worth the try.

We went here for my 40th birthday and it was one of the most disappointing meals I've ever had in New York. Service was subpar. The waiter was not able to help us understand the menu. Subscriptions of items were very vague. 
Now, my husband and I are very willing to spend money on a nice restaurant. Totally fine for the experience, but I felt like we had been totally taken for a ride at this place. The food was FINE, but very small and AMAZINGLY expensive. Not worth the price at all. We had gone to Kawi the night before, probably 100 dollars less and we left so much more satisfied.

  Go for the corn meringue and then BOUNCE. We'd never go back. Save a LOT of your money.

Unfortunately quite disappointing on all levels. After multiple friends having wonderful experiences at Pujol in Mexico City, I thought I must get to Cosme in order to hold me over until I can get down to Mexico. 

The space is sexy and intimate, but the service subpar and the food incredibly disappointing - I can find more flavor at my local taqueria. Beyond the lack of flavor though is an upsetting missed opportunity to enchant visitors with the food's story/background. We were given a complex menu that celebrates deep roots in Mexico, but nothing was proactively explained and our server offered very little explanation when asked seemingly basic questions. You inevitably will find it difficult to know up from down or understand what will best suit your palate. I thought the dining experience would celebrate the menu and create an informative experience, but we were mistaken.

Back to the food itself, it not only lacks taste but takes some real work to get to the heart of a dish. I felt like I was digging my way through plates and bowls trying to find/figure out what I was supposed to be enjoying. The duck carnitas are supposedly the menu's highlight, but even that fell flat. What appeared to be perfectly cooked ducked packed no punch - it was bland. Taking apart the duck ourselves made me realize that reality - they likely don't season the duck, its just perfectly cooked for your to tear a part and assemble for yourself (totally fine with that, but again, wheres the punch?)

The best part was dessert - husk meringue. We got pizza on the walk home. I would skip over Cosme if it is on your list. The value is simply not there.

The interior of this restaurant is minimal yet elegant! Love the vibe at night when the light dims down! Food is pricy but worth it! Every dish is made with so much care and a strong, pleasant flavor.

We ordered the guacamole and the crab dish.  The server was enthusiastic about the food and patiently explained the dishes.  The atmosphere is pleasant, busy but pleasantly neither cramped or loud. The dishes we chose - the guacamole, a crab meat dish, and their signature dessert.  All were beautifully presented.  We loved both the guacamole and chips, and the crab dish.  The crab dish had delicious mole sauce. The signature dessert was very good but much sweeter than expected.  I would definitely return to Cosme.

With a reputation of being one of the best in the world, I was curious to try Cosme. Unfortunately, they did not even come close to meeting my expectations. If the food was truly amazing, I wouldn't mind the fact that the portions were practically non existent. However for the prices- you shouldn't leave a restaurant still feeling hungry. This place should feel ashamed. I don't see how Cosme will survive when the city is full of worthwhile restaurants.

Honestly not impressed by the food, great decor, good vibe but the food was not what i expected for the price. We share an app i cant even pronounce and it was not good. We also share a duck dish, it had good flavor but for 98 dollars for a breast for two is a bit outrageous. We expected more than one breast of duck.  But you live and learn and continue on different experiences.

What can I say about this amazing restaurant? There isn't words to say, I can say if you like art or if you think about paradise ,well this is to be in the paradise the food is a piece of art is a fusion of Mexican , French and Asian. I highly recommend this place.

I had to knock off one star simply because our arrival was rather awkward. 4 of us booked a table for brunch at 11.30 on a Sunday and we got there literally on time however had to gather around the entrance just as everyone else as the restaurant didn't seem to be quite ready for seating their diners. I wouldn't have a problem with that if this was communicated to everyone which wasn't really ok. This whole situation was handled rather poorly and came across super amateurish. This is not what you expect from an upmarket restaurant... luckily once we got seated everything else went very smoothly. The service was very good and food excellent. We were blown away by the flavours of our dishes. Definitely worth a visit for a foodie lovers.

Overly precious without being delicious. Many a taco truck in LA or SF would have made me happier and more satisfied. I had no idea that this place was supposed to be amazing, so I wasn't incredibly let down. It just seemed overpriced and not uniquely yummy. Most of the moles tasted like uninteresting variations on peanut butter. Servings are smaller than a taco truck taco and often cost $40-50.

The music is too loud. There are speakers against the ceiling and the management turns up music so loud it becomes like a night club. The last two times we went out, once as a group with out of town friends and the second time it was my best friend and I, you could barely carry a conversation without having to repeat things. I decided after that I'm not going anymore. :-( 

The food is fabulous, that deserves 5 stars. The wait staff is also very polite. 5 stars for them too. 

But whoever is in charge of blasting the loud music is doing a terrible job. Please change the volume so we can focus on the food. Thanks!

One of the most disappointing meals I have had in New York. The service was truly terrible. First, my date and I were only given one menu to share. Second, we were never assigned a waiter / waitress, and we had to flag down help just to get our order in.

Furthermore, we ordered additional tortillas for our meal. The tortillas never came, and we again flagged down help to give a reminder. After 30 minutes, the extra tortillas came after we were finished the meal. On top of that, they charged us ~$10 for these tortillas. 

There are so many great restaurants in New York. I would stay away from this one.

I'll be fair to both Cosme and to the dining world out there.  This restaurant does NOT belong on the list of best in the world.  Not even close. I'm not being harsh, just honest.    Why?
Service:  unskilled, beginner, not highly trained, basic.  Friendly. 
Food:   Tasty.  Incredibly over-priced to pay rent.  Creative.   Not memorable.   Small portions.  
Atmosphere:   Non existent.  Zero.

Everything here was great, but portions are small. Out of the drinks the aguamiel and paloma were great. They also have Tecate if you don't want a $19 cocktail. Out of the things we ordered, the arctic char, chanterelle, soft shell crab with yellow mole, and the pork chop with chicatanas (ants) were all fantastic. Also if you go you have to get the meringue corn mousse. One of the best desserts I've ever had and totally unique.

Really don't understand the hype. The highlight of the night was the butternut squash tamale, which was very good, but small. The guacamole 
left a lot to be desired, plus it was served with chips that tasted like burnt popcorn. The dish only came with a few chips so when we asked for more, they actually charged us $2 extra and legitimately brought us 2 chips, which when a meal is $250 for 2 people, seems a bit tacky. The signature duck was ok, but nothing to rave about. Drinks were also below average. After waiting a while to get into Cosme, was highly disappointed by the result and do not think it deserves to be considered an upper echelon restaurant. If you want actually good Mexican food, go to La Contenta.
Everything is fantastic. The mexican flavors and aromas are expressed in a very delicate way. The brunch is wonderful, the attention is very good

This restaurant is outstanding. Dining here feels simple yet sophisticated. I've been with a group, on a date and by myself at the bar -- perfectly comfortable for each occasion. Each time I have been, I've deferred to the server on what to order. It never disappoints! I dream about the avocado, endive and pine nut dish starter....
Awful. Ordered guacamole and was served an unripened, hard avocado. The duck carnitas is not worth almost $100. It's just a much worse version of Peking duck.

There comes a meal in every foodie's life that reaffirms why they chosen this path of deliciousness.

Sure your family and friends have confused your passion for obsession... and sure, sometimes you're told "you eat like a dude"... but that won't dissuade a true foodie OR a self confident woman whose milkshakes bring all the boys to the yard.

Now granted, I am reviewing an evening at a restaurant over four years ago on a cold night over Thanksgiving weekend but if there's one thing my mind remembers as I get older, it is the enjoyment a meal has given me. 

So what do I remember? The delicious duck carnitas. The cobia al pastor with pineapple pure and cilantro. The chonky guacamole. The cocktails. The crudo which was a raw sea bass with sea salt, EVOO, cilantro, tomatillo and jalapeño. Honestly if you see anything on the menu that is raw, just go ahead and order it. I'm a big proponent of anything raw - can I get an AMEN ladies? 

Also I'm just going to say it. Go to Cosme for the damn duck tacos. You paying attention? You listening to what I have to say? If you've made it this far, then repeat after me - I WILL ORDER THE DUCK CARNITAS. I have heard Cosme raised the prices of this dish (used to be around $70 when I first went!) but go with a group of people who aren't selling their sperm/blood/panties on the internet in order to cover their rent and you'll be fine splitting the costs... Believe me, there's enough to go around.


Oh and I'm back, my fellow Yelpers. You're welcome.

Food: 3/5
Service: 5/5
Atmosphere: 5/5
Value: 2/5

------

I was so excited to try out Cosme, especially given its recent awards, but unfortunately, we left pretty disappointed. We snagged a 9pm reservation on a Saturday night, and the restaurant was still decently packed when we arrived. The vibe is low-lighting and trendy, great place for a date, we came for my birthday. Started with some drinks, they were just fine, overpriced. Tried the cobia al pastor (SO GOOD, highly recommend), the pork chop (tasty, liked the novelty of the chicatanas), and the mole (we were both very unsure about this one, it's certainly a mole unlike any you have probably tried! i'll leave it up to you to decide whether that's in a good or bad way). Wish I had gotten to try more things on the menu, but between two drinks and three dishes, already up to $200 - impressive price tag for a somewhat casual-feeling meal. Worst was that we didn't realize the duck carnitas were only available if you reserved ahead! Fair warning for you if that's what you're coming for.

All in all, cool experience, glad I got to try it, probably overhyped.

Nominated the 23rd best restaurant in the #50worldbestsrestaurant I wanted to try it while I was in New York. I believe they deserved the award. the food was fresh and excellent.The presentation was great. I wanted to order the fish too bad they only prepare 20 a days, but I tasted it from a customer it was yummy!
We had a good spot parking very close to the restaurant. The ambience was great! It was a great experience. Employees was very polite and helpful.

My coworkers took me here for my birthday. The waiter was not very nice & seemed to be annoyed at having to explain what the menu items were since there was no actual description on the menu itself.  Also the service does play into opinions about a restaurant & the person we had was certainly lowering expectations.
The food might have been good for other people but we were not impressed at all. We ordered the pork which was cooked medium rare. Not sure if that was intentional but if it was that might have been mentioned upon ordering since that is not something you commonly see. The best thing we ate was the guacamole. Can't comment on drinks since we did not order any.
If you're into trendy food then this could be the place for you but if you go to enjoy the atmosphere as well as knowing what food you're getting then this is probably not the place for you.

Food was very fresh, presentation was excellent, and the flavors blended together phenomenally. 

Staff was super attentive, which makes sense for the first seating of a weekday lunch when few other tables were there. 

Even so, I'm not sure the price of the meal was merited compared to similar, lower cost food that can easily be found.

Still a five star--Absolutely terrific. 
If you are looking for a beautiful combination of subtle but refreshing burst of flavors, look no further. 

If you are looking for massive portions of American Cheese, iceberg lettuce and ground meat spiced generously with a quote Mexican spice blend, you might wanna go somewhere else.

I'm shocked, but also not that Cosme made the top 50 best restaurants in the world. The restaurant is beautifully designed with sufficient space in between tables, which is so unlike NYC. 

The cocktails were good and priced heavily at 19 dollars a glass. They must use some top shelf alcohol, but a margarita is a margarita no matter how you make it. 

The server told us that usually people order 2 plates per person for the whole table to share. I was surprised that the restaurant didn't serve anything complimentary like chips and salsa, but I guess this is fine dining and not your average Mexican joint.

We shared a lot of things on the brunch/lunch menu. We had 2 of the mushroom quesadillas and one of the espacito. Each quesadilla was 9 dollars. They were very tasty and not very greasy. We had the lobster, chorizo and bean dish for about 27 dollars, which was very delicious and I would definitely order it again despite the size and the price. 

I've never really had chilaquiles before, but I liked both the green and the red ones! The sauce was amazing. My friend from the west coast loved it, but has had much better for less in San Francisco. 

The duck mole dish was very interesting. The whole table laughed when i yelped "holy molee" after taking a bite as it had a very strong woody earthy taste. I discovered my love for mole on a Tulum trip that I exploited as well when I was in the Cancun. I'm not saying I'm an expert, but I was not a fan of this duck dish. 

Lastly we shared the lamb dish for about 70 dollars, which came with warm tortillas, onions, avocado and shishito peppers with three different types of sauces. I would get this again in the future. 

I can see why this place is hovering at a 3.5 star as no doubt it serves great food, but the price is very steep.

You got to be kidding me. All the hype I read in online reviews and all the ravings on yelp about their food. Must be paid reviews. 

We got their duck dish for $98 and then their corn husk merengue dessert. Both were average at best.

The duck was okay, it was tender and cooked nicely. Flavor wise? Not much. The salsas that came with it were bland as well. For $98?!?! Heck no. The dish was probably worth $40...if that. overpriced and really not that great. Don't fall for the trap, get other items. 

The corn husk merengue dessert was also subpar. The casing of the dessert has a texture that is kind of like airy dried sugar (which I didn't like but it's supposed to be like that so I was fine with it) but the main problem was the inside merengue is salty and buttery. And I mean straight butter...like biting into a stick of butter. Not great. Was so disappointed because I came specifically excited to try this dish. 

The only thing nice was the service, they were speedy (to the point of kind of rushing us out, but I didn't mind because I like fast service). 

Probably wouldn't come back as the prices are way too high for why you get. I prefer many other local New York spots.
The quality of the food and atmosphere are good here. Good -- but not astonishing. However, the prices are astonishing -- sickening really --  given the size of the dishes. $30 for one or two bites?

I want to start off with the crux of the review: I paid $25 for a bowl of raw cherry tomatoes that the bartender was pushing us to get. Yes the dish was good... but I've had better bowls of raw tomatoes at Crown Shy. 

Having said that, the restaurant is close by us so we will likely return, but avoid the basic items and focus on dishes that require effort in preparation. 

Avoid their money makers like guac and a bowl of freaking raw tomatoes. 

The corn husk dessert was very good.

I came to Cosme for lunch to check out the location for a potential future dinner event and was really impressed.

The restaurant is modern and trendy. There are a few tables in the front with a bar area. The dining room is in the back.

We returned after dinner another night and the place was really trendy and like a club. A bit loud for me.

Anyway, lunch was excellent. I ordered the Arctic char tostada and the sole entree. Every bite was delicious and flavorful. Portions are small to medium but if you savor every bite, you definitely eat enough. I finished with the signature meringue which is amazing.

Atmosphere is really modern and trendy. Service was excellent.

I also had an agua fresca avocado lemonade. Delicious.

Prices are on the higher end but if you want unique modern Mexican, this is the place. This is not a traditional Mexican taqueria.

Let me start by saying the food was good and the service was excellent. The prices have increased a lot in the the last two years alone and it's hard to justify. We shared the tataki al pastor which doesn't overpower the delicate texture and flavor of the fish, but still captured the essence of al pastor, the pineapple purée is a stroke of genius and the tortillas are fresh and lovely. We both could have done without the fluke tostada, very small and the flavors were too subtle. The soft shell crab was good though I would probably try something else next time. We enjoyed the chanterelle volcán (what's not too like about that cheesy dish) but I've had huitlacoche quesadillas that packed as much flavor, more adventure, and were 1/30 the price. We finished with the famous husk merengue which did not disappoint- it was salty,sweet, creamy, rich, with delicate and crunchy/chewy merengue. The carajillos were good but not as wonderful as the ones we had at Pujol and contratar (to be fair this is nyc not cdmx and it was nice to be able to order one at all). Still, drinks are $19 now not $14 so order wisely. Will probably be back once to try the duck carnitas everyone raves about if the meal can be expensed. Definitely order the al pastor and husk merengue. I enjoyed my meal but this one isn't going on rotation, not even for a date night splurge.

This place is ridiculously priced. $19 minimum for anything including cocktails and guac. If it were mind blowingly good or generously portioned this could be forgiven. But it was neither. I will say the cheesecake dessert was very good.

Cosme is one of the best restaurants I have been to in quite some time. The atmosphere is modern and trendy and the service personable. Our waiter recommended the El Ninja, a mezcal based cocktail which did not disappoint. I found we enjoyed the small plates and appetizers most so I recommend ordering and trying as many of those as possible. As far as main courses, we ordered the soft shell crab, the mole, and the sole. While the soft shell crab and mole were amazing, the one disappointment I had was with the sole. It was very buttery and while delicious, I feel it is something I could have had at any French or Nouveau American restaurant in the city. However, this one dish was not enough to ruin the night... Dessert was soon to follow. If you go to Cosme you must order the Husk Meringue and Corn Mousse. It is perhaps one of the most delicious desserts I have ever tasted in my life. I would go to Cosme every day just to eat this dessert so kudos to the pastry chef. 

After visiting Pujol last year in Mexico City, Cosme reminded me what I love most about Enrique Olvera. I can't wait to return and trust me I will be back soon. Overall, Cosme is a must go if you are in New York City. 5 stars well deserved.
Good service but horrible music and volume is insane and they keep changing the volume and we tell them 20 times and run out of everything

We were anxiously looking forward to coming here since we had a wonderful dining experience at Pujols in Mexico City along with Cosme having been named to the top 50 for a couple of years. Got here for lunch and found the menu totally lacking. The signature dishes we hoped to try were not available for lunch. We tried the seafood tostada, swordfish al pastor, soft shell crab tempura, and there signature merengue dessert. The soft shell crab was okay and dessert was uninspiring. The other two dishes are not worthy of a review. Maybe dinner is a better choice. It's puzzling how the top 50 restaurants are chosen. We've dined at at least 20 places that have made he list, and all of them can make a case for their ratings. Cosme though is a real head scratcher.

Herb Guacamole is a must, such a beautiful burst of flavor. 
Cobia al pastor, pineapple puree, cilantro is to die for!
10/10 would recommend!

Atmosphere and cocktails are great. As you would expect a mezcal and tequila list that hits all the bases. And homemade sangrita is hard to find in this city. Arctic char crudo with aquachile--delicious, as was the fluke on a blue corn tostada. Should have skipped the bok choy--this place is Mexican, what was I thinking?  Duck carnitas for two were pricey ( $98) but oh soooo flavorful. And the sauces were also delicious. Corn husk meringue dessert, crazy good!! This is a special occasion restaurant (wallet can't handle it too often) and while good, I would likely spend $400+ better elsewhere.

Our waiter made our meal. Everyone seems happy to be working there which is really nice to see. I loved the food, innovative & delicious HOWEVER it's expensive and the portions are small. Don't go super hungry.

Got to Cosme super early! I had time to walk around the block and wait outside their doors and I wasn't the only one. 

My server was Rafael G. He was, for the most part, attentive. He seemed relaxed and nonchalant. It could be because I was alone.

Super clean place, the restrooms are AMAZING. Even though we visited separate times, my friend and I still rave about them to this day. 
 
 Cosme is not for the light-hearted, light-wallet-ed, or lonely. I wanted to try EVERYTHING, but it was a little too pricey for me. I didn't have anyone to share my lunch with. 

The Duck Enmoladas were delicious, but the mole made them a little overwhelming. I don't have enough mole experience (I didn't grow up having it, but it was seasoned well and consistency was great.

The Corn Husk Meringue is a MUST. Sadly, I couldn't finish it all. It has such a distinct and rich flavor. Unforgettable.

Overall, it was a memorable experience. Though steep, the money is right for the quality.

Crazy that at such a high end, top 1% restaurant, they can't figure out how to answer the phone!!! I spent an hour with the phone just ringing and ringing, trying to ask a question.....Food is good, but don't go hungry, and don't try to reach a person there!

Cosme truly lives up to the standard of being one of the best restaurant in the world. We were quite luck to get a reservation before the 2019 World's Best Restaurant came out and Cosme is becoming a even bigger hype. We had a wonderful double birthday celebration and felt privileged for an indulging meal with two of us came back as a return customer. Our waitress was very helpful and really made efforts to explain the menu, giving recommendations and accommodating dietary restrictions. Among the four of us, we had herbal guacamole, Crab infladita with morita and avocado (2 orders), Butter nut ha'sikil p'ak castelrosso and fluke al pastor as appetizers to share, mole negro (vegan) and duck carnitas for main courses, and Husk meringu with corn mousse, Acacia Mexican chocolate for dessert. We enjoyed every bite as the dishes are beautifully presented and well balanced with flavor profile and spices. I'd like to review the highlights of each dish: 
Our guac came with crispy blue corn tortilla chips for dipping. These chips are so crispy and light, not greasy at all and pairing with the best fat in the world, it was a perfect combo. 

The butternut castelrosso which was recommended by our waitress (sorry I forgot her name) is quite amazing, the toasted pumpkin seeds add great texture to the dish. It was so refreshing and soothing and the very vibrant orange color really opens up your appetite just by looking at it. 

The crab infladita is cleverly constructed inside a crispy shell and reminds you of a real crab. The fresh crab meat is top quality, so sweet and tender. I've never had any crabs taste this good.

The fluke al pastor paired with mango sauce and unripe pineapple, and came with freshly baked yellow corn tortilla. So fragrant and light.

The mole is very rich in flavor and spices. We used the mole to pair with our duck and they compliment each other so well.

Oh, and the duck, it is definitely the star of the entire meal and we did not want this to end getting the very last bite. I had many ducks before and have cooked ducks, I was so amazed by what this star dish has to deliver. The duck is fully cooked but the meat is so juicy and tender. There is not a slightly hint of gamey taste from duck meat you'd normally expect. And there was so much meat and makes me wondering perhaps it is from a super breed of duck lol.

Now let's move on to dessert,

The Husk meringu with corn mousse is one of the best desserts in my mind and it is going to be there for a long time. I loved every piece of it, great contrast in flavor and texture and the natural fragrance from sweet corn, sweet but balanced with sea salt, airy and creamy but crunchy at the same time. It was quite fun to destruct this dessert and scoop up all elements in one bite.

The Acacia Mexican chocolate is rich and deep. Even none chocolate lover would enjoy it. The cream and ice cream cuts down the heaviness and makes the dessert easier to enjoy after a stomach full of meal. 

P.S. For folks who think ethnic food can't be fine and does not deserve a fancy price tag, it is you that need to open your horizon.

Food and service are good. I'm not surprised that the serving size was not that generous because it's a fine dining but they should add a little more to match with their pricing. Some of the servers were very attentive and some were not. We really went there to try the husk meringue and it's really good. I just can't taste the husk though. But overall, it was a great experience.

Best tamal I've ever had. Period. Lamb belly tacos excellent. Have some self respect and pass on the foo foo drinks and get yourself the Mezcal from Chihuahua. Be in the moment. Enjoy the latinas direct from LatAm to do some shopping and sporting fresh nose jobs. Grab a cortado and dig into the husk merengue with corn cream. Life is good.

Tasteless food. All show no delivery. When asked if it was a special occasion, they never acknowledged.  Their signature duck dish had no taste and all fat the skin wasn't even crisped. Totally overpriced.

We visited one of our friends in NY and she suggested Cosme as being a top rated restaurant nationally.
Walking there was a nice vibe, the theme, lighting and music. Modern and hip. Felt like NY.
Our early experience with ordering drinks and addressing gluten free needs was a challenge. We felt like there were many helpers but no help. The servers did not converse or explain too much. Order and off you go.
The menu was very creative. Nothing I have experienced before. Given names we did not understand, we needed help. Hard to get. Short on explanations, which came in a hurry when asking again.
Appetizers and entrees were beyond spectacular!! Delicate flavors, great presentations, left you wanting more and looking forward to the next dish. 
My wife ordered the Sole without butter (dairy free). A gentleman delivered it and started pouring the butter on the fish! She told him "no" I ordered it without butter. His answer, "we have to, this is how we make it". You imagine we were upset. They took it back after asking if we still wanted it. Very odd. 
The deserts were out of this world.
All in all, I feel the food in all aspects deserves 5 stars. At the prices we paid (over$100/person) we look for "an experience". None of that. We have food. Not an experience. Not coming back. I will miss the food. Then again, many great places in NY that create a dining experience, at that price and less. The chef deserves better front for the spectacular cuisine.

This place should not hold a 3.5 on Yelp. It makes me worry about the "popular vote" of yelpers. This place has been around for a few years in New York. It has been named one of the top 50 restaurants in the world. So the haters line up to attack. But the truth is, this is the best fine dinning Mexican food experience you will find in New York or maybe all of America. I had to check it out and I can be a hater too, so I went in a little apprehensive. Even as I walked in and saw the layout and decor I was worried and saying to myself, "well I see why they don't have a Michelin Star." Even the cocktail didn't really impress me. But that's where it stops. The care and brilliance of the food says it all. Fresh, local, inspired flavors. Every dish is beyond and, contrary to some belief, worth the price! The guacamole, the bok choy with green mole...unreal! The tamales so good. The pastor, char, and fluke are rich buttery and lovely and light. The duck carnitas are insane. Best duck ever! To cook that large a piece of duck that tenderly is a skill. And the mole, which people gripe about saying, "it's just mole and tortillas," well yeah but it's the best mole ever. Also they have no idea what's been put in this 1000 day old concoction. It is rich and deep with notes of coffee, chocolate, peppers, beef and pork...so complex and so delicious!! Plus the desserts. Now the two of us got all this with drinks and the house gave us several complimentary dishes all for 300 bucks. That is better than most of the other best restaurants in New York, where one person costs 300 bucks. Plus we left full and with leftovers. I don't know what these people giving it one star missed? Plus the staff is A+. This is a New York gem and I will be back!

We were able to get a reservation for brunch this weekend and it was really good! The service was fantastic and the food was really good! We shared the huevos rancheros, Duck enmoladas, and Chilaquiles. The food was all delicious! The temp on the chilaquiles could have been warmer, but overall a great meal! Next time we will try dinner.

Service was horrendous. We have to wave down the servers for everything and even remind them for change of plates and silver for next course. 

The music was too loud and I asked it to be turned down a little since our table had to yell to have general table conversation. But it just stayed too loud or got louder.

Duck dish to share for $95 was good but we were charged extra $8 for more tortillas...how are you supposed to each half a duck with 4 
tortillas??? Lame move for the extra charge. The pork chop was served with one side RAW. When I brought it to their attention, they told me it supposed to be like that. It was NOT called Pork sashimi.

The hostess was a buffoon. When we asked for the manager, she replied with "do you want me to call him"? Then the manager came off uninterested and really did not care. AVOID...AVOID - save the cash! Overpriced and overhyped. For this price point I would expect a level of service and they did not come close. You would get better service at Taco Bell.

The food is too good to give a score below 5 stars. Yes it is absurdly expensive, yes it can be hard to get into. Despite this the flavors are always the best, a bomb of excitement in my mouth. The chips/tostadas are spectacular and unlike anywhere. The masa used throughout the restaurant screams ancient grain and smells mesmerizing. My go to drink is the one with dehydrated pineapple and gin based. Exceptional. They used to have a savory saffron and tomato water cocktail that was OUT OF THIS WORLD, very unique. Carnitas, crudo tostada, tamal, hongas, cobia, husk dessert, beet dessert, etc etc ... everything is great. Order double what you think you should if you can afford it.
Very delicious, the service was excellent would definitely go back. Flavors were amazing and well worth it, the lamb belly tacos were fab!

Horrible. Not really vegetarian friendly. I dined with a group of 15 people and I needed to get pizza afterwards as there are very little vegetarian options. Of course, the bill was well over $250 per person with cocktails. Not worth it. Go elsewhere.

The food? Excellent.
The dessert? Impeccable.
But the cost? Save your money for someplace nicer.

I came here because I won a gift card so thankfully I didn't have to pay for my meal. If I did, I would've been severely disappointed in how much I paid for what I got.

Their signature Duck Carnitas is excellent but $100 for a roasted duck and some tortillas? Completely not worth.

By far the star of the night was their dessert: Husk Meringue with Corn Mousse. This was possibly the most unique dessert I've ever tasted, with the savory corn mousse complementing the sugary meringue perfectly. But the price? A whopping $19.

And don't even get me started on the cocktails: $19 for a "fancy" margarita. You could get better handcrafted cocktails at Death & Co for less than that!

Overall, I'm glad I got to try this restaurant for free but I would not come back again unless they offer the Husk Meringue dessert for takeout.

We went there without reservation ,after seeing it in World's best 50 restaurants list and sat at the bar. We ordered Crab infladita ,Lamb belly tacos, fluke tostada and Husk meringue as dessert. Food is extremely delicious but portions are very small.Stuff and ambiance is lovely.Will definitely be there to try lunch and brunch menu.

Listen....I don't eat red meat or pork and recently stopped eating chicken but I was talked into going here for one reason...their duck carnitas and OMG IT WAS SO GOOD!  It was falling off the bone and I was basically licking my fingers after. It's probably a good thing that I live 3000 miles away from this place or I would go back there a lot. If you go please make sure you order them. You will not be disappointed!

I am Mexican, from Mexico City, and Enrique Olvera is one of my favorite chefs. His restaurant Pujol in Mexico City is incredible, so I had to try Cosme. My experience was very positive. I went with my family of six, and we shared the barbacoa, the enfrijoladas, the mole, the omelette, and the chilaquiles. The omelette, which is topped with a corn sauce of sorts was spectacular. The dessert of the corn husk was also mind-blowing. After this meal, corn has become increasingly intriguing to me. I have been back four times now. The only thing that bums me out is that the menu never changes. I have tried everything on the menu now, and I am hesitating to go back. Yes, all of my meals have been delicious, but I want to taste something new.

If you like spending $19 for guacamole that barely contains two avocados and comes with stale chips run to Cosme.  

If you like soggy tostadas then Cosme is your place. 

If you enjoy spending $19 on a cocktail that is horrible then run to Cosme.  

If you want to order drinks and then wait 15 minutes for them to arrive then head to Cosme 

Best move of the night: not ordering entrees, paying our bill and then leaving.

Cosme has been on my list for years. I learned of it quickly once I started getting into the restaurant scene here, and seeing the Chef's Table episode on Chef Enrique Olvera only made me more intrigued. There was just one thing holding me back this whole time: the money. Though I had never seen the portions for myself, I had still seen the dizzying number of reviews on all platforms lamenting the absurdity of the prices here, considering what you receive. And they're not wrong. It's bordering on outrageous. To still be nearly starving after consuming $90 worth of food is just stupid. I was planning on docking a full star from the experience due to the price. But the food just kept getting better as the night went on, seemingly unfathomable given how beautifully it all started. By the end, I had no choice. I wanted to stand my ground, unrelenting, but at every turn Cosme was hellbent on changing my mind. Every last little detail here was so pristinely perfected--from the service to the food, to everything in between. Cosme sits at #25 on the list of the World's Top 50 Restaurants, which I suppose warrants the bill we were met with at the end of the night. The technique and creativity are some of the best I've experienced, worth staying in for the next few weekends to repent for the money we spent. A fabulous venue, worth all of the acclaim.

Came here at 8:45pm on a Saturday night. The space itself feels like an upscale catalog's rendition of a living room. Certainly on-brand for this area of Flatiron, the city's mecca of fancy home decor. The space itself is quite big. Dark and sleek, fairly minimalist, leaves the fireworks to the food. 

Drink-wise, Cosme is known for its tequila and mezcal cocktails--bad news for me, as I'm allergic to both (long story). So while I didn't get to try Cosme's specialties, I got to watch my bf enjoy them and still had some solid drinks myself. I first ordered the Martes Gordo (Michters American Whiskey, Paranubes, Avua Cachaca, lime, guava) and then moved to the Gin & Shrub (Farmers, Perry's Tot, guava shrub, lime, Q Tonic). I preferred the latter--wonderfully seasonal and fresh. If you're not into guava, they have strawberry and pear varieties as well.

The food here is otherworldly. I've already watched Chef Olvera's Chef's Table episode twice, but it may be time for a refresher. Not that I need to see the food on a screen at this point, I've experienced the real thing. The concept here is just perfectly executed in every way. New, creative and sophisticated spins on traditional dishes and flavors. True mastery of technique and brilliant flavor profiles. The dishes may appear simple at first glance but the precision and attention to detail is significant. I highly recommend sharing. The dishes--even the entrees, it seems--are quite small, so you'll need to order a fair amount to fill up. The only substantial dishes on the menu are the carnitas and pork chop--the rest are teeny tiny. I almost feel like this should be a prix fixe/tasting deal given the price and the portion, but I don't make the rules. See our eats, below:

Arctic char, sea buckthorn aguachile, turmeric: A
Melts in your mouth, fresh and light. Beautifully presented, gorgeous colors. Simple in presentation, complex in flavors. Comes with a few thin tortillas if you desire. 

Razor clam tostada, salsa macha, peanuts: A+
One very thin tostada with one very thin covering of razor clams and the rest, sitting atop a decorative stone. For such a delicate protein, so much is done with the flavor here. Perfectly balanced, the peanut coming through at the end of the bite. Expert.

Crab infladita, morita, avocado: A+
Delicious, fresh crab nestled inside a puff pastry of sorts. Pairs wonderfully with the avocado crema on top.

Tataki: A+
Not sure what kind of fish this was, but it was served with thinly-sliced pineapple on top and a sauce on the side that can only be described as extraterrestrial. An explosion of magic and brilliance. Sensory glitter, minus the cleanup.

Bok choy, green mole, morita vinegar: A-
Still yummy and aesthetically lovely, a little less exciting than the rest. We just wanted to add some veggies to the bunch. Like the rest, served with tortillas specially made to pair with the dish. 

Lamb belly tacos, chayote, tamarindo: A++
Silly that these two small tacos are considered an entree, yet easily one of the best plates I've ever consumed. Rich and flavors, cooked perfectly, a truly harmonious bite. 

Butter nut, ha'sikil p'ak, castelrosso: A++
Still a little hungry, we tacked this on and it's no doubt the unsung hero of this menu. Yes, we should've tried the carnitas, but my god, even as a sugar addict this might be better than most desserts I've tried. Unbelievably rich, savory, nutty, overwhelming in how delicious it is. I'm working myself into a frenzy just thinking about it. 

Obviously the corn husk meringue was just a joke. You don't need my review for any hot takes, it's a no-brainer.

Refined Mexican food? Yes. Atmosphere? Yes. Food worth the price? NO.

A 3 bite tostada with razor clams was different but the spice overwhelmed the clams. The lamb belly carnitas was delicious but count that a 3 bite taco for $13.

We dine out quite but this was not worth it in the least bit.

Cuisine: 7
Service: 8
Decor: 8
Value: 6
Overall: 7

We had a bachelor party dinner in the private room.  It's been a while, so I can't remember all the details, but the Duck Carnitas were excellent. Most of the other dishes were fancier versions of what I get in Jackson Heights or Woodside, and not necessarily better. The service was quite good, making sure that we had an endless supply of Tequila in shooters that could hold triple or quadruple shots. Needless to say, most of us stumbled out of the restaurant happy as a kite.

This is our favorite restaurant for the last two years running. The creativity, ingredients, ambiance, service can't be beat. We're in love with everything this place is and serves. The food is original, deep. I feel love and amazing talent in every bite.

Wow the people giving this place bad reviews are totally right.  What a woefully underwhelming experience.  Food was "good" but NOT earning of its place on the "world's best" list (quite frankly eating here makes me wonder who composes these lists and how much places pay to be on them).  They even rushed out dinner, to the point we had 3 dishes crammed into our table at one time.  I say avoid this place and spend your $$$$ elsewhere!!

The food is absolutely delicious. The lighting and seating is great. I had a pleasant experience with the staff at the restaurant as they were all very friendly and accommodating. The hostess, Arabella, was truly amazing as she helped us being sat even though we had scheduling issues. She did a wonderful job arranging our party and taking care of our coats.

Insanely over-priced but insanely good! We had a $30 endive salad with pine nuts that was about 8 strips of lettuce. But it was delicious. And we had the Arctic char, about 6 thin pieces of fish, but about the purest, highest quality I've had anywhere. Extreme sticker shock but I would gladly go back.

Beyond impressed with all the flavors of the food. 
Highly recommended. Also try the corn husk meringue whipped corn!!! To die for

I had a wonderful lunch at Cosme during a trip to New York last month. I live in Los Angeles, which does not lack for great Mexican food, but where I'm guessing it's harder as a result to get people to shell out for the sort of high-end interpretation on offer here (see also, New York vs. L.A. Korean food; L.A. obviously wins both of these battles, but not in the fancy restaurant department). I'm glad I got a chance to check this place out while I was in town.

I was able to book a table for Friday less than two days in advance, so I'm guessing it's possible to walk in for a weekday lunch. Our reservation  was at noon, right when the restaurant opened, and I got there ahead of my friend, waiting for her at the bar area by the host stand. I was only there for a couple of minutes, just long enough to experience and appreciate the incredibly high barstools. I'm not short, and I kind of had to climb a little just to sit down. I didn't mind, though, and both the bar and stools were very attractive, like everything else in the restaurant. Cosme is a stylish place with a spacious, modern dining room. We had a comfortable table in the back, with cool but normal-sized chairs.

The service was excellent, very attentive and helpful. Our waiter Jose was an enthusiastic guide with a deep knowledge of the menu. When we asked for recommendations, he gave us detailed explanations of some of Cosme's signature dishes. He helped us figure out what and how much to order and just took great care of us throughout our meal.

I had a couple of cocktails with lunch, and they were both great and kind of unusual. I started with one of the Gin & Shrubs, made with Tanqueray, Empirical "Charlene McGee Blend," sun-dried tomato shrub, lime, and Q Tonic. It was really tasty, light and zesty and not shy with the vinegar, which I very much enjoyed. When I knew dessert was coming, I got the Arroz Con Rum, sweet and kicky with Santa Teresa 1796, Avua Amburana, Fernet Vallet, Ancho Reyes, and cashew horchata.

The food was outstanding. When I told the friend I was staying with I was going to Cosme, she said I had to try the fish thing with the pineapple. This was the cobia al pastor, which seems to be the restaurant's most renowned dish. We ordered this to start, and it was wildly delicious, cobia--a lovely white fish I'd never tried before--prepared al pastor, served in firm, semi-rare slices topped with cilantro, chile, and pineapple. The fish came with a sweet, silky pineapple purée and fresh corn tortillas to make cobia al pastor tacos. We also had the Arctic char tostada, a smaller appetizer with four gorgeous, fatty pieces of Arctic char perched on a crunchy tortilla round with salsa macha and salmon roe, a tiny wedge of lime on the side.

For our main course, we shared the duck carnitas and the mole negro, which actually worked very well together. The duck carnitas was a hefty entree, a skillet of juicy duck, crispy skin and rich flesh, served with onion, radish, and cilantro, as well as two salsas, lime, and tortillas to make duck carnitas tacos. (I guess this is technically the most money I've ever spent on what could be described as a taco lunch. I have no regrets.) The mole negro was also superb, a dish of nuts and grains in a complex, earthy black mole. I like meat in my mole, so I don't know that I would've ordered this alone, but it paired perfectly with the meatfest of the duck carnitas.

We shared the husk meringue for dessert (the friend I was staying with had also raved about this), and it was pretty phenomenal. The meringue was delicate and not too sweet, flavored with charred corn husk, and it came with a delectable, velvety corn mousse. We all but licked this plate clean. We were sent off with a last bite of Mexican candy, what I'm guessing were tamarind pate de fruit.

I had a fantastic time at Cosme. I thought it was well worth the splurge and would recommend it to anyone looking for a decadent meal in Manhattan. I'm also looking forward to the Cosme team's L.A. venture, which is set to open later this year. I expect there will be some scoffing if there are $30 fish tacos on the menu, but it won't be coming from me.

Wow.  Went here for my 10 year wedding anniversary after hearing the mostly positive reviews.  The place feels more like a lounge than a high end restaurant where you will drop more than $ 400 for two.  The meal started with a fluke tostada which looked liked it had been shaved off the  leg of a corpse.  Perhaps the most ugly piece of food I've been served.  Other apps were okay but for $ 25 to $ 35 a pop, outrageously overpriced.  The cocktails were deeply uninspired.  The high point of the night were the duck carnitas, but for $ 98 it's not worth a repeat performance.  Lastly, this place tolerates people taking flash photography of their food (low brow and rude).  Cosme is clearly past its prime and is running on fumes.  Very disappointed.

I give this restaurant 4 stars! The service was great, love the decoration, and the food superb, but its overpriced. Love the duck carnitas and the lamb, the cocktails are very good! This is the kind of restaurant I will go once a year. Love Mexican food, so I rather go to a Mexican Food truck!

I've been wanting to visit one of Enrique Olvera's restaurants for a long time, after seeing the episode of Chef's Table about him on Netflix. We've tried a number of the restaurants that have appeared on that show, and are not a stranger to high-end "fine dining" or the prices that come with it. As for Cosme, it was a good meal, the food is very pretty and the flavors are excellent, but the menu is very limited for an a la carte restaurant (unlike Pujol there is not a pris fixe menu) and the portions are (with a couple of exceptions) very small. This is a restaurant where, if you order what  you would consider to be a normal amount, you will pay more than you expect, and you will go away hungry. I must say I expected more. I'm happy I tried it once, but I would not go back. It was not a "wow" for me.

We were really excited to try Cosme. I've heard about it for awhile now and to be honest I was pretty disappointed. The food was absolutely amazing and tasty but each dish was so limited that even ordering doubles wasn't very satisfying. Although the food was tasty I do not think the amount of each dish and lack of any type of side was nearly appropriate for the price. It wasn't THAT good that I was satisfied with just one piece of fish with sauce on top as an "entree" type and nothing else accompanying it. On top of that I was very disappointed with the service. In a restaurant of this caliber and trying to hold itself to a high standard, I believe service should be impeccable. The waiter was not kind at all, it almost seemed as if we were annoying him by eating there. Also, I had to flag down someone who then brushed me off and sent over someone else to order another round of drinks after our cocktails had been sitting empty. I would have assumed someone would have noticed and asked if we would like to order another. It felt as if we were absolutely not a priority to the wait staff and that we were a burden to them. I will not be going back and to the people who have already asked me my opinion I did not recommend it.

We had to try Cosme when in NYC recently. We were late diners, arriving near 11 pm, but still managed to try five different dishes. Each was amazing and as delicious as the next. The service was excellent and I would highly recommend Cosme. I wish I could have tried each dish on the menu!

Cosme used to be an amazing restaurant. Now, it's overpriced and underdelivers on many fronts. The service is way less polished, and the flavors more muted. When you drop 150-200 per person, you tend to notice these things more. The only constant is that husk meringue, which is still one of the city's best desserts. 

Is it just me, or did the price of the duck carnitas double and become a smaller portion?

This rating has evolved over 4 visits.

Overall the quality of the food is good. However, the quantity leaves something to be desired. I ordered lamb tacos for $28 and received two small tacos. Also cocktails are priced at $19-$20 which higher than average price ($14-$16), quality of cocktails are on par with other cocktail bars.
I want to like this place but it simply doesn't grow on me. Tried here twice. Both times left a bit underwhelmed. The food is hit and miss but the decor and drinks are on point.
SO MUCH FUN to go here for lunch.  Totally relaxed and unpretentious service, bright and vibrant food, and the corn meringue dessert is the true story!

After hearing all the buzz, I finally made it to Cosme with reservations for 4. And the hype is pretty much accurate - yes, it's Mexican cuisine, yes, it's pretty pricey, and yes, it's delicious. 

Traditional Mexican dishes meet seasonally and local-ingredient inspired dishes.  Do they serve tacos? Yes...but they were lamb belly tacos.  It's a pretty trendy spot, but not pretentious and demand or imply a more-than-casual dress code. Service is prompt, waters constantly refilled, etc. Again, you pay for what you get.

For four of us, we ended up getting:

Cobia al pastor, pineapple puree, cilantro - appropriately raved about, this was absolutely delicious. Prepared in a sort of 'flash-seared' fashion, it added an awesome char and bite to the otherwise raw/sashimi slices of fish. Pineapple puree made for a nice tangy twist on the dish. Yum!

Butter nut, ha'sikil p'ak, castelrosso - this was such a unique and tasty dish! The butter nut puree was delightful and the tamal stuffed with castelrosso (cheese) and ha'sikil p'ak (pumpkin seed salsa) was just phenomenal!

Mole Negro - The dish is essentially a plate of mole sauce accompanied by a plate of greens and some tortillas. The mole is fantastic - smokey, earthy; kind of reminds me of Casa Enrique's mole. But yeah, as an entree, I'd just wish it came with some sort of protein - that would have taken this dish up a notch.

Lamb belly tacos, chayote, tamarindo - these...these were amazing. Lamb belly was super tender and had a nice spicy rub, while chayote and tamarind nicely helped cut through the richness. I experimented with some of the leftover mole and it was beautiful.

Duck carnitas, onions, radishes, cilantro - the dish is for 2 people, and priced as such ($98), but its popularity is well-deserved. DIY tacos with tender, succulent duck. Hard to miss with this, and it was surely a hit.

[DESSERT]

Eucalyptus cheesecake, cucumber, elderflower - I like cheesecake, so I enjoyed this, but seemed overdressed with layers that didn't impart much flavor. But, it undoubtedly was devoured in its entirety.

Husk meringue, corn mousse - Winner! Again, it's popular for a reason. It's wonderful. Sweet meringue meets a slightly sweet, slightly salty, creamy corn mousse. Awesome.

[DRINK]

I asked what their 'driest' cocktail was and was referred to the margarita. lol. It was fine, though, as far as margaritas go. I guess, when in Rome...

All n all, Cosme offers some very creative takes on traditional Mexican cuisine for a unique and delightful dining experience. It's pricey, yes, but it's worth at least one outing to have a taste.

I have to say, out of all of the top 50 restaurants in the world we have tried so far. This one is a bit disappointing. Half of the stuff we ordered didn't taste that good, don't think we got our money worth. The only thing that's good is the guacamole and the crab meat inside of a puff shell. Their signature dish duck carnitas were the most expensive duck I've ever had, it was good but not as amazing as the price. The fish dish and the 1000 days mole and the butte but with pine were no good, I couldn't even eat it. They look pretty, that's about it

This place is ridiculous. The share plates are tiny and most don't work well for say a business dinner. 6 of us spent $1100 and left hungry.  
Oh - we went for a slice of pizza after.  
Never going back

There seem to be a number of posts that complain about the price of dining at Cosme, but this is #25 on the WORLD's top 50 restaurants, so if you are looking for a deal, maybe you should pick your restaurants more carefully.

If, however, you are looking for an extraordinary Mexican/Mexican Fusion dining experience, you are in the right place. 

From the very first item we had, (a very humble tostada with a chili/sesame seed oil to accompany it), we knew Cosme was special.  The ingredients they choose for their dishes are the highest quality and uncommon varieties and the care they take in sourcing shines in their dishes if you take the care to make note.

From the tiniest nibble on the introductory blue corn tostada, our mouths burst with a rich corn flavor, surprising us and catching us off guard.  We still can't stop talking about it.  Wafer thin, so light and delicate.  We were marveling how on earth they could pack all that flavor in a simple tostada.  This is pure artistry.

Our crab infladita was the same, each dish brimming with extraordinary flavors that have an underlying complexity exposing the care and preparation.  I still don't know how they created this corn tortilla balloon filled with crab, it was a beautiful to see as it was magical to eat.

We saw the Chef's Table episode on Olvera's mole, so we had to try it and it did not disappoint.  It is the most smooth, refined and complex mole you'll ever taste, accompanied by a perfectly supple blue corn tortillas, I'm assuming that were made from the same corn varietal as the tostada.  Honestly, if you told me we were going to be marveling over the flavor of corn at the end of our meal and satisfied with a plate of mole for dinner, I would have responded you were nuts.

I was also excited to try the Pork Chop with Chicatanas (flying ants from Oaxaca).  They were a nice accompanyment, with a very unique smokey flavor but not from any wood you have ever tasted.  I only wish there was more of it, as it was spread on the bone and not the chop itself.

The service was impeccable and super friendly, the waiter was very knowledgable, the drinks were on par and a worthy compliment to dinner.  Overall it was a truly special culinary experience.

We had dinner at Cosme on Sunday. The place is nice but ridiculously expensive. It was $400 for 4 of us. The service was OK, but I found the waiters to have a bad attitude. Asking them to bring more tortillas was a chore. The tortillas they serve are delicious but they don't serve enough. 
The Cobia al Pastor and the Duck carnitas were excellent. The Fluke Tostadas are not worth the price ($25 for 1 tostada).  I would recommend eating here once.  Would I go back?  Probably not.

Cosme:
A Famous Mexican restaurant.
Came here for the dessert and it turned to be the truth. The dessert churros and meringue are soooo great. The Guacamole is  also great. The portion of the taco is so small and does not worth the price. The duck enmoladas is disappointing. 

------------------
Recommendations:
1.  Husk Meringue, Corn Mousse
2. Churros and Mexican Hot Chocolate
3. Arctic char Tostada
4. Guacamole

Modern and spacious inside. Some dishes are great and some are more on the weird side. I would recommend the duck here! It's very tender and not greasy at all. But other dishes we had were not too memorable.

This is a great place to go with a smaller group. Food is amazing but as we ask for recommendations I found it hard for the server to pick stand outs opposed to going through the entire menu. Our group was too large with many different tastes as we had to go against the grain with sharing everything. 

My recommendation is go for the razor clams - you won't find them on many menus and the lamb tacos which are rich and beautiful. The strip tease cocktail was a glorified mezcal margarita but still worth it! All in all good experience, a bit over priced, and service was a bit too pushy to get us to order. 

I would 100% be back but maybe a one on one or max party of 4.

Service was good, ducks barbacoa was large and succulent, flavorful, to die for! The duck embolada was moist and also delicious, but a little on the small potion size for the price. We then had the margaritas which were perfectly balanced. The corn merengue was airy, decadent, and crunchy, the churros were a tad oily and lacked some density, but overall tasty with delicious Mexican chocolate dip. Would highly recommend for brunch. The Tex mex and Latin music hit home for me.

This restaurant is outrageously overpriced and incredibly disappointing. 

At these price points -- we're talking ~30 for an appetizer portion of aguachiles and $98 for the duck carnitas -- you'd expect flawless service and execution of the food. That is not the case. To start, a few days before the reservation, the restaurant asked if we had any dietary restrictions to be aware of and if we were celebrating anything. I told them I'm allergic to gluten and dairy. And that we were celebrating my father-in-law's 70th birthday.

+ They did not know that when I arrived, which would be fine at a normal restaurant, but not at a super prestigious and expensive one. 
+ When we ordered our meal, the waiter asked if we had any allergies, and I told him. He said, "okay," and then put in the order, so I assumed everything we ordered either was fine for me as is or could be made differently. (Mexican cuisine tends to be really good for people like me because it's not super-reliant on bread.)
+ When the servers finally brought the appetizers -- which were all in tiny-sized portions -- our waiter came over and pointed out that I couldn't eat one of the dishes because it was cooked in butter. I was like, okay, but why didn't you tell me that when we ordered it? And he said, "I am telling you now, so you know not to eat it, and there are still two other dishes you CAN eat." So I told him that if we knew that dish was made with butter and couldn't be modified, we would have just ordered something else, and frankly telling me that I should essentially be happy I could still eat 2/3 of the pint-sized dishes on the table was ridiculously inappropriate. He eventually acknowledged that point and comped us a free appetizer to make up for it. But still, WILDLY unacceptable at this price point.
+Finally, we go to the main courses. Since I don't eat meat, I ordered the fish main, while my husband and in-laws ordered the duck carnitas to share. We also got the vegetarian mole to share. Everyone seemed to love the carnitas, and the mole, while small in size, was very good. But my fish dish was disgusting. As in: basically inedible. My husband and father-in-law ate my dish to prevent it from being wasted, and at that point, I was too tired to fight with the kitchen staff about how gross it was. 
+ Finally, we got to the end of the meal and promise of some kind of birthday surprise. Instead of doing any kind of slice of cake or fun thing for him, they have him a tiny scoop of sorbet with a candle. It felt cheap and insulting. 

And here's the kicker: As irritated as I was was, none of this would have prompted me to write a Yelp review, except that this is one of the more expensive restaurants in the city. 

For comparison, Gramercy Tavern -- which is legitimately worth the price -- is staffed with people who know every single ingredient in every dish, modify the menu to suit all kinds of restrictions, are deeply kind, thoughtful, and gracious, and go out of their way to make celebrations feel really celebratory. I have been to Gramercy Tavern several times and will happily go again. Even at its price point, it's a genuine value for the experience you receive. 

Bottom line: Yes, the duck carnitas are supposedly very good. No, this place is not worth the money, and no, I'm never going back.

With the exception of the delightful corn husk meringue, my experience here was quite average. The would-be main star duck carnitas was not as good as I remembered from my visits some time ago. And the various dishes we never heard anything about but ordered anyway due to our party size, were unremarkable, which is unsurprising in hindsight. The meteoric rise of Chef Soto-Innes in recent times did not, to me at least, push forward the restaurant and its food. It has become more overpriced while the quality has slipped a bit. I hope to return to find a better experience soon.

Very disappointing. Bland overpriced food. Duck was Ok.. but way too expensive for what it is. Other dishes were just bad, overly saucy but without taste (which is actually hard to do). Don't remember the names of the other dishes but ordered 4 + the duck. I left feeling like I got scammed, not really an enjoyable experience. 
Service was just OK as well, they push you to over order and the guy messed up the bill to make it $100 more expensive. He self corrected it when he saw me making faces. Just stay away there are way better value places around.

Found!
This restaurant does not serve Mexican cuisine, rather it serves gourmet cuisine with a Mexican influence. To be honest the menu is confusing as it is difficult to imagine the descriptions in your mouth; given the fact that they are not based upon known recipes, or entities for that matter, it is really difficult to know what to order or expect. Nonetheless, have faith, most everything coming out of Enrique Olvera's kitchen is excellent. The setting is modern, dark decor,  with spotlights on each table...maybe to highlight the excellent food from this showman!
For more great reviews visit TheLoupe!

I'd rather say it was a huge disappointment. We were so excited when we made a reservation for our anniversary at Cosme but ended up being not excited and hungry. When people talk about service with a smile it's definitely not about Cosme. I don't know why everyone is so serious there, it made me think of service at badass steakhouses but at least you don't leave steak house hungry after paying all those money. I've been to all sorts of Michelin restaurants and I've never experienced that "unwelcome" atmosphere. I guess they only care about rotation of their tables instead of providing great dining experience. Especially having anniversary and putting it in reservation notes - ended up sitting in between two loud tables with even louder atmosphere around, so loud that I could not hear what my husband was saying the whole dinner. So we both practically shut up and decided to order duck carnitas (that basically saved the day) after our dinner because we were still hungry. I've ordered a glass of wine for a dessert, by the time we got those desserts I didn't have any wine left cause it took so long. How long does it take to do three quenelles of sorbet? Flavors are awesome and chef is putting great thoughts in his food but I guess that's where it ends . 2 stars for duck carnitas.

In summary: Great cocktails and yummy food but definitely overpriced for what you get. 

Came here for dinner on Tuesday and sat at a high top since we didn't make a reservation. The ambiance of the restaurant feels trendy and fun! I ordered the gin and shrub cocktail which was delicious ($19) and my friend and I split 3 tapas (each around $30 for a small amount aka two tacos). Like I mentioned above all of the food was delicious I just wish it was a little cheaper. Our waitress recommended 6 tapas to share but that definitely would have been too much. 3-4 for two people is fine!! It seemed like they were trying to over sell. All of the staff was friendly and had good recommendations! 

 I'm really happy I tried it but definitely would only come back for an occasion since it was on the pricy side.

Is Cosme terrible? No. Is it extremely underwhelming and overpriced? Yes. 

I came here for a work lunch and we ordered half the menu (we tried at least 6 dishes). I don't really mind food that is small or pricey, but it better be DAMN tasty if it's a $90 duck carnitas. And it just wasn't. Our duck carnitas honestly tasted overcooked and a little dry, and just didn't have that fatty, tender succulence I was expecting from a carnitas. Seasoning was meh. The tamale was lacking flavor and the textures were off. The cashew horchata was powdery and too thick. Most of the dishes were raw fish, which is fine, but not what I was expecting from an upscale Mexican restaurant. 

As other reviewers have said, we also found most dishes too small and awkward to split at our table of 4. One dish was served with 2 tortilla chips. Another was placed on a single chip. 

On taste alone I would not want to go back.

The food was not well seasoned and just ok but a bit pricey. However, the presentation was beautiful and picture worthy.  Given the size of the dishes, the prices were definitely disproportionately $$$$ - HIGH.   There aren't any prices on their website but nothing is under $25 and the first portion of the menu is small bites/appetizers.  I shared the Cobia al pastor, razor clam tostada, sweet corn tlayuda and the crab infladita and water - total bill was a little over $150.. The atmosphere was nice.

My guest and I arrived here on a rainy Friday evening in April; the space is a converted gentleman's club and the ambience was definitely contemporary and modern. Our table wasn't quite ready yet which came as a relief as we were slightly behind schedule after hopping out of the taxi.

I want to say first off that the service here is impeccable. The items we ordered were the lamb belly tacos, the duck carnitas, corn husk merengue, eucalyptus cheesecake, avocado lemonade, and horchata. I was actually surprised how quickly all of our items arrived. I want to flat out state that the duck carnitas dish was probably the best duck dish I have ever had outside of a peking duck preparation which o enjoy as well. The duck meat was succulent while the skin and fat had a roasted, savory unctuous umami flavor to it. The accompanying warm corn tortillas and salsas were perfectly complimentary to the duck as well; major compliments to the kitchen for producing this fantastic dish. The lamb belly tacos were also bursting with flavor and neatly adorned with slivers of cucumber as a garnish.

The corn husk merengue dessert has to be one of the very top if not the best dessert I have ever had. The mousse was not too sweet, ever so slightly salty/savory, and had a wonderfully fluffy texture with a great substantial mouth feel to it. Simply divine. The baked merengue gave a very nice textural contrast to the smooth and airy mousse. The drinks and cheesecake (with a cucumber sheeted sorbet) were good as well but not on the level of the duck carnitas and the corn husk merengue dessert however.
