I am so glad we came to this restaurant despite the negative reviews on Yelp. I can't wait to come again and try everything else when I'm back in the city.

This is an upscale ""wannabe mexican"" restaurant but its definetely not mexican couisine, except for the mini tortillas they have, so dont expect a guacamole,  I felt I ate like a bird because the portions are so small and it esa mostly raw fish.. the only good thing I of taste was the duck.. Its overpriced!! So get ready to spend more for less!!!!!
I was here again recently and had the cobia el pastor, herb guacamole, razor clam tostada, artic char, and the grey sole.  Amazing.  Drinks were perfect also.

Insanely overpriced and incredibly loud because of all the hard surfaces. Rushed service with an attitude. Food is underseasoned, as in salt, not talking about spice, particularly the duck carnitas and fluke tostadas. No prices on their website and hard to blame them because they are absurdly high and it would probably chase people away. Portions are really small as well. Cocktails are so-so. Hard, very hard pass here.

Very expensive Mexican food. While the ambiance is lively and fun, the dishes were not lack of trying in terms of flavors. It was not delicious or something I would want to have again. Overall just wasn't worth $290 for 2 people. We didn't order any alcoholic drinks FYI!

After dining at Pujol last year I think my expectations were a little too high coming in. It's hard to top your sister restaurant that's number 13 on the World's Best list, when Cosme doesn't offer a prix fixe menu. 

For the value, I agree with fellow Yelpers that there's no way you can share the food and get comfortably full within a reasonable budget. To start I had the fluke crudo that's served on a blue corn tostada. 3 1/2 bites and it was gone. I also ordered the Telenovela Part ll cocktail which was light and refreshing. I proceeded with the duck carnitas as I was told I'd be an idiot if I came here and didn't order it. The bartender let me know that it's a little much just for one person- challenged accepted and accomplished, I finished it all. The bartender was nice enough to buy my second drink- the Ford's gin & shrub which I loved, & I deeply appreciated the kind gesture. 

I'm a HUGE dessert girl, but nothing on the menu really popped so I paid and finished my drink. While I did tip a little extra for the free cocktail, my bill was just $8.00 short of $200.00. YIKES.

All I'll say is I was perfectly happy to give this place a solid 3.5 stars for pretty tasty, but small, way overpriced food. Service and ambiance were fine... yada, yada, yada.

And then they brought that duck carnitas dish and my life as I knew it will never be the same again. Easily one of the top 5 dishes of any category that I've ever had, anywhere, ever... ever. It's just an all-around perfect dish that makes this restaurant so, so worth it.

If you go to Cosme and you don't have that dish you are officially stupid.

Bottom line: this place used to be very good and now it's very bad. I came in 2015 and gave it 5 stars - I would have given six if I could. Came back in March 2019 and those days are over. Underwhelming food, weird atmosphere, and absolutely horrifyingly atrocious service. They'll continue to skate by on their star average bolstered by excellent reviews from bygone times until enough Yelpers turn the tide and they are finally driven to shape up or ship out.

Female chefs run the best restaurants god damn it. Everything we got was so bomb. Particularly recommend the fish steamed in banana leaf, which was the most tender thing I've ever eaten. Also loved the squash tamale, the char aguachile, and the cobia al pastor. Obviously do not skip the husk meringue for dessert. Specialty cocktails were underwhelming so I would stick with the classics.

Overall, the food was unique and presented very well but lacked options for not vegetarians. I was left very disappointed with the mole dish as it was just greens and a mole sauce and for an entree lacking value. The appetizers that I believed stood out were definitely sweet corn tlayuda and endive plate. The service was absolutely great and they even brought out a small dessert because we had mentioned it was our anniversary.

The food was complex, interesting, and high quality. I would suggest this place to others for the sheer experience for sure. I am also happy I tried it and have no regrets! The service was a solid 5 stars, too. However, to describe these as tapas to share, is not fair at all. With the exception of one dish ( the bok choy) none of the tapas were actually "sharable" to anyone who is actually hungry. If your idea of sharable is one or two full bites per person ( no lie), then sure, you wont be surprised. 

The tostada? it was a cracker. It was good, but to charge like $30 for a cracker, is just not ok. Once dish claimed to have seafood but it was all celery root. Not sure what happened? Charging nearly $30 for celery root shaved super, super thin, is just not honest. 

Now, I cannot vouch for the larger format dishes, but the majority of the items are tapas, so keep that in mind. At around $30 a dish for ONE or TWO BITEs per person ( I was only with another person, mind you), I feel the value vs. cost ratio is just not there. I get it, this is finer dining and the protions are small...but I think this is just next-level when you are talking about price and size. 

Just be prepared.

Needs to work on property advertising hours. Third time I've taken a $15 cab ride well in advance of states kitchen closing only to be rejected from ordering. Manager had a lot of excuses. None satisfied me.

Great food and ambience, but the service and overall experience was way below par. Portions are tiny, over priced, and we were rushed through three courses in an hour. The busser didn't even stop to explain what we were actually eating - just threw the dishes down like we were in a diner! I complained to our server after the first course, it then happened again, so she personally served us the third course. We had a crab dish for first course, cobia fish dish for second and duck carnitas for the third. Because of the service we didn't opt to have a dessert. 

I asked for the manager and complained at the end about our experience. This was our last meal in NYC after living here for 6 years and was a special occasion that was ruined by being rushed and not feeling valued by having our dishes explained to us and a chance to ask any questions about it. You shouldn't have to figure out what you're eating in a restaurant of that standard! He said "sorry to hear that". Not exactly the desired response so won't be going back when we visit again. Very disappointed and upset.

I really enjoyed my dinner here - everything from the service to ambiance, to food was fantastic. Docking one start for the very very high prices though. 

Duck Carnitas and Corn Husk dessert are highly recommended. We also had a veggie/salad app to help cut the fattiness of the duck carnitas. You need a little green on the side because they don't come with anything.

My girlfriend and I had a dinner reservation for 6 pm and were seated promptly. Dinner was going smoothly and the dishes were coming out rather quickly. Once we ate our last bite we had a waiter asking if they could take our half poured drinks. We said no and moments later another person came over and asked if they could take the drinks, AGAIN! After a couple of minutes another person came over and literally asked up to vacate the table! The nerve after we spent over 400 dollars on the bill. I will never go back and I will also notify the manger. Poor customer service. Awful experience

The atmosphere was as vibrant as the dishes - the dining room was filled with lively conversations and laughter. Partially thanks to the strong and flavorful cocktails. The ingredients were so fresh as if you can taste the sea and dessert from the main components to the garnishes. 

The highlight of dinner was definitely the Duck Carnitas, served with the fresh warm soft tacos wrapped in a cloth. Fun fact. They only give you a BUTTER KNIFE for the meat. At first, we thought the server forgot to give us steak knives but ohhhh boy that duck literally FELL APART at the touch of a butter knife. This testifies to the tenderness of this large piece of meat. The various garnishes also provide a sharp contrast to the juicy rich duck - the thinly sliced radish added a crunch and the herbs added a dash of freshness to cut through the fat.

The Husk Meringue is also a must try since the subtle taste was different with every bite. The meringue was the sweetest element. Then the corn mouse was light, savory and slightly sweet. The richness of the corn blended perfectly with the cream. Towards the bottom of the meringue, there was a savory element - we couldn't figure out what but the whole dish gave us a sensation that we were at a corn field. The dessert was visually appealing and tastefully designed. 

I would recommend coming to Cosme in pairs since most appetizers are one piece tostadas and the entrees are meant to be shared by two. If you come with a small group the price per person will significantly increase. At the end of the day, order some drinks and enjoy the meal. This is a place for open conversations - deep and wild topics alike.  

Didn't give it full five stars because I wish the staff would provide more context and description to the complex dishes. It would be amazing to learn about where the ingredients came from and how the dish originated. This restaurant elevated my perception of Mexican food and it could be truly remarkable if made into an educational journey into the Mexican cuisine and culture.
Amazing place. Lovely food and very modern mexican cuisine. The menu can be hard to understand but definitely try the famous mole

How to even begin describing my experience at Cosme. I guess I'll start here - if you are looking at these Yelp reviews in anticipation of your upcoming reservation, like I was yesterday, and are kind of surprised at the amount of negative reviews for such a highly rated restaurant, trust me and just believe the negative comments and cancel your reservation.  I could recommend another 20 or 30 restaurants in the Flatirion/Chelsea neighborhood that will leave you infinitely more satisfied and happy, and a whole lot less frustrated, angry, and mystified.  

I couldn't wait to go to Cosme. My mom was coming in town for the weekend, and my brother suggested we make a reservation for a special dinner out. We were a party of five, all really excited to try such a highly rated and much written about restaurant. I mean, I had seen the Chef's Table documentary!  I was so excited to experience this restaurant!

I am totally fine with spending a lot of money to have a really special dining experience. I'm fine with tiny portions of food, and tasting menus, and I don't need a lot of food, portion-wise, to make me happy if the food is unique/well-prepared/exciting/delicious. Our server came over and let us know that most things were meant to be shared, and that everything except for the several large-format entrees was tapas-sized. Okay.  It is a little confusing that everything is tapas-sized at this price point, but also somehow meant for sharing, but at this point I still had faith that I was in good hands, and that there is no way these $28 to $38 "small plates" could really be single pieces of items that we were supposed to share.  Well, I was wrong about that, because when I asked if the Tostada was shareable, the server said it was one small piece for one person.  Um, okay. 

We ordered five dishes to share (which is what the server suggested), and the duck carnitas to share as well. When I ordered, the server asked if I wanted to "double up" on anything. I was now thoroughly mystified - are the things we ordered not in fact good to share?  He said that they were very small, and suggested we double up on the Cobia al Pastor and/or the Crab Infladita .  "Do you want to double up"?  I mean, does anyone really want to pay $64 for two crab balls?  I think any sane person would say no, but at this point I was worried that we were all going to starve, so sure, give me the two crab balls for $64.  

When other reviewers mentioned that the portion sizes were small I did not believe them. But you should believe me. These portion sizes were shockingly, absurdly, tiny.  The $32 Crab Infladita was, when split between my mom, my husband, and myself, exactly one tiny forkful of crab per person.  It is so laughably NOT a dish that should ever be shared.  I have no idea why any of these dishes would be described as shareable, with the exception of the Duck Carnitas, which, while delicious, at $98, still felt like an incredible rip-off.  

We had ordered one dish, the Pasilla Mixe Aguachile, which the server described as ceviche. I have no idea why I didn't send this dish back.  I am not kidding you when I say that it was petals of very thinly celery root topped with a spicy chile marinade.  With no discernible seafood.  I have no idea how it is a ceviche. I felt like we were being punked basically throughout this entire meal, but when you give me a bowl with two spoonfuls of sauce and seven celery root pieces for $28 I start to rethink my own sanity. 

A number of people on Yelp mentioned that you shouldn't bother going here if you don't get the Husk Meringue for dessert.  I agree completely with them - you should NOT bother going here.  But if you do somehow end up stuck here. you can also feel free to steer clear of the Husk Meringue.  It was completely unremarkable, just a big thin meringue shell filled with cream.  If I didn't know it was supposed to be corn flavored I'm not sure I would have known it was a corn dessert.  It was a fittingly disappointing end to an amazingly disappointing meal. 

I have always wondered about people who ate at a restaurant and then wrote reviews saying "the portions were so small, I left and then we went and got pizza for dinner".  But truly, three quarters of the way through this dinner I was like, oh my god, are we going to spend $700 on dinner and have to get pizza on the way home!?  After paying nearly $700, I truthfully only had a few bites of food the entire meal. 

I've lived in NYC for 25 years, have dined at Per Se, Eleven Madison Park, a number of Michelin-starred restaurants in Spain, France, Germany.  I have never felt so taken advantage of, and frankly ripped off, by a dining experience. NYC is the best dining city in the world - there  are just so many other restaurants that you would be guaranteed to have a delicious, satisfying, fun, stress-free meal at - go somewhere else.  Save yourself!  Don't be the person who is server-shamed into ordering $64 worth of crab balls.

Stick to the known winners and you will love this place. 

Started with the guacamole and pineapple appetizer that was insanely good. Fish maybe? It tasted like butter. 

Of course we ordered the duck carnitas. Best taco I've ever had!!! It was juicy and crisp on the outside. So tender. It was just beautiful. 

Don't skip dessert either. The corn pudding thing was crazy good. 

With a bottle of wine, it came to over $300 for two. Worth every penny.

I was super excited for Cosme, being that it was labeled one of the most recognized restaurants around the world, but I just wasn't fond of what we had. The biggest mistake may have been that I was walking in here with the expectations to have the duck carnitas because my boyfriend knew I would love it since he's had it before, except it was a holiday weekday which left me with a brunch menu and no duck carnitas. 

Instead, we had the duck enmoladas and lamb barbacoa (a dish to be shared between two) which was underwhelming. I have to say, that the lamb did not have a gamey taste and was cooked well, but the pairings just didn't cut it for me with just sliced onions, avocado, tortilla and sauces that didn't offer much variety in taste for me. The only kicker was the habanero peppers, literally. The duck enmoladas is drenched in a black bean sauce which overpowered the taste of the dish, but I was barely able to taste the duck.

I really gave up on the meal and was asking for the check, but the waiter recommended to order husk meringue. The meringue portion of the dessert was much like another other meringue, but the corn mousse was overpowering in a salty flavor that didn't work for my expectations. The light mousse may be a good blend for others, but it just was a big let down for me, especially spending $200 for brunch between two. 

I would definitely consider giving it another go, but only for dinner when duck carnitas are on the menu. Plus, it's a great date night ambiance!

Went here with a friend because my husband has been wanting to go for a while. Have to say that we left disappointed and out of a lot of money!! We liked the ambiance of the restaurant and the place was relatively busy for a friday night. 
 The food and the service on the other hand was not up to par. Between us, we shared the herb guacamole, the fluke tostada, artic char, the crab infladita, sweet corn tlayuda and the duck carnitas. The sweet corn tlayuda and the duck carnitas was by far the best of the dishes.
Lets break it down
Herb Guacamole: Not salty enough, very limey and also half of it was brown!. I told the waiter who did not care nor apologize. I had to ask for another. It was not anything better than what we can make at home.
The fluke tostada was tasteless and the Artic char wasn't special either.
The sweet corn on the other hand was better than we expected and delicious. 
The crab was good but very small and hard to share. They say that its a family style dining option but how can it be when most of the fish dishes are hard to share. 
The duck carnitas was definitely the best of the dishes and its enough to share between at least 4 people.
Furthermore, I did not like that the wine list was insanely expensive!!! The cheapest bottle to share was about $65. We picked out a bottle that had a good rating on a wine app but was encouraged by the sommelier to try a different bottle that was slightly more money. The bottle was not very good and we had a ridiculous headache the next day. Even the cocktails were about $19 each. 
 You can overlook the price if something about the restaurant stood out; like if it was the best Mexican you've ever had in your life or if the service was outstanding!! However, even the service was bad. The waiter never once checked in on us to see how things were going. He took away my friends and husband's wine glasses even though our bottle of wine was not finished!!. When I mentioned it that to someone else, they did not seem to care and we had to ask for another pair of wine glasses. 
 For just a bit more than what we paid individually for each person, we could have had a four course dinner at Le bernardin !! We left feeling very disappointed. Cant recommend the restaurant especially in NYC when there are a ton of other great Mexican thats not even 1/3 the price.

I'm not going to lie the food is spectacular. We got three dishes and a dessert: the honeynut squash, a abalone tostada, the duck carnitas, and the corn meringue. I highly recommend the duck carnitas as well as the corn meringue. It was actually one of the bigger items on the menu and filled us quite a bit compared to the much smaller dishes. Coming into Cosme, I knew the food was going to be expensive, but for so many of the starter dishes to be so small was a little disappointing. 

I actually specially made a reservation online for a "male birthday dinner" as it was an actual option for the special occasion tab. However, nothing during the dinner make it seem like a special birthday celebration. So, why even make it an option when you first book the reservation?? In fact, they accidentally brought us another table's dessert and left it there for a good five minutes. My guest and I knew the dessert placed in front of us wasn't what we ordered because it was a black sesame ice cream. After they finally decided that a mistake was made, they quickly apologized and gave the dessert from our table to another couple two tables down from us, who apparently got our dessert, but were already happily half way done with it. They made us a new one, but it was embarrassing to watch this happen. So, despite the our table eating our dessert and a hefty price tag, we were not given any special happy birthday treat or even the words "happy birthday" even though it was placed on our reservation. 

Overall great food, but if you want to be treated well  and get the good service you expect at an expensive restaurant like Cosme, don't come here.

Cosme is an upscale, contemporary Mexican restaurant in Flatiron. Chef Enrique Olvera, perhaps best known for Pujol in Mexico City as well as his appearance on Chef's Table, opened it in X to rave reviews. Since then, prices have steadily risen, giving this destination restaurant a price tag that has caused some diners to balk.

I'll admit to being among them. I came with my parents around Thanksgiving, and though the food and service was very good, I don't know how I can justify their brunch prices, which are lower than their dinner. Notably, they don't publish any of them on their site.

We came around noon for brunch on a Saturday, when they had just opened up and the room was a third filled. The restaurant is sleek and a bit industrial, with plenty of space between tables. Glassware and furniture are well-designed. Spotlight-like lighting overhead.

Their brunch menu offers takes on Palomas, Bloody Marias, and even horchata. Their margarita ($17ish) is served stylishly on large ice cubes and with a dramatic salt half-rim, but is otherwise normal.

For starters, arctic char tostada ($23ish) had lovely and plentiful fish and roe, though messy to split. Burrata ($18ish), topped with veracruzana, a tomato salsa, and quelites, wild Mexican greens, was fine, but most memorable were the fresh tortillas that accompanied it.

For our main, we opted to share the lamb barbacoa ($70ish), a cauldron of slow-cooked meat, shishito peppers, and greens, served with avocado, salsa, and tortillas. This is where the restaurant came to life for me: a delicious DIY taco feast. I would happily come back and get this alone. It'll feed 2 very hungry people to 4 lighter eaters.

For dessert, a cappuccino was a nice complement to a fantastically loopy churro ($12ish) with thick melted chocolate. You can't really improve on the classics.

Service is smooth. Reservations are necessary, but quite easy to come by during daytime hours. I'd recommend that as the prices are lower and you'll be less tempted to rack up a drink bill, though the atmosphere is not exactly buzzing then.

If a restaurant completionist or money is no object-- check it out. I don't know that anyone in New York is doing the same modern, luxurious Mexican they're doing, and I do like their point of view. But I'd just as quickly recommend more affordable downtown sister restaurant, Atla, to see their perspective.

#5 stars on service. Like whoah. The service was amazing on Valentine's day. Our server even told us the story of the beautiful chef here & all his creations. The hostess were accommodating & the bar had excellent unique cocktails . However.. I wasn't so impressed with the food. The tacos were amazing- but the rest of it.. mediocre. Now it could possibly be that I am not experienced with my palet- but the prices were just too scary for the amount of food we were given. I would like to come back when I am a 5 star chef... but for a mediocre person, I just don't get it. I appreciate the service. You guys were awesome.

Don't even try to say this isn't anything less that pure passion in food!  There is pure commitment to comfort, taste, authenticity, using only the best foods and flavors from south of the border.  
I'm from San Francisco.  We have whole neighborhoods committed to Mexican flavors as well as Central America. But nobody uses the ingredients to produce the feeling you are eating the best from the region.  
 But enough about the food.  Let's just say that EVERY employee is committed to give you the best of everything you can ever expect. How about the wine.  What a selection, perfectly selected for the food.  This takes real bravery not to load everyone up with popular but totally inappropriate wines.  Tequila, and mescal are also totally appropriate with the food.  The bartenders (Ulysses) would have spent the whole day teaching me of his mixing talent and the nuances of the brands.   
 No body is rushing you in and out.  Again. Everyone is there to make you happy.  
I love this place!   You will never find this anywhere in the US.  It's not the cheapest. It's not cliche.  It's real.  You'll leave full.  You'll leave happy. And I hate to say it.  But you'll have a wonderful experience provided you are a wonderful person.

I absolutely fell in Love with the Infladita! Would've ordered a second but if I did, there was no way I was going to fit the Lamb or the Honeynut Squash or the Mexican Chocolate! Our server was genuinely nice. He checked up on us and explained the dishes as they came. As for drinks, Hierbas y Raices and El Ninja. (There were 2 other drinks we had that I don't see on the online menu but everything was Great!)

Food is really good, the experience could be better. 

The food was superb. I really could not have asked for more unique, well-executed, rich flavors and textures. We had the abalone tostada, crab infladita, the cobia al pastor, the duck carnitas, followed by the husk meringue w/ corn mousse. Every dish was stellar but the cobia al pastor was something truly unique with almost a sashimi-like smoothness of pork against a semi-sweet pineapple puree that was so delicious. The duck was unbelievably tender and rich, with a nice counterbalance from the radish and onions. The husk meringue was the star and pinnacle of our experience - a hard, sweet shell with a silky texture of corn (salty) and rich creaminess of regular mousse. 

But outside the food, something felt a little "off". It's hard to pinpoint but I think this place suffers from the "in between" syndrome or "trying to be something for everyone" identity. It was not fine-diney, not casual, sorta sceney (but not terrible), just mixed. The servers were very fast and impersonal and the dining experience did not feel "welcoming".  Very little effort to explain the menu. I think ownership did not go down the "fine dining" route because they wanted this restaurant to be more "affordable" and for the masses. The problem is because the portions are SO small, you end up having to spend a lot of $ to have a worth-while experience. I wish they would have just had this on a tasting menu and made it a high-end restaurant. Instead, despite the excellent food, because the overall experience, we left feeling like we spent too much money (4 dishes, 1 dessert,1 martini, it added up to $250 pre-tip). I think it's a 3.5 but I'll round up because the food was great.

Great vibe and excellent service, but simply waaaaay overpriced.  When I asked about portion size and was told that if you are hungry, three dishes should do it.  As I recall they all start at $25 and go up.  I should have ran then, and I should have checked the menu online before going - my bad.  I had the Mole Negro for $32 and consisted of a cup sized portion of black beans and mole sauce.  Add my $8 bottle of Negra Modelo, and I was up to $40.  I went to Little Beet and filled my belly afterwards.

No go. Wanted to love this place since it was highly recommend by a friend from Mexico but left hungry. Maybe worth going for a drink or perhaps if the menu is seasonal maybe we didn't order the best things. The atmosphere was very cool and trendy and the service was excellent and the music and vibe was cool. We ordered the sweet corn teyluda with truffle and while I could see the shavings there wasn't the slightest taste of truffle. The waiter deducted the truffle mark up once we inquired and said it was the last week of the season they'd be serving them. I was sad they didn't have any good cocktails or vodka that I liked. The best thing was the crab cake appetizer, very fresh and delish. But very small portion. The spicy oil and blue chips weren't anything to write home about. The entire menu was gluten free which was cool. The pork was good but once I realized what was crusted on the bone I could eat no more. See pic and guess...my hub said he ate one and it was bitter! They did bring over a dessert for my husbands birthday with a candle so I was happy they acknowledged his birthday but we arrived late for our reservation and were rushing to give back the table as they requested and I couldn't wait to go to the next stop since this place was dissapointing.

I had been to Cosme before, shortly after they had first opened, and thought the food was pleasant but nothing particularly special and far too expensive. I did, however, love the ambience and felt I would definitely return for a drink.

When my sister kept raving about her dinner here (and of course, the many accolades you're no doubt aware of), I realized I had to come back soon and see what I missed the first time.

So we came for brunch, and--wow. I still stand by my opinion that the starters (we ordered the aguachile) are far too expensive for what they stand for. But all of that gets immediately thrown out the window when the lamb barbacoa ($79 for two, lunch/brunch only I think) hits the table, because for the next precious moments we were in pure heaven. Everything about the dish was perfect: the house-made tortillas, the salsas, the impossibly delicious braised lamb, the perfectly tart greens, the beautifully tender shishito peppers ... I could go on.

There's no question it's remarkably expensive for what it is, and yes you can certainly eat better Mexican food for less, but you'd probably gave to be halfway across the world to do it and certainly not in the heart of Manhattan. The Paloma was a perfect accompaniment to the meal and rounded out the flavors wonderfully.

Now I'll definitely have to return for dinner to try the duck carnitas I keep hearing so much about...

Came back to Cosme after 2 years and found it to be as great as before -maybe better. The drinks were fantastic and the food even more so. Not much to add to my previous review other than photos of the meal.

I love Mexican food, I was so excited to eat here with my girlfriend so we booked a reservation for Brunch. I've eaten in a lot of Mexican restaurants in NYC and I spend time there as well. However I was really disappointed with the food, the sauce was bland, the mushrooms in the quesadillas had no flavor. The Arctic chard had no flavor, the chicken chilaquiles did not have enough sauce it lack in flavor and was dry, food was not hot. Our drinks got to our table as we were almost done with our meal. The waiter did not check on us and did not apologize for the late drinks. 

Overall this place was not what we expected, I think the Chef needs to spend more time training her staff.

Great menu for celebrating an occasion. The drink menu had plenty of options and was impressed with the quality of the cocktails. The waiter did let us keep a cocktail menu at our table, which I found extremely odd. The waiter was rushing us in the beginning of our meal and with clearing our plates, but disappeared towards the end and made it hard to get our check. The duck carnitas are everything they are thought to be and more. The fluke is nothing special and the squash did not impress me either. The roasted corn with truffle was amazing and the corn dessert was everything I thought it would be and more. 

Very disappointed the uni tacos were no longer available on the menu. Overall a great experience celebrating my friends engagement, but will probably not return.

Cosme is definitely a splurge meal but it's so worth it! The atmosphere is very cool and the service was solid. We ordered the following for two (we have big appetites and this was enough):

Cobia al pastor- trendy take on fish tacos; fish cooked medium rare. Really interesting and would recommend 

Guac- pretty standard and tasty- would only order if super hungry 

Beet tetela- delicious fried tortilla filled with goat cheese/beets with side of beet hummus. Third favorite dish after duck carnitas and dessert 

Sweet corn tlayuda- basically a fancy tostada with cheese, mushrooms, and corn. Very good 

Duck carnitas- must order; super meaty and paired with very fresh salsas and veggies; two of us were hungry and ate all of it. Second favorite after dessert 

Dessert - Corn husk merengue- truly outstanding. One of the best dishes I've had in NY; it was my boyfriend's birthday and they also brought out a complimentary slice of cake with a candle. The cake was great but don't miss the merengue.

We also each ordered two cocktails each. If you're drinking, prepare to spend ~200 per head. Again... worth it for a meal of delicious, creative, and authentic Mexican food!

The dishes at Cosme were very hit-or-miss. The highlights were definitely the duck carnitas (they were delicious AND gorgeous) and the "nixtamalized honey nut squash, ha'sikil p'ak, castelrosso" dish. These two were absolutely fantastic, the squash was so rich and delicious, and the duck melted in your mouth. The dishes that were not so impressive were the "crab infladita, morita, avocado" and the guacamole. The guac was extremely underwhelming, and the crab puff was not very flavorful. The ambience of the restaurant was very hip and cool - almost too cool! The lighting was super dark and my mom had to whip out her flashlight to see the menu. Overall though, it was a great meal because of those two fantastic dishes.

I'm surprised Cosme has such low rating. I give it 5 stars!! This place is amazing. It's a sleek Mexican spot with a big bar for locally sourced share plates, plus tequila & mezcal cocktails. The service was great and everything we ordered was on point!

Things I ordered:
- Fluke tostada, blue corn aioli, finger lime
- Beet tetela, goat feta, beet hummus, hazelnut butter
- Duck carnitas, onions, radishes, cilantro (MUST GET)
- Crab infladita, morita, avocado

Mediocre service, awful food. Living on past reputation I have to assume. The lowlight of the night was a laughably bad fish starter wrapped in a leaf. I actually had to hold in my laughter when I saw it. It was tiny and cooked in what I can only assume was a microwave judging from how bland and dry it was. The other main I ordered was the porl chops, it said it was a "to share portion". Maybe toddlers could share that and be satisfied. It was okay.

Ive been to cosme 3 years ago. The food quality has decreased dramatically. Dont order the FISH WRAPPED IN A LEAF ( it was dry possibly smaller then a 2 oz portion and overpriced) uni taco and sruffed avocado was off from
Their menu which didnt make sense as these were the dishes they become popular for

Also it was my boyfriends birthday, i requested a birthday cake surprise and the manager confirmed my request via email, and the waiter didnt know anything about the occasion. He offered us the dessert menu post dinner. So my whole surprise got destroyed not that the mains (fish and the pork arrived to our table very cold)

Beautiful. Great vibe. Food is delightfully delicious tho frightfully small. However for a restaurant with a reputation like cosme has and a chef with such talent, the service is rough around the edges and careless. This was the first time I didn't eat at the bar, and had a reservation set for 9. It would be nice , especially paying for a dinner we knew would be $$$$, to have at least an acknowledgement from anyone of a request for an earlier time if possible. And it would have been nice if they honored a promise to at least get us seats at the bar if they opened, which they did but we were not offered the seats. Or they could have taken the wine glass from the cocktail table to the dinner table instead of getting rid of it. Or they could have given us a table that opened up earlier when a couple stayed at the bar and gave up their table. They could have done any little thing to show a little attention. But they did not. Shame on them.

Walked in on a Saturday night without a reservation and we were clear we were there for dinner and drinks. We were told we would have to wait close to 2 hours for a table. This was confusing as there was a table in the front with 12 seats open. We asked if we could sit there and they claimed they had a reservation. I did a quick scan of the tables in the back and counted 6 open tables we could sit at but apparently they were all booked. Fine. 
We eventually were sat in the front by the door at these lounge tables which did not have enough space to have dinner. We asked again about moving to the table of 12 open seats or any of the tables in the back and were denied. We ended up staying till closing and that table of 12 was NEVER filled - no party ever showed up and they never asked if we would prefer to move there at any point. 
The food was very mediocre and the portion sizes were pretentiously small. The best part of the evening was the bottle of red wine we had. 

I would not return here.

I have eaten at some of the best restaurants in the city and this restaurant does not compare in any way. The food was alright but extremely overpriced.  They actually told us we needed to leave because we were there close to two hours and wanted to turn over the table. Maybe they should have done a quicker job bringing out the tiny portions of food. On top of it all they have a drink menu that states something about our President that can't be repeated. I can't believe a restaurant would out such garbage in their menu. Stay out of politics!

Where do I begin? 

A friend of mine made the reservation a month ago, because it was dificuIt to get one. I dine in the city often at great places and I have never been so disappointed.  I have never written a Yelp review, but after my experience at Cosme I felt the need share.

This place was awful.Overpriced and the portions were so small.
They have the audacity to call these dishes family style. We left hungry.

Terrible service and the worst meal I have eaten in years. 


The Mexican waiters must be laughing at all the idiots in there eating that  overpriced garbage. Don't waste your time and money. The Halal truck on the corner is better than the crap they gave us....and I don't eat street meat!

If I could give them 0 stars, I would. I heard about this restaurant, so I wanted to try it. Everything from A-Z was horrific. The waiters do not even greet you to start. He approached our table and just stared at us without saying a word.  He did not explain the menu to us at all. (When we specifically said its our first time and wanted to know what was best on the menu) We consistently had to ask what was in each dish because we have allergies & also they name all their foods differently. The food was cold and did not taste fresh.

Midway through our appetizers, we wanted to order more food and our entrees. We could not find our waiter, as he did not come back once. Every time we wanted even more water, we literally walked to the host stand to flag someone down.  Then a bus boy told us we cannot order food because the kitchen was closed.

We were utterly in shock. So our waiter went home and didnt inform us that the kitchen was closing? When he knew we didnt order dinner yet?

It just continued to get worse. Never have I ever experienced such rude and awful service or a restaurant in general operate in this matter.

I would advise anyone to NOT GO HERE. One of the worst dinner experiences I've ever had.

Without a doubt or dissension in our group, the worst and most shameful meal we've ever had in New York or wherever our travels have taken us. I never write negative reviews (not even one so far) as I like to give businesses the benefit of the doubt etc, but this...this was particularly egregious. We all thought we were being punked! I think the $69 fried tortilla with corn/a piece of mushroom and some truffle took the cake, followed closely by the minuscule steamed fish wrapped in a leaf that smelled like an ace bandage left in a high school locker room were among the highlights...as was the mole rice dish for $32 that was the burned rice on the bottom of an old pan...in our defense, we did ask our waiter to describe these dishes but the descriptions never really matched up. I will say, we all haven't laughed as much in ages, especially as each deep bowl came and we all stood up to get a glimpse of the little morsel on the bottom that left an even worse aftertaste than the bandaged fish!

To be ranked on the world top 50 we expected the quality of the food, service and ambiance to be on par with others on the list we have visited. This was a far cry from either of those. It made me Google and re-google to ensure this restaurant was really on the list.

The signature dish - duck carnitas - was good but not mind-blowing good. When ordering wine with the first course after cocktails, the wine came after we finished the course and didn't actually get what we ordered. To be fair, the waiter removed the two glasses of wine from the bill and comped us an additional appetizer. 

If it were any other restaurant these sort of misteps it would be ok. The overall meal would be good - albeit over priced for what it was - but just not what you expect from such an acclaimed restaurant.

The whole experience was underwhelming. Quality to price ratio is extremely low. Food was mediocre at best. Some dishes were inedible. Bok choy with green mole was hard to eat, too much vinegar. Mole negro was just not tasty. The representation of food was nice though, dishes looked good. The service was nice, but the ambiance not so much. The experience is similar to eating at a club. I was always surprised that it was in the world top 50 list and did not have a Michelin star, but after eating here makes sense why

This is one of my favorite restaurants in NYC! I'm from Mexico and love their take on traditional Mexican food. They've taken traditional dishes and fused them into something unique and delectable. Also, the service is great, the bartenders remember you, and the setup is amazing. Best of all, they have carajillos which no other restaurants in NYC carry. It's a Mexican after dinner drink that has espresso and Licor 43. After dinner I tend to feel heavy and always want to go home, but after this drink, I can continue the night away.

The portions are tiny and if you are a man and not an old lady, there is a good chance you would leave the place hungry after spending $$$$. The duck  had a lot of fat, which, i believe, should be removed prior serving, unless it is a special thing in Mexico. The lamb was salty. Crab and char were excellent. Other dishes had interesting combinations of tastes and it was rewarding to try them. Mole negro is something to remember. Service was good; no complains. Meringue and chocolate are the best deserts. The wine list is pretty good and has interesting wine. For example, there are several wines from Jura mountains of France. Overall, if you are hunting for interesting food and wine, it is worth to try the place once. Otherwise, it is not worth the money.

Elevated Mexican food. Food is not traditional Mexican but has an interesting twist. Everything we ate had amazing flavors, we were very impressed. Also great ambiance. The margarita is perfection. I can't wait to go back!

Really awkward dining experience. Despite its delicious food and stunning interior design, the level of service provided was probably among the worst I've experienced. Our waiter began by not taking down our drink order, and half way through the meal, we were still wondering when our drinks were coming up. When we pointed out we were still waiting for the drinks, waiter paused and then casually said they were coming up. Well, it was another 10 or 15 minutes before our drinks actually came up. And service was practically non-existent after that. 

If they don't do something to improve their service team, Cosme will soon see its end.

This is a very mediocre restaurant who has no qualms at charging the most ridiculously high prices.   The duck carnitas was $98 for a duck dish that is nothing special and tastes like pulled pork.  The two sources offered were completely off mark.  The Sweet Corn Tlayuda (an appetizer) was $69.  It was a soggy taco with some cheese, corn and flavor-less shaved black truffle.  The portion was very small for the price.  The mole negro at $32 was an unedible risotto dish with a mole sauce.   The only good thing at the restaurant was the corn mousse dessert.   On top of bad food, the sommelier had the audacity to give a $190 bottle as his first suggestion and said that 190 was about the  average price of wine in the restaurant.  We are New Yorkers who have eaten at many top restaurants in NY and around the world.  This is the first time we have ever felt so cheated.

The food was a beautiful experience. The chefs really know what they are doing. Great service and relaxing ambiance. Well worth the money. Plan ahead and make reservations. Vegetarian and vegan dishes available.

Disappointing. There is simply no other way to describe it. Cosme has been on my list forever and finally had the opportunity to try it. To be clear, there is nothing wrong with Cosme - it's just that the food is mediocre at best and probably worth half the price. You could easily find better spots in NYC for same dishes tasting much better at 25% the cost. Service was just fine but it didn't come across like the staff took a lot of pride in the menu which tends to be the case in good restaurants. Bottom line - you'll spend $200 per head and are likely to feel that you've made a bad choice. And honestly wouldn't go back regardless of the price.  
Sorry Cosme, just being honest.

I have been dying to try Cosme for quite some time, and now I have NO IDEA why. 

We ordered a wide range of dishes: crudo, endive salad, guacamole, bok choy, beet triangle, and the sea bass. We figured that everything would be more than a bite size since the were priced from $20-$38/$40. We thought we could always order more but there wasn't even stuff that sounded insanely appetizing.
I mean if the food was incredible I wouldn't care about how expensive it was- haha I wasn't paying - but that was the issue. The food wasn't even great. I make a better guacamole than they did. Everything was beyond bland and tasteless for 1) a Mexican restaurant 2) a restaurant that is apparently world renowned and 3) for their prices. 
I went to dinner not even hungry but somehow left starving. So I guess only go to Cosme if you want to put a dent in your bank account, eat bland tasteless food, all in a dark environment.
Went here for brunch.  Everything was amazing. Including service.  The drinks were superb.  Stay for dessert.  The meringue was to die for.
Horrible. Bland food. Bad service. The service could've saved the bad meal but it didn't. Top 50 restaurant? NO WAY!!
The dishes are exquisite. Atmosphere is chic & elegant (like hotel elegant). Wonderful staff.

WASTE OF TIME, MONEY & CALORIES. 
I've been wanting to try Cosme for a few years and could not be more disappointed.  The space was loud.  The margaritas were mediocre. The Paloma was so watered down and with so much sugar, it tasted like cheap soda.  The service alternated between overbearing and forgetful.  We asked for sparkling water and the bus staff alternated between sparkling and still all night, which resulted in just a weird flat not quite sparkling yet not still item.  The $68 truffle flatbread did not taste like truffles at all.  The Bok Choy dish was uninteresting and boring. The Carnitas were fine but for $100, not good enough.  It was incredibly bad we just felt used and abused.  Even when we went to get our coats, the coat check could only find my husband's coat, they'd lost mine.  It was a waste of time, money & calories.  Not only will I never go back, I plan on telling every one I know not to bother.  This is the type of absurdity that can only happen in NYC, the scene takes over the quality.  Yuck.
Different from Pujol but delicious and authentic. The duck carnitas are worth it and so is the cold brew cafe de olla.

OVERALL - Let me preface this review by saying I'm a huge foodie and I've had Cosme on my bucket list for years. I've also been to Pujol, their "sister restaurant" in Mexico City which is by the same chef and a Michelin star restaurant. So I really had every intention of coming here and loving it when I made a reservation to celebrate my husbands promotion. It was very very good, some of the dishes were excellent (others were just bleh) but it received its 3/5 star review because of that inconsistency and because it was so overpriced to match. COCKTAILS were $19 and were just okay. I work at the world's largest spirits company so know my drinks and these were NOT worth the price tag. THE MENU is meant for sharing but frankly isn't big enough to choose from to allow this. We got 5 dishes for 2 and it was a struggle to pick this many from such a limited menu. THE FOOD was, like I said, inconsistent. The two tostadas we had were excellent but were the size of a silver dollar and $25 a piece. We splurged on a $70 Mexican pizza thing with corn, truffles and cheese (my three favorite ingredients in the WORLD) and it was so beyond average and disappointing. And the size of a small taco tortilla. So overpriced and a waste. The cobia al pastor fish with pineapple sauce was the highlight of the meal for me and was more decently sized. The $38 lamb belly was so under seasoned, over fatty and average tasting. The dessert on the other hand was fantastic. Caramelizas cacao crema with pistachio gelato and freeze dried dehydrated raspberries was incredible, innovative and a perfect way to end the meal. We definitely considered the duck carnitas as it's the their most famous dish but for $98 we couldn't stomach it. OVERALL, the dishes that were good were OUTSTANDING but some of them were just plain megh and at $25-$98 per dish, most of them overwhelmingly tiny in size, that inconsistency is just unacceptable. Go if you don't mind spending $300-$400 on a good meal but personally I don't think I will be returning (unless it's on a corporate card or expense account).

Food was decent, but not amazing. Service was not wonderful. Plenty of open tables and seats, yet made to wait and not even offered a wine list at the bar. Maybe they're working out their kinks, but for all the hype, I am sad to say I wasn't overly impressed. So unfortunate!

I went to Cosme for the first time last week and I am having weird feeling about writing this review. I went in with pretty high expectations and I wasn't disappointed but I also was not blown away. I thought the food was really solid, the drinks were really solid, and the service was great. We ordered the guacamole (our favorite part), the fluke tostadas, the squash, and the duck carntias for two. I thought the food was a tiny bit pricey for the amount of food that we got in relation to how good it tasted. I do not feel an immediate need to go again, which is why I am only rating it a four star. Overall, I WOULD recommend going and eating here, as the food and experience was really strong for me. I just do not think it warrants 5 stars.
Wow, the food, the service, the simplicity was on point. Chef Olvera does it again. We had the duck carnitas and I just wish I could have eaten more. Incredible
Duck carnitas to die for - this place is superb!  Great food at not your typical 50 Best pricing.  The menu of drinks and food was very good and pleased the entire group.  We will be back.

Was excited to join a girlfriend tonight whom I hadn't seen in months because of the holidays and when I got there the bar area seem like it had some room but the chairs were so hard to pull out they're so heavy and then the next conflict was having to get onto the chairs because they're so high. Then it was decided that our backs the next challenge was sad and cocktails and wine from the wine list and everything just seemed a little bit higher than normal and higher than average terms of cost Miley mind you it was all good but was expensive I want to do guacamole and it didn't really come with chips it came with blackboard almost like cardboard Christmas that he had to break apart and there wasn't anything unusual in the guacamole other than maybe some mint leaves and some other leaves not what I was looking for for the book for guacamole for good guacamole someone. I left feeling somewhat disappointed and we had to remind the woman to bring it to us after quite a bit and she told us the behind the scenes printer wasn't working.

Love this place. The food is so creative and tasteful.  Its quite expensive for the amount of food you get but it's totally worth it. The waiters are nice and pay attention to detail. Get the merengue as a desert it never disappoints.

We came here onNew Years Eve for dinner. The staff was warm and welcoming. The food we ordered were super delicious, and you could clearly see the thoughts and efforts put in behind each dish. They gave each table complementary dessert for the evening as well. The whole experience was very pleasant. The only complaint I have is the price tag tbh. However, I don't think you could get the same quality of food or experience anywhere else in the city, the occasional splurge could be justified.

This experience was a solid 3.5 stars for me but their service was weird and nonexistent at certain points which is why I'm giving it three stars. 

My family and I came in for dinner recently. We ordered many items from the menu, a lot of which were pretty good (the tuna was excellent, as was the beet tortilla) and others which were not (crab was a total miss). 

The duck is their signature dish and for good reason. It is excellent and a huge portion. This was enough for the entire table and we had five people. We also ordered a fish entree and the quail. I liked the quail but the fish was forgettable. 

In terms of dessert, the corn merengue is surprisingly tasty. It might be the best merengue I've ever tasted. We also ordered the chocolate dessert which I liked the most, since I love all things chocolate. 

We also got a complimentary fruit cake which was one of the most disguising things I've ever tasted. I know that is harsh but I couldn't even swallow it. It was a weird combination of flavors. If the owners are reading this and contemplating putting this on the menu, please don't. 

The service was lackluster and our waiter basically disappeared after the appetizers and came back half an hour later with our entrees. They didn't do a great job at explaining what the dishes consisted of and weren't very friendly either. 

I would come back for brunch, I think, and hopefully raise my rating.
Food is tasty but portions are tiny (36$ for maybe 4 ozs of of flat iron???) and very expensive. And cocktails are the same. The prices and portions are what will keep me from coming back...

Super great food, SMALL portions. Waitress was nice but the hostess' were NOT friendly. 
I would not recommend for a get together but maybe a casual date.

Everything here started out great. We sat in the bar area since we didn't have reservations and were able to sit down right away. Ambiance is really nice here, good mix of music. Our waitress was fantastic. She explained every menu item to us, accounting for our dietary restrictions on each, and was really knowledgeable about the menu. She really made the place. Food was top quality and very good. However, the portions are a bit small. It's not a great value for what you're paying. After spending $200+ on dinner I don't expect leaving hungry and having to go home and eat. We ordered 6 dishes for 2 of us and felt unsatisfied. I would really give this 3.5 stars, but since we can't give 1/2 stars it was bumped up to 4 for the service. We enjoyed everything we ate, just wish it was more substantial.

Food tips: Arctic Char, Crab Infladita, Honey Nut Squash, Mole Rojo
Wow.  The husk meringue with corn mousse truly was divine.  At $19, it was quite expensive, too, and small.  Disappointed that they were out of the black matcha latte.

The inside of cosme is modern and minimal. It feels comfortable and the seating is very open. We came with a reservation made a couple days before and it was probably a good idea to do so as it was packed at 12:30 on a Sunday.

The inside was thoughtfully designed as the light strikes each table exactly.

We started with a cocktail as we asked the waiter for some recommendations. I don't recall the name but there is horchata in it and it was good.

You would think it's standard for there to be guac on a menu at a Mexican restaurant but Cosme offers it as a special. From other people's yelp pics, it seems to always be offered - maybe it's a marketing thing. We ordered it anyways and it was pretty good! The chips were super thin and large, I wish they gave us more chips with it.

We also got the Seafood, which is presented covered with a large chip (same as ones from guac). They described this dish as a ceviche, which makes sense as the raw fish is soaked in citrus juice and there are some spices in it. This dish was pretty good but nothing out of the ordinary.

The epazote and mushroom quesadillas were quite different. The epazote was explained to us as a mint quesadilla, but it was really just a cheese empanada with a piece of mint inside. We didn't really taste the mint at all. The mushroom quesadilla had quite a few different mushrooms in it and it tasted really good.

You have the option of choosing a green with chicken or red with egg chilaquiles. We went with the green with chicken. The chicken didn't taste that flavorful, but the sauce made up for it. The chips were quite thin and made it a bit difficult to pick up the sauce and chicken with. I've recently had chilaquiles elsewhere and definitely prefer thicker chips. 

The dish we (or at least two out of the three us) were anticipating the most was the lamb barbacoa. The portion was massive and the large bowl presentation was nice, but the flavor was lacking and beyond disappointing. It tasted like the lamb was just cooked with no flavor at all. My friend said select pieces that were fatty were tasty...

We finished with the husk meringue corn mousse. I'm not the biggest fan of meringue, but the flavor of the corn mousse was interesting and tasted good.

The service was attentive. One of our friends eats like a kid and made a mess after each plate which the waiter always cleaned up. The only confusing thing is that it seemed like we had no set waiter. 

Overall, I didn't find cosme that special.

I am so confused how this restaurant was so highly rated. I stopped in on Sunday for a quick bite, expecting something phenomenal with all its accolades and swanky look. The food was terrible. I had the lobster that I could not bite through. I hope they have cameras in this restaurant so they can rewind the videos and possibly catch me on tape fighting with the lobster in my mouth- It was like tearing into rubber, so tough even the knife that they provided would not cut through- I am not exaggerating on the level of rubber texture . I also must have ordered mole soup. I think there was duck that was part of the meal but it was more like mole soup and a few bites of shredded duck. The flavors were not there. Between trying to chew on a rubbery lobster and fishing in the bowl for the supposed duck, lost among the mole soup, I didn't get any taste of whatever they were trying to execute/sell. Service was inattentive, my server barely was able to explain the menu or he could not be bothered with me asking couple questions- the menu only lists about 3 ingredients in the dish so you have no idea what you are ordering. I would skip and not give into this hype or accolade. If i didn't say it enough... here I go, terrible food and terrible service.

Cosme is one of the best restaurants in the city. We went on Christmas Eve and it was overall amazing! We would definitely recommend the duck (probably our favorite entree) and the signature dessert (husk meringue), which is our entire families favorite dessert now. Totally loved it!!!

It is not often one can say they taste the love and effort put into every dish but this is one such restaurant. I can see why Chef Daniela Soto-Innes won the James Beard Rising Star Chef of the Year Award in 2016. After experiencing this contemporary approach to Mexican food, one would get no argument from me if you told me that Mexico was the food capital of the world. 

We followed the suggestions of our wonderful service team Carlos and Alejandra who were friendly, knowledgeable and who took joy in explaining the techniques and ingredients used in each dish. Each dish was spot on. The duck carnitas were divine and you could taste the fact that the duck was prepared with love over the course of 4 days. I made sure to savor every morsel of the duck that was fall apart tender. The sweet corn tlayuda, king trumpet, cured NY cheddar, chanterelle that we had as an appetizer had the appearance of a mini pizza but to call it pizza would be an injustice as this was one of the best mushroom dishes I have ever had. The guacamole was simply amazing and again, one could taste the freshness and complexity and thought that went into this creation. Finally, for desert we had the corn husk meringue and my wife, who does not like meringue in general, was glad to equally share it with me and called it one of the most original and best deserts she has ever had. I was scraping the plate for every last bite. 

Cosme is Mexican food like we have never had before but which we will certainly have again real soon. 5 well deserved stars as you can taste the love, imagination and thought that went into every dish. Thanks again to all for a very amazing dinner.  Cosme is now my all time favorite Mexican restaurant and what I will use as my baseline in comparing all others.

Dishes ordered: 

Red Mole 
Sweet corn tlayuda (amazing) 
Flat iron steak (could've been cooked better for my taste, it was too rare) 
Dessert: Sorbe duo 

The reason why I am giving it a four star is because the service could've been better, it was quite slow and it wasn't a busy night. We came in expecting a top notch customer service being that this is a top 25 best restaurant in the world. I've been to Pujol before and I understand Chef Olvera's expectations.

I enjoyed my experience at Cosme! All the dishes were well executed and full of different dimensions of flavors. Service could have been more attentive but the food was on point so we left happy. We tried:

Lamb belly tacos with pickled radish - I have never tried lamb with tangy crunchy radish but it was surprisingly very very good. The dish came with warm soft tacos, which complement the crispness of the radish very well. 

Striped bass with a sweetened bean paste - This dish was very good. The bass fillets were fatty and melted in every bite, which went well with the bean paste.

Abalone tostada - this was a little difficult to eat because the abalone was quite tough

Husk meringue with corn mousse - this is their signature dessert and I love anything made of corn so had to try it. It did not disappoint! There is an extra layer of smokiness from the corn husk, which made it even better.

Avocado ice cream - I liked the avocado cream part but the shaved ice that topped it was a little sweet for me. 

Overall a really good experience and would love to come back to try their other dishes!
Food was ehhh but expensive in small dishes. Better places to go in that area.  Would not go back even if someone else was paying the bill.

Came here for brunch the other day and was prepared for what to expect after reading all the reviews. And you know what, I am to blame, Cosme is overpriced, the portions are very small and the cocktails are ridiculously expensive. To make matters worse the food wasn't even that great. One dish which we thought wasn't up to par was the Duck Enmoladas, everybody in our party thought the Mole which was supposed to be sweet and spicy had a bitter sour after taste to it.
Needless to say after spending $60 a person plus tip for brunch and leaving hungry we will never be back.

So its been over a month which I feel is proper time to evaluate my experience because I initially left very confused. I believe Cosme represents the hurdle that "most" people feel prevents them for enjoying fine dining as a hobby. While everything that we had tasted fine- the experience was not worth the equivalent of two business class tickets to Mexico City. The inside was done I am sure by some "trendy" architect/ lighting designer and the chef does what she does well; this is not a critique of her- but rather the owner Enrique Olvera. Its clear that there is no shame in exploiting the "cool" factor- as a Latina I know what Mole is and it is not something to charge $40 on its own. Mole is suppose to blend with other meats and vegetables. It pains me that Olvera goes on Chef's table and talks about his mole sauce at pujol like this is a concept that he created himself. This has been done- and done well by the Mexican people for hundreds of years. The difference is that these people didn't come from wealthy backgrounds and exploit it. In the end I hope Olvera is putting some of the money from his restaurants back into the country that gave him everything

- On the flip side Mexican food in NYC while scarce-does exist! Get on the 7 train and take yourself to Casa Enrique. Worth the trip through Queens borough plaza.

Just had an amazing meal at Cosme. The duck really is to die for, and the black sesame yogurt is mouth watering! Why not a 5-star review then? Cause I'm still hungry!! What is up with the ridiculously small portion sizes?! Call me cheap, but I don't think a $98 meal should leave me starving?! ‍

Tried to write a review last month after a terrible experience: TLDR this place is not gluten free / safe for celiacs despite what they say. I got violently ill hours after eating here despite talking to the waiter about my allergy. I called the manager and he was extremely rude and dismissive, completely different from other restaurants when I have had this issue in the past. Oh, this was also a birthday meal where we spent over $500. Thanks for the hospitality. 

The food is fine but very small portions for the price. After this ordeal, I am not surprised to hear they got passed for a Michelin Star yet again. I won't be back and I would think twice about eating here if you have any sort of allergy. They are nasty.

If you are into paying outrageous prices for tiny portions, and feeling entirely underwhelmed by the food and experience, then this is the place for you.

For starters, I have no issue paying top dollar for good food and experience. However, I do have an issue with paying top dollar for tiny portions, mediocre food and leaving hungry -- which is exactly what Cosme is.

With all of the excellent dining options in NYC, there is no reason whatsoever to go to Cosme. The portions, combined with the pricing, leaves the customer feeling ripped off and hungry when you leave. There are much better options in NYC and would strongly suggest going elsewhere.

Don't come hungry-I'm so glad I had eaten a full meal just before. The portions are very small and almost insultingly expensive. This restaurant is really about the art of how food tastes rather than presentation of food or filling you up. It's the #25 restaurant in the world, though, so it should definitely be on on your food bucketlist. 

We got the abalone tostada, crab infladita, cobia al pastor, nixtamalized honey nut squash, flat iron streak, and husk meringue for dessert. Looking back, it might have made more sense to split the duck carnitas as our main dish. Overall, the combination of flavors was interesting and my favorite was the crab infladita.

The service was outstanding, on the other hand. We were well taken care of and the staff was very pleasant, genuine, and waited on us hand and foot without being too intrusive.

The menu doesn't have any descriptions and everything is so bizarre I had to try to google items. We ordered the steak and the fork and knives are so bad I couldn't cut through it. Then some bowl with what looked like lily pads came and some yellow mushy goop on a tortilla. Overall overpriced and completely confusing.
No-fun Mexican with laughably tiny pricey portions.  Menu was very limited.  Unhelpful staff in regards to menu selection.

You get what you pay for. And unlike other reviewers, we did not find the prices "outrageous" (for NYC fine dining!). Could this be one of the better spots in the City (of course Alta is a bit better and pricier)?

We had the Arctic char, burrata, and lamb barbacoa. All were spectacular - especially the barbacoa that can easily be shared by 3 or 4. 

We finished with 2 orders of churros with chocolate. Our mistake - one order would have been plenty.

Damages for a party of 3 with tip was $225. Note that only 2 alcoholic drinks were involved so our bill could easily have been $300 for this lunch.

Food          5/5
Service      5/5
Value         5/5
Cleanliness  5/5
Noise         5/5 (you can chat)
Decor         5/5 (and tables are not on top of each other)

Still absolutely incredible -- some of my absolute favorite food anywhere.

Most recent visit, we got the sweet corn tlayuda, crab infladito, duck carnitas, and two desserts: the husk meringue and Mexican chocolate. I don't think there was a single bite that wasn't among the best you can get anywhere in NYC. The duck carnitas and husk meringue are staples, but this was the first time we had gotten those other dishes, and all of them were incredible, particularly the tlayuda, which really blew us away.

Yes, the food is crazy expensive, but there's just nothing else like this place (besides for Atla, obviously...). Worth every penny.

I really liked Cosme. It's definitely on the higher end of prices / very difficult to get a reservation, but the food here is solid and the vibe is very good. The duck tacos are definitely the standout thing to get here, but nothing will really go wrong.

We walked in without a reservation, not a good idea on a Saturday night. The hostess could probably work a little more on explaining your options, anyways. We headed to the bar where Issac and Parker were beyond amazing, they orchestrated an incredible experience despite how busy the bar was. We will absolutely come back!

I am overwhelmed with shock that this place got onto the World's Top 50 restaurant list and received a Michelin Star!

First of all, we had to wait 15 minutes for our table which was fine. After being seated, service was slow and underwhelming. The waiter didn't take time to explain the dishes.

All that could be forgiven if the food amazed my wife and I but every dish was so poor in terms of taste and very bland.

The guacamole was so uninspiring that a 10 year old could probably make a better version with more zing.

The crab was ok but under-seasoned and very ordinary, not special.

The sweet corn dish was very disappointing. Cold, bland and something that seemed to come out of a microwave.

Now to the worst part, the flat iron steak. This dish had my jaw dropped. We were served a bland piece of steak with nothing else but a bowl of cold grilled onions.

I also asked for my wife's sea bass to be served at the same time as the steak as she doesn't eat beef and they completely forgot. Our waiter was hard to get hold of.

All in all, this place is over-priced. The venue itself is done nicely but the service and food is extremely poor. My wife and I have had the pleasure of dining at some of the best restaurants in the City and Cosme is not at all in the same league as them, let alone other one star restaurants.

You're more likely to be satisfied at Chipotle.

@Michelin have lost their way and dropped their standards.

Mohit Dhillon
Very good neighborhood place! I like it's sister restaurant in Mexico City (Pujol) better but this is still one of the best Mexican place in town!

PLEASE READ - I had an absolutely terrible experience at Cosme and got violently sick, but the experience I had after with management was deplorable. I have celiac disease and Cosme is known for having a gluten free friendly menu. While I explained my dietary restrictions to our waiter, he had a cavalier attitude and assured me the menu was "mostly okay." I got violently sick like clockwork later that night. I spoke to management today to explain my experience. The manager was extremely dismissive and did not seem to think there was any way his restaurant could have caused my symptoms. Despite the fact that I mentioned I was there with my family to celebrate my BIRTHDAY of all things, he did absolutely nothing to try to improve my experience or make me want to return ever again.

For anyone with dietary restrictions esp. gluten sensitivities who thinks Cosme is a good option - THINK AGAIN. You can get very sick eating here and management couldn't care less. In fact they will continue to say they are gluten free despite evidence to the contrary. This has been very different from my experiences with other restaurants who have been much kinder. No wonder they missed getting a Michelin Star yet again - the management here is sub par.
Hard reservation to secure, but wanted to try it for a while. The space is very cool. Food is inventive and excellent. All dishes are shared, and are quite small and expensive. The service was great.

wow! we got a little excited our first night in town last weekend. ordered one of everything on the menu. including dessert. 

for three of us, it was a lot of food. i was impressed we ate almost everything! the waiter advised us each to have one of one of the crab infladita, which was everyone's least favorite it turns out, so i could have done without that. 

FAVORITE things: abalone tostada, scallop aguachile, sweet corn tlyauda, squash tamal, endive w aycote beans

flat iron steak was OK. a little bland and not as tender as expected, mole... well i don't like mole, but i'm glad we tried it.

i was too full when the duck came around but the boys raved about it & luckily our friend took the leftovers!

anything else on the dinner menu i didn't mention was not bad, just not memorable.

dessert: husk meringue was UNREAL. mexican chocolate i will dream about. sorbets were wonderful too. 

the staff was perfect about timing all the dishes. quickly explaining what each was & disappearing. 

agua miel cocktail was so yummy, balanced. benny blanco was very refreshing too. 

only docked one star for the hostesses, who i can only describe as curt & useless. 

overall, great dining experience.

There's much hype about this place coming off of Chef's Table with Enrique. The food is very tasty and artfully composed, but it's really quite pricey and portions are small. It's definitely playing off all the buzz knowing folks will want to come and try it out.

The duck carnitas is no joke at $90 for the order, but it is very, very good. Great flavor and they leave just a bit of fat which pairs so well with the richness of the duck. Luckily this is quite a good sized dish to share with the table. It was fantastic and paired of course with handmade beautiful corn tortillas.

I'd say it was worth trying out, but not likely going back for a while.

Interesting is the operative word....I think the problem with this place for me is my undeveloped palette.....Not generally a fan of lamb BUT it was delicious. The coffee and liquor drink was literally unbelievable.... atmosphere and wait staff completely on point... overall a remarkable brunch experience

I've been a quarter way through my life and never have I been so disappointed. Not even when I received my fine arts degree that cost 250,000 that was more worth it than this food for ants. Ruined my birthday and starved me have to sleep in the streets tonight. Dios Mio

Very expensive and food is sub par. Out of the 6 dishes we got, around 2 were actually flavorful/worth it. Cocktails are mediocre. Service is not the best- food took a while, they forgot to put parts of our food order in, they tried to take plates away while literally still eating, still food on the plate. Not worth it- so expensive - go to a taco truck and you will eat better Mexican food. 

I wanted to like it, but we were so disappointed. Save your money.

I love this place so much. I went fo the 2nd time last night with my best friend and my boyfriend. It's a bit pricy, but I think it's 1000% worth it. I love the ambiance and the decor and the food is to die for. 

Sweet corn tlayuda - I LOVED this, it's sweet and savory and crunchy. I could probably eat this everyday for the rest of my life. 

Lamb belly - So delicious. I was trying to decide between this and the fish and I'm so glad I went with the lamb. It comes with tortillas so you can make yummy little tacos. Big fan.  

Husk meringue - if you don't get anything else from Cosme, you must get this. One of my favorite desserts ever. My only regret is not ordering two of them. 

Also for those who are gluten free, this place is a hidden gem. My boyfriend has celiacs and is severely allergic to gluten. The entire dinner menu is gluten free and it was so refreshing to be able to eat somewhere together where everything on the menu was safe and he didn't have to worry about getting sick.
Love the atmosphere and food. Duck tacos were amazing. A little pricey but worth the experience!

The food was overpriced but pretty good. 

The whole experience was spoiled by a bartender who was very unfriendly and arrogant.
I felt angry because when I go to an upscale restaurant I expect to be treated in a nice way without being pissed off. Good food can't go with bad service.
For such expensive dishes, the taste just isn't good enough. Service is great though.

Cosme is a winner!! It was my first time eating at a fine dining Mexican restaurant and I was thoroughly impressed. The service was top notch, the atmosphere was lively and bright without being unpleasantly loud, and most importantly, the food was incredible.

I got to taste a number of items from the menu but the dishes that stood out to me most were: 

Crab Infladita: I believe this is a new item and it is so so so good, probably my favorite thing I tried (aside from the dessert)

Duck Carnitas: Yes, you must order this. So tender it practically melts in your mouth! 

Husk Meringue: I'm not a huge meringue (or corn) person, so I wasn't super excited about this but WOW this was truly life changing. Don't even bother eating here if you're not going to order this!!

Overall, I was extremely impressed with my experience at Cosme. Though it is pricey (even by NYC standards), its so worth it.

This is expensive for what it is.  I know that they are the top restaurants in the world list so I guess that's why they can get away with it.  My wife took me here for my birthday.  Cocktails in the beginning were good.  The guy who helped us with drinks was very nice.  We had the duck carnitas, kobia al pastor and a squash dish that was delicious.  The short rib was bleh.
