The service was ok.  Honestly this is a visit once say that you have been... but likely don't go back to.  

Also don't ask for more chips because they charge you extra money for them without telling you.

Pricey, yes; but a wonderful dinner experience.  Incredible service and hospitality.  Stark walls as the food is the show.  Low lighting gives the place an earthy and primal atmosphere. 

I had the scallops and lamb's belly.  Lamb was excellent! Looking to return for the duck carnitas.

Can't understand why this is touted as one of the world's best restaurants.  $94 duck carnitas should be mind blowing but they weren't.  They were moist.. but flavorless. And nothing that came with it did much to improve the flavor.   I give it a solid "meh". Not worth the effort, price tag or the calories.  Some dishes were good like the mini mushroom pizza but all were too expensive and not really anything super special.  The only thing I really enjoyed were the scallops and the husk dessert. That saved the whole meal for me.  Service was not great. Waiter hovered over me with bad breath.

A great restaurant that continues to be underrated. It is a rare day when a restaurant is not just nourishing but thought provoking, and this place achieves that. This isn't just Mexican food, it's not even just food. There is a message that this place has for the city and the world, and they just happen to have chosen a medium that tastes good to share this message. It is evident a lot of thought went into the simplest of details. I've been here a few times, and I will concede it can be hit or miss on some of the food, but there are definitively options that can be competitive for best dish in the city on every single visit. The environment is always top notch - I even managed to sit next to a certain saxophone based celebrity on my second visit (Kenny G).

This is the rare restaurant that can be competitive with the best restaurants in the world (worthy of its current ranking of 25th in the world), but also humble and (most importantly) the kind of place that will leave you with cravings for subsequent visits. 

Don't miss this place.
Expensive. Small plates and good luck figuring out what you're eating. Great service though

We were back again for our fav duck carnitas last night, only to find that the portion has halved, the price has increased (now $98 for a dish that is barely shareable) - and that even the smaller plates had shrunk in size but prices were the same. I'm not sure what happened but I hope things go back to the way they were and soon!

I'm completely completely disappointed with that dinner. Starting to we missed one of the dishes ordered, and one of the bottles of wine. When we finished our glasses of the first bottle, none refilled them. I had to ask for it.

The food was overall good. The duck carnitas were delicious, but being one of the 50 best restaurants in the world I expected so much more. A better service and better food. We tried almost all the dishes they offered and none blew my mind.

And the WORST THING was that I was super specific doing the reservation and the confirmation, letting them know how special that dinner would be. That dinner was my wedding present for my two best friends, and the birthday present for him, after not seeing each other for years. And they didn't do any single thing special. Not even a tiny chocolate saying congratulations.

I got out of the restaurant feeling sad, angry, and sorry for them at the same time.

Short version: overpriced, way below average food, not friendly staff

Long version: Cosme was on my list for a long time, finally I made a reservation for 9pm for 4 people (weekday). It was 9.20 when we finally seated, it was annoying since the wait time for walk ins were only 30 mins... When it came to order we asked for suggestions but there was no help. Finally we ordered grilled octopus, king crab, guacamole, scallops and duck to share. Other than the duck everything was just bad. Octopus was ice cold, king crab dish was cold, small and not seasoned well, scallop was raw and not marinated (basically just scallops with some sauce), guac was half mashed avocado with some herbs on top. Duck was pretty good, nicely cooked and served with onion, cilantro and two different sauces. After dinner we ordered husk meringue, caramelized cacao butter and Mexican chocolate, I'm not sure what we were thinking... Meringue wasn't cooked at all it was more like whipped cream, cacao butter was an unnecessarily complicated dish and wasn't good at all, Mexican chocolate was as bad as a chocolate dish can be. We also tried three different cocktails (gin based cocktail, strawberry and rhubarb) non of them was good. There are tons of better restaurants in NYC, do yourself a favor and don't go to Cosme. It just doesn't worth it.

Ah Cosme, my go-to restaurant if I want a reliable meal and drink. Yes, it's overpriced, but who can resist the duck carnitas? I've been here so many times I've lost count, but no longer order anything beyond multiple margaritas and the duck carnitas, so I'm not the best authority on the rest of the food probably... but here goes:

The Good: 
- The duck carnitas, the star of the show, the dish I dream of on a monthly basis. 
- The margaritas are great, always reliable. 
- Fun, trendy environment!

The Not So Good: 
- Unremarkable service (except the somehow clairvoyant bartender, who brought out my drink a mere .2 seconds after I ordered it...). Service is there, but nothing to write home about at all...
- Some dishes I've occasionally ordered outside the carnitas have been underwhelming. There was a raw fish appetizer that was inedible, and the chips & guac are not good-- stale chips and totally unseasoned guacamole. 
- Value for money leaves a lot to be desired.

I can't believe I'm giving a restaurant a 4 star solely on one dish, but I can't fathom giving it anything below this. Not sure why, but Cosme holds a special place in my heart. I would recommend going once for the experience, and maybe you'll get just as hooked as I am. 

Food: 9/10 for the duck, 6/10 for everything else...
Service: 6/10 
Ambiance: 8/10

Overall: 7.8/10

The negative review is really value for money.  $58 for a mocktail and a bowl of mole. 

Had read good things about the food, so stopped here for a quick bite at the bar.  Easily found a seat and ordered a mocktail as suggested by the bartender.  Delicious!  

Ordered the mole for $30, assuming, Yes, that's a lot for 1 dish, but it's mole sauce, which done right, is very complicated and laborious.  Comes out and it is no joke, a plate with mole sauce, some greens and 4 tortillas.  That's it.  No protein. No other sides.  I almost asked if this was legitimately all there was, but chalked it up to, this is a typical over-hyped, overpriced trendy spot.

To be fair, the mole was amazing, but I basically had to spoon it into my mouth like a soup.  They also charged me full price for the drink ($18) despite it not having the alcohol in it.  Cherry on top.

Great if you're here on the company's or someone else's dime, but I would never go here again on my own.

Cosme is responsible for my favorite meal I've had in more than 15 trips to NYC. Vibe is dark and trendy while the food and drinks are top notch. Enrique Olvera really knows what upscale Mexican cuisine is. The must-orders? The Cobia Al Pastor (probably one of the 3 best dishes I've ever had) and the Corn Husk Meringue (of course). It's not inexpensive, but it's absolutely worth it. This spot is great for the special date night or business dinner, but you'll want to come back as often as you think of how delicious the food was.

The menu could be broader, especially for a tapas-type place, plus tiny portions at inflated prices. Also, as others have pointed out the service was B+ when it should be A+ for the cost. Our table was in the back corner-too dark and RIGHT next to the waiters' station so there was always someone behind my chair putting orders in. BTW my server did  not know what seltzer was; finally understood when I asked for sparkling water.
Excellent food, good service, nice atmosphere, and warm decoration. One of my to go places.

4.5 for the food, 2 starts for our waiter who was an a-hole. Wish I remembered his name. 

Duck Carnitas dish was cooked exceptionally well and we really enjoyed it. Drinks were great as well. 

Waiter was pushing hard for us to basically order the entire menu. We ended up with a starter, duck carnitas, and a dessert and were stuffed. The waiter was crazy to think we should have ordered 2 more things. Waiter started giving us attitude when thats all we ordered, and rolled his eyes at my wife when she didn't want a second drink. 

Anyways, worth going to but the waiter prevented this from being a special dinner.

We had the cobia al pastor which was one of my favorites. The pineapple puree with the cobia and pretty much anything else was so yummy. We also had the flat iron steak and the duck carnitas. Everything was  delicious even the margaritas. I can't wait to go back.
Long waits and rarely an actual table is available but the duck tacos and palomas make it worth it.

Pretty tasty food. It's a bit pricey and the line was long but we got lucky and got seated quickly. Both the food and drinks were very good and tasted great. If it was slightly cheaper it'd be 5 stars.

Getting no.25 restaurant in the world is a very high standard for NYC restaurants. Unfortunately living in NYC for 20 years make me to not give this place more then 2 stars.  The food was mediocre. The cocktails were good.  The service was so so. Our waiter was nice but I.e filling my glass of water and spilling water in the table more then once is not no.25 in the world. Serving coffee and no spoon but I am stirring with a fork is not no. 25 quality. The special desert was very very low quality. A variety of sweets and very little taste. There is a lot of great Mexican places in NYC and besides the lamb dish which was good the rest was mediocre. I was disappointed after the overall experience

I'm surprised this place was ranked number 25 in the world?! The ambiance is simple/modern.  Didn't fit with the Mexican fusion food.  The guacamole was great, but it went downhill from there.  The raw scallops tasted fishy and not fresh- we sent them back (I have never sent back food before!).  The steak was bland/simple.  The duck carnitas was "okay" but definitely not worth the $90.  Service was good.  I won't be coming back.  Place way too overpriced.

Not a bad restaurant, but not a great one. I mean, if it's rated 25 on world's 50 best and the fame of chef Olvera has, you expect much better. Ambiance is nice but a bit too dark for my taste. A suggestion, order wine bc cocktails are just ok. Some of the food can be good, some dishes aren't structured well enough, some lack seasoning. We had several dishes, it's more like a tapas style kind of place, which was good since we were a party of 4. Service is very good even though it was a very busy night. We shared about 10 different dishes and 3 desserts. Best dishes were duck carnitas and tlayuda with morels. IMO 3.5 stars.

Cosme is a good restaurant, but like most reviewers I don't think it deserves to be a top 50 restaurant. During my visit I tried the following:

1. Horchata with nuez - The horchata was decent and so was the price 

2. Egg sope - The best dish I had at Cosme. You can really taste the corn tortilla. The beans were great. The egg was perfectly made. The salsa verde was well prepared and had a distinct taste. 

3. Duck with Mole - I'm not a mole expert, but I do think it could've been better. I'm not sure how it is traditionally served in Mexico, but I didn't like that the tortillas were already place inside the mole/dish. 

4. Fish dish - disappointing. The fish was very bland and the texture was too soft. It came with a sauce and it had nothing special about it. It tasted good when prepared as fish tacos, but totally not worth the price. 

Costumer service: customer service was great. We got stuck in traffic and called that we were going to be late. They were responsive and accommodating. 

Ambience: The decor was nice, but I also expected more. I liked the minimalist exterior with the name of the restaurant in small letter against a matte background. 

I would definitely come again for the sope and would be willing to try their other dishes.

The Cosme of Enrique Olvera fame is too pretentious IMO. If you want real Enrique Olvera, I would suggest getting a ticket to Mexico City, way more cost effective. But the desserts here are quite delightful, that I recommend highly!

The two of us shared four dishes - arctic char tostada, chicken chilaquiles, duck enmolada, and the enfrijolada. The arctic char was decent, but it was nothing I would choose to come back for; the chilaquiles were the only things that I would want to have again, and it is probably the most simplistic dish.

However, I mentioned a food sensitivity while ordering, and it was only after the dishes came out that the server mentioned that food item was in the mole sauce. Let's just say that I took a few bites that I probably shouldn't have. It would have been nice to ask about allergies and then warn the person before the food comes out that it included that ingredient.

We were seated almost at the time of our reservation, and the service was impeccable. We had drinks at the bar while we waited as we arrived a bit early. The mixed drinks were good, but we were surprised that the beer cost almost as much as the mixed drinks.

Overall, I would probably not return. It was okay, but I think there is much better food throughout New York.

The food I had here was so good, I think back to my experience at least once a week. We made a reservation a week before coming and was seated within minutes of arriving. I loved everything I ordered (except for the white wine I got). Although I did find it difficult talking over all the other loud conversations and music in the restaurant. 

For drinks, I got white wine and my boyfriend got the paloma (delicious). For appetizer, we ordered the cobia al pastor which came with soft tacos. I loved the combination of the mango puree and jalapeno with the fish. We then got the duck carnitas ($94 for two people, and I'd say it was worth it). I can't even describe how great it was! The meat falls apart upon putting your fork into it. It was so tender! It was topped with onions and radish. I liked how it also came with soft tacos to eat with the duck. The two of us couldnt even finish it and took it to-go. For dessert, we shared the corn husk meringue. I was a little sad that I didnt get to crack it open myself to see the cream ooze out, but I guess I could let that pass. You can really taste the corn. It was so good we considered ordering another one.

I share the same sentiment as most of the other yelpers. The food is good, but definitely not the 25th best restaurant in the world. 

We made reservations for 9pm, but we weren't seated until close to 9:30pm ... that already was a terrible start 

Dishes to definitely order:
- Sweet corn tlayuda, king trumpet, cured NY cheddar, black truffles ($48) - this was good but we got NO black truffles ... what the??... 
- Duck Carnitas 
- Lamb Belly 
- Corn Husk 

Dishes that are meh:
- Scallops
- Sea Bass (this entree is Tiny) 
- the other two desserts we got (black sesame was good but it came with a scoop of yogurt but when they mixed omg don't do it)

Cosme never fails! Great ambiance. I am very impressed with all their unique flavored dishes. Each time I go there - I always like to try something new! I recommend trying their horchata smoothie and merengue dessert. Absolutely delicious!!

This place was so disappointing. It looks beautiful ,but besides that looks everything else was so underwhelming. The hosts had an attitude, and although we had a reservation and there were some available sports they made us wait. The drinks came twenty minutes after we got our dishes, the dishes were small and flavorless and the wait staff barely explained what they were serving. The dishes were so small and the I got home hungry even though We paid 400 ( before tip) for a table of four. Rip off.
I don't get the hype. The food was pretty good but not wowing. Nothing surprising, but for the price I don't feel the need to go back. Good cocktails, though.

Meh. Have no idea how this place made top 50 restaurants. I left food on the plate and as an son of immigrant parents I never do that. Guacamole was flat, lacked acid and depth. Corn and mushroom tlayuda was too sweet. Abalone tostada was poorly executed. Abalone was too delicate to be put on a corn tostada which was unevenly smothered with sauces that were too salty. The lamb belly was also way too salty. Over cured. 

One of the worst meals for the price I've had in recent memory.  However service was prompt
And attentive.

The watress' explanation to us, a group of large-size male adults, that the dishes are meant to be shared so we could taste a veriety of dishes, while the serving sizes were mostly small to petite, instead of warning us not-to-share and in some cases consider ordering more than one  per person (if the high cost is not an issue) seem to reflect the gap between the hype and the reality of our experience with this restaurant. There were solid signs of the star chef's talents and the ingredients are top notch but the curse of pretentious and sometimes overly sofisticated interpretations of Mexican food (althogh tradition is still there and even strongly presented with food like the amazing tortillas), the trap of modern artistic food presentations, along with the too small portions that were actually unshareable - all ended up with a feeling that we fell into another expensive hype trap, in this case of modernized Mexican food. Obviously all of us wanted very much not to have this feeling but it ended up, unfortunately, as less than expected type of experience and a very expensive one if you want to have fun and not leave hungry.

I am pretty baffled at the recognition of Cosme as one of the top 50 restaurants in the world. While service was top notch (our waiter was incredibly prompt, friendly, and knowledgeable) and the atmosphere was nice, I expected far more. Overall, I found it too pricey to not have my socks completely knocked off. 

My party of three shared a few menu items, with the only two standout fixtures being the octopus and lamb belly. We ordered the razor clams which should have 100% been served in their shell. Instead, the clams were chopped up into microscopic pieces and masked entirely by an overpowering blend of herbs and green chorizo. 

Furthermore, it seemed like the accouterments (bland, blue corn tortilla which tasted like something out of a bag and hot sauce which tasted like Valentina to me) added nothing. Poached jicama also made its way into multiple dishes (scallops and lamb belly) and brought nothing to the table.

I'm not writing this review to complain, but I sincerely hope that Cosme management will take this as constructive criticism and improve menu items for the better. There is definitely room for improvement IMHO.

Amazing lunch! This is the first time in a long time that I've eaten at a place with 3.5 stars on yelp, and I couldn't disagree with the rating more. We followed the recommendations and got the cobia (sooo tasty), the duck carnitas (great and sizable portion), and the corn husk dessert - all delicious. Also had a drink with Elijah Craig and mezcal which was a perfect "fancy cocktail"

Too expensive to not be impressed. Would not return. 

Had the octopus, that was in such a tart broth, that you could not sip it from the spoon. I checked with the waiter to make sure this was not a mistake, and he assure me it wasn't. Surprised by that. 

Had their signature Duck taco dish. Duck looked great, but it was forgettable, not well seasoned. 

the best dish was this dessert that looked liked a cracked egg.

Cosme is an unfortunate case of an ethnic cuisine given the New York treatment - that is, overhyped and overpriced to the extent that the food that made the restaurant so good in the first place is crushed under the weight of expectation and criticism.

Let us not bury the lede - Cosme has some excellent interpretation of modern Mexican cuisine. The cobia al pastor ($27), sweet corn tyaluda ($48), and duck carnitas ($94) are all inspired and delicious - especially the tlayuda. However, at their respective price points, it is hard to justify spending all that much money on what amount to appetizer-sized portions, even if they are to share. Even the legendary corn husk meringue is a tough sell, as innovative as it may be.

What sadly defined my Cosme experience most of all was the wine service. We had requested a bottle on the menu, but were presented with a different vintage altogether, with a weak explanation from the maitre d' that they had run out of the vintage listed. This was most unprofessional from a distinguished restaurant such as Cosme, and the rest of the dinner simply did not do enough to make up for this misstep.
good and creative food. has been a long time since i went and have not felt desire to go back. but i did enjoy it.

Back in New York, let's try # 25 in the world Cosme. It started as simple when we're in the Appetizer portion and really feeling it but Wowowee when we got to the Mina Course. The Steak was fabulous. The Ranchero was terrriiificcc. I recommend it. Thank you for the experience.

Came here because I heard it was one of the top 25 restaurants (in the world?) and it had a Michelin Star, AND it was one of the cheaper Michelin Star restaurants. I was really looking forward to it but was disappointed at the value compared to cost.

The waiters and servers were great. They knew the whole menu and was enthusiastic about some of the dishes.

The dishes themselves varied in quality. The guacamole was DElicious but not worth $17. Though I guess that's what you'd expect at a Michelin restaurant?
My favorite dish was the Cobia al pastor with pineapple purée and cilantro. Apparently this is traditionally a pork dish, but they used a white fish. It was very soft and all the little garnishes complemented the purée. My favorite bites!
We also got the razor clams, flat iron steak, and endives which were okay.
We really wanted to get the duck carnitas because we were this was one of the famous dishes at Cosme, but it was $94 (WAY past our budget) so we settled on a lamb dish. This was a mistake. The three of us all disliked this dish. Lamb was super salty, and the purée did not play well with the other ingredients on the dish.
We had the famous husk meringue for dessert. Delicious!

Every dish ranged from $17-40ish (most were $20-30ish), which is more expensive than we originally thought.

Overall, it's a decent place. If you really want the experience of a Michelin Star restaurant you can come here. But I honestly don't think it's worth the price. It's fancy, for sure, but I can think of a handful of other places I'd rather spend my money on.

Is the food at Cosme super duper tasty? Absolutely. Does Cosme deserve its distinction as the 25th best restaurant in the world? That's where it gets tricky. The food at Cosme is superb, but the problem is that I can recall several meals at other NYC establishments that have been better. Your expectations at Cosme are through the roof, as they should be, but you're not getting some haughty tasting menu like you would at other Top 50s. If you watch Chef's Table you'll hear that Olvera wanted to counter the notion that the best Mexican food is found on the streets, but no matter how good and over-the-top Cosme is, I've 100% had better tacos before (like at Hija Sanchez in Copenhagen). 

Started with chips and guacamole. Nothing life-changing here, but if you're in the mood then go for it.

The best savory dish was, by far, the corn and chanterelles. We originally ordered one to share, but it was absurdly good so we ordered a second.

I actually liked the abalone tostada but the rest of my family wasn't too pumped about it. I wasn't too crazy about the cobia al pastor, which is basically a DIY fish taco, but my family seemed to like it. 

The lamb belly was excellent. The seabass was okay.

Looking for the most pretentious dish on the menu? It's the mole. Again, if you have watched the episode you know what you're in for. Spoiler alert: it's just sauce on a plate. It's dolled up with some greens and tortillas on the side. I thought I needed to order this but I was wrong. Just don't. It's so bad and bitter, and you'll be down 30ish dollars for absolutely no reason.

We were still hungry after ordering about 400 dollars worth of food and drink, so we decided to tack on another hunnid and order 3 desserts. There was a new one that was a take on Mexican chocolate which wasn't bad, but anything with chocolate in it (that isn't Cosme's mole) is usually a heart-eye emoji in my books. We also ordered some pistachio caramel thing. I think that's what it was. It was also good. 

I'll be honest. I was fully prepared to give this place a 3-star review at the end of the meal. But, at dessert, an extra star rose from the ashes. And those ashes were the corn husk meringue. Don't even bother showing up if you're not gonna get dessert. It's one of the best desserts I've ever had. It hits every note: creamy, crunchy, savory, sweet. 

My big takeaway: Enrique Olvera is, indeed, the corn-whisperer. If there's corn in the dish it's probably going to be spectacular (see: corn husk meringue, corn and chanterelle). If you're only coming here because it's on 50 Best, then turn around because you're not getting the obvious ticket. If you really want to try fine dining Mexican done well, then this is the spot.

Really great experience and loved the food. I would highly recommend the following:

Their guacamole and chips is amazing
The Arctic char with the spicy sauce is divine
The corn and chanterelles is the best thing on their menu
The sea bass steamed in the leaf was outstanding

The thing we didn't care for was the fava beans which just lacked balance. Other than that it was a stellar meal though it is definitely on the expensive side even for New York.

So... I was nervous about this place given all the spotty reviews. I started off with two appetizers. The Albaquore and the octopus. I thought they were okay but way too much lemon... and I love lemon... then it was on to the duck. What a game saver. It was fabulous. And the bottle of red wine ... priced at a measly $110 was phenomenal! Phew. This place would not get 4 stars if it wasn't for the Duck. Service was good, nothing out of the ordinary but not bad. I have to say, that I share people's reservations about the rankings and ratings, but the duck was the best I ever had. Of course, it was $96 for two!!!!!

Mediocrity at its finest.. If I could give this place 3.5 stars I would.. 3 seems a little low but it definitely doesn't deserve 4. 

We found this place on a "Best Restaurants in the World" list where it most definitely doesn't belong. It's not bad food or anything, everything we had was "just fine" but nothing to come running back for.. 

The portions were Tiny and incredibly expensive (over priced no matter how you swing it) For dinner for 2 you essentially needed 5 dishes + desert @ around $30 each, with wine and tip landing us @ $300 for a seemingly unmemorable experience. At that price, there's much MUCH better options available in New York, in my opinion.

On a positive note, the desert was delicious and their coffee was really good and the atmosphere was nice.. service was okay too.

This has to be the most expensive taco ever! Seriously, the duck carnitas taco is $94. The portion is large enough to share and it was delicious. Other good dishes are the yellow tail collar tempura taco, the tuna taco with pineapple purée and the flat iron steak. The herbed guacamole and the fava bean tetela are good appetizers. Wonderful flavors at this restaurant so it's worth a visit but probably not worth a repeat visit. Of course, the bar is amazing so be sure to have some tequila or a $17 margarita with those tacos.

Keep an eye on the clock at this place!   A great looking interiors with fantastic food  (albeit tiny portions) is scolded for making table turning way too much of a priority.  Every single staffer..  "Are we waiting on a guest?".... topped off by our waiter (we admitted, upon entry, that my wife was running late) comes up for our entree order like a gruff pizza joint guy...  "LET'S GO!".   Really???    I'm so glad I called him out on a terrible gaffe.   He rightly apologized to salvage his tip.  

SMH.  Why not embrace the attitude by placing a timer on every table?   Spin it into a defining feature.   "Cosme, fine Mexican cuisine.  We guarantee you'll enjoy a fantastic meal and be on your way in 105 minutes.   Perfect for theater goers."

In order to meet our deadline we skipped dessert.  

In spite of this, Cosme, is an excellent Mexican restaurant. 

My time has run out.

Outstanding food and service. Remains one of my favorite restaurants of all time. 

(Side note, since I've read some less-than-impressed reviews here: I think that Americans have a major issue deciphering between Mexican and Tex-Mex, so if you're expecting more Tex-Mex-like flavors that's not what you're going to get, and that's not Mexican. Also keep in mind that this is refined Mexican, so there's a lot of nuance going on; it's not always in-your-face flavors.)

With the most amazing restaurants in NYC, I am baffled at the status of this restaurant. It has ranked number 25 best restaurant in the world. I have been to a lot of these restaurants on that list and I have to say this one is an outlier. The restaurant has a clean minimalistic atmosphere but the service was just sub par. We waited for fifteen mins for someone to greet us after we were seated and finally had my guest go flag someone down where then we had the waiter come and get our drink order. 

The menu is very limited and although they boast that they have vegan and gluten free options, the night we were there - there was only one. It was the mole. By the picture you can see that it was size of an appetizer at best and was more bitter in taste and lacked finesse. I have had some good mole and this was just okay. However, the small homemade tortillas was soooo good and hold up on their own. My partner ordered the sea bass which had no taste and lacked any kind of seasoning and almost seemed just steamed. The plantain mash that accompanied it tasted like really bad baby food and We ended up not ordering anything else after barely finishing the two dishes and headed else where to grab dinner.

Was very excited to try this place. We went without a reservation and snagged a seat in the bar area - totally fine (though the seats were crazy uncomfortable but, we had a seat and we totally expected an uncomfortable experience in the bar so this was all fine). Then we had the menu. We had the duck carnitas which were absolutely fantastic but this place was far and away the most expensive non-fine dining restaurant. Just be warned. This place will charge you the fine-dining per plate prices for a rosa mexicana type experience. The food was good but absolutely not worth the price.

All around, a terrific experience with the Duck Carnitas centerpiece orbited by well executed smaller dishes that effectively serve as supplements leading up to the main event (again, that Duck Carnitas) all presented in a sleek contemporary, earthy, intimately lit, unstuffy atmosphere.  Unapologetically strong and elegantly presently cocktails were a plus... along with the obligatory very sweet Corn Husk Meringue ending.

For those that have only taken an interest following its notoriety on certain 'lists' -- save the trouble and go elsewhere, as it absolutely will not live up to the pretentious (or price) standards of most the rest of the restaurants that typically and predictably dominate those lists.  Otherwise, well worth a visit for the inventive experience.

Love this for true culinary experience for Mexican. It's authentic and breaking the mound of what people always think that Mexican food is. We had some great items, loved the dessert. Had a scrumptious red wine that paired beautifully with the mains. The Bartendar made us something special for a cocktail. Got it going on

Service was very attentive and pleasant.  Discussed several items on the menu with our waiter who was very friendly and informative.  Creative, tasty small entrees; the Duck Carnitas did not disappoint!  Corn husk merengue was out of this world for a light delicious dessert.

My only issue was deciding what to order, because I wanted to try everything! I went for brunch with a group of people. My favorites were the duck enmolada and corn husk meringue. I was hoping to try the lamb barbacoa but the other folks in my party were vegetarian, and the dish is meant to be shared. I would recommend this place to anyone, and hope to come again soon! Can't wait to try the dinner menu next time.

Start with the amazing strawberry tonic ! The aguachile scallops were so fresh and sweet ! The razor clams were divine ! I was a little disappointed with the mole . I know it's delicious on its own( and very complex)but I wish he would have paired it with a protein. Why are the duck carnitas so large ? We need a smaller version of this ... The staff is friendly and helpful with the menu. I actually prefer this location. I also live in Mexico City and  Pujol just seems too stuffy and pretentious... it's lacking the NYC vibe . Well done chef Olvera !

Great mexican food. Little bit over priced but hey, NYC. Guacamole on point, fish, steak and the dessert were all delicious. Service was good too and they took care of explaining the menu, one step at a time.

Wow, this place was amazing.  Menu keeps changing so beware when you look at the old picts.  Just let your waiter be your guide.  And for wine,  get the 'Cava' from Spain.  Great, low price, and clean wine.  Perfect for some the dishes that have a little heat.
Great brunch! Enjoyed the lamb carnitas and the great atmosphere. Great Mexican food experience.

I was reading some magazines on the plane and came across the list of top 50 restaurants and saw that Cosme was in it . Since I had already planned a visit NYC, I wanted to make sure I tried the place out . I looked for reservations online and was surprised to see that they were pretty open for most days and most nights ( which was a red flag )that I obviously ignored. 
Even on the day of the dinner I could book a table for two just an hr ahead of the actual time ( Red Flag no 2 . And then we finally arrive at the restaurant about 20 min early . The host was cordial and checked us in and we waited for our table. The restaurant felt upscale and hip but u know it didn't give the impression of a top 50 restaurant of the world . Then my doubts grew firmer as I looked to see if they had any Michelin stars. Turns out none . I still wanted to give them the benefit of doubt and waited until I tasted the food . It was Mexican food but you don't see the waiters describing the dishes unless asked for . 
We got the abalone tostada , kampachi (ceviche ) in cucumber and Cobia their signature dish, 
Cobia Ofcourse was the best abalone tostada was good , kampachi missed the mark . 
Then I was trying to order a salad but the waiter suggested Duck another one of their signatures. 
It was 94 USD!!!! Well what the heck we are here so we got the duck . 
Duck is a hit or miss like lobster in my opinion so I was in two minds about it. 
But they apparently slow cook it for 9 hrs , so I was hopeful. To my surprise it was actually well cooked, 
tender with cilantro and onions. But was it worth 90 dollars...  I don't think so . 
To finish the meal we had some ( husk meringue another signature )and raspberry pistachio sorbet with cacao butter which was complex to say the least . 

All in all it was like any other decent restaurant, definitely not Michelin level. 
I was gonna brag to my folks that I went to the top 25 th hotel in the World , but Cosme changed my mind .

I made a reservation here after reading it was named one of the top 50 restaurants in the world. In the world??? That sounds pretty amazing and it's right here in New York. We definitely have to try it. I was really excited and even more excited that we got reservations very quickly. Actually I started to get a little confused that I might've been making reservations at the wrong place. How can one of the top 50 restaurants in the world accommodate me so easily? Well they could and we went last night. Our greeters were lovely and status to our table. Almost immediately we were served tortillas which were soggy. Granted it was about 95° in New York last night so we figured the food may have been affected by the temperature.
I had read online to order three dishes for 1 couple. We ordered the clams, the sea bass and another dish.

The food came out rather quickly and although it was lovely it certainly was not extraordinary. I was actually slightly disappointed to be perfectly honest. While we were at the table I double checked that we were in the right restaurant. I still couldn't believe it was named top 50 in the world. Although it was a lovely experience in the food very tasty it was nothing extraordinary. I don't want to criticize too much because I can't say the food was bad but it's certainly didn't wow me too much. We exited the restaurant at 6:58. More than anything I felt that we were rushed through our meal. I was incredibly disappointed after that. Felt like we didn't really have an evening even though our bill was like $200! I ordered a margarita which was a regular old margarita except it was $17!
I never mind paying for good food and drink but this was no experience at all. I am really shocked that it made the list. In retrospect I wondered if we didn't order right or my expectations were too high. But I'm just putting it out there that I've eaten in quite a few dining establishments that have been top notch including some of the Michelin rated restaurants and this was no comparison.

I'm glad we had the experience but I would not go back there nor would I recommend it.

This meal started with such promise and then went downhill. The cobia al pastor, octopus aguachile, and sweet corn tlayuda were just wonderful - elevated Mexican flavors with depth and personality. The remaining items - flatiron steak, grilled manouri and mole rojo just fell flat. The steak had zero Mexican flavors and frankly not much flavor at all. The mole was literally a PLATE OF (underdeveloped) SAUCE with some unseasoned wilted greens and tortillas (and the tortillas, while tasty, will cost you to refill). The cheese was actually quite good but the rest of the salad was so boring and it was just a really weird cheese to choose to grill because it was so crumbly and not oozy.  I feel like we must have missed something that got this restaurant on the list of top 50 restaurants in the world, but the menu's not that big so everything should shine. We skipped dessert because, honestly, nothing sounded even remotely good and our guard was already up after slugging through the second half of the meal. Sorry, Cosme.

The duck carnitas was excellent, albeit a bit pricey. But overall I think this place was just 'ok'.  I didn't leave the place thinking that I had to go back.  The dishes were certainly expensive for tapas style, and each item on the menu had some fancy ingredient that I hadn't heard of before, or it was in another language (and not just Spanish). The cocktails were below average, although one person in our group did say it was one of the best margaritas she's ever had. We were a big group and shared most things on the menu; the best ones were the duck carnitas and the hiramasa tostada.

Fabulous Lunch ... June 26... near perfection on portions and subtle taste! Being from California and spending  a lot of time in mexico - I can appreciate a light hand and seasoning in Mexican food Stateside.  Fresh Flavors and great presentation.. a cool and calming space as well as attentive wait staff... Super glad I was taken for lunch there and would recommend Cosme highly! ( as a matter of fact I already have ! )

Being a devout foodie, living in food heaven, NYC, I ran to check out Cosme after the release of 2018 top 50 restaurant list. It was an utterly disappointing experience. The service is not what one would expect for a top 50, not of this price range.  Our waiter could barely describe the dishes, to answer our request for details on the dishes, he just reread what was already printed on the menu. By far, the most disappointing components of the experience all relate to the food - small portions, barely interesting flavors, etc. If you want a good laugh, order the Mole it is literally a small amount of mole sauce (not very good) drizzled on a plate with a little bit of greens - that's it! Hilarious and insulting considering that IS one of the main dishes that that you get the pleasure of paying them $30 for that!! Awful. Awful.

Had an excellent brunch at Cosme last weekend. 

Our waiter was very knowledgeable and recommended that we share several dishes. This was a great strategy and we all especially loved the lamb barbacoa. 

The only issue we had (and this honestly wasn't even really an issue) was fixed immediately--one of the girls who was dining with us is pregnant and cannot have undercooked eggs. We told our server this and he assured us that he would tell the kitchen to fully cook any dishes with egg in them for us. Our huevos rancheros initially arrived with very runny eggs BUT he was extremely apologetic and fixed this immediately, even sending over a complimentary appetizer as well. He really went above and beyond to accommodate us (especially considering we ordered an egg-centric dish). 

For those of us drinking, we all loved the cocktails we tried. Very bright and refreshing, the perfect accompaniment to brunch. We will definitely be back.

I will say that we were somewhat divided on the desserts. We all split the churros and the corn husk meringue. The churros were lovely and while we all enjoyed the meringue itself, the corn filling was a miss for all of us. It's extremely savoury and reminded us of buttered corn on the cob. This may be a matter of personal preference, but for us this mix of savoury and sweet just didn't work.

So I'm scrolling through Yelp reading some unflattering reviews about Cosme and thinking the reviewers are just trying to be contrarians. Then I go there and those reviews all made so much sense.

The place is clean and modern and we were seated promptly. After perusing the interesting menu choices, we chose the Burrata as an appetizer and the Duck Emoladas and Enfrijoladas for our entrees.

BURRATA (veracruzanna, lemon tempura, quelites) - the veracruzanna is a sauce that contains tomatoes, onions, peppers, olives, capers, etc. The  veracruzanna, the lemon, and the herbs all overpowered the burrata. The previous evening, we had a burrata with olive oil, pepper and sliced snap peas at an Italian restaurant. This combo at the Italian Restaurant let the burrata shine whereas Cosme's overpowered it.

DUCK ENMOLADAS (mole rojo, creme fraiche) - The duck wrapped in tortillas was overpowered by the mole sauce. Couldn't tell what kind of meat I was eating was it pork, beef, etc.?

ENFRIJOLADA (ricotta, hoja santa, queso fresco) - This was a bowl of tortilla chips with black beans, herbs, and queso cheese. The taste was unremarkable.

The place is nice and the service was spot on, but we both agreed we wouldn't want to eat any of the food or drink [Bloody Maria (chipotle)] again. At the end of the day, I was thinking about a 2 star review because that seems reasonable for a place you would never plan on visiting again, but decided on a 3... for no particular reason.

I have been to Cosme twice and really enjoy the restaurant! The ambiance and vibe is fresh, fun and well-decorated. The drinks are pricey ($16+ cocktails), they are well-made using top-shelf liquor. I've gotten the margarita and Paloma, both delicious. They also have an excellent wine list - curated and refined. 

The food: Must get the duck carnitas. It is not over hyped, is 100% worth it! For two people, it is plenty and you only need 1 or 2 other appetizers/small plates. It would be perfect for 3-4 people so you can order other items. But sharing with 1 other person, you get more duck!! The corn tortillas are life-changing!! I've been to Pujol and the quality of corn is the same. 

The other items are good but do not recommend the fish wrapped in banana leaf. The menu does change. It is bold and all very delicious.

I recommend the corn dessert, also not over-hyped. Very worth it, i could eat a whole one myself!

Amazing food, spectacular duck, and spicy drinks.  We always enjoy it.  However, last night  manager Emmanuel Martinez and his assistants were extremely rude, unprofessional towards us. I hope this great establishment hires better managers.

Husband and I came here for brunch today and really enjoyed. We started with a margarita and guacamole. The guacamole was very flavorful and garnished with fresh herbs. The margarita wasn't too sweet, which we very much appreciated. We then split the chilaquiles (green and chicken) and a mushroom quesadilla. The chilaquiles came with a lot of chicken and were extremely filling. The chicken was soft and fell apart to the touch. The quesadilla was nice and cheesy and was quite big. That would've been enough food for us, but we had to finish off with the duck. The duck, too, was extremely tender. I don't usually love mole, but theirs was quite well-balanced. Overall a satisfying meal -- and five hours later, I'm still stuffed.

Cosme transports you from Nomad to Mexico with every bite. As one of the worlds 50 best restaurants at #25 as of this week I can say it's truly a unique experience when you walk through the door. The ambience is amazing, cocktails are to die for, and ultimately each and every dish has an explosion of flavor unlike any Mexican spot I have ever dines at outside of Mexico. The aguachile, Duck carnitas, and pork belly were clear standouts. But to the reason it gets a 4 and not a 5. I thought the portions were very small for the price we paid. With tax and tip we looked at $95 a head (party of 4) with one cocktail and we all left still a bit hungry even after the server indicating we had ordered the perfect amount and we would all be full. I will return at some point because the dishes were truly elevated Mexican cuisine.

Telenovela cocktail- you had me at pisco & st.germaine. It was petitely proportioned but wow does it pack a punch. Smooth and silky with lemon lime flavor and floral notes- If humanly possible and I could- I would savor a half gallon of it over the course of the night. 

Housemade blue corn chips with the most special Chile garlic sesame hot oil. I swear I was eating a roasted black bean hot sauce but the server swore up and down its their 4 chili sauce- no beans whatsoever. So good I wanna slap that on everything.

A cold tapa of finely sectioned octopus swimming in scallions soy-lime vinaigrette and angel hair onions. It was savory and tart- made you going back for more.

The House Special:

Duck Carnitas- so instead of giving you this play by play, saliva inducing rendition, I will keep it simple by simply saying- it's all true what they say about this dish. 

Oh, and it's big enough to share for 2 if that's all you order- you're welcome. (Essential equivalent of 4 actual tapas)

Corn Husk Meringue:

I'll be even simpler- It's all true about this one too! Only even better. Don't you dare leave without ordering this Bc the thought had crossed my mind and BOY, am I glad i didn't! You're truly welcome.

Overpriced for what you get plus very bizarre service.

Who asks for ID when ordering a drink? I replied asking if they have a lot of children ordering drinks. Never experienced that at a top restaurant, it impacted the dinner vibe for sure.

Went three times, was never really impressed.

This venture into fancy Mexican is a departure from my norms. Honestly I'm happy with a $2 taco if if tastes good. But then there was Cosme who introduced me to duck and cobia as taco fillings. I've already run through tripe and tongue and savored all kinds of al pastor. But when a little known to me fish is the center of al pastor and that pineapple puree...damn that's good!

The duck carnitas is not just for two. I ate that again and again. It will solidly feed four people or maybe two people with large appetites. The duck is deliciously meaty, earthy, and tender.

The squash was also good but my least favorite of the three things I tried. The table next to us thought it was "life changing". 

The Drinks are good. Everything is Manhattan priced. I wouldn't come here to complain about that. I mean the obamas came here...what do you expect?

I know, I know, it's **supposedly** the best Mexican in the US and a top 40 out of best 50 restaurants in the world right? 
I don't think so! A broccoli dripping in oil after deep frying, a tortilla that's so hard to chew you opt to eat the filling with a fork instead, under seasoned fish and flavorless chili oil.  Now that doesn't sound like a good restaurant does it?
Save your money. Go to la esquina, go to Mexicue, etc. 
Whatever strings they pulled to get to be a top 40 restaurant won't fool you.  Especially in New York. 

Mexican food reminds you of the acidity of lime, freshness of the cilantro, the kick of the jalapeño, the smokiness of chipotle.  

It should NOT therefore taste like deep fried oil, flavorless fish and under seasoned sauce.

We enjoyed the food but 2 stars only because of the staff members I spoke with on the phone when making the reservation.  A woman named Danielle was so rude and unhelpful when I asked her for their available times available for our party (why anyone with her attitude would choose to go into the hospitality business is beyond me).  I then asked to escalate the call to her manager and was passed to a gentleman named Herman who didn't seem too bothered by her manner.  I won't be returning.

Amazing food at Cosme. Highlights were the fall apart in your mouth duck and the corn mousse.

We started with the endives, Cobia and Abalone tostada. Were not spectacular and could skip. Endives has pine nuts, and was too bitter.

However the main course was wonderful. Everything was cooked to perfection. We had the mole, steak, lamb and duck. The duck is a must get! It is very fatty and I would recommend getting something light and acidic on the side to cut the grease. I would skip the steak however since the portions were too small and the flavour was not unique. 

I am not a dessert fan but you must get the corn mousse! It is not overly sweet and very light. Every bite was heaven!

I was a bit skeptical after reading some reviews with 'underwhelming' experiences. That was not experience at all!  Everything we ordered were good, very suitable for my gluten free diet and not over seasoned!  Prompt service.

The short: one of the better Mexican fusion meals I've ever had. Food, service & ambience were all killer. 

The longer: we came as a walk-in on a Thursday night around 530pm & were able to sit at a high-top table near the bar. 

Our waitress was so sweet and helpful in selecting menu items to share. We did all appetizers and smaller entrées. The fish tacos with pineapple were absolutely amazing. The tamale was crazy. The corn dessert was insane. Every single bite of food was a perfect combination of sauces and flavors. 

Quick tip: they have an interesting variety of wines. I didn't like any of the ones I sampled and opted for bubbles, so I'd recommend cocktail or trying out a wine before you order it. 

Overall, his spot was amazing, pretty reasonable (since we mostly did small plates) and I can't wait to come back!

Cosme had a really nice atmosphere.  The food for lack of a better term was interesting.  Not bad but also nothing amazing.  It's one of those places that try's too hard to be something.  Mexican is Mexican don't try and make it gourmet French. You end up with weird combos.  The chilaquiles were tasty but mostly a bowl of tortillas, the huevos rancheros had one egg no cheese and mushrooms. Not really huevos rancheros but ok.  The guacamole was really the only thing I would say impressed me.  The drinks were hit or miss (again trying to hard with crazy flavors).   I don't remember which tostada we had but it tasted like cheap 4 day old sushi. The waiter recommended it so if he does say no thanks.  Also the service was ok. Nothing great.  And the prices were extremely high for what we were served.  Would I go back? I'd try it for dinner, but never again for brunch.  It wasn't worth it.

Such a pretty place to spend Saturday nights with besties. Enjoyed the experience overall- great ambience, not too crowded or loud, server was friendly and helpful in terms of explaining the menu and signature dishes, very nice presentation of every course.

Decor: 9/10
Food: 7/10
Service: 6/10
Ambience: 8/10

Was a shame that we didn't order the duck (everyone was talking about it below literally) because we wanted to try more dishes. 

Personal favorite was the lamb belly, tender and juicy inside and outside grilled to the crisp, served with sweet and sour sauce and pickled radish(might be wrong lol). Perfect to eat with the tangerine-flavored slightly sour soft tacos. 9/10

The abalone appetizer was okay. The tostada shell at the bottom was a bit weird- definitely not crispy enough but still rough in general, a bit dry also. 4/10

Cobia al pastor , pineapple pure , cilantro was pretty good, a little special as in the fruity notes blends well with the slight fattiness of the fish. I found it a bit too sweet but my friend loved it. 8/10

Striped bass- the presentation was pretty the fish itself was a bit flavorless. The sauces (bean paste) were good tho. 5/10

Husk Meringue with corn mousse- 7/10 

Avocado ice cream, coconut cream, shaved ice- this was supposed to be my favorite if they'd be more careful with the use of dark chocolate at the bottom- very close to the coconut cream. The combination of the bitter dark chocolate with coconut cream tasted a bit weird like incompatible ingredients were reluctantly put into the same level of the fridge. The avocado ice cream at the top was amazing. So was the coconut on the shaved ice. 6/10

Not much atmosphere went on a wed at 6pm thought. The food literally has no taste. Our server was nice. The duck was ok super tender I've had better flavor tho. The sorbet trio was amazing but how can you mess up sorbet?

I came in with high expectations, left underwhelmed and disappointed. 

Ambience: 4/5

Service: 2/5 The server didn't even bother explaining the menu, which is far from a traditional menu

Drinks: 4/5

Food: 3/5

Value (price) for what you get: 2/5

Before I start, I want to make it clear the food at Cosme is actually good, BUT it deserves one star for a multitude of reasons. First, I along with the majority of New York find it absurdly disrespectful how Cosme has raised its price 2-3 times since gaining some fame. Secondly, if you enjoy being disrespected by the wait staff as while as being put behind those who pay the hostess money to hold them seats (not reservations) is absurd. I do not recommend Cosme as if you are looking for good Mexican food there are countless restaurants that are both fairly priced and have better food (ex Casa Enrique).

We came to this place after our originally planned restaurant had too long of a wait. The pros are Cosme has a trendy interior and excellent service. However the cons were substantial. The portions are tiny for the price, there is a very limited menu and it's not clear what most items are, and the food was subpar. I had the steak- it had a grainy texture and was way too salty. My table shared the guac which was fine but not great, and it only came with three tortillas (which were too hard by my standards).  

To be fair we did not have dessert or cocktails which is what this place advertises but probably would not come back based on the food.

I eat out allot way too much actually and the times where I feel that a restaurant blows me away are unfortunately far, and few between. Every morsel at Cosme was a trip to somewhere between a street corner in La Condesa circa 2666 and a mind f**k pre-Colonial Aztec/Mayan pre- sacrifice feast

Food and service were fantastic. Not the atmosphere. The restaurant is cold, both literally and figuratively, as well as loud. The tables are large, so it's hard to talk. The prices are extremely high, and we were not comfortable at all, so we would never go back, even though it was insanely delicious.

I absolutely loved Cosme. What a beautiful example of fine dining Mexican cuisine brought to us by Chef Enrique Olvera and his brilliant culinary team. Boosted into celebrity status especially after the latest Chef's Table on Netflix, Enrique Olvera showcases flavors that are rarely seen in a fine dining setting. I love how bold the flavors are and how his food truly made me take a look around and ask how I have never experienced that combination of flavors before.

I booked Cosme almost a month in advance and made a special trip to the city to eat here. After a day of walking around the town, we decided to get to the restaurant a little ahead of our reservation and sit at the bar for drinks. The antihistamine and the telenovela were my favorites. They were expertly put together and it dangerously made you forget you were drinking alcohol. All of these are hallmarks of a good cocktail.

As soon as our reservation time came around, we were promptly invited to sit at our table. The menu isn't long but pretty much everything that is on there are things that catch your eye. Seafood, veggies, meat. It fits all palettes. I will say that if you are part of that small population of people who doesn't like cilantro, it will be difficult to avoid this. They do their best, however, removing the garnishes where that is possible and remaking the guacamole to ensure that everyone can enjoy it.

The service was quick, efficient and polite. Love the modern/formal atmosphere of the place with books on the shelves to make you feel like you're in his home... his modern home. The food quickly arrives to the table soon after ordering. We had the abalone, the kampachi, razor clams, sweet corn tlayuda, mole rojo, lamb belly and the duck carnitas. Each of them showcased a familiar flavor something that you would expect to find at a Mexican restaurant but it also displayed a unique spin that made you craving more. Of the dishes we ordered, the mole rojo, lamb belly and the duck carnitas were must haves! They were each served with their own unique tortillas made from different types of corn. Each basket was filled with a rainbow of colors highlighting the heirloom products that Enrique and his team are trying to reintroduce into culinary language. 

As for the dessert, oh man, be sure to save room for it. I have NEVER had desserts like the ones served here. Works of art to the eye and to the mouth. Corn husk meringue and the cacao butter are a foodie's dream. This is a must try restaurant. I can't wait for the day when I can make it to Mexico City to try Pujol. Will definitely be back to this restaurant on my next trip here. Highly recommend this to all my fellow yelpers out there!

The main reason I am giving only 2 stars is for a restaurant at this level, I would have thought that they would accommodate our dietary preferences. The ambience was good, people were nice but the food did not please me as much.

There were not a lot of vegetarian options on the menu now would they switch the meat out. We started with the HERB GUACAMOLE of course, which was pretty good. I like the tortilla it was served with, they were crunchy but soft which is not found very often. 

For our main course we ordered Endive, ayocote beans, avocado, pine nuts /// Broccolini, pistachio pipián /// and Kabocha squash tamal, ha'sikil p'ak, castelrosso. Out of the three dishes, the best was the squash tamal. The squash puree was flavorful and tamale was fresh and tender. It was a good combination. The Broccolini was slightly bitter and I meeded more of that pistachio sauce with it. The endive with avocado dish was pretty looking but I was expecting to experience more flavors from it. The avocado was unseasoned and the bean puree was not enough. 

The highlight of the evening and the most awaited dish was the Husk meringue, corn mousse. Now this is what I am talking about. The meringue was light crispy and its pairing with corn mousse was great. This dish is the reason I went to Cosme and it did stand upto the expectations. 

Overall, am I going again? I dont think so.

Fantastic!

We sat at the bar. Chema (Jose Maria, is his real name I think) was the man in charge and did a fantastic job.

We took all his recommendations - sherry, wine and food - and were really, really happy with everything that was put down in front of us. The lamb belly is something I will remember.

I'm an amateur cook. I always rate food according to whether or not I think I could replicate it. Not a chance in this place. We will definitely go back and will definitely look for Chema behind the bar because he's clearly a bloke who knows the food and drink. Good job!

For weeks I was greatly anticipating this reservation having been in the industry for 15 years and hearing great things about the food. I'll start by saying the host staff was lovely and the bar staff was extremely attentive - providing recommendations on the cocktail list when we asked. There was also a woman next to me looking for a particular wine and the bartender was very patient and truly trying to find her the best glass for her taste. 

We sat for our reservation on time and then the night took an awful turn. Our waiter took 10 minutes to come to our table, though the busser came by to give us water. We finally got to look at the menu and decided to order two apps and share the $100 duck entree. To my disappointing surprise, the entree came out with the apps. We wanted to take our time and in no way wanted to eat our entree with our first course. I was shocked our server didn't bother to ask if we wanted our food coursed out (but I would always would assume, yes, that you fire the entree once the guests are finishing up appetizers). We finally got to our entree and it was on the colder side, but we ate it. Not once did our waiter ask how our meal was. When we finished, the waiter came by with dessert menus. We ordered two and 5 minutes later, the desserts came out. So we sat, dined, ate dessert and paid all within one hour. I've never felt so rushed at a restaurant before. 

Working in this industry, I never post yelp reviews because I understand it can sometimes be viewed as a venting platform for patrons, but this was truly the worst experience in NYC. I felt compelled to tell the manager, Christian, about my experience before leaving the restaurant. He seemed like he cared and apologized, however, at no point did he ask me for our reservation name or where we were sitting. So the entire time he had no idea which server I was talking about. I was shocked. What could have served as a teachable moment for the wait staff just flew over his head. Such a shame for a restaurant of this reputation. 

I hope this was a fluke and not indicative of all the servers, but I will not be returning or recommending this establishment.

Very nice food , ambience is excellent and the wine was delish. Service , everything. 
Highly recommend. I will be back

Very cool restaurant. Aesop soap. Malin + Goetz candles. Chic interior. Bloody expensive and meh food. The flavors were all pleasant, but unoriginal and not substantial in portion size to justify the expense. 

$29 for red mole sauce. No meat or vegetables. For sauce. Puréed pumpkin seeds with tomato and spices. Somewhere an abuelita is crying. Not at the price, but the fact there was no substance to the dish.

I was really excited to try Cosme after hearing all the rave reviews about it.  I wasn't disappointed but I wasn't blown away either.  Some of the dishes are really innovative (baked trout, avocado ice cream, etc), but some of the dishes lacked originally and were quite frankly, too expensive for what it actually was (there's an entree that's literally just mole sauce for $25).  Go if you want a lively NYC scene but stay for one cocktail and appetizer to share at the bar.

I been to Pujol in Mexico City I honestly I am
A true fan of Chef Olvera and Im proud Mexican and so happy if the success of this chef so I had to go to Cosme and glad I did everything was excellent

If you're looking for upscale Mexican cuisine don't look further than Cosme. It's considered one of the top restaurants in the world. It's a nice spot to go for a date or a fancy lunch. I had their mole enchiladas and it was bold in flavor and absolutely delicious! 

-@EricHoRaw

Loved the food here! It's definitely worth the price. The pan dulce is made in house and was very soft. The huevos rancheros were also really good and the green chilaquiles as well. Definitely adding Cosme to my list of places to eat when I'm in the city.

After many months of research and planning my NYC trip, I was sure Cosme would be a slam dunk (despite the lukewarm reviews on here). As it turned out, this time, the Yelp average is on point. 

Am I glad I went? Yes. After all, the only way to have an opinion is to experience it. Will I return the next time I'm in the city? Maybe just for the duck carnitas and dessert? Maybe, but probably not. Why? Well, even with the highs they did have, NYC a ​whole has way too many other options to explore. This one is more of a try-it-once-and-forget-it experience.

And that's just not good enough. I now feel the media accolades are incredibly exaggerated​. How is this restaurant on 'The World's 50 Best Restaurants' list? I mean, it's not terrible by any means, but 40th? IN. THE. WORLD.?​ No. Just, no. Is it because Pujol is on the list at 20th? Kind of like Keller's Bouchon has a Michelin star? Politics? 

Arrived right when it opened for lunch, received a standoffish welcome from the hostess, and got seated immediately. Studied the menu and placed several orders at a time to make sure we weren't bombarded with everything at once. 

HERB GUACAMOLE. Was it good? Of course, it's guacamole. But no way this would win in a blind tasting against any other authentic Mexican place. C'mon now. 

The COBIA AL PASTOR with its pineapple puree and cilantro tasted a little more special, but again, World's Best? No. Estoy segura que no. 

HUEVOS RANCHEROS same thing. All ingredients I love...the refried beans, mushrooms, and queso fresco. The egg was perfectly cooked and delivered that foodporn shot when it broke and oozed out. 

I usually say: "If you can't afford a place, then don't go and certainly don't complain about it if you do." But coming from a humble Hispanic​ background where I find it ridiculous when I encounter overpriced and overhyped Cuban food, I can't help but balk at a $17 guacamole and $24 huevos rancheros. Just on principle, GTFOH. Even if they are organic. Even if they are farm to table. Did the chicken lay a golden egg? I don't care if Enrique Olvera himself laid the egg. I kid. And I'm NOT saying it's ALL overpriced, but some things definitely are. The rest, well, I suppose we DO have to pay not only for the high-quality​ product, but also for the knowledge and creativity you and I don't have to conceive and execute some of the dishes. 

The DUCK CARNITAS did live up to the hype. Highly recommended, as is the HUSK MERINGUE and WARM PECAN TART with salt & pepper ice cream. Those last three were decadent and executed to perfection. 

Not the norm, but I did not have cocktails or wine during my visit. Despite having a full bar (and 'Q Tonic' on the menu), I found it strange ginger ale was not readily available. In fact, no sodas were. For the record, Q makes a killer ginger ale. Don't they use any as a drink mixer? 

Given I usually praise New York city the most for its stellar service at nicer dining establishments, I found the service at Cosme lukewarm and odd. Our waiter took our order, but the busier the place became, the harder it was to find him. A​ gentleman (manager?) constantly walked around the room and huddled in the corner with other staff members whispering with hands over his mouth while looking around the room. Awkward​. I wish I wouldn't have noticed.

The crowd on this Thursday afternoon seemed to be mostly business lunches. A lot of suits, ties, and heels mixed with bohemian and hipster types. The vibe was definitively "happening."

On my way out, the hostess mindlessly handed me my coat and snarkily quipped​ "Wow, you sure take a lot of pictures." as I snapped some of the entrance areas​. Well, thank you Captain Obvious. Again, not hospitality at its finest. 

Side note: I recently attended an event in South Florida where Chef Soto-Innes cooked one of the courses, and it was out of control delicious, and nothing like I experienced in NYC. That dish WAS note-worthy. You win some, and you​ lose some I suppose.

The cocktails we had were incredibly well made.  The food, as expected, was the highlight of the evening. Unique, and delicious Mexican cuisine in New York City. That uniqueness comes with a hefty price tag, but worth all the experience. The dishes are well executed with style and finesse. It was an incredible experience. The service was excellent. The restuarant vibe is very chic and trendy with modern designs. Crushed it. Verdict: Worth it.

Service is terrible at this restaurant.we had dinner and the servers were arrogant and rushed us to order everything at once while still enjoying the cocktails. Although the food is good the service doesn't match it at all!

Big disappointment.

I heard a lot of good things about Cosme and I was curious to dine there. 

We had several plates which were nothing extraordinary at all. What really shocked me was the total check amount. this is absolutely insane.
I live in NYC and am acquainted with the usual rates in restaurants but this was clearly beyond what I've experienced in similar restaurants.

So in short:

food: OK but nothing impressive. just ok
price: they're totally insane (15$ for a meh beer, 17$ for peeling an avocado and serve it with cilantro), I mean come on!
service was just ok. I asked for a stella and they the waiter told me we don't have that but we have something similar. yeah, at 15$ a beer. Thanks.

I will not go back to this restaurant.
This place is like Mexican fusion type of food... not impressed... very blah... Atmosphere was nice though.

Honestly, I don't get it. A little while back, I came here for a group dinner with a group of foodies. The menu features some gems as a plate of mole sauce for $25, which is literally a plate of mole served with some tortillas. That's a bit too fine dining for me...$25 for a plate of sauce.

Between the five of us, we tried a handful of dishes. The highlight was definitely the duck. At ~$94, it's pricey, but we were able to split it between a group of 5 people. It was definitely the most delightful, fatty and fall of the bone flavorful duck. Honestly, if I were to come back...it would just be for the duck. I would split it and call it a night.

The other dishes were okay, but not remarkable nor worth the hefty price tag IMHO. For a restaurant that's touted as one of the best, I was unimpressed. Service was rushed and although the interior was elegant, this did not seem to be a fine dining experience.

Food-wise, the chef is definitely talented and there are bound to be huge hits on the menu. The dessert was incredible, for instance. And as I mentioned, the duck is definitely worth splurging for...even if it's the only thing you order! However, the rushed service and the absurdity of some of the menu items (I can't get over $25 for mole sauce. Sure, I get it...days of work and spices...at least serve it over something to pop the flavor!) make this an AOK experience.

After trying Mexico City's world famous Pujol, I had to give this restaurant a shot. Cosme is a tonned down and more casual version of its Mexico City parent restaurant. Nevertheless, it's exciting and a foodie worthy stop. I would highly recommend the duck carnitas; they literally melt in your mouth! My wife is obsessed with the corn meringue, It's truly epic. The atmosphere is NYC chic with "mexican-bossa nova" in the background.

I'm so happy to have finally come by this place. My brother was visiting from California so I wanted to show him a different Mexican food scene. This review is solely for the lamb barbacoa as that was the only dish we ordered. 

The presentation was nice. The lamb came in a big ceramic pot, which I thought was interesting. There was a side dish with sliced onions and avocados and three different sauces for the tacos. The lamb was super tender and juicy. It was not at all gamey, which was something I was worried about. You can ask for refills of the sliced onions and avocados at no extra charge, which is amazing since I know some places charge upwards of $8-$10 for adding avocados. 

The food was great, and we both enjoyed the lamb a lot. However, if you ask if the $69 price was worth it and if I would come back for it, probably not. I did enjoy the tacos, but not infinitely more so than the regular carne asada tacos at local joints. I would definitely come back for the duck carnitas though. We came here with the hopes of ordering the duck, but they unfortunately don't serve it for brunch. I'll update my review once I've tried their signature dish!

Very disappointing. It's like the people who work here know the restaurant is popular and has gotten positive reviews, so they don't have to try. Not a good recipe for repeat business. 

The food is generally pretty good. But the portion sizes are small. And, unlike many other restaurants in a similar price range, you leave Cosme feeling like what you got wasn't worth anything close to what you paid for it. 

The service was also sub par. The hostess was unprofessional, rude and set a bad tone for evening. You'll find a warmer and more competent greeting walking into an average chain restaurant in an exurban strip mall.

Incredible experience!

The service here was top notch. Some of the best I've had...Ever!

The cocktails we had (most of the menu between the four of us) were incredibly well made, ranging from creative to classics. 

The food, as expected, was the highlight of the evening. 

We started with Cobia Ceviche and Albalone Tostada then moved to the sweet corn tamal and mole and finished with the Duck Carnitas. 

At any other restaurant, each dish would have been the best of the evening so it was amazing to experience them all back to back. 

Do yourself a favor: don't skip dessert! We had four different desserts all of which were different levels of magic. 

Can't wait to return with friends.

Overall: 3.5
Service: 4.5/5
Ambience: 4/5
Food: 3/5

Come here if you're looking for a foodie experience and an innovative Mexican fare with a unique twist, but stay far away if you aren't ready to shell out the big bucks. 

I came here with a couple coworkers the other day and opted to get items to share, after having asked about their extremely confusing menu. We ended up getting: 
- Herb guacamole: Solid guac with a nice and unique mix of herbs. I personally loved the mint in it. 
- Cobia al pastor: A make your own tacos style dish, this fish was cooked to perfection and the flavours of this one were definitely the winner of the night. 
- Razor clams with green chorizo: I started out curious about this but was quite disappointed when it came out. The flavours did not do it for me and a bit too sour for my expectations. The clams were cooked well but the chorizo left much to be desired.
- Sweet corn tostada with truffles: one of my coworker's favourite dishes of the night. This item is great for sharing and among my top three dishes.  
- Steak flank (something like this, can't remember the name): Just like regular steak to me but much smaller. The puree that came with it was pretty good though, but nothing to write home about
- Lamb belly: This dish confused me so much. I went in expecting something really hearty and ended up with a mouthful of sour flavours. I can't quite remember what was listed on the menu but I really felt deceived. 
- Husk meringue: Their signature dessert, I actually found this to be quite delicious (or at least that one bite that I nabbed from my coworker)
- Sorbet trio: I honestly got this for the pneapple/coconut/ginger scoop though the prickly pear sorbet was also quite refreshing. The former definitely won the trio for me.
- Nixtamalized apples: Another one of the strangest things I tried that night (again, at least that one bite that I nabbed from my other coworker). It was like a whole apple but arranged into slices and prepared in a way that made me think it should have been in a pie with a nice crumble on top.
- El Ninja (cocktail): I think this is what it was called... but I really enjoyed this Mezcal cocktail. I thought it was really refreshing and the citrus was done just right. Definitely recommend this one. 

Overall, I found the food to be okay. I came in expecting to be super dazzled, but the food (even without the crazy price points) fell a little flat for me. The service, however, was phenomenal. Our waiter was extremely attentive and switched out our plates often. I definitely felt taken care of there. Cosme is probably not on my list of places to go back to anytime soon, but if hanging with a major foodie for a special occasion (or one who has deep pockets), I wouldn't mind stepping into this establishment again.

Cosme offers exceptional upscale Mexican in a chic New York environment. The menu is appealingly small and well suited for sharing or ordering independently. It's also entirely gluten-free, with a variety of delicious options for vegetarians and pescetarians. And the service is extremely knowledgeable about preparation and dietary restrictions.

I only remove a star for price. There's only so much you can charge for a simple, albeit excellent, broccolini taco; Cosme pushes it.
Brilliant takes on Mexican cuisine: flavor combinations you'd never imagine but that feel so natural they might become standards henceforth, such as the "herb guacamole". Exceptional restaurant.

My husband and I came here for dinner and decided that we will never come back. I'm glad we tried it but this restaurant is outrageously overpriced and the service is subpar.

Menu:
If you're going to separate your menu items into 3 different sections, why do you not have a header? It would have been nice to receive a bit of an explanation as the waiter was handing us the menu. We were confused as was the table next to us. Even after we asked the waiter, we still did not understand the layout. 

Service:
As we drank our cocktails, we noticed that the table next to us (who sat down about 15 minutes after) already received their first few menu items, some of which were the same ones we ordered.
