The waiter did come over to apologize but it was still frustrating given that our tables were not ready to begin with. If I'm paying an outrageous amount for your food, I am going to expect to be seated exactly at 7pm which is when I had my reservation.

Food:
We first ordered the razor clams ($26) and sweet corn tlayuda ($48). While these were appetizer portions with entree prices, they were quite good. I don't think it was worth the price but still, it was tasty. We were a bit startled by the $26 Broccolini but we decided to give it a try. Who knows? Maybe it will be mind-blowing. Nope. It was very underwhelming and honestly, I could have made that at home. The mole rojo was even more of a disappointment. You would expect that when they charge $29, they will add on some protein. Nope. It was literally just a plate of red sauce with a little greens.. oh and some tortillas. Thanks. We refused dessert because we were both outraged at this point.

Don't waste your money. This place is a trap. I have dined at Eleven Madison Park and other expensive restaurants in New York where I can see the justification in the price but I truly felt robbed at Cosme.
One of the best restaurants in NYC! At night get the duck carnitas, but don't miss the brunch: Chilaquiles, Pan Dulce and a Michelada!

All Food to cocktail was amazing!

I loved the Uni and duck.
Meringue desert was something to try at Cosme too!

The food was delightful and innovative. I would come back just to eat the corn husk meringue again. We order the recommended amount and spent quite a bit here, but did not feel full and thought the portions were on the small side. 

The service was not up to par for a high-end restaurant. The waiters were not attentive or knowledgeable about the menu. The hostess was quite impolite. When we were waiting to check in with her, she did not acknowledge us and kept her conversation about famous celebrities and gossip with another staff member.

We came here for brunch. The waiter was in a rush and kind of angry and the duck was not good at all.

Won't come back again!

One of my favorite places to eat Mexican cuisine. For lunch, the uni tostada is a wonderful starter if you like sea urchin. The short rib is very tender and worth a try. Basically you order 2-3 items per person and share. Guacamole is fresh but you can decide if it's worth $17.  For dinner definitely get the duck carnitas to share. If duck isn't in your wheelhouse try the octopus or the steak. He ambiance is hip and the drinks are good. Definitely worth a visit.

Worth the hype? Yes. But I wasn't blown away. Food is incredibly unique, inventive, tasty and beautiful. We had the mole with greens, cobia with soft tortillas, steak and the bass - all really flavorful. And the meringue with corn for dessert. I had 2 glasses of sake and my daughter had a glass of beer; $195 before tip. Service was excellent; everyone including our server was warm, helpful and efficient. I would happily go back.

This place is supposed hot spot honestly underwhelmed me a bit. 

We were seated at a communal table and they were very gracious in accompanying the members of our party who arrived (very) late.

We ordered the chilaquiles with red sauce and egg, which was pretty good.

We also ordered the duck enmoladas, the enfrijoladas, the huevos rancheros, and a mushroom quesadilla

Everything was good, which the exception of the enfrijoladas which, in my opinion, wasn't very good because of the red mole sauce. But even what was good didn't blow my mind. It was really ordinary. 

The service was also a little off because no one but our specific waiter seemed to know anything about our food, and I would expect each waiter to know about the food they served. They also served us coffee that had grounds in it.

The bright spot, however, was dessert: we ordered the (corn) husk merengue which was DELICIOUS! The filling which tastes like corn actually comes together really well.

We also ordered the churros, which were pretty much like churros anywhere else. They did come with a Mexican hot chocolate sauce which was slightly bitter but it was an interesting pairing.

So when it comes to its complex flavors and surprising the palate this place lives up to its reputation. The mashed potatoes had a bit of lime juice in them, its not the most fitting combination I would've ever thought of but they pull it off perfectly! Pleasantly surprised, for sure, I don't kbow how they do it. But in the other hand, the prices compared to the portions are ridiculous! Plus the big plates and bowls don't help either, they just help empasize how small the portion is.

Wonderful place for a nice dinner. The menu is intimidating, but the well-trained staff gives beautiful explanations of the menu as a whole, as well as individual dishes. Very accommodating to gluten and dairy allergies.

Other than the cool vibes & lighting here, the food was overpriced (and overhyped.) 

A $300 price tag was nowhere near what this experience should have been, taste-wise or portion-wise. I don't care if the Obamas came here... 

The only dish of note was the "signature" dessert, a merengue made with corn, savory and sweet. Impressive, but again, couldn't save the experience.

3.5*

You can find some amazingly low-mark up/delicious rare wines here. Great list.

uni toast, cobia, duck carnitas - all good. It was a great atmosphere and service, but not sure if the food was entirely worth the hype. 

To each his/her own.

The food here is great and you can tell a ton of time, thought and talent was put into making it... it just comes with a hefty price tag.

I went here for lunch during the week with 5 people and we ordered about six or seven dishes. Two guacamole's for the table to start -- really good guacamole. There were slices of jalapeño in it and it added just the right amount of kick. Would absolutely recommend this.

For the entrees (it's a sharing style type place), we had the cobia al pastor, enmoladas, huevos rancheros, duck carnitas, and the quinoa salad. The duck carnitas are their staple dish and it was the first thing our waiter recommended, rightfully so. They were tasty. Almost every dish is served with corn tortillas, so you can essentially mix-and-match and make tacos with any of the dishes you get (maaaybe not how it's intended, but this really made the tacos better, in my opinion). For instance, if you mix the duck with the enmoladas (vegetarian cheese mole -- really good, legit mole), it makes a wonderful taco. Alone, I'm not sure how it would be.

The cobia al pastor was really good as well. It's served with a pineapple purée that's absolutely the perfect texture. The other dishes were good as well, but it honestly comes down to the price for me. The food were solid, but I wouldn't come here often unless I really wanted to splurge. However, if this is your style, I highly recommend. And you'll definitely pay for great service, as well.

We are a family of foodies. We know menus and we know restaurants. We just didn't get Cosme at all.

We heard it was THE best Mexican in NYC and that's why we drove in from NJ...to have the best.

Yes, the place is cool looking and the service was good. I'll give it that, but the rest of it...I'm still shaking my had and asking my husband if we were duped?

There are a TOTAL of 17 items on the menu. All need explanations and even when you get the explanation, you're not really sure what to do. 

$17 guacamole that came with 3 large chips (1 for each of us) and still required my fork to mash it all to eat it. Basically 1 Avocado with some herbs...nothing special. 

We ordered the $30 Mole which was literally a plate with sauce and some lettuce leaves. This Mole tasted like thin dirt and I'm not joking.

The $94 Duck Carnitas also required some manual labor to put together and while it was hearty, it was just average...nothing special and definitely not worth $94. 

The $42 steak was 10 2 inch pieces of meat that were just okay. 

The corn pizza with truffle was probably the item most interesting but it tasted a bit to earthy for me. 

We bagged dessert and grabbed a slice of NJ Pizza on our way home.

$300 bucks for this place just isn't worth it. 
I wouldn't recommend, and I wouldn't go back.

If you want interesting or different Mexican...go to Empellon. NOW THAT'S AN AWESOME OPTION!

Cosme puts a seriously elegant twist on traditional Mexican cuisine. We were there for brunch, and ordered the duck, quesadilla and the arctic char tostada. The duck melted upon touch and was a large portion - I wasn't able to eat it all. We didn't expect much from the quesadilla, but cosme has elevated what it means to make them. The arctic char was a beautiful blend of many flavours. All were seriously delicious, and although pricey, worth it for the food and beautiful decor/atmosphere.

Service, dessert, pumpkin were super great and memorable, which did impress us. However, the sea food we tried was not as great as we expected.
Consider the price....hmmmm

Not sure where the negative reviews are coming from. Ok I can understand the little piece of octopus for $30 complaints, yes. However, if you appreciate Mexican cuisine, this is a must visit in NYC. Restaurants are expensive in New York, this is nothing new. Enrique Olvera warrants that extra dollar sign.

The waiters brought out an additional dish that we did not order (green chorizo and razor clams) which was amazing. They said it would be comped but ended up on our bill nonetheless. When asked about it they removed it and updated our bill for us, small inconvenience for a free extra dish.

Tip: research how a regular tortilla is made before you come here, then ask your waiter at Cosme the process in how they make their corn tortillas. That ridiculous flavor he achieves in a normally bland appendage of a taco is a true testament to their talent.

One of the best meals I've had in NYC!!! The ambiance is great - very open floor plan but the decor is modern and chic. The cocktails were AMAZING - we got the Striptease and Antihistemene (both tequilla based and SO good). Also got the Paloma and that was equally as delicious. The food - WOW. The best guac - it has mint leaves in it which is a really nice touch. We got the cobia al pastor - which was unlike anything I've ever had. It comes with warm blue corn and white corn tortillas and this amazing pineapple gnash. Lastly we got the duck dish. Hands down the best thing on the menu. Since it was valentines day the portions were a little smaller (and price was also lower too), but it was still just enough food. For dessert, we got the miragne and HOLY COW. It was so beyond delicious. You HAVE to try it!!
This is one of the nicer places for dinner, wouldn't say it's easy on the wallet, but 100% worth it. Highly recommended - make a reso far in advance and I would also recommend requesting a stand alone table - the half booth half table seats are pretty close together and way less intimate.

Oh Cosme. Cosme, Cosme, Cosme. Off the bat, I'll certainly agree that this place serves up some of the most unique, and (mostly) delicious Mexican cuisine in New York City. That uniqueness though comes with a hefty price tag. 

The scene here is modern and fitting to the food you'll have, and the service was friendly and attentive. 

We ordered four of the small plates, one main, one side, and one dessert. The portions here are relatively small, so ordering this amount of food felt like an appropriate amount. 

Guacamole - well, it's guacamole. Only thing that makes this unique at all is the addition of some non-traditional herbs like mint and tarragon. The chips served with this were really good, but you can skip the $17 guacamole. You won't regret not ordering it, I promise. 

Cobia - this is what I'm talking about when I say it's super unique and delicious. This is like the ultimate fish taco. The creaminess and sweetness of the pineapple purée paired with the fish is a perfect match, all wrapped up in a soft tortilla. My only issue with this dish is the size... you end up with 2 thin slices of fish per taco. Size aside, it's a most delicious dish, and you need to order this. 

Razor Clams - razor clams are just plain awesome, and if they show up on a menu, I'm ordering them. These are diced into small chunks and served over a super flavorful green salsa. Highly recommend this one. Very unique, very flavorful. 

Uni Tostada - let me start off by professing my love for uni. I can't get enough of it. The uni tostada? No, no, no, and no. The uni here is completely overpowered by the salsa and it's not a good pairing. This dish is and overreach and a miss. It doesn't work. This was the only dish of the night I didn't enjoy. Don't let the fact that it's uni tempt you. Skip this. 

Steak - the good? The steak is super tender and well seasoned. The purée (which now escapes me) is light and creamy. The bad? I could probably consume the entire steak in two bites. It's tiny. It's hard for me to call this a main dish, but similar to the cobia, the spot on execution of the dish partially compensates for the minuscule size. 

Brocollini - excellent side for the steak. The leaves have a slight char / crispness that's just right, and the green purée it's served over packs a lot of flavor. It's served with tortillas as well, if brocollini tacos are your thing. 

Husk Meringue - Cosme's signature dessert. Following the theme overall theme of this review, it's extremely unique and delicious. If you've never had a corn ice cream / mousse, you don't even know what you are missing. It's reminiscent of the corn ice cream at Empellon, but mousse style. You must get this. Portion here is large enough to share, but I won't judge you if you don't. 

Aside from the uni tostada, I'll say that everything we had was both really delicious and wholly unique, and also a minuscule portion for what you pay for each item. Drinks were solid as well, though expectedly pricey. Total damage for all of the above dishes, two alcoholic drinks, and two non-alcoholic drinks came to $231 after tax / before tip. You could cut $40 off of that without the guacamole or uni tostada. 

The one thing we didn't do was the duck (now yours for $94). Both tables on either side of us ordered it, and from what I saw, it falls apart with the gentlest pull of a fork, and it's way more meat than two people with normal appetites should be finishing. That being said, I want it. 

So what's the final verdict? It's worth the splurge to give it a try, and I want to come back for the duck. Skip the guacamole and the uni tostada. Get the cobia, razor clams, and husk meringue.
One of my favorite Mexican restaurants in the city. Definitely always recommend the mole and everything on menu I am sure you won't be disappointed

Overview: A place I truly wanted to love, but the dishes are overpriced and you need to know what to order. 

Items Ordered: The style of this place is tapas-esque. So my partner and I ordered the uni tostada, cobia al pastor, an aguachile, mole rojo, and a corn tostada with black truffle. I also had a Paloma to drink and we shared a husk merengue for dessert. My top favorite dishes were the uni tostada and the mole hands down. The uni tostada was soggy at the center so you needed to eat that fast. The mole was unbelievable about the flavor profile that it had. Every bite was unique and amazing. However, the other dishes felt average with me wondering why the dishes were so expensive (except the black truffle tostada. I understood that price). The husk merengue was fabulous and I've never had anything like that. I felt that in order to truly experience this place you need to know what to order. Otherwise you're going to not enjoy your experience at Cosme. 

Service: amazing service. They were there if you needed help with understanding the menu, but weren't too overbearing. As soon as we finished a dish they were ready to serve the next one. 

Other Observations: I couldn't help but wonder for the price we paid for this dinner if it was truly worth it to dine here. They're pricing the food that only exists at other Michelin Star restaurants, yet I was nowhere near impressed. I wanted to love this place as I'm a fan of the chef and watched Chef's Table to get excited for this place. However, both my partner and I were just disappointed.

I went in with low expectations because I tend to be kind of ghetto with Mexican food.  I like taco trucks, tex-mex and taquerias.  Every time I go to a "fancy" Mexican restaurant, I crave the cheap stuff.

But I ended up loving Cosme.  We started off with the Cobia, Hamachi and Guacamole.  Of these, I loved the Cobia the best, though I would say to go easy on the pineapple puree because it kind of overwhelms the flavor of the fish.  The guacamole was great too and interesting with all the herbs, but at the end of the day it was just mashed up avocado, and so I'd skip it next time.

Next, we got the squash tamale, a sweet corn and truffle tostada and a white bean and endive salad.  The tamale and tostada were amazing, and probably my favorites of the night. 

Then for our main, we got the duck carnitas and the broccolini with a green mole sauce.  Both were extremely delicious and came with special flavored tortillas for each as well as a couple of different sauces.  

For dessert, we went a little overboard and ordered the husk meringue, the cacao butter and the avocado raspado.  I loved the meringue.  It had a really interesting flavor and the corn went very well with the sugar and vanilla.  The cacao butter dessert was just ok, and the avocado dessert, I just plain did not like.  I have never liked avocado in dessert form and don't think I ever will.

I do agree with others that this place isn't cheap, but I think you need to dine here (or any place that serves small plates meant to be shared) with a strategy.  First, if you want to try a lot of stuff, then go in a minimum party size of 4 people.  Second, if you get the duck carnitas, it is an ENTIRE duck breast and definitely serves 4 - 6 people on its own.  Finally, if you're in a smaller party, just know that if you get 2 dishes per person and then dessert, you will be just fine and plenty stuffed and can try more dishes on a future visit.  The staff at Cosme says everything is a "small plate", but most are really mid-size plates (4 - 8 bites) or downright full entree size.

The reason for no 5 stars?  The place is a little loud without much insulation for sound (high ceilings, hard floors and tables).  The bar stools, for some reason, are incredibly high, and you have to literally jump off the stools to get down.  Sparkling water is complimentary, but the glasses are really small, which I think is the reason the servers leave the pitchers on the table.  But if you're a party like us and having flat and sparkling water, those pitchers take up a lot of room on the table that could be used for the food.  Wish the servers would just carry the pitchers to our table when we needed water.  And finally, the menu is a little confusing, which required a fair amount of questions from us, and the waiter kind of had a little bit of an attitude.
Delicious, especially the tamale, duck carnitas, and husk meringue. Super chic atmosphere.
Great place and great food. Make sure to make your reservation before time for the dining room. Loved the fish they prepared. Must try!

There are great things about Cosme. There are also terrible things about Cosme. I was looking forward to this reservation for a while. There were four of us. First off, our waiter was a little rude for no reason. We had never been there before so we had a lot of questions - he seemed particularly annoyed. OK, moving on. 

Drinks were very delicious! Food is expensive and you don't get much for your money. 

I can't quite recall all the menu items names. But some things we got... 

Two tostadas small - good for two to share
Manouri: I believe these were the tamales, Very good but tiny. 
Mole: Literally, tortillas, sauce, and cheese. For almost $30 dollars. sigh.
We got a few other sharable plates, but I can't remember them, They weren't memorable enough, clearly. 
Duck carnitas - can't miss these. Only substantial food item on the menu. 
Dessert - meringue was really tasty. 

Very disappointing experience. Way too expensive for small food items. Honestly, we felt like we were eating mostly sauce on tortillas for dinner. Our game plan should have been: two duck carnitas and straight to dessert.
One of the best Mexican restaurant in New York the food is amazing good selection of tequila I definitely I come back

I had a lot of expectations and since the beginning i have been disappointed. First you need to expect a lot of noise, close table from each other (not a fancy place but more on the trendy side) i did not mind that much this, i was just expecting something different. As we a arrived promptly on our reservation slot, we were told to go to the bar which was crowded with no place to sit and no place to hang (we were 4) we initially ask the receptionist how long more or less will it takes to get our table and she answered that she could not know(strange when you make a reservation) 
After we were sit (couple of minutes), the waiter came quickly to ask what to order, we asked for suggestions to what he said he recommend 3 plates per person( place are about 30 dollars each so have yr wallet ready) the duck carnitas were delicious but 96 dollars for it it s really TOO expensive. We also had the tlacuya which was 48 dollars and was not worst it all. Also it came with an extra extra spicy sauce that they did not warm us about how spicy it was, my husband lived in mexico for a couple of year and did found the sauce extremely spicy so be careful. It was a shame the waiter did not care enough to warm us ( for record, for the first sauces bought alongside other plates, they did told us it was spicy and surprisingly we could all take it). An other negative point, our food arrived before than our drinks ( strange for such a upscale restaurant ) and they did get the order wrong too, bring a wrong plate which was not charged at least! Overall it was not a nice experience, i wont go back, i found it really TOO expensive for what it is and i do think you can find a much better option in the city. Also they definitely need better staff, better trained. Food was overall nice but does not justify those high prices

Very very overpriced Mexican fusion food. I found the menu very confusing, there were 3 paragraphs of menus and I couldn't tell if it was appetizer, main, etc. 

I loved the vibes and the decor and understand the necessity to charge a premium to the food menu prices however it was incredibly hard to justify. We had a tostada for uni and it was one piece and it was oversalted. Our other hot plates also were cold by the time it arrived for the other hot dishes. In terms of drinks, I think I had one of the most overpriced margaritas in the world and wasn't exactly impressed with it was well.

In terms of service our sever was nowhere to be found and we had to wave other servers to help us throughout the night. Clearly there is much to be said about many of the similar threads of complain with regards to service, lack of clarity in menu and just overpriced food.

Came here with a party of five on a Sunday night to celebrate our friend's birthday.  We reserved a table at 7:30 but we are running 20 min late but we did called and make sure is ok.  When we get there the host told us since we are late our table had given to another party, and ask if we want to share a table with another party.... for a restaurant with this price point and atmosphere I won't expect we have to be ask to share a table. We are a group of 5 ppl.  Anyways after all we worked it out and got our own table.   

Pros:  cocktails are awesome, grac is good, Cobia al Pastor, duck carnitas are super tender, desserts is really great, nice atmosphere.

Cons:  Fluke Aguachile is a rip off- taste like fluke sashimi soaked in Chinese hot chili oil.  DO NOT ORDER MOLE - big red flag here- $29 for a plate of sauce that taste like Hoisin sauce with watercress granish.   Overall service is kind of slow and I don't feel too welcoming.  Menu is very confusing for a first comer.  Food is overpriced in general, you can find better Mexican food with lower price in most places in NYC.

Very pretentious and over rated.  

The Good: Cocktails were great. 

The Bad: Mediocre and overpriced food and as a bonus a menu that will be baffelling to most. 

$24 for basically a taco chip with 3 thin slices of abalone which was tasteless due to the over powering chile sauce. 

Pulpo which I wanted to love but the 6 inch $30 tentacle was like rubber.

Carnitas were ok but seriously... $89 for carnitas? 

The Ugly: Attitude from the staff and one person in our party did not get served for 15 minutes while the rest of us were waiting and having our food get cold. Poor service for a restaurant this is supposed to be of such a high calibre. 

There are so many other places in NYC that are worth your time and money, for us this is not one of them. If you go hope your experience is better.

I think most of the reviews are pretty unfair. This is not Mexican 101 it's from a completely different region completely different style and completely different flavor profile. We really enjoyed it and have eaten all over the city in a variety of Mexican restaurants you should go give it a try. They are very very busy very successful And found the food very interesting
Best restaurant I've ever eaten at the food and service is by far out of this world puts every restaurant I've ever eaten at to shame absolutely amazing, bravo!!

Oh, Cosme. I really wanted to love you. :( 

If this review were based on the service alone, it would have been five stars and I do have to say that. Each person we interacted with from the hosts to the wait staff were polite and on point. 

However, I found the menu and food to just be..meh. I expected a wide variety of mexican inspired dishes and this place has been on my "try it" list for months. It's not that the food was terrible tasting as it was just sort of boring, bland and mediocre. There wasn't much to choose from and when the food came out, our table kind of said, "oh, thats it?"

I think better mexican food can be found at a quarter of the price, and I'm glad I tried it - but sadly its a one and done for me.

If I could go back in time and choose another restaurant, I would. I sat down with my date (who was much hotter than the food, that is for sure) at 10:15pm for dinner. Our reservation had been moved from 9 to 10:15, which was irritating but not a huge deal. The tables were so close together, more so than many other places in New York and that is saying something. We started with cocktails, which were average, but certainly the best part of the experience. 

For dinner, we split the cobia al pastor which was pretty much raw and complete fat. People raved about the pineapple puree, but frankly I found it overwhelming and also not the slightest bit Mexican-inspired. We then ordered the razor clams (the smallest things I had ever seen in my life). It was essentially about 4 clams diced up into tiny pieces. The best part and most Mexican-inspired part of our entire meal was the salsa or whatever the clams were served over. Don't get me started on the next dish - grilled octopus. It was lukewarm and not grilled whatsoever. Nothing was hot, everything came out one after the other in roughly 5 minute increments. It felt like the food was already ready to go in the back, just waiting to be ordered. 

I had heard a ton of hype surrounding Cosme, so we were both very excited and promptly let down at the conclusion of our time here. It's a total scene, but I will give them credit for the decor - very sleek and trendy. It's definitely a fusion restaurant, fusing what, I am not sure. We were expecting a Mexican food experience, and a delicious one at that. While Cosme claims to be Mexican, we were sorely disappointed. Food and service were both mediocre at best.

Spoiler alert: You don't get a bang for your buck here. However, the food that you get here is top notch and experimental to an extent. We had 3 items (pork, mole sauce and the bass) which were interesting to the palate and satisfying to various degrees, but never boring/tedious. The gem to top off a good meal was the corn husk meringue which was exceptional. The flavors or rather their combination were something I hadn't experienced before. The drinks were solid as well. Efficient service supports this restaurant. I probably wouldn't visit again since there are similar restaurants that offer a much more involved experience (be it a different setting, or slightly larger portions, or slightly improved service). It's not a criticism of Cosme, but just setting expectations prior to anyone's visit. It is however, definitely at least a one time visit.

*3/5 review is based off food

Came here last weekend with a group of friends. Cosme has been on my list for a little while and we left underwhelmed. We ordered the Fluke, Cobia, Honeynut Squash, Manouri, Duck Carnitas, Husk meringue, and Caramelized cacao butter dessert. Out of all the main dishes we ordered, the Honeynut Squash and Manouri were the best. Both desserts were pretty good as well. 

-Fluke: 3/5
-Cobia: 2.5/5
-Honeynut Squash: 3.5/5
-Manouri: 3.5/5
-Duck Carnitas: 3.5/5
-Husk meringue: 3.5/5
-Caramelized cacao butter: 3.5/5
-Ambiance/decor: 3.5/5, dark but very lively environment
-Service: 3.5/5, staff was a bit scattered

This spot is super trendy and fun. The food is good, we had the duck and it was tender and delicious. The only comment I have is that we were a party of 2 and the dish was WAY too much for us, we ordered a few apps as well. The server could have suggested we consider the amount of food we got. We were visiting on business and couldn't take it with us. 
it's a great Friday night out with friends and a cool date spot.

I love this restaurant.

Bartenders and cocktails are amazing but I can see how some think it is to expensive. For me the cost was inline with the experience.

Food was amazing, I suggest coming as at least a party of four so you can order more dishes and share. Like the Cobia Tacos with pineapple butter, These were my favorite. The Duck Carnitas is the perfect size entree for 4 people to share and all have a good amount each.

This is also great place to sit at bar for apps and drinks and make sure to ask for Tiffany, she is amazing bartender and will guide your experience.

Pictures will be uploaded as soon as I get a chance. Also you can check out their sister venue (more casual) Atla.

Superb. We had dinner here last night and everything about it was incredible. We were a party of eight, so the family style was perfect. The plates were a good size and packed with flavor. Every dish we had was fantastic. We had scallops, fluke, octopus, duck, broccolini with pistachio mole...  and then ended up reordering as it was so good. The service was flawless and friendly, lighting is good and there's a great ambience without being too loud. This is probably the best authentic fine Mexican food you can eat in America and a perfect example of what makes Mexico City such a hot destination right now.

Biggest ripoff.  Our waiter said the $49 corn appetizer "to share" was one of the best things on the menu.  It was ridiculously small, and was essentially a stale small single tortilla with what tasted like canned corn and melted cheese with truffles shaved on top.  It tasted terrible and was definitely not big enough to share.  The $17 guacamole was a single avocado they barely took the time to smash with some sliced jalapeños and lime and a single large tortilla chip per person.  They wouldn't give us extra chips!  It was the craziest, most comical dining experience I have ever had.  And for the record, this is the first negative restaurant review I have ever gone out of my way to write...

This review is for brunch and one of the most memorable meals I've had in recent months! I know Cosme is expensive but the brunch menu offers great deals. Food is fresh, delicious and you will truly savor every bite. I ordered the chilaquiles (green with chicken) and quesadillas and they were both fantastic. The space is large and well designed, the service impeccable and you will be blown away by the inventiveness of the food! This is a not to be missed restaurant in NYC.

went here with a friend Jan 2018 for dinner. Had the 2 moles with fresh tortillas, the bass, the corn and multiple mezcal drinks. I left disappointed by the food and the service. The homemade tortillas were a bit burnt and tasteless, overly chewy on the center. The mole dish was just a splatter of the sauce, which was not full of the usual cocoa and nutty taste of traditional mole. As for the mezcal drinks, started out with the grapefruit/absinthe drink (believe it was called the striptease), it was just some sort of syrup and okay tasting mezcal...thy didn't even rim the glass with mezcal or smokey salt. The acclaimed "Ninja" mezcal drink had an overwhelming amount of ginger. Finally, the expat martini was okay but I mean, is it even possible to mess up a gin martini? lol. 

As for the service. The greeters were sweet and friendly, so were the bartenders. The waiter was a pretentious dick, always made strange gestures whenever we had questions about some of the the dishes. 

This is by far not one of the best Mexicans in New York. You guys have a long way to go.

I just don't Get It

This place is frequently packed, so I guess they are doing something right but I JUST DON'T GET IT.  I was disappointed the first time I went - had mediocre food and left totally hungry after spending $150+ for two.  I figured maybe we just didn't order well.  Went back.  We asked the server for advice and apparently the duck is their signature dish . . . OK, I'll try it regardless of the $94 price tag ($120 with tax and tip with nothing else, no drinks, sides, nothing).  It was duck meat with skin - that's it.  I guess it was OK as far as plain duck meat but worth 120?  Not close.  I guess I will continue to be perplexed about this place and why people continue to frequent it????

Loved everything about this place. From the very friendly waitstaff and bartenders who explained everything clearly and answered any questions without hesitation to the amazing cocktails at the bar and delicious food, this is a go-to I will definitely revisit. Must try the duck carnitas after all that's why you came here, right? And to complete your meal, must have the corn husk meringue, melts in your mouth.
Atmosphere good. Food decent. Portions ridiculous. Price obscene.  If you go there plan on spending your rent money and leaving hungry. Skip it so many better places to try.

Don't be fooled by it marketing strategy. It is a joke. Very bad service and food.

1. The menu is totally incomprehensible. The names of dishes are just some random ingredients in Spanish and American Indian words with no explanation. You feel like a fool when looking at the menu. This is not the customers' fault, it's theirs.

2. Painstakingly polished but tasteless food. Only good for Instagram but not for eating. This is the common problem of most "modern" restaurants in New York City.

3. Annoying service. The waiter kept harassing us while we were eating and talking, asking "how is everything". I said "everything is okay" several times but they still came and ask over and over again as if they were deaf. I perceive their behavior as they were driving us out, so we went away.

Expensive for serving size at this high end Mexican tapas style restaurant. We were 6 people and 6 items was enough despite the servers suggestion of 2 items for each dish. We did order 2 short ribs though.  I thought the highlights of the meal were the duck, the short ribs and the desserts.  This restaurant lost a star for me (and I easily give out 5 stars) due to its service.  Taking plates away while some are still eating, not being clear when describing dishes and not really being attentive in general was a let down. 

Conclusion: Good spot. Great food. High price. Okay service.

Went here with my family and a friend after making a reservation about a month out since this place has become so popular.

After perusing the menu, we decided to split a few dishes:

Uni tostada (2.5 stars): I don't get what all the hype is about--this dish did not do anything for me.

Cobia al pastor (3.5 stars): This dish was very good, especially with the pineapple salsa.

Honeynut squash tamal (4 stars): This dish was good, but the sauce was excellent--perfect amount of sweetness and spice.

Duck carnitas (4.5 stars): This dish was super tasty and a large size--the price tag ($90) is a bit absurd, but this is the whole reason why you're coming to Cosme. The homemade corn tortillas are a real sleeper as well and pair nicely with the duck.

Overall, this place has a great duck dish and serves some other serviceable dishes to accompany it. And the duck is delicious, but severely overpriced. In addition, our waiter recommended 8 additional dishes to the duck, which was utterly wrong as we were perfectly fine with the 3 extra dishes for 4 people. Finally, we each had a $17 drink here and weren't particularly impressed by any of them. Though this place is deserving of the hype for its duck dish, there are plenty of other well-rounded dining experiences that are more bang for your buck around the city.
$200 for a plate of FAT. Awful food, unapologetic service, terrible restaurant. Do not eat here.

Maybe I am just suffering from a bit of culture shock, having dined fairly recently at chef Enrique Olvera's Pujol in Mexico City (at the original Calle Francisco Petrarca location). Cosme surprisingly lacks any echoes of what I assumed to be his signatures: A delicately subdued and earthy atmosphere, ingredient-centric storytelling, and gracefully attentive waitstaff choreography. Instead, Cosme felt like Midtown blah meets the ABC Kitchen bar. Obviously, the two are intended as completely different classes of restaurant, but at Cosme I totally lose sight of the through-line; of what the kitchen aspires for my meal to be.

The stand-out dish was an appetizer: Hiramasa (yellowtail) tostada with plantain aioli, avocado, and quelites (wild greens). Perfectly balanced, bright, and crunchy with clean-tasting, butter-soft fish. Things took a downturn at the ayocote bean salad served on massive raddichio leaves. Yuck! Imagine a multitude of bitter leaves loaded with what basically amounted to hummus, with random sprinklings of dill. It was unpleasant... and heavy! "Heavy" is not a cute look for a starter salad. 

The guacamole fared a bit better. But it's hard to mess up guacamole, especially for $17. I will say that it was nice to taste soft, fluttery cilantro and fresh mint in the dead of winter. Given Olvera's maíz-mastery, though, I was surprised to see it served with salty tortilla chips rather than something like warm blue corn tortillas. We did finally get those for transporting the duck carnitas, which had, yes, a delicious, crisped, fatty, lovingly-cooked piece of fresh duck. However, New York City does have Chinatown.

I do regret not trying the chicken mole, but given the track record of the meal at that point, I could not bring myself to resurrect the sanctified memory of Olvera's 300-day mole madre.

Finally, maybe I'm a petty child (okay, I am a petty child!) but I do expect a *bit* better for a birthday lunch reservation than a seat near the bar in direct line of the drafty door, or than zero acknowledgement from the staff (I see you, fellow Yelper with the wee birthday cake photo!). When asked about dessert, we were given the main course menu again, so that about settled it. I didn't even feel compelled to order a celebratory beverage, settling instead for a grainy horchata. I resented my fizzle of a celebration, waiting for a communion that never came at this spotlighted trap for ladies-who-lunch.

Expectations matter greatly when reviewing a restaurant.  For example, if you're Stephen Curry and you scored 15 points in a game, I'd say you had a lousy game.  But if you're a benchwarmer whom I've never heard of and you scored 17, then I'm going to be mightily impressed.

The same is at play here.  I knew Cosme was named a top 50 restaurant in the world.  I expected a dining experience commensurate with that honor.  And sadly, this was not even one of the top 50 restaurants I tried in NYC, let alone in the world.

The highly-acclaimed duck carnitas was ok, but not exquisite.  I'd rather have a Peking Duck.  

This is not to say that the food was bad - it really wasn't bad.  It's just not top 50 in the world good.

The food was bad. Basically what we received was nothing but sauce, thin tortilla, and ricotta. We couldn't believe what we were given, that we couldn't help but laugh after we left. We got pizza after eating here as there was no substance, no enjoyment, no nothing in our dishes. Give it a shot if you must, but go as an experience. This is not good food.

It's so ridiculously expensive, but the hype is real, this place is amazing. The duck carnitas is the way to go. Don't believe it when they tell you to get a ton of dishes. The duck carnitas plus 1-2 things is all you need. We had to wait for around 15-20 minutes past our reservation time so they comped us two drinks which was nice. It was so packed late on a weeknight, they must be minting money here.

I think people are rating it low because of ingrained notions that Mexican food "can't be expensive". Would they have as much of a problem paying these prices at a French or Japanese place? Personally, I think it's awesome that they are elevating the cuisine.

I've been here a few time and I love it. It's better to make a resevation in advance but if you walk in it's easy to get a table at the bar.  The service is very good and it has a great atmosphere.

The food is delicious. I totally recommend the guacamole (10/10), short rib and the merenge for  dessert!

Classy and with lots of dark mood lighting, this place was a great venue for a birthday dinner. 

We started with the Cobia al pastor - it was a type of sliced white fish that also came with tortillas to wrap. It reminded me of sashimi / ceviche and had a nice delicate flavor to it. 

Next was the grilled octopus with potatoes and capers. I loved the emulsified potatoes (?) mixture that came on top and the combination of the different pieces. The pieces of actual potatoes were a little bland and undercooked but was fine when you ate it with the other things on the plate.

Our "main courses" were the short rib and branzino, which also came with its own set of tortillas. I highly recommend getting the short rib. It was the best thing out of all the mains because it was cooked to the point where its tender but still a bit crispy on the outside. The scallions and other parts of it were good enough to eat by themselves.

The branzino was just okay, so I would skip this one. It was just too bland and even when you added the cilantro / avocado dipping sauces, it didn't help the flavor too much. 

Lastly, we ended the meal with the corn husk meringue that everyone kept on raving about. I was honestly a little disappointed. Yes, it was good but it just tasted and looked like whipped cream. The sugar husk was just a hard shell of sugar, so nothing too exciting there either. I don't think it's worth all the hype it has received.

I appreciate and dislike the tortillas accompanying every dish. I like that the tortillas do help make you a bit fuller given the small portion sizes, but it kind of downplays or lessens the taste of the dishes. However, overall, I did enjoy this meal and liked how it was a different take on mexican cuisine.

Exceeded expectations.  Guacamole was chunky but good and subtly spicy.  Scallops wrapped in pear had good acidity. Octopus was tender with Rich, buttery mashed potatoes. Traditional mole was least amazing but I'm not a mole guy. Except the white mole was amazing with the mushrooms, sesame, and veggies. Dessert was corn husk meringue

I'd been to Cosme twice before but I hadn't Yelped about it. In my book that just doesn't count. So as I entered Cosme for the first time last night, I had a weird feeling of deja vu. It felt familiar - as if I'd been there before. 

Cosme is all about the ambiance. It was packed on a Sunday night. And loud - as the voices of many merged into that eager hum of a restaurant in its prime. The space and tables are large so that it doesn't feel cramped even at capacity.

Food takes front stage at Cosme. I had the "short rib, scallions, cipollini, avocado." The rib meat was cooked to perfection and the charred onions added the perfect contrast - glossy white on deep brown, crunchy sweetness on tender umami. Additionally the guacamole was top notch. The amuse bouche little nut dip with cracker defined sophisticated quality. And the little chocolate nib dessert amuses bouche were surprising in their soft melty texture and the powerful depth of their rich flavor. 

When you come to Cosme, you do it for the cocktails. The menu is full of exciting concoctions, but I had a plea for our waitress. "Ma'am may I have a spicy margarita," I pled. The spicy mezcal drink that arrived a few minutes later was very good.

Going to a Saturday brunch at noon in a trendy, sleek, extremely hip restaurant full of beautiful people, clubby music, and fancy cocktails is totally opposite of my personal brunch sensibilities. But change is good for everyone, and in this case, I very much enjoyed Cosme.

This is a New, or Nuevo Mexican, or contemporary Mexican, or just fancy Mexican food. Whatever you call it, just know it's definitely on the high end side and not at all comparable to the places you might be used to. Still, you can't deny the uniqueness and freshness and quality of the dishes. We started off with cocktails. I did a Michelada which was amazingly good. We decided to share the lamb barbacoa for two, since so many people around us were getting it. The lamb is served in a large crock with shiso peppers and topped with some greens. It comes with sides of avocado slices, radish, lime, hot peppers, an an array of sauces. You get a bowl of fresh warm tortillas to make your tacos. From there it's just a big eat fest. I thought we wouldn't use up all the tortillas (we did) or the fixings (we did). There was an enormous amount of meat though, and we definitely didn't get through that, though we tried. The lamb was incredibly tender, flavorful, and pretty much just melted in your mouth. 

Service is actually pretty good and not nearly as snobby as you would think.  It is an expensive place though, so be prepared to drop a decent amount of $$$.
What an outstanding spot. I am so glad we got to experience this restaurant. Service was spot on. Duck carnitas were worth every single penny and the short ribs delicious.

I made a brunch reservation here because i came for dinner.  Everyone said the brunch was much better ( hoping so i thought the dinner was just ok).  I made a reservation at 230 on opentable.  So its not like i asked to come in that late.  I was rushed from the moment i walked in.  Literally we didn't even get seated and they told us the kitchen is closing.   I said right then why would you have a 230 reservation open if you are closing.   Subsequently the waiter reminded us they were closing the kitchen.   So we rushed our order.  They forgot several dishes and when i reminded them what was missing they said again the kitchen is closing.  They served us with so much attitude. I don't understand why that whole situation occurred but really turned me off from eating there.  I do come back to sit at the bar and have that dessert.  I put up with the weird service to enjoy that one item.

-Bustling, exciting, modern atmosphere.
-Friendly hostess was willing to hold our table even when one in our party was running late.
-Waiter was helpful and gave a lot of suggestions.
-Benny blanco cocktail was delicious--similar to a negroni, but with tequila.
-Herb guacamole was phenomenal and a generous portion.
-Honeynut squash tamal was ethereal and delicious--the lightest tamal I've ever had.  Tamales are so often too dense.
-Black trumpet mushroom huarache was earthy and satisfying.
-The duck carnitas for two is pricey, but worth every penny.  It's one of the best dishes I've ever had.  The meat is perfectly tender, shredding the second you put a fork in it.  The flavors are complex and on point.  The spice level is appropriate.  And it's served with amazing homemade corn tortillas!
-We were pre-theater, and they made sure to get us out in time.
-Great experience--we can't wait to come back!

Best new Mexican I've tried in a long time. Cool dark mod atmosphere but you can see your food and people. Not too loud. Service is excellent. Waiters are good about explaining drinks and dishes.  Yes, the uni tostado and duck are the winners.  Liked the scallops as well. Cocktails were great. but a bit pricier than most places but the amount they give you is more, so OK.  If  you get the duck, its definitely good enough for 2-3 people if you get 3 or 4 other dishes depending on what you get. Meringue dessert is very unique, light and not sweet and a great way to finish. Definitely go back.

Overall experience was great for us! I hear and read about the food being good but the service is bad. However, our lunch date was perfect! The mezcal that was picked out for me was tasty, each dish was flavorful and executed nicely, the decor is appealing, and the service was great! We had the duck, ant and corn mousse (dessert) dishes. Recommended to the non-judgey foodies!

It pains me not to give Cosme 5 stars, however, when a restaurant reaches the level of recognition they have, mixed service can't be ignored.

First, the food here is simply amazing. Maybe I'm anchored having just spent some time in the Yucatan but each dish we had was incredibly satisfying. This, in and of itself, is an amazing feat here in NYC where quality, authentic, Mexican food is ironically difficult to find.

Starting with the drinks, she got the El Ninja and I ordered the special, which was a play on the traditional Michelada. Both were refreshing and fun. We ordered a few more drinks throughout the night and loved them all.

Next we ordered a number of dishes, including the Uni tostada, an octopus cibeche (ceviche), some pork, and the Duck carnitas to share. Each dish was bright, salty, fatty, and/or everything else that makes Mexican food so delicious!

There is just one critique of the whole night and that would be the less than stellar service by the Maître D'. I won't go into great detail other than to say that, from reading other reviews, there seems to be an ongoing culture of apathy and almost disdain for the guest by some of the staff.

COSME, if you are reading, this lack of service is holding you back from being a great restaurant versus just good.

All in all though, I highly recommend coming here if you are looking for genuinely Mexican influenced cuisine.

One of my favorite spots in NYC.  Great food, staff and concept. My favorite dish is the braised duck, oh my, it's so tender and full of flavor, an amazing dish!! The bar menu is also pretty good, has a great line of cocktails.

I really wanted to like this place, but the food was alright at best and the service was terrible. The only reason I feel obligated to give this place a 3-star rating is because the manager did end up comping us for the food.

Came on a weekday with two friends, with reservations.  The waitress was completely disinterested from the moment we sat down.  She took our drink orders and guacamole while we decided what else we wanted. She came back and took our orders; overall we ordered 5 things minus our drinks.  We sat for a good while with just our drinks, sans guac, when 2 of our main dishes came out. At this point it was clear the guac wasn't coming, so we informed our waitress. She did not seem remotely concerned, and seemed more annoyed at us when we told her we no longer wanted it. When our third dish came out, we weren't sure which it was, but could not stop her to find out.  We ended up stopping another waitress.  Our waitress saw this, pulled aside the other one to find out what we asked, but never herself came over to check back in (including to ask if we wanted another round of drinks). As we continued eating, we realized our last dish had not come out either - which makes 2/5 dishes missing overall. When the waitress finally made her way back over, we requested to speak to a manager.  While she went to get him, they brought over the after-dinner mints; so clearly didn't give us an opportunity for dessert.

When the manager came over; he listened and then told us that he could see how that would make someone never want to return, but did not offer a way to correct the situation!  After 5 minutes, he offered us dessert, but at that point we were ready to go and asked for the check.  He left for a good 10-15 minutes, only to come back to offer us more food.  No sir, we'd like to leave.  He then took another 10 min to bring us the check, with just the drinks on it.  Yes, it was nice of him to comp us the food.  But I would rather have paid for a full meal at a place with good service.

Food was great but crazy expensive for the portions. The service stunk. Our waiter kept trying to get us to order the duck tacos at $90 and tequila shots. We also were asked to exit our table seconds after we finished our dessert. I was with a group of 8 and we spent about $825 - I think you can allow us to finish our coffee.
Interesting dishes and flavors. Overall was good but   a bit expensive and the food wasn't exactly our taste. Desert though was really good! The restaurant decoration is really nice.

Having lived in Manhattan for 7 years I have not been impressed with the Mexican restaurants except for one other well known place in Soho.  I was a little skeptical about trying Cosme but heard great things about it.

I love this place.  As a native Californian and often in Mexico I found the food to be phenomenal.  The service was on point and attentive.  

The only drawback is the reservation availability (which reflects the strong customer support and frequency).  All in all, fantastic food if you are in the mood for a true culinary treat of Mexican food .

1. Hostesses were not friendly -1

2. Food menu was short and to the point +1

3. Service was speedy +1

4. Food and cocktails were really good +1

5. For Mexican food these prices were kind of high, there's a stigma here that I can't get around -1

Fantastic meal. Started with chicatana ant fluke aquachile -- very interesting flavors on the fish and nice light way to start the meal. Worked into the tamale and the pastor taco (forgetting the fancy name) which were both fantastic as well. We then shared the duck carnitas which were incredible (but needed to be for $89 plate...). The corn husk meringue desert was my favorite of the desert options at the end -- very light and unique. Overall the service was good, but food incredible. While expensive we had a fantastic time.

I wanted to love this place more, but couldn't.  

There is some incredible food here (IE: duck, fluke) and solid cocktails, but there was also some dishes that weren't great (octopus) and one dish that I thought was a joke --- the Mole Rojo.  The mole was just some mole (sauce) on a plate with a side salad.  No protein.  Really?

One of my friend's tacos had a rootbeer leaf ("hoja santa") stuck to the bottom of it.  The manager tried to convince us that it is typical in Mexico to serve tacos with rootbeer leaves.  I lived for 5 years in Mexico, traveled all around the country and never saw this before.  It was a strange moment.  

Small nit, but we arrived a few minutes early for our 5:30pm reservation and were told we couldn't sit at our table. Despite an empty restaurant.  So we had to just stand there.

I give Cosme props for showing New Yorkers what Mexican food can be, but I found the place missing consistency and most importantly, true Mexican hospitality.

I won't be going back.

Given that Cosme is on many of the "top 50/38/2948389" lists, we as a group of 6 came here for a birthday dinner with high hopes. To be paying the high prices such as charged here, we expect to be somewhat (or at least slightly) blown away by the food and flavors, but we were not. Since we were a "large party" for Cosme's dining style, we sampled majority of the menu. Everything was delicious, but nothing stood out. The famous duck carnita was very tender and juicy, but did not have much flavor on its own. In addition, the portions are extremely small (basically catered to one person for some of the dishes) and even those that the server recommended as "good for sharing", we needed to order 2 servings. All of these factors combined, we felt that we spent a lot but did not feel satisfied at all. The setting is very dim and romantic so it would be more suitable as a date night kind of place. Cosme also has some interesting cocktails but again, somehow none really jived with our palette unfortunately (perhaps the flavors were too eclectic? some were spicy and some were salty..). I would also say that this place is not great for kids as most dishes are very "refined" flavors (and also given the price range). There is no high chair available either so you need to bring your own booster.

After being told ten times that the kitchen was closing at 3- we quickly ordered. The portions are extremely small for the price point. Guacamole is super fresh, tasty and aromatic with fresh herbs on top. The chips are warm, non-salty and perfect size for dipping. The lamb was sold out, duck not on the brunch menu  the cold brew coffee is phenomenal. So nutty & flavorful. No sugar or creamer is necessary. 
Avocado ceviche had a nice balance between crunchy and smooth. 
The uni tostada is smoky and silky but really overpriced for the portion. Literally nothing on this menu is able to be shared. Margaritas are perfect.  I am a huge fan of the desserts. The churros were perfect, not dense or oily but light, fluffy & delicious. The birthday girl in our party had a yummy tres leches with phenomenal sprinkles and whipped cream. 

If I go again- I will only order the guacamole, cold brew and the corn husk meringue which is out of this world!

Definitely a fan of this dark sleek sexy restaurant in flatiron district.  Came with my sister to celebrate a belated birthday.  The atmosphere and vibe of the room is great.  the quality of the food is amazing, and that says alot coming from a very finicky new yorker.  We shared small plates starting with the lobster which blew me away.  The food definitely is the star of this restaurant, the wine list is excellent with nice bottles in every price points.  The staff were friendly and guided us to a perfect evening.  We left the restaurant satisfied and not bloated.  Will definitely be back.  Not a cheap place to go.  figure about $100 per person

I ordered the Uni Tostado ($21) as my appetizer to whet my appetite. You know, just to tease my tongue a little bit for what's about to come. Cosme's Uni Tostado came with fresh avocado, bone marrow salsa, cucumber, and cilantro. Despite the spectacularly italicized ingredients listed on the menu, I wasn't blown away by the actual product, given the price. Although the uni, tomatoes, and avocado were fresh, the tostada itself was stale.

The Duck Carnitas with onions, radishes, and cilantro ($45) was my second favorite dish from Cosme. The duck itself was cooked perfectly, mesmerizingly smooth, and easy to pull apart with a fork. In fact, the texture reminded me of pulled pork. The duck meat was extremely flavorful and possibly one of the best I ever tasted. The skin is full of mouthwatering duck fat that elevates this dish's savory depth.

I have been to Cosme many times for dinner and have never been disappointed.  My husband is a real fan which counts for the multiple visits.  We decided to try their brunch today.  We both felt a little let down by our choices.  

I ordered the Enfrijolada, ricotta, hoja santa, queso fresco.  Now, I never complain about the price of a dish but for $19 had put in front of me a bowl with 2 corn tortillas smothered in pureed black beans topped with a sprinkle of cheese.  This was just a gloppy mess.  There was no way to eat this with a fork and it was totally unsatisfying.

Because I was so disappointed with my first choice and didn't want to eat just sauce with a spoon I decided to try another dish.  I ordered the Chilaquiles; green with chicken.  Out came a bowl piled high with tortillas drenched in green sauce and sprinkled with very little chicken.  For $18 I felt this was just another gloppy mess.

My husband ordered the Huevos rancheros, black beans, mushrooms, queso fresco which we both found to be very tasty but certainly not worth $24.  However, since I don't base my ratings on price this was a satisfying dish but served in a bowl and again a little too drenched in sauce.

Also, the bar stools.  Ridiculously high bar stools.  I needed my husband to give me a boost up.  Not long after we sat down at our table I watched another woman try for 3 minutes to get up onto a bar stool.  

On a positive note, the cocktails are spectacular, the space has a very cool vibe and the service is attentive.

Beautiful restaurant in every way. Food is inventive and creative but taste wonderful and is presented beautifully! Ask for Tiffany Hernandez to make you a cocktail, she is a wonderful bartender and will start your day or evening off just right!

Surprised to see Cosme rate 3.5 stars on Yelp.  I expect there will be a lot of reviews penalizing Cosme for high prices.  

IT'S ON THE EATER 38 PEOPLE !!!
http://bit.ly/2j0Uel1

I had a scallop aqua chile with tortillas which was an easy way into my meal.
I had the ayacote bean salad which disappointingly had a lot of lettuce in it.  I'd pass on this dish.
The piece de resistance is the DUCK CARNITAS.  Order this. So delcious.  I never thought I'd have anything but pork carnitas.  So good.  

I also had 3-4 margaritas.  Not surprisingly I lost count.  Note: If you want to keep the bill down, don't order so many margaritas.

Heavily overrated and over priced! If you enjoy spending $400 on tiny plates of food that you're not even sure what you're eating then this is the place for you! I was super excited to eat here as I had been hearing about all the hype, not to mention that this is one of the top 50 restaurants in the world - but I was let down terribly.  The service was just ok, nothing to rave about. Restaurant is tiny dark and very loud.  Had the famous duck carnitas which were yummy but nothing to write home about, the husk merengue was interesting and different but nothing over the top amazing. When you go to one of the top 59 restaurants in the world you expect to be blown away - not the case here!

The first time I went to cosme for brunch, I was like...meh. I didn't understand the hype, especially coming from several Mexican friends. I went back this past wknd (after more than a year), and holay molay. It was amazing. I didn't order right the first time around but now, I need to go back for three things in particular:

1) Duck Enmolados - lemme preface this by saying mole sauce is not my thing. While I didn't have the actual duck, the sauce is incredible. 100% would order again.

2) Lamb Barbacoa - O.M.G. I don't even like lamb (unless it's in kabab form) but this was unbelievably good. It's BIG, and meant to be shared (we were a party of 6, and still had leftovers). It comes in a huge pot with pea shoots on top, and homemade corn tortillas on the side as well as a variety of salsas, limes, onions and aguacate. So, so good, and we managed to get the last one of the day. Literally going back for this ASAP.

*While we did find hair in the dish, our server immediately apologized and removed it from our bill ($69!).

3) Husk Meringue (dessert) - ok so when it came down to order for dessert, this was the least appetizing thing to me between the meringue (which I'm not a fan of) and corn mousse (which didn't sound particularly appetizing). But my Mexican friends said they too would never have ordered it had it not been highly recommended, and it's now a favorite of theirs. It is so different from anything I have tasted and comes with homemade vanilla-infused whipped cream and sweet/salty corn mousse that is a total game changer. Delicious + so creative.

Our server was fantastic - and truly added to our experience. Can't wait for my next visit! Also, it's good value for your money in my opinion - we would have spent around $36pp had the lamb dish remained on our bill. Not bad at all.

P.S. The Bloody Maria is delish -- the chiles are soaked in tequila and add a great kick to it.

Sunday visit for brunch. A mixed bag.
DRINKS. Fantastic! My group started at the bar before the table was ready. The Gin & Shrub with beets wasn't bad, the El Ninja with mezcal, gin and vermouth was bracing, but the smokiness of the mezcal was balanced by the sweetness of the shio shrub which could be considered a dried, chewy pineapple. The Striptease was also excellent with the mezcal and vermouth countered by the tincture of absinthe and the absinthe salt. The Micheleda was a wonderful spicy and effervescent version of a bloody mary.
FOOD. Delicious, but. The oysters were fresh and yummy. The uni tostada paired the briny saltiness of uni with the fatty smokiness of bone marrow salsa. The hiramasa tostada featured beautiful silver skinned slivers of yellowtail but they couldn't quite shine through the competition from the plantain aoili and the copious topping of greens. The green chilaquiles with chicken were very good as the nachos retained a crispy counter point to the spicy green sauce and tender chicken. The highlight were the duck enmoloadas in mole rojo. The mole sauce was amazing as it displayed the confidence to let the sweetness of the chocolate peak through when many mole go in the direction of the bitterness. Deftly judged flavors an textures.
DESSERT. The husk meringue was fantastic and the churros were crispy on the outside while being soft and fluffy on the inside.
And now the but. The tostadas were $21 and $22 and each. A steep price for a bite fit for one, maybe two people at the max. The 3 duck enmoladas and mole sauce were excellent, but at $25? Expertly prepared food, but eye-watering prices that aren't commensurate. Loved the food, but leave this place to the trust-fund babies and expense account flashers.

Food was delicious. We ordered a Mexican Red wine (pictured $80) which was excellent - medium flavored and paired well with the food. Their signature Duck dish was really good and can feed 4 ($86). The bean salad is also quite large. Can't remember the 2 fish tapas we ordered but they were both excellent. The Short rib with the avacado spread also great. For desert we tried their corn mousse special which was very different and nicely done. Service was very good.

I rarely give reviews but my experience with Cosme was so terrible that I felt I had to give one.  Before I start I have to say that the two hostesses were the best part of the experience. They were super nice, professional, friendly.  

Aside from the hostesses, the food was subpar and the service was terrible. The restaurant is also not kid-friendly which is fine (we were told to bring our own booster seat), but what I felt was insulting was the fact that they continued to skip my son who is almost three whenever they brought anything to share for the table.  We were six adults and one child.  Every time they brought the tortilla chips, they only brought 6!  The chocolates they brought at the end - also 6.  My son is almost 3 and we ordered food for him so it's not as though he's still an infant who would only drink milk.  This was just ridiculously bad service and to be honest, pretty disrespectful.  

We spent  600 for the 6 adults plus one child and came away from it dissatisfied - the fluke we ordered had a hair in it.  Yes the general manager came and apologized and took that plate off the bill but never brought a replacement.  We also had ordered two plates of that but only one (the one with hair) ever came.  The drinks were pretty but did not taste good.  The duck, which is supposed to be the signature dish, was rather dry and tasteless unless you add in the sauce.  

I was so excited to see the uni dish on the menu, as I love uni. I was so disappointed with the taste. The only dish I liked was the honey nut squash.  

5 stars for the hostesses and 0 for food and service.

So, been wanting to try this place for awhile. Don't bother coming here. It seems to try really hard on the menu, but it falls flat in my opinion. The octopus was weird. The trumpet mushroom thing was okay. The fish was okay, not great. They seem to really try and be creative, but its just not that good. It's really busy and the service is pretty bad. Definitely never going back. Go elsewhere in the neighborhood, there are a lot of good restaurants surrounding it.

Wow this place is amazing. The food wow I honestly wasn't expecting this and the bar tenders are all so sweet and make great mixed tequila drinks. I'm a tough cookie when it comes to my tequila and I gave the bartender a high five for how excellent their spicy tequila cucumber cocktail was. Place is a little busy but worth it.

What really hurts this place is the fact that everyone knows it is one of the top 40 restaurants in the world right now. Obviously, expectations are high. We got here last Friday for dinner - I had a reservation for 10.30pm. In spite of getting there in time, the receptionist asked us to start at the bar till our table was ready. I didn't argue, she looked busy. 

The bar was extremely busy as well so my friend and I waited awkwardly till someone took notice of us. Fortunately, another member of the waitstaff approached us and guided us to our table. It was super squished to the tables next to ours and I was worried I would knock the glass of water at the table next to ours as I made my way to the sofa seat. 

It's difficult to have a private conversation because you can 100% hear everything exchanged at the tables next to yours. For instance, the couple next to me was on a date. The girl wasn't impressed by the duck option on the menu. But her date insisted that the duck here is super popular and she'd truly love it. It seems the duck is super filling and most people don't get anything else on the menu if they order this particular dish. She thought it was okay but said that it would have been nice if they ordered a bunch of small plates like the tables next to her.

So we took her advice, I guess. Not that she intended to give it to us. We started off with drinks - I got the striptease while my friend ordered the Paloma. Our waiter told us those were the 2 sweetest cocktails - they weren't all that sweet tbh - but both were amazing. I genuinely enjoyed the striptease cocktail.

We then ordered 2 vegetarian small plates - the Manouri tatemado, nopal, cascabel, avocado ($19) and the Honeynut squash tamal, ha'sikil p'ak, castelrosso ($20). This was obviously after we consulted google to figure out what those words meant. I honestly have no idea what it was that we ate - the avocado salad was good. The other honeynut squash plate was funny. Not adjectives I was looking to describe food I would eat at such a fine establishment.

Also, the table next to ours got complimentary blue chips and this pumpkin butter. I was going to ask why we didn't receive it but it seemed strange to have to do that at such a coveted restaurant. Anyway, we finally just got the corn husk meringue which was delicious.

There is a large selection of food, in portions that are laughably small. And in language that not everyone understands. The waiters don't take the time to explain what their menu choices mean. I'm going with 3 stars - one each for the drinks and one for the dessert. You can't be one of the top restaurants in the world just because you can cook ducks decently well.
Does not deserve the hype. Small, noisy, tables packed close together, loud music, stingy  portions, crazy expensive. On top of that, hostess staff inexperienced and unhelpful.  Would never go back.

The duck carnitas was delicious and easily serves 4 if you also get a small tapa or two. The scallops with jicama were one of the best things we got! The guacamole was good but nothing special beyond normal guacamole. The squash dish had a delicious sauce, but the squash itself was not well cooked. The mole was not great and the uni tostada with bone marrow tasted fishy and was poorly seasoned. 

The cocktails were amazing! The smoky mezcal in the El Ninja absolutely exceeded expectations. Finally, the corn husk dessert was FANTASTIC as was the postachio and dried raspberry. Don't skip dessert here :)

Nice food but got a particularly bad waiter.

Had been wanting to try this place for ages. Showed up for brunch with two friends. When the server came to take our order, we asked what we should try and he pointed to the lamb. The lamb was 69 dollars, by far the most expensive main on the menu (others were around 30). So we hesitated for a bit. He said it's been on the menu for 3 years. It's not that I don't believe him and I'm sure it is good but besides the price factor, we also were interested in trying a few dishes and it seemed like the lamb was a very large dish and if we went for that, it would pretty much constitute the entire meal aside from one appetizer and a dessert. So we opted for other things.

I didn't think much of that exchange until later as we just could not find our server the entire time. He never once returned. Other wait staff refilled our waters, took our dessert order and even our check. 

It seemed to us like our designated server was offended that we didn't go for the most expensive dish on the menu and/or felt like as three young women, that we probably weren't going to end up being a table that had a large bill, so why bother to offer us service at all. There were several minutes of just looking around, trying to catch somebody's attention. We told another waiter, one that actually served us on his behalf, about it. That one said, he did tell our server that we had ordered dessert. We said, yeah so you reminded him that we existed and he still didn't come over. The colleague also mentioned that he wasn't defending the other guy but that two people didn't show up for work that day.  

We paid our bill and left. Our original "server"--putting it in quote marks--because he didn't really do anything for us, never once looked at us after taking our orders. Find it really snotty and intolerable.
Everything was tasteful! The service was on point, our waiter was constantly making sure we were served with water,drinks,food anything we needed he was ready to cater us with our requests.

On Saturday night I enjoyed a delicious meal for a friend's birthday. We started the evening at Cosme where our waiter forgot our order of guacamole, where I'd had to research each menu item before our visit bc nothing is described properly or listed in an order that would help you determine which dishes are appetizers, which are entrees, and which are just large bowls of mushrooms, and where for $25 you can enjoy 3 whole scallops and some cabbage leaves for dinner. I love the whole dining out experience, and don't blink at spending too much money on a good, fresh, interesting meal with excellent service, but the atmosphere at Cosme was unwelcoming (with the exception of the hostesses who were lovely), the service was far below what we'd expected, and while most of us enjoyed our "meals", like the joke about nice restaurants usually goes, we all left starving.

Luckily, there was a taco bell along the way to our next stop, which welcomed us in all our glittery Saturday night finery, fed us quickly and sufficiently and without pretension, and cost about $6.
My gf took me here on one of our first dates. We split the duck tacos and it was phenomenal. The margaritas are delicious.

I work in the same building were the restaurant is located and I always see the staff and they are just rude including the cheff Daniela doesn't say hello and talks bad about the security in the building in Spanish very rude and not nice at all. so I still went to the restaurant for dinner with a friend and waited 20mins for my reserve table and when it was time to eat the food was not all that hype to be I've eaten in better Mexican resturants in the city the duck horrible no taste at all and drinks were not worth paying for, so overprice for blah service and food .... And please chef Daniela and staff be consistent in being nice everywhere not only in the restaurant it will show more in your food and overall atmosphere.

author.name: Karen G.
author.location: Long Island City, New York, NY

reviews.review: This place is amazing. We ordered tapas for the table and wine. It was fabulous and the service is wonderful.

This the 5th time I've been to Cosme. It's always on my list when visiting  NYC. 

Started with the Cobia then moved to the soft shell crab. Both were delicious but really it's all about that damn corn husk meringue dessert which is the most delicious thing ever. Sweet, salty, creamy, smokes. Believe the hype.

My family dined in this place recently and they all got food poisoning afterwards. We contacted the restaurant and informed them and they promised to reimburse us for the meal. A month has gone by and so far we are not getting any responses to our emails or phone calls and they have blocked us. This is a horrible place to dine at. Not only they are outrageously overpriced, but they have also zero customer service. Would not recommend this place to anyone!!!

Terrible customer service!!!!!!  It was overprice for the quality of food and the icing on the cake was a case of food poisoning .  When it was brought up to management it was not handled with care.  I do not recommend this place!!!!!

Duck carnitas is all you need to know. It is perfect for sharing, prepared simply and deliciously with cilantro and thinly sliced jalapeños. We also enjoyed the 2006 Rioja available by the glass, and the ambiance of the dining room. Only thing I'd avoid, for the ladies, are the super tall bar stools. There is no graceful way to climb down without making a mess of your drink and/or outfit, even when you've just had one drink.

4.5 stars! Starting off with an inside tip, "don't order the herb guacamole" as it's located inconspicuously way down at the bottom right of the menu. We all know Mexican restaurants serve guacamole. But I've been told, at Cosme, it's more like an afterthought than a dish they'd recommend.  I'm sure it's good given the rest of the menu is excellent...but I couldn't say for sure.  

The evening started with some complimentary blue corn tortilla crisps with a wonderful Terra cotta colored spread/dip.  Not sure what it was exactly but had a hint of almond I believe.  I ordered the Paloma cocktail (Tequila & top notes of grapefruit and lime with grapefruit salt) and my bestie ordered the "Striptease" (Mezcal & a nice smoky yet fruity flavor and salt).
