My favorite and the must try dish of the night was the uni tostada with avocado, bone marrow salsa, and cucumber, oh sooo delicious! I secretly would've wanted to order three - just for myself (and make that my meal). The combination of flavors and textures were unlike any I have ever encountered (and believe me, I love me some Uni)!  

Other dishes I liked:  the fluke aguachile with chicatana ant (yes, ants - but they are all ground up, you can't see it) and sesame - it was tasty.  And the manouri tatemado with quelites, nopal, cascabel, and avocado were also very good.  Chef Enrique Olvera and his team sure know how to make great combinations of flavors.

There was one dish I must say, in which I was sadly disappointed.  It was the scallops with avocado aioli and jicama. Sounded great and even reviews highlighted it.  But on my visit, it would seem it was prepared differently from when my bestie experienced before.  The jicama was sliced into a ribbon like pattern and posed like a wonton wrap, hiding a gorgeously seared scallop sitting atop the avocado aioli. The colors were there, the scallops were delectable, but the jicama was not.  They took a mildly flavored refreshing vegetable and turned it into a salt lick.  It was completely drenched or overly salted; like a pickled brine. Terribly salty. I had to drink a lot of  water to wash the taste down.  I was so disappointed in this dish.  Dear Chef...please reinvent this dish again...put it back to how it was made previously.  

The good news for me, after that dish, we still had two more dishes to come to make this review 4.5 stars.  The salad we chose was the Ayocote bean salad.  Paired with mixed greens and a charred cucumber vinaigrette.  Note, we still had an order of duck carnitas to share which by the way, was heavenly!  The onions, radishes, and hint of cilantro...superb.  This dish is not for the faint of heart, it was $89 but was meant to be shared!  The meat was fall off the bone soft and fork tender.  Accompanied by never ending house made tortillas which I used to eat it like a taco.  This is their signature dish and what they are ultimately known for.  Well worth the price, great for sharing and is a must try.  

Lastly, we had to have dessert.  Couldn't leave without sampling the popular signature dessert -- the corn husk meringue with corn mousse.  It is one of the most famous/ best desserts in NYC.  The unique combination of textures and complex, subtly sweet flavors - yum!  And, as a bonus, it is also beautiful to look at!

I thoroughly enjoyed my dining experience at Cosme.  Was super glad I got to try it and with only a month in advance reservation.  FYI.

I'm not really impressed.  

I came alone for lunch.  The hostess wouldn't let me sit at a table, instead I sat at the bar.  Normally I don't mind but the barstools were so tall I sat hunched over and my back started to hurt.   The hostess and bartender were prompt but wholly unenthusiastic about their jobs.  I think I saw one person smile.  

I ordered the Herb Guac appetizer ($17 for a very small dish and 6 large blue corn tortilla chips).  The dish lacked any real Mexican flavor.  The herbs (dill, basil & tarragon...?) added a strange earthy taste that didn't remind me of authentic Mexican Guac.  The few peppers I found were hot without adding flavor (like a Poblano or Jalapeño would) and it lacked tomatoes, onions, lime, cilantro or the other elements I normally expect in guacamole. 

The avocado was fork mashed (as it should be) but the avocado pieces were too large - forcing me to cut my guacamole before dipping the chips.  

I left after the appetizer.  No need to stay for lunch.

I really wanted to love Cosme don't get me wrong. I have had so many friends rave about it, as it has just become a trendy Gramercy go-to. However, I was not blown away. Our server was a bit pretentious adopting the attitude of the restaurant with their high prices. The cobia was AMAZING, but I mean $17 for guac that I could probably make in my kitchen.... Come on. All in all the food was pretty good, but I probably won't be returning because how good it was was outweighed by the subpar service and prices.

TLDR: I eat out a lot. Trust me when I say Cosme isn't worth the hype by any stretch of the imagination. I love Yelp but so many 5 star reviews make me wonder if folks know what they're talking about or buy into the hype because it's a hard rez to get. I usually don't care enough to write a review even if I don't have a great experience because I get it. It's New York. It's hard to impress in food. But given the price you'll pay for what you get here, I felt compelled to share my view. 

Full version: Every NYC restaurant is worth checking out...at a certain value. VALUE. It's what it always comes down to. Cosme was fine. Is it better than a corner stand taco? Sure. But does that warrant all these 5 star reviews and the prices they charge. Most definitely not. I love spending money on food (and lots of money) so this isn't coming from a penny pincher.

- Uni tostada: come on guys...those of you raving about this...just come on. If you gush up and blush every time you see uni, then sure, but otherwise this was just fine. Needed much more acid.  

- Cobia: this was delicious. No beef with this dish. Very well done. Clean, full, crisp flavors. 

- Scallops: ridiculously unbalanced. The jicama was very, very sour. Scallop itself was nicely cooked though.

- Octopus: very disappointed in this. Loaded with mounds of queso fresco and 8 small slices of octopus. Couldn't taste anything other than cheese on a soggy memela. Kinda a joke at $28 bucks. to put this into context, it was a pretty thick memela, with some black beans spread on it, tons of cheese, and 8 slices of rubbery, overcooked octopus on it. 

- Hen of woods: full credit here. Tasty. 

- Duck carnitas: lots of youtube videos on this hyping it up. This may take a long time to prepare and it was tasty and I don't want to take anything away with regards to technique, but again, value. This is absolutely not worth $89 in anyone's wildest dreams. 

I basically look for reasons to give my money away for food. Take my money! But at Cosme you're going to be out at least $200-$250 for 2 people without drinks. You could go to Gramercy Tavern one street down for that amount. Let that sink in. 

Positives: very cool setting and vibe, friendly waitstaff. No beef with the front of the house or decor...just with the food at the price they charge.

Blown. Away. Next level Mexican dining. PSA: I despise ridiculously priced places. But I try some a few times a year to remind myself of the horrors of socioeconomic status. Cosme was one of the most exceptional dinners I've had this year, and it happened for me and my wife's 2 month wedding anniversary. 

We were told we had to order the duck carnitas (tacos)..which is the best advice one could give and get (I saw the enormity of that thing later in the night), but we weren't starving and knew we couldn't take leftovers so we got 3 dishes. 1 off each section of the menu. Sections are 1) raw fish/ceviche 2) veggies/salads 3) entrees
Entree: We ordered the Short ribs w/ roasted cipollini disk onions and scallions and avocado puree!! I'd kill a man for it again.
The Fluke aguachile ceviche with chicatana ants (harvested after the first major rains straight from Mexico) was something I never thought I'd ever eat. Light. Flavorful. New. Fresh. Delicious.
That salad lookin dish actually featured a dank black bean tamal with warm, stringy, stracciatella cheese under those delectable purslane greens. Another completely unexpected dish of greatness.
The rim of my drink was covered in salt and bee pollen. It was a culinary experience all in itself. 
Dessert was an unbelievable corn husk meringue w/ corn mousse. It was a vanilla-y, salty and sweet, corn treat.
Then we capped the night off by watching Jose Reyes beast with a 2 HR night as the Mets cruised to victory.
I'll be back for the $90 duck tacos..

Everything I had on the menu was nasty!!!! I've been to over 100 restaurants in NYC and this is by far one of the worst tasting places I've been to. The service is good and the drinks are good but the food is literally nasty. No one in my party of 6 likes the food!!!! Strongly DO NOT RECOMMEND this restaurasn

Inclined to write this because I feel like the majority of the negative reviews are just hung up on price. the prices are not cheap,but they are FAIR. Dont come here looking for taco stand prices then complain about pricing.

For dinner the duck was fantastic. The Branzino was my favorite dish and the Fiancee's favorite dish was the Hiramasa tostada (the uni was good, but this one blew me away). This white fish tostada worked so well with the mint, cilantro, basil, other herbs, and a sauce that perfectly balanced the dish out

Chef Enrique Olivera has earned himself the Michelin star at Cosme through his unique flavor profiles and his upscale take on classic Mexican flavors. My last trip I had the lobster with brown butter, shisho and ginger mojo. I don't think I've ever had a more tender and perfectly cooked piece of lobster. The star dish at Cosme is the enomoladas though. The complexity of flavors in the mole made by chef Enrique is awe inspiring, paired with the freshly made blue corn tortillas and cojita cheese makes this a dish that will stick out in your mind for a long time to come. Finally for dessert the famed corn husk merengue will surprise you with how many ways he incorporates corn in the dish. Easy 5 stars for me.
good place, very good service very good attention the food is perfect the drinks are good I was delighted with the rich food,

My co-worker recommended me this place to go with my friend so I decided to give it a try. 

Cosme is known for Duck carnitas which means, everyone should try it. Personally, I am not a fan of duck but this restaurant changed my mind. The duck is simply AMAZING.

The server said the duck was for two people but the portion was way too big for us. He even recommended we get a salad with the duck which we did. We ended up not eating everything but it was still amazing. I think the duck, and the salad overall would be great for three people. 

Unfortunately, we had no room for dessert but next time I go, I will def try the dessert.

Food was good, but not worth the crazily high price and hype. Reservations on weekend nights are hard to come by, and we had to make reservations weeks in advance. The ambience is romantic since the lighting is very dark. We were advised to share 3 plates each. But we found that 4 dishes for the two of us were more than enough. We ordered the uni tostada (the hubby liked this, I didn't), the guac (liked the mint in it), the fish tacos, and the short ribs (both came with tortillas and were delicious). 

The waiter seemed a little stuck up, but we had a good experience overall. But I'm sorry, $89 for duck carnitas is just too much for us to try the signature dish.

Chef Enrique Olvera doesn't disappoint with his first venture outside of Mexico Cities World Renowned Pujol and was pleased that Cosme also made it into the Worlds best list. 

Service was A+, went in early for my reservation that I happened to snag last minute while I was in the city. It was early but the restaurant quickly filled up which might have been from the fast moving showers that caught many by surprise. It wasn't long before the hostess had our table ready for dinner. I was also thrilled to see chef Enrique was at the helm and to be in NYC during my stay. 

Food was captivating. By far the pulpo in agua chile was the star that grasped you in from the very first bite, you keep trying the sauce even after you devour the pulpo. 

Btw they make one mean Paloma 

The dessert was also brilliant to cap off the meal. The corn mouse lives up to the reviews it gets on here. Had a coffee, from Mexican origin, to end my night. 

All in all Cosme is worth the effort to try and get a reservation although next time I'm in the city my aim is to try Cosme sister restaurant Atla

Cosme is known for its duck carnitas. Sweet, supple and damn delicious. But I went for brunch. And they didn't have the duck carnitas. So after 10 minutes of debating whether I should just swill back my too-early-to-be-drinking glass of wine and make a run for it, I decided to order the lamb barbacoa.  And it might be the best decision I've ever made.

WHAT WE GOT:

LAMB BARBACOA (5/5)
You know when you eat something and it's so good, you begin to question why you ever put anything else near your mouth? I think even a tear trickled down my face as I took a bite of the lamb-stuffed blue corn taco. Served with copious amounts of sliced avocado and fun mix-ins, this dish throws serious shade at most egg-y, hash-y pancake-y brunch options.

**It was so good, I canceled my ABC Kitchen reservation and took my mom for barbacoa the next day **

I came here for lunch for the second time, and it somehow topped the first!

There were about 7 of us, and we asked the waiter to send over an assortment of food for the table. He did an excellent job, and we left full without feeling like there was too much food. Despite the concerning name, the poisoned oysters were delicious. They were simple, but tasted incredibly fresh and refreshing. The uni tostada was great as well. If you're an uni person this is a must try - some of the best! 

The stuffed avocado is one of my personal favorites - it's filling while still being healthy and protein rich. The seafood inside is delicious and well rationed. The Huevos rancheros were also good, but wouldn't put it top of my list if only for the alternative more interesting options. I really enjoyed the branzino: I thought it was well cooked and plated. The short ribs also were a hit with our table. Finally, the duck carnitas are a must try - they were perfectly cooked, and were the perfect consistency and tenderness; so worth the wait!

In short, this place is great. The space is neat, the service is usually on point (occasionally it can feel a little slow), and you can't go wrong with the food no matter what you order!

AMAZING. I never would've thought to go for high end Mexican while visiting the Big Apple, but a Chef friend told us we HAD to dine here, and I am so glad he did! The calamari, the duck carnitas, the Husk Meringue with corn Mousse, all were so delicious. The service was impeccable, as well. This restaurant DESERVES to be as highly regarded as it is.

I went there with my son and boyfriend to celebrate my birthday. Beautiful restaurant. I had the cobia al pastor and duck canitas, both are excellent. My son and boyfriend were very happy with their choice too.The cobia is the high light of the meal. The service is a bit shaky, but I give 5 star anyway base on the food.
The service and food was awful. The food had no taste and the server had no idea of how to take care of customer. Never coming back.

I have been there 3 or 4 times. I can't believe how this place changed comparing with the last time I was there. First of all the place is expensive, but at leaser in the past I felt that the food was good. Yesterday the food was super disappointed. They called "enfrijoladas" but it is really mole with some frijoles, that dish was just a sauce with some cheese. We also had "chilaquiles verdes" they were average and again super spicy! Cocktails cost average are 17 dlls. And honestly there are not extraordinary. I expected a cocktail with Mezcal but nothing. Finally the check came and it was 60 dlls per person for a brunch. Next time I would prefer to be in Gramercy Tevern, Loteria, Casa Mezcal before Cosme. Enrique Olvera, as a Mexican try to set the bar higher and if you are going to have those prices, make people think it was worth it

Ranked #40 in the World's Best Restaurants, Cosme can be slightly tricky to get a dinner reservation to. The restaurant generally has reservations available for weekend brunch a week or so in advance. Cosme serves one of my favorite dishes during brunch (the Stuffed Avocado with Seafood). The restaurant also has great cocktails and desserts.

Ugh!
First time visited here when it just opened, I recall I was not very impressed.
Second time visited 2017 Summer, still quite disappointed.

Started with uni and oyster- both dish were not fresh at all. And my cocktail was literally a cup of ice. Already lose appetite of this place.

We shared several entrees, nothing really stands out besides the Duck Enmoladas, this one was pretty good.

I recently had dinner at Cosme and I thoroughly enjoyed the experience. I would rate the herb guacamole a 5 :)

Cosme lives up to its goal of serving contemporary Mexican food. I love Mexican food and was surprised that I didn't understand the menu. However the servers are knowledgeable and can describe the ingredients and dishes very well. The service is amazing and the decor is very modern. 

The duck carnitas live up to the hype and the dish easily serves three people. We also ordered the short rib, ayocote bean salad, morel huarache, and finally the husk meringue because I wanted to try it all. 

Bottom line - dinner here is delicious and it's a wonderful experience. Yes it is pricey, but you know that ahead of time. See my photos for more!

We weren't impressed with Cosme. We didn't have any issues with the service, but of the 5 dishes we ordered, only one was really good.

Cobia al pastor - best dish we tried. It was the perfect mix of acidic, sweet, savory, and spicy. Our favorite.

Octopus memela - we were completely underwhelmed. This was bland and lacked flavor. 

Corn tempura soft shell crab - Just okay. Not a lot of flavor, just sauces to put in top to add heat.

Short rib - the accompanying avocado didn't pair well, and the short rib wasn't tender but more chewy. 

Duck carnitas - the meat was very tender and it was good, but it wasn't great. For $90 it should have been amazing and flavorful. It wasn't.

This place deserves a Michelin Star! I came here after watching Enrique Olveras on Chef's Table. I love his story and the way he think about food. 

The vibe of this place is pretty relaxed. It gets a little loud sometimes but it matches the relaxed, chic and modern atmosphere. 

The first time I came here was with a girl friend. We ordered the duck fajitas to share and oh boy it was delicious! The duck pulled apart easily and had so much flavor. Also, it was the last seating of the night (1045pm) and the chef gave us broccoli Tamal on the house. I wouldn't have thought to order it but gosh it was delicious!!! Needless to say we gobbled it up.

The best part is definitely the dessert. One particular dessert, to be exact. The corn husk meringue. To die for! I could eat this everyday. It's slightly sweet, creamy and salty, with the crunch from the shell of the meringue, and the chewiness of the middle, creaminess from the burnt vanilla crema and the salty butter-I was of the corn mousse. I would recommend everyone to come here just for that. Absolutely amazing!

I've been back a couple times since then with my husband and we tried a few other dishes. But the top 2 must is definitely the duck fajitas (huge portion btw) and the corn husk meringue.

Subdued looking Mexican food that is so delicate and refreshing, it sneaks up on you leaving you to wanting a lot more.  Appetizers were only ok. The artic char tostada had an absurd amount of avocado, it wasn't easy to eat. Seafood salad was solid, bean salad is an easy skip. The star is the tacos and I'd love to just jump right back to them only. The duck and branzino were both not just cooked perfectly, but the colorful presentation was something to behold. The tortillas are the best I've ever had, and pulled everything together. The ambiance is a bit to sterile, too serious.  

I'd come back for dinner.

I've been to many restaurants in the 50 best list and they all offer great food, great service and something unique. Cosme brings little of this to the table. The Al Pastor was really but that was all. I wouldn't even put Cosme in a "top 50 in Manhattan" list.

My wife was craving Mexican food during our visit to NYC and we had just seen the Netflix episode of Chef's table... done.

After reading a lot of the mediocre reviews, I just figured people had different expectations.  I knew not to expect Chipotle or fajitas, but a twist on traditional food.  Service was excellent without being overbearing and the scene is fantastic.  Overall, the food was good.. not great.  I think the $17 guacamole is absurd.  We shared a couple of the small dishes and the flavors were familiar with a twist.  The duck carnitas. amazing.  The side of duck comes deboned in a cast iron skillet with some sliced radish.  We shredded the tender meat, hoping to incorporate the fatty goodness.  Combined with the salsas and warm corn tortillas, these were delicious.  Maybe it's because the flavors were more familiar to me?  Hmmm.

Anyways, the cheesecake was certainly more savory than I was expecting, but still good.  I don't think I need to revisit... but would recommend you try it once for yourself.

Lo ciento, Cosme! I really, really wanted to love this place. It's experiences like this that remind you that service can make or break. We dived deep into the menu. We had the Striptease cocktail with smoked Mezcal and the Grüner Veltliner white - both had great acid and tang to cut light fish/poultry fare. For eats, we had the broccoli tamal, Arctic char, cobia al pastor, and the enmoladas; all super delicious. For a shareable main, we had the braised short ribs with cipollinis, and avocado cream - yum!

It all came down to forgetfulness, and a nagging feeling that there was literally no pass off between shifts. About a third of the way through, we stopped seeing our original server and, instead, experienced a new person every time a drink or new dish was served. Everyone was super helpful and explained what they were serving, but no one remembered that we wanted to keep a copy of the menu in case we wanted to order more later. Everyone kept trying to take it. My husband order a drink the same time I did and I got mine, but he was made to wait. Both tables around us ordered after us and received their drinks before us. observed our server come up to take our orders only to turn on his heal and high-tail it to the bar to place his (our) forgotten drink order before trying to talk to us again. That was the last we saw him. No one remembered that my husband was gluten-free (Celiac disease) after establishing this at the beginning. No one remembered that I had asked for a replacement cocktail after I finished my first round. ("Would you like to order a refill?" to which my reply was "I already did...")

I don't know - the food was amazing, but it can't carry a business 100% of the way. I would have gladly taken the tad-cheesy TGI Friday's/Red Robin approach of "Hi folks, I'm going to be taking off for the night and Carrie will be taking care of you, ok?" than be forgotten about. I'm sure there was an attempt to forego this bit of dialog to ensure a seamless experience, but it fell apart dismally.

We really loved Cosme!  We were very sad when we were in Mexico City a few months ago that we couldn't get into Pujol, but were extremely pleased with a birthday dinner at Pujol.  We completely over ordered and when the Duck Carnitas arrived last we could only eat about 1/3 of them, but we were blown away by everything *prior* to that.  Our favorites were the Octopus Memela and Cobia Al Pastor, they were truly phenomenal.

We also sampled the cocktails and liked pretty much everything we had, which is unsurprising given the delicious source material of Mexican liquors and cocktails and the quality of the establishment.

This is certainly now our favorite "not-cheap" Mexican food in the city (they're really two different cuisines, right?).
The lamb dish for two was AMAZING! The shishito peppers in it were so good, gave it a good kick but not too hot. Great atmosphere and really cute plates. Can't wait to go back.

Could not be more amazing and Danielle the hostess is SO nice

Extrodinary food and most innovative.   Every dish was absolutely. Extraordinary

We had the most wonderful experience

Margaritas with fresh grapefruit are  so fabulous. 

Run don't walk and try to score a reservation

Came for dinner and got the duck carnitas to share. The waiter recommended 4-5 dishes for two people to share or 2-3 before the carnitas, but I don't have that kind of money. Luckily, I read some other reviews saying that the duck is pretty big, so that's all my boyfriend and I ordered for dinner.

Turns out the duck carnitas were big enough after all--both of us were full after devoured the whole thing. It came with two spicy sauces and a basket of tortillas. The skin was crispy and the meat was tender. I'm not sure it warranted the high price, but there was no denying that it was delicious.

However, the star of the show for me was the corn husk meringue. I've never had a dessert quite like that before and every now and then, I still get a craving for it. The creamy mousse inside the meringue complemented the crispy shell very well and I loved how the corn flavor was noticeable, but subtle. 

All in all, I would definitely go back for the corn husk meringue and to try some new dishes for dinner!

Finally we have a chef who makes elegant, sophisticated Mexican food. As a Mexican i feel proud and very happy to have a chef like Enrique Olvera. This restaurant became my favorite Mexican establishment. The food is incredible, and the desserts are amazing.

I should have trusted yelp - never go anyplace rated lower than 4 stars. Food quality has gone down - it used to be a lot better. Our server was okay but hostess at front was unfriendly at best. I guess they feel that they don't need to try since the place has gotten popular. Overall a waste of time and money

I came here for lunch and would come back again.  There are a few vegetarian options that we ordered.  The menu is a little confusing so I spent most of my time looking at what other people were getting.  The desserts were the highlight.  Their specialty--the meringue,  was awesome and I usually don't like those.  The other desserts were great too.  The drinks were only okay--just tried their regular margarita.

Delicious!!! The hostess and bartenders were so accommodating. We ate dinner at the bar and were blown away by the flavors. The three of us shared the duck carnitas, shift shell crab, lobster, enmoladas and the cobia el pastor. 

Duck carnitas: definitely get this- it was so tender and juicy!! It was a lot of food! It took about a half hour to forty minutes to make but the wait is well worth it. 

Soft shell crab: really good flavors and texture

Lobster: huge clumps of lobster- it pairs really well with the slaw

Enmoladas: rich smokey and spicy flavor! I would say this was my least favorite but I would still eat it.. so that shows how flavorful it was

Cobia el pastor: the mango and fish paired so well! It's seasonal so get t while it's ok the menu!!

My experience may have been biased by my high expectations. The food's presentation was beautiful but the flavors left much to be desired, however, the scallops were delicious. My girlfriend was not feeling well after our first courses so we asked if we could have the rest of our meal to go. We left a sizable tip for only being there about 45 minutes and no response from the waiter on her wellbeing as we left. Kind of rubbed me the wrong way. Overall I can understand its popularity but from the three dishes and drinks we tasted, we've had much better food at much more reasonably priced restaurants. Seems to be more of an "it" place than a quality eatery.

I thought Cosme was good, but definitely not so much that I would recommend it incredibly highly or consider it a must-go.

I came on a Sunday night (made a reservation several weeks in advance), and the restaurant was fairly crowded but not completely full. The service was great and attentive, but not too attentive, and no one was rushing us out (which I take with a grain of salt since it was a Sunday night).

We ordered almost all the veggie items on the menu and found some of them to be to die for and others to be good, but not something we'd order again:

The to die for:
Manouri tatemado (semi-soft cheese dish)
Morel huarache (kind of like a pizza, an open faced piece of dough with amazing mushrooms on the top)
Guacamole

The fine, but not what we'd order again:
Ayocote bean salad - a lot of flavors were going on here
Enmoladas - the mole sauce was a lot sweeter than expected, which some might like, but was not my thing

I also thought the spicy margarita was amazing, but the regular margarita left something to be desired.

After two visits to Cosme, I can now officially declare myself a fan.  Our first visit was mid-winter, and we managed to avoid the wallet damaging duck carnitas, opting for a more seafood focused meal. It was excellent - the cobia al pastor remained a particularly high point and lingered in my memory enough to make a return trip.

Fast forward to July and the menu has had some nice variations both seasonal and interesting.  This time, however, we felt compelled to try the duck and were not disappointed. Yes, it's very expensive. But having spoken with our waiter about the process involved, and having stuffed ourselves silly with this beautiful, glistening, savory vision of heaven itself, it was hard to argue with the bill. 

Service was impeccable...friendly, warm, happy to answer questions and spot on with suggestions. Cocktails were superb, and we just couldn't say more about our experience. I know Cosme is one of those places where you never feel quite pretty enough to be there, but don't let that entry vibe fool you. You'll leave feeling very grateful to have gone.

This is a great place for a nice Thursday dinner with friends, but I can't say I loved it enough to recommend it highly nor save it for a weekend event.

The drinks were fine and the food was par, but I can't say anything jumped out at me, especially because of the high expectations I had walking in. Overall, great place to hang out at casually with friends if you're in the area.

What a great dinning experience. High end Mexican with unbelievable flavor profiles. From cocktails through desert just one great course after another. Excellent wine list as well. Definitely coming back!!

Came here for lunch recently and am now a huge fan of Cosme. Not sure why the reviews are so mixed. Cosme is a beautiful, spacious restaurant that uses high quality ingredients to produce aesthetic plates that satisfy all 5 senses. I like that they kept ever dish simple and focused on the natural flavors of the ingredients. Quinoa salad with black sesame salsa, nopal, and watercress was really refreshing. Short rubs with scallion, cipollini, and avocado was just the right amount of everything and meat fell off the bone. Duck carnitas, the most popular item on the lunch menu, was not surprisingly the best. Served with onions, radishes, and cilantro, the duck meat was juicy, flavorful, and the right amount of fat. The Cornhusk Meringues with Corn Mousse dessert was single-handedly the best meringue dish in NYC. Super crispy outside with rich sweet corn filling on the inside. They even sprinkled it with charred cornhusk powder. Thoughtful creation and perfect execution! Could Cosme have done more? Probably, but I think they've perfected the simple yet upscale Mexican cuisine and I most certainly will be returning again, and definitely for dinner.

There are so many reasons to applaud the inventive and delicious food at this restaurant, it's a shame they committed the fatal error of including on our bill a $29 dish that we did not order and were not served.  Shame on the staff for this careless mistake.  If you go, make sure you understand each charge on your bill.

By the way, the relentless techno sound track gets tiresome after 20 minutes.

Omg! The worst place ever! They probably paid to be on the Top 50 restaurants in the world!! We order stuffed avocado with ceviche they brought it in a dirty plate with old piece of lime and it was so frozen that my teeth start hurts,
And the fish what so frozen that you can't even feel the taste of it,
Mushroom quesadilla just tasteless in a frozen tortilla...
Huevo ranchero just wrong weird with soggy tortillas underneath the dish..
And the service.. it was just horrible 
Awful experience

Terrible service!!! Do NOT eat here. No matter how good the food is it is not worth the headache of dealing with the completely incompetent and rude hostesses. I will never return. There are plenty of options in the city with the same food quality, but with professional service.

In a word, pretentious. Particularly, up front, from the hostesses. The rest of the staff were hit or miss. The air of importance is palpable and off-putting. We had a lot of food, drinks, and deserts, a party of six, and the general feel was, overpriced and "not all that". Sooooo many other establishments to visit it the city. I would pass on Cosme, nothing was memorable, and the rest of my party felt the waiter was outright rude and condescending. Disappointing. D+

Absolutely delicious. The mole was incredible. The ninja (mezcal cocktail) was legitimately one of the best cocktails I've ever had. It was definitely worth the money. Just let the waiter guide you and you'll have a great time. I can't wait to go back for dinner.

I went there with a friend from LA to this restaurant for brunch yesterday. As a New York local, I have never heard of this place. But my friend's son picked it. So, I went along. 

I ordered avocado ceviche and a simple egg white omelet. Didn't eat dinner as I was not hunger in the evening. But I had stomach pain in the afternoon and went to bathroom 3 times at night, then this morning another 3 times. Food tastes mediocre but my concern is the quality of the ingredients.

I went to Cosme last night for my birthday, which was the same day as the pride parade. Half of our party arrived exactly on time for our reservation but my parents were stuck in traffic due to the parade. They left with ample time and I did not expect them to show up late. The hostess told us we had to wait at the bar since they cannot sit uncompleted parties. I explained to her it was my BIRTHDAY and that my parents were stuck in traffic and were doing anything they could do to get here. She simply stated that if they didn't arrive in 15 minutes that I would loose my reservation or we would be rushed and had to be out by a certain time. I understand that there are rules when it comes to reservations but the restaurant was not crowded what so ever (even to the time we left). Finally my parents showed up at 5:50 PM and they ran to the restaurant. By the time they got to Cosme the hostess immediately was off putting and not welcoming. My parents who were exhausting from running to the reservation and pushing through pride parade to avoid being without a BIRTHDAY reservation we were told that we could sit but we would have to be rushed out of our table (when we were already rushing to get there ) when my dad muttered "Jesus Christ" under his breath. The hostess immediately starting yelling "do not curse at me" multiple times and threatened to call the manager over and over again. Needless to say this ruined my birthday evening and she didn't try to do anything to calm the situation or help us out. We ended up sitting at the table in the front, where people sit when they do not have a reservation. It was very awkward because we were sitting near the hostess stand and I could feel the tension. Although the food was great and our waiter was wonderful and gave us great recommendations, I did not feel special on my SPECIAL day. Needless to say  I will not be coming back to Cosme. This was the worst birthday I have ever experienced.

Lively ambience and great vibes! I didn't particularly enjoy the food as much though - we ordered the enmoladas and the morel huarache! Thought that the enmoladas was very average but the huarache was delicious!
More trend and hype than substance. Perhaps because it has won awards recently, there were large crowds, long wait times and high prices. Good, but does not live up to the hype.

I'm a big fan of Olvera's cuisine and Pujol is one of my favorite restaurants. Cosme is unfortunately overhyped and contrived. The food is ok. The hostess & waiters were obnoxious. We arrived 17 min late because of traffic. I tried calling their phone and nobody answered. When we got there they said they were fully booked with plenty of empty tables on plain view. We sat at the bar, where the chairs seem to have been purposely chosen to make you feel uncomfortable, and a waiter rudely told us we had to order everything immediately since their kitchen was closing. I hope they step up their game because Enrique's cuisine deserves it an New York needs better Mexican restaurants.
I was so excited to try Cosme! But was so completely disappointed!! Food was cold...hosted very unfriendly...and worst of all found a hair in my food. Waiter did not even care.

I really liked it here. The food was great, the ambiance was absolutely perfect and the service was up to par.

A friend and I had a variety of dishes that we shared. The octopus dish and the white bean salad were among my favorites.

The ambiance was so good. My friend and I had a lot of catching up to do and this was the perfect spot. It's somewhat dimly lit, but you're able to see at the table. It was really crowded that night (which is surprising because it was a Monday) but I felt that we had enough space, and there was a really lively vibe but it's not loud.

One the way out, we asked a gentleman of the service staff to take a photo for us and he was more than willing, and also really witty.

If I had one complaint it would be either that they're strict about making your reservation on time or the fact that there was a prolonged period of time between our first and second courses (but we actually really didn't mind that night because, like I said, we had a lot of catching up to do).

Definitely worth a try!!

First off, the design of the place is exceptional. Love the modern and clean feel of it. The waitstaff was incredibly friendly and accommodating and went above and beyond to make us feel comfortable. The food packed really unique flavors and all in all, I really enjoyed having brunch here. Definitely fantastic for both dates and groups.

Came here on a work lunch, it's a very clean modern establishment with a high energetic staff. We got the short ribs and duck enmolados. The shorts ribs were amazing, I would definitely suggest those. The duck emolados were good, for my taste they had too much sauce, but definitely use the white sauce it comes with on the side.

If they tell you the spicy margaritas isn't spicy, beware it is.

Loved it and can't wait to go back!  Compares with some of the finest meals I've enjoyed in Mexico City.   We had the latest reservation for lunch, and although we were told we needed to order when we sat down because the kitchen would close soon for lunch, we weren't rushed at all during the meal, and we had wonderful service throughout. Everything we tried was great, but the two things that stand out were the duck carnitas in mole sauce, and the spectacular corn husk meringue. That dessert alone is worth the trip!

Overpriced, but delicious. One star off for the ambiance, a bit too dark and loud in there. The waitress and hostess were really kind and upbeat. The ginger ale is made there and has the most distinct taste of ginger I have ever had in . It was really great overall!

Came here due to popularity, definitely trendy 

Could not understand the menu or what we were really ordering 

Waiter was not helpful nor friendly 

Ordered a not too spicy Margarita, ended up being super spicy. They fixed it by adding more alcohol it seemed. I watered it down to make it drinkable. 

Got the soft shell crab and a torta like dish with mushrooms. Ended with the meringue which was the best dish. 

Good for an overpriced, trendy, small meal. 

Would not recommend or come back.

"Lunch on a Friday"
Really amazing, high quality, and savory food - taking "Mexican food" to a direction and higher level that I've never had before.  Even the cocktails were definitely on the elevated level than many other Mexican or south American restaurants in the city.

We had uni tostada, aguachile, hueveo rancheros, fried oyster torta, and finished with duck carnitas.  This was a lot of food, even for our leisurely Friday lunch for 2; but we ate it all and everything was so good.  I especially loved the uni tostada.  Never had uni in mexican flavors, but it was amazing in my mouth. 

The ambiance was more chilled than I had expected - but then again, we were there for late lunch.  The decor is more like a cool living room than a restaurant with sleek but comfortable furniture and lighting.  The staff was really friendly and professional.  They never rushed us even though it was past their closing time.  Well, if we're spending more than $100/pp for lunch, this is how it should be ;-)

I see why it's hard to book a table for dinner at this place.  But now I do want to come back during dinner time to try more food.  (I just hope it's not too loud.)

Items Selected:
Horchata
Arroz con Rum, Santa Teresa 1796, Avua Amburana, Fernet Vallet, Ancho Reyes, Cashew Horchata
Herb Guacamole, House Tostadas
Uni Tostada, Avocado, Bone Marrow Salsa, Cucumber
Pink Peppercorn and Axiote Seafood Aguachile
Fried Oyster Torta, Chorizo, Black Beans, Chipotle
Duck Carnitas, Onions, Radishes, Cilantro
Husk Meringue, Corn Mousse
Warm Pecan Tart, Salt and Pepper Ice Cream
Oaxacan Chocolate

More impressed by Pujol than many have recently been, rumors of lousy service and dumbed down food not witnessed across seventeen dishes and nearly 180 minutes at the new location in March, it was with slightly lower expectations that a party of three sat down at Cosme on Memorial Day in New York City, the "World's 40th Best Restaurant" according to San Pellegrino probably a bit overrated in that regard, but nonetheless putting out several great plates with service that was friendly, informed and efficient.

Owned by Enrique Olvera and toqued by 2016 Rising Star Chef Daniela Soto-Innes, a smash hit with New Yorkers and culinary tourists ever since opening in 2014 thanks to its upscale Mexican Cuisine, strong Drinks and fashionable Flatiron location, it was minutes before Cosme's noon opening that several groups gathered in the restaurant's small foyer as ethnic music blared overhead, everything turned down immediately as the clock struck 12:00, diners led past the long bar full of Mezcal and shelves decorated in various knick-knacks, a seat along the left back corner mostly shielded from the conversation of others with a few view of the room's dynamics.

Approaching the restaurant as Mexican with a focus on local ingredients, the Ant Larvae and Pulque of Polanco replaced by Hudson Valley Duck and Produce from the Union Square Green Market, Cosme offers lunch till 2:30pm on weekdays and dinner from 5:30 till eleven o'clock at night daily, the weekend Brunch slightly different from Lunch service largely in terms of a Pastry Basket and Lamb Barbacoa in place of the famous Duck Carnitas, that fact alone enough to suggest a weekday visit as the sharable entrée featuring crisp Skin, supple Flesh and cold Vegetables plus housemade Tortillas was every bit worth the $45 cost with enough meat to form at least eight generously portioned Tacos.

Perhaps getting ahead of things by describing the Duck first, though for most couples that plus an Appetizer or Dessert would be plenty of food for dinner, let alone lunch, it was actually with a stiff Rum Horchata and one virgin version that the meal got underway, the former requiring a bit of Ice to melt before it was smooth enough to sip, though the spicy flavors of Fernet did go well with chunky Guacamole laced in Herbs served alongside piping-hot Corn Chips.

Told that the kitchen does a wonderful job with Seafood, the lunch menu particularly tilted towards pricy raw preparations including a $21 Uni Tostada that makes up for its lack of size with three full 'tongues' made even more creamy by Avocado and Bone Marrow Salsa, those who do not enjoy the flavor of Urchin would be well advised to invest in the Pink Peppercorn Aguachile featuring mixed cuts of Fish in a spicy bath with Onions, Cilantro and Avocado slices, the lack of Tostadas or chips admittedly a bit chintzy considering the $28 cost though the fried Oyster Torta is fairly economical with good Bread, Chorizo, Black Beans, Lettuce and Avocado for just nineteen dollars.

Rounding out the afternoon with Dessert, no meal at Cosme complete without snapping a photo (or several) of the famous Husk Meringue cracked open and oozing Corn Mousse, those who fancy the flavor of creamed corn will likely be impressed by the smooth and light composition while those looking for something else would be well advised to check out the smoky Pecan Tart served with Salt and Pepper Ice Cream that works not only with the Pie but surprisingly well on its own.

Cosme caused me to rethink what Mexican food could be. Growing up in the south, we have our share of amazing Tex-Mex restaurants and terrific taco trucks but nothing like this contemporary Mexican cuisine. No wall is going to stop me from eating these estupendo dishes:

Uni Tostada - the butter of the sea (uni) + butter of the land (bone marrow) are all you need to know.

Stuffed avocado - with fresh ceviche and horseradish for a kick

Chilaquiles - I prefer the red with egg but the green with chicken is bueno too.

Duck enmoladas  - The mole sauce burrows deliciousness into your taste buds but the duck was a bit dry

Husk Meringue  - corn mousse is a must try, unlike any dessert you've ever had

Churros - the airiest fried cinnamon dough in existence

Superb. As expected from such a great chef team. I tried a variety of dishes and desserts, and was completely satisfied with each and every course. Full flavors in a luxe, dim (semi-crowded) atmosphere. 

The scallops with avocado aioli were so flavorful. The Cobia al pastor was out of this world. Again, superb. I was so satisfied with their dinner offerings, that I went down the entire dessert menu. The corn husk merengue was of course, the star of the show. A must when visiting Cosme. The sorbet trio was amazing. The goat cheesecake was impeccable. I had a few other selections that I really liked as well, but those I mentioned are definite standouts.

The only not-so-negative thing I have to say is that the horchata was not sweet enough for me. But that's just a personal preference. I thoroughly enjoyed it, nonetheless. 

I will be visiting again. I will be recommending Cosme. An overall amazing, fine-dining experience.

I have to first disclose that my family is from Oaxaca, Mexico where Cosme's ingredients and food is very much inspired from. I was very excited to try Cosme but was very afraid that I would hate it, I thought that it would be too experimental and not authentic enough.
I went with my sister whom probably goes to Cosme about 3 times a month, she insisted we not make a reservation because the bar seating is her favorite, there is more light and it allows for conversation with your bar neighbors. We ordered the duck carnitas,, guacamole, the white mole, and husk meringue with corn mousse. 
1. The duck carnitas, are as good or better than I could have hoped, they reminded me of food I ate growing up, we ordered extra salsas (habanero and other) as well as extra limes. The portion is big, I had about 3-4 tacos, my sister did too and there was enough to share, I made tacos for two people sitting next to me.
2. I didn't try the white mole, as the bartender forgot to put the order in, even though it was a very lame move, we were a little happy that we didn't get because we were full from the carnitas.
3. Husk Meringue with Corn Mousse, this dish was everything. It reminded me of my mother. I told the bartender to please tell the pastry chef, that this dessert as well as the rest of the meal was an honor to my culture.

Mexican food is underappreciated and is not respected in the culinary world. I thank Cosme, Enrique Olvera, Daniela, and their very informed staff for demonstrating to NYC and the world that Mexican food is not only delicious but beautiful and requires true talent. I left feeling so happy and proud of the accomplishment.

Had lunch here and was amazed at the creativity and freshness of the flavors. Ordered Branzino, an egg dish, and an artic char tostada that was amazing. The produce, and fish were all super high quality. Great meal, friendly staff and expensive... But worth it!

5 stars for food - super high quality, unique ingredient combinations, decent vegetarian offerings.  Really enjoyed unique flavor of herb guacamole and the flourless chocolate cake dessert was decadent yet fresh.  

5 stars for ambiance - as you'd expect from a NYC establishment, very cool scene with complimentary, unique, and comfortable decor.  Basement bathrooms were vintage and unique as well as quite clean.  

4 stars for service - nice, friendly but not legendary

3 stars for price - ok, I am from Ohio, so I get that NYC eating will be more expensive, but $17 per cocktail and an $89 duck confit was a bit excessive.

Everything was excellent and exceeded expectations.  I went in knowing I had to try the duck carnitas and knowing I would probably think they are overpriced ($89).  However, that duck carnitas probably yielded something like 15 tacos and I had plenty of leftovers the next day.  Not to mention, scallops appetizer with avocado sauce and jicama was out of this world, along with the infamous corn husk meringue.  Mezcal cocktails on point too.  Not sure that I would go running back too soon,but definitely worth a try one time at least.   Service was very good too.

Cosme earned its fame for a reason - clearly it is one of the best Mexican places in the city featuring contemporary Mexican cuisine, but more so due to the fact that Cosme tried to attach its dishes with stories, so that diners could have a full context of the ingredients, and thus, a real talk with the chef.

I stopped by on a not-so-busy Tue noon, while the restaurant was still half-empty. Unfortunately the renown dish uni salsa was not available on the day, so I decided to substitute with the half avocado stuffed with seafood. Refreshing was the better word after I took my first bite, a very unique taste! Main course I went with the duck enmoladas, cooked with red mole sauce. Admittedly, it was on the salty side, yet duck meat was prepared tender and juicy. I could not help but to order the corn mousse, earned its fame through NYT. Soft, creamy, yet on the light side, it was as if sitting inside the heaven! Cannot think of a better way o end my lunch!

I wish I could have the privilege to try the duck carnitas for two, yet I was unfortunately dining by myself. It was a lovely meal, nevertheless. Another world best 50 nailed!

Cosme is a great restaurant and I truly believe they deserve 5 stars. The duck carnitas is soft and flavorful with a crispy skin. The salt-and-pepper ice cream was a different and odd experience. The meringue is amazing. Highly recommended!

Good but not great. The good: ambiance is nicely done, the staff is very knowledgeable, and the ingredients used are all top notch. The Duck Carnitas for two was the star, excellently prepared and presented. For dessert the Husk Meringue is both beautiful to look at and very different with savory and sweet tastes blended together. 
The bad: the drinks were expensive but lack any presentation at all. A margarita is served in a rock glass with salt on the rim; for 17$ I would've expected a nicer presentation. A bourbon neat in a nondescript little glass. The guacamole appetizer was bland with almost no seasoning and basically just avocado and some cilantro while  the tortilla chips were ok I've had better in many Mexican restaurants. The staff although very knowledgeable did not provide great service; our party had 2 plates come out at least 15 minutes later than the rest, not what I'd expect a $100 per person restaurant on a Monday night.
Delicious. Just don't over order. Portions are great for sharing. Service was attentive. Everything is gluten free, which makes it so easy for those with gluten sensitivity to order!

Extremely disappointed. Hostess service prevented us from even eating here. We had a reservation through OpenTable, showed up 3 minutes early and were told the system had our reservation at 5:30pm even though I showed the hostess my phone and the reservation still showed 8:30pm. She proceeded to tell us it was going to be awhile before we could be seated. We chose not to wait since the restaurant was not honoring our reservation and did not even attempt to correct their error.

Great exeprience! I'm quite sure that most people dining at Cosme aren't aware of the fact that it's one of the best restaurants in the world, and, technically, the best Mexican restaurant in the US. That's probably because it feels a bit like another NYC restaurant/bar join, packed with people enjoying the evening to loud music. But the food is exquisite, if you understand it and are open to rediscover the Mexican cuisine. Definitly try the duck!

A true culinary experience! Starting with the avocado seafood starter and the cocktails...Had duck for the first in my life here (Duck Carnitas). If all duck tastes like this- sign me up. The Husk meringue wCorn mousse is out of this world. The flavors are so perfectly balanced. The service is spot on. Definitely make a reservation - it is absolutely worth it!

The atmosphere was lively and the service was great. I enjoyed the two small plates we ordered and the Duck Carnitas was more than enough to fill up two people. The preparation of the duck left it moist, but not greasy and tasted amazing. I would have given 5 stars, but the price to quantity for the small plates was not warranted. Overall a good restaurant.

We had a reservation for lunch, but ended up sitting at the bar because we were early and they could not seat us till later --perfectly fine with us and boy did we luck out.  We had a wonderful bartender/waitress Lilliana who took awesome care of us and was very helpful with recommendations.  We had the stuffed avocado with seafood, herb guacomole, egg sope, and short ribs.  These were all excellent choices that went well with my glass of wine made specifically for the restaurant and my boyfriend's perfectly done margarita.  For dessert we had the corn husk merengue ad pecan pie with salt and pepper icecream. Both were incredible !  We cannot wait to come back for brunch and hopefully get the same service with our new favorite bartender/server.  5 stars absolutely! Flavorful and wonderful atmosphere

Yes, believe the hype. This restaurant lived up to its accolades. Prior to dining here last night I was a bit taken aback by the negative reviews, they are unwarranted. We dine out and good meals deserve praise and sometimes a high sticker price; Cosme included. 
Start with a cocktail; we went for the least complicated and extremely delicious   Paloma and a Margarita. Served in a large, heavy glass with exactly the right sized ice cubes. Refreshingly tart with the right amount of alcohol. Score 1 for Cosme. 
Now the food... the great thing about the menu is things are meant to be shared. Although Leon and I don't eat the same proteins there was plenty to share and we were sooo full. 
Try the herb Guacamole with these long amazingly, crunchy and Fresh chips. Plenty of heat and avocado. Next up the  
Cobia al pastor which  comes with fresh tortillas so you can make your own tacos. Very healthy serving size. The Pineapple purée with cobia... what was that.... pure Delicious and so Unexpected. 
Broccoli tamale, a must try. Next up 
Scallops with jicama. Freshest tasting ever. So clean and crisp with a little heat. 
Ayacote bean salad with market greens. We have never tasted anything like this lemony, smokey bacon flavor bomb. There's No trace of meat here, just flavor.  How can a salad be so complex  with heat slowly unwinding with bursts of fresh crunch watermelon radish. The Manouri although delicious, was so different than other dishes our palates were confused by the nod to Mediterranean  flavors. Or is it Mexican with med cheese, tilting a Mexican  dish on its head. 
Every dish was perfect and well balanced. Complex combos of acid,heat and salt. Each dish differed from each other but had commonality of complexity. 
The ambiance: Energetic  and vibrant with a creative playlist. Another nice touch, 
All utensils swapped out every course. 
And don't forget desert... the much reported Husk meringue is a must. Light fluffy whipped cream with a salty savory corn mousse. Yes it is a "broken egg". And delicious. Omg We ate too much, but worth it.

No wonder this is listed as one of the 50 top restaurants in the world. It is one of only three or four and New York City and is deserving of every Accolade it gets. The food is Mexican but this is not a guacamole and taco joint; if that is what  you want in a Mexican restaurant, this place is not for you. Food is world class. It has interesting new combinations of flavors and taste with Mexican overtones. Portions are small but if you have three courses plus desert you will not leave hungry. It is expensive but worth every penny because this kind of food is hard to come by.  This is a restaurant where wine is king - not Margareta.  I recommend this restaurant for people who are adventurous in their tastes.

Was really looking forward to trying Cosme with my friends and we all walked out severely disappointed.

We had empty cocktails for a solid 20 minutes before we had to ask for our waiter for another round.

Every time there was a single bite left on the plate  a waiter was there to immediately clear the plate, making us feel rushed and like people were hovering. 

The food was good but kind of tastes all the same. The pineapple butter is amazing and the cocktails were very tasty but nothing truly outstanding.

When we left, we spoke to the manager to let him know we were disappointed and felt rushed and he was mildly apologetic.

Save the $400 (for three people!) and go to one of the other 2,000 restaurants in NY that make you feel welcome and comfortable.

The ambiance and interior were great, everything appeared simple but worked together nicely. The staff was professional and very helpful. The dishes were tapas style so we ordered several dishes to try. We started with a glass of champagne and I also had the Paloma, both were good especially the cocktail it was delicate and flavorful. We had the arctic char and avocado tostada it was crunchy, the raw arctic char and creaminess of avocado was harmonious. The fried oyster torta was a cute little sandwich looked really simple but it was so tasty with the subtlety of the oyster flavor coming through every bite. The NY strip tartare was special, larger chunks of rare beef but it was so soft it melted in the mouth. I made a wrap with the lettuce, smoked bean paste and cured egg on top it was magical. The huevos rancheros was full of umami flavor loved the use of mushroom with the eggs in a delicious tomato based sauce. The stuff avocado with seafood - they choose the most perfectly ripe avocado topped it with a seafood cocktail that was fresh and tangy with the tomato sauce. One of our favorite dishes was the beef short rib - it's really amazing! It was cooked to tender perfection along with the charred spring onions and cipolini onions we put a little of everything in a freshly made corn tortilla it was so delicious! The Duck enmoladas in red mole, it was so flavorful I could lick the whole bowl. The other duck dish, duck carnitas was fork tender it came off easily assembled it in the fresh corn tortilla, I have to say the corn tortilla really comes through in flavor. The deliciousness and amazing flavors are attributed by the freshest high quality ingredients, that what I tasted. The desserts were very good the husk meringue and warm pecan tart, I could taste the fresh corn in the meringue. By the time I got to desserts, I was really really full and could only try small bites of them. It was really worth the trip to have lunch there. They were also kind enough to help me store my Dominique Ansel birthday cake in their fridge.

The whole meal was mehhh. Good atmosphere, a lot more lively than I expected for such an expensive restaurant. We had the lobster, grilled manouri cheese, brussel sprouts dish, short rib, and the corn merengue for dessert. The only thing that stood out and I would recommend is the dessert. Not sure if the restaurant simply wasn't my taste, but everything else was not memorable.  The flavors of the grilled manouri cheese dish were good. Neither of us liked the lobster dish at all. Overall, not worth the price.

I don't know how this place only has 3.5 stars! Seems a lot of folks are turned off by the price but if you do your research before dining, you'll have a better understanding of what to expect. This isn't just Mexican food. It's carefully executed, beautifully constructed, absolutely tasty Mexican food with an upscale twist. The seafood, particularly the scallops, is treated so simply it's like you're right on the water. Cocktails are OK. The bar crowd was packed on a weekend night at 8:00... the vibe much like a Meatpacking cocktail bar whereas the dining areas are a little more cozy.

The only gripe really would be not enough chips for the guac. The dessert - although good - not the star. We'll return when the menu changes and give it another go for sure.
So delicious, this place exceeded my expectations. The Cobia al pastor, duck carnitas, and corn husk meringue were all amazing. Totally lives up to the hype.

One of the most memorable meals I've ever had.  It's on the pricey side, yes, but you get what you pay for.  AMAZING birthday dinner.  Had the scallops, which were tender and delicious; the cobia pastor, which was my favorite.  Also the octopus, bean salad, and short rib.  All were incredible.  Husk meringue was not what I expected, but it was delicious!

If you're complaining about price at this place then you didn't do your research.  Food was exceptional and lived up to its ambition of elevating the traditional concept of Mexican cuisine.  Excellent service, elegant ambiance without pretension.  We had the Uni Tostada, Cobia al pastor, memela, duck carnitas for 2, and the merengue.  Shout out to the habanero sauce alongside the memela - amazing.

I came here with my Mammy last week on a "Broadway Show" trip to see "Hamilton". Didn't care much for that play as I thought the casting choices were strange to say the least... never the less, I wanted to take ol' Mammy to "Cosme" (which I learnt from Google means Greek for "Order" in Mexicano) because I had gone one before with my girlies and ooohhhheee it was "delicioso"! I live in Los Angelinos so this girl knows good Mexicano when she tastes it. But unfortunately this trip wasn't up to snuff!! My biggest complaint here was the famous "duck carneitas" are now $89!!!! That's US Dollars not pesos!!!! Last time I came here Hamilton tix were 100$ and Duck carneitas were $50. Now Hamilton is 500$ and Duck carneitas are 89$ what gives!!!!??? Last time I checked there wasn't no Duck famine going on.. last time I checked ducks weren't no endangered species... we have a sayin in Tennessee where I'm from in Texas that says "if it looks like a duck, quacks like a duck, gosh darnit it daggum better taste good!!!!"
Anyhoo, 89$ for carneitas is one thang, but when they came out- dare I swear on ol' Mammy- these were dry!!! 
I hate to pester over a typically stellar establishment, but ol Mammy sure is real ol and who knows how many more meals she got in her... 
If her health holds up maybe we'll be back to give those ducks another shot.
As they say in Mexicano, "¡Ay Carambo!"

The cobia al pastor was amazing, best dish of the night. Margarita was good. Husk was very good and unique. Lobster was a little disappointing. Brussel sprout dish was between okay and good.

I'd like to go back. Service was great, portion size was smaller than I expected but I didn't mind it.

I was expecting more out of Cosme given all of the accolades they have received. Definitely came in with very high expectations and was a bit underwhelmed in the end.  The food was very good but service was lacking.  The staff wasn't particularly friendly and we had to ask several times to get more chips.  Best dishes I tried: ayocote bean salad, broccoli tamal, short rib, and duck carnitas.  Of these, the duck carnitas was the star. Also, the striptease cocktail was very good. Cosme definitely offers a fresh and modern take on Mexican cuisine, but I do think it's a bit overhyped.
That duck. Omg. Its almost an impossible feat but my sister and I finished the entire duck by ourselves... It was that good and totally worth getting!!

It goes without saying that the food here is great. Obviously get the duck. The waiters and barmen will always do a great job of helping you decide what's great to order.  Since my boyfriend lives across the street, we frequent cosme whether it's for a quick bite and a drink at the bar (cocktails here are fantastic) or sit down dinner. On the night of my birthday we figured we'd get a few drinks here before continuing to dinner at another place. Some how the hostess overheard us talking, picked up on the fact that it was my birthday and sent us over a cake with candle. Just goes to show how much they care about their patrons and their attention to detail. This was so sweet and made us feel cared for, even though the restaurant was absolutely packed and bustling. The service is always wonderful here and for that reason we always find cosme a pleasure to visit.

What a wonderful dinner with friends!
Lucky to be 5 people so we could try so many delicious dishes!
The atmosphere is intime and the restaurant is very well simply decorated.
Service was wonderful, our waitress came with recommendations about how was the beat way to enjoy the meal, portions,... 
We had:
- scallops: oh so yummy, creamy and the radish were perfect. Yummy!!
- cobia: first time eating cobia. Very tasty
- strip tartare: i am not a tartar fan but i tried it and it was good. My friends were delighted
- lobster: oh my! A+ presentation and A+ taste!!! 
- chicken
- branzino
- short rib: super tender!!!
- duck: wonderful!! A must!

Deserts: cheesecake and something woth chocolate that I dont remember...

Considering it is posted #40 world's best restaurant, the price was fair. We payed (including 1 bottle of wine) around 100$/pers in New York!! Totally worth it!
Does anyone actually answer the phone here?  I have been serial calling because I have an urgent question related to a food allergy.  Nobody picks up.

Where do I start?
We made reservations online a month prior to our Sunday brunch. 
The day before our brunch our friend had a death in the family so I tried to call several times to cancel. The phone line was compromised so couldn't get through even though I tried all day and the following morning. 
We went anyway because I was fearful of the $50 per person cancellation fee. 
When we arrived we were frankly 20 minutes late...mainly because we had to get our friend to the airport to make it to the viewing and funeral. 
We were treated like we were 1 hour late...
The service was also just not good. The waiter couldn't explain the dishes intelligibly and give a clear explanation of the spice level of the dishes. 

We had to ask for chips several times before getting them. 

The mole dish was really more like mole soup. The huevos rancheros were tasty but we asked for Christmas style (half green and half red sauce) and it came with only 1 color sauce. 
Just very disappointed overall.

I was so excited to eat here - despite already having been disappointed at Pujol in Mexico City. I had confirmed reservations at the bar. We even got there a little earlier to have a drink.  The hostess was AMAZING and was so embarrassed to tell us that our seats were being held by the manager for someone... well that someone who showed up to take our seats were two girls... I guess someone was trying to get lucky.  Either way, we decided to patiently wait. You would think the manager would have come to excuse himself or even apologize about the situation.  A piece of bread would have been great while I waited lol...After waiting for a while, I decided to leave to another place where I would be serviced.  Will definitely not be going back!

Pretentious and fluffy. Mexican inspired food does not need to have myriad of variants on corn, no matter how clever. The bland interior is lit to hide the ultimately dull and department store like atmosphere. The table service was good but since we were asked how things were around 10 times during the meal,  it became sticky and annoying, with the threat of having small portions wisked away by overzealous bus people. The duck was good  however and if the portion was larger than others it might be connected to its 90$ price tag. The ladies working the front, as if cast for a cliche, were rude to our fellow diners. We were threatened with losing our 5:30 reservation  because one person in our party did not arrive until 5: 45 (its rush hour in Manhattan 2017 and you can choke on your policy even if other restaurants engage in the reprehensible habit.) Truly ruined our evening which was to be a bday celebration. 
Still have bad aftertaste from this over rated and over priced sleight of hand insult to meso american legacy, culture and hospitality.

I love Mexican. Cocktails were not even close to their Mexican originals, way too much ice. All appetizers were amazing, especially the scallops. Short rib and duck for main did a good job. Spicy oil is amazing. Deserts were good, though other at the table thought they are very good.

I really wanted to enjoy this restaurant. I read that it was ranked one of the 50 best restaurants (it placed 40th), and I had seen the Chef's Table episode featuring the chef. So I was hopeful, but I left feeling a bit let down.

Uni Tostada - I have had much better uni, I was not particularly impressed by this dish. 
Steak Tartar - Something about the texture was really off. I expect steak tartar to be light and refreshing. But this was mushy, almost gelatinous. It sat on a bed of beans which did not help with the texture. 
Brocoli Tamal - This was almost flavorless, it was a lighter version of a tamale which was nice. But I think there wasn't much in terms of taste to recall. 
Octopus Memela - I enjoyed this dish, the octopus was cooked perfectly.
Duck Carnitas - These were pretty good, but I was pretty full from the not so great appetizers. I wish that perhaps we had only gotten the duck carnitas and the spicy margaritas. Perhaps that would have helped with the rating. 

The service was good, we didn't have to wait for our reservation to be filled. I liked the high ceilings, large plants, and atmosphere of the restaurant.

I'll start with the excellent service because really, it was. I'm giving this place 3 stars but if there was a 3.5, that would be my choice. So many menu items were raw - it was like confused Mexican. I guess I wasn't expecting extremely expensive uncooked Mexican. The place was packed so obviously lots of people love it -- I'm just unfortunately not one of them. 3.5 stars (not 3).

Best brunch I have had in a long time. The Bloody Mary was well worth $17 and the chips and guacamole were the best I've ever had. Entrees can be pricey but I ordered one of the less expensive options and still left feeling full. I was very excited to try this restaurant after it was ranked #40 in the world and it definitely lived up to my expectations!
Sorry but nothing about this place is as low as the current rating. Every dish was outstanding and the duck worth every dollar. The drinks are excellent and the service perfect

My friend and I had made a reservation here before it had been named one of the top 50 restaurants, so we were excited to try it. 

It's actually bigger than I thought it would be. When you come in there are a few small lounge tables and a big communal table. There's a long bar, and then you go back to the rest of the restaurant.  It was pretty packed on a Tuesday night at 7pm, which I don't know is normal or not, but I'd probably recommend making a reservation.  We browsed the drink menu and I settled on the Paloma, my current drink of choice, and my friend got the striptease. While looking at the food menu we asked the waitress how it worked, and she explained that it was meant to be like tapas style where everything was shared.  We put in an order for guacamole and said to come back for the rest of our order.  The waitress had suggested 4-6 dishes for 2 people, which actually wound up being too much food. We had wanted to get dessert, but we were way too stuffed!  A good excuse to come back. 

The guacamole came and it was really good. Not too much other stuff in it, but it definitely didn't lack flavor. Next up were the scallops. They were cooked perfectly! A little crispy on top and soft on the inside. Also the avocado aioli was great, and better than I imagined. Then came the Tlayuda, which was like a big thin crust pizza with black beans, chorizo, avocado, stracciatella, and salsa borracha. It was really good, but also really big for two people with more food on the way. My favorite part was the cheese! And the chorizo. We left over a couple slices cause we were waiting for our other dishes to come, and they kept trying to take it and make more room for our other dishes, but we held strong and kept it. The enmoladas and lengua came together. Our last dishes. At this point we were pretty stuffed, but we wanted to try everything.  The enmoladas were pretty much a combo of mole sauce, tortillas and cheese. Nothing wrong with that! The lengua aka tongue was huge. It also came with tortillas to make tacos, but we were really stuffed and didn't do it. We each tried some, and it was really good, but we left over a bunch. We wound up getting the tongue and Tlayuda wrapped, since both were great and we didn't want to go to waste.  

Overall all the food was great. The service was mostly great except for when they kept wanting to clear our plates, and then when we wanted to get stuff wrapped it seemed like no one was around. Always works like that lol. We definitely ordered way too much food, but I enjoyed it all. I would definitely come back for some drinks and the dessert I had wanted.

Deserves to be at 40. Just an overall unique food experience. We had a variety of dishes and loved them all. It's a complete hybrid of NYC/Mexico that we happen to appreciate. From the dark decor to the modern Mexican. If you're looking for traditional dishes, or a quiet setting, this place isn't for you. This is an upbeat, and non traditional food experience. We ordered 6 dishes, and 2 desserts, a little too much.
I do know I'll never forget the mole sauce and the corn meringue.
Thanks Enrique!
Also people complained about the food. We didn't find that a problem. Service was superb!

How this place only has 3.5 stars boggles my mind. This should easily be a 4.5, if not a 5. The restaurant is very trendy with casual background music accentuating the minimalist decorations. But, we're here to talk about food.

The Duck Carnitas (to share) are one of my favorite dishes in the city. Beware: they come with cilantro. It's an enormous duck breast with crispy, delicious skin. It's extremely well-marinated (I'm told for 4 days in Coca-Cola).

The Husk Meringue for dessert is an absolute must. Admittedly, my boyfriend thought that all meringues were citrus-y because lemon meringue is the most common type. I guess I can let that slide...maybe. Save a few bread puddings at my favorite restaurants, this is one of the best desserts I've ever had.

The guac was well-prepared and came with an endless basket of chips.

I'd also highly recommend the Sliced Raw Fish, Lobster, Brussles Sprouts, and Short Rib.

Our waitress made the slightest mistake at the beginning of the meal and couldn't have been more apologetic. I don't know if it was a third strike situation, but she seemed absolutely terrified of her manager and it couldn't have been less of a big deal. I honestly felt bad and left her an extra-nice tip. I know, I know, the tips are pooled. Whatever, just let me be.

Me and my dude Danny B went here bc we heard they got a Michigan Star nd that's like getting a gold at the XGames for Motocross, so I don't even feel lik I need to review this resto bc those cats in Michigan know wassup. But I'm doing dis bc they only have lik three and half stars on Yelp and that's wack.

Nyway if you known me you know that i dont eat ethnic food but this place has "poisoned oysters' and I had to try that bc that is metal! \m/ If you don't now that symbol that is metal hands \m/ rawk! I never have an oyster before and it was pretty bawse.

My dude Danny B got Duck in Red Mole bc he loves Turducken and wanted to try a Mole stuffed wif a Duck. It looked like the Mole exploded when the duck went in tho bc the plate had red but not Mole. But my dude Danny B said it was "Mexicellent" which was funny because this was a Mexican resto. \m/

Was referred by a friend to try this place out and was not disappointed. The food was DELICIOUS and the staff very knowledgeable and nice. Great mezcal selection. The bar was pretty too, the tlayuda is a must try.
The pretentiousness of it all made the lackluster meal even harder to digest. Big disappointment ...

After trying many times to get a reservation, we managed, on short notice, to get a seating at 5:30 PM on a Saturday night. A bit too early, but ok.
The restaurant is very stylish, there is ample space between the larger tables, but why there is so much space between two people at a small table I do not know...The music is a bit odd for a Mexican restaurant and the staff is friendly, except for the main waiter who seemed to think we should be lucky to be there. 
The food was amazing and so beautifully presented. It is pricey and the portions are small.
It is a good idea to share dishes. We loved the sliced raw fish with avocado, bergamo and poblano. It was tender and full of flavor. The branzino was delicious and made with a creamy avocado sauce. The broccoli tamal was a little more bland. A Mexican sauvignon blanc was very nice. Our favorite was the flourless chocolate cake with peanuts. Definitely our favorite NYC Mexican restaurant!

Food - flavorful and good presentation but definitely wasn't worth the price tag. The duck highlighted the day, otherwise I'll have to come again to try other items from the menu.

Service - nothing spectacular. Standard like most other restaurants and diners. 

Ambiance - the interior had a chic and modern twist to it. Music started to get a bit too loud around 330pm almost reminiscent of eating inside of Verboten. Bathrooms had a cool look to it. 

Cocktails - order the palmero  (had 2) and set the mood right. Very well balanced cocktail. 

I'll come again, but after I make my rounds with other new upcoming Mexican restaurants first.
