This place has nasty and disgusting customer service I called exactly at 5:30p.m. to tell them I am looking for parking and will be 15 minutes late. No one answered the phone. I literally walked in a minute past 5:45 exactly at 5:46 the hostess tells me how they do not accept walk-ins past 15 minutes. I told her are you serious im a minute late. She said yes because the table window is until 7pm. Do not even bother to spend your money here. There were plenty of open tables in the back and if I were seated and ate past 7pm what would you have done lifted my table up and thrown me out the door.

Ultimately safe food that doesn't do anything to challenge anyone in any way because chefs in NY can't afford to take risks.  Can find equally satisfying food to be bored by at a much lower price point all across the city.  At this price point though, the food should actually do something...and it doesn't.
Great experience from start to finish. Very flavorful dishes. Excellent service. Excited to try Atla!

Enrique Olvera is a genius and I will gladly eat anything he puts in my mouth. This is, in my opinion, the best Mexican restaurant in the city and one of my favorite restaurants. Granted, eating here will cost you but, for the amazing cooking and creative flavors you're unlikely to get anywhere else, I say it's worth it.

Some of my personal favorites on the menu are:

Uni tostada - I love sea urchin and the urchin here has an incredibly fresh taste with that soft melt-in-your-mouth texture that would make any uni lover swoon. The fact that it comes on top of a tostada adds some interesting textures to the dish but the highlight is the uni itself.

Cobia al pastor - the first thing that hits you is the freshness of the fish, but the truly amazing part about this dish is how well the flavor of the fish balances with the pineapple puree (which is in itself a perfect balance of sweetness and acidity).

Corn husk meringue - to me, being able to eat this dessert alone makes a trip to Cosme worth every penny. It is one of the two best desserts I've had in the city (the other being the popcorn mousse at Contra). The flavors are creative and so unforgettable it haunts my daydreams.

There are still many dishes I have not tried on the menu and look forward to coming back many times in the future.

Place it's great both times I went food was great can't go wrong with the duck carnitas, tlayuda and enmolada. The antihistamine drink it's delicious deff try to stop by once a month food is reasonable price an excellent experience

Mexican. Uni. Bone marrow. That's how my date at Cosme began. Well, almost, I actually started with a Carajillo (Mexican liquor combined with espresso). Nailed it, esp for brunch. I did't eat much because I had already eaten but on a friends reco, I couldn't leave NY without stopping by. The uni tostada was great. I will def be back for a full brunch next time.

I want to give a 4 star for this restaurant, because Cosme is a beautiful, modern, upscale latin/Mexican restaurant with very tasty/well executed dishes. 

But I am giving a 3 star due to under delivered service and the lack of value for price. 

Service - Wait staff and hostess were bit casual and nonchalant (as if like we were dinning at random restaurant in the hell's kitchen corridor). Our bill came to $360 (with tips) for 5 drinks, two appetizers, ribs for entree and the duck to share for two. For that price, I expect more polished and professional service level. 

Food - everything was delicious, but the price tag was a bit too much for what you get. The duck for two was $90, almost a steakhouse porterhouse for two price; you get a lot of food, and the food is great, but the executive and presentation does not live up to a $90 dish. Both the short ribs and ducks were served in fajita style with corn tortilla on the side. 

I think part of the under delivery and over price problem is due to the perception that latin/Mexican food served in fajita style is associated casual latin restaurant; so the price point at Cosme is a bit hard to take in. The restaurant can use some tweaks in terms of service delivery and pricing to better position itself.

Extremely overpriced for no reason - other than you are paying for an opportunity to see a celebrity here or there in the dark dining room.

To each their own of course, but this is not the place to enjoy food and drinks. It is one of those dark, seductive labs for which a girl drops $300 at a salon beforehand and a guy takes one of his top sports coats from his walk-in closet and pairs it with elegant Italian hand made shoes. Don't forget to add red lipstick, low back cut dress and a Patek Philippe. If you are after this wow factor, it is your lucky day - most likely you can get a reservation the same day. 

Foodwise? Well, it is Mexican food. You can be as creative as the devil itself, but Mexican is a very down to earth food. As neat and thin you can make your tortillas, as buttery and tender your lobster and as foamy your condiments - a tiny village in Yucatan can still beat you at that with their eyes closed. Food was good, but I would not order seconds of any dish we had. Also, the price for everything is staggering, even if it is just two micro bites of something - which I am usually fine paying elsewhere, but lengua tacos at $28 is just hard for me to swallow. Add to that $17 cocktails that they serve - with a twist of sophistication I guess? - in a half-empty glass - and a dinner for four quickly turns into a $400 check. 

Perhaps you can go quickly downstairs to lather your hands with Aesop goodness and inhale aroma of hand poured top line candles to make up for the expensive night. Who knows - Daniel Radcliffe could be standing next to you.

Cosme is a fine upscale dining experience in the Gramercy/Flatiron neighborhood, a location with abundant choices in the category.  With a few tweaks this could be a truly exceptional dining location.  Giving it three stars for now.  Environment is amazing, buzzy/trendy, modern upscale - truly evocative of the neighborhood and dining at this moment.  The team did a tremendous job on the interior design of the space, though some two tops are spaced a bit close for comfort.  

In terms of food, our waiter recommended two each of a seafood course, vegetable course and main course, being told plates are on the small side.  In retrospect, I tend to disagree, as even the vegetable courses were quite filling.  We selected two vegetable courses (Broccoli Tamal and Enmoladas) as well as the Short Rib and Duck Carnitas (for two) entrees.  Knew we were at risk for ordering far more food than warranted on the entree side, but really wanted to try the Short Rib as well, it sounded too good to pass up.  Everything was delicious, executed well and full of flavor.  Ultimately, I would recommend ordering two vegetable course (or one veg and one seafood) as well as one main (or the Carnitas for two) as an appropriate amount of food.  The Short Rib on its own was a decent amount of food.  Brown Butter Tamal was a fine way to conclude the meal.

For drinks we sampled both cocktails and wines by the glass.  The Expat Martini was quite well done, as was the Paloma - at $17 these were priced in line with general NYC standards.  The 2012 Tinto de la Casa from Valle de Guadalupe, Mexico was a nice compliment to the meal, but seemed overpriced.  Not a fan of the Contadino from Sicily which was on the sweet side.  Overall, the wine list was a bit uninspiring - not particularly extensive and a bit of a hodgepodge.

Service was polite and friendly, though frankly not anywhere close to the amount of polish I would expect of a restaurant striving for this caliber and quality or price point.  I expect more professionalism and decorum for a location of this type from the hostess through dining room staff. 

Overall, with a few tweaks this could be an oustanding location.  It certainly has the right ingredients for success, but pricing and service need to be sharpened up.  Would agree with other reviewers that the pricing felt aggressive for what was delivered in terms of experience.

What a great place to visit for our first meal in NYC.  Beef short ribs along with the brussel sprout dish was excellent. Make sure to get a confirmation on your reservation otherwise you aren't in the list!  We were able to eat at the common table and enjoyed our evening!

Food was five stars and worth every penny.

Service was awful.  Truly awful.  No set waiter per table; just chaos with random servers bringing out dishes with no attention to timing.  One server took away a near full basket of corn tostadas I was still eating.  I asked for it back three times and never got it back.
We wanted a second drink and my husband had to spend ten minutes trying to flag down someone to order.  We were done with our food before those drinks came out.

$460 for four people; I have no objection to that price based on the food...but the service...?  You gotta be kidding me.  It's just plain rude to provide that bad of service to people who have waited a month for the reservation and are spending that much money.

There is too much sauce on everything. 
The duck rolls were fine but they were completely immersed in sauce. It would have been so much better with more tortilla. 
Same thing with the huevos ranchero.
The Uni Tostado that I was really excited about turned out completely frustrating. The icy cold chopped tomatoes, avocado and uni did not go together with the hard tortilla shell.
Churros were mediocre - it's hard to say anything good about it really.

Came for the extensive mezcal selection. Very nice atmosphere, but the truly astounding prices are a deal breaker for me. If dropping $100+ on one or two mezcals and a bowl of guacamole and chips for two is no problem for you... knock yourself out. I think you're much better off saving the money from a couple of dinners and flying to Mexico.

In a city flooded with Mexican restaurants, Cosme remains as the best in my book. For brunch, no one else could make huevos more savory. The Chilaquiles in red sauce is hands down the dish you want to choose for your first brunch experience. The dish showcases the chef's depth to his sauces and control in each plate. Mexican spices and sauces can often overpower or overshadow dishes and that's not the case at Cosme.

For dinner, each plate pops with deep, ruch sauces with well-balanced acids. Again, the chef showcasing his control in the kitchen. The standouts for us were the lobster and the duck carnitas (a constant on the ever-changing) menu. You may double guess the duck due to its steep price, but don't. It's worth every penny. The duck cooking process alone takes days with the chef soaking it in brine then condensed milk and shredding it and cooking it... only to cook it again a second time. Whatever the process may be, the dish is top notch and deserves a spot in heaven. Lastly, if you haven't read it a million times already: the husk meringue and corn mousse is a dessert that would make me drive into the city for again and again. Get it.

I had high expectations from Enrique Olivera, and i wasn't disappointed. We had the scallops, Whitefish, bone marrow salsa, then the short ribs, Branzino, and lobster. 3 desserts, everything was delicious and very different. I had an amazing time.

For what it is, Cosme is extremely overpriced.

We were a little late for our reservation and called to try to push our reservation back by 15 minutes. They let us know they would hold it for 15 minutes, but didn't offer to push the reservation back although we let them know we were in the cab making our way there soon. We got there 16 minutes late from our reservation and thought they'd still honor our reservation. They did not. Granted we were the ones that were late, but given that we called, and were only 1 minute late from the time they hold the reservation, it was surprising that they told us to seat in the bar area. They claimed they'd seat us in the main dining area once something opened up, but they never did for the entire dinner.

Regardless, we ordered the Paloma, and El Ninja for our drinks. The paloma is described as "cimarron reposado, house made grapefruit syrup, lime, soda, grapefruit salt" and is $17. All I could taste was just alcohol and no notes of grapefruit came through. Although this might seem like a plus to some people on some occasions, considering I am paying for a fancy cocktail at a fancy price, I wasn't exactly expecting to drink something that might as well be liquor. El Ninja was ok. It's also $17 and described as "union mezcal, beefeater gin, americano vermouth, shiso shrub, ginger, lime."

Uni tostada: "uni tostada, avocado, bone marrow salsa, cucumber" because I love uni. Unfortunately, the bone marrow salsa was so overwhelming the uni's unique salty sea taste, its creaminess, and subtle sweetness were all lost on this dish. The bone marrow was all I could taste. Which was interesting, but it made the salsa quite heavy, which was also an odd experience. It was quite an oily salsa as a result as well, and overpowered everything. All the ingredients simply did not go together. And at $21 and the tostada smaller than the size of my palm, I expected to experience something incredibly delicious.

Mackerel: "mackerel, blue corn aioli, little gem, castelrosso" as I love all of these ingredients. The dish comes out covered in the cheese. The cheese is a very pungent salty cheese. There were 2 pieces of mackerel and each piece was the size of maybe a thumb. The rest of the large plate was little gem. The mackerel flavor didn't come through at all on the dish which was incredibly surprising as mackerel is so strong. In fact, this entire dish was so salty, I couldn't taste anything. The mackerel itself was bland, and the skin that was not removed was extremely chewy like overcooked meat's tough muscle fibers. The little gem lettuce was so drenched in a sauce that it was limp. The blue corn aioli had no flavor of corn, just salt. This was $25.

Lobster: "lobster, shiso, ginger mojo, brown butter" and it's $29. Again, tiny pieces of lobster as you can see in the picture. The foam is the brown butter. Which actually surprisingly didn't add much flavor to the dish. I was surprised to find after the previous salt plate that this was bland. The lobster pieces were very small once again, and all I could taste was ginger in this one. shiso was inserted into the dish not a part of the ginger mojo and did not blend with the flavors well. I couldn't taste lobster in this with all the parts together which I didn't enjoy. I think overall the savory dishes just weren't executed in a way that the flavors of the different ingredients went together.

Meringue: "husk meringue, corn mousse" $16. This was the best item we gotThe meringue was very crisp on the outside, soft on the inside. The corn mousse was also quite creamy and sweet. The two together was very good. The waiter described the moussed as whipped cream when he brought it out, and it basically tasted like whipped cream. I wished I could taste more corn flavor in the mousse. Also although the pictures look as though it's a big meringue, it's about the size of your fist.

Overall, none of the dishes I could justify paying for at their price point and I would not go back to Cosme.
Way overrated. Tiny dishes. They are tasty, for sure, but nothing spectacular. My enfrijoladas came with a piece of foil. The husk merengue is quite good.

Disappointed .  Did not enjoy the margarita . It had a weird aftertaste . The food was strange. My entree was mole ( although excellent ) with a side of Brussels sprout and tortillas. How is that a meal ?  Their signature dessert the merengue was just ok . We had the tostadas as our appetizer and it was unique and good . I considered myself a foodie until I came here . Guess I just like REAL food . Price never an issue for me as long as I go home remembering having the best meal ever . This place does not qualify as memorable.
Outstanding place! I like Mexican food, but this is a really upscale culinary experience. We shared many dishes and everything was excellent. A must go!
Amazing cocktails, mezcal selection, and service. By far one of my favorite spots in Manhattan. Two words: Duck Carnitas . Their service is consistent and genuine. Bravo Enrique Olvera

I have visited this establishment probably more times than any other place in NYC. And I only have good memories from every visit. With friends, family, date night.

All five stars: service, food, ambiance, people. The guys at the bar are the best. This review may be biased because I really like the staff here.

Drinks:
- El Ninja: comes with a dried pineapple, my favorite drink in all NYC, get it!!
- Striptease: not too sweet, just hits the right spot
- Carajillo: more of a dessert or afternoon drink. Licor 43 (sweet liqueur), espresso, ice. Get it!

Food - recommend at least three plates to share between two:
- Guac: guac is guac, you can't have a bad one, but the consistency and the chips make this one a great one!
- Cobia al pastor: personal favorite appetizer. Fish with an awesome pineapple sauce. Get it!
- Arctic Char: also on top of a tostada, looks like raw salmon, but it's something like you've never had before!
- Uni tostada: it comes on top of a crispy tostada (like a big nacho), I liked it, boyfriend didn't
- Scallops: loved the avocado aioli and white vegetable on top. Scallops were three small pieces, still good.
- Lobster: love this one! The presentation and taste are impressive
- Aycote bean salad: to be honest, just get another dish, the tlayuda has same amount of greens. The bean pure is delicious, but that's it.
- Tlayuda: OMG, this "Mexican pizza" is great. Crispy base, cheese and lots of greens. Get it!
- Branzino: soft and very well-seasoned fish steak. Get it!
- Lengua: I don't eat much meat, so didn't like it. Boyfriend loved it, though. So if you like meat, you will love this. Comes with tortillas to make your own tacos.
- Duck Carnitas: Delicious and abundant. Comes with tortillas to make your own tacos. Two or three people can share this.
- Husk meringue: there is a rumor this is the most Instagramed dessert. Still you need to try this, no pic will ever make justice. Get it!
- Warm apple crumb tart: loved the mescal vanilla ice cream. Still, get the Husk meringue!

In short, perfect dinner for two: Cobia, Lobster or Tlayuda (depending how hungry you are), Duck Carnitas or Branzino (again depending on hungry or fish/red meat pref) and Husk Meringue.

Brunch food:
- Stuffed avocado: seafood in an avocado. My favorite in the brunch menu. Get it!
- Quesadilla: had the mushroom one, very good to get with something else.
- Chilaquiles: boyfriend's favorite
- Lamb barbacoa: tasty (even for a non-red meat eater!) and abundant. Comes with tortillas to make your own tacos. Two or three people can share this.

I would recommend watching Netflix documentary on chef Enrique Olvera. It helps get a sense where he came from, how he thinks about his plates. And also makes a good point on how we are biased to think that Mexican food should be cheap, but not the same for other cuisines (like French or Italian). The food here is all top noch quality, fresh and you can see that a lot of effort and time was put in making each plate look like a piece of art. As other reviews said it, very well worth the visit.

Fanciest Mexican restaurant I have visited! Restaurant has a beautiful interior design, but it was pretty dark and felt very intimate. 

Highlights on the food/the most important part of the review: 
Duck carnitas - Huge duck breast with a crispy and amazingly flavored skin! I tried to get a piece of skin with every little taco I made. The tortillas were fresh, warm, and so soft that came out in a little basket with cloth covering it. 

Cobia al pastor - The cobia was so well cooked! The texture was like meat and if you didn't tell me it was fish, I would have totally guessed otherwise. Beautifully balanced with the pineapple puree and a great interpretation of al pastor. 

Husk meringue - There must be a reason why this is every other photo on Yelp. Light corn flavor in different textures!

Uni tostada - I really really wanted to love this, but this was my least favorite. Uni was fresh but I'm not sure I was into the bone marrow salsa (I love bone marrow btw!) and avocado. 

If there was anything that is under-highlighted at Cosme, its the tortillas. So good we had to get extra.

Ok food, overpriced and small/tiny portions. Great drinks and atmosphere.
I've had better Mexican...and cheaper...
They literally NEVER answer their phone, even if you transfer to extension 12 line. This is absolutely ridiculous. I've called six times throughout the day.

It's very expensive for what it is. The margarita is decent, worth $17? Nope. We had the guacamole, it was good besides the fact that they tried to give it to the table next to us. With these prices the service should be impeccable, it's decent at best. The complimentary salsa thing they give you is disgusting, tasted like cat food. The uni tostada was ok, very small. The mackerel you get very little fish and it's served with charred romaine that was slimey. The lobster again was ok, I don't want to ever eat it again. Then we were given dessert menus, I had to remind my server we never got the Branzino, which was also, ok. The table next to us gave us some duck tacos, they were tasty, not worth $89 for a half duck! Ridiculous. La Chine doesn't even charge that and it's the best duck in town.

Went in with my party and sat a few feet away from the bar. Wonderful decor and lighting. Dim lights and low key table settings were very casual for a night out in town.
      Absolutely love the space! Its spacious and the setting its a fusion of sleek, mod, romantic and shic. We started with cocktails, the Ninga and the traditional Margarita. Boy those were amazing! Yes cocktails are at 17 dollars but id pay for them as they are flavorful fresh and new. 
     We shared a Tlayuda with stratiacella cheese that came with a salsa borracha, it was a knockout. Crispy, cheese, enough greens and refreshing. Definitley recommend it for sharing. Carne cruda came with a smoky sauce, had the meat been more grounded i wouldve enjoyed it more but it was tasty.
     And then the holy duck carnitas arrived and almost gave us a food coma. Very sweet, savory, light and fresh feeling when that meat hots your mouth. $90 again I cant fight with the prices as the result was enjoyable. Carnitas came with tortillas which were fresh, we got blue and yellow corn ones. 
    Dessert hit the table and you bet, it was the corn husk meringue! It was outstanding,  delicious, light and a wonderful presentation. Slightly sweet and creamy, airy to say the least. It was so much fun cracking the egg shape dessert and would definitely get that again!
     Service was prompt, and steady. Although being greeted by the hostesses would be nice, the food makes up for the service. Our servers were attentive and very down to earth. Music was on the hip hop edge, other times is mexican themes which are more of a highlight for a fun dinner. 
      Definitely worth the visit. Be ready to spend a few extra bucks, we left full so it all depends on how many courses you want on your dinner. Would definitely come again.

Great Mexican is limited in NYC and the unfortunate thing about Cosme is you have to go to a high end restaurant for stellar Mexican food but it really is worth it. Inventive dishes that feature the fresh ingredients and stay close to traditional recipes. 

Great service, excellent food. Mushroom quesadilla, chilaquiles and merengue were the highlights. Oh! And the michelada

Such a great place to spend a Friday night after a busy week. Went there with my friend who loves this place so much. So do i. Everything was 100% well done: food, service, atmosphere. We tried Cobia al pastor, Scallops and couple more dishes(hard to recognize all the names). Such an interesting way of creating Mexican dishes in a fusion way. My best wishes to the chef. And yes, the dessert was also great. Husk merengue with corn mousse.

I'll start by saying the food and cocktails were overall really excellent. I was thrilled to have wine from Valle de Guadalupe again, too. I had previously eaten at Olvera's Pujol (wonderful) and Manta (not as wonderful). Cosme was up there with Pujol food-wise.

But like other reviewers said, the upselling by waiters really takes away from the service experience. First, if you're getting the duck carnitas for two people, you do not need to get four other small plates, as the waiters all recommend as soon as you sit down. We decided to get two small plates (cobia al pastor, ayocote) plus carnitas, but the waiter really pushed us to get a third or fourth thing, saying we would be very hungry. So we said sure, let's throw in some guacamole and you would have thought I asked the waiter for Old El Paso tacos. He said, "I'm going to be honest with you. You are at Cosme. You do not get guacamole at Cosme. You can go to Rosa for that. We put guacamole at the bottom of the menu for a reason." Okay, I get this. But it was my birthday and guacamole sounded yummy. Why would you offer something on the menu and then tell people they shouldn't order it? Just don't offer it. We took his recommended for the sliced raw fish, which was good.

In the end, we regretted getting three dishes (the ayocote was the only thing that disappointed, everything else was fantastic). We left feeling overly full. Also, it took us three tries to get extra tortillas for our carnitas, and then we were charged $4 for them. I'll happily pay $4 for more homemade tortillas, but not when I have to sit there for 15 minutes and keep asking waiters and bussers for them while my carnitas get cold. No regrets about eating at Cosme, but I don't think this will enter the regular rotation.

UNI tostada good
Warm citrus
Two types of Uni.  There was a good interplay of warm/cold/crunchy/creamy.

That was the only thing. 

Service was BAD.  Our waiter was a mexican from Mexico, but forgot the drink order (didn't place it) and forgot that I asked for other items as well.  When I asked about them the second time he made excuses as to why they didn't come out.

And the mexican food was BAD.  You know why?  
It was for Americans.  I asked for any salsas or hot sauces, they said it's not really that hot, because it's for Americans.  

Enrique talks about making real mexican food in the chef's table documentary, but sadly this was not.  The shit was whack - lacked depth of flavor and lacked soul.  The real reason Mexican food is so good is because of the latter.
Decent guacamole but I found most other dishes and the cocktails expensive and unsatisfactory. Unlikely to be back again.

Very cool restaurant. Bar area is great which works because you will have to wait even with reservations. Drinks are very well made, get a mezcal based drink, it's definitely their strong point here. The decor, while simple really is interesting when you're there in person. The food is very creative and the menu is organized by the size of the plates. Cobia al pastor and buratta were my favorites.

You're living in Manhattan and you've haven't been to Cosme yet? Shame! Shame! Shame! 

But seriously get on it. Sure it's expensive, but it's the only Michelin Star rated Mexican restaurant in a city known for its incredible food. After getting nice and sauced up at the Nomad Elephant Bar, we moseyed on over to Cosme for my girlfriends birthday. Fortunately, she also works in the industry so we received a friendly personal greeting from the start, with the occasional sampling dish for her big day. 

The guacamole was like the smoothest Mexican butter my lips have ever tasted - and no more expensive than any other overpriced place downtown. 

We started with the Cobia al Pastor, which comes with tortillas and this phenomenal pineapple puree that will leave you begging for more. I almost cried, but luckily they brought out the Sliced Raw Fish so I wouldn't soil the table with my tears. Imagine if ceviche and sushi had a baby - that's what you'd get. 

After a few more mezcal cocktails and some people watching (our favorite being the silver fox and his wife to our right enjoying a 13-year-old bottle of red on a Thursday night, bless them) - we continued onto our main course. 

I had the pleasure of enjoying the Bronzino, which was cooked to perfection in some unspeakable marinade. I say unspeakable because someone will probably kill me if I tell you. 

We were also treated to the Seared Brussels Sprouts with Mole, which my girlfriend said was delicious, albeit a little too limey, but great all the same. I couldn't partake due to an allergy to pine nuts (I do still love pine trees).

The meal was topped off with an adorable and aggressively delicious piece of Tres Leches with a candle on top served with two glasses of Carajillo. Let me just say something about Carajillo real quick - it's as if the most beautiful Mexican woman was pouring espresso with a light dusting of vanilla liqueur down into your mouth from her bosom. What I'm saying is that it's intoxicating and delicious. Yes, the Tres Leches was also phenomenal, I'm glad you asked.

All said and done around two bills on payday, but it was absolutely worth it. You'll spend half the meal with your eyes closed just savoring bites and talking about the intense flavors. You're paying for the experience and the quality - so go enjoy yourself.

Hands down best dining experience of the year! Each dish was so flavorful and fresh tasting. Highly recommend the duck carnitas and corn husk meringue. Cocktails were yummy too. Will be coming back!!!

I was looking forward to eating at Cosme. And I was wrong. It's a mess of an experience. Not quite a train wreck. But close. Read the review someone posted on 1/5/17....(god in heaven, I hope that's a peformance-art piece.).....Anyhow, you'll get a sense for what you're in for. 
There are a few bright spots. The three young women at the front of the house are very good. They deserve a better place to work. And there is some indication of skill from the kitchen. Some of the food shows promise. But not more than that. Promise. Not brilliance.
The bad? Everything else.
Shockingly incompetent service. Unfocused. Expediters who haven't a clue. 
Wine list - atrocious...and I do mean absolutely horrible. Three different bad wines. (More later)
Cold food where it shouldn't be. Inappropriate plating. 
Uncomfortable, stupid seating. 
Total lack of supervision. (This shows up everywhere.) And a real lack of understanding.
Just me, I REALLY hate it when the owners' ego shows through as contempt for the customers' experience. It does at Cosme, in spades. 
Anyone who believes that this restaurant, or the cuisine, is truly representative of the 'renaissance in Mexican cuisine' is....well I'm going to try to be kind.... they are 'grossly mistaken'. 
After a kind and professional greeting, it's clear that the seating designed to look cool...your comfort / convenience / dining experience be damned. But you're at a trendy place, so suck it up.
A glass of wine? Ok. Well we get a little lecture about bio-dynamic wines. Fine. (I was in the wine business. Have French friends who are bio-dynamic producers. Whatever.) The first wine is actually bad. Not even close. Bad. Acetifying. Obvious. But the som will only say it's a little funky. The second wine (his choice) is still undergoing malolactic fermentation in the bottle. Not actually awful, just not good. Add some off-oily scents and barely present fruit, and this doesn't even pass for decent jug wine. Well ok, switch to white for a bit better luck maybe? There, it's a thin over-acid Gruner Veltliner. Three strikes. None of this stuff should be within 100 miles of a decent restaurant that had any self-respect, much less respect for their customers.
The food....here it's a complete hit-or-miss. Most plates are interesting, at some level. The cobia is pretty cool. Interesting. Not Michelin one-star, but well-executed. Then a mole, which turns out to be bowl of mole and two tortillas dumped in it. That's it. A big cold bowl. With now cold mole. Seriously the stupidest thing I've been served in a restaurant in a long time. Some extra tortillas.... to try to rescue a bit from this (because the mole was interesting)? Well.....that took 15 minutes while service people stood around, chatted each other up and, I think, posted crap on Facebook.
Just keep going like that. An interesting tidbit or bite, along with two complete misses. And nobody 'minding the store'. The longer I spent here the more infuriating it got.
Sorry. A lot of people at Cosme need to get set right. Hire somebody from Danny Meyer's empire or from Vongerichten's or Astrid & Gaston. Tell them to clean up the mess. And pay them well. They have a LOT of work to do.

2 people, 5 plates, 2 desserts, and a cocktail- $200

And so worth it!!

A recent trip to NYC at Christmas was all about the food and drink in Manhattan. My friend wanted to try this Latin inspired restaurant because it was a top 50 in the world.  I truly tasted why. Wow. 

They offer small plates so we chose 5, not listing them- check out the pictures. All were beautifully plated and made with fresh ingredients. Flavors that were so bright and wonderful they made my skin crawl. The yellow corn tortillas were indescribably delicious with their pop of corn flavor, hot of the grill and so soft. I think we ate three baskets of them.  We tried save room for dessert, there was one in particular we wanted to try - the burnt husk meringue. It was very interesting and good. We also tried the dessert tamale- the texture was a little coarse for me and it was the only dish that didn't excite me. 

Reservations are a must, and we were able to get one two days in advance. It's one of the larger restaurants we were in. Dimly lighted and tables rather close together. Staff very polite but extremely busy. 

I got home and felt like Mexican food, but not sure I'll ever find a meal that delicious again. Definitely a repeat.

Wine list: dumb. Service: slow. Food: flavorful but a total miss. e.g. Enmoladas mole was more like "soup" ... for which requested tortillas arrived after the dish congealed. Price: insulting. The servers friendly but not tuned in. Front of the house team gracious. Sadly, a fail.

TLDR: food is really good, service is snotty and patchy for the price. 4 stars for the food, 2 stars for the service (specifically, the hostesses and the kitchen timing -- our waiter was lovely).

The Good:
The food here really IS phenomenal. We loved almost all the drinks and food that we ordered. I really recommend the top section of the menu, which is basically comprised of Mexican-style sashimi. Here's what we ordered, all of which I recommend (with some reservations):

- Uni tostada, avocado, bone marrow salsa, cucumber (good, but keep in mind that it's a giant cracker that costs $21)
- Arctic Char, elderberries, yuzu, avocado (ditto)
- Sliced raw fish, poblano, finger lime, avocado, black lime
- Cobia al pastor, pineapple puree, cilantro
- Mackerel, blue corn aioli, little gem, castelrosso (maybe my least favorite of what we ordered -- tasted like a fancier Caesar salad)
- Lobster, shiso, ginger mojo, brown butter
- Ayocote bean salad, market greens, charred cucumber vinaigrette
- Short rib, scallions, cipollini, avocado 

Our waiter was also very friendly and provided great service.

The Bad:
The two hostesses at the head of the restaurant were SO INCREDIBLY RUDE AND SNOTTY.  No smiles, no greetings, nothing! What a great welcome into the restaurant! They also seemed sort of disorganized? When I stated that I had a reservation, both of them looked surprised. When it turned out I was the first of my party to arrive, they literally did not say anything for a good 2 minutes. I had to ask: "So... should I wait at the bar then?" At which point, they deigned to nod without looking up from their guestbook. This was one of the worst experiences I've had walking into a restaurant, and really not acceptable for a restaurant of this caliber. Really shameful.

My party could only get at 6PM reservation, which, yes, is on the early side. You could TELL the restaurant wanted us out of there as fast as possible to turn our table over. There was absolutely no pacing of the dishes -- everything came out at once, and two members of my party had to actually CHUG their cocktails in order to be able to order a second round of drinks. I'm not even joking. There was about a 2 minute wait between appetizers and mains, and had we not gotten dessert, we probably would have been out of there in 20 minutes. Waiters hovered around our table, and the moment a plate was cleared of food, it was swept away. Not usually a bad thing, but it really felt like we were being pressured to get the F out of there this time around.  

I wish I could rate this place higher because the food was really good, but some parts of the service and experience were just unacceptable given the prices!

I LOVE COMING TO THIS RESTAURANT. LOVE!!!!!

Not because the food is amazing ( It certainly is!)

Or because the ambiance is on point ( It is ! and I am a douche who makes a point to dine at word's finest restaurants)

But because just like the most exclusive Russian billionaire clubs in Moscow it's a tet-a-tet sort of place where you go to see and be seen, not actually eat food, silly. And prepare to feast your eyes on this crowd !

You like people watching ? Watching other's awkward first dates brings you great entertainment and joy ? You love watching escorts on dates with men 40 years their senior ? You love New Yorkers and hearing their conversations because let's face it we are special people ? 

Then you will LOVE this place. So trendy and so sophisticated, so New York-ey and yet so dysfunctional at the time. I think this might be actually the best restaurant in the city. 

Last time I was sitting at the bar and saw Daniel Radcliffe walk in and stand a foot away from me.

 My husband asked who he was and as I was replying that this was the Harry Potter guy - I was immediately corrected mid-sentence by a friendly neighbor couple that he was more than just Harry Potter. Before I even had a chance to speak, my neighbors deliberated what a hard life must be for Daniel Radcliffe walking around encountering ignoramuses like me who know nothing about his theater work, only his kid movies. Theater, that's where it's at, not TV. 

And so I walked away from this meal not only with food in my stomach, alcohol in my loins and spring in my step but with an educational lecture by fellow sophistiant New Yorkers on Daniel Radcliffe's ambitions and dreams. 

And so, how can you not come back to this place ? 

Re: Food. It's good, like gooooooooooood good. Portions size is a human size, not Vegas buffet, meaning this might be one of the few Mexican restaurants where you'll walk away not feeling stuffed and not guilty about the meal you just had.

Yummmmmm!! The corn custard dessert was creamy in the inside and sweet and hard mernigue on the outside. Order that! The duck mole was delicious and rich in flavor and my favorite meal dish. The lamb was very good too.

Just finished having NYE dinner at Cosme with my boyfriend. While the food was fine albeit small portions, the service was absolutely horrible. After spending $200, the waitress scoffed at my boyfriend when he modified his beer order from a Dos Equis to a relatively cheaper ($8) beer. From then on, she treated us with disdain and disrespect. She talked about us within earshot and even left the Dos Equis on the check, forcing us to uncomfortably ask them to remove it. When you're spending this much on food, you would expect the service to be on par. I wouldn't recommend this to anyone else.

We feel bad as we like a lot of folks are going to walk in with a bias to want certain things in their Mexican food and there is no way a place like this that is trying to do something different is going to win.

Most of the dishes flew straight over our collective heads and we feel kinda stooopid admitting that the most straightforward and strongly flavored dish - the enmoladas - was the most memorable...probably because it was the most familiar and if you cut us open we will bleed mole negro.

The rest of the uni tostada, the mole verde, and the tamal for dessert were not items we would think about coming back to have.

We probably could have and should have sampled more dishes but by the time we were done with the enmoladas, we were struggling to cross the finish line and were over it already.  Looking thru the pictures, we probably should have tried the husk meringue instead of the tamal for dessert...

I love when chefs go funky on traditional cuisine, and this is definitely the funky take on Mexican. The duck entree was melt-in-your mouth perfection. Can never go wrong by starting with Uni tostada, Cobia al pastor and scallops - each is a delightful, and different, mix of tastes and textures. If you still have room: seared brussel sprouts and short ribs are also uniquely tasty. This is fun for the palate! It is not often that I come across a high end restaurant that I revisit any chance I get.
I agree with the reviews that say bland and boring. There's a reason they take reservations for brunch, and were still half empty on Sunday at noon.

Nuevo Mexican. That's the best way to describe what they're going for at Cosme. That's mostly a good thing, less their principled stance on not having guacamole (yeah, seriously).

Go here for some expertly crafted margaritas. The bartenders know what they're doing. We asked for two levels of a spicy margarita (off-menu) and they easily accommodated and nailed them both. The perfect citrus balance with the Cimmaron tequila was complemented by the custom square ice cubes and the glassware that is not filled to the top, by design. There's nothing worse than getting sticky hands from your margarita, right?!

For a snack we opted for the short rib taco. It's build your own but with the homemade soft tortillas it's so worth the minimal effort. The short rib was tender and full of flavor. We ran out of tortillas and they gladly brought us a new set (blue the 2nd time). 

Because we were craving guacamole we had to finish on that snack but will definitely return for more margaritas and to complete a meal.

Super popular place with a different approach to the Mexican cuisine: you'll hate it or love it. Brunch is just ok, dinner is a more recommended experience. Reservation is a must. Save room for the churros with chocolate.. sooo good!

Food- 4.5
Atmosphere - 3.

The food was great, expensive...but the portion size was pretty decent, easy to share. The sauces were pretty great.

The atmosphere- not in love with it. "Trendy" but certainly not timeless. i.e. electronica/clubby with spotlights on each table. Yet, it wasn't crazy loud and there was a good amount of space between the tables so conversation was fine once you get used to the music.

The biggest negative was the service. The hosts were nice, but our server was arrogant and trying to get information about the dishes seemed unwelcome. Oddly aloof.

Price - $100/head (2 drinks a piece).

Overall...I wouldn't recommend it to friends necessarily...but if someone told me they were going, I'd be interested on their thoughts on it.

Fantastic duck and excellent bar fully stocked and a lot of variety of drinks.
The service was excellent also. I went with my husband and a friend and we had a wonderful time. Would highly recommend the margaritas, scallops and duck carnitas. The flavors were delicious.

The server asked if we'd ever come here before. After saying it was our first time, he suggested we order 4 items on the menu as well as the duck carnitas that are for two and cost $79. We only ordered 3 menu items with the duck, but it was way too much food! My date feels he was trying to rack our bill up for a higher tip. Best dish of the night was the mole verde with Brussels sprouts, which incorporated Brussels sprouts in 3 different forms. Cobia al pastor was also well executed. The uni tostada was okay but all the other ingredients on the tostada overpowered the uni. Overall our experience was ehh... duck was dry and we couldn't even finish it. If you want a really amazing duck dish, go to Chinatown for pecking duck.
Overpriced menu trying way too hard to offer Mexican haute cuisine. Ambiance and service are great, the food was not super special.

At first, I thought the menu was a little odd, but as the items were rolled out, and I tried new flavors put together, I really loved the food. The one that was like a Mexican pizza was to die for. The duck carnitas were also amazing, though I was so stuffed by that time, that I didn't have too much of it. Cocktails were yummy also- had one sorta like an old-fashioned. Fun restaurant, great service, and loved how fresh the food was. Downstairs in the bathroom area, don't try to open the door with the girl painted on it. That's not the ladies room, it's a broom closet. Whoops.

It's hard to get a reservation, but it's worth it.  I'd say the decor was early 90s LA, which isn't exactly my jam, and the service can be hit or miss, but the food and drinks are so delightful, that they more than make up for it.  Favorite app: cobia pastor.  Favorite main (to share): Duck carnitas.  Favorite dessert (on this planet):  Blue corn husk meringue with corn mousse.  Cocktails are all bright, fruit, and herb forward.  I like the el ninja in particular.  Margaritas are also amazing.

Not sure what the hype is all about. Went here for brunch. The bloody Maria was too tart and not very good.  Neither one of us finished our drinks, which was an indicator that we didn't like them. Wife has The huevos rancheros (decent) and the I had the chiliqueles  shared The cactus salad. 

Service was not commensurate with the high prices. Took 15 minutes for the server to come start our order. The water boy was on his game though. I hardly ate my food because it was not good, but no one ever came by to check on how we enjoyed our meal.  We were handed the check and that was it.  I won't return here and can't recommend it to anyone.

Loved lunch at Cosme!  Light and fresh looking spot and the food is beautiful and delicious.  Suggestions include the Uni Tostada with avocado on blue corn tortilla. Egg Sope was soft egg on top of a tostone and also just great. The Fried Oyster Torta was filling and good to share. Also LOVED the Duck Enmoladas in Red Mole.  Ask for extra tortillas as that mole sauce should not go to waste.  Mop it up! And save room for the Husk Meringue dessert. Sweet corn but not too sweet and perfect end to delicious meal.

I know that I may sound like a real plebeian  but this joint is just so overrated and overpriced . Looked at the menu ahead of time and it looked reasonable.  Dishes priced in the the $30-$40 range  Was then told by the server that she recommend that we order 2 or 3 dishes per person!!  So now we're talking $60-$90 per person just for the entrees.  First the $20 Belevedere martinis come out.  The glasses were the size  of thimbles.  Then the dishes arrived, so tiny that they barely served one person.  Most of it tasted  ok but jeez, you're still hungry after you're finished.  The hyped meringue dessert was ok, nothing special.
So if you're willing to spend $200 a person to leave the restaurant hungry, go for it.  You've found your place

Mexican food taken to the highest level of excellence. The flavors created an explosion in my mouth that elevated my senses. One of my top restaurants I've ever been to ever. 

We ordered the burrata which tantalized my taste buds, octopus fish with scallops, the tostadas with tuna, another see food appetizer with white fish, avocado slices and finger limes- I didn't know these little guys existed, so yummy!! The fish al pastor. What can I say about this dish except next time I visit I'll have 3 orders!!! My favorite by far. The tlayuda was bursting with flavor (next time I'll order it with more choriZo). Also, the enmolada was very rich. The duck carnitas were also really good, ordered extra tortillas. Lastly we finished with the raspado, next time I'll order one for myself, a corn mousse dessert, and the peach tart with ice cream. Everything was amazing.
Incredible food, small portions. Incredibly pricey - but worth it. Make sure to get the soft shell crab and do not leave without trying the corn husk meringue.

Holy hell expensive!
Food was good; but not memorable for the price. Service was disappointingly slow and unthoughtful. Our waiter even told us we only had our "table until 815pm, so we had to place additional food orders asap"..we arrived at 6pm (blank stare). $350 later for 7 tapas we left at 830pm..15 mins behind schedule according to our waiter.

COBIA AL PASTOR
TUNA TOSTADA
ENMOLADAS

I had the duck carnitas that the servers tend to suggest, but I have to say, there are way better things on the menu. Better to get two cobia al pastor instead of the duck. The decor is incredible, the wine list is DELISH. The cocktails (I had the Anti Histamine) are top notch. 

The only thing (and low hanging fruit for this establishment) is that the bathrooms are gross. One $60 Malin & Goetz Candle is not going to cover the smell of pee and the fact the toilets spit up water onto the walls when you flush. They just need a plumber! Thank goodness the bathrooms are downstairs!

Kind of a huge freaking wow. Great dining experience. A little swankier than I was expecting but the food delivered and the service was friendly and professional and not at all condescending.

There were enough flavor surprises to keep me impressed.The Paloma was a nice starter to help us though the Cobia Al Pastor (a tangy play on the taco subbing fish for pork)and the octopus and scallop cocktail (a "dark" interpretation of ceviche using a bean broth).  

The tlayuda used fresh stracciatella. The accompanying salsa added to the depth but overall the mechanics of the dish made it a little rough to eat.  Lots of greens on top of a chewy tortilla. The queso fresco on the enmolada made it easy to keep slurping the mole even when the tortillas were long gone. 

Our server Jai was great - personable and friendly and knowledgeable.  He suggested a great Spanish wine by the glass to accompany our second course.

And dessert - not much I can add to the already infamous corn husk meringue.  Just get it and love it and don't embarrass it with any more pictures. The huckleberry raspado was a nice compliment (cheesy and fruity refresher) and I was happy to finish this while the hubby made quick work of the corn.

Went here last night and I felt the need to review it. We ordered the entire menu except one entree. The overall experience was great, from the excellent service to the food. I will go back, but wont get everything next time. Keep up the good work!

Lunch over weekend...they called to reconfirm, overall good experience.

Mole is Awesome!!

Surprised us with birthday desserts. good ambience, service.

Hands down one of my favorite restaurants -- for the bar, table reservations, and group events. 

Cosme should hit the bullseye for anyone that loves: (1) mexican, (2) sushi/fresh fish and (3) interesting. Big, bold flavors that are most impressive in their uniqueness -- the rare place to actually try something new. Check out the menu, it speaks for itself. The creativity and quality extend to the drinks and the decor. Books up far in advance but front desk does a good job of accommodating. 

Potential good thing OR bad thing - high energy place that is noisy. No worries for 2 people, but 4 or more and acoustics can start to get iffy. My only knock, while the staff is very professional, knowledgeable and friendly, the busing and table waiting can sometimes get weird - in one meal can range from feeling laid back to rushed.

Dinner was great, but brunch was only okay.

For dinner, I really enjoyed the duck carnitas, but it was all the other appetizers and small plates that surprised me on the upside.  Particularly memorable -- uni and tuna tostada were great, sliced raw fish was light and refreshing, the charred avocado in the octopus-scallop cocktail was surprisingly good, enmoladas in mole sauce met expectations (and I have high expectations for anything in mole), NY strip tacos sounded ordinary but were not...the tortillas are not normally something I notice but these were so fresh and tasty on their own, and the spelt espultes dip looked questionable but was so delicious.

The corn husk meringue for dessert was unique, but meringue is not really my preferred type of dessert, so I personally didn't love it.

FOOD FANTASTIC / new age Mexican / however be aware of the bullies at the desk and their attitude on "first come first serve" at the bar seats.  I LIVE HERE AND WOULD COME BACK HERE CERTAINLY- But a MUST DO WHILE IN NYC - or entertaining guests.

Terrible service and mediocre food !! Nothing good to say.  Waiters had a attitude but u guys still just a waiters !! Drinks...... Boooooo nothing to say Rosa Mexicano is better all the way!!!! Not recommended!!! Mg ? I never saw one !! Lol

I am personally not a huge fan of Mexican food and never thought Mexican can actually be high end but I was taken back when I arrived at Cosme. The hosts were all very inviting and friendly. After being seated I browsed the menu and decided to go with 3 dishes, 1 of each size and save room for dessert as I am huge on sweets. My friend and I ordered the softshell crab, Scallop and Octopus salad, and the Duck Carnitas.


The softshell crab were fried perfectly and sat in a tart Asian sauce and slices of daikon that went pretty well with the sauce. My main takeaway was the Scallop and Octopus salad. I cannot get over how phenomenal it was. The salad tasted exactly how Summer should taste like - fresh, exciting, different, and refreshing. The scallop and octopus were cooked right, not chewy at all and easy to bite into. Sitting on a bed of zucchinis and squid ink sauce, the flavors balanced each other greatly. By far one the best salads I have ever encountered.


Now onto the Duck Carnitas. First off, the dish was huge and can definitely satisfy 2-3 people. This dish didn't really blow me away as the duck was a bit dry in certain areas but the spicy sauce that it came with really helped with that. My other main takeaway was definitely the Cornhusk Meringue. I never had too many meringues in my life but I heard about this infamous dessert so I just had to see what the hype was about. MY GOOOOODNESS. If you were to dine here, please just do yourself a favor and get this dessert. Probably one of the best $14 I have spent my entire life. The outer layer was a bit sweet, but the corn mousse that was inside was a bit salty and it balanced the shell perfectly. Very light, I did not feel guilty eating that dessert. Highly recommend this dessert and the salad. Not to mention Todd English's son (Oliver English) was dining there as well. Talk about eye candy all night!

I topped by one the places I always craved about and I had such a great tome with Jorsan and eddy so much fun with the staff, Juan the server was a great experience, I liked ve it so much that I'll be back soon

I've eaten so much mole while being completely confused as to why anyone would ever eat it, but then I had it here with the duck dish and wow, now I get it. This place isn't the quick simple usually US Mexican or Tex Mex kind of place, it's haute Mexican. The setting is also great and lively with very good service.

Pretty disappointed the first time around. We had watched this test on the CHEFS table, great show btw and the expectations on this restaurant were way too high. 
We had a reservation for 815pm. Arrived at 8pm, had some drinks at the bar which were amazing. At 815pm the hostess confirmed that we would have to wait another 10-15 min. We ended up waiting 20min, and not even an apology or any reason to be concerned about the delay on our reservation.
Second, when we ordered our food, the menu did not describe the section of appetizers vs entree. Neither did the waiter explain any of the menu at all. He was very general, vague, and did the least amount of his job. 
We ordered our food thinking it was an entree, and ended up being 2 appetizers instead. The portion for the appetizer was also very small than expected and a little bummed about the staleness of the tostada. Not fresh. 
The last order of our dinner took extremely long. Waited a good 30min in-between orders. Not good. Voiced the wait and the unclarity of the menu to the waiter, and he was very brash about it. He asked if we wanted to order more. Apparently, he did not get it or just didn't care. 
Anyway, definitely wasn't a great experience, and for the price, definitely never again, nor will I recommend it to anyone. Too long of wait, lazy waiters and not good service, too pricey for portion, and unclear menu. 
The atmosphere is also just a trend. A typical NYC style atmosphere, trendy and a wanna be fancy. Not necessary, for a restaurant that could focus more on food and service! 
Hope this helps! Thank you for your time.

I was struck by the beautiful lighting in this restaurant, and great staging and ambiance. Drinks were also very thoughtfully prepared and our waiter was just that small amount of sassy that keeps things fun. The duck carnitas were incredible and large enough to make probably 15 small tacos. Rich, flavorful, but not too fatty, very salty (it tasted good but probably wouldn't help out someone with high blood pressure). Possibly the best thing was the husk meringue desert which featured a meringue that was perfect - not too whipped not too creamy texture and also not oversweet. Amazing crunchy texture to contrast from the shell encasing. We had a few other of the raw appetizers, but I remember less about those. Guacomole was also great.

The food is so fresh and the dishes are so unique. The quevos rancheros and the chilaquilas (green w chicken) are out of this world. I am from Texas and have never favorably reviewed Mexican in NYC. Outstanding!

Noise level pretty high, but not so much that we couldn't have a conversation.  modern, clean ambiance. Friendly front of the room, but our waiter was somewhere between indifferent and bored.   If you like bars with stools and no backs, then fine, but I was glad we had a traditional table.  The service was fine and all the food was fresh, delicious, and unusual given that the food has a Mexican influence.  Everyone raves about the duck carnitas and it lived up to expectations.   Specialty cocktails were excellent.  A bit pricy, but not outrageous.  If our server had been good, we would given the restaurant 5 stars.

3.5 Stars

Came here for lunch. Excellent service. Pretty busy for lunch in this area. Food was good, but only the uni tostada and corn mousse dessert were delicious/extraordinary. 

Food:
Burrata - good 
Guacamole - good but not Dos Caminos good
Poison oysters - good but basically these are just regular oysters
Duck enmolada - good
Beef short rib - good 
Uni tostada - delicious
Corn husk mousse - delicious

We went there a week ago for lunch and were very disappointed with the service and food. We requested our server to check on a certain menu item for a child with allergies. He did not show up for 45 minutes the menu was very limited and the food was awful simple dish like huevos rancheros was badly executed we paid a large bill for very poor experience. We will never return there

I travelled to Mexico City to go to Enrique's first restaurant, an incredible experience, both the service and food was another level. So when Cosme opened I was really excited to try it. It's a more relaxed atmosphere and different style of eating but the food but just as good. 
The food is fresh, creative, modern Mexican but while keeping it's authenticity. The service was attentive but relaxed. 

It's higher price bracket but if you're looking for a treat then you'll love it.

Pretty expensive for a pretty average experience.  We walked in wthout reservations to an empty restaurant. Told there was not a table for Us- btw, we finished our meal  (at the bar) before anyone else showed up in the dining room I had the sopre, my husband had the huevos rancheros and we split the mushroom quesadilla. Worst quesadilla I have ever had - cheese not even melted. He had a Bloody Maria which was ok. I have a Paloma which was good. The sopre was yummy, but huevos rancheros were flavorless. Service was nice and restaurant was pretty.

This was a disappointing experience. 
Cosme is an upscale and HUGELY OVERPRICED  Mexican. 
There is no real course menu- promisingly upscale to begin with. The waiter was very insistent on us getting at least 4-5 dishes for two, although he had a very hard time explaining what any of the dishes really were. Even harder was for him to explain how the mysteriously wicked linguistics of the menu was translating from Spanish/Japanese/???-ese into regular English and folding into dishes, all of them of small size. If you are curious, please have a look at the Cosme website and read their dinner menu-WOW!!!  what a "linguow"!!!
So you don't really know what you gonna get (unless you try google translate first and then consult some foodie connoisseur on modern). You're waiting for a surprise- like you would expect from many innovative restaurants these days. A surprise being an intrinsic element of the experience. Then it comes. The Uni dish was indeed surprising.  Although, Uni being  the sea Urchin gonads is/are quite exotic as they are, so not sure if that originality could be attributed to highly innovative culinary skills, particularly that Uni is a raw "roe"; Short ribs were very good but not really that experimental and the raw fish was a nicely done sashimi- an original element for Mexican cuisine, yes; the Enmoladas- ricotta, hoja santa, queso fresco- still don't quite know what that was, but it was simply disappointing. 
Let's be fair: this place does have a transformative approach to Mexican food, and above all- a lot of "pretention".
It is obscenely overpriced for what it has to offer. There is a lot and lot better in NYC city if you're ready to spend close to a 100$ per person or much less (for 2 tapas-like dishes and a bear !) and you would expect the waiters to know their job so you are not left in "lost in translation". 
The $$ sign that you see next to Cosme on Google page is hugely misleading and should be corrected. This place is definitely kicking into $$$$ category price-wise (as shown on Yelp). 
I'd definitely much rather go to a different place if I were to get a $$$$ dinner experience!!

LOVED our dinner at Cosme.

The duck carnitas were to die for, the mole enchiladas were good... (I'm not a huge mole fan in general but my husband loved it), I really enjoyed the tuna tostada, and the husk meringue/corn mousse was AMAZING. 

Everyone who walks in the door must order the duck carnitas and husk meringue.

My only beef with the restaurant is the super high bar stools. I am a young, average-height, agile person, and I couldn't get off! And I watched as other people had the same problem. Such a bizarre choice in stool.

Next level food. Not sure if it gets better.
Service is nyc tough. But food is really special.

This was our anniversary meal so we were okay spending a bit more than usual and we did! That said, the food and wine were worth it. The raw fish, short ribs and Enmoladas were to die for. We also got be octopus which was good and interesting but just not my fav and the duck carnitas (same).  House wine is amazing (made just for them). My four stars is for the food. 
Service was a 2.5/3 of 5.
As others say here-the service was really disjointed and they try to force you into 3 orders/person which is WAY too much food! 
Order two dishes each and share a dessert and you'll be fine. (The duck is $69 for two but easily could've been a dish for 4 people when ordering this way). Go for the food, expect not great service--they were nice but when we switched to wine for our second course we had to flag down 3 people to get the menu and it barely came in time for our last bites of course 3. Also the decor is very modern and pretty dark so it's great for romance but not if you like to see the restaurant around you or catch your waiters eye!

Food was good, service was lacking.

1) don't upsell the number of dishes needed- either you're just trying to plus up the bill or you weren't trained appropriately. Either way it's annoying.
2) don't deliver a dish that wasn't ordered and when told that don't even once question the guest- I'm not at Burger King
3) after just 2 hours don't start rushing us out by asking several times if we're done and especially for a place with this price point don't bring the check until we asked for it

Like I said before food was good but I was disappointed in the overall experience.

Cosme- you left a bad taste in my mouth.

I'm only concerned with the food and could care less about the instagramability of the deserts or the decor - though it has a great bathroom. 

We had the Uni Tostada, Octopus Cocktail, Spare Ribs, Soft Shell Crab, and the Corn Husk Meringue. What drew me to the place was the reviews and the interesting combination of ingredients, but after trying all of the above, the flavor profiles just didn't do it for me. Probably the best was the Uni. The Octopus is in a balsamic glaze and nothing special. The Spare Rib was OK (there is one) but the meat did not really seem like it was marinated or flavorful - I thought by merging it with the Avocado and onion that it would give it something special.  Maybe for some people these flavors work together but I was left unimpressed - definitely OK but just fell short of the reviews here and what I expected from a new style mexican restaurant. The supposed signature desert (Corn Husk Meringue) was just very sweet and corny. Not looking to save money, but honestly $12 for a draft Dos Equis seems a bit high even in NYC.  The highlight, for me, was the cookie that came with the Cortado.

Obviously you can't expect anything less than delicious food at this restaurant, particularly given the prices. However, some of the prices were outrageous, such as $69 for the duck and $21 per each tuna tostada. Yes, they were delicious, but not - blown away delicious. The food here is scrumptious, but if you're looking to be amazed and for value, you are better of with a top degustation restaurant. There were too many staff fussing about your table, and no one seemed to be a knowledgeable sommelier. Cocktails were fantastic. Overall the food is great, the drinks are great and if you have money to burn to go ahead and book a table here. Otherwise, save your money and head to the best degustation menu or Michelin starred restaurant you can find which would probably end up the same price but taste better.
The mole is amazing, and the cocktails refined. Pricier than I would have expected, but worth the experience.

This place is sexy. With excellent food from a 3 star Michelin chef. Sliced fish and guac as a starter. Solid. Great tequila drinks. Branzino and soft shell crab were quite tasty. Chi chi Mexican done right even in New York. And to finish with the corn meringue. Fun night.

The service was great which is why I'm giving three stars. Unfortunately I had what amounted to verde soup with tortilla chips in it. It was supposed to have chicken but I only found a few small pieces. Very disappointed especially because of how much it cost. Couldn't even finish it. We did have the stuffed Avacado which was good but not outstanding.

It was my second visit to Cosme and I so wanted to like it... Elevated, modern Mexican cousine from the 3 Michelin star chef Enrique Olvera - the siren song to my global foodies ears.... I brought my vegetarian husband and the server was not able to explain any of the vegetarian dishes in a concise and comprehensible manner - I had to guide him with questions and then we had to look up some of the ingredients on the Internet. Finally we made our decisions and ordered one dish each, only to be told by the server that "usually people order 3 each". OK, we get it, you have a tapas concept but unless you call it a prix fixe it is still our prerogative to order as many dishes as we'd like and at a pace which is convenient to us. And no, we are not going $200 dollars in before we get a better idea of what your vegetarian dishes are like. We also ordered two glasses of different sparkling wines - the server poured my husband's glass almost right away but then it took quite some time for him to come back with the wine I ordered (I had to follow up) - in the meantime the wine in the first glass went flat... We got our dishes pretty quickly - my husband's spelt esquites was aggressively acidic without finesse and just plain boring - the corn (a star ingredient of the Mexican street fare this dish was supposed to be an elevated version of) was nowhere to be tasted - the server mentioned that it was emulsified to become part of the sauce despite the fact that the menu listed it as a separate ingredient - the sauce tasted bland and overall this dish has brought on absolutely no associations with Mexican street corn, elevated or otherwise. My husband asked for a few cherry tomatoes similar to what I had in my dish and was told that the kitchen was "too busy". Hmmm, we have never had this type of response in any NYC restaurants including Michelin star ones... Perhaps, the food is pre-made and pre-portioned before service, rather than made to order? This was odd.
The blue shrimp was bright and fresh and that's why I am giving 2 and not 1 star. 
Snaps to Michelin reviewers for not giving Cosme a star - they definitely have not earned one yet. And to NYT reviewers, just because we finally get a Mexican fine dining establishment in the city (long overdue), does not mean we need to get so overexcited that we drop our high standards - I know, I know, it is easy to get seduced by a unique Mezcal tasting list, my poor darlings, but then a restaurant is about FOOD and SERVICE and then about drinks...
AMAZING Bartender Chris who started our night off with great cocktails .Our party move to table and the food great but the descerts and service knocked  it out of the park

Cosme is upscale and modern. The food here is very good. Although I'm not sure my opinion is comprehensive because I'm allergic most of the menu (seafood). But what I did try was great.
Stand outs for me were the duck carnitas (their signature dish) and the brisket. I don't typically care for duck or brisket but these were both outstanding. Extremely flavorful and juicy, you did not even need a knife to pull these apart.

The menu is intended to be served family style yet each dish is still small so you can try a bunch of different options if you do share. The service was very polite and attentive although it did take some time for food/drinks to come out. I had a few palomas to drink which was delicious but seemingly light on alcohol.

Apparently, the husk meringue is the most instagrammed dessert in NYC but I have no idea why. It was indeed very good but I wasn't blown away like I usually am when I try something incredible. I don't understand the hype?

The decor is immaculate. So much detail is given to the set up. The restaurant is dim yet the lighting is set precisely to hit the center of your table so your family-styled dishes are illuminated just perfectly and more so than the perimeter of the table where your own plate would be. Who even thinks of this.

Pricing is a little outrageous but you're paying for trendy, quality food and a sophisticated atmosphere. This is definitely a place for foodies and dates rather than people that want to enjoy a traditional meal.

One of the best meals I've ever had. New Yorkers do not know what they have in this place. Everyone around us seemed to come here expecting to be fed typical "Mexican food." They ordered guacamole and asked for their dishes to be prepared "not spicy." Not sure if they would ask French James Beard award winning chefs to make so many accommodations. The duck carnitas are the most typical Mexican dish. Imagine that!  Have them with the emoladas. The octopus cocktail is incredible. The sliced fish was so unexpectedly simple. My favorite was the huarache. It was a citrus bomb in my mouth. If you grew up eating limon y sal, you will love this dish. The specialty cocktails were great. Don't come here and order the margarita, order the ANTI HISTAMINE instead.
Excellent drinks, beautiful room, and the best churros I've ever tasted. Not to mention the husk meringue with corn mousse...

I thought the Duck Carnitas were so fantastic, and I am not a fan of duck. My wife encouraged me, and wow, was I glad she did. Just delectable. I also thought the Enmoladas were tasty and memorable, and would definitely order them again. For drinks, I tried the chipotle-infused Don Juan, which was sweet and perfect for me, and my wife had the Scoville Sour, which was zippy. The waiter was attentive and friendly, and explained the dishes when we had questions. I enjoyed the quiet atmosphere where the light shines on your table, and you are surrounded by relative darkness. An intimate setting with plenty of space.
This place was amazing. Every dish was done well and had a unique taste. The guacamole, the cobia fish was a must-order, the short rib and the duck carnitas were all top notch. Highly recommend.

My husband and I went to Cosme with a big group and overall we were disappointed.  We heard great things and it just did not live up to the hype.  While the food was good ( not great, but good ) especially the duck carnitas, the restaurant is so overpriced.  We don't mind paying for excellent food but this did not measure up and we have had much better Mexican food for half the price. 

Please don't review this business if you received a freebie for writing this review, or if you're connected in any way to the owner or employees.

Overrated and expensive. Got a bunch of dishes to share and none of them were really memorable. We got scallop and octopus, which was decent, guacamole, soft shell crab, duck carnitas, tlayuda, husk meringue, and rhubarb dessert. The only thing I say you definitely need to try is the husk meringue! It was special. The others combine flavors that don't always go well together. Reservations are a little tough to get too.

The food was like nothing I had ever eaten simple elegant and extravagant the staff was so friendly it was worth it and can't wait to go back.

It is a place I will take my out of state business friends to show off NYC

We were lucky to go here with folks that know food and the chef. We didn't order anything from the menu and let the chef build the experience for us. It was a five hour dinner on a weeknight. We went to bed in food coma's. As a vegetarian, I was taken care of beautifully. The staff is unbelievable. Very knowledgable about the history and lore of the food they are serving. Obviously I didn't eat the duck or the fish but the table ooohed and ahhed when the carnita's arrived. (They arrived after we thought dinner was done!). The meal began with a mezcal margarita and ended with a shot of mezcal, just the way I like it.

Went there for anniversary and I am compelled to say this restaurant has the best experience of any other place I've been to in Manhattan in recent memory.  Staff is kind, attentive, personable and intuitive.  The food quality is superb and drinks are unique Mexican avant garde.  I especially want to commend Xavier for being a marvelous, considerate and friendly host.

I have been to Cosme at least 4 times and every time I had a great experience. I was shocked to see that they went down to 3.5 stars and tonight I learned why. 

Perhaps there was a change in management because our experience started early. We had 8 PM reservations and were not seated until 8:30 PM. The ordering process was not bad, the waiter was nice, but then the service dropped drastically. They accidentally cleared a drink that was not even done, the appetizers didn't come out until we asked about it (30 minutes later) and our waiter pretty much disappeared for the rest of the night. 

The food was not as memorable, the crispy tortillas tasted stale, somewhat of a disappointment. When the food came out, the introduction was horrible, probably because the waiter was not around and the bus boy was left to answer the questions. 

What does the Maitre d' of this restaurant do? No, I'm sorry for the wait, how was your food, etc, etc. Lots of great restaurants in NYC with better service that's in the same price range so get your staff together and make your guests dining experience better or risk closing down your restaurant. I'm saddened by the experience tonight, you used to be one of my favorite restaurants. 

The most memorable thought of the night, on an evening that was not inexpensive, was wondering where our waiter was... What a sad way to spend hard earned money.

Considering the amount of money our party of 7 spent here, I really didn't appreciate our servers coming up to our table every 5 minutes trying to clear everything before we even had a chance to finish our meals.  Even our half-full (very overpriced) drinks and dessert were quick to be cleared and we were in the restaurant for all of an hour and a 30 mins at this point.  I'm sorry, but if I'm going to dish out $69 for a subpar piece of duck, I want to at least try to enjoy it and not feel rushed and unwelcome. And this is coming from someone who has worked in restaurants for several years and understands what it's like from the other side. Completely ruined our experience here. Unacceptable!!!

Hands down the best Mexican cuisine restaurant in New York City. Cosme is umami. 

Mexico has a tremendous variety of foods--way more than tacos and tamales. Every region has different dishes; different traditions. 

Chef Olvera embodies every aspect of Mexican cuisine in his dishes. 
The staff does a fantastic job in making you feel at home. 

The best thing on the drinks menu is the "striptease" a truly amazing combination of Mezcal and guava. 

If you're ready to step up your Mexican food game, Cosme is the place to do it.

Meh.  Hostess had serious attitude (yawn / girl, bye.) and we sat down 30 mins late with a reservation. Waiter spilled a glass of wine on my friend.   

Food was decent.  Duck was dry AF.  Lobster and tuna were great. Nothing really had any spice though.   Totally underwhelmed, especially for the money.
A unique, sophisticated Mexican experience. I wouldn't expect traditional plates. The food was mind-blowingly good (duck tacos and short rib are delicious), but I would skip dessert.

3.5 stars! 

Love the decor! This has been on my list since forever. We got the tuna taco which was amazing however very small for the price you are paying. The duck main dish which was..... Not the greatest. It was definitely unique but the sauce seems a bit overpowering. We also got the quinoa salad with sesame dressing or some sort and that kick that it had was amazing. It is probably one of the best salads ever! We also got the corn husk merengue dessert, and it was not to my liking at all. It wA too sweet, the texture was not pleasant  but I reallllly wanted to like it...... :(
