I would come back to try new dishes but definitely get the quinoa salad.

I am a fan of Mexican food and have been to many Mexican restaurants. Cosme has been my favourite. The Cobia Al Pastor and Short Rib tacos were simply amazing. My only regret is not having had tried more dishes! The ambiance is great as well -- trendy and lively.

Very cool place... Guac was good. The margarita was OK but the other food was 'meh'
I can't believe the waiter sold us the zucchini chocolate cake and we still tipped him. Horrible! Horrible!!

I was excited to try cosme when recently in New York.  I had seen the Chef's Table episode of Enrique Olivera and his Mexico City restaurant Pujols.

We went for brunch.  It is a beautiful space, spacious and with a huge staff.  The menu seemed pretty limited for brunch but all the choices looked amazing.  I tried the chiqualiques and they were some of her best ever- the tortillas were sublime, and the salsa s. I ordered also a Bloody Maria, which was super spicy but super delicious. I would highly recommend.

Scoping around all the best restaurants and still this is my favorite in Town, every dish is perfect..the right amount of seasoning, I never leave dissatisfied...if only Chef Daniela could be my mentor lol. Not my grandmother's cooking it's a different take on Mexican food which I appreciate it takes risk to change dishes that are traditional and to make them great its an accomplishment on its own!

Came here on Father's Day with 6 family members, and I was shocked at how terrible the food and the service were. I have been to the best restaurants in the world and I was expecting that Cosme would live up to what is evidently a false reputation. I have never experienced such a sub standard level of food, taste, service, and general treatment of my guests and I. Cosme deserves no stars but unfortunately the system doesn't allow that low level of review. I have recommended to several hundred of my friends and acquaintances, many of whom are in the restaurant industry to avoid Cosme like the Black Plague. Whoever reads this should avoid Cosme at all costs. I have had better Carnitas on the street in Mexico City, Phoenix, and In various street carts in Manhattan. Cosme should be truly concerned about the slop they serve and the indifference and hostility of its servers.

Had dinner here a few weeks ago at a communal table. The service was mediocre, we only saw our waitress two times, to take our order and cut our duck entree. The food was good, but not as great as we expected given the reviews. 

Unit Tostada - First time having uni and was not a big fan. The dish was not explained very well and was average. 

Duck Carnitas - The focus of our trip to Cosme was disappointing. The duck was juicy but not very flavorful and there were no other real other accompaniments to the entree for our "tacos". At almost $70 for the entree, this was overpriced for the quantity and overall quality of the dish. 

Corn Meringue Dessert: This was the best part of the meal. Light and fluffy, as well as really different from the traditional desserts at most NYC restaurants.

Food 4
Service 3
Ambiance 4
O/all 3.5

Maybe an expectations game where a chef that is known to be a 'top 50' in the world would showcase that brilliance in nyc, a truly global stage....but no luck.

Things to note:
1/ food was good but portions were tiny and quite pricey even for nyc standards
2/ not very creative
3/ service was surprisingly reactive and not proactive, esp considering this type of establishment

Worth at least one try and you decide for yourself...

I'd heard of Cosme before but like another reviewer it was after watching Chefs Table that I decided to come here. My husband and I came for dinner on a Friday night. It pays to reserve several weeks in advance: we booked 4 weeks before online and could only get a early table, at 6:15pm.

We ordered 6 dishes including a salad plus one dessert, which was plenty. The servings are medium sized; I wouldn't describe them as small. We definitely left feeling full. If you're not starving, 2 plates each might suffice. Plates are grouped according to "lightness". Three of our dishes were from the first group: uni tostada, octopus scallop cocktail, ayacote bean salad. I liked all of them and definitely recommend the uni tostada. Calamari was fine as was the soft shell crab and branzino but we were quite full by the fish serving time and couldn't have many of the accompanying tortillas. We did make room for dessert because I had been dying to try the corn mousse and husk meringue. It was my favourite dish of the night.

Yes, it's pricey, just like any other nice meal anywhere, especially New York. The setting is dark and modern. I would say noise levels are quite high. Our service was very good.

I enjoyed our dining experience. It is nice to have the flavours of modern Mexican with fresh lime, avocado and many herbs with good quality seafood in a refined way. I would return especially to have the meringue and corn mousse again!

Nice cozy brunch spot with beautifully simple decor. 

The kitchen was closing 4 minutes after we got there basically so we had to order all the food we wanted right away ... Kinda turned off about this. Why would you let me make a reservation basically at closing time ? The portions were super small here & I left hungry because I couldn't order any more food.


But anyway,

Oysters. Some potato appetizer. Egg sope. Husk meringue

Everything tastes delicious! The egg sope did taste a little bland to me though, could have had a little more of a flavor without having to drown it in salsa verde.

The best thing I ate was the dessert, man o man that husk meringue is A M A Z I N G. I shared it with my girlfriends but I secretly wanted to order another one just for me :) 

I would recommend coming here but try catching the lunch or dinner menu. Also ! Make sure you have time to order some more if you're hungry after finishing ... Which I'm sure you will be.

When visiting New York from Texas, one of my colleagues recommended this place. So on our last night in the big apple we had a girls night out and decided to dine at Cosme.  We tried several dishes every dish was incredible. We
We were very impressed with the chef!!!!

Throw your preconceived notions of Mexican cuisine out the door. This is refined modern cuisine with Mexican flavors done to perfection. From the raw small plates like the tuna tostada and sliced raw fish to the decadent cobia al pastor, short rib, soft shell crab, and duck carnitas, everything was on par with top restaurants in New York. Don't skip dessert because they husk merengue will blow you away!

We were in the neighborhood and saw the communal table was open so we decided to give it a try.

18 minutes later and multiple requests for menus....

guac was average - really had no flavors besides the avocado and it was $15 for a small serving. The chips were delicious.

The soft shell crab dish and margarita were the highlights for us - great flavors, spiciness and crispness. Everything else hugely underwhelming.

Most disappointing and almost comical was the service. Three times we got wrong items and because our server was MIA we had to leave our table to get things corrected. We had to ask any passerby employee for drink menus, salsa, a fork,etc.

One of my dining partners is vegan and they refused to leave off the cheese that was sprinkled on top. I get it - chefs art and all that but come on.

The best duck we've ever had, and we have had our share. We came in with high expectations after the New York Times food critic listed Cosme's Duck Carnitas first on his list of the 10 best dishes from last year. Hard to live up to that expectation but they did. The culmination of a four day cooking process which includes deboning, marinating, slow cooking for 12 hours, then crisping up the skin, this dish for two has me salvaging again as I write this.

The restaurant is a sleek, beautiful place. Also impressive was our waitress who was expertly trained.

After I watched Season 2 of Chef's Table, I just had to go to this place. Yes, it's overpriced. Yes, it's small portions. But I still quite enjoyed my experience here!

My friend and I ordered the uni tostada, tlayuda, short rib, and corn meringue. It was just about enough for the two of us, and we didn't break the bank. 

The uni was amazing paired with the crispy tostada and tangy line. What an awesome combination of flavours. 

The tlayuda was quite dull...just some flava beans and peas on a large tortilla. But at least it helped fill us up. 

The short rib was my favourite!! It was so tender. It just melts in your mouth. And I loved the corn tortillas that came with it -- you can really taste the particular corn species. 

And finally, the corn meringue was lovely, if you love corn, which I do. I think I largely liked this place because of the prevalence of corn in the tortillas and even in the dessert.
Incredible cocktails with unique flavors. Solid but unpretentious service.  Great dishes. Only misses were those with too much spice. Cobia and crab and short rib were incredible.

i might have to break up with enrique olvera. very cute place (yet loud!). we ordered a bunch of plates, but a couple of days later I can't remember any of them. that unmemorable? plus they kept trying to take our dishes away even though we weren't finished. dont rush me when I am paying 25 freaking dollars for a mini-tostada!!

Hugely disappointing

Ate here about a year ago and had a terrific, if expensive, meal from start to finish, so I was really looking forward to this visit.  Although it was as difficult as ever to get a Sat. night reservation, the food was about as different as could be. 

First dish was soft shell crab in yellow mole, which certainly sounded fabulous. The dish delivered was the first hint that things weren't right.  The breading was so thick it completely overwhelmed the crab flavor, and the yellow mole was restricted to about a spoonful spread on the bottom of the serving bowl. Even an amateur cook should know how to properly bread seafood.

Second dish was a purple potato tamal.  The kimchi on top was actually good with a bright pickled taste, but the rest of the dish was a bland, unseasoned mash potato cylinder. Guess the shape is what made it a tamal, but no one bothered to make it actually tasty.

Third dish was their signature duck carnitas, which carries an astounding price of $69.  What we got was a large piece of duck with some sliced green chiles and a mound of cilantro that looked like it had bolted.  The duck skin was not crisp and much of the duck breast was dry and overcooked.  It came with two small bowls of salsa, a very ordinary salsa verde and a chile arbol sauce too hot to eat.  Most telling of all about the lack of care in the kitchen was the tortillas.  Last time they were handmade and had a lovely corn fragrance and taste.  This time they were machine made like you'd get in any old taco joint and bland -- in a $69 dish!

Not sure what's happened here, but the place seems to always be full so maybe the kitchen is overwhelmed. Or maybe they feel New Yorkers don't really get fine Mexican cuisine. Whatever the cause, I won't be returning. 

I will say the service was cordial and attentive.

Argh. What a disappointment! 
I watched Chef's Table and got really excited to try this place and it just fell so short of what I expected! Before I start, I want to let you know that I lived and worked in Mexico and paying $270 for 2 people at a "Mexican" restaurant is such a crime when it doesn't meet expectations.

We started with drinks. I made sure to get something with mescal in it and the Ninja was amazing. My girlfriend ordered a margarita which was equally amazing as well. We later ordered another drink with mescal that was a hit. When it comes to drinks, definitely A+

We started with the uni tostada. The uni itself was delicious but the combination of the uni and bone marrow and pico de gallo was not a hit to me. It just lacked authentic Mexican flavors and I wasn't impressed. The same goes for the soft shell crab. I was really looking forward to the molé and God was it a disappointment! The crab was well done but once again, it lacked Mexican flavors to it. We finished off with the duck carnitas which was good as well but definitely not great.

We had the meringue and sorbet for desert. Nothing spectacular either. 

I feel like I didn't get my Mexican fix from this place and I know the chef mentioned that he didn't want to stick to fat and make Mexican food in more refined ways but this doesn't really enhance Mexican food. Therefore, I was disappointed

Before I begin let me say, I'm not Mexican and Mexican American food isn't my thing. I came here because of the chef and I heard it's an upscale spin on Mexican cuisine. I also can't speak for dinner, I came on a Saturday at 1.

This is definitely a different interpretation of Mexican food. It's more like bite size tapas.. Which is funny because my server made my group of 7 (2 fairly large guys included) believe that we would be filled if we ordered 8-9 plates. Speaking of him, he was fairly attentive. We often asked for water/ice and waited forever to have it. My request for their bubbly water was completely ignored.

Speaking for the food, it fell short of expectations'. Certain things were flavorful but nothing that surprised me more than the spices at a local Mex-American place. The plate arrangement and appearance didn't necessarily make the meal look more appetizing. I figure that it's not easy playing up so many dark colors, once they mix it looks so bad. The drinks were alright.

Regarding the layout of the restaurant, I was not a fan. I felt like I was walking into a colleges sophisticated cafeteria. It was interesting that upon entering, the entrance looks spacious but then you get to the tables and they're crammed next to each other.

Been wanting to go here for awhile now and now that I know they made the top 100 list I am glad that on a rainy Sunday we were able to snag a table. 

Let's start with the high notes. 

We went for mostly fish and I enjoyed how they sent our dishes coursed to share beginning with all fish. 

Uni tostada with bone marrow salsa- Smokey from the bone marrow. Extremely fresh and delicious uni, winner. 

Cobia al pastor - the fish is cooked perfectly. Super tender well seasoned served with a lovely pineapple purée. This makes a wonderful taco. Don't pass this up, seriously good eats. 

Soft shell crab with yellow mole- Again this dish is really good. The yellow mole is seriously amazing... Notes of coconut, fruits, with a lovely depth of spices served with a papaya salad. the crab lightly tempura'ed, crunchy, perfectly cooked. Who doesn't love soft shell crab season? 
Eat it. Truly outstanding. 

Scallops and oyster cocktail- Black aguachile, avocado and ink. There was a deep smokiness from the charred "sauce" that rested underneath the fish that was interesting but I found this overacidic, unbalanced, and frankly underwhelming. The octopus is nice and the scallops tenderly sliced but for the price tag I think this is a skip. 

Tlayuda (to share) with hoja Santa, peas, and cheese. This dish was a total cop out. For me the chef was honestly like "oh fuck we need a spring dish with English peas, let's put it on tlayuda!"
Uninspired, boring. The hoja Santa was somehow flavorless (where did they buy it from?) and covered my entire plate. the peas were overcooked. However.... The salsa verde served on the side, damn that was good. should be bottled and I would drink that (maybe would be better than the boring cocktail I had)

We got the kimchi dish, spicy and bland at the same time somehow... And the spelt. It was good but heavy and again kind of bland. 

I wanted to try different dishes because I think it's a true test to make your veggie plates as good as a duck, but we should have just skipped those plates and got the carnitas ...


My meal ended with the corn husk meringue which instantly made my whole meal better don't skip desert. The wine we bought was really great too. I wanted to order a different bottle but the list was quite expensive.

Cosme was worth it. But I was a little let down that such an acclaimed place had big misses.

Now being mexican, i was happy to see a establishment being held in a  prominent part of manhattan. I was really excited to come here, BUT, from the interesting choice of decor, to the ambience, Something jus doesn't make me feel like its authentic? I'm not sure if thats what there were going for. i mean it is NY and all. A very important element was missing. Their Margaritas just weren't wat i expected, specially for the price points.. I did like the unique items created by enrique olvera, The Duck carnitas were outstanding i must say, the desserts were jus ok and i wouldn't order them again, same for drinks.. service was fine though, I was only not feeling it because of the ambience and the delivery of some of the products just diidint hit like they should of. O yea this ahi tuna tower was better than average. thank you for representing mr Olvera. Cheers

A hit or miss. This place should be so good, but not everything is great. Drinks are fantastic, some tostadas are great. Duck Carnitas, uni, salmon, fantastic. others where are bit of a miss. Service was good, greeters made the place feel a bit snobbish, but lots of NYC places are like that nowadays. Would definitely give it another chance.

I really like Cosme! The flavors are deep and true. I love the tostadas they bring out to start with the sauces, which (surprise!)  don't have to be spicy to be flavorful. My favorite menu items are the cobia al pastor, the enmoladas or enfrijoladas, the duck carnitas, and the chicharron they used to offer. I love the different mole flavors they use from the poblano to the yellow mole - serious, serious skill involved in making those. The tortillas are to die for. Also, the mixed drinks are SO good. 

After reading the disappointing reviews, I wouldn't advise people that are expecting/want Americanized "Mexican" food (cheesy enchiladas, fajitas, guacamole, queso, etc) to come here. That's not Mexican food.

Amazing meal at Cosme last night. 

Good service, attentive but not pushy. 

I had the Striptease cocktail which had absinthe in it. I couldn't taste it for the mezcal but it might have made me extra giddy. 

Uni tostada, beautiful and surprisingly hearty. 

We barely spoke while eating the octopus ceviche or "black cocktail". It was so good I asked for a spoon to finish the squid ink juice left in the bowl. 

The enmoladas had a beautiful mole. The tlayuda was a meal itself with  fresh peas, pea shoots, burrata and poached egg. So good.

By the time I got my short rib I was a little full. But I got my pescatarian husband to take a few bites. With food this good, you know it's worthwhile. 

I knocked off 1 star because the noise level got annoying. It was tolerable when we sat down but as the meal went on it seemed they matched the diners' noise level by raising the music volume. Oy.

The food is indeed delightful. Delicate flavors with creative preparations. Good use of ingredients. Serving portions small but pricey but not a complaint as the food is that good. However, being asked to clear the table for another party shows an utter lack of class and understanding that we pay the hefty price tag for an overall dining experience. Wood I recommend the place, well certainly the food not the place.

I can't remember the last time I finished a meal at a restaurant and thought, "Wow, I'm impressed." 

Cosme impressed me.

I stopped in with a friend and managed to get a seat at a bar table. Every course was excellent. We started with the raw fish, which was very well-balanced. (although a little overpriced) We then moved onto the duck carnitas, which were really just superb. The duck was perfectly moist. We finished with the famed husk meringue and corn mousse along with the fennel ice cream/raspberry raspado. The meringue was quite tasty, although the fennel ice cream dish better suited my palate with its refreshing lightness and mix of textures.

Both I and my dining companion agreed it was a phenomenal meal. 

FINAL RATING:
4.5
The service is attentive. The place is chic. The cocktails have a nice kick. The fish is delicious and fresh. But keep in mind the servings are small and in summary the place is overpriced.

Over rated!!! So sad as this place has been bookmark for over a year and the reservations are slim unless your a 9pm eater. We finally made it and I faced the fact that I will starve until 9:45p. Walked in at 9:15p the place was packed! Checked in with the hostess and then proceeded to the bar where I was hoping I would love my jalapeño margarita... Unfortunately it tasted like water down juice. Waited until 10:15pm to be seated and started ordering. 
The wine list was not impressive at all but we found a mencia one that would hold us over. The mark up was ridiculous and they charge a $50 corkage fee so what do you do??? The only thing that was good was the purple potato tamale and the octopus starter. Also, their hot sauce lacked any heat... A little disappointed for all the hype this spot has been given.

I'm going to agree with the 31/2 stars. If you are a tourist and want a "New York trendy dining experience" definitely a must go. If you are New York foodie and have an extra few hundred it will be ok. Otherwise sit at the bar, order some drinks and a couple aps and call it done.

It's hurtful to put 3 stars because is a Very good looking place; all staff (I counted like 30) friendly and smiling. And I'm Mexican feeling proud of the great job they're trying to do, but it doesn't make sense...
I went for brunch, got the pancakes (15$) I do not care about the price, but I care about the quality and portion. I checked many pictures in Yielp and Cosme's portions are for a models with eating disorders.

Work on it guys, the place has a lot of potential.

As a bi-coastal person who normally stick to the LA = TACO and NYC = PIZZA rule, I bow down to the greatness that would have me order an Al Pastor taco on the right coast. Jeez Louise this was insane. The sliced pork, pineapple and sauce in a tortilla is like a dream I had once. 

These cocktails are on point. It's like the tequila version of NoMad cocktails. Holy whoa yum. My new go-to when I'm in this area of town. 

The cheesecake at the end was quite savory and special. Thank goodness people with class and taste created this lovely establishment.
Wonderful place.  Amazing food. Don't know why it's Mexican genre. Has nothing to do with Mexicant.
Amazing. Been here 5 times now. Each time better than the next. Must get duck carnitas and husk meringue. Richard was my server most recent time and he was stellar. Highly recommend!!!

Overpricing drags it down from three stars. Much like the chef's flagship Pujol in Mexico City, highly uneven--though the highs are not as high and the lows not so low. Best course at a recent lunch was the crudo/oysters/raw blue shrimp. Our party of four had all three of the "big" plates, which were collectively a disappointment: an unrefined duck in red mole, a fresh but bland whole fish, and a wonderful short rib in a shockingly small portion for the price ($35).

Had a similar impression at dinner here last fall, though I'd agree that the duck carnitas--unavailable at lunch--are worth the price of admission.

Good bartender, though--terrific Palomas.

had brunch, all good, love the corn cake! 
most dishes have cilantro:parsley tho so ¯\_(ツ)_/¯

Food was good, nicely spiced but eating huevos rancheros and ridiculously saucy chilaquiles out of bowls was challenging at best. Service was so rushed we thought there was a prize involved for turning our table in less than 30 minutes!

Great cuisine. A little pricey. Artfully presented. I enjoyed the sommelier the most. He recommended excellent wines with different food pairings. Champagne with the scallops and fish and a Spanish red with the duck and short ribs.

Went for lunch and the experience was fun.  There were high and low notes so I will try to enumerate them so you can see why I'm giving this only three stars, when it probably ought to be able to do better.
When we arrived on time for our reservation there was a bit of fumbling around and mistaken identity at the front desk.  Not unfriendly, just strange.  Given that the place was half empty and stayed that way through lunchtime, you would think they might not have cared whether we had a rez or not, would simply have been happy to see paying customers!  That same theme prevailed when, again despite an empty house, we were taken all the way to the back of the restaurant and seated by the swinging door to the kitchen.  Why do so many places do this?  It is infuriating to walk past scores of empty, better placed tables when you have showed up on time for your reservation.
Our table service didn't start out well  - after we had been given menus we had to ask twice for someone to fetch our server to take a drink order.  She was a bit frosty about being called over, however, once we got started with the meal she was super friendly and helpful.
Some of the food was absolutely delicious.  The avocado with seafood was perfect, half an avocado stuffed with raw (ceviche type) fish and shellfish and a re smoky sauce.  Just delicious and fresh.  The buratta with greens was also really good.  The duck enchilada (that's not what it is called on the menu but that's how the server described it) had a very good mole sauce and a crepe- like wrapper, all good.  But the duck itself was sort of mashed up and tasteless.  The Veracruzada fish dish was good, again raw, so if that's not your thing you probably won't like it.  The Margaritas were perfect - not at all like the sweet syrupy things you get at most bars, but fresh and light with the lime and tequila flavors shining through.
Finally the famed corn husk meringue dessert.  I get that this is a novelty and it obviously takes a lot of work to make but we thought it definitely odd tasting - sort of like a can of creamed corn.  Would not order it again although it was very pretty.  So all in all a nice lunch, some pleasant surprises and some not quite up to par.  But holding down the stars is the value question.  With tax and tip, lunch for 2 people came to over $225.  I don't mind footing a big bill like that if everything is really special but the price/value thing didn't add up here, IMHO.

Atmosphere: kinda lounge-y which was not what I expected. The music was fun but the mood lighting and couch seating were heavy-handed.

Service: we had a reservation and had to wait about 20 minutes, which seems like the norm according to other reviews. The service throughout dinner was really attentive and well-timed. Also informative, but a little brusque.

Food: It was good but not great. We got the legendary duck carnitas, but I was more in love with the tortillas. The raw fish was excellent quality but the plating and accompaniments were dull. The tlayuda was tasty, but confusing and messy. The corn husk meringue was every bit as incredible as the reviews say. I wish that I could have it again, but I won't be back.

This was my first time in NYC and I did a lot of research into high-end restaurants as I only had enough money for one. I feel like I wasted an opportunity.
My friends and I were blown away by the avant garde nature of this menu. Duck taquitos, mescal inspired dishes. Really unique cutting edge Mexican food.

I've always wanted to eat more Mexican food in NYC, but I don't get around to it as much as I should. When Cosme opened last year, it was far too difficult to get a reservation - and it's still quite popular - but we finally ended up coming here for a chill Sunday night dinner last weekend. It was packed, and even showing up on time for a 7:30 reservation required us to wait at the bar for a little bit (about 5 minutes or so) before getting seated. The space has a very contemporary feel to it, with a bit of homeyness - the dining room is surrounded by bookshelves that have a cashier, many bottles of wine, books, and other decorative pieces. The service was pretty solid, with the food brought out in well-spaced segments. The beer selection is okay, if a bit on the light side for crafts; however, the cocktails here are delicious. The two I had (the Anti Histamine and the Telenovela) were both fantastic; both were infused with a healthy dosage of mixers (honey for the former; pineapple for the latter) that really blended and complemented the liquor well. That said, I didn't actually order the Telenovela (I had wanted El Ninja), and the fact that the order was definitely forgotten - I had to remind the waiter about it - and then brought improperly is pretty sloppy for a higher-end restaurant.

The food itself was quite delicious and amply sized, especially if you are two people splitting the duck carnitas. The main course is a treat - a half-duck cooked carnitas style and dripping in delicious juices. As with many dishes, it is served with freshly-made mini-tortillas with which you can make your own tacos. The duck is absolutely delicious and extremely succulent; the smokiness of the meat really adds a bit more depth than the usual salty fattiness of pork carnitas. The intro courses, which are generically separated into raw fish and vegetables (not really hard categories at all, based on the ingredients) were also good but were overall a bit more of a mixed bag. The uni tostada was fantastic - the creaminess of the uni on the hard, crunchy tostada was a great contrast of flavors and texture. The cobia was also excellent - very lightly seared, giving the fish a good texture without being too cooked, but infused with enough flavor to give it a very mellow, slightly spicy taste. The 'vegetable' plates were a bit less interesting, in large part because they were doused in so much sauce. It was a bit disappointing relative to the other starters, as well as the tostadas (which were served as bread would be at an American restaurant); those were more subtle but still expressed a wide gamut of flavoring. I did like the beets with the stracciatella more, as the strength of the beet flavor shown through the sauce. However, the sunchokes were absolutely drenched in the adobo paprika sauce, rendering it (and the fried calamari it was served with) a dish that felt like you were eating a lot of sauce and it happened to have other items in it. After barely finishing off the duck, though, we did end on an excellent note - the husk meringue here is phenomenal and probably the best meringue I've had. Great texture, very light, and just the right amount of subtlety on the corn flavor.

Dinner here overall was quite good, and I enjoyed the atmosphere as well. The food, on balance, was above-average, and I'd definitely come back again to sample some of the other items as well. The service was generally good, too, but I'm just not a fan of when people get an order wrong / miss an item entirely. That said, I do like the modern, cosmopolitan take on Mexican cuisine, and I will come back in the future!

Truly a great experience! If you love fresh seafood  with Mexican flavors this will be a winner! Try the sliced raw fish with lime, avocado, poblano and black lime, also the thin slices of raw scallops in the yummiest marinade are insane. The duck carnitas are out of this world! Ps: the interior decor is killer! Love the minimalistic vibe! This is def on my new fav' dining list!

Took my husband out to dinner for his birthday.  Our reservation was at 8:45pm and we got there a little early so we had a drink at the bar. The bartender was very nice and let us try some mezcals.  We were then seated at 8:50pm and we were both starving.  We ordered the Uni Toast and Burrata to start and shared the duck carnitas for our entree.  Server told us that would be more than enough food.  The Burrata was the highlight (which was unexpected) but it comes with this smoky salsa that's so delicious.  The Uni toast was fine but nothing spectacular.  The duck carnitas were really good but not sure if it was worth $70.  The food overall was decent.  However, our server rubbed me the wrong way when I asked her for some extra salsa that came with the amuse tostada.  I wanted to put some on the duck carnitas because I like spicy.  She said no problem.  10 minutes pass by and no salsa, and by then we were halfway done eating the duck.  I figured she had forgotten- so I asked her about it again and she threw me some serious attitude!  She said in a very rude and condescending way- " UM, yeh I already asked for it and it has not come out yet ".  I looked at my husband and we were both like- uh, okay? Her tone was so nasty its as if I said something offensive.  It totally threw off the vibe of our night.  Anyways, it ended up coming out super late and we were pretty much done with our entree.  All she needed to tell me was it takes time to make it or something along those lines.  It was as if I had bothered her by asking twice.  Very strange and unacceptable behavior from a server.  We ended up ordering the corn husk merengue for dessert and it was very good BUT I called earlier in the day to tell them that we were celebrating my husband's birthday and would like for them to do the candle in the dessert thing at the end.  They said no problem, we will make note of it.  Low and behold- no candle in the dessert.  I really wanted to like this place because I've heard such good things. And I love authentic Mexican food.  The food was good but unfortunately, the service made me dislike my experience there.

I just went here with three friends for a drink at the bar. Two of the servers were rude and the drinks were mediocre, but very expensive. I will not return to this restaurant and I won't suggest it to anyone.
Best Mexican restaurant in NYC.  Favorite dishes - bean salad, calamari, cobia, short ribs.

The chef is amazing in his Mexico City restaurant. But this one is a joke. Milking his reputation but delivering mediocrity all around. He should fire his team and prevent further damage to his reputation. Avoid unless you only care about a cool environment, which they certainly have.

This is currently my favorite restaurant in NYC! 

I love a tapas style sharing place concept because you get to try more things! For starters we had Tuna tostada, Cobia al pastor (white fish ceviche tacos) and Ayocte Bean salad. They were all sooo delicious and so fresh. We also had the Tlayuda (which is like a delicious salad pizza) Spelt equities (amazing!) and the steak tacos. It was all so delicious!!!! So fresh! So good! The drinks were also really good! I already have a reservation to go again!

The The food was creatively presented and most of it was delicious. The only true and terrible negative was the aweful hostess. As I walked it, was greeted by a sneer and then as my friend arrived and she gave another hostess a menu to seat us, she said "oh don't seat them, seat these guys first" in relation to another couple. Even if they were there first, which they were not, the way she handled it was just a way to diminish the customer. Which is a shame, because I would have otherwise come back.

aesthetically speaking, this restaurant looks like an apple store that sells fancy Mexican food. it's kinda cold and big with modern furniture that is fine for ppl who are fun-sized but not for anybody who is over 5'5". i was here for a work dinner, which i was jazzed up about bc that means mama ain't payin! im supes into treats from all over, but i hafta say for a pre-board mtg dinner, prolly not the best place to go. dishes are meant to be shared, portions are relatively small and like i said, the seating isn't ideal if youre a business person w a lot of girth. service was on point. good for a date w deep pockets or dinner w amigos!

My husband and I finally went to Cosme for dinner and what a great night / meal!! We love going to different restaurants with an open mind and trying as many dishes as we can!! Not to be missed items - the bean salad, the calamari, the duck carnitas, and the husk meringue. Not sure where some of the other reviewers were coming from regarding portion and price. Yes, it's expensive. But this place has three stars from the Times - so of course it's going to be pricy. We ordered five items including dessert and were stuffed!! Can't wait to go back!!

My 200th review!

Went for brunch and can happily recommend you do the same -- our party of four had one drink apiece, shared a ceviche appetizer and had four mains for about $150 plus tip, which seemed more than fair for the caliber of cooking and the surprisingly generous portions. Not sure I could say the same for dinner, where the same amount of food and drink would probably be substantially mas dinero, based on everything I've seen and heard.

The most memorable items were the Bloody Marias (never had such a fresh-tasting Bloody Mary before) and the wildly flavorful scratch-made tortillas (Pete Wells correctly said that "there are no tortillas remotely like this in New York").

Through and through, the ingredients were top-notch and the elements of each dish were very precise. My only real quibble was that some of the dishes were very similar - for example, the chilaquiles and the duck enchiladas both were essentially tortillas enveloped in a reddish-brown sauce and garnished with crema and onions. They just looked different. 

Anyway, a very fine, friendly restaurant overall and well worth visiting, at least for brunch or lunch.

Did a good job living up to seemingly insurmountable hype. I went in January 2016, so I was likely a year or so too late for the true craziness. 

Had a reservation for 9 PM. We didn't get seated until about 9:30. To soften the blow, they started us off with mix drinks on the house. Their drinks were delicious, so I quickly forgave them. 

I read the reviews, so I arrived expecting small, upscale-Manhattan-scale portions. When served, I was pleasantly surprised - small but not too small. 

I started with the burrata with salsa verde and "weeds." The flavor was mild (the salsa verde didn't have too much kick) but the texture was out of this world. I'm still not 100% sure what the "weeds" were but they perfectly complemented the burrata's gooiness. 

My main course was the duck carnitas. I love duck and I love carnitas. After this meal, I'd say that as a rule, duck carnitas are better than pork carnitas. It was phenomenal. A lot of reviews I've seen fault this dish for being "too greasy." If you've eaten duck before, you know that it's an inherently greasy bird. The preparation at Cosme did nothing to add to the greasiness and the provided fresh blue corn tortillas absorb it quite well. Best of all, this meal filled me up. Likely, had I ordered anything else, I would have left on an empty stomach. 

My girlfriend and I split two deserts: the celebrated (and frequently Instagrammed, guilty of this myself) corn husk merengue and the manchego popcorn cheesecake. The merengue was everything I hoped it would be. Like with the burrata, Enrique Olvera's textural mastery was in full display. The cheesecake, to my dismay, was another story. It tasted like passable cheesecake covered in Cheese Wiz and Smart Pop white cheddar popcorn. It's a shame that that was the last thing I ate. 

Overall, the highs far overshadowed the lows and I'm eager to return.
delicious. duck tacos is a MUST. everything was delicious. raw fish, uni dish, hand made corn tortillas.....

Cosme has a nice vibe albeit feeling a bit like an upscale office. Their menu has fairly authentic Mexican food (we had to google a lot!) but the egg white omelette, mole, and egg sopa were all nice dishes. 

It's a bit overpriced for what it is i.e. Not 'American' portions. But for a lighter fare brunch it's very nice. 

Cocktails are very strong - I tried the Paloma (grapefruit flavored) which was light and delicious, where as my friends had the bloody Marias which were quite strong and I've had better. 

Overall a nice hide out away from tourists in union square but not a must see. 

Side note: we did spot churros at another table and they look delicious!

Cosme has been on my list for quite some time, so with this NY trip I decided to just make it happen. I made reservations on open table a couple weeks in advance for 9pm on a Wednesday. 

Upon arrival, it was bustling. I checked in with a manager-type guy who didn't communicate to the hostess so I had to re-checkin at 9:20 but was then ushered to the seats. 

Our server Marco came over, took drink orders, answered a few questions, and offered up guacamole/chips while we decided. The tapas style menu was structured with meat/veg items on top, vegetarian items in the middle, and the "bigger" dishes at the bottom. 

SCOVILLE SOUR - Serrano infused Siete Leguas tequila with lemon, agave and garnished with a spiced cucumber. Not spicy. For my second, I had the guajillo-infused... Warmer. I probably should've opted for the Arbol straight off the bat, but why ruin a perfectly good cocktail with *too* much heat? 

UNI TOSTADA - I'm not a fan of uni. Never have been. When I saw that this was a top rated item I figured I'd try it. I had a bit with each component: the bone marrow salsa, avocado, julienne Serrano peppers, and cucumber, and I get it. It works beautifully. I just can't get past the uni; personal preference. If uni is your jam, get excited! 

BLUE SHRIMP a la VERACRUZANA - ceviche style with green and kalamata olives, avocado, yellow cherry tomatoes, drizzled with garlic oil. It was okay - but it wasn't bursting with any discernible flavor. Not a whole lot of Veracruzana happening in this dish. Certainly not $22 worth. 

BEEF TONGUE - carpaccio served with lettuce and a coffee oil and cactus. Tasty, but I've had better in San Jose. 

OCTOPUS - delightful. Crispy on the outside, tender on the inside, over a purée of some sort. 

DUCK CARNITAS - the reason people come here. They say it's serves two. If you're ordering other dishes, it'll go a lot farther than that. We ordered 2 ducks for the group of 6 and had left overs; should've only ordered one.  The server comes over and presents the whole breast and the proceeds to cut it up in front of you with instructions to douse with lime - total showmanship.  It was delicious, but not $69 delicious. 

Would I return? Probably not. Am I glad I went? Definitely.

Hmm.. Im not really a mexican cuisine kind of girl, but I was with friends that were. They seemed to agree with me that the food was either really good or just eh. The atmosphere was nice.

Out of everything we ordered, I enjoyed the lobster bisque--very rich and delicious.

Mexican is not my favorite cuisine at all, but it is the favorite of my dinner companion so I made reservations here for the other night after high recommendations from a very good friend.

First - the space was packed!  All the staff was very friendly, from the hostesses to the food runner.  Our waitress was fantastic, and I wish I remembered her name; she had black rimmed glasses, and I think multi-colored hair (it was dark so hard to tell).  She made amazing recommendations, and was on point with the ones that we went with.  

Because we had the duck carnitas, which is Cosme's signature dish, she advised only two more dishes max.  We went with the uni tostada and the mushroom and squash barbacoa.  So good!  We still ended up taking some of the duck carnitas home!

Finally for dessert, the husk meringue was recommended again.  She said this was their signature dessert and if we didn't like it, she would bring us anything else from the dessert menu.  WOW - that dessert was probably the most beautiful I've ever seen.  I rotated the plate a couple of times before digging in.  

I'd definitely like to go back to try more things out on the menu!!  Highly recommended!!  Thank you, Cosme, for the fantastic food and service!

Sat at the bar for a snack and drinks. The bar is super high and the seats are too! Don't pull a muscle climbing up and down the stools, though I almost did.

The bartenders were friendly and helpful.

I asked for a medium bodied wine and the bartenders recommended a glass of the Antigua Rioja ($16) and it was really delicious and exactly what I wanted.

The beef tongue ($24) was one of the best I've ever had. They sous-vide it so it's extra tender and season it very well. The blue shrimp ($22) was smoked but still raw and it was almost like having it sashimi style but with that extra smokiness. Really interesting and delicious flavors from both of these dishes!

I definitely want to go back for the duck carnitas!

A hip, trendy, modern vibe in here with dim lighting and clean lines in the decor. It's kind of loud both from the beating music and conversations.

The appetizer of blue corn tortilla and pumpkin seed salsa was tasty and a touch spicy. I liked it.

The raw fish with avocado and a little bit of basil was good, though not a favorite. The fish was cut a bit thick and the salt and pepper mix on top was rather salty.

The uni tostada was a small round blue corn tortilla chip topped with salsa, uni, and avocado. I really liked this one and would recommend it. The crunchy, lightly salty, creamy texture was excellent paired together.

The mussel tostada with chopped up pig feet meat and topped with about of romaine was okay. The taste of the spicy oil on it overwhelmed the whole dish. I didn't taste much mussel and the texture didn't work well for me.

The tyaluda reminded me of eating a salad on a large tortilla shell - the tortilla had black bean spread and it was piled high with cherry tomatoes, mixed salad leaves, baby radish slices, avocado, chincharrones, sliced jalapenos and a white cheese. It was a bit strange to me, I would opt out of this one.

The corn husk meringue was unique and quite good. The meringue was light, airy, and mildly sweet, it had some kind of filling inside, and some a salty cream on top. I recommend!

The caramel at the end was a nice touch.

Overall, the contemporary food here is interesting and worth trying. (The appetizers are pretty small and expensive though.)

The service was superb, the dishes were brought out one after another, and water glasses were constantly refilled. Waitress was friendly.

I would like to come back for the duck carnitas one day!

The food was hit-or-miss, but overall I think the experience was deserving of 3.5 stars thanks to the friendly service and cool ambience. 

Uni tostada - underwhelming. The smallish fried tortilla was very small and very pricey. Toppings are high-end but didn't deliver much in flavor or satisfaction. 
Scallops - very refreshing and light but I found it overly acidic. I liked the crunch of the jicama contrasted with the soft and mild sweetness of the scallops.
Mushroom and squash barbacoa - Mild textures and mild flavors - it could've been so much better! The portion was larger, enough to fill 4 tortillas. 
Duck carnitas: - amazing. A VERY hefty price tag but it was delicious and quite a large portion (fills 8-10 tortillas). Shred with your fork and get a good piece with both crispy skin and tender meat, then drizzle any or all sauces. 
Husk meringue: highly recommend! It's a very unique dessert yet also simple and unfussy. Delicate and airy meringue, milky and mildly sweetened mousse. Overall it's a really nicely balanced dessert. 

We thoroughly enjoyed the cocktails and the tortillas were memorably good, but many dishes were underwhelming. Still worth a visit if you're willing to spend $$$

While the guacamole disappointingly lacked flavor, everything else we ordered killed!

The uni app was amazing and had a liberal
Helping ! And can be easily chopped in half so you can justify spending $20 on one cracker of it. 

The raw fish app was also so good and fresh. My friends loved the scallops; I wish there was more of it. 

The mushroom tacos were delicious. The duck tacos were great too and could easily be shared amongst 4 people and not just two like they described.

Their desserts were incredibly creative. The meringue and cheesecake desserts had me sit up with flavor confusion at first and then I couldn't stop eating it.  

Our server was incredibly patient in answering all our questions. We overstayed our welcome at our table, and he wonderfully moved us to the bar area and offered us another round of cocktails on the restaurant, which was really above and beyond!

Cosme features "small plates" for sharing.   Small plates = big tab.  

What we ordered:  Scallop Aguachile ($21); Mushroom & Squash Barbacoa ($26); Enfrijolada ($20); Spelt Esquites ($17).   A basket of small tortillas was placed on our table, and the server explained they were to scoop or roll our food in.  

We ran out of tortillas before the food was gone, so my husband asked our server to please bring him 1 more tortilla.  One more tortilla!  The server said that was not possible.  Restaurant policy required us to purchase a whole extra order of tortillas.  They couldn't simply bring him one.  

My husband hit the ceiling.  He felt it demonstrated a miserly business model, showed a lack of hospitality, and was not concerned with the diner so much as maintaining the pretentious self-image of the restaurant.   

Including beverages our tab with tip was $229.  You'd think they could offer us the extra tortilla.

I'm sure they couldn't care less that we will neither return to nor recommend Cosme.
The cobia al pastor, duck carnitas, and husk merengue were all outstanding!!! I also had the Don Juan cocktail and it paired nicely with the carnitas. I wish I could eat like this all the time.

Nice space, both otherwise completely underwhelming. The food and service were average at best. We had the cobia al pastor and the NY strip. Any exciting flavors either may have had were suffocated by tortillas and guacamole that were seemingly pulled straight out of their respective containers from the grocery store. I actually wasn't surprised; the awkwardly giant bland tortilla chip that came out first was a sign.

For dessert, we had the cinnamon tamal. Glorified churro at best.

As for service, our waiter was nice, but seemed disinterested. The bus staff dropped a spoon with guac on my sleeve and offered a quick apology and a napkin.

I won't be back.

Underwhelming!

For any establishment that charges their tapas dishes at $20, the food should be spectacular. Alas, it is not.

I had really high expectations for this place, I ended up going for brunch. 
The mexican bread basket was really good.
The $18 huevos rancheros a total rip off. Nothing especial.
We also had the chilaquiles, very tasty, but also, for $18, I would expect the chicken to be a significant part of the dish and not just a mere topping.
The bread and the cocktails were the best part.
All in all, a rip off... the brunch experience didn't entice me to explore the dinner menu.

Really loved Cosme! 

The food is great : my favorite was def the duck for two and their famous dessert the husk meringue and corn mousse.
The Uni tostada was good but I;m getting a bit tired of the Uni trend.
The cocktails were pretty good as well.

Now the place is pretty large and the design is great but the tables are not the most comfortable. The place can also get pretty noisy and hard to get a reservation...

I was so hoping to love Cosme- it got excellent NYT and NY mag press, and I love Mexican food. 30 minutes late being seated for our reservation, really uncomfortable chairs, so loud I had to yell to be heard, and $70 duck carnitas. The $3 carnitas at Chelsea Market are better. Couldn't wait to leave, sadly.

Mexican cuisine, elevated to the next level. A bit on the pricey side, but some of the dishes were definitely worth it! I saw this restaurant featured on a TV show and figured, hey, why not try it out and see the hype of this husk meringue!?

I'll list what we ordered and also provide my opinion of each dish:
- uni tostada ($19) - super delicious, but such a small portion! I wish they had given more since it was just too good that I didn't want to finish it. I wish the uni was more intact since ours was a little on the mushy, untextured side, but it was still tasty.
- sliced raw fish ($24) - pretty yummy, aside from the fact that they used some citrus zest that kind of ruined each bite I took since it was a punch of bitterness I wasn't expecting! Without the zest, it would have been a really refreshing dish.
- scallop aguachile ($21) - this dish was the first one we tried, and the presentation is beautiful, but it's very underwhelming. There's a decent number of scallop slices in the dish, but the dominant flavor in this dish is the cucumber, which is already really light in flavor to begin with. I kind of wish we didn't order this because I don't think it was worth the price or room in my stomach D:
- cobia al pastor ($24) - I was not sure what cobia was, but looking at other Yelp photos, I wanted to try it. I ended up ordering it and then Googling it to find out it was a type of fish, and I was pleasantly surprised. It's a white-meat fish, and it was seared to a medium rare cook, with a pineapple puree. It was very different, but in a great way. I loved this!
- blue shrimp a la veracruzana ($22) - I don't know if this isn't done in Mexican culture, but most people who serve shrimp would de-vein them!! Ours clearly were not de-veined which was kind of aesthetically offputting, but the dish itself was alright in flavor, average but not amazing.
- black garlic rubbed NY strip for tacos ($35) - for $35, I was expecting more meat than what we got! The waiter told us it was about 3oz of meat, cooked to a medium rare. The steak was very tender and flavorful, so it made my wallet cry a little less haha. The avocado-tarragon puree just tasted like avocado to me, not too special. The steak was definitely the star of the dish, as it should be.
- duck carnitas ($69) - I was hesitant on getting this dish because of the price, but so many people reviewed Cosme and ordered this dish, so I had to at least try it right?? The duck breast was extremely tender and fall-off-the-bone (even though this was boneless) and flavored pretty well. We had a mild spicy sauce and a tomatillo sauce which went well when eating our DIY tortillas.
- husk meringue with corn mousse ($14) - this was the dish I came here for, the one I saw on TV and the one everyone raves about! I couldn't really imagine "husk-flavored" meringue, but NOW I KNOW! It has a really subtle "burnt" flavor from the burned corn husk, but overall it's pretty sweet with the corn mousse. I was a little disappointed at how little corn mousse there actually was, since the majority of the cream was actually whipped cream and the corn mousse just sat on top of that.
- manchego cheesecake with lemon tapioca, popcorn and chamomile ($14) - this was a mistake to get, maybe because I'm just not a fan of cheese. The cheesecake itself was great, but the popcorn just didn't really make sense, and there was a cheese-flavored "cream(?)" where the cake was sitting and it just punched me in the mouth, in a bad way. I did not like it, even when I combined the cheese with the cheesecake. I really tried to give it a chance, but I couldn't bring myself to enjoy this dish as a whole.

For future reference for anyone who wants to come, it's pretty difficult to get a reservation, and I made mine a MONTH in advance to get a 5:30pm dinner reservation on a Saturday evening. The waiters are very attentive, always check in to see how you're doing and to clean up your table when your dishes are finished, and they always fill your water!

Would I come here again? Perhaps! :)

Atmosphere is quite comfortable, modern.
I usually eat tiny amount, so the portion is ok for me. 
Had Cobia al pastor, seared white fish with pineapple puree.. very interesting, I like the slightly spicy taste to it but it only comes with 4 mini tortillas, even I could eat 6 pieces myself! 
Also had the bean salad, overly sour, the acidity takes over any other taste from fresh veggies and Ayocote beans...
Octopus was nicely grilled, crispy and watercress surprisingly matches.

Hostess was not so nice about my request of charging my phone because I didn't bring a charger with me,, (the entire restaurant only has ONE charger available in the office....) It was raining, I needed my phone to be charged to reserve Uber please.

Well, overall, the food quality is good but quite pricey. And service needs some warmth and improvement.

I was shocked to see some of the less than stellar reviews. I thought this place was amazing. We walked in on a busy Friday night without a reservation and were able to get a cute table in the bar area. Everything was delicious. The drinks were creative...not your typical margherita and michelada. The food was inventive, fresh and delicious. It was a little loud, but vibey. Sitting close to the door wasn't awesome since it was cold out and several people were walking in leaving the door ajar. We also had the corn husk dessert which sounded odd but was so yummy. I would highly recommend.

Overpriced, tasteless. Not worth the hype. Went for their brunch and food was mediocre at best. Was hoping that their churro would save the experience but was disappointed after taking a bite and it was way undercooked. Churro was doused in sugar and the inside was mushy, eggy, and unlike any churro I've tasted. Will not return again.
very hard to get reservations, but definitely worth trying the "day of" for cancelations. beautiful restaurant and delicious food. beet salad, duck tacos, and the flan were to die for.
Duck, buratta, raw fish with avocado and corn meringue.  Don't forget the mescal with pineapple.  That's all you need to know :)

There are much better places to spend $200+ on a meal for 2. Came here for dinner with a friend and ordered 6 small plates - SMALL being the operative word. The portions are almost comically tiny. We ordered: scallop, blue shrimp, uni tostada, enfrijola, burrata, mushroom and squash mash, manchego cheesecake, and corn meal meringue. I am not typically one to complain about portion size (to the contrary - I often split regular-sized dishes in half), but the mushroom and squash mash was the only dish that was even remotely filling (also the only dish I'd order again). After spending $225 on the meal (with no alcohol), my friend left and picked up a slice of pizza on the way out. Ambiance is nice but the dishes are not anything to write home about. I will not be returning.

Creativity is core to the gastronomic experience. The chef takes seemingly simple Mexican dishes and making them an inevitable delicious surprise. Taste the esquite dish the beats. The desserts are a must.

I was very excited to get a last minute reservation to cosme and the review is based on service, food, ambience and price point.

Service-excellent, v attentive and helpful

Food-duck carnitas with the fresh tortillas are a must have. Mushroom/squash were v tasty in a slightly spicy sauce, beets were fresh tasting, but nothing new. Meringue was incredible, so light and not super sweet.

Ambience- simple decor, nothing over the top, felt relaxed

Prices - egregiously expensive! ~$25 for each vegetable dish which was also a small portion, not sure how the restaurant is justifying that. Duck is a big portion, too big for two people if ordering other things, at 70 bucks, feels like there should be a half portion option.

Total bill was 250, for three dishes, three beers and two cocktails...

Would go back for a drink and dessert, not a full meal.

Visited this restaurant about a year ago. I was SHOCKED. The food was terrible, the service was painfully-slow and it was overpriced. I would recommend you take your date night elsewhere -- you'll be disappointed. Promise.

I was quite shocked when we got a last minute reservation to Cosme on a Friday, as the place is a hot spot. Unfortunately, the restaurant did not meet the expectations of a place that is so "hot". 

I understand this place is newer, but the service was not acceptable. The timing to which food was received was terrible. Between our first and second courses, there was an unusually long wait. I had to remind our server twice about drink re-orders. She had blamed the bar twice, but I could tell she had forgotten. You'd assume your want to serve as many $16 cocktails as possible. 

The food was good. I say good because we had an amazing Cobia dish (fish taco equivalent) that was fresh and flavorful, and a salacious beet and cheese dish. However the rest of the food was subpar and someone frustrating to accept as a $25 dish. 

Overall, Cosme isn't terrible, but frankly for the cost I don't see the point in recommending this restaurant when there are so many other places that are on point in NYC.

Good, not great. The space is nice. Good vibe. And the cocktails were really good. Especially the El Ninja. As for food, I thought almost everything was under-seasoned. The guacamole, for example, has the perfect texture but needed more salt, and more heat. The duck carnitas were great, but the onions could have been so much better if they were sautéed a bit, and the duck itself was a little dry and needed more seasoning. The cobia al pastor was a standout--perfect as is. All in all, it's a fun spot, and the food is good, but not worth the money and doesn't quite live up to the hype. Stop in for a cocktail and a cobia al pastor taco some afternoon you're in flatiron. Don't make this your Friday dinner plan.

This is barely 3 stars, but cognitive dissonance bumps it to 3 instead of what it really deserves which is 2. I went in so assured it would be great for NY mag and other media outlets gushing over it. Apparently most of the good reviews are for dinner and the lesser ones are for brunch. We, unfortunately went for brunch. 

The place is very sleek, modern, and trendy, but that's where the positive adjectives end. First of all, the prices for brunch and the portions are offensive.

Second the taste was underwhelming. The "chilaquilles" were basically 18$ subpar nachos you could get at a bad food serving sports bar. The chips were flavorless and it was covered in a green salsa that tastes as bad/good as a jar from trader joes. The flavor was completely one note, salsa verde without any depth or complexity, there was no contrast in texture as the chips were soggy, and the cheese and sour cream added nothing in the way of flavor. Worst of all the chicken was quite possibly boiled, as it came out completely without seasoning, utterly bland and stringy. It tasted like those Costco canned chicken breasts. 

My friend got a quesadilla, which thank god was only 6 or 8$ as it was half the size of a small plate (it was literally served on a coffee cup sized plate) and looked like something a drunk kid in college could make in a microwave in 3 minutes. There was absolutely zero flavor and texture. I was actually embarrassed for Taco Bell, as they represent Mexican food more respectfully. All in all, the food sucked and was not worth half what we paid.

We each had a cocktail which were decent and get that extra half star, but they're 16$. Honestly they're worth about 11$.

Don't go for brunch, maybe you'll have better luck at dinner.

Terrible food.

Let alone Mexican food. Reminiscent because they use avocado? This is offensive.

Quality is bad.

Technique of bad.

Bad ingredients with the fish and sea urchin.

Even the drinks weren't good. But who cares. I went for the food.

The price doesn't matter if the food is good. It is not good.

Consistently great! Been here 3x. All the cocktails are amazing! The best thing to eat is the duck carnitas - by far - and the corn husk dessert. Everything else was very good, but if you go you really can't miss those carnitas.

Wow! Went to Cosme today for a birthday brunch and had the most wonderful experience. The setting is beautiful, minimal but warm with a gorgeous bar int the front and dining in the back. Our server was polite and attentive and made helpful recommendations. We ended up ordering most of the items on the smallish brunch menu for our party of 4. Standouts were the seafood stuffed avocado, the chilaquiles (had the amazing complex red sauce and poached egg) and the quesadillas. The tortillas were handmade blue corn and excellent. My 9 year old daughter had the chilaquiles and says she loved the warm flavorful spicy sauce. We ordered both mushroom and epazote quesadillas (this came like an empanada), the latter which was slightly better (hard to find restaurants that actually use epazote). Overall loved the food and the service. Kudos also to the sweet bartender who made up a special birthday cocktail for my sister and then took the extra step of coming over to wish her a happy birthday!

This restaurant was outstanding. My fiancee and I went here the night we got engaged and it was just perfect. The cocktails are interesting and tasty and the food was delicious and filling. 

We had the uni tostada and the beets to start. Surprisingly, the beets outshone the tostada. The combination of the cheese, salsa, greens and beets made for a perfect bite. I think I may have licked the bowl. The ingredients on the tostada were great but I didn't feel that the tostada was the best mechanism for eating the uni, nor was it particularly flavorful. 

Our main course was the duck carnitas. We still talk about the duck carnitas and we went to Cosme 3 months ago. Just get them...and make sure you share them. We were both very full afterwards!

This place is tough to review because I really WANT to like it but it doesn't all come together. Servers are all over yet have 3 at your table causes confusion. We were brought side plates twice even though we didn't order sharing food, weren't served bread and I didn't even order a meal. The cappuccino was so so so good though so that was chosen well. The crowd is almost like you'd find in DC - creative older types in a quiet, zen like setting. You'd never guess by the name of the place. The menu is pretty limited and entree portions are tiny so I wouldn't go back to eat. The only thing I would like to try is the corn husk mousse dessert which wasn't available for brunch.

I am not totally sure I would call this fine dining, but I'm not totally sure I know what that means anymore. This is really delicious, comfort type Mexican food reimagined in delicious ways. This to me feels like what every New Yorker is always looking for. Unhealthy foods reimagined and rebranded as "fancy" so they can feel good about eating Burgers (Shake Shack) Cold Stone Creamery (Ample Hills) Mac and Cheese, BBQ, or any of the other myriad things that take hold here. The wine list is good, excellent if you compare it to other Mexican places, and the corn husk dessert thing is worth the trip alone.

Mexican.  Flat iron. 
Had a romantic dinner there Saturday night with my husband.  

We shared several small plates.  
The Scallops Aguachile were playfully presented.  The jimaca is cut to resemble scallops with the actual meat located below.  Light & tasty.

The Burrata & Ayacote Bean Salad came next.
Both were heartier (although still small plates) & delicious.  A nice play of texture & color.

We shared the Duck Carnitas for our entree.  Well cooked meat that shredded easily, served with tortillas.  Warm & filling.  Big portion.  (We had leftovers).

The clear winners for me were my Scoville Sour cocktail (spicy) & the Corn Husk Meringue dessert.  I can't rave about these two things enough.  I would go to the bar any day of the week and order a cocktail and dessert.

But does it live up to the hype?  One of the best/worst things about Cosme is the hype.  So many people go trying to either poke a hole in Pete Wells review or crown it the best food in the city.  I think Cosme deserves it's good press.  I'd recommend it with no reservation to an out of town visitor.

But I also think this city is filled with amazing dining experiences that are on or at least approach the level of food offered here.  I don't know I'd say for $200, this is the best restaurant in NYC.  I'd equate it to ABC Cocina... which is awesome, right?  But I'm not sure it's better dish after dish.  I'd certainly say the dessert at Cosme is perhaps my favorite I've had in a long time.  But otherwise it's a top tier restaurant worthy of the excitement you feel after scoring the elusive reservation.

Food is a low 4, but well-executed. However, while I don't mind high prices for quality, I've never felt as gouged by cost and small portions as I did here. $20-30 dishes that last two bites, are good but not amazing, and are not backed up by cost of ingredients. They seem to almost invite criticism. Lower your prices or raise your portions, because right now you're telling your customers that they're dumb and you're happy to rob them. Shameful.

For a restaurant that has received blessings from Pete Wells, and countless other critics, I was truly disappointed -- horrified even. Not only is everything true (pretty much nonexistent portions, extremely high prices, so-so service), but there really wasn't one singular dish that could have saved the overall dining experience in any way.

Our waiter was a little off-putting and borderline rude, which is not a deal breaker for me when it comes to reviews since we are in NYC, but his recommendations fell flat, and the fact that we ordered a variety of dishes and STILL left hungry was a nightmare. Add two rounds of not-so-great or potent cocktails on top of that and all we have is a fat check that leaves a bad taste in your mouth.

For reference, we had: uni tostada, scallops aguachile,, cobia al pastor, the chicharrón, and garlic rubbed steak for tacos.

ALSO, on the topic of our waiter. We were 200% certain we ordered the garlic rubbed NY steak NOT the duck carnitas (boyfriend can't eat duck). I even remember the waiter telling us it was 4 oz (ha!) of meat. We said it was alright and that we'd go for that dish. About 1.5 hours later, the duck carnitas arrived at our table, which we said were not ours. The busboy went back confused. Then, the waiter had the audacity to come back and tell us we did indeed order the duck and that was that. My boyfriend didn't raise his voice but politely said we did not, because he couldn't eat duck. The waiter gave us a nasty attitude about it and went back without saying a word. I saw him checking the monitor and alas, mystery solved. It was the table next to us who also happened to be an Asian couple -- maybe he just couldn't tell the difference, but really? He never apologized and just went on with his business, never checking up on us to ask if our food was okay after we received our correct order. There's no need for that sort of arrogance or snobbery.

The scene is trendy, vibrant, and sexy, but that's about it. There was nothing innovative or mindblowing about this place. So long, Cosme. Never again.

I wanted to like it so much...Cosme has a beautiful hip ambience wasted on average and overpriced food. Came for a group brunch and immediately impressed with the sleek, modern, and spacious interior, but found that wasn't enough to make up for the price - nearly forty for my entree and a shared dessert, no cocktails. I enjoyed my green chicken chilaquiles which the waiter recommended as one of the best two entrees alongside the duck empanildes...but they weren't unique from more moderately priced spots nearby. Caution against ordering the kale empanadas which the waiter warned as being very small on portion size. 

Added to the low vale...the service was very slow - it took 40 minutes until someone even came to take our orders and reminders to the waiters for other members of my party's to get their drinks. 

The one main highlight - the churros. Light, hot, crispy on the outside and soft on the inside all coated with delicious sugar and a melted chocolate sauce. If you are here, sweeten the rest of an otherwise average meal with this delicious dessert.

The entire place looked exactly how I would expect a fancy Mexican meal to be. Everything was hip and beautiful. Until... The food came out. Which is why we came here. Horrible portions and took every suggestion from the server and then the check comes out to almost a grand for six people?! Won't be back. Sucks because I had high hopes and plans of coming here for over a month

Terribly disappointed.  Sexy place but way overpriced. Took recommendations of "order two of this and two of that, two of the other" for our table of six. Wow, $975  later we went out for pizza afterwords. Won't return.

Came here for brunch on a Saturday afternoon with a few girlfriends.  I was absolutely STARVING -- Mistake #1.  I ordered the Egg sope which was the tiniest portion known to man -- Mitake #2.  I was still actually starving and wanting an entire burrito when I left.  My friend ordered the kale tamale which although very tasty, was SUPER tiny.  The Chilaquiles was the only dish with a decent portion and my friend said it was pretty good.  Service here also needs a bit of work, we asked for the check about 3 times before it finally arrived 15 minutes later.    

Come here if you are into the scene and trendy vibe, but not if you want a good satisfying meal.  There are enough mexican restaurants in NYC to satisfy your enchilada craving.

Some things you have to see to believe and we had to see the tiny portions at Cosme to truly believe it. Come here on an empty stomach and you'll be leaving with an empty wallet. That being said, with fine dining, value for money doesn't just come in portion size, it also comes in flavor, execution and atmosphere. Sadly, Cosme just didn't deliver on any front for us. 

Service was efficient. Seating was functional. Read between the lines on those descriptions. 

We found the much lauded duck carnitas were greasy ($69), our Scallop Aguachile was sandy ($21) and though the uni tostada ($19) tasted nice, the minuscule bite was over so quickly that we didn't even have the time to react. The NY strip ($35) was good but honestly, if you have a quality piece of meat, it's not exactly a technical feat to cook it well is it? The best part of the meal was the cobia al pastor which had great flavor and was accented by the surprising tang of pineapple. It was the sole dish we felt actually lived up to the praise so often heaped on this restaurant. 

For dessert we went for the famed corn husk meringue which was pleasant but not something I would crave to have again. There was also a disappointing chocolate confectionery that's best forgotten. 

Our friends were treating us to the meal and usually the best way to make people overlook imperfections is to make something free but even with that, it was hard to rate the meal too far above mediocre.

This has got to be Mexican food for the upper east siders. Brunch was great but I want to start by saying that serving non dairy milk should have been an option available to me. 

I ordered the red chilaquiles and I was very happy with my choice. My friends ordered the kale tamal and the egg sope. Though the dishes taste great, the portions are very small. An average of $15 for a three bite size plate. The servers should advise a table that they might be looking for a burrito after they sign the check because the dishes couldn't even satisfy an appetizer.

I'm optimistic about coming back for dinner because each dish really did taste great. SERVICE NEEDS A LOT OF WORK.

Absolutely loved my meal here. Don't usually love Mexican but this was fine dining with unique takes on traditional food and it was AMAZING. The restaurant itself is very pretty - modern, dimly lit, and trendy. 

My boyfriend and I started out with the Cobia al pastor, the octopus, the burrata and the guacamole. The cobia was unreal. It was a type of white fish that I had never experienced before. The others were good as well. Then we shared the NY Strip Tacos which were delicious. I hate when steak is too chewy and this was not the case. For dessert, we shared this unreal corn husk meringue which you must get. It was so unusual and it was tragic when the dessert was over. 

This is a solid restaurant in flatiron and I can't wait to come back!

Good, but not as good as some of the reviews or the New York Times would suggest.

The duck, while extremely well-made, did not have enough flavor to justify the convoluted cooking/seasoning process. The corn tortillas, however, were splendid.

The corn meringue and oatmeal ice cream were delicious and wonderfully light desserts. The beet flan had perfect consistency, but unfortunately tasted exactly like Werther's caramel candies.

The most memorable part of the meal for me was the salsa given with the chips at the beginning of the meal - strangely it had a strong aftertaste of chicharrones. The waitress said it was made with lots of greens, and I promptly spent the rest of the meal wondering where the taste of pork rinds came from.

MUST GET THE DUCK CARNITAS!
it almost behaves like pulled pork
make sure you scrape the bottom of the cast iron skillet because there r bits of flavourful fatties that you wanna get in your tortilla
this duck carnitas moment was like a mexican peking duck meal
quite nice.
i would skip that tortilla chip pizza...meh*
burratta - good
bean salad  -good
uni bone marrow app - GET IIIIIIIT
for fun sure - the merengue dessert - it was good 

overall get duck carnitas & uni
must must muuust
One of the best restaurants I have ever been to! I went with some Mexican friends and they said it was a fantastic restaurant! Truly recommendable!

Very lively and great New York scene. Despite having reservations we had to wait nearly an hour to be seated. It was raining and hostess failed to be accommodating and take our coats. I was going to give a 1 star review however once we were seated the manager was accommodating and service was excellent. Overall good was very good, especially duck. Great cocktails as well.

Delicious, creative and very cool version of Mexican food. We tried and loved: enfrijoladas (loved the hoja santa taste), the uni tostada, the octopus, the tlayuda, and loved (even more) the desserts including the pumpkin nixtamalizado and the merengue. Both had unexpected and delicious looks and flavor. For drinks we loved the telenovela, striptease, Paloma and a Margarita. Totally coming back to try more!

Don't waste your time or money. Place has a nice atmosphere so maybe go there for drinks. Dont bother ordering any food. everything was bland and over priced. dont understand the hype over this place.  duck carnitas decent def not worth the 69 dollars. prob the only thing memorable was the corn husk merengue.

Had a birthday dinner with a friend at Cosme and it was lovely.  The restaurant has a trendy/busy vibe, staff was friendly and helpful.  We could only get a very early reservation -- 5:30 and then due to a little travel mistiming got there even earlier at 5:15.  Although not technically open yet, they let us sit at the bar and order drinks to wait.  Drinks are not cheap but my cocktail (Cuba) was delicious and pretty good sized.  Once seated we reviewed the menu and decided to share both the beet salad and the duck carnitas.  And we started with some guacamole -- which had a wonderful light fluffy texture and a great uncomplicated fresh flavor.   The beet salad with farmer cheese was off the hook yummy.
