And the duck carnitas are  completely worth the asking price.  In both dishes the flavors were wonderful, with depth and complexity -- but they still felt simple and straightforward.  We are looking forward to going back to try more on the menu

I am astounded that this restaurant attracts a crowd.  It is essentially insanely overpriced for what it is and the portions will make you laugh.  The chef has a propensity to dress everything with cilantro and cucumbers.  The food itself was not at all flavorful and the wine list starts at 45 (only 2 bottles to choose from) and quickly escalates from there.  I've eaten at restaurants around the world.  Whether they were trendy or not, this is the only restaurant I've ever eaten in where I felt i would have been better off just burning my money.

December 18 dinner started bad we almost left before we even ordered, the waiter was so rude and pretentious! He had such an arrogant attitude that alone ruins ur evening! The food was so minimal and expensive u leave hungry and spent a fortune and I'm not one that needs large portions! The raw fish served with a tortilla was lost, all u can taste is a tortilla! Not the delicate fish. The waiter hardly came around the bus servers were actually waiting on us. We only had one drink the 1.30hrs we were there because he never returned! The only thing I would return back here for would b their merengue dessert that was delicious! Otherwise their food doesn't meet the hype! Flavor got lost in the artsy part!

This place is beautiful but doesn't generate enough warmth or true elegance to cover up the strip club history.

Cosme requires everyone present to be seated and getting my girls anyplace on time is like herding kittens. A bunch of guys bought us drinks. While I was appreciative and even with that said, the whole vibe was a little heavy GTL / Ashley Madison chic. 

We were a large party and ordered most items on the menu.

The highlight was the duck carnitas tacos. However even that was nothing special. Just a fatty confit like duck with a few tortillas. I just don't get it. Inauthentic food, micro portions and a somewhat cool vibe. 

The escolar was gross. Mushrooms boring. I left hungry and sober and for about $125 per person for drinks and dinner - not worth it.

We went for brunch, and the food was really good. However, the service was slow and brusk, almost rude when we asked for refills on coffee, for example. We waited about 20 minutes to put in a drink order and another 15 to receive coffee and tea. Our food service was also slow, and one dish was forgotten. Good menu, but will not recommend or return.

Love the decor of the restaurant! We came as a group for a celebratory dinner and we were seated after our whole party was here. The presentation was fun and thoughtful. The service was attentive and detail oriented. I was very expectant to try to their duck, however, it didn't have the wow factor like the reviews. The blue shrimp was my favorite! Would totally recommend getting the shrimp and scallop if you're a seafood lover!

I really wanted to like this place.  It has everything going for it; well designed space, a good crowd, a world-renowned chef at the helm and then this happens...

- 45 min wait for a table despite having reservations
- a forgotten entree
- ordering dessert from the host/ floor manager b/c a server isn't around in a 3/4 empty dining room.

The worst of all: overcharging on drinks and food.  That's thievery from customers!  Shameful.  

I'm disappointed, very disappointed.  Enrique Olvera is one of the best chefs in the world and to be connected to a restaurant that cannot charge correctly and match the prices set on their menu is amateur at best, stealing at worst. 

Cosme has been open for over a year. Bad service and incompetence shouldn't happen after a year of operation.

1 star for food.  The food is tasty especially the duck carnitas (my overcharged entree) and the meringue.  Negative stars for bad service and overcharging customers.  

To be fair, the staff is nice and pleasant but being nice and pleasant doesn't give  a pass to the issues experienced at a restaurant of this caliber. 

So people if you decide to eat here, check your receipt and make sure it lines up with their menu prices.

Couldn't be more overrated. Maybe we just ordered the wrong things. For reference, we had the guacamole, cobia al pastor, enfrijolada, and the garlic rubbed ny strip tacos. The guacamole was the highlight and it was nearly flavorless. I could go into details about each dish, but suffice it to say that they all lacked flavor, were absolutely nothing spectacular, and in the case of the steak it was visually and texturally unappealing and looked like it had been sitting for a while and was slightly below lukewarm. I can't believe that this restaurant is so lauded for being one of the only good Mexican options in NYC. To summarize...nothing special, flavorless dishes, and way way overpriced ($120 for 4 small dishes without drinks). Terrible!

Overall: not worth the $$$

Atmosphere: trendy, good for groups and high energy

Service: average

Food:  food is good, fresh, portions are small and price is very very high!

Ordered the Uni which was delicious, well put together

Fresh scallop: very fresh, just wish is a larger portion for the price!

Octopus: was tasty, but nothing special ...for $26 should have been more substantial 

Corn meringue: very light, good balance not too sweet

Walked out still a little hungry :-(

I went to Cosme this week with out of town friends. We ordered a broad sampling of all the highly recommended dishes and found them uniformly disappointing. Beside the fact that the portions, with the exception of the duck, are obscenely small, all the dishes we sampled were absolutely without taste. Had the very helpful waiter not explained what we were eating, I am not sure I could have identified any of the dishes. I understand that Cosme offers "haute" Mexican cuisine, but I could detect absolutely no connection to anything remotely Mexican that I have ever eaten. I am completely mystified by the positive reviews this restaurant has received in the press and on Yelp. I cannot recall ever being so disappointed by such a well-reviewed restaurant. I agree with one of the earlier posts that predicted that Cosme won't be around in a year.
I have never before written a Yelp review, but my after my experience at Cosme, I felt I simply had to speak up. Be fore-warned...

Duck duck duck duck duck.  OK we loved the duck carnitas.  At $69.00 per serving an entree had better be good.  And it was...falling off the bone, swimming in fat and tender, OMG it's so tender.  And the portion was big enough to take some home for lunch the next day.

While the other dishes were good, they were, as the other reviews all say, very very small.  And while the prices for these dishes were not $69.00 there wasn't much value per portion size no matter how delicious they were.  They were, crispy octopus, with a hazelnut mole and pickled potatoes, and watercress - $29.00 dollars and only one tentacle.  And an uni tostada, with avocado, bone marrow salsa, and cucumber.  So small that sharing it seemed like my wife and I were in one of those war movies where the survivors of a siege are making their food last as long as possible.  It was delicious, but very very small - $19.00.

Mexican wine...Hmmm we ordered it because we'd never had Mexican wine and it was pretty good, but $18.00 per glass (and not the most generous pour), is kinda pricey too.

Service was professional and attentive.

Get the duck for an almost life changing experience, but if duck's not your thing, not really a place to eat.

This place is expensive but somewhere you have to visit at least once. The duck was delicious and the husk meringue was out of this world. It was crowded but you're there for the food more than the ambience.

I came here on a Friday night with a girlfriend to do some long overdue catching up. Unfortunately, the place was so loud we struggled a bit with the conversation. Each small dish that is brought out is explained by a waiter. We were both unable to hear the majority of what was said in the explanation. It was a trendy place. Cool atmosphere. Way too pricey for my liking. Portions were very tiny. I will not be coming back.

I do not understand how anyone could think that this is a great restaurant. We were taken here by good friends and although we had a great time with them, I would have rather they spent their $$ elsewhere.
The space is nice and the service was good (although not at these prices), but the portion sizes (tiny), prices (laughable) and food itself was extremely disappointing. I do not mind (and do so very often) spending a lot of $$, but to leave hungry and not even like what I ate (or be unsure of) is really bad. We ordered about half of all the items on the menu, so I think I can fairly say, as a person who has dined in the best and most popular established restaurants, this place will NOT last and whatever hype exists now, will soon fade. Also, the pours on all alcohol is extremely poor.....$16+ glass for a glass of wine, one should get a "nice/respectable" pour. Same goes with all the drinks we ordered. The pours were tiny. We will not be back and would not understand who would go back for dinner more than once.

This is the place to go to for authentic Mexican food. Finally a restaurant in Ny that offers more than your typical tex-mex style menu! If you've never heard of chef Enrique Olvera, look him up. His restaurant Pujol is on the top 50 list and Cosme (his NY outpost) is just as delicious and inventive without any of the pretense and at a much more reasonable price. If that doesn't get you there, there wine and mezcal list should!

the lobster and corn creation was AMAZING. sat at the bar with a friend for dinner, the bar stools are insanely high, so warning to ladies wearing high heels and or a skirt, do not attempt to hoist yourself onto bar stool. beyond that, service was attentive, the PALOMA cocktail was wonderful. the corn mousse for dessert was lovely. all food was superb

Food: 2-3
Ambiance: 4
Service: 5

Nicely decorated restaurant, but the most boring Mexican food I've ever had.  I guess I prefer street and mid-range Mexican fare to this overpriced, upscale stuff.  (Where's the chips and guac?!?)  

We ordered the radish salad and some fish entrees.  The ingredients tasted fresh, but the dishes were underwhelming.  I loved our amiable server though!

The multi-stall BRs are located downstairs in the back.  Separate multi-stall BRs for men vs women, but they uncomfortably share sinks and mirrors.  That's never a good idea.  His and hers bathrooms are a thing for a reason...

I'm sure the hostess thought we were auditioning for a sketch comedy show. The three of us approached the stand a few minutes after 10. I wasn't sure which name our table was under, but then my friends informed me they thought that I had made the reservation. There was no reservation. 

Thankfully it was 10:10 on a Wednesday evening and we were seated right away. Dinner moved along at a nice clip, so even with a complimentary corn starter, a cocktail and six plates divided into two presentations, we were done by 11:35. I appreciated this, being someone who doesn't like being out that late on worknights. 

Even though our waiter left halfway through the meal, the service was seamless. In this small plates culture, it's unclear how annoying it is for dishes to come at random intervals into you have a meal where the plating actually makes sense.

We were warned about Cosme's relatively small portions and noshed on some cheaper food around the corner with an early pint. It turned out to be a good decision. For the food is not generously proportioned. Realistically I think you'd need to add the duck carnitas to make it a full meal. With adequate insight, it was fine. 

The food was well-executed as expected. Particular favorites were the burrata with salsa verde and weeds and the eggplants with blue corn tortillas. The long strand of octopus was elegant to look at, but probably would have been better with char rather than fried. The al pastor dish made me wish I was eating an actual pork al pastor taco rather than this fussy version. Everything else was surprising and worthwhile. 

For an elegant, somewhat special eating experience, Cosme definitely fits the bill. And with cocktails the same price as they are everywhere else in the city - $15 - and the atmosphere great, this would be a great stop for a drink as part of a longer evening.

Some dishes are really good while some are so so. The blue shrimp dish was excellent. But the guacamole lacked acid. I had the roasted pumpkin dessert which is served with cream cheese and oatmeal ice cream - it is good but the oatmeal ice cream had no oatmeal taste

I had dinner here this evening and I really enjoyed the dining experience.  The waitstaff was attentive and the environment was cool.  On to my review of the food.

Uni Tostada
I am a big fan of uni, but this dish didn't do it for me.  It was different than anything I've had before, but it just didn't come together.  My girlfriend liked it though.

Mussel Tostada
I loved the flavors in this dish and textures.

Buratta 
Very tasty with the salsa

Cobia al pastor
I really liked this fish version of a dish that normally is made with pork

Duck Carnitas
Amazing....

Corn meringue
Strong corn flavor, interesting, special

Lots of very small plates...need to order 4 dished just to be satisfied.
The flavors were average, nothing special here.

Wonderful experience here. I was worried after reading some of the reviews but the service was not pretentious at all. Ordered too much food, ended up feeling terrible from overeating (the tortillas that come with the duck carnitas tend to expand in your stomach), but I tend to do that when the food is that good. The much-hyped corn husk meringue is out of this world.

My only regret is not drinking more sherry. The cocktails were excellent but you can get good cocktails anywhere. A good sherry list is something you don't see every day, at least not in this city.
Very intriguing menu. Everything was super-tasty, including the Paloma cocktail! Loved the Cobia al Pastor, Uni tostada, and duck Carnitas for 2. Will be back!

I loved this place. It actually stood out among all the hyped up NYC restaurants I've been to and is the first to impress me in a while. Went for brunch and arrived early for our reservation but were seated right away. Ordered the stuffed avocado which was basically an avocado cut in half with seafood ceviche served in the hollow. Simple and delicious! We also got the chicken chilaquiles because the girls next to use ordered it and if we didn't also get it, we would have had food envy. They did not disappoint. Had a bit of kick and the chips inside were still crunchy despite being drenched in salsa. The chicken was tender and tasty. The waiter also recommended the egg chilaquiles which I will happily return and try next time. Finally, we got the corn johnny cakes which were basically corn pancakes. They had a little bit of a corn kernel texture and were light and not heavily flavored. It was a nice compliment to the chilaquiles. I also got the pina para la nina agua and thought it tasted just like a sweet fruit juice. I'd probably skip it next time. Nothing too special about it but it wasn't bad either!

Service was excellent - no complaints. Waiter made recommendations upon request and was helpful with the menu. Ambience was your typical nice NYC restaurant. Neutral decor.

What a great place for dinner! I went to Cosme the other day with my friend for her birthday and it was such a good choice. We had a reservation for 8pm and were seated immediately. The server was very knowledgeable and friendly and made some great recommendations.

We ordered the Uni Tostada, Roasted Eggplant, Burrata, Steak Tacos and Guacamole and it was all fabulous! I definitely need to go back to try the rest of the menu.

The vibe of the place was great. It was very trendy but very comfortable at the same time. I will definitely be recommending this place!

Let's get this fact out of the way: Cosme's food is as delicious as you'd imagine given the hype surrounding this place.  But a restaurant this ambitious should have service to match. Cosme does not.

My party dined at 5:30 on a Saturday, so the restaurant was mostly empty. We ordered a bottle of red wine. The server brought the bottle and offered a taste. After pouring each of us our first glass, the server placed the bottle in the middle of the table, turned to leave, and KNOCKED THE BOTTLE OVER, spilling it onto the table and my wife's designer leather purse in the empty fourth chair!

The spill caused an immediate reaction from the wait staff. The spilled bottle was removed, napkins placed over the spilled wine, and my wife's purse taken from the chair and dried off. So far, so good. Everyone makes mistakes, and Cosme seemed to handle this one quickly and efficiently. 

The waiter brought a new bottle and apologized for causing the spill. My wife's purse had a red wine stain near the handle, but luckily it had been closed so nothing inside was destroyed. We did not receive a visit from the manager on duty, but we figured that at some point the manager would come over to discuss the purse and the spill. That never happened.

When the check came at the end of the night, it was presented without comment or a renewed apology for the spill. I was surprised that nobody had come to check on my wife's purse or discuss the incident with our table. Worse, there was no consideration in the check for the spilled bottle of wine or the damaged purse. Not even a note from the manager saying "Come back again and your meal/wine and dessert is on the house."

I can't imagine Eleven Madison Park or Le Bernadin ignoring a server's damage to the customer's property. Cosme apparently believes that it's good service to pretend nothing happened and hope that the customer doesn't demand compensation or leave a negative review. 

We were intensely disappointed with our experience.

Had dinner with my friends last night and it was great. Tried the spicy cucumber cocktails which were so delicious some of the best cocktails I've had. We then shared the raw fish, scallops, burrata and had the duck tacos for main and each dish was spectacular. Dessert was amazing too I tried the lemon mousse and friends got the pumpkin dish. Loved mine was v fresh and light. There's not one thing I wouldn't order again. Service was great and I loved the atmosphere. Can't wait to go back

Trendy restaurants in Manhattan many times do not live up to the hype but in the case of Cosme, it does.  It is a winner as far as I'm concerned.  Some of the portions may be a tad small for the price but each dish is carefully crafted and presented and the dishes are extremely flavorful.  The staff won me over.  As a single diner, one is often overlooked, but I experienced genuine care and cheerfulness and attention to details.  I loved my waiter Miguel and the busboys were equally kind and attentive.  The brunch menu is quite different from other brunches in the city with many unique dishes.  The huevos rancheros were unlike any other and prepared very much like a soup.   But the flavors were perfect.  The slice striped bass was refreshing and fresh.  The churros were amazing with Mexican chocolate.  I will return to try dinner one day.   Kudos to all the staff!  Great place to try!

The hype is real.  Come for the corn husk merengue and duck carnitas.  Order the La Paloma cocktail and ask to be seated with Stacy, she was fantastic.  None of the other dishes we tried blew us away; uni tostada, cobia, eggplant or octopus.  They weren't bad, but I wouldn't write home about them either.  Excited to come back and try their brunch menu.

I was expecting to be "Wow'd",my food the steak tacos were good,my drink the Paloma was delicious, but our waiter was awful.  He barely explained  the menu. He didn't seem happy  to there. He brought  us way dishes  after they brought  out a complimentary  tortillas, our water was warmish. He seemed abrupt with  us. Not sure if I would  come back.

I'm all for this modern/high-end Mexican trend and was excited to try Cosme for the first time.
Modern and darkish space with a large bar up front and seating in the back. Space for largish groups it seems. The night we were there had a whole mix of folks: tourists, families with kids, date night couples, neighborhood locals dining out. The waitstaff were knowledgeable and helpful when it came to the menu. We did the uni tostada (looked great but I though the uni was lost in the vibrant flavors), cobia al pastor (yum), crispy octopus (was it too crispy? maybe), and a few other items but I can't seem to recall them because I was eating dinner and drinking wine and enjoying the company of my lovely spouse.
Blue corn tortillas. I remember those from the cobia (right?). Those were great.
I will note, as a former-somewhat-pro-photographer, that others have mentioned that the light is good if you have to photograph your food. I agree. Nice little spot lights on each table.
Large wine list with a good selection.
Dessert was solid. We had multiple items and for the life of me I can't recall what they were. But we licked the plates clean.

Went for brunch with husband and really liked it. Will have to come back for dinner.
The decor reminds me a lot of Hotel Americano: clean, simple, light wood table, mordern furniture. Mexican influence into a clean and modern space and the menu is the same. You will find some traditional good dishes but revisited in terms of presenation and some of the ingridients. It is very tasty and feel much healthier than your traditionnal Mexican dishes.
My highlights: the agua fresca with liquor, chilaquiles and kale tamal.
The only down fall was that we arrived around 11:30am so at the begining of the brunch service and they were out of some interesting items on the menu like the razor clams. You can't start the service and have already some 86 so needs to work on that in my opinion.
And while you there, don't forget to check out the restrooms. I really loved the decor.

The food was delicious and the server was quite helpful. However, we were celebrating a milestone birthday and I told the host that when we got there. She told me that they had a special dessert. It sounded great


When dessert time came, the server forgot to do anything for it. Ok, mistakes happen. Particularly when the restaurant is understaffed as this one seems to be. 

So I went to the host and explained what happened. She remembered my telling her and told me that she had told the server. I asked whether there was anything they could do. She refused to do anything. I was rather incredulous but also didn't want to cause a scene. It's too bad. It's a very simple fix to offer a free drink or dessert. 

The understaffing shows itself in minor ways - drinks coming later than food courses, etc.
Not sure what all the hype is about.  The food is so-so and the service isn't great. Save your money and go somewhere else!

Hands down, the best mexican/fusion restaurant in this city. Duck carnitas are a MUST. The sliced raw fish was also out of this world.. I wish there were more pieces in the dish because it was amazing!! The octopus and burrata were also great, so I recommend ordering all these dishes to the center and sharing them.. Its the best way to taste all of them. Order the corn 
Merengue for last.. Enrique Olvera did a great job.. Cannot complain and will keep coming back any time I can!

Amazing selection of Tequila's. Lovely staff and the food was playful and adventurous. Best plates in our party were the Uni and Bone Marrow Tostada, the Duck Tacos and the Lemon Mousse with Avocado Dessert

Having had some fabulous meals in Mexico City, Monterrey ..... I was excited but skeptical. 

Chef Enrique did not disappoint. Each dish was unique, flavorful and just delicious!

To top it all, General Manager Gonzalo, helped us experience tequila just like we do it in Napa. Well we do it with wine in Napa and Gonzalo was awesome helping us experience food and tequila perfectly paired.

This just became my favorite Mexican cuisine experience. Muchas Gracias Gonzalo for the experience and Chef Olvera for the incredible cuisine!

Enrique Olvera is a culinary genius! He elevates the Mexican Cuisine to a place just dreamed by others. The complexity of the flavors on each bite, the masterful presentation and the perfect marriage of all ingredients make each item on the menu a masterpiece by itself. This is a restaurant for foodies that can appreciate the fundamentals of cooking perfectly executed and that are willing to embark into a culinary journey of flavors that are bold, balanced and border line orgasmic. In this foodie paradise elements like sour cream, melted American Cheese and ground beef shell tacos are condemned to culinary hell.

My personal favorites are the scallop aguachile, the Uni tostada and the crispy octopus.

Among the most ridiculously overpriced places I've eaten in NYC. Portions are TINY. This is a really bad place to go with a group as each dish only has a few bites. If they didn't continue to bring tons of tortillas (ok, those were pretty good), everyone would leave starving. I had read the yelp reviews and expected small portions, but not THIS small. We ordered a ton of stuff for a party of 4:
Guac ($9) - was solid. That's table stakes and good guac is a dime a dozen. 
Uni tostada ($18) - pretty tasty, but way too small. Couldn't be shared for the table.
Cobia ($24) - fish itself was delicious, but portion was insanely tiny. It was suggested to make tacos out of it, but there was hardly even enough fish to fill one taco and it wasn't served with any accoutrements to fill it up
Raw blue shrimp ($21) - couldn't find the shrimp! seriously.
Beets ($17) - not going to complain about the portion size on this one, just that it had no flavor.
Burrata ($25) - again, only served ~1.5 bites each
Duck Carnitas ($59) - this was very yummy and the portion was big. But maybe not big for $59. And any normal sized portion looked massive after being served all of these other tiny dishes. 

Two positive notes. Cocktails were really good. Also, hostess staff was really professional. We had a reservation but had to wait ~45 minutes for our table. They were extremely gracious and offered us free drinks and guac. We didn't have to complain or anything, they proactively did this, which was really refreshing.

Being from Texas with family from Mexico, we know Hispanic and Latin food, and everything we tried ranged from great to awesome. The house made cocktails were outstanding, the vibe was perfect for a brunch on a beautiful day, and the music was just right. The Chilaquiles were excellent and duck enmoladas were great. We also really enjoyed the corn Johnny cakes. This is a great brunch spot.

Absolutely delicious food.  Unusual, yet simple and comforting at the same time.  The duck is not to be missed, and same for the corn husk dessert. We loved everything that we ate, and fabulous cocktails as well.  This is upscale dining with a modern and cool vibe.

My (Chef) boyfriend and I walked into Cosme incredibly excited to eat after reading great reviews and waiting a month to get a reservation.  Our mouths watered as we read through the menu but I wish someone would have stopped us there because we ended up unsatisfied, disappointed and 350 dollars poorer.  

Our "culinary" experience started with the guacamole which, was in fact, not guacamole at all but $13 mashed up avocados with no flavor, lime or salt.  We exchanged nervous glances as we knew this was not a good start.  We were right.  The remainder of the meal followed suite.  

Stick to drinks and dessert here as they are the only things worth your money.  As a culinary school graduate myself who studied and worked in pastry I can confidently say these are some of the most creative and well executed desserts I've ever tasted.

I was really excited to try Cosme, and while the food was good (though not great), the service was so appallingly bad that it ruined the experience. We ended up waiting an hour and a half for our main courses...it was only an hour into the wait that our server stopped by to apologize and offer us a comped appetizer, which we declined because at that point we just wanted the food we'd ordered. Later the manager stopped by with a beer for my husband (also declined, because he had a full beer sitting in front of him), though strangely no offer to me for a drink even though I was sitting there with an empty glass. The duck carnitas and rib eye we'd ordered were good, when they finally arrived, though my judgement was probably clouded by starvation at that point. They did give us a comped dessert to go at the end of the meal, which I suppose was nice, but it just ended up feeling like they were trying to make up for a horrible experience in the cheapest way possible (really, offering a comped beer as compensation for a 1.5 hour wait?). So, so disappointing.

Back when Cosme was in soft-open stage, a little birdie told me that they weren't yet taking reservations, but that the restaurant was empty every night and you could just walk in. At the same time, I watched the foodie internet orgasming over the fact that the reservations module on Cosme's website was showing no availability for the next two months.

That's because it literally wasn't functioning yet, doofuses.

Cosme just started their brunch service a few months ago - the most dangerous meal, in terms of sheer potential to be sucked into a void of poached eggs and hollandaise. But Cosme and all its hyper-conscious Mexicanness seriously shone. 

- Caviar - the blue corn tortillas that came with this appetizer were so good, I feel bad underappreciating the caviar itself. I'm not sure the caviar plus that rustic tortilla worked very well. Separately, it was all delightful - though $62 is steep for what you're getting.

- Quesadillas - we ordered the mushroom filled ones. Tasty, but again, the star is the tortilla they use! Such great corn flavor.

- Duck enmoladas - the duck was fantastically tender. The mole was rich and smooth and complex - one of those foods you could eat on multiple different occasions and notice something different about each time.

- Chilaquiles - again, wtf tortillas are these and how do they have such perfect texture. Even though the tortillas had been sitting in salsa verde for several minutes by the time we got to them, they were still fantastic. Even if you're like me and you harbor a deep love for the $8 chilaquiles at your local Mexican place.

- Enfrijolada - stupid good, and one of the most interesting things on the table. Black bean puree is layered with tortilla, hoja santa (sacred leaf), creme fraiche and ricotta to form an artful dish that tastes satisfying and humble, but also weirdly elegant. 

- Johnnycakes - not Mexican, last I checked! But of course they make these with Mexican yellow corn and hold up now I'm suddenly beginning to realize that our entire meal was probably gluten-free by happenstance. The johnnycakes came with rhubarb compote and syrup, kind of like a mini breakfast with which to end your meal. The rhubarb was fantastic. 

What else?
- The beer they use for their micheladas (Damiana) is sourced especially for that purpose. It's a Mexican corn-based beer that's mellow and vaguely citrusy and served at the exact perfect temperature (if you want it by itself).
- The michelada itself is great, spicier and crisper than any I've had. Also, served by a very cute Korean-Mexican bartender.
- Even the coffee is imported straight from Mexico. It's on the sourer side for my taste, but served in teacups that look like soup bowls, and they are attentive with refills. 
- I sipped my friend's agua fresca and it was fantastic.

Combine all this with a restaurant with absolutely beautiful decor details, from seat cushions that are just the right amount of cushiness for yo tushiness (sorry) to fresh flowers at every table. It's far from a cheap meal, but the conscientiousness and care they take in creating your food is obvious, and the flavors convey passion and pride.
The meal was phenomenal from start to finish! I would say the duck carnitas is the dish to try here. The meat is cooked to perfection and is too good for words!

I can't say enough good things about Cosme.  FINALLY a Mexican restaurant in NYC from a chef with real expertise in Mexican cuisine.  The service was top notch and every dish we had was delicious.  The flavors and creativity made the whole dinner really enjoyable.  I wish they bottled all the different salsas and sauces we tried -- I would buy all of them!  Definitely planning to go back so we can try different dishes.

I was so hoping to love this restaurant.  It was not even a thought in my head I would not.  There is only one nice thing I can say about it, and that is that it is a very attractive space.

I thought the food was close to awful.   Everything just was off, too acidic, or sour.   I was shocked.   I thought perhaps it was just me, but my friend who I was with dittoed my feelings, and the couple next to us said they will not be back as well.  I always order dessert, but we decided to end our misery early, and go buy a Haagen-Dazs bar.   

On a personal note, while it is nice to have my water glass refilled without having to ask, the minute you took a sip, the staff was there to refill the sip.  I thought perhaps they wanted to join us at the table (maybe they did, having heard we were leaving for ice cream).

Needless to say, I will not be back.

Came here a few months ago after all the hype this place was getting from every online food blog. It doesn't help that getting a reservation here is not easy at all. Pricier than your average Mexican fare, Cosme delivers a few stable dishes you can't go wrong with and a standard casual-fine dining service. The two of us ordered the three things every review raves about: uni tostadas, duck carnitas and the husk meringue. The tostadas had a good portion of uni and left us wanting more but we were so glad we didn't order any more appetizers because the duck carnitas WILL fill you up. It's essentially the equivalent of having five tacos per person. The sauces that came with it were fantastic too with the flavors marrying each other perfectly - we combined all the sauces and got extra hot sauce for kicks! On to dessert, the consistency of the meringue was delightful with every bite filled with creamy goodness and the crunchy sweetness from the shell. I would come back just to have this dessert again and again although my wallet wouldn't be too happy with the rest of the pricey albeit delicious food.

Ughh! I'm so disappointed by Cosme that I actually went through the trouble of tracking down my Yelp password so that I can express just how much our dining experience sucked. Not only was the food overpriced, under seasoned, overly fussy, and trendy in the worst way, but the portions were absurdly small and the service was a joke. In the span of forty five minutes, we were misserved three times and someone tried to collect my (tiny) plate before I was done. When my dinner companion complained that one of the items listed on the menu was not, in fact, on his plate, the Maitre D explained that it had been replaced with an aioli in a tone that suggested that aioli was the hautest of haute cuisine and we peasants were lucky to be in an establishment that served such a thing. Then they brought us a dessert menu instead of the check we firmly requested. We were charged a hefty sum for very little food and one of the most lackluster dining experiences I've had in NYC. I don't know how things could have gone so steeply downhill since Wells' review in The Times. Do not bother.

It is a small restaurant, very well designed and properly lit with a good atmosphere.
The food was excellent ( except enfrijolada ) every single dish I tried (10 ) was executed very well with unique flavor and I was happy to see you using authentic Mexican ingredients.
This place has a modern approach to the Mexican cuisine.
Initially, the staff was super attentive, however both during and toward the end of the meal, they seemed less accommodating and did not seem completely knowledgeable of their entire menu. 
We ordered four desserts and none
were truly satisfying except the merengue, that was super delicious !
As for the drinks, the Margaritas were merely okay. The beer I tried, Damiana, was not appealing at all!
I don't usually voice my opinion when it comes to food and service often, but I felt it necessary to make my opinion heard. Especially considering the expense in regard to this service, which was a bit overpriced, I was displeased to say the least.

Food is an amazing experience of mexican's traditions.
Excellent vibe and great stuff.
Worth it to try.

I went to Cosme for a meeting in the private room in the back with high expectations. I read Pete Wells' review in the New York Times beforehand, and I saw why he praised it so highly. I was at a wine event, so I didn't have a chance to try their cocktails or ask for pairings from their wine menu, but each dish that was brought out got better and better.

There is a perfect amount of heat in each dish. The homemade tortillas served with each course are for savoring. I'm usually not too crazy about different types of sauces, but each dish was paired with a sauce that added so much to an already extraordinary meal. 

The food comes with a high price, yet for a special meal it is well worth it. Personal favorites included the crispy octopus, duck carnitas, scallop and sirloin carpaccio.

There's nothing that can be said that hasn't already been said, and I recommend reading Wells' piece if you are debating Cosme for an upscale meal.

Rounding up, but I give it a solid 4.5 stars. 

It has been a while (April?) since my husband, our friend, and her mother went but I do remember everything we ordered (which was A LOT) was super tasty. My friend happens to be gluten intolerant but we lucked out and literally everything on the menu was gluten free. Portions on some dishes seemed small given the price, but again delicious. Of course the one thing that stood out and I still dream about are their duck carnitas! I can't wait to go back for more. 

All of our cocktails that we tried were great as well. Well balanced and paired. 

Service - SPOT. ON. Unfortunately I cannot remember the name of our waiter, but he was on top of everything, had great suggestions, and was not overly pushy to try to increase our check.

It is on the pricier side, but if nothing else, go for the carnitas!

Cosme really blew me away with the ingredients it was using.  I had just been to Oaxaca a few weeks before and brought back a bunch of ingredients I assumed I was never going to get in the US (certainly not San Francisco, where Oaxaca is apparently not a part of Mexico any restauranteur has heard of).  And here comes Cosme, with its pasilla mixe, chicatana, and rompope.  All used as a means to interpret otherwise standard menu fare like octopus and carpaccio.  The main reason I am writing a review though is to give a shout out to my bartender/waiter, whose name appears to be Jorsand according to my receipt.  I had a great time talking to him about ingredients and mezcal.  If the front of the restaurant is that passionate about what they do, I can only assume it is the same in the kitchen.  (Well, I don't have to assume - it was proven on the plates.)  My only word of caution - try your plates before squeezing lime on them.  I wished I had not used the provided lime at all on the carpaccio - it was too dominant.

I went there with a group of friends and high expectations but found it to be underwhelming and overhyped. The ambiance and decor were very nice, but the food was bland and overpriced (e.g., $21 for about one scallop). The scallop aguachile was uninspiring and blah. We tried a handful of other dishes, including the burratta, and found them to all be similar.

Best things on the menu: duck carnitas, crispy octopus, and the meringue dessert.

$59 for the duck carnitas, but it is 8 hours of roasted duck that is pull apart deliciousness. The crispy octopus came with this amazing sauce. 

I'm usually not a dessert person at all, but the meringue was the best thing I ever had. So creamy and smooth. We ended up ordering 2 because it was so good. $14 for the meringue!

This restaurant is amazing.  If you want upscale Mexican food you will not be disappointed!  Whoever did the interior design in this restaurant is brilliant.  I've never seen such colors and lighting and furniture meet in such a harmonious design. The service was good but the food was oh wow my goodness.  A little pricey but worth it.
Well-priced wine list. Get the Duck Carnitas and Husk Meringue-you won't be dissapointed

KenScale: 8.5/10

Cosme was one of the best and hottest restaurants in NYC last year. Recently, it launched Sunday-only brunch, so I was very intrigued to find out what they have to offer even though I'm not really a brunch person. I was hoping to see chef Enrique Olvera's magic touch to brighten what could be pretty dull brunch menu, and overall the restaurant did deliver quite nicely.

I was somehow drawn to oysters and sangrita when I first looked at the menu. The oysters were certainly fresh, but I felt sangrita didn't add that much to the flavor. On the other hand, stuffed avocado with seafood vuelve a la vida (a sort of seafood cocktail) was really delicious despite its simple appearance. The combination of lightly touched seafood with avocado had a great balance of flavor and texture and would certainly be an ideal start to any meal. Tortilla soup with chochoyotas and langostine broth was another winner; I was soon addicted to the aromatic flavor of the broth that was so soothing without overpowering in flavor. Cosme also has a brunch version of its famous duck carnitas in the form of duck enmoladas and crème fraiche, and this was also a great dish with elegantly sweet flavor and nicely cooked duck meat. I ended the meal with corn Johnny cakes (a sort of corn flatbread) that came with cherry-red currant jam, which was not particularly memorable but was still a solid dish to end your brunch.

The restaurant was certainly packed in the course of my meal, but getting a reservation for brunch was definitely not as daunting as dinner time. There are some brunch cocktails (with or without alcohol), so definitely order a glass or two to go along with your meal. I'm glad Cosme decided to enter the brunch game, as it shows how seemingly predictable brunch menu can really shine with the ingenuity of the kitchen.
good modern mexican , try it , you will love it

I love this neighborhood for food.  Cosme is a wonderful addition; it's a beautiful space filled with well-dressed, (mostly) attractive people.  Actually, people watching is one of the highlights.  We managed to snag an open table without a reservation at 7:45 on a Wednesday night -- no idea how that happened, come prepared with a reservation -- and as the night went on, the people coming in got better and better looking.  Come dressed up when you eat here.  

I had the El Ninja cocktail - Union Mezcal, Beefeater Gin, Cocchi Americano Vermouth, shiso shrub, ginger, lime.  Loved it.

FOOD
Ayocote bean salad, radish, charred cucumber vinaigrette $15
Burrata, pasilla mixe salsa, weeds $25
Duck carnitas, onions, radishes, salsa verde (to share) $59

I liked the first two dishes; they weren't terribly memorable.  However, I loved the DUCK CARNITAS.  I'm definitely coming back, just for this.  It was a huge dish so definitely one you want to share with someone else.  We couldn't even finish it, so I might get the Uni tostada (comes with bone marrow salsa - sounds delicious!) next time with the Duck carnitas...that should be enough for two.

To me, small plates that pair tortilla chips, salsas, and soft taco shells with the likes of octopus, uni and burrata just doesn't jive.  Also, i'm not sure the aforementioned staples of Mexican cuisine demand a $200+ per couple tab.  I love me some good Mexicano cuisine, no doubt, and there's genuine creativity here in the presentation of each dish, but next time I'm feelin' la comida Mexicana, I'll head on over to the more satisfying Empellon Taqueria, La Palapa, Rosa Mexicano,or Dos Caminos, and the like.

Took my girlfriend here for our anniversary and it was an amazing experience from start to finish. In the past I had stuck to the fancier, "jackets required for men" type places for special occasion dinners, but we enjoyed Cosme's more laid-back, upscale vibe with a meal that would have been worth  wearing a sports coat for on the hottest day of the summer. 

We arrived at the restaurant a few minutes early and were invited to sit at the bar while we wait. I think the blistering heat outside kept many people home that evening because there was a surprising amount of empty seats at the bar and empty tables (which may have attributed to the outstanding service we received). The bartender was very helpful making a cocktail for my girlfriend based on some hints we gave him regarding her taste (a grapefruit French 75), which she loved. I ordered a Paloma, which was equally delicious and refreshing. By the time we received the drinks our table was ready

As I stated, the service we received was outstanding. Our waitress was helpful with some recommendations and consistently asked how everything was. Our waters were constantly topped off, our napkins immediately folded when we excused ourselves. The hostess happily agreed to take our picture to commemorate the occasion without a hint of the common NYC hostess attitude.

We started with the Uni Tostado and Cobia al Pastor. The bone marrow salsa on the Uni tostado was very interesting, the portion of the Cobia al Pastor was a little disappointing, just enough for 3 light tacos, but we ordered so much food we didn't mind much. Just would have been nice if it was enough for 2 tacos each.

Next we had the fluke with pork jowl and the burrata with salsa and weeds, and both were equally amazing. The burrata was a nice change of pace from the light fish dishes. As two cheese lovers, we were practically scraping the bottom of the bowl it came in. 

We wanted to get the full Cosme experience so we obviously had to finish with the duck carnitas, followed by the corn husk meringue for dessert. As advertised these were the two stand out dishes. The duck carnitas dish was the best duck we had ever had, in the best tortillas I've ever had. The portion of duck is insane. We must have taken down about 10 tacos before I started seeing stars and remembering about the corn husk meringue. I recommend only getting one round of starters if you're ordering the the duck. 

And then that meringue.. I laughed as I watched my girlfriend's eyes close in a state of euphoric bliss as she took the first bite, and then the same thing happened to me. Probably the best dessert I've ever had. 

There were a few negatives that nearly tempted me into taking a star off, the prices for the portions (specifically the Cobia) would have been a turn off if this wasn't a special occasion. The gentleman at the table next to us gagging from a complimentary shot of liquor he received for knowing someone from the restaurant nearly made my girlfriend lose her appetite,  but with a meal filled with so many "best ____ I've ever had, it's impossible not to give them 5 stars.

i do not understand why this place is every food reviewers wet dream. its totally overrated. the dishes are expensive with tiny bits of protein. basically you're paying 20-30$ for tortilla chips with sauce and three bites of chicken when you order the chilaquiles. guacamole is good, but thats about it. they really take advantage of you here. find better mexican elsewhere.also the service is absent. had to ask multiple times for things- i think he forgot to place orders for. skip it!

Every time we're in NYC we pick a new restaurant for our "date night" and it's mostly a Meatpacking District 'new cool place', but this time I had read about Enrique Olvera's Cosme and its heavenly merigue dessert and we decided to skip the MD and go to Flatiron instead.
It was difficult to get a table (I think I booked a month in advance and could only get a 10 pm seating) but it was worth it. The atmosphere has a cool and lively vibe, the place was packed with people having drinks or late dinner, service was fast and attentive.
The food: Thankfully we weren't starving because I must say the prices are a bit high and the portions are smallish, which is to be expected - if you want hearty Mexican food, this is not the place - but if it's quality food and creative pairings you want (and you don't mind splurging for one evening) then this is the place.
The guacamole was perfect, so were the blue corn chips, after the guac starter we had 2 mains and 2 desserts. Mains were the half lobster pibil with black bean pure and the crispy octopus with mole - both very good, loved how the flavors mixed. Of course we had to save some space for dessert and it was not difficult because as I mentioned, portions are not huge.
We got the husk meringue with corn mousse and the chocorrol with tamarind curd and sorbet. Chocorrol is a Mexican sweet snack that I used to eat as a kid in Mexico and I loved it, it's like a chocolate cake with a creamy filling and covered with chocolate crust; Cosme's version of chocorrol has tamarind in it, and while it sounded good, it didn't have a super special taste, but the tamarind sorbet on the side was very much appreciated. But the real deal was the husk meringue - if you have read anything at all about Cosme, you have definitely read about the famous husk meringue and I can say that it lives up to the hype, it's probably the best dessert I've ever had, the corn mousse inside is so yummy and the meringue is just perfectly done *drooling*... I would just come back to this place for that meringue!
The wine list was a bit disappointing and ridiculously overpriced, this and the prices (I would just lower them 10/15% and they would be fine - or increase the portions) made me take a star off.
However, our experience at Cosme was great: the food was very good, cool atmosphere and the delicious husk meringue dessert.

Went here for brunch and left feeling hungry/ not satisfied.  I felt we spent $100 for two people on tortillas and not much else.  The duck enchilada was great- but only 3 small pieces; the same for the razor clams.  Chilaqulies is a bunch of tortillas with swauce and boiled chicken on top- pretty boring.  Pacing of the dishes was slow.  The churro was fresh, warm and delicious.

The duck carnitas are excellent - they come out in a piping hot cast iron skillet and if you are an animal like me and my dining companions, all dining etiquette goes out the window and you claw at it with your hands. I think they're braised with orange juice and Mexican coke and the result is a sweet, caramel-y delicious pile of fowl. The tortillas they come with are some of the best I've had in our fair city.

Unfortunately, this one dish was basically the highlight of our meal. The much hyped about uni tostada is good, because, well, uni, but otherwise pretty flavorless. You can basically get better pork rinds at any gas station than the crispy chicharron here. The rest of the dishes we ordered fell into the same vein of being bland and uninteresting.

I'd come back for the duck carnitas but for the price, I could eat tacos for a week in Bushwick.

Went there last night and was very disappointed.  Food was ok but incredibly overpriced for what you get.  Felt rushed throughout the entire meal.  Again, food wasn't bad but certainly not memorable especially for the price.  Definitely would not go back.

Went here for dinner with my better half and was very impressed with everything. The setting and ambiance of the restaurant was amazing. I have been to some really good restaurant cosme lived up to all my expectations. The food was beyond spectacular. I ordered the sirloin steak and I prefer my steak a bit well done, however the medium rare steak with avocado and chill pepper was by far the best steak i have ever had. all the flavor complimented each other well. the choice for wine was amazing and i don't remember the one we had for dinner, but trust me when i say this, it was pretty amazing especially with the steak. Dessert was one of a kind. we had the sorbet with mango jalepeno and passion fruit. it was the best sorbet i've ever had. customer service was on point as everyone was on their game to take care of us. i would definitely recommend cosme to anyone that would like good food within a good environment. Taking mexican cuisine to the next level. Oh I definitely be going back with some more friends!!!

I am sorry to have to agree with the serious gripes I've read about this much-hyped place. We were prepared for outrageous prices and tiny portions, but these are taken to an absurd level at Cosme. They are all small plates, really only a few precious bites, and they typically cost $25 (some in the teens, some in the 30s). The food is truly fine, and my margarita was perhaps the best I've ever had. (But should my wife's martini have cost $17?) The service was very uneven: I had to ask 3 times for a drinks list, and then the drinks took a very long time to arrive; we asked a waiter a question before ordering one, and he said he would go check, but he never returned. And this is the noisiest restaurant I have ever been in - not only impossible for conversation, but actually painful.

An Exciting and Enticing New Resident from Mexico City

Fantastic.  I wrote a long review that didn't get posted because I had not verified my email address and I am not writing it over again.  So you'll have to trust me, here are some highlights:  Mezcal demystified and explained by Dimitri the bartender.  A sexy downtown vibe.  Beautifully served, delicious and adventurous cuisine.  Prompt service.  An opportunity to experience a slice of Mexico City's fine dining scene brought to us by chef Enrique Olvera.  This is not a margarita bar.  This is serious dining delivered in a fun, buzzy venue.

* I was generous giving Cosme 5 stars but did so based on this being Yelp! and not Michelin or even the NY Times.  That said, some kinks in the operation should be worked on:  notably the format of the menu needs to be less confusing and stop with the annoying "these dishes are meant to be shared" thing.  Cosme is far too ambitious (and expensive) to promote splitting dishes family style.  Imagine going to Jean Georges and being told "these dishes are meant for the table to share."  Come on.

Over priced and over staffed with poor customer service.  
Clearly we should have looked at YELP first and seen the 4$$$$.  (Google had 2$$). We spent well over 100$/person for what was essentially tapas.  Waited 30 minutes to get a table that we had a reservation for...no offer of even sitting down at the bar.  The drinks are scary bad.  Waited forever to get waited on when we sat down.  There are employees everywhere, but nobody could take an order except the waiter for our table who had multiple tables to cover. 
On a positive note, the duck carnitas are fabulous.  If we had to go again, I would order only that and guacamole.

Went to Cosme last night after reading Pete Wells' NY Times review - 3 stars. The restaurant we went to was not the one Wells reviewed - the food entirely lacked complexity and was bland and flavorless, the space is equally generic  and the service can't keep up. All this is delivered at prices that match those of really good restaurants, many within a 5 minute walk of Cosme. 

We had misgivings the moment we walked in and heard the music. Far from Wells' description of lively background music, it was overly loud and the crowd matched and exceeded its volume. Conversation was impossible unless you were prepared to shout, something that the table next to us chose to do.

The food is unacceptably bad in New York, where so many chefs are doing so many interesting things. Absolutely every dish was underspiced and lacking complexity - and salt. The chicharron was entirely flavorless, as was the octopus. The hamachi crudo was disappointing; mono flavored, a touch of citrus would have lifted the experience. The sepia and ayocote salad were equally uninspired and tasteless. Walk over a couple of blocks to Casa Mono to see what can be done with both. How the octopus could be so bland is something we are still debating .The only dishes that had any interaction of flavors were the king crab and the ayocote tamale. Dessert was horrible - the chocolate cake with tamarind and the sweet bean tamale. 

Service is pleasant and well meaning but lacked efficiency and at these prices I don't expect to have to ask for my wine to be refilled.

Bottom line - Cosme is going to have to raise its game substantially to exist. If you're in the flatiron district, there are a number of good - even great - restaurants: Gramercy Tavern, Craft, Craftbar, Maialino, Casa Mono - don't waste time and money here. Really, really disappointing.

So I don't quite understand some of the low reviews on here. I have been wanting to check this place out for quite a while. The venue is actually nicer than what I expected. The service was great and the servers were knowledgeable. All the dishes were supper yummy. I especially like barbacoa mushroom dish, the tostada and the duck carnitas.  Love this modern take on Mexican and common they use malin & goetz candles in their bathroom. Go here...don't listen to those people on yelp. Check out for more pictures on my IG: t2theN_go.

We scored a last minute table tonight at Cosme. Service was wonderful, friendly, knowledgeable and attentive. Place was pretty bumpin, but that's ok. Foods, now, they're GREAT! They're some of best meals we had in a while. They're subtly packed with a punch. Subtle Mexican foods you say? Yes they're sophisticatedly good! We opted with a bunch of small plates as opposed to entrees and wasn't disappointed. We had Uni tostada, hamachi, potatoes tamales, mushroom Barbacoa, and al pastor. And desserts were really good too. Overall they're great!
Loved the Red tortillas with beets and the unique dessert sweet tamal with yogurt. Service wasn't as attentive and wine lost by the glass not as good

Awesome meal, look here's the deal, Cosme is upscale, the food is amazing, and it has the prices to match. We went on a Friday at around 10:30 pm, for whatever reason the whole place was a sauna and the A/C was not working, but that didn't affect the food we just drank really cold drinks. We did an abbreviated menu because I have been dying to come here. We went with the king crab, the beef tartare, the NY strip tacos, and of course the corn meringue dessert. The only thing that was average was the beef tartare and I think that was because it was a unique preparation mixed with beans on a tostada. The king crab was amazing as was the steak tacos, their tortillas here are just ridiculously legit and I am still dreaming about them. Now on to the corn meringue dessert, the most instagrammed dessert, did it live up to the hype? Yes and then some, next time I am ordering my own and not sharing. Cosme is an amazing addition to NYC and I am super excited to come back in the near future.

So glad I dined here this evening.  Unique and creative ingredients with some bold flavors, as well as on point service, make this a great night out.  The Cobia al pastor with pineapple purée is off the hook tasty. Oh, and don't pass up on the lemon mousse and coconut sorbet with avocado for dessert. Fresh, light, and flavors that captivate.  This place is fun, attentive, and boom-  each dish brought forth is a rewarding and flavorful journey.  Worry not about the price point.  Just go have fun.

This place is really as good as it gets.  This is Mexican food like you've never had it before.  Because we went in a larger group (9 people), we ordered 1 or 2 of most of the items on the menu, and so I can attest that YOU CAN'T GO WRONG!  However, the duck is as good as the hype suggests.  Also the drinks are incredible.  One tip: the place is dressy, come dressed to impress.

I cannot wait to come back!

Was able to secure an 8pm saturday night reservation at Cosme so the wife and I decided to try this place despite the (recent) mixed reviews.

Bottomline, Cosme is a great restaurant addition to the NYC fine dining scene, the food was unique and the service was attentive.  For our starters we had: chicharons, kampachi, and the mushrooms and squash dish.  The chicharons were the best I have ever had and showed me what refined cooking can do to this simple dish.  The fried pork was rendered down and crispy, not too salty and paired well with the garnishes and sauce.  The kampachi was good, but honestly not something that we would order again since its available at other establishments.  We really enjoyed the mushroom and squash dish and it was great in the corn totillas!  

For the main, we split the duck carnitas.  The duck was perfectly cooked and the portion size huge.  I am not sure what some of the reviewers mean when saying this restaurant has small portions, the duck carnitas has to be the best deal for a duck main in the city (since most places charts mid/high 30s for their duck dishes for one).

The dessert was the meringue, which was melt in your mouth goodness and perfect ending to the meal.

Service was great, our waiter helped us navigate the menu well and the somm came by to check on us as we had ordered a bottle of wine and she wanted to make sure we didn't need it decanted (it was one of the cheapest bottles on their list but she thought it would benefit from decanting, we thought it was fine the way it was but the gesture was nice).

For those old enough to remember how the NY Times star rating used to be, think of Cosme as a 2 star with 3 star prices, and 1 star service. It's interesting, clean food in a nice setting. But some of the prices are just ridiculous and the service is heavy handed and unrefined. 

I'm glad I went, but when you're talking $130 per head (with tip) and leave hungry, it's a bit disappointing. I can't see Cosme being open in 5 years time in this format.

There was a mishap and our reservation was not in but still they found us a table. 

Everything was slow, I think it was just too busy, they gave us complimentary items in between dishes so we're not just sitting there.

The place gets super loud so prepare to talk loud yourself. 

Despite some minus points, I think they serve some really delicious food here, my parents loved it too.

Meh. The service was terribly slow, so I can't  comment on whether the food was legitimately good since I was legitimately starving. The portions were on the small side and kind of overpriced for what they were. No plans to go back anytime soon...

This is very expensive Mexican food, but the flavors were quite extraordinary.  The space is casual and relatively tranquil, with a decent noise level.  The waitstaff was attentive and helpful.  I'd recommend Cosme for a special occasion, but it's hard to imagine going there often.  Perhaps the menu items will change frequently, and that would be interesting.

Yes, the corn mousse dessert is a must try.

The Cosme experience is such a special treat from Enrique Olvera! With a chic interior, delicious cocktails and incredible food, Cosme is the perfect package ideal for a special occasion. For the full experience, I would recommend sharing all the dishes with a small group of close friends so that you can savor all the unique creations.

For cocktails, the Scoville Sour was unique option with a touch of spiciness to help stir up an appetite.

In terms of appetizers, we shared the dishes below and were left craving for more:
- Uni Tostada: Small and good for two to share; it is like a firework of deliciousness with a combo of uni and bone marrow
- Sliced Raw Hamachi: Fresh, simple and mouthwateringly delicious
- Scallop Aguachile: Delicately sliced scallops paired with slightly spicy wasabi-cucumber-lime dressing is nice and refreshing
- Cobia al Pastor: I love pineapple, and what is not to love of the pairing of fish and pineapple sauce?
- Smoked Raw Sepia: Mixed seafood served in a fresh, creamy avocado...need I say more? Delicious!
- Burrata: At first, I wasn't sure about ordering Burrata in a Mexican restaurant. Alas, Cosme has proven me wrong with this creation of soft, creamy burrata cheese paired with greens and a light salsa dressing

As for our main, we shared the Duck Carnitas. It more than lived up to its hype! It is cooked to such perfection and the meat is so tender that it falls off its bones as soon as cut into it. This dish can feed at least 4 very happy people.

We were stuffed by the time we polished off the suck. But, we just have to get the Husk Meringue with Corn Mousse, and it is a lovely icing on the cake. The slightly savory corn mouse makes this dessert absolutely unique and decadent. I loved it so much that I was giventhe "honors" to clean off the last bit of mouse that I licked off my fingers.

Finally, the service was friendly but not over-bearing. The staff was very knowledgeable of Cosme's offerings and gave us some great recommendations (as we could not decide among the many choices we have). And oh, make reservations way ahead of time...it is well-worth the hassle!

Overall, it was a fun, lovely evening of perfection!

Amazing experience I had when I first knew COSME. It was that good that I have been there four times already. It is hard to find authentic mexican ingredients with high end preparation. The cocktail list is great as well.
I would definitely recommend sharing dishes to try the most you can.
Prices are reasonable having this excellent treat, high quality ingredients and the cool mood this place has. COSME staff have created a unique way to order courses as there is no difference between starters and main courses.
Specially the duck carnitas, burratta and steak with shishito peppers are great. The only complaint I can make to COSME staff is that they stopped to sell the mussel tostada that was a must. Overall, I could say is a perfect 10.

Gorgeous interior space paired with an excellent and attentive staff.
Portions are small for the price point, but the presentation and flavors in each of their offerings justify what they're asking. Expansive wine list, but with a cocktail menu that I find to be on the sweeter side.

This has to be one of the most over priced restaurants in NYC. Outrageous prices for tiny portions of subpar food. With that in mind you would expect great service to make up for the food quality, but unfortunately our waiter was very surly. When asking for recommendation the waiter would only mention the most expensive items on the menu without explanation for why.

Excellent service, the waiters and the hostess are really nice, the food is amazing you must order the burrata, the duck carnitas, the potatoes tamal and the meringue or the lemon mousse as a dessert, both are amazing!! The atmosphere is great either if you are in the lounge or in the restaurant!! Been there 3 times in the last month, I LOVE IT.

Make a reservation in advance because if not the wait can be long, although If you do not have a reservation the bar is great for a couple of drinks while you wait.

A bit expensive but it is worth it as the chef, Enrique Olvera is one of the top chefs around the world, actually I was there the same night as Chef Thomas Keller and we agreed that both the service and food were outstanding.

I would definitely recommend it!!!

Exceptional food and service!

Great ambiance. Excellent for special occasions. Book in advance

Don't leave without trying duck carnitas

Excelent cuisine. Charming anda excelent decoration.  We has the best duck carnitas. Delicious scallops. And the desert incredible:  merengue with corn cream!!!!!   Anda the hamachi with chile serrano wow!!!

Nice looking restaurant. Very nice staff. Food was good in the restaurant but was sick all night and the next morning after. Only had one cocktail that night at the restaurant. Maybe it was something else but only ate a bagel that morning.

Anyway, a lot of the complaints are that the portions are too small for a high price. I thought that the size was appropriate for each dish.

We started with the guacamole. It was simple guac but still tasty. Nothing that you couldn't make at home.

Had asparagus, burrata, bean salad, tamal, and meringue husk desert. The meringue husk was pretty to look at and had an interesting taste. Expect a salty taste though. 

Mostly 3 stars just bc being sick was aggravating and we tried an asparagus dish at the nomad restaurant which tasted better. The drinks were good, we tried paloma and margharita. Worth a try, I'm sure my experience wasn't the norm.

Came here last night for my birthday. It was a happening place on a Wednesday night. Very hard to get reservations. The ambiance and service was very good. Our glasses were always filled with water and the server always stopped by to check on us. The food on the other hand was ok. Overpriced and portions were extremely small. We got the duck carnitas since that's what everyone recommended but it wasn't flavorful at all. In fact it was very salty. We also had the mussels and the scallops. Both were very fresh and refreshing. The steak tartar was also very different. The crispy octopus was ok too. 
The most disappointing dish was the dessert. We got the chocolate cake and it looked like a yodel. Very dry and not very chocolatey. 
Definitely wouldn't come back. Not really sure what the hype is all about.

this really deserves 3.5 stars.  the portions are pricey and small.  the drinks too sugary.  but the Duck Carnitas is amazing!  and a hefty portion.  skip everything else. go straight for that, and you'll leave happy with money to spare.

This place is great, but it keeps you guessing. If what you want is food you're expecting, this may not be the place for you. If you enjoy finding something new in the familiars, then you'll have a great time. The food is expertly prepared and well imagined, and the atmosphere is friendly and professional.

My dear friend was so excited to get a table at this new " hot spot" last month and so my partner and I joined him for dinner tonight. I wish I had never gone unfortunately. Wasted calories and wasted money. 

The martinis were by far the worst I've ever had in Manhattan. Too much vermouth, even though I we asked for dry, and watered down. When we brought this to the attention of the lady who seemed to be the manager, she came off as defensive.  

The food portions are small. And while the ingredients may be of high quality, the dishes such as the octopus, mushroom appetizer and bean dish were tasteless. The only tasty dish was the duck. But not in a good way. Was extremely gamy.  

Definitely not going back and not recommending.

After all the hype for this place and after visiting Pujol, I was very much looking forward to dinner here. That said, I made sure not to compare Cosme to Pujol (as I know it's not the same concept and definitely a different geography), and let Cosme stand on its own. The thing is - it didn't. In short, the food was really pretty bad (along with being expensive)  and the service was only fine. The restaurant is beautiful, however.

The hostess didn't acknowledge me when I walked in, and I actually got a little confused about whether or not I was paying attention to the right person (turns out I was) because she wouldn't look up at me and just continued chatting with her coworker. After we were seated, we couldn't figure out who was the busboy or the waiter because it took 15 minutes for the waiter to show up. He was fine. I was disappointed in having to give him the tip we did because he was far, far short of the value we paid. He WAS nice, though, when he graced us with his presence! 

We had the octopus, which was horribly dry and lacked flavor, the duck, which was really good and a good size, and a few other not so memorable dishes. For dessert, we shared the chocolate cake, which I assume was a year-old hostess cupcake roll unwrapped and plated at the rate of $14. It was very dry and very bad. We also had the guacamole, which was flavorless. 

I would not recommend this to anyone for the food, but I'd understand if they want to go once just to experience a restaurant by this owner. Go to Mexico CIty instead and try out Pujol! Definitely worth it...and cheaper.

I was not going to mention it, but since others have done so I will say that I too became sick after having dinner at Cosme. The next day I had it coming nonstop from both ends. That lasted eight days or so.

I had the Duck Carnitas, Uni Tostada and Corn Husk Meringue. The Duck Carnitas and Uni Tostada were okay. The Corn Husk Meringue was very good. Service was fine and the ambiance was nice.

I had the most amazing experience. Cosme is so far my favorite restaurant in town. I've been both to dinner and brunch, and I have to say it was far beyond my expectations. I'm from Mexico but have been living in NY for years. Cosme has the authentic flavors of Mexico but feels like a NY place. The food is insane, ambience is perfect, and service is friendly and warm just like home. I'm hoping to come back as soon as I can get a reservation again.

Wow - what an amazing treat for NY to have an Enrique Olvera restaurant! I have been to Pujol in Mexico City and Moxi in San Miguel de Allende and could not wait to continue my Olvera love affair at Cosme. It did not disappoint. Although, unlike its Mexican counterparts, Cosme is extremely expensive so save this for a one-time celebration type of meal.

Make a reservation far in advance. Even on a Sunday night every table was booked. The restaurant is dark and has a sexy atmosphere. Our waiter was rather standoffish and didn't crack a smile once the entire night but other than that, we enjoyed the evening tremendously.

The food was incredible. We started with the uni tostada, the raw scallops, the wagyu beef tartare and the potato tamal. The scallops were tasty but I've had similar dishes at other restaurants so it was not particularly memorable. The beef tartare was probably the least favorite as the whole dish tasted more of beans than of meat. The uni tostada was decadent and delicious. The favorite by far, though, was surprisingly the potato tamal, which was the most delicious potato I've ever tasted topped in a beautifully creamy ricotta cheese. It was earthy and rich and wonderful.

For main dishes, we had the lobster pibil and the duck carnitas. Don't miss either of these dishes! The lobster was soft and tender in a bean purée and the duck carnitas - wow where to even begin on this one! A huge piece of duck meat (off the bone) cooked to such perfection that it falls apart when your fork touches it. Served with pickled onions, radishes, warm blue tortillas and a couple of spicy sauces. This duck dish is big enough for 3-4 people to share!

And of course don't miss the corn husk meringue. This dessert absolutely lived up to the hype! The chocolate dessert was interesting with tamarind ice cream but did not compare to the corn.

Read about Cosme in Conde Nast Traveler magazine and was excited to give it a try. The four of us left very underwhelmed, unimpressed, and feeling that we did not get our money's worth.

The pros - famous chef, attentive staff, good cocktails (El Ninja was very tasty), and we liked the lighting in Cosme. The staff was very polite, explained each meal and dish, and provided us with complimentary tostadas. While these were all nice, we were at Cosme for the food and it did not live up to the hype.

The food was very small portions and not worth the amount you paid for them. They had very little flavor and while the presentation was nice, the garnish, sauce, and salad was arranged in a way to hide the fact that you were getting very little of the good stuff. Case in point, at $35 the black garlic rubbed NY strip came with an abundance of garnish and 2 very small pieces of steak per person. Each of us was able to finish our taco in 3 normal-sized bites, making this the of 2 small pieces of steak in a taco priced at $9 each. The chicharron tasted like cardboard and i found myself dousing it with hot sauce to get some semblance of flavor. The scallop aguachile was good, but it was heavy on the jicama and very light on the actual scallop. I was really looking forward to the octopus and hazelnut mole. While this was my favorite dish, the best part, (the mole) was little more than a few drops and left all of us very unsatisfied. 

Conde Nast - you have steered us wrong and hopefully Yelp will provide a more accurate account of what you get at Cosme.

Good food but there was no wow factor and no real excitement in any of the dishes.  I've had better modern Mexican in NYC for far less.  Very pricey so not a good value.  Nice to try it once but I won't return.  Overhyped in my book.

IN SHORT: Exquisite New York City cuisine comes by way of Mexico in this dark, brooding Flatiron space. Prepare to have all your expectations exceeded here, for Cosme is the restaurant that has finally illustrated what it means to elevate Mexican food to the discipline of fine dining.

THE STORY: 2004 was a landmark year for restaurants. It was the year we saw Noma, Per Se, Masa, Blue Hill at Stone Barns, The Spotted Pig, Momofuku Noodle Bar, and even Shake Shack open their doors for the first time. These were restaurants that changed the culinary landscape of the country, of the world, and simultaneously redefined what fine dining would look like and feel like in the coming decade.

I think, perhaps another 10 years from now, we will look back on 2014 with almost equal deference. We will look at it as a year that experienced another positive economic and cultural shift that resulted in daring new innovations in the field, and at the forefront of these changes to the discipline, I think we will recognize Cosme and Enrique Olvera as the harbingers of serious Mexican cuisine.

Mexican food for me has always been a cuisine that brings back intense memories of steamy corn tortillas enjoyed with freshly sliced avocado under a hot Southern California sun. It is food that reminds me of a little girl whose earliest culinary accomplishments included a perfect bowl of creamy guacamole. It is the smell of lime that reminds me of the evening when my mother told me her favorite cocktial was a margarita, and when she showed me how to make one without tequila so I could be emulate the woman I saw in her. It is food that recalls the magic hour of my childhood, looked back on with a warm, sunny nostalgia for the tacos and beans and corn that fill the eternal summer of California.

Cosme is not that food. Cosme instead takes me intensely back to my most favorite dining experiences in New York, with a local excellence and hospitality so simultaneously thrilling and refined it could only be found in this city. It is a restaurant that reminds me of falling in love with New York for the first time, of deeply connecting with a part of its storied culture.
