Cosme rejects labels that could trap it under weighty definitions of tradition and authenticity. The flavors are indeed Mexican, crafted by the world's foremost Mexican chef, but the interpretation is New York, full of elegance, subtlety, and power. The chicharron (fried pork skin) is covered with impeccable slices of radish and avocado, and begins to snap, crackle, and pop as soon as a bit of lime juice is drizzled over it. With a little heat from hot sauce to draw out even more flavor, it hits all five senses with sensational strength.

The Duck Carnitas for two have emerged as one of Cosme's signature dishes, but exploring the menu with an assemblage of smaller plates can be far more satisfying, and far more telling about the conceptual strength of the restaurant. The Potato Tamal with ayocote beans and fresh ricotta is creamy and earthy, reminiscent of a pre-Columbian tradition but decidedly fresh and tangy.

To round out a meal for two, two larger plates can be shared, ideally the Half Lobster Pibil, a slow-roasted preparation from the Yucatan region that renders the lobster utterly succulent and tender on top of a chorizo and black bean puree, and the Black Garlic Rubbed NY Strip for Tacos. The little squares of steak are perfectly soft and pink, and could so easily be enjoyed on their own without the light, airy corn tortillas that come on the side. But then one would miss tortillas unlike any other in New York, and that would be a tragedy. The avocado-tarragon puree that appears in quenelles across the plate is also one of the most richly flavored treatments of the fruit I've ever tasted, an ethereal, creamy fantasy that pairs smoothly and beautifully with the protein. The dish is so clearly composed for New York, but its Mexican roots and underpinnings make it a completely novel experience.

Having opened in October of 2014, it's clear that Cosme is already making a difference in the field, showing the city that it is decidedly new and yet intimately a part of it with its picture-perfect lighting, dark, cool setting, and clarity of forward-thinking, boundary-pushing flavors. This is what makes Cosme the only 5-star Mexican restaurant in the city.

Yes, 2014 was a good year.

I went here for the first time on Thursday 5/21 with 2 friends and honestly was not the least bit impressed. The food was just ehh, nothing really had enough flavor to it, and I was severely disappointed.  To top that off, I woke up Sat am with horrible stomach pains, and had stomach issues that lasted me a full week.  I didn't think to even talk to my 2 friends I dined with, thinking I just got some virus, and after speaking with them today, they both had the SAME EXACT issue. So we're convinced it was something from eating at Cosme.  They either didn't handle the food properly and passed on some of the bacteria to us, or something terrible is going on there.  There's no way all 3 of us would have been sick with the same stomach issue by coincidence..and this was not a fever/flu type of issue. Needless to say, I will NOT be going back there ever again!

Finally got a chance to write this review.  With all the hype and pricing, I was expecting a much better meal.  The highlight of the meal was the uni tostada, what a great dish but  at the price expected more food.  For the main we had the half lobster pibil (which lacked some seasoning) and the very expensive duck carnitas which was an  intriguing dish but lacked the extra sides to place in your carnitas (cheese, pickled veggies, etc) to make it something special at close to  $60.  For the price of this meal, I would prefer to go to a better restaurant or spend a lot less and go to another great mexican place.

This was a nice meal but a bit of a disappointment due to high expectations.  I didn't love the style of the restaurant with the dark room - doesn't give me a warm feeling - so perhaps I started with the wrong mindset.  The waiter was pleasant and seemed to know the menu reasonably well.  He did disappear a few times which was frustrating when we wanted something.  

Overall, the food was very good.  We enjoyed every dish.  The main issue was service - they either have problems in the kitchen or don't plan very well.  We had long waits between dishes - twenty minutes at one point which really kills the flow of the meal.  

If this was a $100 or less meal, I would live with the above issue - for $200+ (with only one glass of wine!) you expect more.  Honestly, as much as I enjoyed the food I don't know if I would go back.

I came here with my sister since there was so much hype about this place. We ordered Paloma which was very good.
-Uni tostada was absolutely delicious.
-Burrata was a little bland and heavy...not a big fan of it.
-Mushroom and Squash Barbacoa was delicious except a little salty
-Duck Carnitas: awesome but I would love to see more onions or radish to pair with it.
-Grapefruit Raspado w/earl grey ice cream: very very good and I prefer it over Husk Meringue

It is shocking that the Health Dept has not shut these guys down.  We know of at least 15 people who are now taking Cipro after a weeklong bout with E Coli after dinner here.  They have been relatively unresponsive and have done nothing to deal with this awful Health issue.  The service was also not great and the Hostess was one of the nastiest we have encountered in New York.  In summary, interesting cuisine but you have a better chance of staying healthy by eating Street Meat!!!

Cosme was a big let down . Service was poor at check in and despite being the only ones in the place, they felt compelled to seat us next to the kitchen door. Waiter hurried the order and moved us along the entire meal. Food was average although by the time it arrived I wanted to leave anyway . Rather spend 20 bucks at a food truck than 350 here for average food and a seat that essentially told us to leave. Not sure what food critics are talking about...

Pros:
- Great Drinks
- Sceney Ambiance

Cons:
- Horrible Service
- Overpriced food

First of all, I'm from Los Angeles and I've had amazing Mexican food from an upscale restaurant to a taco stand right outside a concert. While visiting NY, my best friend tried to get a reservation with no luck. After a day of walking around NY like a tourist we happened to be in the same vicinity as Cosme. I suggested to my friend that we should just drip in for a quick drink and appetizer. We walk-in a little after 4:00 p.m. in the afternoon and the place was half full. Since we didn't have a reservation we asked if we could sit at a lounge table by the bar area. Our server came over to us and immediately asked if, the hostess allowed us to sit here and if he could check in with the hostess to confirm. We didn't mind and he quickly walked away.

At that point I could tell that, 1) My best friend is about to go on a valid rant about Cosme 2) I'm going to need a drink for this rant. 

My best friend made a few valid points about the server having an issue with seating guests with no reservations in an half empty restaurant and how her dollar is no different than any other individual in there. Let's be honest this place is a nice shi-shi Manhattan scene but don't give your guests a hard time or skimp on the service because we had no reservations. We had some of the food and I wasn't too thrilled with it. I've had better Mexican food at a similar venue like Pez Cantina or Border Grill in L.A.

Great "New-Mexican" restaurant in Flatiron. The food is really amazing though, and you can actually pay your check right from your phone with Dash- and If you do - it's $10 OFF your check, PER PERSON! Here's the link! www.getda.sh/invite/COSMENYC

Been there 3 times! Real Mexican flavors with the best ambiance! If you are looking to have a great dinner in a cool place with mind blowing dishes this is the place to be. You need reservation but they accept walk in and if you have no luck you can still order great drinks at the bar!

I ventured here for the first time a few days ago. We had a 9:15 reservation, and ended up not being seated until 9:40. A bit of a bummer seeing as it was already so late and having run 5 miles a few hours earlier to say I was starving is an understatement.

We sat at the bar as we waited. I had the Scoville Sour cocktail which was a unique combination of refreshing cucumber as well as spice. During dinner I had the Anti Histamine which was also a bit spicy and featured bee pollen. Shoutout to our bartender who was super friendly, and went on and on about his upcoming trip to swim with whale sharks. Good luck! 

Our courses for three people were:
Uni tostada, Scallop aguachile, mushroom and squash barbacoa, burrata, black garlic rrubbed NY strip, and the duck carnitas. We were looking forward to having their signature uni dish, but according to our waitor the prices have sky rocketed globally so they have removed it from their menu. 

Out of the first 5 dishes I listed, I really enjoyed the scallop dish. It had an intersting cucumber but spicy sauce. I had never had raw scallops before, but really enjoyed them. I also enjoyed the steak dish. I was really excited for the mushroom and squash barbacoa, but only thought it was okay. 

I honestly probably would have given this place three stars had it not been for the last dish: the duck carnitas. This is the most expensive item on the menu (at $59) but it was truly great, and in my opinion, well worth the hype. It was cooked perfectly, and had a pulled-pork-like texture. 

We also got the signature meringue-husk dessert at the end. Honestly - I didn't think it was very good. It was a weird combination of flavors for me. I also really enjoy meringues and have made better myself. 

Overall - glad I went because it was a unique assortment of flavors, but don't think I have much of a reason to go back. 

In total the bill was probably close to $100 per person.

With so much hype you might expect to be underwhelmed by Cosme, but let me assure you that my husband and I were well and truly whelmed!   We started with the delectable Arctic Char Tostada, Cobia al Pastor and Mushroom and Squash Barbacoa, all of them beyond delicious, and followed with the incomparable Duck Carnitas, incredibly moist, tender and flavorful even without the delicious salsa that came on the side.  Their housemade tortillas are highly praised for good reason.  There was enough duck to take home and enjoy for brunch the next day along with the wonderful tortillas that they thoughtfully included.  We were really too full for dessert but we could not fail to share the husk meringue with corn mousse that totally justifies its reputation. It was light and delicate, not too sweet, but the corn flavor was mild so it was not like eating a savory course.  I realize it's a cliche but I had to try a Margarita and theirs was first class, though I switched to a glass of red wine for the main course that was also terrific.  Seating was comfortable and very social.  Service was excellent.  Overall a fabulous evening that we'd love to repeat if we can snag another reservation.

I went to cosme last week with my wife and four friends. The service was terrible, the food was mediocre and overpriced and every person in our party had serious stomach problems for four days after. We believe we got E. coli with serious diarrhea and stomach cramping. All the people that ate food at cosme got sick. Do not go!

Service was soso.  Wait staff was not very attentive. The food we had lacked bold flavor and inventiveness, but the presentation was nice. We thought it was overpriced and left a bit underwhelmed.  We had the scallop aguachile, the octopus, the enfrijolada, and the corn husk dessert. However, decor and general ambience was nice..

I hesitated writing a negative review for Cosme and decided to voice the concerns I experienced with a letter to the GM.  After that went ignored, I've now decided to post.

It's a growing irritation of mine that customer service has totally gone downhill just because a resto is the hot place at the moment.  It's all about the dining room being filled to the rafters every night, not about the service or returning clients.  It's a shame.

The food and atmosphere are excellent.  I have no complaints with that.  It was the service, particularly the wine service, which was poor.

To make a long story short(ish), I ordered a bottle of wine and when I tasted it, it was definitely corked.  The gentleman took it away and returned a minute later saying it was indeed corked.  Decided to order the same bottle.  Tasted it and while not as offensive as the first bottle, it still wasn't very good.  At that point, a woman, who I suppose was the head sommelier, came over and said, I agree the first bottle was corked but the second wasn't as bad.

Wasn't as bad?  What does that  mean?  Should that even be an option?  No.  Wine should be drinkable or not.  This wasn't drinkable.  

She then helped me pick another bottle but kept steering me towards more expensive bottles than the one originally picked.  We agreed upon a white burgundy.  She brought it to the table, then disappeared, and then reappeared with the bottle already opened.

What?  No opening it in front of me?  Did she switch out the bottle?  I was pretty appalled by this service, especially at an establishment like Cosme.

Some of you may be thinking I'm a complete wine snob.  Ok, maybe I am.  But I'm employed in the wine industry...I know right from wrong when it comes to wine protocol.  I expect right, regardless of its price and where I'm ordering it.

At this point, I didn't say anything to the somm because I was out with friends who were helping celebrate my birthday.  I just didn't want to ruin the night for anyone. And after all the inconvenience of the poor wine service (not to mention having to wait over a half hour at this point for any sort of drinks), there were no apologies.  Just business as usual, as if they couldn't be bothered with a group of 4 willing to spend a fair amount of money for their dinner.

As mentioned, the food and vibe are great.  But there are a ton of restaurants in this city where the food and vibe are great.  If you enjoy a bottle or two of wine with dinner as well as feeling appreciated that you're spending your hard earned money at their resto, I suggest taking your business elsewhere.

Mexican food at it's finest!  One can tell how much thought and creativity has been dedicated to the dishes that are served at Cosme. The fusion of different ingredients and spices make such a magnificent symphony in one's pallet.

Good food especially the seafood dishes but expect small portions.  The corn merengue dessert was excellent, not too sweet and a the perfect combination of saltiness.  The service was somewhat spotty but I would definitely give this place a second chance.

Can't say I'm impressed by the food or drinks and I dine out almost every night.  I've had much better food at other places.  Ordered 3 apps and 2 entrees amongst two people and we were still hungry. $14 a drink which is great but glass isn't as full as supposed to be compared to every where else in the world.  Service was also very slow. Over $200 later we left pretty unsatisfied, hungry and disappointed. Btw, servers if you're going to sneeze please cover your mouth! 

Uni Tostada - I enjoyed this but my friend hated the texture. 

Cobia Al Pastor - no distinct flavor, small portion, stop with the tortillas, it's just all too dry. 

Scallop Aguachille - Was good compared to the other two 'apps'

Half Lobster - Sad little portion, stop with the tortillas!! 

Broiled Red Snapper - Probably the best out of everything although I've had better. 

Drinks - Scoville Sour was very good and the desserts were great.  

Overall I probably would not come back unless there was a major change in the food and ambiance. Sorry to be so harsh guys! Only reason I give 3 stars is because well I don't know. I feel bad.

Amazing restaurant. Me and my friend visited Cosme today, both really enjoyed our dinner here. This is one of the best restaurants that serves Mexican food I have ever been to, truly deserves five star. The food and service was fantastic. I simply loved the place. Great ambience, amazing decor, fantastic vibe. The food was not only delicious, but it was also very nicely decorated, it was pleasant to look at it and to eat it. Cocktails were amazing too, Very rich and full of flavor. I'll try to come back here again, however getting your situation here is really hard. Overall we had a fantastic time here, and would love to visit it again.

Cosme is a special occasion type of place for us. The food is really good, but for the price you are paying the portions are really, really small. You won't walk away hungry though because the corn tortillas will fill you up.

I especially enjoyed the complimentary spicy pumpkin sauce they serve you at the start of the meal. The copia al pastor was amazing. The corn husk meringue is also not to be missed. It was weird but delicious (not to mention instagram worthy).

I actually didn't think the cocktails were amazing, especially based on how hyped the bar program is supposed to be. I would also skip the mushroom and squash dish. It was absurdly small for $25!  They could also work on their service. Our waiter was fine, but not very attentive. We waiting a long time between drinks, for instance.

The food is really very good but then you are expected to pay for it.  A classic New York #hottesttableintown scene inside... I'm pretty much over that. Not sure I will rush to go back until it gets a little less trendy and/or someone else is paying. But I'm glad I went.

So overrated, so overpriced. Came here with high expectations, left very disappointed. I really don't understand the rave reviews. Most of the dishes were average at best, and even the ones we enjoyed were nothing that special. Spent around $100 per person on food and at that price point, there are SO many better places in the city. Don't bother.

- Uni tostada: This was my favorite dish of the night, but I love uni and bone marrrow and tomatoes so you would have to try really hard to make me not like this dish. Would order again.
- Razor clams (celery salsa, crystal hot sauce): Celery salsa overpowered the razor clams. Nothing special. Would not order again.
- Scallop: Decent but also nothing special. Basically exactly what you would expect, but I've had better.
- Black garlic rubbed NY strip: Taste was average. Not bad but not worth the price tag.
- Duck carnitas: meat was tender, skin was crispy, but flavor was lacking. Got boring very quickly. Taste of the duck was so mild that when you eat it with the tortillas, you can barely taste the duck. Don't understand the hype at all. There are way better ducks out there.
- Husk meringue: points for uniqueness. It was interesting and I enjoyed this. The corn flavor was interesting. Would not crave this but would order it again if I were ever forced to come back.

Had another dessert that was unmemorable. Also, thought the drinks were weak. Thinking of all the other places I could have gone for the money spent makes me sad.

I had high expectations going in so that could be the problem. Don't get me wrong, everything was good, service was great, venue was a good scene but prices were high and the flavors weren't new. Overall it is solid food but it just didn't live up to the hype and I won't be rushing back. Started with the Char, Scallops, Cobia and had the Duck for the main. Best dish was the Cobia al Pastor.
Really enjoyed the entire meal here. Pork rind, asparagus, octopus, duck tacos, strip steak, cobia, burrata, lobster, uni, husk meringue... they were all great. Also, try the Mexican wine.

This is one of those 'as good as it gets' restaurants. Prices are super high for the size of dish you get, but it's a culinary flavor adventure that is worth taking at least once... although I will definitely be coming back. 

+ UNI TOSTADA - first timing having uni and not a huge fan of the texture. the flavor of the rest of the salsa, homemade tostada, etc was amazing though
+ CUCUMBER LIME JICAMA SCALLOPS - YUM! so fresh and flavorful. 
+ MUSHROOM TACOS - this dish was a great flavor combo and a mush if you are a mushroom lover
+COBIA AL PASTOR w/ PINAPPLE PUREE - AMAZING! terrific quality fish and the flavors jump out and punch/massage you in the face in all of the right ways. The pineapple puree takes this to the next level.
+ DUCK CARNITAS - People aren't kidding when they say this is the best things ever. The most tender duck meat ever in existence plus amazing homemade corn tortilla.  Truly enough for 3 people.
+ BEET SORBET CHOCOLATE GANACHE - beautiful presentation and heavenly flavors. you def need to like beets for the sorbet portion of the dish though
+ HUSK MERINGUE w/ CORN MOUSSE - sounds weird.. it AMAZING and yes kind of weird. 

Terrific service. Kind servers. Fun atmosphere. Terrific food flavors.

Delicious food with vegetarian/vegan options. But the portions are TINY for the high prices. Same with drinks - a few sips in a big glass with bigger ice cubes. Go on someone else's dime. Also noisy/industrial vibe if that's your thing. Great wait staff.

Overall disappointed and expected a lot more. Food portions were small, except for the duck, which was ridiculously overpriced! Food was okay in general and there weren't many good cocktail options. Service was good.

This week's fashionplate is at avant garde Mexican spot Cosme in Flatiron.  Even though it's been open for months it's still uber hard to get a reservation, you need to make one in advance unless you want to brave the bar when they first open.  The blond wood bar is expansive and they have a huge tequila and mezacal selection which is pretty dope.  I actually started with the expat martini which was good but I wanted to move on to margaritas after that. My friend and I decided to share a few of the small plates.  We got the arctic char tostada which was yummy and perfectly flavorful.  We also got the scallop ceviche which was my favorite, light and perfect.  The enfrijolada was a more comforting dish that was also quite good.  We then decided to get the steak tacos which were also good.  Yes, the portions are small but we went there already knowing this.  We ended with the chocolate ganache which was our least favorite part of the meal, it wasn't bad just not as chocolatey as we like.

Now on to the fashion part of the fashionplate, the crowd was a mix of trendy couples on dates, young professionals expensing their meals and friends looking to enjoy Thursday night.  Definitely dress to impress but keep it cool.  See how I paired out new Katherine shirtdress below, the perfect day to night look to take you from work to dinner to Tribeca Film festival afterparties for the Adderall Diaries at American Cut.

I definitely would not recommend this restaurant. Food is good, not great. Prices are ridiculous, particularly the octopus entree which was an appetizer portion. Shameful. The bean salad and chocolate ganache was a joke. On food alone we paid $70 per person and left hungry. When the waiter says each person should order 3 things, he is correct. We were still hungry though when we left. Enough said, but I'll describe a little more about the experience otherwise. 

First of all I'll say, we didn't get the duck carnitas. The pictures on yelp of the hamachi and the cobia are not how it came to our table. The hamachi was missing the green sauce and the cobia was sloppily in a bowl. 

The waiter and food runners are knowledgeable about the menu which was nice. The mescales was delicious.

A rip off, sadly. Pitched as "modern Mexican" but more like a modern Hunger Games.  A nice atmosphere, but super small, over-priced portions.  We got an app ($18) and then an entree that was advertised as meant for 2 (price $60). The entree was bare bones and although we ordered an entree for 2, they gave us 1/2 the normal tortillas. The servers, upon seeing we were not happy about the price/offering, retreated vs. engaged to see what can be done.

One of the best Mexican restaurants I've ever been to! All the food was fantastic and the drinks didn't disappoint either. We had the uni tostada, the cobia al pastor, and the duck - the cobia was one of the best things I've ever had, the pineapple sauce was unreal. I can't recommend this place enough!

This is my first time ever writing a review, good or bad about any establishment but our dinner last night was so offensive that I had to comment.  This atmosphere is pretty and the staff was attentive but the portions were so tiny and over priced that we left after many small plates in search of the closest pizzeria.

I went to Cosme on the day before Valentine's Day with my boyfriend (I know, late review). Overall, the experience was okay, but could be better. 

The main reason I wanted to go to Cosme is because I wanted to try the well spoken about Meringue with Corn Mousse. 

This is what we ordered: 
Uni Tostada: It's basically a round tortilla with bone marrow on it. I personally didn't like the taste of the bone marrow. Overall, an interesting dish to try that you probably can't find anywhere else. 

Stuffed avocado, seafood vuelve a la vida, horseradish: It's half an avocado stuffed with salsa and pepper. I didn't taste the horseradish. The salsa had a lot of flavor, but thought it was a little too overpowering the more I ate it. It's probably best to eat this dish slowly. 

Mushroom and squash barbacoa, chilpachole, hoja santa: I overall dislike this dish. It tastes very earthy and I'm not quite fond of earthy flavors. If you like dishes with an earthy taste, I would strongly recommend this. 

Potato tamal, ayocote beans, fresh ricotta: A soft tortilla with beans on top. Probably wouldn't order this again, because you can get tortilla and beans pretty much anywhere. What makes this dish different than other restaurants is that the beans in this dish is very fine. It has a paste consistency. 

Iced Chocolate Drink: This isn't the real name of the drink. It's a sweet and spicy drink. Imagine hot chocolate, but cold with added spicy-ness to it. It's an interesting drink, but not sure if I would order it again.

Then it was time to order dessert. We ordered the pear ice cream. It was delicious with the perfect amount of sweetness.

Overall, I'm quite disappointed with the restaurant, not because of the food we got, but because of the dishes they were missing. We originally ordered the lobster and the duck carnitas, but the restaurant ran out of it. I felt really bummed out. I felt even more bummed out when our waitress told us they ran out of Merengue with Corn Mousse.

Why doesn't this place have a total 5 star review for everything?  Its sooooooo good. Service was perfect...they didn't miss a beat. Always someone table side to get water or wine.

Every dish came out hot and delicious. We seriously had no fails on any one dish. They were all truly unique. Did use Yelp reviews to guide us to specific ones though. Will try different dishes next time for a more rounded review.

Pricey but worth it.

I wouldn't be surprised if Cosme makes the list of Michelin-star rated restaurants pretty soon

My top recs: duck carnitas, hamachi and husk meringue

THe FOOD:
The duck carnitas was out of this world, unbelievably amazing, great flavor, super tender. It is a huge portion,enough for 3 people, easily. The sauces were a great compliment.
The hamachi was delicous and did not disappoint. However, I must admit that I am devoted fan of yellowtail sashimi and jalapeno).
The burrata was good but I do not think it was a highlight. I feel the same about the chicharron, it was ok but I probably wouldn't order it again. We also tried the frijolada which was good and different.
Now for the dessert, we ordered the husk meringue and the chocolate ganache. The husk meringue did live up to the hype and I would have it over and over again. If you are a fan of majarete, you would love this dessert. The chocolate ganache was good but the highlight was the husk meringue for sure.
Drinks: my entire table loved the Striptease..we liked and definitely recommend, it's light, refreshing and not too sweet. The Ninja was good, but I preferred the striptease.

THE PLACE
I loved the place; the bar is pretty spacious with a good selection of drinks and wines. The dining area is small which supports why it is so hard it is to get reservations at this place. I appreciated the effort behind the lighting fixtures: the lighting focus was the center of the tables giving the place the appearance of a dimly-lit restaurant but making your food the center of attention.

THE PRICE
Cosme is on the pricier end but well worth it given the quality of the food and very well crafted meals and flavors. Definitely a place to impress any foodie, great for dates.
Love!! Best Mexican Along with a fun trendy crowd! Just make sure you makes resos way in advance unless you like to eat at 5:00 or 11:00

A bit on the expensive end, but very good, high quality food and drink.

We spotted a reservation for four on a Sunday evening, and the place was quite busy throughout most of the evening. We split a bunch of apps and entrees--for starters, we split the uni tostada, the hamachi, and the burrata, all of which were good but not that outstanding. The burrata was probably my favorite, while the hamachi was clean but ordinary and the uni tostada fresh but didn't suit my fancy that much. For entrees, we split the octopus, red snapper, and the duck carnitas. The duck was quite tender and flavorful, and I'd definitely recommend it for groups. The octopus was solid, although it could have been a bit less cooked, but I didn't enjoy the snapper that much. The corn husk meringue we had for dessert was outstanding--the flavor was unique, and it was a nice, fairly light end to the meal.

The drinks are nice, and the service throughout is helpful. It's a bit on the pricier end, but if you're willing (and able) to get a spot here to enjoy higher end Mexican food, I'd suggest coming here for a meal.

The entrance of the restaurant has a stunning bar.

We started the meal with the Jack be Nimble Jack be Quick, made with Dickel Corn Whiskey, Elijah Craig 12 yr Bourbon, Zacapa Rum 23, Smith and Cross Rum, house made corn syrup mole bitters, and flamed orange twist. It was delicious!

To start the meal, we were brought complimentary chips and salsas. They were much fancier than your typical fare and I didn't really prefer them.

To start, we split the Burrata (so trendy, plus it had weeds! who knew?) and Cobia. Both were nice and lighter. We were prepping for the duck and needed to save room for the heavy dish!

The duck carnitas were out of this world - so rich and full of flavor. This is the most expensive entree on the menu ($59) and meant to be shared. For the two of this, it was challenging to finish as the duck is quite filling. If you're with four people, it would be perfect. It is that large a serving. 

For our second round of drinks, Frank got the Scoville Sour which featured a spiced cucumber garnish. I got the classic margarita, made with Tequila, Cointreau, Curacao, Lime and Salt. 

For dessert, we got the dessert drooled after by foodies on Instagram: the Husk Meringue with Corn Mousse. This is an incredibly unique dessert, especially if you aren't a "dessert person" - it is sweet without being cloying...think...sweet like corn. duh!

I had a delicious experience at Cosme. The food, cocktails and service are top notch. Give it a shot...if you can get a table :0

While it took me two months to get a decent reservation, i was not disappointed : duck carnitas, uni/bone marrow, corn husk meringue, and atmosphere, everything was great. 

I was slightly disappointed by the lobster dish - try something else !
cocktails here are pretty solid. my fav dishes here were def the uni and the meringue dessert. the king crab and octopus dishes are also good but beware the portion is super small.

Great restaurant and love the ambiance. I need to caveat this with the fact that it was really hyped up to me before I got there but it was a really good meal.

Everyone raved about the duck. The duck was really good. Everyone at my table claimed that this was the best duck that they have ever had. Now I thought the duck was good but again, a lot of hype. 

Other things I enjoyed were the hamachi, uni, and steak. Everything as you would expect were all perfectly cooked. The drinks were also all well balanced. At the price point this place was charging the meal lived up to expectations and was very good.

Worst meal in NY. We came here for our last night in town because we had seen such glowing reviews. We had to wait to be seated for our reservation. But we were having a lovely time at the bar. Then we went to our table. The waiter seemed to have more tables than he could handle. Drinks were left empty. Plates were hustled into place with mumbled, 'I'm sorry's. The dishes were supposed to come out in two flights but we were left for 2 hours with dishes coming out only after we asked after them. My sister who ordered a bottle of wine was left for 10 minutes and then her date was offered the taste. Most people working were bumbling, pouring sparkling water into still water glasses. All would be looked over at a cheaper establishment. But to have a 28 dollar 3oz octopus dish, we expect a certain level of service. When we approached management about our disappointment they were despondent and argumentative. As we were left to drip dry (no toilet paper in the bathroom), we begged for our coats only to be greeted by our bill with a 'have a great day' (our reso was at 930pm and we couldn't escape til nearly midnight, still hungry). I have never been so insulted by clumsy service. Run from Cosme. Go to any number of incredible NY restaurants with a lower price point and better food and service.

This must have been an off-night for this restaurant. We read such glowing reviews, we couldn't wait to go. But, when we arrived, the hostess never made eye contact with us or her staff when she had us seated.The waiter didn't know what a confit was until I explained it.  The mojito was so over-limed, we had to send it back. The burrata was excellent, but the guacamole was less than mediocre, and certainly not what you would expect from a supermarket let alone a high end restaurant. The scallops were fresh and delicious.  The stuffed avacado was very good. The sirloin steak was hillarious. It was several miniscule slices with absolutely no flavor at all. I didn't even recognize it was steak when it was brought to the table.  I thought they brought us the wrong order. The cod was a joke. It had no seasoning or favor, and the sauce it was served with tasted like bottled barbecue sauce. The best thing of all were the chips served with the guacamole. The interior of the restaurant is very appealing, and we loved the atmosphere.  Too bad the food was so bad.

Enrique Olvera has done it again. I love the ambiance, very good service, great cocktails and most importantly, good food. 

Must haves: Cobia al pastor, crispy octopus and the duck carnitas. 

I was rather disappointed at the enfrijoladas but the desert made up for it- one the most exquisite I've ever had. Do not leave without having the corn pudding and the beet sorbet.

Overall I feel very meh about Cosme. The food and service were ok/fine, but not outstanding. Because of this, it also felt seriously overpriced. Yes, we ordered most of the "must have" dishes mentioned here several times, plus others. Good, but none were terribly memorable. And I just can't justify $35 for a few tiny pieces of steak when one of them was so inedible (a bad, chewy cut) I was forced to spit it out. Our waiter was informative yet barely around. We had to do a lot of searching to find him for more drinks, food and the check. For this type of restaurant I expect a certain level of attentiveness which just wasn't there. 
I did love the decor and the vibe. And the bussing/running staff was good, if not a little overeager to clear. 
I wanted to be wowed, and maybe since it was my birthday I was a little more excited than usual, but I definitely left disappointed.

It is really tough to get a reservation for this place, but easy to show up late and have a seat at the bar. 

The service is merely ok. We sat at the bar and conversed with the bartender, who was helpful but by no means irresistable or Union Square Hospitality Group-level-charming. Just basic, decent service. 

The food was OK. It is pricey, portions are small. Cooking is pretty good, but doesn't justify the prices or the novelty. Standouts were the duck carnitas (in which you essentially get an entire confit of duck for $60. Bargain? Not according to Chinatown or any French bistro standards.) 

Only thing on the menu where the hype may be justified is the husk meringue. That thing is light, airy, and ethereal. 

Was really excited, but sorry, Stupak gets my votes.

I am so torn. Fantastic margaritas, great service, beautiful venue, interesting dishes...but...not worth the hype. Way overpriced, too few vegetarian options for my fellow diner, and well, I've had better Mexican food in the city. Given how hard it is to get a reservation I will be giving this one a miss in future.

A solid meal, but definitely doesn't live up to the hype or the 3-star Times review.  The two no brainers, as others have mentioned, are the duck carnitas and the husk meringue corn mousse dessert (easily the best single thing we ate.)  otherwise, i would skip the burrata -- bland and def not worth the $25 price.  I'd have felt better about the meal if the portions were bigger and the prices were smaller.  The cocktails were tasty but also didn't live up to the hype.  Bottom line: decent meal, a couple of great dishes, but really expensive and I don't think the value lives up to the price tag.  Other than the husk meringue dessert, I'm not sure anything else here stands out as truly memorable 18 hours after the meal.
Not much else to say than what had been said, great vibe, great food, portions are small but amazingly tasty and well presented. Worth going to and worth waiting to return to.
Service great! Food needs lots of work! Small portions and not tasty at all! One of the girl Manager on duty very fake smile! Stay away if you want real food.

Definitely worth the hype. Would label the food and drinks "Trendy Mexican" . Tasted very authentic but the presentation made it very NYC trendy. Amazing food and ambiance and can be great for friends or dates. Would not recommend for large parties. Their drinks are spectacular and go very well with the food. The restaurant is nicely decorated and located in a great part of town. The service was good and pretty quick. Do not expect to be seated within the hour if you do not have a reservation. Will definitely go back.

Super average and excessively over-priced. The best bet here is to sit at the bar, order the uni  toastada, the corn husk meringue, wine rather than any of the watered down, not-as-advertised cocktails, and leave happily. Those are the only dishes that stand out (and they're not life-changing), everything else can be had better elsewhere. Money is not an object for me when it comes to dining, but it should be proportional to the experience, the quality, the imagination and the artfulness of the dishes and the service. None of those were in line here. The cocktails particularly were a joke - the striptease with mezcal and absinthe salt (read, just salt, not a trace of absinthe flavor to be found anywhere in the drink) aside from a very faint mezcal flavor, tasted almost identical to the Paloma (tequila and grapefruit).  Steak tacos were fine but meh. And the $20 dollar burrata, which sounds like a divine idea over salsa verde, lacked any bit of the delicious oozy cream that burrata should have. It was more like rubbery, store-bought mozzarella with dainty greens on top. Service was slow and mixed up. The waiter(s) were decently versed in the dishes but seemed more concerned with telling us that we weren't ordering enough (we were). Had we listened, the two of us would have ended up with two dishes a piece from each of the three sections of the menu. Despite the small size of the plates that would have been Guy Fieri sized over ordering. We went with three from the appetizers, the burrata, split a main (steak tacos) and dessert. Props to our bus boy who was by far the most attentive of the 3 or 4 different servers who waited on us. Not at all worth the month long wait or the hype - this place is no Dorsia ;) There is far better and continuously engaging Mexican to be had in this city - Empellon Tacqueria is miles above this over-hyped flavorless joke and it's always evolving, as are the other Empellon restaurants. Pompano in midtown is better than this if more traditional, Maya in the East Village, hell I'd endure the Sex in the City vibe of Dos Caminios over this place. The decor was pretty lacking at this level as well - I'm not sure if they actually were, but it looked like they were hawking wares, along the shelves lining both sides of the restaurant. The lights were dim which was good because if they weren't the IKEA chic decor would have been revealed in all its lackluster glory. I can't imagine this place will sustain itself after the hype is over. Actually that's not true, there are plenty of folks with average palates and too much money in the city, and many of them eat along Park Ave South. To them I say "Enjoy!" To everyone else, have those two dishes and say you did, then book a table at any of the better Mexican places in town. Oh and lastly: we took our remaining food to go and they only gave us half of it. I guess we should be thankful for that.

Great ambience. Great food. Order the duck and then the corn mousse dessert. That's all you need- I wouldn't waste money again on the tiny appetizers. Duck and mousse were among the best dishes I've had in my life. Best duck I've ever had. The ganache with beet sorbet was actually outstanding but my mind was so blown away by the mousse that I couldn't focus on it. 

Appetizers are small and difficult to share. While good to very good generally, they were very expensive for the size and not super memorable. The bussing staff was excellent and attentive but our waiter wasn't within sight as often as we would have liked.

Ultimately the bill was over $100 each with no drinks and feeling a bit hungry after.  I wasn't thrilled about this- if the duck and dessert wasn't so amazing it would not have been worth it- but it absolutely was.

Ok here's the deal. You need to come here and order the duck carnitas. Forget about everything else. Splitting it between more than 3 people will turn into a violent fight, because everyone will want more. Everything else is pretty good, but the duck is the main reason to come here.

Takes about a month or so to get a res for this place but it's definitely worth the hype..overall amazing dining experience as the food and service were top notch! We started with the uni tostada which was basically a purple corn tortilla smothered in avocado, bone marrow salsa and topped with a cucumber . This was amazing; the perfect blend of fresh but never overwhelming flavors. We also tried the stuffed avocado with "vuelve a la vida" which means back to life; and yes the flavor combo in this seafood ridden plate will do just that!!!
For the main dish we had the duck carnitas accompanied by two different salsas and this was delicious as well. DON'T SKIP THE SALSAS!!!
The corn husk meringue for dessert was so light but the most perfect way to end such a feasty meal. 
Will be coming back to Cosme just for the bar as they had the most extensive and interesting drink menu!
Olvera successfully fuses Mexican and New York cuisine into an beautifully tasteful experience.  Order the burrata, red snapper, and the ayacote bean salad.

It was a total stumble upon not planed walk in.  They have a heavy velvet curtain at the door makes the entire inside very private. But once you walk in its a gigantic rectangle space. They have very special dishes here looking amazing but we just had dinner. I got two dry white wine from the cute girl bartender and she's very friendly and he got a lemon cake which is very small with cake on side and a lemon ice cream on the other side. Very nice. The bar area is big and spaces which I like a lot.

The British usually start with an apology before being critical.  However, on this instance, I will skip this and go straight into criticism... Cosme is, simply put, the most overrated and overpriced restaurant I've been to in a very long time.  

The dishes are pathetically small, taste nothing of Mexican food except for the tortilla and cost an arm and a leg for not much in the plate.  I've haven't been that disappointed in a very long time, particularly since a few people kept telling us to go there after reading good reviews.

I most certainly shan't be returning.

I knew bf and I were going to stuff ourselves and indeed, we are still recovering from last night's feast this morning...but the binge was worth it.

Uni tostada: Probably my favorite bite of the meal. The uni was almost overpowered by everything else on the chip, but overall I loved the way the flavors and textures intermingled. I could eat this every day.

Sliced raw hamachi: It seems like different tables get different numbers of pieces, at least according to what I've read from other Yelpers' reviews. (We got 5 pieces.) The fish was delicious and succulent and fresh.

Guacamole: I didn't even notice this on the bottom corner of the menu until bf ordered it. Guac was very tasty and made even better when eaten with a bit of the spicy pumpkin salsa they give you to start. However, I would only order this if you're in a group of 3 or more, otherwise it takes up too much room in your stomach that could be better used for other delicious dishes!

Potato tamal: Granted I don't have a lot of experience with tamals so I'm not sure what they normally taste like, but this was the most forgettable dish of the evening. Texture was nice and smooth, but it didn't have a lot of flavor. 

Burrata: Might seem heinous to pay $25 for burrata, but this was SO GOOD. The inside was all gooey and the flavor was addictive and well-balanced. Yum yum.

Broiled red snapper: A very good piece of fish. However, its subtle flavors paled a bit in comparison to the spectacular deliciousness of the other dishes.

Duck carnitas: I know it says "to share" but we underestimated just how much duck was going to come in this dish....it is a LOT! (Especially after all the other stuff we ate lol.) The meat was juicy and tender, and the blue corn tortillas were warm and just beautiful. I wished that it came with a larger vegetable component, however; all that meat just becomes too much and needed something more than sauce/lime to balance it out.

On to dessert!

Husk meringue: Not very impressive to look at -- resembles a smashed ostrich egg -- but light and airy and tasty! Only some bites get that strong corn flavor, so you might have to dig for it. Bf's words: "luscious corny goodness and potentially as addictive as Oxycontin."

Parsnip flan: Was super disappointed that the sweet potato flan had become parsnip instead...regardless, it was super creamy and good, just not very flavorful (I'm told parsnips don't really taste like much).

Nixtamalized carrot, cinnamon cake, cream cheese ice cream: I get that this is supposed to be some sort of deconstructed carrot cake, but it fell kind of flat for us. The ice cream was the best part -- just delicious. The dense cake lacked flavor and was a bit dry. The carrot was just weird -- tasted just like water, as if all the carrot flavor had been boiled (or "nixtamalized") out of it. The three components didn't seem to work well together. 

I also had a margarita (at 6:15, they were already out of the cocktail I wanted -- Bonita Applebum -- wtf?), which was delicious.

All the hype surrounding Cosme is 100% deserved. I can't stop thinking about the duck carnitas and the corn husk merengue. I think they're going to haunt me for the rest of my life. The husk merengue was so good we ordered another one after we finished it. And we were considering doing the same for the duck but we stupidly decided against it. I want a lifetime supply of merengues and I wanna eat one for breakfast everyday so that I can start everyday loving the shit outta life.

My only gripe was the "half lobster" - it was teeny tiny (we thought describing it as 'half' lobster was misleading) but it was still excellent. 

Everything was fantastic though- I can't wait to go back for more. If you can get a table. go now.

5 stars for service  and taste...0 stars for what happened after...I had a fabulous experience  at Cosme--the bartender gave great recommendations and I loved every course however I had the worst food poisoning of my life afterwards. Mind you I ate every creature under the sea, I was so ill I was unconscious most of the night. I would like to think it was from drinks earlier because I had great service at Cosme!

Exciting Mexican in NYC - a hard table to get so be sure you make reservations.  I am sad they took the chilaquiles off the menu - it was so good :(
The tostada and salsa to start are delicious, its a refined version of getting chips and salsa!
The Duck Carnitas are delicious - come with an appetite, its enough for 2-3 ppl.  
For dessert, of course the must talked about Husk Meringue with corn mousse must be ordered.  It sounds intriguing and the presentation is striking.  I enjoyed the difference in the sweet Meringue and the salty corn mousse.  The meringue had a nice chewy texture but the corn mousse was little too salty.  I definitely appreciated the novelty of the dessert, because it really is different.

Worth reviewing!

The hype is confirmed!  The ambiance of the resto was trendy and simple.  Had 30 minute wait from our reservation time, which gave us a chance to scout the place. 

The one page menu definitely had very appetizing content.  We ordered the chicharron and the ayocote bean salad for apps.  They were delish! 

Chicharron had great hint of flavor of chili powder with textured easy crunch to it.

The Ayocote salad was refreshing with heartiness to balance the dish. 

For our main: we opted to share duck carnitas and that sealed the deal.  It was the best duck we've ever had and we've had plenty of fine dining experience.  This dish will be added to our list "for best [duck], go to cosme."

Credits to the staff.  The water glass was quite small and my water was replenished in real time once it reached close to empty status.

Definitely worth reviewing and will be back to try out the other dishes!

Cosme is fantastic!  I made a reservation a month in advance and glad I did. We arrive for our reservation and maybe had to wait 5 minutes so quick by New York standards in terms of waiting. I had read about some of the popular dishes so I came ready to order. My bf and I started off with a margarita and a mezcal cocktail. Both were fantastic. We ordered the scallop crudo and cobia appetizer. Both were fantastic. We then ordered the duck for 2. The duck is clearly their signature dish since everyone was getting it and it's been written up in numerous publications. It was delicious. IMO it was quite big because between me and my bf, we made around 7 tacos and still have meat to take home. We skipped the dessert (despite hearing about the corn husk) and had some mezcal instead. The service was exceptional. At one point, a bus boy took my marg away before it was finished. There wasnt much left but I did mention it to my waiter who immediately ordered me another one on the house. Trying to get a reservation to go back asap!

1). All things come to those who wait.
2). All is well that ends well. 

I think those are two proverbial phrases that nicely sum up my first* visit to Cosme. Let me explain!

1). All things come to those who wait. 
And wait we did. This restaurant has been super popular, so I understood that getting a reservation would be near impossible, but when we somehow (luckily! astonishingly!) did get a last-minute reservation we hoped that we'd at least get seated soon after our arrival. But we waited for 45 minutes before we were seated!! The hostess was apologetic, but still!

The 45 minutes did give us plenty of time to observe the dining room and really peruse the food and drinks menu. While the bar area was crowded and loud with anxious walk-in diners, the dining room area was spacious, dark, sexy and cool. And despite the dim lights elsewhere, lights shone down from above onto each table so diners knew exactly what their food looked like. The drinks menu was dizzyingly impressive; there were lots of creatively-named cocktails ("Jack be Nimble, Jack be Quick"!), Mexico City staples, wines (so many from Spain, Chile, France, and even one from Lebanon!), tequilas, and mezcales. 

The waiting didn't really stop. We were brought to our table and still had to wait a few minutes for our server to take our orders. Then more for the drinks to come. Then quite a bit until complimentary blue corn tostadas (so delicious!) with a pumpkin seed and habanero butter (packed some heat!) came.

2). All is well that ends well. 
Then...a dish came. We looked at it and took small bites that quickly turned into enthusiastic bites, and it was almost like our earlier disappointment had never even happened. After one big sigh of relief, an overwhelming sense of excitement for what was to come washed over us. I do have to say that the first dish that came out was something we didn't order, but they let us eat it anyway. Win.

a. Uni tostada: The crunchy, earthy goodness of that tostada was the perfect vehicle for the avocado, uni, bone marrow salsa, and a splash of lime. I was surprised with the generous amount of smooth, silky uni that was on top. J's shellfish allergy prevented him from enjoying this, but it was actually only an amount for one person anyway.

b. Chicarron: The chicarron was huge, crispy, and well-seasoned. The tomato-y hot sauce was the real winner of this dish, though. We jokingly considered ways to sneak the bottle out. 

c. Burrata: I was surprised that he wanted to order this, but I was glad we did! The burrata was thick on the outside with a really creamy center and that center mixed wonderfully with the salsa verde to create a heavenly dip of sorts. There was only one lone tostada to scoop everything with, though, which was a shame. 

d. Broiled red snapper: This was the dish that came by mistake, but we were so lucky! The snapper was cooked absolutely perfectly (so lean and moist), and the Thai hoja santa salsa added such a unique burst of flavor to elevate the dish.

e. Duck carnitas: Wow. The carnitas were braised in orange and Mexican Coca-Cola and served to us on a big skillet. The duck was sweet in a non-cloying way, and was the softest "melting in your mouth we don't even need knives" duck I've ever had. Building our own warm tortilla tacos with the duck and salsa verde was just...sigh, we felt so spoiled. 

We chatted briefly with two diners from Mexico seated next to our table who were writing an article about Cosme for a magazine. They were impressed, as were we, and they were happy that the chef was introducing the versatility and energy of Mexican cuisine to New Yorkers. They were also quick to inform us that this was just a small sliver of the different styles of food Mexico has. Until more restaurants open, I'll gladly eat these exciting dishes - dishes that are far from the fast food we've come to associate with the country. 


Likelihood of another visit:
*A second visit is almost guaranteed as the food was so delicious. I can't wait to come with friends. My golly gee, I'm still dreaming of the duck carnitas. The prices were very steep, but none of the dishes disappointed me in the slightest, so the wallet will just have to fatten up before a second visit. Hopefully the service will be better next time.

Starving in New York I wanted something interesting for dinner.  I picked one of the newer hotspots Cosme.

Like many restaurants the exterior is way to hard to find.  Black awning and lettering are not big "here I am" call outs.  The black drapes obscuring any other light only makes matters worse. So I ventured in on amateur night with great trepidation.   Fortunately for me there was room at the bar.  The decor is trendy/ modern with house music slightly audible above the patrons banter.  Light is dim, not can't read the menus dim but have a hard time seeing across the restaurant dim.  It creates a certain feeling of privacy even in a packed restaurant.

I sat down and was presented with the daily food menu as well as an ample menu of beer, cordials, wine and a nice cocktail list.  The cocktails were phenomenal.  vibrant and refreshingly paired to the menu.  

I started with the el Ninja - a delightfully playful drink with a kick at the end.  It pairs nicely with  my first the scallops.  Shaved and served with diced cucumber and jalapeno slices - the thinly sliced scallops melted over the tongue.

Next came one of the most wonderfully clean dishes I have ever had in a Mexican restaurant.  The perfectly cooked strip had a vibrant red that sat in stark contrast to the grilled peppers, pickled cucumber, and avocado tarragon puree.  The trick to this dish is enjoying all of the parts together, otherwise you risk missing full pallet immersion.  You know, I found this with most of the dishes I enjoyed here.  The warm tortillas worked perfectly to liberally fill all ingredients.

As I wrapped up dinner I wistfully dreamed of what the restaurant would be like with a full menu.  Until my next taco dine fine.

Awesome cocktails, sophisticated and generous.  The food was beautiful and equally delicious.  The palate is elegant and has delicate notes to full on earthiness that truly satisfies.  Great date and special occasion spot.

It has been quite some time since I have gone to such a terrible restaurant. In brief, here it goes: (1) the drinks are thimble sized - perhaps this is part of the wannabe perception that this is a high end restaurant; (2) signature dishes include the uni tostada avocado bone marrow salsa, cod, octopus, duck carnitas and NY strip for tacos. The tostado was god awful with absolutely little to know avocado surrounded by a mound of marrow and bland salsa on top. Cod was spice-less and tasteless. Duck was greasy and strip steak had no resemblance to steak and a meager portion for a family style menu. In an effort to fulfill our hunger to the very end, we ordered dessert, only to, once again, be disappointed with the lack of taste and creativity. Cosme managed to ruin "contemporary mexican inspired food" and is less than inspirational for aspiring chefs and foodies eager to try a varied form of Mexican style cuisine. In the end, I defined the cost of the evening as an expensive drinking night. On a positive note, the space is industrial meets modern and is very pleasant to dine in. I hope this one doesn't last long so some future talented chef can reap the benefits of a spaciously attractive interior space.

Ok so this is sort of 2 separate reviews in one ! First time I walked in was about 2 weeks after their grand opening & read online that they open at 5 turns out they open at 6 ! Not a big deal right? Well I walk in at 5 & there are ppl in the restaurant some eating some standing all dressed differently not sure if it was a soft opening or if it was staff b4 they changed or whatever but I walk in & sit at the bar & the hostess runs over like her hairs on fire & says their closed they don't open till 6 I say oh ok I'm just waiting for someone who should be here any minute could I wait for them I was refused & rushed out the door! For a restaurant that just had a grand opening I was appalled ! Now believe it or not I went back ( mostly due to the pressure of a friend who was dying to try cosme) this time was sooooooo much better the hostess sat us in a lovely lounge section in the front & was very sweet as was our server ! I had the duck carnitas & the husk meringue & about 3 tequila mixologist cocktails all was amazing ! One problem: it is very very very expensive! Would love to go back but not quite sure if it's worth the price tag !

Cosme has been much hyped, but this is one of the few places where I would say all the hype is worth it!  I had such an incredible meal here last week, and I'm not even really a fan of Mexican food.  Enrique Olvera is doing really great things in his kitchen and if I ever find myself in Mexico City I will most definitely pay his restaurant Pujol (one of the World's 50 Best) a visit.

Everything on the menu looked delicious, so hard decisions were made, but ultimately we went with the uni tostada, the hamachi and the eggplant tamal for starters.  The uni tostada was delicious (how could uni not be?), but the highlight for me was the hamachi.  The pieces were so fatty and simply melted in my mouth.  The eggplant tamal I would skip though on my next visit.

The duck carnitas were next, and this is a must-order.  Grubstreet recently ran a feature on how these are made, and they are a work of art.  They are cured for three days before being roasted, and the meat literally falls off the bone.  For $59, I almost felt this was a steal considering how many "chicken for two" dishes there are in Manhattan above the $60 zip code.  We finished the 6 tortillas they provided, and were promptly given 6 more.

At this point we were stuffed, but couldn't resist ordering the husk meringue.  The shell was kind of like an oversized macaron, and the corn mousse was SO creamy.  One of my all time favorite desserts.

This restaurant is not to be missed, and I look forward to coming back to sample more of Chef Olvera's menu.

Simply put this place does very little to live up to the hype.

On arrival waited 30 minutes for our table. Got attitude when I went back to check with hostess what was going on. After finally being seated, waiter never came over, when we finally requested to another staff member the waiter visibly sighed when one of our party asked him to take us through the menu. The whole staff vibe gave off the impression this place was too trendy to care about guests.

By this point, the whole experience was already ruined. That said, much of the food is very good. The duck carnitas are great, the burrata was tasty, the eggplant tamale was great too, and the octopus was solid. The drinks were very good too, including the margarita. That said, there is nothing exceptional about any dish we tasted. For the prices and the meager portions, once would expect something at least to blow you away. That never happened here, just good quality.  

Overall I wouldn't come back. Empellon is far better, Mesa Coyacan in Williamsburg is too, and for value and quality Casa Enrique in LIC blows this place away.

lots of hype on this one, appreciate the resume but just fell a little flat for me and my wife.

the food was very good but not amazing, and we really struggled with how to eat the tacos bc the portions of meat were too large to make a pocket and the meat itself was actually a little touch.

very cool ambiance and industrial aesthetic which usually puts me in the mood for whats to come but it honestly just felt like the meal never lived up to the hype.

the corn meringue was a very interesting dessert but not something i would ever crave or order again.

drinks were stellar but for a $250 dinner i expected just a little bit more from the food

I get that there's hype because the hottest chef out of Mexico City is making a statement in Flatiron. But the food just falls flat. 

Came here for a double date on V-Day. Decor is very hip, hostesses were nice, coats were taken. Couple next to us getting frisky. Ooh yea.

Drinks were 4 star. Off menu michelada - nothing to write home about. But other cocktails were stellar (expat martini, some others). Cheers to pouring large drinks given the price (ie scotch on the rocks). 

Food though... I've had mexican in the bronx, brooklyn and california. All better. This seems like watered down, high quality dishes. Everything was missing 'pop', was expecting a fresh take; Uni tostada was good but quality of the uni was midgrade. I thought all of their tostadas were overly baked/fried. Good crunch but flavor was cooked out. Beef tartare was good actually - just pint sized portion wrapped in a flaccid green pepper. Some more spice and citrus would have been appreciated. NY strip was very underwhelming. Meat was bland, not tender, and not sure if they let it rest properly. Flour tortillas were alright. Husk meringue was neat however the combination was odd. Sweet "husk" unbalanced with creamy corn mousse in the middle. I tried but couldnt. 
Veggie dishes did win over the meat dishes though. 

Service was good, but sloppy at times. Water spilled with no apology a few times, no plating or silverware at other instances. 

Its not a bad restaurant, but I just dont see myself going back.

This restaurant delivers on all levels. Great room, strong strong helpful and attentive service, fantastic cocktails with very informed and creative bartenders.  The food is great, not traditional but everything was so tasty.  I loved the chicharon and the duck carnitas, but the scallop dish was my favorite. So light and tasty!  Looking forward to going back.

Thoroughly confused by a mix of positive and scathing reviews that accompanied the opening of Enrique Olvera's NY outpost, I can nevertheless say that Cosme is one of the most exciting restaurants I have been to in the city.

What is brilliant about Cosme is that it can serve innovative Mexican food without falling back on culinary clichés or the gimmicky nature of some of the more unusual cuisine of the city.

The most memorable dishes were some of the raw options, which mixed the challenging technique of some Mexican classics with prime ingredients not immediately relatable to Mexican food. The Uni tostada was a prime example of this, mixing the briny, rich taste of sea urchin with the crispness of the tostada and a refreshing bed of chopped tomatoes.

Warm dishes excelled in both flavor and presentation. The tamal was soft and had a spectacular texture, and its dimensions were perfect in the context of the tasting menu. The green mole was of a gorgeous color, and a perfect mix of textures with several vegetables cooked properly al dente. The tortillas accompanying the dishes were unforgettable.

I second everyone's comments on the desserts, which are absolutely unexpected and refined. The corn husk meringue was an excellent play on flavors and textures, and Olvera escaped the temptation to make that sort of dessert cloyingly sweet. The parsnip flan was brilliant, especially considering how unappealing it would sound in any other context.

The level of service was excellent as well. All the staff was attentive, helpful and well informed. Definitely not something to be taken for granted in NY.

Walked in for the 4 course prix fixe on Valentines Day and was greeted by the friendly hostesses and seated shortly after. 

My server was quite knowledgeable about the wine list and described the red wine, Tinto de la casa, perfectly. I love this medium bodied wine from Mexico. Also they have an extensive wine list. Lots to choose from. Love that. 

To start, were tostadas served with a very good pumpkin seed habanero paste. Very tasty - I enjoyed this tostada more than at some other Mexican restaurants I've been to. 

I then had the uni tostada which I thoroughly enjoyed. Every bite had interesting textures and flavors. Very creative dish which I will certainly order again. This dish had thoughtfulness in flavor, but was never too intense that the flavors became distracting. One of my favorite dishes here. 

Next.. I had the wagyu tartare.. this was tangy, spicy and delicious.. I only wish that there was a little more beef to really enjoy the best part of it. The tartare is wrapped up in cucumber and served with a tostada. Good mix of crunchy/raw textures. 

For the main course, I ordered the garlic rubbed ny strip steak tacos with shishito peppers and avocado puree. These were some of the tastiest tacos I've ever had in my life. The steak I believe was medium rare to rare which is just how I like it. I ate four small tacos without feeling too full. It was perfection. Not too heavy which left me room for dessert. 

as for the highly anticipated husk meringue and corn mousse...  although the flavors were excellent...there was something about the combination of flavor and texture that did not amaze me. It's a great unique dessert with very interesting flavors, but I will try the parsnip flan for next time. 

Overall.. One of the better new restaurants that I've been to in a while. I will be back very soon. For creative contemporary Mexican cuisine.. definitely at the top of my list.

The decor is really nice, reminds me of an industrial loft. Lots of plant decorations that portray Mexico. Cool clay looking plates that also remind you of Mexico.

Like many other reviews, the hostesses were a bit brash. We had the sense that they gave off an attitude like "Are you guys walk-ins?". We got there a little early and waited by the door after they told us to wait. Nobody asked us to check our coats until we checked up on our table again later. This didn't happen with some other guests. Hostess was also just chomping on gum with her mouth wide open, pretty classy.

Wait staff is a lot better though, really attentive, polite, and explained everything. They even changed our cups (which were dirty and wet when we sat down) before I mentioned anything.

We ordered the Expat Martini and El Ninja for drinks. El Ninja is really great, lots of complex flavors. Expat Martini is pretty plain, very dry though, which is nice.

They ran out of the duck carnitas so we couldn't order that. It looked good on the table next to us though.

Food is decent, 3.5/5
Value is pretty darn awful.


The food:

Complimentary Tortilla with pumpkin seed spread - Tortillas here are pretty bomb. The spread was nutty and delicious with a little spice.

Hamachi - Really tasty, amazing acidic and spicy taste to this dish. You get 6 pieces of fish for 19$. Probably one of the best values on the menu and also one of my favorite orders.

Uni Tostada - Really delicious, you get a tiny 4 inch diameter tostada for 17$.

Burrata - one of the best dishes, super rich, really great flavors here. Pops open like an egg and just oozes everywhere. 24$

Octopus w/ mole - Ridiculous, you pay 28$ or 29$ for a 4 inch long tentacle. It was decent, but not even that good. We laughed when we saw the dish. One tiny tentacle. On a plate.

Black Garlic Rubbed NY Strip Tacos - 35$ for 6 slices of steak. A bit undercooked and pretty tough, not tender at all.

Red Snapper - overcooked, 28$ for a filet. Dry on the inside.



All in all - much better food for the same price all over NYC. The #1 chef in Mexico failed to impress. I would much rather go to Corona and spend 40$ for a boatload of food that has more flavor and is better cooked, than be all fancy and have pretty mediocre food with a few exceptions.

I do not recommend, there is too much hype. Maybe we went on a bad day, but I don't see what the fuss is about.

A MUST Try for you a MUST return for me.

Venue (4/5) Trendy, Trendy, Trendy without the cheesiness of the promoter type crowd.  Definitely a place to see 'the beautiful people' 'the beautiful couples' but without the obnoxious or pretentious feel.  Only mini problem... bar stools make you feel like you are getting into a truck, super tall (You'll understand when you visit)

Food (4/5) 
Food here is pricey, small plates, yet delicious.  Don't come here expecting cheap eats.  Think Mexican, Japanese fusion type tapas.  Very good!  I loved the uni dish and the instagram favorite corn dessert.

Service (4/5) good service.  Bartenders are fun and creative.

Cosme is the Carbone for Mexican cuisine. It absolutely blew me away. 

For starters, the service is impeccable. My glass was never empty and the wait staff anticipated my needs for more salsa, tortillas etc. The wait in between courses was a little long. 

We started off with the Uni tostada and the sliced raw hamachi. It was a little disappointing that the uni tostada is meant for one and it is $18. Instead, we split this in half and shared it. One thing to note is that you need to eat this right away or else the sauce from the uni will make the tostada soggy. 

The hamachi was impeccable. We got four slices of fatty hamamchi seasoned with fermented serranos, fish sauce and black limes. For the price, it would have been nice to have a few more slices. 

The Eggplant tamal was served with fresh ricotta. The presentation needed a bit of work. It wasn't clear if the wrapping was edible. The dish itself was delicious nonetheless. 

As our main entree we ordered the duck carnitas. This was absolutely phenomenal. The duck was cooked to perfection and the skin was succulent and flavorful. They offered salsa verde, salsa rojo and another sauce to top off the tortillas. I couldn't stop eating this even after I was full. 

For dessert, the musk meringue is a must! I am still reminiscing the flavor of the corn, the vanilla bean and the moist cookie. It is truly both a culinary masterpiece and aesthetic work of art. I can't wait to go back.
Shady rolled into NYC's next newest and hottest spot late on a frigid weeknight to check out all the fuss. Lets just cut to the chase, shall we? Duck Carnitas. Thank you. Good night.

Not sure why NYC still struggles with Mexican food. Duck carnitas were off the charts good...everything else was very average - all the way from the guacamole to the lobster.   Drinks were good, but unfortunately the bartenders will remind you so.   Service was slow, 2 hour 15 minute dinner for a 6:15 weekday reservation is a looong dinner.  Perhaps they are just working out the kinks.  

I really want to like this place, hopefully I can go back in a few months and give it five stars.
How much is this place paying for these Yelp reviews ? The portions are horrendous (smallest ever). Cosme won't be around in a year. My drinks were literally half full.

Hottest new restaurant, ridiculous to get a reservation- book well in advance, but if you manage to get in... You then understand why it's the hottest new restaurant that everyone wants to go to. 

Upscale Mexican. Great flavor, original, trendy environment. It's a place you must try. The atmosphere is industrial, something that you would probably see more so down in soho. Very cool and the tables are set up well. They didn't take long to seat us and the service was very prompt, polite and accommodating. 

For starters we ordered the lobster pibil, mussel tostada and chicharron with avocado and radishes. 

First off- for the starters, the lobster was hands down my favorite. The beans were extremely flavorful and it came with little tortillas. I could have ate 3 more bowls of it myself! The lobster was juicy and I was extremely sad to see it was all gone lol. 

I took only one bite of the mussel tostada because I'm just not a big fan of mussels unless it's cooked in some sort of broth. That's just my preference. The mayo sauce was really good though. The portion was really small and if you think about sharing that- think about how you would cut a tostada in half. Little difficult. Wish it came with two for one serving but then again, I just gave it away because I didnt care for mussels. 

The chicharoon was really good. Simple and fresh but nothing impressive. It reminded me of the bag of pork skins my sister loves with avocado and citrus- minus the price. And it doesn't come sliced or anything. It's just a long strip of fried pork skin and you need to cut it yourself. It would have been better if they at least cut it for you or fried it in circular disks. 
It was too simple for my taste. But it was still good. 

For the main dish we had the duck carnitas. Huge serving for two. I'm pretty sure everyone gets this. It's a large duck breast that you must shred yourself then comes with two different salsas and tortillas. 
Flavorful, juicy and extremely tender! You should easily be able to pull it a part with a knife and fork. There was so much left over that we needed to take it home. You could easily share it with 3 people. It's like a build your own duck taco. Delicious! 

The dessert we got was in my opinion the best part of this meal. A husk meringue with corn mousse. I don't even know where to begin with this dessert. 
The meringue is light, crisp with a pinch of saltiness that brings out the subtle sweet flavor of the mousse. This is one of the best desserts that I've ever had because it's so light and not overwhelmingly sweet. It's perfect. The mousse if fluffy and with combination of the meringue- it Comes together perfectly. This dessert is nothing short of sweet genius! 

Overall I left feeling satisfied and stuffed! Clearly the hype is not overrated at all and deserves another visit. Unfortunately the wait is about a month long! However well worth it! 

Highly recommend! I will be returning shortly and trying new appetizers, keeping the main dish and the dessert! 

Soooooo good!!! Can't express that enough times!

Great atmosphere but food was a flop. 

Guacamole was standard. A bit salty. Ordered the seafood stuffed avocado, it was alright. The eggplant was terrible. Presentation and taste was way off. 

Cod and snapper were both good for the entrees. 

On the plus side, the Striptease cocktail was great.

I was sorely disappointed by my visit to Cosme for dinner this week after reading all the great press about it. 

Ambience - it's extremely dark, not in a cozy way either. It's very sterile looking. On top of all this, it's way too loud in there! At a table of two, I couldn't hear my dining partner.

Food - all the food was oddly at room temperature. I don't know about you guys but I like my food hot when it's supposed to be.

Guac - not sure what the hype is about. It was very standard, nothing special. 

Uni toast - decent but watery

Al pastor crudo fish - not much to the dish in terms of flavor or filling. The tortillas that come with this dish are way too big.

Squash and mushroom dish was pretty good.

The bean dip was lackluster.

Steak tacos...the steak was very odd-looking. It almost looked smoke because the outside was gray but the inside looked like sinewy and red. Again, nothing special. Weird texture overall. 

Snapper - wish the skin was crisp. The squash spaghetti was plain. 

The famed tortillas were pretty good.

Margaritas were nothing special. The house Mexico City vino by the glass was excellent. First time having wine from Mexico City and I was thoroughly impressed. I was told it was specially bottled for this restaurant, which is too bad because I would have liked to buy it immediately to enjoy at home.

Service - found it to be intrusive and awkward.

Overall, I left full of tortillas and disappointed.

We have been waiting for a long time to eat here. Overall it was a good meal and by far the duck was the best dish. I was disappointed by the lack of flow though in bringing us drinks. The sommelier needs to improve her attitude and listen to the customer.
