I asked for a specific type of white and was directed to the most expensive bottle on the list and when I said it wasn't what I was looking for she seemed to become disinterested. It then took about 10-15 minutes to actually get the wine to our table at which point half our appetizers had been eaten. Next time i would likely come back and sit at the bar. A few kinks to be worked out but I would return.

Was very excited about this recent addition to the neighborhood. It's a gorgeous restaurant with an exciting menu.

However, it's safe to say the anticipation did not live up to the experience. Let's break it down

1. Service. Lovely hostess sat us at the communal table - we love a good communal table by the way. Though some how we blended into the woodwork because everyone else seemed to get served and we seemed to wait for what felt like ever to even get our drink order in (and I am not someone who likes fast and rushed, i love Spain and I love the way they do it, but 20 minutes to get a drink felt a wee bit much for this guy who love himself a cocktail). 

And well, I hate to say it, once our waitress made her way over it felt like we were supposed to feel grateful she made time out of her busy schedule to attend to us. I had questions on the menu (cuz when you see the menu it has loads of things I haven't heard of - which is fun and exciting) but when i ask what aquachile or pibil or smoked raws sepia is please don't explain those items to me as if i asked what oregano or horseradish was. (2 stars). 

2. Drinks. Though we waited a while for the the drinks, once they arrived they were fabulous and inventive and delicious. Cheers (4 stars)

3. Food, meh! Nothing was a standout to be honest - and if you read James L's review it says it all. I won't try and write as well as he did, so just go look. (2 stars)

4. We were excited enough about the place that we "might" give it another shot. I don't want to let one server sour my opinion totally, the bartenders looked super fun and engaged from where we were sitting, so fingers crossed the next time is a bit more fulfilling (and filling).

Fantastic service!  Guacamole is the best. I look forward to visiting again once the restaurant has evolved.  Best of luck!

@If you are not happy with something just let management know. These guys are working on a new business model and are welcome and eager to receive your feedback.

By far one of the best meals that I've had in a long time.  Great and original preparation, with ingredients that just mix perfectly.  Had the hamachi to start, moved onto the eggplant tamal, lobster pajil, and steak tacos.  Finished with the husk meringue.  As someone who isn't a huge dessert person, I'm so happy I gave it a shot bc it was phenomenal.  Like others have mentioned, the portions aren't huge, but it gives you the opportunity to indulge in a variety of things.  Would consider coming back for the duck carnitas, but knew it would be too much and had other things that we wanted to sample.

so after waiting 2 months for our reservation...I have to say don't bother..really, the hype is all it is hype.  the only dish worth going here for is the duck and that is the only reason I am giving Cosme 2 stars or it would be 1 star 
I was excited to eat here,  so the let down/disappointment was big. We had to return the steak - 2 people politely spit out their piece into napkins.  The tamale was so dry we sent it back also.  The guacamole was OK but had much better in low key hole in the walls.  I think mine is better and that really isn't saying much. The service was horrible - they were trying to take dishes away while we were eating -we finally asked them politely to let us finish our food which was still in the plate  before taking it away ..didn't work they still kept hovering in a very inappropriate manner for wait staff - it made us very uncomfortable. The mussel tostada, Mushroom and squash barbacoa and duck dishes were very good, Uni was OK too - Octopus do not bother - tamale - take it off the menu - steak - no clue what happen I just hope it isn't always that bad.  here is last one last comment - asked if we wanted dessert - I replied not sure but it is a birthday dinner - reply: oh, I will bring a cake - don't worry, I reply thanks that would be really nice (and thought making up for service, food, etc) - He never came back with cake!!! - at this point we were just laughing as this chef must be all the way to the bank on his customers dollar.  Really, this is just not worth the price you are paying for this food - way too many better places in NYC to buy into Cosme's hype  - and don't go hungry you will be starving after dinner...yes, the plates are that small (except the duck) and that expensive.   
Almost forgot - the bartender - he is good and makes good drinks so go for a drink at the bar but don't eat!!
Hostess/manager that night useless - they look great but that is about it  - just like the restaurant - all looks no show.  When we mention our problems they just stared at us like deers caught in headlights I guess they are use to people sucking it up and not saying anything bad...
Greateset Restaurant in NYC right now.  Amazing food and beverage service.  Very tough find anything to complain or even upgrade.

I was not expecting homemade or traditional cuisine, but something simply delicious from somebody who knows and understand mexican flavors. Maybe my expectations were too high, but definitely doesn't worth the $120 pp we paid, specially in NY.  It´s very far from Pujol.. 

As a mexican, I didn´t understand the food. Enrique needs more good friends and less flatterers and rankings.

Although, the staff was very attentive and they have a varied bar.

*** EDIT: Good place to brunch, the food is better and more affordable

good: corn husk meringue dessert, drinks

bad: inattentive server- forgot our complimentary tostada (didn't check on us after we got our apps, he was busy schmoozing with a 5 top VIP table), food was so-so, the chocolate ganache beet sorbet dessert was BITTER, the duck carnita was cooked to mush

according to Eater this place was the most relevant restaurant in 2015, many yelper said it was life changing (please read Anna E review- i summarized it below for you), but the only thing that changed for me, was that my wallet felt a lot lighter after leaving the restaurant. ($250 included tax and tips for 2)

Anna E review: 
Four days ago three talented cooks from a high-end, luxury hotel and a former member of a restaurant consultation company and amateur food writer (me) sat in silence, completely "wowed," while  we made our greatest attempts to bring ourselves back to reality from varying states of bliss. (GAG)...My boyfriend, lover of desserts and highly skilled, critical, and trained at two of the top restaurants in Connecticut (  2 OF THE TOP RESTAURANTS IN CONNECTICUT!!!! 2 OF THE TOP RESTAURANTS IN CT!!!!!!!)even declared that it might be the best dessert he has had in his life. ANNA E'S BF TRAINED AT TWO OF THE TOP RESTAURANTS IN CT! THIS PLACE MUST BE MAGIC!

Outstanding meal at Enrique Olveras restaurant, very unique dining experience and a must when in NYC. The only downside were the cocktails, not their forte. The Wine on the other hand was exquisite. I will be back and the topping of the night was the Merengue with corn mousse, WOW!

Trust me when I say that I am one to gawk at Emperor's new clothes as much as the next person, since I've been known to stand in line for hours in foul weathers, arthritic knees and all, for cronuts, ramen burgers and whatever thingamajig sweeping through NYC at any given moment.

I was shocked by the minuscule amount of food on the heels of those exorbitant prices.  I'd venture to say that three people can comfortably consume the entire menu without feeling like a pinata afterwards.  Naturally I wasn't expecting to pay Taco Bell prices for high-end, transcendent Mexican food, but the same money for 15 Chalupas was a lot to pay for 3 meager pieces of duck breast meat.   

I was there the night Wylie visited and he seemed to enjoy the food, without the meal being comped I might add, so I probably don't know what the heck I'm talking about.

Enrique Olvera is doing some pretty great work at this Flatiron hot spot, with an expansive menu of inventive and lovingly crafted dishes. I have got to say nothing I ate here really blew me away but it was all generally quite delicious.

I didn't bother with a reservation and just showed up here at like 5:40 and sat at the bar. The bartender, busboys, and general staff were all amazingly on point, helpful, and welcoming, which made the so-so meal better.  

Best dishes in declining order were:

1) The Mussel Tostada: I feel bad for anyone who comes to Cosme and gets the Uni Tostada instead of this only because this was definitely the best dish of the night and the Uni Tostada was by far the worst.

2) Mushroom and Squash Barbacoa: The flavors in this were amazing and well balanced but it kind of made me wish I was sitting at Mission Cantina.

3) Husk Meringue: This was really good. But look, it is simply a giant hollowed out macaron shell that has been split in two with whipped cream in the middle. It is extremely delicious, but that is literally all it is.

4) Half Lobster Pibil: This was actually pretty good although it did have a somewhat muddy taste, perhaps due to the beans. The salsa that comes with this is absurdly delicious though.

5) Uni Tostada: The uni on top of this was really fresh and quite excellent but the "bone marrow salsa" and lack of seasoning made the whole thing eaten together kind of a weird affair.

So, tldr: very awesome service, doesn't exactly live up to the hype food-wise, get the mussel tostada, oh and SUPER delicious blue corn tortillas served with the Mushroom and Lobster dishes.

Cosme is supposed to be one of the best new restaurants but I was underwhelmed . I started with the eggplant tamale. That was pretty good . I was off to a good start. We also had the frijoles app. It was also fine , nothing amazing . 

For entrees I had the lobster( if you want to call it an entree) . The portions are minuscule . I didn't like the combo of lobster with beans underneath. We also got the steak which was a very small portion. 

Last we had the husk meringue everyone is raving about .  I just don't get it . I didn't see anything really special about this either,   While the food isn't bad , you're paying a lot for tiny portions and i just didn't get much of a  wow factor with the flavors.

The food was extremely underwhelming especially since I had been looking forward to  eating at this place for sometime. The only dish with any flavor or substance I enjoyed on the menu were the Duck Carnitas and the desserts. I'm pretty sure the mussels, hamachi and uni gave me a stomach ache for the next two days. I am not exaggerating either becuase it was a company dinner and 4 of the 7 of us expressed the same sentiments. The drinks however were delightful. I'd suggests the Paloma. I had two!

Cosme is a new restaurant, filled and great fun. The service is excellent, mostly because there is a huge staff, much more than you would see normally. 

The food is delicious. The smaller seafood plates are beautiful to look at and subtle in their flavor. But the real winner is the duck entree. It consists of a perfectly cooked breast of duck which you break apart (easily) and eat on just made tortillas. There are a number of sauces to go with it but the flavor of the duck carries the dish. For those not concerned with calories, there is something like a giant round pork rind, which you eat with sauce slathered on top. I felt guilty as hell and happy as a clam. The first photo shown below is a desert we had. I can't even tell you what it is, but it was delicious!!. 

All these small plates add up, but here it's worth it. The decor is good, the lighting is good, but if you're looking for an intimate place for a first date, it's not here. Go with a gang, drink the delicious margaritas, and share amazingly good food.

The food was good, but I am not sure what all the "guato" is about. 

I had seen all of the hullabaloo about Cosme...months to get in...Pujol in NYC. I have eaten at Pujol, maybe 8 years ago. When we were able to get a table, I was surprised and excited. We arrived thirty minutes early. We ordered a couple of Palomas. They were good. And were seated about fifteen minutes before our reservation. The space is nice and reminds me of my uncle's house. 

We started the evening with blue corn tostadas and a pumpkin seed and habanero spread. The spread was one of the more cleaver items of the night. Next, came the guacamole that according to our dinner neighbors was "sublime." It was good, but sublime it was not. It was mashed avocado with cilantro and white onion and some chips. Then came chicharrón with Valentina sauce. I liked this dish. Simple and refined at the same time. Chicharrón and Valentina sauce are a Mexican staple. Cosme, however, up'ed the ante by adding a salad on top--thinly sliced avocado, heirloom tomatoes, serrano, and radish with some greens and cilantro. I would order this again. It reminded me of the vendors outside of church. 

The next course was a tostada with bone marrow. Again, good, but wow it was not. But, the next dish was wow. I loved the octopus with pickled red onion with Mexican oregano, black beans, cilantro, and charred avocado. It took a little bit of work to get everything on the fork at one, but it was worth the work. Great dish!!! If all of the plates had been this good, the guato would have matched the experience. For the main dishes we had the Pozole and the New York Strip tacos. They were okay. For dessert, we had the sorbets and a tequila, Clase Azul. The prickly pear was very good and the tequila list was legitimate. 

Bottom line--it was good, I would eat there again, and I would recommend it. But other than the pumpkin seed spread, chicharrón, and octopus, the rest of the meal was just good. It did not match they guato--hype. I would have really like to seen a molé on the menu and I would like to have tried the duck, maybe next time.

Wow! So little food, for so much money! The food was very tasty and inventive, and the waitstaff was very attentive, telling us lots of details, but because the music was so loud, we couldn't hear much of what they said. We enjoyed the burrata cheese, about the size of a baseball, for $24, as well as the six small slices of hamachi. The steak for tacos was nice, but there we had to get more tortillas. 

After spending close to $200 for 3 people, we were still hungry, and went elsewhere for mac & cheese to fill up. The food is very nice, so if you're on an expense account, or someone else is paying, then fine, go there. You'll want to order a lot, or you'll go away hungry.
How soon can I go back?  Duck carnitas!  It's a Pujol-light version, but still worth it.  Service and drinks are solid too.

Nice environment, interesting food, but I wouldn't go there again. The duck carnitas is great and large enough for 3 people. The Burrata is amazing, I actually don't like Burrata but this one is really good! The tamales with eggplant are good and the octopus salad is a disaster. Again, is an interesting restaurant that you should visit but in terms of food taste and quality, nothing to write home about.

I want to start by saying the girl who answered the phone is rude so ignore her. The dining experience was nice but the food was bland.  It's like sushi meets Mexico.  Everything is like tapas style but your left waiting for your favorite bite. We ordered guacamole wanting something filling and it's an avocado diced up in a bowl with tortilla chips, that's it!  Avg price is $20 and you get 4 bites if your lucky.  Vibe is good and decor is good but if your hungry I do not suggest you go here!

Service great, decor and atmosphere of restaurant very good,  Found food to be very interesting and very good.  And yes, it is not a typical NYC Mexican (i.e. tex-mex) cuisine.  However, the food tastes did miss a little of the "kick" one gets from what we usually take to be Mexican food.  Desserts and coffee were excellent.  In summary, very much enjoyed the experience and would go back, but at same time, cannot say any of 6 food plates we ordered were OMG and yet, dinner for 2 easily exceeded $200.  .

Cosme is going fast to be the best mexican restaurant in New York City.
The attention to all details is complete and fancy.
Its a whole new experience of very good mexican food and a place to be with friends, family or doing business.
Congratulations to all partners-owners for this wonderful place in New York City.
Mexico is very well represented.

Cheers,

Leonardo Estevez

I chose Cosmo to celebrate my husband's birthday. The food was delicious. This is definitely Mexican fine dining. We enjoyed the sepia and white bean dishes as our apetizers. Our main meals were very impressive. The sirloin steak and branzino were prepared perfectly to our liking. We will definitely be back.

Great ambiance. It's near impossible to get a table but they have lounge seating available up front and it is just fine. Service was attentive and friendly. Came just to have dessert but opted for a savory bite and got the uni tostada. Well balanced dish - texture and flavor wise. Right amounts of spice, salt & acid. The uni was on point. 

Had heard about the corn husk meringue so that followed the tostada. It definitely merits the hype. Just the right amount of richness, not overly sweet.  The only quibble - $14 is kinda pushing it for any dessert even in this town.

Lot's of hype going on for this new hot spot. It's located in flatiron in a pretty big space, and quite trendy. So excited I got reservations. Let's just say I'm glad I did!

They start off with complimentary tostada and a dipping sauce..
- Snacks we had the Uni Tostada: Great but not over the top
- Octopus was good as well but also not the star of the night
- Lobster: pretty good and comes with corn tortilla
- Duck carnitas for two: Winner! This is by far the winner of the night. The duck was so tender and soft. Definitely was more then enough for two people. I was completely full after this dish.
- Of course for dessert we had the famous Husk Meringue, corn mousse. Quite interesting but the corn mousse was pretty delicious.

Overall this modern mexican restaurant will be pricey. All dishes are very small, so best to order quite a few dishes. Would definitely come back.

Having been to Pujol in Mexico City, I was excited to try Cosme and I have to say, the original is far better.  The dishes were more inventive and everything we tried at Pujol was transcendental.  With that in mind, Cosme is a solid 3.5 stars and the only reason why I rate it a 4 instead of a 3 is because the dishes that were hits were very very good. 

The stars of the meal was the salsa, entrees and dessert. None of the appetizers were all that impressive. 

For starters, we tried the Burrata, Sepia, Octopus, Cobia al Pastor and the Uni. So yes, we had the opportunity to try ALOT of the apps. Everything tasted good but Olvera is one of the best chefs in the world, so I expected much more. The Sepia and Burrata were nothing special. The Uni was fishy - my favorite was the Cobia AND the complimentary salsa and chips.  

Cosme does not have your typical salsa - their version is smokey with a sesame like flavor - we loved it so much that we kept on asking for more.  

The entrees is where Cosme really shines.  Our group of 4 shared the Duck Carnitas and the NY Strip.  The Carnitas were AMAZING - my friend whose generally skeptical of duck dishes also felt that it was delicious.  The strip was very tasty and served with an awesome green sauce  - I would get both again and return just for those dishes AND the highly touted Corn Husk Meringue 

Yes, the Meringue is THAT good. We ordered two just so that we would have enough and I'm glad we did because it lives up to the hype as one of the best dishes of 2014.

An out-of-town friend recommended this place so I thought I'd check it out. Things started out pretty well at the bar where the quite attractive mixologist served up a good tequila with a sangrita chaser. Ironically enough the bartender had recommended the Fortaleza Reposado (they didn't have Chamucos, my favorite) but when she went to get it, discovered they were out. Not a good sign at a Mexican restaurant. Nevertheless we proceeded to order some food. The uni tostada was pretty good but the "toast" was stale. And what isn't delicious with a nice serving of uni on it? Also ordered a couple of other unremarkable dishes (a rubbery and dull pulpo) and finished with the duck which was highly recommended by the bartender. It was tender, tasty, and served with fresh corn tortillas. However, it wasn't much different from the classic Peking Duck I've had in Chinatown. At this point I was pretty much done and we asked for the check.  When it arrived my friend and I discovered that they had added a dessert to the check which we hadn't ordered (or eaten). When we brought the error to the bartender's attention she gave it to an assistant to fix and her demeanor changed drastically, perhaps because they expected us not to tip them well after this egregious and quite suspicious error. I've seen this happen on a number of occasions at New York City restaurants and it's really unacceptable. I noticed that another reviewer was overcharged for his desserts...I'm hoping it was an honest mistake and if I hear back from the restaurant with an explanation I may try them again because the place is pretty and the menu (although not very well executed last night) is quite creative.

We are still dreaming about this restaurant. It is fabulous. The food is delicious, inventive and fun. The food was on par with D.O.M in San Paulo at a fraction of the price. It is not inexpensive but not expensive. We shared all the plates. The appetizers are larger than standard appetizers but are light. We were full but not over stuffed.

It is a great date restaurant since the food provides great conversation and sharing. The atmosphere is very casual but trendy without mind splitting acoustics especially, at the back of the restaurant. Kudos for understanding that acoustics matter. The tables were nicely spaced apart but we still managed to have fun talking to our neighbors. 

We ordered: 

*Stuffed avocado, seafood vuelve a la vida, horseradish. 
*Half lobster pibil, chorizo, black bean and avocado leaf purée
*White ayocote bean salad, radish, charred cucumber vinaigrette
*Husk meringue, corn mousse

Each dish was amazing. My descriptions could not do the food justice other than to say, we were practically licking the empty dishes. The flavors were so unusual and the presentation was inventive. The dessert was as amazing as the photos look. We were blown away by each item we ordered. This is clearly, not your standard Mexican restaurant. I am a huge fan of Empellon Cocina but this restaurant has raised the Mexican ante. 

My only criticism was the complimentary initial salsa with the chips. It is good but to us, it needs a bit of tweaking. It felt like something was missing from the salsa and not up to the standards of everything we ate. But it was a welcome change from the traditional guacamole and chips that I feel like the server expects you to order before you even have a chance to review your menu.

The staff is knowledgable and lovely. We are real foodies and the staff graciously, explained the different dishes and ingredients to us. The service was flawless including the bus boys who repeatedly refilled our water glasses. 

We had such a fun meal and want to thank the restaurant for accommodating us at the last minute. It was a real treat. We look forward to returning.

I came here for 3 dishes. The uni tostada, the chicharron, and the husk meringue. The first 2 were not available so we were quite disappointed so we got other items on the menu. The two seafood dishes were very flavorful and good but incredibly small portions. We also got the duck carnitas for 2 people which was massive and good at first but it came with various garnishes which helped it have more spice to the dish. The relishes were fairly small in portion so after a while the duck tasted bland since we didn't have anymore salsa or cilantro to help with flavor. 
The dessert was excellent. Overall, the meal was ok thanks to the dessert but the fact that 2 of the dishes we wanted was already at 8.30 on a Saturday is quite a let down.

Having been to Pujol in Mexico City, I was excited to see Chef Enrique Olvera was bringing some of his wonderful food to the states. As a former resident of Mexico City, I often long for excellent Mexican food. While I would trade anything to bring some of the cheap Mexico City street foods north of the border (perhaps they are already here, though I never seem to find them), I can settle for one of Mexico's pricier offerings.

Honestly after feeling like I overpaid a bit at Pujol (considering that you can get fantastic food for cheap in Mexico City), I wasn't quite as bothered by the high price point here in expensive New York. Specifically, I personally paid about $150 in Mexico for my meal plus a drink or two that still left me somewhat hungry. At Cosme, meanwhile, $100 bought me 6 plates (to share with one other) plus a drink that left me feeling full and satisfied.

Make no mistake, Cosme is not the high-class restaurant that is Pujol. Cosme is more casual and trendy for sure with no fixed menu. It has a high ceiling, moderate levels of music and noise, and dim but sufficient lighting. There is bar seating (for those like me who came without a reservation) at the front and reserved tables at the back, though the same menu is served for both (as the wait staff informed us about 4 times). 

As for the food, it was excellent. It definitely seems to cater more to American taste buds (e.g. many dishes came with tortillas to make little tacos). Wacky ingredients (to me, at least) such as escamoles (ant larvae) were missing, but that's probably the right call for conservative American eaters. Likewise, there is noticeably more of a fish-themed menu in general at Cosme than Pujol. Nonetheless, the food still felt distinctly and elegantly Mexican.

My favorite dish was probably the cobia al pastor. Honestly, I was almost fooled into thinking it was the traditional pork al pastor from the appearance and taste with only the texture noticeably differing--bravo. 

A few more points: 1) our waiter recommended 3 dishes per person which is a safe bet--I felt quite satisfied. 2) With 6 small plates, one cocktail, and one cappuccino, the total bill came out to about $180 including tip, so expect ~$100 per person. 3) This place may be booked for reservations, but walk-ins were available at the bar and some of the smaller cocktail tables. Walk-in seating was abundant and distributed on a first-come, first-served basis. We sat at a smaller table that was perfectly comfortable for our meal.

Hot New Mexican ''Cosme'' by Chef Enrique Olvera


Cosme is a hot new Mexican restaurant that just opened a few months ago on 21st Street in the Flatiron District of NYC. It's described as Mexican, but it is not your topical Mexican cuisine. It's more of a New American/Mexican fare created by the famous chef Enrique Olvera. 

I came here for dinner in October. While we were waiting for our table we had cocktails in the first room. This room has walk-in tables and you can just have a drink or order from the full food menu.

I noticed right away that they had more than the average number of staff members for a restaurant that size. It may have been because they just opened and wanted to make sure the guests received quality service. Good idea :)

We got a perfect table for two with great lighting to take photos. Thank goodness ;) I'm often afraid that a restaurant doesn't have enough light for me to take good pictures of my experience. 

When we finished our cocktails we decided to move on to a bottle of red wine just as our first appetizer, Cobia al pastor, arrived. Cobia is a type of lean and firm textured fish. It came with soft tortillas to wrap our own fish tacos. The tortillas were nice and warm when they arrived and stayed that way under a cloth it was presented in. 

The second appetizer was Scallop aguachile, poached jicama, fresh wasabi-cucumber-lime. I don't care for cooked scallop, but I'm a huge scallop lover if it is sashimi style. This appetizer was raw just how I love it. It was tasteful, although the portion was quite small. 

Finally, the entree. We ordered Duck carnitas - $49 for two people. This entree is the most expensive dish on the menu. Our server told us that if we were ordering this then we don't need to order another entree. I still wasn't sure. (My eye is always bigger than a fish's.) I'm glad he told us the truth without pushing us to order another entree. The duck came out hot on an iron-skillet frying pan. It was huge and came with warm tortillas on the side again. It wasn't for two people, it was more like 4 people to share! My friend and I weren't able to finish it. I highly recommend you order this dish. It's even perfect to order for the table as an appetizer to share, each getting one duck taco. 

On to their famous dessert now. ''Husk meringue, corn mousse'' which I didn't have!!!!!!!! This dish is posted on every food blogger's Instagram this month. I was too stuffed to order this "BucketDishList". When I go back next time I am definitely ordering it. I think I just created a new excuse for me to patrol again :) 


Here is what I ordered: 

Cobia al pastor, pineapple sauce, cilantro. 23 1/2

Scallop aguachile, poached jicama, fresh wasabi-cucumber-lime. 20 

Duck carnitas, white onions, radishes, salsa verde (to share). 49



"Cutie Patroller is always on the prowl in NYC for cute places and good food."*\(^_^)/*


XOXO

Cosme just opened 2 blocks away from my apt and that is a dangerous dangerous thing. I ate here for the first time on my bday and loved every minute of it. Mexican food is my one true love and this place delivers. 

Since we didn't have a reservation, we sat in the bar section up front, which I think has a slightly different menu than the full restaurant. Of course had the guacamole to start, which was standard but delicious. For my main I had the chilaquiles which honestly I could eat every day for the rest of my life and be ok with it. They're spicy and come with a poached egg on top. Absolutely delicious. The drinks were also on point, with some creative cocktails as well as the standard mexican fares like palomas (my personal favorite) and margaritas. I'm dying to go back and check out the full menu! This place would also be a great date spot as the atmosphere is kind of dark and swanky.

I an pretty particular about what I eat and drink. Cosme has a stellar vibe, an extensive menu of highly unusual dishes. It also has an offbeat wine list with many crowd pleasing alternatives. Wine service was spectacular. You should just go and find out for yourself.
Woody

A truly memorable experience. The staff was attentive and professional, they did not hover but were always there when you needed anything. The style and atmosphere matched the food and preparation, sophisticated refined and elegant. A wonderful experience. Chef Olvera shows very well in the BIG APPLE.

Great great great place to go. Flavors are Mexican authentic. The mezcal list is impressive. Try varied dishes as you can, you will not be disappointed. 

Five stars for the food, five stars for the chef, five stars for the wine and liquor selection, five stars for the service, 4 stars for the ambience.

Feels like you're eating in the cool part of Mexico City. Amazing aesthetic. The duck carnitas are dope, never had anything like that before. Servers were genuine and brought the whole experience together.
The meringue corn mousse dessert was incredible!!! The guacamole and the tamale apps were also amazing. The lobster was good not spectacular.  The ambiance was gorgeous.
everything on the menu exceeded expectations! this place is worth the long reservation wait and lives up to the hype.

Great innovation mixing traditional Mexican dishes with international preparation.
Innovation is going to be the key to success of this restaurant

The best of the best!!!!!!!!!!!

And believe me, I am Mexican and from Oaxaca, so I have pretty high culinary standards for Mexican food. 

I recommend the Ninja, the Duck Carnitas and of course the Merengue.

If you are lucky enough to get a reservation at Cosme, then you are in for an unforgettable dining experience.  Last year my wife and I went to the sister restaurant in Mexico City called Pujol, andraved about it.  When we heard that he opened a restaurant in NYC then we flew all the way from Maine just to try it with our adult kids.  We sampled 4 appetizers and 4 entrees and 2 desserts.  We also had the Don Julio 1942 tequila courtesy of my amigo Manuel.  Muchas gracias Amigo!  We all had a difficult time picking our favorite dish because everything was so good.  We can't wait to go back!

Excellent, creative cuisine.  Great wine list and list of tequilas and mezcals.  Very busy, but made a good, bustling atmosphere.  I had been looking forward to this opening and it did not disappoint.  Be sure to save room for their excellent desserts, especially the sweet potato flan and corn husk meringue.

Like many others, I religiously followed the consistent stream of news about Cosme, Enrique Olvera's first stint in New York City. Chef Olvera is no newcomer to the restaurant scene, as his success with Pujol, his fine-dining restaurant in Mexico City, demonstrates, but New York City is a whole new territory. The marketing for Cosme was certainly well done, however, as the restaurant was nearly completely booked for three straight months within a week of opening.

I was able to snag an early Saturday evening reservation for a party of 2, and a quick check-in process meant that we were seated promptly. The restaurant is divided into two separate areas - the bar and waiting area as well as the main dining room, which is almost completely separate from the entrance. It's a modern, well-spaced interior with plenty of two tops, several four tops, and even fewer options for larger groups. Surprisingly, the two of us were seated at a table meant for four, but I certainly wasn't complaining about the additional space.

We had our drink orders quickly addressed, and our server was efficient in going over Cosme's menu, suggesting that three plates per person would be an ideal order. I'd fully prepared myself to leave still somewhat hungry as we didn't want to spend a fortune that night, so we stuck with three items from the relatively compact menu for our meal.

After an amuse of blue corn tostada with a pumpkin seed butter, our first two plates were brought out. First on the table was the Sliced Raw Hamachi, a plate that consisted of four small cuts of the protein. I had fully prepared myself to dislike the plate, but the balance of the dish was commendable. The fish was clearly of top quality and freshness and the seasoning of fermented serrano peppers and black limes, incorporating elements of spice and acidity, was absolutely spot on. The Burrata dish was also memorable, although I found it slightly incomplete, as I'm used to eating cheese with a carbohydrate component. The mainstay of this dish was a generous ball of Burrata Mozzarella cheese, which was plated with a salsa verde and topped with various "weeds". The texture of the cheese was decadent, with a milky center that spilled over, and the salsa verde was a much-needed savory and acidic counter to it. 

There hasn't been much mention for the Duck Carnitas, but I'm certainly glad we ordered this. The duck is served still sizzling in a cast iron skillet, with a plate of warm blue corn tortillas and a chile de arbol salsa. It's essentially a "make your own taco" dish, as we took turns scooping out the protein onto our tortilla shells, layering in the various onions and radishes, and then adding a spoonful of salsa before eating. The serving of duck is very generous and definitely more than enough for two people; the skin is crispy and nicely caramelized, and the underlying white meat still tender and juicy. There's a good ratio of lean to fatty protein too, which makes for an even more flavorful taco. The salsa is simultaneously spicy and salty and acidic, which complements the duck very well.

By this point, dessert was slightly out of the question, so we opted out of a final course; our server suggested we return for the Husk Meringue, however, noting that my "photo collection wouldn't be complete without it". There were several reviews prior that mentioned several flaws in service, but I found both the timing of courses and the interactions with the staff to be on point. To be fair, I was a little surprised that they charged us for the additional tortillas, but I'd have to agree that good food is certainly worth paying a premium for.

This restaurant has the potential to be great. The major issue was the lack of proper training for front of house. Upon being greeted at the host stand one is faced with the typical airhead hostess rocking attitude like it's this seasons Stella McCartney, who then deign to show the guest to their table. Honestly, should I be surprised? 

My co-diner and I sat at the communal tables. It took our server upwards of 5 minutes to acknowledge our presence. While we patiently sat he eventually noticed us and asked for our water preferences. Another 5 minutes passed and our water glasses were still decorations on a table. We eventually reminded him that we were without and then an awkward sparkling/still water snafu ensued. Our server then asked us if we could get started with drinks! Yes! Drinks! We'd love to imbibe...but we never received the cocktail/wine list. Altogether an easy 30 minutes wafted by until we had water, alcohol and our food order in. 

What I have to commend is the support staff. The runners and bussers are extremely tentative and atune with the goings on of the floor. When a plate was dropped infront of me and my guest they explained the dish clearly. They did not rush to clear plates. They consistently filled water glasses despite there being a glass water pitcher on the table. Also, I must commend the back of house. Dishes were plated with a careful artistic eye and all the food came out in a timely fashion. I also appreciated that plates came out individually.  It gave us the chance to properly taste the dish and not have it be muddled with other flavors. The only time an obvious hiccup occurred was when we had to interact with our server. We waited around 10 minutes for glasses of wine whereas our cocktails we started with came out immediately, questionable...seeing as the former logically involves fewer steps.

When we asked for the bill we received it immediately (everything else was a wait so I can only assume Flojo was reincarnated in our server for that brief moment in time) and asked to split check. After the cards were rung I discovered that my card was rung twice, once for the full amount and the second time for half the check. After pointing it out we got a murmur of an apology and my card was then re-rerung  (3rd times a charm, aye). 

It's a shame that so much apparent thought and effort went into the esthetics and menu of this restaurant but they are not equipped with a properly trained front of house. 

In summation, people go out to eat because they are hungry for an experience and a well trained service staff is a crucial aspect of that experience. The bussers and runners should be servers at this restaurant. Their English may not be as fluent as the current servers but they have a lot more passion and drive for what would be to most a menial job.

Not one to be late to the game when it comes to new restaurants in my neighborhood, I finally went to Cosme and I was overwhelmed by the entire experience!  It's unlike any Mexican restaurant I've ever been to - no Mexican hats and blankets on the wall!  The décor is simple and elegantly sparse.   But warm and inviting too.   I felt like I was in Barcelona, not in a NYC Mexican restaurant.  Cosme is what I call, simply elegant.

And the modern décor matches the food. You won't find tacos and burritos here.  Instead the menu had me spinning because I'd never seen anything like it.  My first challenge was choosing between a starter of burrata with salsa verde or swiss chard tamal with ricotta and salsa -- my taste buds were going crazy!   I went with the burrata.  When it came to the main course, I had to defer to our amazing waiter (really helpful and not at all rushed).  He suggested the NY strip with shishitos, avocado and tarragon.  Both were out of this world delicious!  And to top it off we indulged in the lemon cake with grapefruit and quince sorbet for desert.  Heaven.
   
I suggest not just showing up -- make a reservation because the wait without one is painfully long.

Viva Cosme!

Scored a reservation last minute. The atmosphere is dark and chic, sexy and modern.

We shared the lobster pupil. Really tender lobster that you role into blue corn tortillas. Loved the black bean purée and chorizo. This was my favorite savory course of the night.

The duck was massive. Good for three or more. You also make tacos with the duck. It had huge pieces of fat (although it was sweet tasting fat), so it was really rich for two of us to share and made it hard to try anything else as it was so rich and filling.

Corn meringue was very good and reminded me of a child dessert that I cannot put my finger on.
Everyone loves the octopus but this was not my favorite. I prefer cooked octopus to ceviche style.
 Cocktails were strong and tasty. Service was impersonal and rushed. I would not rush back.

the place is charming and such a far cry from the usual cliches of Mexican cuisine. the chef Olvera is known as the best chef in Mexico and perhaps globally. prepare yourself to be surprise.

the food will delight you, it is light refined and wonderful to look at. the diversity of textures and ingredients is wonderful.

the best choice of Tequilas one could ask for. really high end stuff.
you will find no large hats or mexican curios rather some high end mexican engravings on the walls.

the food will delight you, it is light refined and wonderful to look at. the diversity of textures and ingredients is wonderful.

the best choice of Tequilas one could ask for. really high end stuff.

the atmosfere is cool and elegant.

a must go with you guapa or con tus amigos.

enjoy. nothing like it in NY if you wish to discover high end Mexican Cuisine at affordable prices.... (for now).

Guy

By far the best Mexican cuisine I've had in the States. The pumpkin seed and habanero salsa you get, with authentic tostadas, at the very beginning, are a fantastic start. We were a party of four, so we had a chance to try a lot of dishes. Outstanding ones were the scallop aguachile, the enfrijoladas, the burrata with salsa verde, and the mushroom barbacoa (that comes with real tortillas, made with single origin Oaxaca corn. Forget the white, cardboard-like, flavorless crap you've been having all this time. These are what real Mexican tortillas taste like).

But the best dish by far was the duck carnitas. Amazing flavor, soft and juicy, and the salsa verde to complement is amazing.

For dessert I had the merengue with corn mousse. Best dessert I have had in the last couple of years.

Things that could be better? The time between dishes felt long, and the other desserts weren't anywhere near the merengue. But it's not enough to drive it down to 4 stars... the food is THAT good. 5/5.
Amazing food and drinks. Favorite dishes the agua chile, cobia al pastor, steak and duck carnitas. Like nothing in NY, really cool crowd too.

I was so looking forward to trying Cosme, following all the hype.  So I sadly have to report it was a major disappointment.  Maybe it was just too early after the opening, but the food was OK, and relatively bland and tasteless.  It was not cheap either.  And sitting in the front room during a cold night was almost unbearable.  With so many good places to try-The Nomad, Piora and also elan just around the corner, you can do much better.

I'm a fan of Pujol in Mexico City, and excuse my excitement of joining the hype that is surrounding Cosme, but overall I'm glad I was able to dined there! 

Let's talk about food... it's fantastic! I'm Mexican and really enjoyed to see how Mexican Food was taken to the next level. The tortillas and salsas are fantastic, maybe I've had better salsas, but these are excellent and having them paired with perfectly executed dishes is fantastic. I did some research on favorite dishes, so I was prepared to enjoy the Duck Carnitas and only ordered two dishes prior this: Cobia al Pastor and Enfrijoladas. Both were good, but the Duck Carnitas stole the show! Do not order more than two dishes before, even if you're hungry.... we were so full and barely made it to dessert. The average tapas dishes are $20dlls, and the Duck Carnitas are about $45, easily can serve up to 4 people  so there you have an excellent deal. The Husk Merengue is a must try, a combination of sweet and salty, it reminded me the good experience you have when eating a sweet corn tamal. The drinks are great, interesting combinations, and really loved seeing a Carajillo for after-dinner (Liquor 43 and espresso shot). 

Now... let's talk about service. 
Here is where Cosme really has a lot of room to improve. We read comments about service so we were prepared with lower expectations (I told you I was there about the food). The host and hostess were the odd pieces there. When we were leaving my BF told the host that we had an amazing meal but they should keep looking at the reviews since service seems not to impress, and the host said that he hasn't even look at them, that the NYT gave them raved reviews (the NYT only talked about the hype of Enrique Olvera BEFORE the opening and the day of). The staff at the main dinning room are very very very nice, but seems that they're in early stage and the waiters still need to improve the skills on how to explain the dishes. In Pujol they almost recite the ingredients. It took a bit while to get us the tostadas and Carajillo at the end. 

My tip to make it during the "so-impossible-to-get-a-reservation-season"  is that show up no matter what. I luckily  scored one a month ago for last night, but I noticed a couple of tables were empty by 10-10.30pm, and there was plenty of room at the bar (well, it was 27F degrees outside). Maybe during winter and early in the week might be easier to be seated. 


We spent $200 dlls tip included for 4 dishes (Cobia, Enfrijoladas, Duck and Merengue) and 7 drinks (cocktails, wine and after dinner liquor), and left VERY full. At Pujol we paid $300 dlls tip included for 2 tasting menus and about 5 drinks and left just full. So Cosme can be a deal for NYC standards. 

Should I go back? Sure, not too soon bc is bit pricey.... but that Duck Carnitas will be a motivator to continue going to the gym! I really wanted to try more dishes so maybe I'll go to the bar to try two or three over a drink. 

Food: 5/5
Drinks: 5/5
Service: 3/5 (mostly well earned by the staff at the dinning room)

I've just had the most unpleasant dining experience in recent history that I felt the need to pen this review (I rarely write these reviews because I don't feel that passionately negative about most dining experiences in the city). I wanted to find a way to get in touch with the general manager, but I couldn't find any contact information online. I would love to give this feedback to Enrique Olvera himself in case he cares. 

This place opens at 6 PM, but we had read somewhere that it opens at 5 PM. Didn't have a reservation, so wanted to do a walk-in, so we went at 5 PM. The door was open so I walked in and seemed to have caught the group of staff prepping by the bar off guard. The host (Adam was his name I later learned) came rushing to say that the place opens at 6 PM, not 5 PM. I was supposed to meet a friend so I was peering inside to see if my friend was anywhere and asking if anyone had come by, and I found the host to be completely rude as he was busy shooing me out of the restaurant, repeatedly emphasizing that Google has the wrong information about the restaurant being open at 5 PM. He was completely dismissive and testy, and the short interaction was very off-putting and unpleasant. He was so rushed to get me out of the restaurant (kept backing me into the front entrance area) that I had to tell him "I am leaving!! I got it!" 

We contemplated whether or not to go back, but went back at 6 PM. I really wish that we had gone elsewhere. UGH!! 

We found the servers very nice (no complaints there), but there was a woman who was probably a host as well (didn't get her name, tall, brunette?- probably not helping much with that description). After finishing our meal, on our way out, we gave her our coat tickets to get our coats. She didn't show for a good chunk of time, and we were beginning to wonder where she was. It was a longer than normal period of time to be waiting for our coats at a restaurant on our way out. By the time she was making her way over to us, we were both impatient, and I don't deny that we must have looked it. She came straight up to me and the first thing she says is: "I don't need you to give me that look." EXCUSE ME??!!! I told her that she doesn't need to say things like that, and she said that she had been trying to apologize (that's her way of apologizing??) but that I gave her a look. I reminded her "You never apologized just now. That is NOT an apology." I left in a huff, needless to say. 

The food itself was fine here (I liked the duck very much as well as the meringue), but the staff especially the hosts need to be trained better in how they talk to and engage customers. These interactions, albeit short, were incredibly unpleasant experiences, and I will NEVER be coming back nor will I be recommending this place to anyone I know. Ironically, I had gone there because a close friend couldn't stop talking about the meringue. 

My goal in writing this review is less about publicly condemning this place which seems to be generating a lot of buzz with the innovative cooking, but more about my wish to NOT have anyone else experience what I did tonight with poorly trained, defensive, rude, unpleasant staff, having spent close to $200 for two people. Hosts are the faces of a dining establishment, and the first and the last set of interactions between customers and the restaurant. It is hardly acceptable that I started and ended my dining experience here on such a negative note. I sincerely hope that the restaurant looks at presenting both impeccable food AND customer service.

Oh and the restaurant opens at 6 pm so don't dare go early!!

Clean // Modern // World Class
Fine + Casual Atmosphere
Quality resonates in every detail. 

Famed Chef Enrique Olvera dreamt of opening a restaurant in New York City. With handmade tortillas, timed to perfection. Each and every detail of the dishes seems to reflect passion from the heart.

Came here with a friend to try some drinks and appetizers at the bar. At $14/drink they were not unreasonable considering the environment, and location. I loved my bourbon based drink, and we tasted several other drinks which the bartender made. All hand crafted and well thought out. Their drinks definitely pair well with menu items. Looking forward to coming back for dinner.

Rumor has it reservations are 6 months out -- popular place!

The Scene: Modern, Legendary Chef (from Mexico)
Destination Rating: 8
Date Rating: 9 
Hob Nob Potential: 1

Strong Suggestion: While our service was great, I couldn't help but notice some of the reviews. Remember this restaurant is new and working things out, service should improve over time... We had a GREAT bartender, and a solid experience.

Nobody's writing about the duck? Maybe it's not being ordered because it's expensive and to be shared by two? What a mistake! Think the best of pulled pork and Peking duck. The moist meat is tender, rough-shredded, beautifully seasoned, and left with some fatless skin but no gnarly bones or gristle. You serve yourself from a heaping casserole (that could serve four) by lining a fresh, warm taco with a terrific green salsa and then creating the ultimate hand roll with piles of the meat. The combination of the richness of the duck, the kick of the salsa, and the comfort of the soft taco is stunning. We also loved the octopus and he squid, but talk about after-thoughts! Yes, the welcome service was chaotic, but I'd put up with much worse to get back to that duck.

There are 16 options in the menu and portions are small. My friend and I tried the tamal,  octopus,  lobster and enfrijoladas which were delicious!!! From the dessert menu, we loved the merengue and the cilantro sorbet!!! The lemon cake and chocolate mousse were ok but not great. The margarita wasn't our favorite thing to drink. The staff was extremely nice and we really enjoyed our visit. We definitely recommend it.

After enjoying a meal recently at Pujol in Mexico City we were excited to head to cosme. The food didn't disappoint in the least and it is an elegantly cool spot. But the service was way subpar for a restaurant of this caliber. 

All the food was delightful and especially enjoyed the carnitas and barbacoa. We were encouraged to order one item each from each of the three categories. It proved too much food. 

But I'm not sure how fast I will return because the service was really lousy. Food came out haphazardly despite being told it would be spaced, I had to ask literally four times for a replacement napkin when mine fell on the floor, no one checked on our drinks or food, no waiter ever made eye contact so as to give us an opening to make a request. It also seemed like no one was in charge; lots of busboys running about and the occasional waiter. I normally don't focus on service but it was so lousy that this bears mentioning. 

So 5 stars for food and 1 for service.

We did it! After reading how this restaurant is booked through next year, I didnt know when I would get to check it out. My bf surprised me and snagged a late reservation. The food was wonderful- we ordered the guacamole, lobster pibil and chilaquiles.  The menu was very unique and when we ordered we had no idea what we were going to get on our plates. So yummy! The striptease and paloma went down very smooth. Overall this restaurant is actually worth the hype!

Food - Full 5 stars. Service 2 Stars. Nett 3.5/5. $180 for two people for all vegetarian fare with two glasses of wine each.This place in new, they have to improve their service dramatically. Extra-ordinary food paired to less than ordinary service can be dangerous for a new restaurant like Cosme.

Burrata  5/5
Ayocote 5/5
Tortillas 5/5
Tamal 5/5
Enfrigolades 5/5

Wine paring needs to improve significantly. On service we were attended to by   6 people from time to time, which was very strange. We had to repeat our requests/ food choices  for almost every course.    .

I had a great experience here from start to finish. The staff know what they are doing and the kitchen delivers. The menu is easy to understand as it is categorized from fish, to vegetables, to meats. 

I highly recommend the burrata, the mushroom and squash barbacoa, Chilaquiles, salsa roja, queso fresco, runny egg, and the husk meringue for sure. The tamal was a skip for us. The food and presentation is really clean and modern. I highly recommend trying this place out.

The restaurant is still struggling with the service but there were some bright notes.  Good drinks from Eric at the bar and tasty guacamole comped due to a very long wait for the table despite a confirmed reservation.  Our waiter was nice but the timing of everything was wacky and the other wait staff was sort of scattered and not as gracious as we would have liked. 
The food was good but did not sing as the food we had at the chef's restaurant in Mexico.  Very nice interior design. We root for everything to come together and will try the restaurant again in several weeks.

I tried this restaurant just over a week after it opened formally. Given how tough it is to get a reservation and how well-known the Enrique Olvera Mexico City restaurant is, it was pretty disappointing.

The food was, for the most part, very flavorful and delicious. However, the service was nothing short of atrocious. It was almost comical, except for the fact that at that price, you'd hope that you could get the cocktail you ordered at the beginning of the evening before the meal was over, and without reminding 10 different staff members, many of whom did not know much English. We had to explain how to make a vodka soda to the fourth person that took our drink order. After reminding about 5 waiters that we were still waiting for our simple drinks, they took another 20 minutes to arrive. This happened over and over again with the drinks.

All in all, the food here gives this place promise. If they don't learn to get it together and hire competent staff that is attentive, fluent in English, and familiar with the menu (bar and food) and service etiquette, it's really going to drag this place down. I hope they iron out the kinks and become something impressive!

Sublime interpretation of the Mexican lexicon of flavors. The dishes have depth without being overwhelming. This is fine dining in a relaxed atmosphere. It is not cheap, but the ingredients are remarkably fresh and the dishes thoughtful. I can't wait to try it again.

Simply amazing! My fiancee and I started the night at the bar, where we got two amazing cocktails (if you're into mezcal you have to try the Ninja). At the restaurant we tried a large variety of dishes and they were all delicious. Highlights included: tuna tostada, cobia al pastor, enfrijoladas con hoja santa, and lobster pibil. I am from Mexico and I found all of these to be rich and innovative renditions of Mexican cuisine classics. Even if you don't have room for desert, you HAVE TO try the corn husk merengue... it's sensational!
Duck carnitas is the best duck I've had in years. Tortillas nixtamalized in house. Husk meringue is a must

I've read the raves, and wanted to put my 2 cents in. We were there on opening night, very excited to have snagged a reservation. We left an hour later sorely disappointed. First, the drinks at the bar ($17) were nothing special. That made us uneasy. Once we were seated, we decided to start ordering small and if the food was great, to keep going. Everyone's right - small portions, so if you're hungry, be prepared for a big bill. Anyway, we got our first dish, and the unease deepened. I had the scallop dish. It sounded great, but all I could make out in this white dish was a fairly flavorless soft taste (I assumed was the scallop) and a crunchy taste, and some heat...and very little of either, since it looked like there was one scallop in there sliced very thin. The main flavor was olive oil. My friend was disappointed as well in his lobster and chorizo dish - not terrible but really nothing special. We stopped ordering and left (hungry). Maybe it will get better, but I cannot endorse the glowing reviews at all. We're both very happy to drop quite a bit of money if the food is outstanding (Dovetail, 11 Madison Park) but I'd rather eat at the rich and flavorful taqueria in my neighborhood than spend hundreds of dollars here.
After we were seated we finally got to see their overly hyped menu.  After looking at the menu we could not find anything on it that we would be interested in eating, so we got up and left.

Visited on the third day after they officially opened and it shows. 
Kitchen is turning out very good high end Mexican cooking but are backed up by extremely uneven service. 
I'll cover the downside first, showed up early for our reservation and were asked to be seated in the bar area which we were more than happy to do. Took over 20 mins to get a cocktail after we ordered it. 
Cocktails were good and had some snacks of the mussel tostada which was fantastic and the smoked sepia which had a nice subtle smoke flavor but a texture that is more of an acquired taste. 
Waited for quite some time after finishing the drinks and snack and finally after it was 10 mins after our reservation time went up to ask if we could be seated. 
Maitre d' said we could sit at a communal table or wait 30 mins. 
I expressed confusion since we had a reservation to which he acted surprised like he had never seen us before despite the fact we had specifically checked in with him and sat in his direct line of site for 40 mins. 
He then simply walked off and another female hostess came up and said she would see if our table was ready. 
We sat down for 10 more mins and watched several empty tables before the original male matre d came back and just stared at us oddly. 
My wife asked "are you ready for us?" And he said yes. 
He walked us back to our table and finally at the table offered to take our heavy coats which we had carried since we came in only after he saw us trying to put them on the chair backs in confusion. 
We were then handed menus which were stained with salsa and avocado from previous customers and ignored for another 10 minutes. 

Thankfully, after that things started to improve significantly. 
The staff in the dining room were much more attentive and pleasant and very soon we were able to make drink and food orders and proceeded to have a good meal. The only other hiccup was that my wife reported the bathroom as out of order. 

So on to the better news. All the dishes ordered ranged from very good to excellent. Single-origin blue corn tortillas were fantastic and had a range of salsas very well balanced with enough heat to notice but not to be overwhelmed. 

We ordered:
Octopus cocktail - excellent octopus with delicate heat and red onion with purple corn. 

Burrata with weeds - cool and creamy and delicious with a wonderful herby salsa verde. 

Cobia al Pastor - slices of cobia tataki with pineable. The cobia was a more neutral flavor but carried the bright pineapple and included tortillas and salsa. 

Lobster Pibil Sope - A standout dish with lobster and chorizo and creamy black beans. 

Duck Carnitas for 2 - a lot bigger than we expected and very rich. This one required careful eating. You had to balance it with just the right amount of skin and fat and salsa. Otherwise it came across as somewhat dry. But eaten in balance was good. But by this time we could not finish it all as we were too full. 

Had to skip dessert which was hard since we heard the corn mousse was very good. 

All in all solid cooking and I would love to try again when they hopefully have everything running smoothly. 
If that were to happen this could certainly be a 4 star review or better. This is Enrique Olvera of Pujol so it's obvious he can produce 5 star food. But given the comically bad service to get seated and being handed dirty menus  it started off a good meal with a bad taste in our mouths.

The Mexican-inspired fare at @CosmeNYC by @EnriqueOlvera is New York City's hottest! During my time living in NYC, one of the biggest complaints had always been the lack of quality Mexican food. While visiting from San Diego, we had the pleasure of dining at Cosme during their soft opening on Saturday October 25th -- it was mind-blowingly good. 

Including dessert, we ordered and shared these eight items:

*Burrata, salsa verde, weeds
-- a fantastic combination of flavors you must order

*Mussel tostada, Russian salad, chipotle mayonnaise
--it's a tostada like no other, featuring chunky portions of mussel coated in a spicy cream sauce. 

*Sliced raw hamachi, fermented serrano, black limes
--great, high quality sashimi

*Cobia al pastor, pineapple, cilantro
-- another must order item! An interesting preparation of the fish, and the pineapple adds a flavor like no other.

*Octopus cocktail, yellow cônico corn atole, red onion, avocado
-- if you love octopus (pulpo) order this, if you're not sure about octopus order this and have your mind changed.

*Mushroom and squash barbacoa, chilpachole
--the sauce is AMAZING!

*Lobster pibil, chorizo, black beans
--a solid dish for lobster and chorizo lovers

*Dessert: Husk meringue, corn mousse
-- This is a dessert that I've been thinking about all day. It has a hardened outer shell or meringue with a light salt taste, along with a sweet corn custard inside, a combo which provides a perfect balance. 

Rare for me, is that there was not a single item we ordered I wouldn't try again. They also have a craft cocktail and wine list, however my only criticism is in the lack of wines from Mexico. The Guadalupe Valley region of Baja California (near Ensenada) features phenomenal wines, and Cosme is the ideal place to introduce paired selections to New Yorkers. We ordered a bottle of the one Mexican wine on the menu and loved it; we think others would too.

I live in the neighborhood. The staff was  very friendly. If you're against very attractive  bartenders and people this place is not for you. I will be back. Dear Yelp friends, you would like this place.

The Eater and Grubstreet hype machines have been doing a good job of making me really want to try Cosme, so I was excited to snag a table during the first week they are open, when they are currently accepting same day reservations, since the online reservations are booked pretty solid through November.

Make no mistake, this is fine dining in a more casual atmosphere. You will either leave starving, or drop a pretty penny on several small plates, which all happen to taste amazing. Our experience was somewhere in the middle:

- Tostadas with Pumpkin Seed Butter
This is an incredibly good complimentary bite to start with. Too fancy for chips and salsa, they instead give you two large, round cracker thin tostadas accompanied by some pumpkin seed butter. The warm, crispy tostadas were tasty enough on their own, but even better with some of that butter spread on. Make sure to request more of these to better get your money's worth.

- Burrata and Weeds ($22)
One of the "in" dishes lately, the Burrata was also recommended by our server, and it was delicious. It is topped with small pieces of those crunchy tostadas, but not nearly enough for the whole dish, especially if you aren't the biggest fan of eating just pure cheese like me, so this is a good time to request more of those that they brought out to start. Much like a lot of the stuff though, I'm not sure about that price tag.

- Octopus Cocktail, Yellow Conico Corn Atole, Red Onion, Avocado ($25)
Touted as the chef's signature dish, this did not disappoint. I never really order octopus, since it can often be too rubbery, so I was delighted to find that this was one of the best octopus dishes I've ever had. It had a slightly chewy, but not at all rubbery texture, and was delicious when paired in a bite with the creamy avocado, onions, and little kernels of black corn. This was definitely the best dish of the night. 

- NY Strip, Shishitos, Peas, Avocado, Tarragon Puree ($34)
These four little pieces of meat were delicious, but not nearly satisfying enough for 34 bucks. The dish was served with small tortillas for making your own little wraps, which added a little more sustenance, but I didn't really taste anything particularly special in the raved about warm tortillas.  

- Cobia al Pastor, Pineapple, Cilantro ($22)
This was delicious as well, 6 small slices of cobia garnished with sweet pineapple and cilantro. Maybe skip one of these pricier dishes though in favor of the strongest thing here, the desserts.

- Husk Meringue, Corn Mousse ($12)
This strange-looking but somehow very attractive thing is in every Instagram shot taken here, and it is worth ordering for more than just the pretty picture. It's a big, white meringue shell with creamy corn mousse spilling out of the center. It sounds like a weird flavor combination, but it is really delicious. Get this.

- Chocolate, Tamarind, Orange Sorbet ($12)
But also get this, another really great dessert. As a contrast to the hunk of meringue mentioned above, this is another one of the very artfully plated dishes here. Thin pieces of chocolate brownies are stacked around a small scoop of orange sorbet in the middle, all on top of rich, creamy dollops of chocolate. Sweeter than the meringue option, this is another great choice.

The atmosphere in the main dining room is one of the coolest I've seen lately. It's almost like there's a spotlight on each table, as it is quite dark, with high, bright lights above each table. The service was impeccable too, making for a very pleasant experience throughout.

Having ordered most of the stuff on the menu (other than shellfish that I am not able to eat), I don't really see the need to return any time soon given the prices and the difficulty at scoring a table. Still, it's definitely an excellent restaurant that's worth trying for the amazing food, as long as you are willing to spend a little too much.

As a rule, I try to wait at least a month before trying a new restaurant in order to give it time to find itself, work out service kinks, etc.  When my girlfriend snagged a reservation during Cosme's soft opening, that rule went out the window.

We were a party of four and the server, who claimed the portions were "very small", recommended two dishes per person.  There were 12 items on the menu, ranging from $12 - $34; we ordered eight.  

I read the NY Times article where Olvera claimed most of his dishes would be under $20; he left out that there would be two to three bites per dish.  Even someone used to eating at Estela every night would notice how little food was on each plate.

The food, though, was very good.  It's a seafood heavy menu and the stars were the tataki al pastor, in the form of perfectly cooked pennies to be wrapped into Olvera's delicious tortillas; the lobster pipil sope, sitting atop a black bean puree; and the mushroom barbacoa, which was a very creative melding of vegetable, meat and sauce.

After the eight main dishes, we ordered two desserts.  The best thing we ate, unanimously and by a huge margin, was the Husk meringue dessert with corn mousse.  Wow.  I recommend getting one for two people max; you won't want to share any more than that.

Across four people, we had eight mains, two desserts and three rounds of drinks; the bill with tip came out to $480.  

I see Cosme settling into a good option before a night out -- it will be trendy and you won't be full.  

(3.5 / 5, rounded to 4 due to anticipated improvements in atmosphere and service.)

For the first time I felt the mexican taste in a restaurant outside of Mexico. Everything made with so much care and gourmet style. I enjoyed every part of it, specially the mescal drinks.. the striptease has just become my favorite.

Such a wonderful restaurant!  I can't say enough good things about our experience last night.  Food, drinks and design were fantastic. The front bar area was a perfect place to have drinks before din -- very sleek design and warmly lit.  Burrata and lobster tacos were our favorite dishes -- the tortillas with the tacos were indeed awesome.  Highly recommend Cosme!

Tried pre opening.  Limited menu mostly small plates.  Innovative modern Mexican.  Excellent food and service in an informal setting. Very good wine list.  The hamachi was outstanding.  Lobster and octopus deserve to be tried.  Will be back after formal openeng.

about: Cosme is a restaurant in New York City's Flatiron District serving contemporary Mexican cuisine. World-renowned Chef Enrique Olvera and his team create dishes rooted in Mexican flavors and traditions, while also celebrating local and seasonal ingredients from the Hudson Valley and surrounding region. Cosme's beverage program focuses on artisanal spirits and mirrors its cuisine, letting the high quality ingredients shine.
